qs.s: Factor \(a^4 - b^4\) as \((a^2 - b^2)(a^2 + b^2)\), then factor the difference of squares \(a^2 - b^2\) to get \((a - b)(a + b)(a^2 + b^2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 - 256\)
Factor completely: \(c^4 - 16d^4\)
qs.s: Factor \(c^4 - 16d^4\) as the difference of squares \((c^2 - 4d^2)(c^2 + 4d^2)\), then factor \(c^2 - 4d^2\) to obtain \((c - 2d)(c + 2d)(c^2 + 4d^2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(m^4 - 81\)
qs.s: Factor \(m^4 - 81\) as a difference of squares to get \((m^2 - 9)(m^2 + 9)\). Then factor \(m^2 - 9\) to obtain \((m - 3)(m + 3)(m^2 + 9)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(16x^4 - 81y^4\)
qs.s: Factor \(16x^4 - 81y^4\) as the difference of squares \((4x^2 - 9y^2)(4x^2 + 9y^2)\), then factor \(4x^2 - 9y^2\) to get \((2x - 3y)(2x + 3y)(4x^2 + 9y^2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^8 - 1\)
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares repeatedly: \(x^8 - 1 = (x^4 - 1)(x^4 + 1) = (x^2 - 1)(x^2 + 1)(x^4 + 1) = (x - 1)(x + 1)(x^2 + 1)(x^4 + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2y^5 - 162y\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2y\) to get \(2y(y^4 - 81)\), then factor \(y^4 - 81\) using difference of squares twice to obtain \(2y(y - 3)(y + 3)(y^2 + 9)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, where \(n\) is a positive integer: \(x^{4n} - 1\)
qs.s: Recognize \(x^{4n} - 1\) as a difference of squares \((x^{2n} - 1)(x^{2n} + 1)\), then factor \(x^{2n} - 1\) to get \((x^n - 1)(x^n + 1)(x^{2n} + 1)\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(6x^2 + 13x + 6 = (2x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(3x\), and the constant term \(6\) by \(3\) to get \(2\). Checking the middle term gives \((2x)(2) + (3)(3x) = 13x\), so the missing factor is \(3x + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(5x^2 - 7x + 2 = (5x - 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(5x^2\) by \(5x\) to get \(x\), and the constant term \(2\) by \(-2\) to get \(-1\). Checking the middle term, \((5x)(-1) + (-2)(x) = -7x\), so the missing factor is \(x - 1\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(3x^2 + 10x + 8 = (3x + 4)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(3x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(x\), and the constant term \(8\) by \(4\) to get \(2\). Checking the middle term, \((3x)(2) + (4)(x) = 10x\), so the missing factor is \(x + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(4x^2 + 8x + 3 = (2x + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(4x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(2x\), and the constant term \(3\) by \(1\) to get \(3\). Checking the middle term gives \((2x)(3) + (1)(2x) = 8x\), so the missing factor is \(2x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(2x^2 + 7x + 3 = (2x + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(2x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(x\), and the last term \(3\) by \(1\) to get \(3\). Checking the middle term, \((2x)(3) + (1)(x) = 7x\), so the missing factor is \(x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(20x^2 - 37x + 8 = (4x - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(20x^2\) by \(4x\) to get \(5x\), and the constant term \(8\) by \(-1\) to get \(-8\). Checking the middle term gives \((4x)(-8) + (-1)(5x) = -37x\), so the missing factor is \(5x - 8\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(12x^2 - 17xy + 6y^2 = (3x - 2y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(12x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(4x\), and the last term \(6y^2\) by \(-2y\) to get \(-3y\). Checking the middle term gives \((3x)(-3y) + (-2y)(4x) = -17xy\), so the missing factor is \(4x - 3y\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(10x^3 + 23x^2 - 5x = x(5x - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: After dividing out the common factor \(x\), divide \(10x^2\) by \(5x\) to get \(2x\), and \(-5\) by \(-1\) to get \(5\). Checking the middle term gives \((5x)(5) + (-1)(2x) = 23x\), so the missing factor is \(2x + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(8x^2 + 22xy - 21y^2 = (4x - 3y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(8x^2\) by \(4x\) to get \(2x\), and the last term \(-21y^2\) by \(-3y\) to get \(7y\). Checking the middle term, \((4x)(7y) + (-3y)(2x) = 22xy\), so the missing factor is \(2x + 7y\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(14x^2 + 13x - 12 = (2x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(14x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(7x\), and the constant term \(-12\) by \(3\) to get \(-4\). Checking the middle term gives \((2x)(-4) + (3)(7x) = 13x\), so the missing factor is \(7x - 4\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(6x^2 + x - 12 = (2x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) yields \(3x\), and dividing \(-12\) by \(3\) yields \(-4\). Checking the middle term, \((2x)(-4) + (3)(3x) = x\), confirming the missing factor is \(3x - 4\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(15x^2 - 14x + 3 = (5x - 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(15x^2\) by \(5x\) gives \(3x\), and dividing \(3\) by \(-3\) gives \(-1\). Checking the middle term, \((5x)(-1) + (-3)(3x) = -14x\), so the missing factor is \(3x - 1\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(12x^2 - 7x - 10 = (3x + 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(12x^2\) by \(3x\) gives \(4x\), and dividing \(-10\) by \(2\) gives \(-5\). Verifying the middle term, \((3x)(-5) + (2)(4x) = -7x\), so the missing factor is \(4x - 5\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(10x^2 + 19x + 6 = (5x + 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(10x^2\) by \(5x\) gives \(2x\), and dividing \(6\) by \(2\) gives \(3\). Checking the middle term, \((5x)(3) + (2)(2x) = 19x\), so the missing factor is \(2x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(14x^2 + 29xy - 15y^2 = (2x + 5y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(14x^2\) by \(2x\) gives \(7x\), and dividing \(-15y^2\) by \(5y\) gives \(-3y\). Checking the middle term, \((2x)(-3y) + (5y)(7x) = 29xy\), confirming the missing factor is \(7x - 3y\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(35x^2 - 32x - 12 = (5x - 6)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(35x^2\) by \(5x\) gives \(7x\), and dividing \(-12\) by \(-6\) gives \(2\). Checking the middle term, \((5x)(2) + (-6)(7x) = -32x\), so the missing factor is \(7x + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(12x^4 + 11x^2 - 36 = (3x^2 - 4)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the leading term \(12x^4\) by \(3x^2\) gives \(4x^2\), and dividing \(-36\) by \(-4\) gives \(9\). Verifying the middle term, \((3x^2)(9) + (-4)(4x^2) = 11x^2\), so the missing factor is \(4x^2 + 9\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(24x^2 - 41xy + 12y^2 = (8x - 3y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(24x^2\) by \(8x\) yields \(3x\), and dividing \(12y^2\) by \(-3y\) yields \(-4y\). Since \((8x)(-4y) + (-3y)(3x) = -41xy\), the missing factor is \(3x - 4y\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(36x^2 - 25x - 25 = (4x - 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(36x^2\) by \(4x\) gives \(9x\), and dividing \(-25\) by \(-5\) gives \(5\). Checking the middle term, \((4x)(5) + (-5)(9x) = -25x\), so the missing factor is \(9x + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(2x^2 + x - 6 = (2x - 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(2x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(x\), and divide \(-6\) by \(-3\) to get \(2\). Checking the middle term gives \(2x(2) + (-3)(x) = x\), so the missing factor is \(x + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(5x^2 + 14x - 3 = (5x - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(5x^2\) by \(5x\) to get \(x\), and divide \(-3\) by \(-1\) to get \(3\). Checking the middle term gives \(5x(3) + (-1)(x) = 14x\), so the missing factor is \(x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(2x^2 + 9x + 4 = (2x + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(2x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(x\), and the constant term \(4\) by \(1\) to get \(4\). Verifying the middle term gives \(2x(4) + 1(x) = 9x\), so the missing factor is \(x + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(3x^2 + 7x + 2 = (3x + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(3x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(x\), and the constant term \(2\) by \(1\) to get \(2\). Checking the middle term gives \(3x(2) + 1(x) = 7x\), confirming the missing factor is \(x + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(10x^2 - 29xy + 21y^2 = (5x - 7y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(10x^2\) by \(5x\) to get \(2x\), and divide \(21y^2\) by \(-7y\) to get \(-3y\). Checking the middle term gives \((5x)(-3y) + (-7y)(2x) = -15xy - 14xy = -29xy\), confirming the missing factor is \(2x - 3y\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(6x^2 + 7xy - 20y^2 = (2x + 5y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(3x\), and divide \(-20y^2\) by \(5y\) to get \(-4y\). Verifying the middle term gives \((2x)(-4y) + (5y)(3x) = -8xy + 15xy = 7xy\), so the missing factor is \(3x - 4y\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(15x^2 - x - 28 = (3x + 4)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(15x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(5x\), and divide \(-28\) by \(4\) to get \(-7\). Verifying the middle term gives \((3x)(-7) + (4)(5x) = -21x + 20x = -x\), confirming the missing factor is \(5x - 7\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(14x^2 - 27x + 9 = (2x - 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(14x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(7x\), and divide \(9\) by \(-3\) to get \(-3\). Checking the middle term gives \((2x)(-3) + (-3)(7x) = -6x - 21x = -27x\), so the missing factor is \(7x - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(12x^2 - 5x - 2 = (3x - 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(12x^2\) by \(3x\) to obtain \(4x\), and divide \(-2\) by \(-2\) to obtain \(1\). Checking the middle term gives \((3x)(1) + (-2)(4x) = 3x - 8x = -5x\), so the missing factor is \(4x + 1\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^2 - x - 2 = (2x + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(3x\), and divide \(-2\) by \(1\) to get \(-2\). Checking the middle term gives \(2x(-2) + 1(3x) = -x\), so the missing factor is \(3x - 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(4x^2 + 8x + 3 = (2x + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(4x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(2x\), and divide \(3\) by \(1\) to get \(3\). Checking the middle term gives \(2x(3) + 1(2x) = 8x\), so the missing factor is \(2x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^2 - 7x + 2 = (3x - 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(6x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(2x\), and divide \(+2\) by \(-2\) to get \(-1\). Checking the middle term gives \(3x(-1) + (-2)(2x) = -7x\), confirming the missing factor is \(2x - 1\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^2 + 7x - 5 = (2x - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(3x\), and divide the constant term \(-5\) by \(-1\) to get \(+5\). Checking the outer and inner products gives \(2x(5) + (-1)(3x) = 7x\), which confirms the missing factor is \(3x + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(9x^2 + 9x - 4 = (3x - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(9x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(3x\), and divide \(-4\) by \(-1\) to get \(4\). Checking the middle term gives \(3x(4) + (-1)(3x) = 9x\), so the missing factor is \(3x + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^4 + x^2 - 12 = (2x^2 + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Treating this as a quadratic in \(x^2\), divide \(6x^4\) by \(2x^2\) to get \(3x^2\) and \(-12\) by \(3\) to get \(-4\). Checking the middle term gives \(2x^2(-4) + 3(3x^2) = x^2\), confirming the missing factor is \(3x^2 - 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(12x^2 - 29xy + 15y^2 = (4x - 3y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(12x^2\) by \(4x\) to obtain \(3x\), and divide \(15y^2\) by \(-3y\) to obtain \(-5y\). Checking the middle term gives \(4x(-5y) + (-3y)(3x) = -20xy - 9xy = -29xy\), confirming the missing factor is \(3x - 5y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(35x^2 - 22x - 24 = (5x - 6)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(35x^2\) by \(5x\) to get \(7x\), and divide \(-24\) by \(-6\) to get \(+4\). Checking the middle term gives \(5x(4) + (-6)(7x) = 20x - 42x = -22x\), confirming the missing factor is \(7x + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(-15x^2 + 11x + 12 = -(3x - 4)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(15x^2 - 11x - 12)\). Dividing \(15x^2\) by \(3x\) gives \(5x\), and dividing \(-12\) by \(-4\) gives \(+3\), so the missing factor is \(5x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(12x^3 + 2x^2 - 4x = 2x(2x - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Factoring out \(2x\) leaves \(6x^2 + x - 2\). Dividing \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) gives \(3x\) and dividing \(-2\) by \(-1\) gives \(+2\), so the missing factor is \(3x + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(10x^2 + 17x + 3 = (5x + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(10x^2\) by \(5x\) gives \(2x\), and dividing \(3\) by \(1\) gives \(3\). Checking the middle term, \((5x)(3) + (1)(2x) = 17x\), confirming the missing factor is \(2x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(8x^2 - 14x + 3 = (4x - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(8x^2\) by \(4x\) gives \(2x\), and dividing \(3\) by \(-1\) gives \(-3\). Checking the middle term, \((4x)(-3) + (-1)(2x) = -14x\), confirming the missing factor is \(2x - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(12x^2 + x - 6 = (4x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(12x^2\) by \(4x\) gives \(3x\), and dividing \(-6\) by \(3\) gives \(-2\). Checking the middle term, \((4x)(-2) + (3)(3x) = x\), confirming the missing factor is \(3x - 2\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(15x^2 - 7x - 2 = (3x - 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(15x^2\) by \(3x\) gives \(5x\), and dividing \(-2\) by \(-2\) gives \(+1\). Checking the middle term, \((3x)(1) + (-2)(5x) = -7x\), confirming the missing factor is \(5x + 1\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(6x^2 + 11x - 10 = (2x + 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the first term \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) gives \(3x\), and dividing \(-10\) by \(5\) gives \(-2\). Checking the middle term, \((2x)(-2) + (5)(3x) = 11x\), confirming the missing factor is \(3x - 2\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(24x^2 - 41x + 12 = (3x - 4)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(24x^2\) by \(3x\) yields \(8x\), and dividing \(12\) by \(-4\) yields \(-3\). Checking the middle term, \((3x)(-3) + (-4)(8x) = -9x - 32x = -41x\), so the missing factor is \(8x - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(24a^2 + 2ab - 15b^2 = (4a - 3b)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(24a^2\) by \(4a\) gives \(6a\), and dividing \(-15b^2\) by \(-3b\) gives \(+5b\). Checking the middle term, \((4a)(5b) + (-3b)(6a) = 20ab - 18ab = 2ab\), confirming the missing factor is \(6a + 5b\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(36x^2 - 5x - 24 = (4x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(36x^2\) by \(4x\) gives \(9x\), and dividing \(-24\) by \(3\) gives \(-8\). Checking the middle term, \((4x)(-8) + (3)(9x) = -32x + 27x = -5x\), so the missing factor is \(9x - 8\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(28x^2 - 27xy - 10y^2 = (7x + 2y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(28x^2\) by \(7x\) gives \(4x\), and dividing \(-10y^2\) by \(2y\) gives \(-5y\). Checking the middle term, \((7x)(-5y) + (2y)(4x) = -35xy + 8xy = -27xy\), confirming the missing factor is \(4x - 5y\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(15x^2 - 19xy + 6y^2 = (5x - 3y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(15x^2\) by \(5x\) gives \(3x\), and dividing \(6y^2\) by \(-3y\) gives \(-2y\). Checking the middle term, \((5x)(-2y) + (-3y)(3x) = -10xy - 9xy = -19xy\), so the missing factor is \(3x - 2y\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(2x^2 - 5x + 3 = (2x - 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(2x^2\) by \(2x\) gives \(x\), and dividing \(3\) by \(-3\) gives \(-1\). Checking the middle term gives \((2x)(-1) + (-3)(x) = -5x\), so the missing factor is \(x - 1\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(4x^2 + 12x + 9 = (2x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the first term \(4x^2\) by \(2x\) gives \(2x\), and dividing the last term \(9\) by \(3\) gives \(3\). Checking the middle term gives \(2x(3) + 3(2x) = 12x\), so the missing factor is \(2x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(2x^2 + 7x - 4 = (2x - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(2x^2\) by \(2x\) gives \(x\), and dividing \(-4\) by \(-1\) gives \(+4\). Checking the middle term gives \((2x)(4) + (-1)(x) = 7x\), so the missing factor is \(x + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(6x^4 + 7x^2 - 5 = (2x^2 - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(6x^4\) by \(2x^2\) gives \(3x^2\), and dividing \(-5\) by \(-1\) gives \(+5\). Checking the middle term gives \((2x^2)(5) + (-1)(3x^2) = 7x^2\), so the missing factor is \(3x^2 + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(6x^2 + 11xy - 10y^2 = (3x - 2y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(6x^2\) by \(3x\) gives \(2x\), and dividing \(-10y^2\) by \(-2y\) gives \(+5y\). Checking the middle term gives \((3x)(5y) + (-2y)(2x) = 15xy - 4xy = 11xy\), confirming the missing factor is \(2x + 5y\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(25x^2 - 30xy + 9y^2 = (5x - 3y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: The trinomial is a perfect square trinomial with first term \((5x)^2\) and last term \((3y)^2\). Since \((5x - 3y)(5x - 3y) = 25x^2 - 30xy + 9y^2\), the missing factor is \(5x - 3y\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(15x^2 - 34x + 15 = (5x - 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(15x^2\) by \(5x\) yields \(3x\), and dividing \(15\) by \(-3\) yields \(-5\). Checking the middle term gives \((5x)(-5) + (-3)(3x) = -25x - 9x = -34x\), so the missing factor is \(3x - 5\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(10x^2 + 11x - 6 = (5x - 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the leading term \(10x^2\) by \(5x\) to get \(2x\), and the constant \(-6\) by \(-2\) to get \(3\). Checking the middle term gives \((5x)(3) + (-2)(2x) = 11x\), so the missing factor is \(2x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(6x^2 - 11x + 4 = (3x - 4)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the leading term \(6x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(2x\), and the constant \(4\) by \(-4\) to get \(-1\). Checking the middle term gives \((3x)(-1) + (-4)(2x) = -11x\), so the missing factor is \(2x - 1\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(4x^2 - 4x - 3 = (2x + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the leading term \(4x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(2x\), and the constant \(-3\) by \(1\) to get \(-3\). Checking the middle term confirms \((2x)(-3) + (1)(2x) = -4x\), so the missing factor is \(2x - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(6x^2 + 7x + 2 = (2x + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the leading term \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(3x\), and the constant \(2\) by \(1\) to get \(2\). Checking the middle term gives \((2x)(2) + (1)(3x) = 7x\), so the missing factor is \(3x + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(24x^2 + 26x - 15 = (2x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the leading term \(24x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(12x\), and the constant \(-15\) by \(3\) to get \(-5\). Checking the middle term confirms \((2x)(-5) + (3)(12x) = 26x\), so the missing factor is \(12x - 5\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(20x^2 - 9x - 20 = (4x - 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the leading term \(20x^2\) by \(4x\) to get \(5x\), and the constant \(-20\) by \(-5\) to get \(4\). Checking the middle term confirms \((4x)(4) + (-5)(5x) = -9x\), so the missing factor is \(5x + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(15x^2 + 29xy - 14y^2 = (5x - 2y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(15x^2\) by \(5x\) to get \(3x\), and the last term \(-14y^2\) by \(-2y\) to get \(7y\). Checking the middle term confirms \((5x)(7y) + (-2y)(3x) = 29xy\), so the missing factor is \(3x + 7y\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(18x^2 - 33x + 14 = (3x - 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(18x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(6x\), and the constant \(14\) by \(-2\) to get \(-7\). Checking the middle term gives \((3x)(-7) + (-2)(6x) = -33x\), so the missing factor is \(6x - 7\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(12x^2 + 11xy - 15y^2 = (3x + 5y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(12x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(4x\), and the last term \(-15y^2\) by \(5y\) to get \(-3y\). Checking the middle term gives \((3x)(-3y) + (5y)(4x) = 11xy\), so the missing factor is \(4x - 3y\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(3x^2 - 7x - 6 = (x - 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the first term \(3x^2\) by \(x\) gives \(3x\), and dividing \(-6\) by \(-3\) gives \(2\). Checking the middle term gives \(2x - 9x = -7x\), so the missing factor is \(3x + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(2x^2 + 5x - 12 = (x + 4)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the first term \(2x^2\) by \(x\) gives \(2x\), and dividing \(-12\) by \(4\) gives \(-3\). Checking the middle term gives \(-3x + 8x = 5x\), so the missing factor is \(2x - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(2x^2 + 11x + 12 = (2x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the first term \(2x^2\) by \(2x\) gives \(x\), and dividing \(12\) by \(3\) gives \(4\). Checking the middle term gives \(8x + 3x = 11x\), so the missing factor is \(x + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(5x^2 + 13x - 6 = (x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the first term \(5x^2\) by \(x\) gives \(5x\), and dividing \(-6\) by \(3\) gives \(-2\). Checking the middle term gives \(-2x + 15x = 13x\), so the missing factor is \(5x - 2\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(6x^2 + 26x - 20 = 2(x + 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2\) to get \(2(3x^2 + 13x - 10)\). Dividing \(3x^2\) by \(x\) gives \(3x\) and \(-10\) by \(5\) gives \(-2\), so the missing factor is \(3x - 2\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(6x^2 - 11xy - 10y^2 = (2x - 5y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(3x\), and divide \(-10y^2\) by \(-5y\) to get \(2y\). Checking the outer and inner products gives \(4xy - 15xy = -11xy\), confirming the factor is \(3x + 2y\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(15x^2 - 34xy + 15y^2 = (3x - 5y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(15x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(5x\), and divide \(15y^2\) by \(-5y\) to get \(-3y\). Checking the middle term gives \(-9xy - 25xy = -34xy\), confirming the factor is \(5x - 3y\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(12x^2 - 23x - 24 = (3x - 8)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(12x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(4x\), and divide \(-24\) by \(-8\) to get \(3\). Checking the middle term, \((3x)(3) + (-8)(4x) = 9x - 32x = -23x\), which confirms the factor is \(4x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the following factoring: \(20x^2 + 31x - 9 = (4x - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(20x^2\) by \(4x\) to get \(5x\), and divide \(-9\) by \(-1\) to get \(9\). Checking the middle term, \((4x)(9) + (-1)(5x) = 36x - 5x = 31x\), which confirms the factor is \(5x + 9\).
Find two numbers whose product is \(3 \times 8 = 24\) and whose sum is \(14\), which are \(12\) and \(2\). Factor by grouping: \(3x^2 + 12x + 2x + 8 = 3x(x + 4) + 2(x + 4) = (3x + 2)(x + 4)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(2 \times 12 = 24\) and add to \(11\), which are \(8\) and \(3\). Grouping gives \(2x^2 + 8x + 3x + 12 = 2x(x + 4) + 3(x + 4) = (2x + 3)(x + 4)\).
Find two numbers whose product is \(2 \times 10 = 20\) and sum is \(9\), which are \(4\) and \(5\). Grouping gives \(2x^2 + 4x + 5x + 10 = 2x(x + 2) + 5(x + 2) = (2x + 5)(x + 2)\).
Find two numbers whose product is \(3 \times 6 = 18\) and sum is \(11\), which are \(9\) and \(2\). Rewrite as \(3x^2 + 9x + 2x + 6 = 3x(x + 3) + 2(x + 3) = (3x + 2)(x + 3)\).
Find two numbers whose product is \(5 \times 6 = 30\) and sum is \(13\), which are \(10\) and \(3\). Grouping gives \(5x^2 + 10x + 3x + 6 = 5x(x + 2) + 3(x + 2) = (5x + 3)(x + 2)\).

Find two factors of \(8 \times (-15) = -120\) that sum to \(-14\), which are \(-20\) and \(6\). Split the middle term to factor by grouping: \(8x^2 - 20xy + 6xy - 15y^2 = 4x(2x - 5y) + 3y(2x - 5y) = (2x - 5y)(4x + 3y)\).

Find two factors of \(6 \times (-20) = -120\) that add to \(-7\), which are \(-15\) and \(8\). Split the middle term and factor by grouping: \(6x^2 - 15x + 8x - 20 = 3x(2x - 5) + 4(2x - 5) = (2x - 5)(3x + 4)\).
Find two factors of \(15 \times (-16) = -240\) that add to \(-34\), which are \(-40\) and \(6\). Factor by grouping: \(15x^2 - 40x + 6x - 16 = 5x(3x - 8) + 2(3x - 8) = (3x - 8)(5x + 2)\).
Find two numbers whose product is \(12 \times 10 = 120\) and sum is \(-23\), which are \(-15\) and \(-8\). Grouping gives \(12x^2 - 15x - 8x + 10 = 3x(4x - 5) - 2(4x - 5) = (3x - 2)(4x - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4x^3 - 10x^2 + 24x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x\) to get \(-2x(2x^2 + 5x - 12)\). Then find two factors of \(2 \times (-12) = -24\) that add to \(5\) (\(8\) and \(-3\)) to factor the trinomial into \(-2x(2x - 3)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(5x^2 + 7x + 2\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(5 \times 2 = 10\) and add to \(7\), which are \(5\) and \(2\). Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping: \(5x^2 + 5x + 2x + 2 = 5x(x + 1) + 2(x + 1) = (5x + 2)(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(3x^2 + 7x + 2\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(3 \times 2 = 6\) and add to \(7\), which are \(6\) and \(1\). Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping: \(3x^2 + 6x + x + 2 = 3x(x + 2) + 1(x + 2) = (3x + 1)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(2x^2 + 9x + 4\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(2 \times 4 = 8\) and add to \(9\), which are \(8\) and \(1\). Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping: \(2x^2 + 8x + x + 4 = 2x(x + 4) + 1(x + 4) = (2x + 1)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(2x^2 + 7x + 3\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(2 \times 3 = 6\) and add to \(7\), which are \(6\) and \(1\). Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping: \(2x^2 + 6x + x + 3 = 2x(x + 3) + 1(x + 3) = (2x + 1)(x + 3)\).

Find two numbers that multiply to \(15 \times (-4) = -60\) and add to \(17\), which are \(20\) and \(-3\). Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping: \(15x^2 + 20x - 3x - 4 = 5x(3x + 4) - 1(3x + 4) = (5x - 1)(3x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(6x^2 + 7x - 5\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(6 \times (-5) = -30\) and add to \(7\), which are \(10\) and \(-3\). Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping: \(6x^2 + 10x - 3x - 5 = 2x(3x + 5) - 1(3x + 5) = (2x - 1)(3x + 5)\).

Find two numbers that multiply to \(8 \times 3 = 24\) and add to \(-14\), which are \(-12\) and \(-2\). Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping: \(8x^2 - 12x - 2x + 3 = 4x(2x - 3) - 1(2x - 3) = (4x - 1)(2x - 3)\).

Find two numbers that multiply to \(12 \times (-5) = -60\) and add to \(11\), which are \(15\) and \(-4\). Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping: \(12x^2 + 15x - 4x - 5 = 3x(4x + 5) - 1(4x + 5) = (3x - 1)(4x + 5)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(6 \times 3 = 18\) and add to \(11\), which are \(9\) and \(2\). Split \(11x\) into \(9x + 2x\) and factor by grouping to obtain \((2x + 3)(3x + 1)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(6 \times 5 = 30\) and add to \(13\), which are \(10\) and \(3\). Rewrite \(13x\) as \(10x + 3x\) and factor by grouping to get \((3x + 5)(2x + 1)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(12 \times 2 = 24\) and add to \(11\), which are \(8\) and \(3\). Rewrite \(11x\) as \(8x + 3x\) and factor by grouping to obtain \((3x + 2)(4x + 1)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(10 \times 6 = 60\) and add to \(19\), which are \(15\) and \(4\). Split \(19x\) into \(15x + 4x\) and factor by grouping to find \((2x + 3)(5x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-15x^2 + 17x + 4\)
qs.s: First factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(15x^2 - 17x - 4)\). Find two numbers that multiply to \(15 \times (-4) = -60\) and add to \(-17\), which are \(-20\) and \(3\), giving \(-(3x - 4)(5x + 1)\).

Find two numbers that multiply to \(18 \times 10 = 180\) and add to \(-27\), which are \(-15\) and \(-12\). Rewrite the middle term as \(-15x - 12x\) and factor by grouping to get \((6x - 5)(3x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12x^3 + 26x^2 - 10x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to obtain \(2x(6x^2 + 13x - 5)\). Then find two factors of \(6 \times (-5) = -30\) that add to \(13\) (\(15\) and \(-2\)) to factor the trinomial into \(2x(2x + 5)(3x - 1)\).

Find two numbers that multiply to \(8 \times 15 = 120\) and add to \(-22\), which are \(-12\) and \(-10\). Rewrite the middle term as \(-12xy - 10xy\) and factor by grouping to get \((2x - 3y)(4x - 5y)\).
Find two factors of \(6 \times 10 = 60\) that add to \(19\), which are \(15\) and \(4\). Rewrite the middle term as \(15a + 4a\) and factor by grouping to get \((2a + 5)(3a + 2)\).
Find two factors of \(10 \times (-6) = -60\) that add to \(11\), which are \(15\) and \(-4\). Rewrite the middle term as \(15m - 4m\) and factor by grouping to get \((2m + 3)(5m - 2)\).
Find two factors of \(12 \times 2 = 24\) that add to \(-11\), which are \(-8\) and \(-3\). Rewrite the middle term as \(-8y - 3y\) and factor by grouping to get \((3y - 2)(4y - 1)\).
Find two factors of \(8 \times (-9) = -72\) that add to \(-14\), which are \(-18\) and \(4\). Rewrite the middle term as \(-18z + 4z\) and factor by grouping to get \((2z + 1)(4z - 9)\).
Find two factors of \(6 \times 12 = 72\) that add to \(-17\), which are \(-9\) and \(-8\). Rewrite the middle term as \(-9x - 8x\) and factor by grouping to get \((2x - 3)(3x - 4)\).
Find two factors of \(24 \times 15 = 360\) that add to \(-38\), which are \(-20\) and \(-18\). Rewrite the middle term as \(-20y - 18y\) and factor by grouping to get \((4y - 3)(6y - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(15x^4 - 34x^3 + 15x^2\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(x^2\) to get \(x^2(15x^2 - 34x + 15)\). Then find two factors of \(15 \times 15 = 225\) that add to \(-34\) (\(-25\) and \(-9\)) to obtain \(x^2(3x - 5)(5x - 3)\).
Find two factors of \(12 \times (-14) = -168\) that sum to \(13\), which are \(21\) and \(-8\). Splitting the middle term gives \(12x^2 + 21xy - 8xy - 14y^2 = (3x - 2y)(4x + 7y)\).
Find two factors of \(20 \times (-21) = -420\) that add to \(23\), which are \(35\) and \(-12\). Rewrite the middle term as \(35x - 12x\) and factor by grouping to obtain \((4x + 7)(5x - 3)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(12 \times (-15) = -180\) and add to \(11\), which are \(20\) and \(-9\). Factor by grouping to obtain \((4y - 3)(3y + 5)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(15 \times 8 = 120\) and add to \(-26\), which are \(-20\) and \(-6\). Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping to get \((5x - 2)(3x - 4)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(18 \times (-12) = -216\) and add to \(19\), which are \(27\) and \(-8\). Rewriting the middle term and grouping yields \((9m - 4)(2m + 3)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(20 \times 12 = 240\) and add to \(-31\), which are \(-16\) and \(-15\). Factor by grouping \(20a^2 - 16a - 15a + 12\) to get \((4a - 3)(5a - 4)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(14 \times 12 = 168\) and add to \(-29\), which are \(-21\) and \(-8\). Grouping as \(14t^2 - 21t - 8t + 12\) gives \((7t - 4)(2t - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(30x^3y - 49x^2y^2 + 20xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(xy\) to obtain \(xy(30x^2 - 49xy + 20y^2)\). Then find two numbers multiplying to \(600\) and adding to \(-49\) (\(-25\) and \(-24\)) to factor the trinomial into \(xy(5x - 4y)(6x - 5y)\).
Find factors of \(36 \times 24 = 864\) that add to \(-59\), which are \(-32\) and \(-27\). Grouping as \((36x^2 - 32x) - (27x - 24)\) gives \((4x - 3)(9x - 8)\).
Find factors of \(24 \times (-12) = -288\) that add to \(-23\), which are \(-32\) and \(9\). Rewrite the middle term as \(-32xy + 9xy\) and factor by grouping to get \((8x + 3y)(3x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-18x^3 + 33x^2 + 30x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-3x\) to get \(-3x(6x^2 - 11x - 10)\). Then factor the remaining quadratic using factors \(-15\) and \(4\) of \(-60\) to obtain \(-3x(3x + 2)(2x - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(42x^4 - 65x^2 + 25\)
qs.s: Recognize this as a quadratic in \(x^2\) and find two factors of \(42 \times 25 = 1050\) that sum to \(-65\), which are \(-35\) and \(-30\). Factoring by grouping yields \((7x^2 - 5)(6x^2 - 5)\).
Find factors of \(3 \times 7 = 21\) that add to \(10\), which are \(3\) and \(7\). Factor by grouping to obtain \((3y + 7)(y + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(2x^2 + 5x + 3\)
qs.s: Find factors of \(2 \times 3 = 6\) that add to \(5\), which are \(2\) and \(3\). Rewrite \(5x\) as \(2x + 3x\) and factor by grouping to obtain \((2x + 3)(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(3x^2 - 8x + 4\)
qs.s: Find factors of \(3 \times 4 = 12\) that add to \(-8\), which are \(-6\) and \(-2\). Rewrite \(-8x\) as \(-6x - 2x\) and factor by grouping to get \((3x - 2)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(2m^2 - m - 6\)
qs.s: Find factors of \(2 \times (-6) = -12\) that add to \(-1\), which are \(-4\) and \(3\). Rewrite \(-m\) as \(-4m + 3m\) and factor by grouping to obtain \((2m + 3)(m - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(5t^2 - 9t - 2\)
qs.s: Find factors of \(5 \times (-2) = -10\) that add to \(-9\), which are \(-10\) and \(1\). Rewrite \(-9t\) as \(-10t + t\) and factor by grouping to get \((5t + 1)(t - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(12y^3 + 10y^2 - 12y\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2y\) to get \(2y(6y^2 + 5y - 6)\). Then factor \(6y^2 + 5y - 6\) using grouping with \(9\) and \(-4\) to obtain \(2y(3y - 2)(2y + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-15x^3 + 35x^2 + 30x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-5x\) to get \(-5x(3x^2 - 7x - 6)\). Then factor the trinomial using factors \(-9\) and \(2\) to obtain \(-5x(3x + 2)(x - 3)\).
Find factors of \(6 \times (-10) = -60\) that add to \(11\), which are \(15\) and \(-4\). Rewrite \(11x\) as \(15x - 4x\) and factor by grouping to obtain \((3x - 2)(2x + 5)\).
Find factors of \(12 \times 10 = 120\) that add to \(-23\), which are \(-15\) and \(-8\). Rewrite \(-23xy\) as \(-15xy - 8xy\) and factor by grouping to get \((3x - 2y)(4x - 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(8x^2 - 14xy - 15y^2\)
qs.s: Find factors of \(8 \times (-15) = -120\) that add to \(-14\), which are \(-20\) and \(6\). Rewrite the middle term as \(-20xy + 6xy\) and factor by grouping to obtain \((4x + 3y)(2x - 5y)\).
Find factors of \(ac = 8(15) = 120\) that add to \(-22\), which are \(-10\) and \(-12\). Factor by grouping: \(8m^2 - 10m - 12m + 15 = 2m(4m - 5) - 3(4m - 5) = (4m - 5)(2m - 3)\).
Find factors of \(ac = 21(-10) = -210\) that add to \(-29\), which are \(6\) and \(-35\). Grouping gives \(21k^2 + 6k - 35k - 10 = 3k(7k + 2) - 5(7k + 2) = (7k + 2)(3k - 5)\).
Find factors of \(ac = 12(-15) = -180\) that add to \(-11\), which are \(9\) and \(-20\). Rewrite the middle term as \(12x^2 + 9x - 20x - 15 = 3x(4x + 3) - 5(4x + 3) = (4x + 3)(3x - 5)\).
Find factors of \(ac = 18(10) = 180\) that add to \(-27\), which are \(-12\) and \(-15\). Grouping gives \(18w^2 - 12w - 15w + 10 = 6w(3w - 2) - 5(3w - 2) = (3w - 2)(6w - 5)\).
Find factors of \(ac = 15(-8) = -120\) that add to \(14\), which are \(20\) and \(-6\). Rewrite the expression as \(15y^2 + 20y - 6y - 8 = 5y(3y + 4) - 2(3y + 4) = (5y - 2)(3y + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(12x^3y + 22x^2y^2 - 70xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(2xy\) to get \(2xy(6x^2 + 11xy - 35y^2)\). Then factor the trinomial using factors of \(6(-35) = -210\) that add to \(11\) (\(21\) and \(-10\)) to get \(2xy(3x - 5y)(2x + 7y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-18y^4 + 33y^3 + 30y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the GCF \(-3y^2\) to get \(-3y^2(6y^2 - 11y - 10)\). Factoring \(6y^2 - 11y - 10\) by grouping with \(-15\) and \(4\) gives \(-3y^2(3y + 2)(2y - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-70p^3 + 68p^2 - 16p\)
qs.s: Factor out the GCF \(-2p\) to get \(-2p(35p^2 - 34p + 8)\). Since \((-20)(-14) = 280\) and \((-20) + (-14) = -34\), the trinomial factors into \((5p - 2)(7p - 4)\), giving \(-2p(5p - 2)(7p - 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(24a^2 - 38ab + 15b^2\)
qs.s: Find factors of \(24(15) = 360\) that sum to \(-38\), which are \(-20\) and \(-18\). Rewrite as \(24a^2 - 20ab - 18ab + 15b^2 = 4a(6a - 5b) - 3b(6a - 5b) = (4a - 3b)(6a - 5b)\).
Find two factors of \(5(-12) = -60\) that sum to \(-17\), which are \(-20\) and \(3\). Splitting the middle term gives \(5m(m - 4) + 3(m - 4) = (5m + 3)(m - 4)\).
Find factors of \(2(-27) = -54\) that add to \(-15\), which are \(-18\) and \(3\). Factoring by grouping yields \(2w(w - 9) + 3(w - 9) = (2w + 3)(w - 9)\).
Find two factors of \(3(-35) = -105\) that add to \(-16\), which are \(-21\) and \(5\). Grouping as \(3p(p - 7) + 5(p - 7)\) gives \((3p + 5)(p - 7)\).
Find two numbers whose product is \(2(-24) = -48\) and sum is \(-13\), which are \(-16\) and \(3\). Rewrite the middle term as \(-16x + 3x\) and factor by grouping to get \((2x + 3)(x - 8)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(3(-42) = -126\) and add to \(-11\), which are \(-18\) and \(7\). Grouping as \(3y(y - 6) + 7(y - 6)\) yields \((3y + 7)(y - 6)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^3 - 22x^2 - 42x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to obtain \(2x(2x^2 - 11x - 21)\). Then factor the trinomial using factors of \(2(-21) = -42\) that add to \(-11\), giving \(2x(2x + 3)(x - 7)\).
Find two factors of \(6(-18) = -108\) that add to \(-23\), which are \(-27\) and \(4\). Rewrite as \(6x^2 - 27x + 4x - 18 = 3x(2x - 9) + 2(2x - 9) = (3x + 2)(2x - 9)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-15y^3 + 35y^2 + 30y\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-5y\) to get \(-5y(3y^2 - 7y - 6)\). Then split the middle term using \(-9\) and \(2\) to obtain \(-5y(3y + 2)(y - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(6x^2 + x - 2\)
qs.s: Find factors of \(6(-2) = -12\) that add to \(1\), which are \(4\) and \(-3\). Splitting the middle term gives \(6x^2 + 4x - 3x - 2 = 2x(3x + 2) - 1(3x + 2) = (2x - 1)(3x + 2)\).
Find factors of \(4(-3) = -12\) that add to \(11\), which are \(12\) and \(-1\). Factoring by grouping yields \(4w(w + 3) - 1(w + 3) = (4w - 1)(w + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(7t^2 - t - 8\)
qs.s: Find factors of \(7(-8) = -56\) that sum to \(-1\), which are \(-8\) and \(7\). Grouping gives \(7t^2 + 7t - 8t - 8 = 7t(t + 1) - 8(t + 1) = (7t - 8)(t + 1)\).
Find factors of \(5(-3) = -15\) that add to \(-14\), which are \(-15\) and \(1\). Rewrite as \(5y^2 - 15y + y - 3 = 5y(y - 3) + 1(y - 3) = (5y + 1)(y - 3)\).
Find factors of \(3(8) = 24\) that add to \(10\), which are \(6\) and \(4\). Rewrite the middle term as \(6m + 4m\) to get \(3m(m + 2) + 4(m + 2) = (3m + 4)(m + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(12x^2 - 23xy + 10y^2\)
qs.s: Find factors of \(12(10) = 120\) that add to \(-23\), which are \(-15\) and \(-8\). Split the middle term to group: \(3x(4x - 5y) - 2y(4x - 5y) = (3x - 2y)(4x - 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-6x^3 + 7x^2 + 20x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-x\) to get \(-x(6x^2 - 7x - 20)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial using factors of \(-120\) that sum to \(-7\) (\(-15\) and \(8\)) yields \(-x(2x - 5)(3x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(10y^3 - 25y^2 - 60y\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(5y\) to obtain \(5y(2y^2 - 5y - 12)\). Then factor the quadratic using factors of \(-24\) that add to \(-5\), giving \(5y(2y + 3)(y - 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(6a^2b + 19ab^2 - 7b^3\)
qs.s: First factor out \(b\) to get \(b(6a^2 + 19ab - 7b^2)\). Then find factors of \(6(-7) = -42\) that add to \(19\) (\(21\) and \(-2\)), yielding \(b(2a + 7b)(3a - b)\).
Find factors of \(15(-21) = -315\) that add to \(26\), which are \(35\) and \(-9\). Group as \(5z(3z + 7) - 3(3z + 7) = (3z + 7)(5z - 3)\).

Find two numbers that multiply to \(12 \times (-14) = -168\) and add to \(-13\), which are \(-21\) and \(8\). Rewriting the middle term gives \(12k^2 - 21k + 8k - 14 = 3k(4k - 7) + 2(4k - 7) = (3k + 2)(4k - 7)\).

Find two numbers that multiply to \(10 \times (-15) = -150\) and add to \(-19\), which are \(-25\) and \(6\). Rewriting the middle term gives \(10y^2 - 25y + 6y - 15 = 5y(2y - 5) + 3(2y - 5) = (2y - 5)(5y + 3)\).

Find two numbers that multiply to \(20 \times (-6) = -120\) and add to \(-7\), which are \(-15\) and \(8\). Rewriting the middle term gives \(20m^2 - 15m + 8m - 6 = 5m(4m - 3) + 2(4m - 3) = (4m - 3)(5m + 2)\).

Find two numbers that multiply to \(8 \times (-15) = -120\) and add to \(-14\), which are \(-20\) and \(6\). Rewriting the middle term gives \(8t^2 - 20t + 6t - 15 = 4t(2t - 5) + 3(2t - 5) = (2t - 5)(4t + 3)\).

Find two numbers that multiply to \(20 \times 15 = 300\) and add to \(-37\), which are \(-25\) and \(-12\). Rewriting \(-37xy\) gives \(20x^2 - 25xy - 12xy + 15y^2 = 5x(4x - 5y) - 3y(4x - 5y) = (4x - 5y)(5x - 3y)\).

Find two numbers that multiply to \(15 \times (-24) = -360\) and add to \(-2\), which are \(-20\) and \(18\). Rewriting \(-2xy\) gives \(15x^2 - 20xy + 18xy - 24y^2 = 5x(3x - 4y) + 6y(3x - 4y) = (3x - 4y)(5x + 6y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-14t^2 - 13t + 12\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) first to obtain \(-(14t^2 + 13t - 12)\). Then find two factors of \(14 \times (-12) = -168\) that add to \(13\) (\(21\) and \(-8\)), yielding \(-(2t + 3)(7t - 4)\).

Find two numbers that multiply to \(24 \times (-35) = -840\) and add to \(-22\), which are \(-42\) and \(20\). Grouping terms gives \(24x^2 - 42x + 20x - 35 = 6x(4x - 7) + 5(4x - 7) = (4x - 7)(6x + 5)\).
Find factors of \(8(3) = 24\) that add to \(-14\), which are \(-12\) and \(-2\). Rewrite as \(8z^2 - 12z - 2z + 3\) and factor by grouping to get \((4z - 1)(2z - 3)\).
Find factors of \(4(-3) = -12\) that add to \(-11\), which are \(-12\) and \(1\). Rewrite the middle term as \(-12y + y\) and factor by grouping to obtain \((4y + 1)(y - 3)\).
Find factors of \(5(-6) = -30\) that add to \(-13\), which are \(-15\) and \(2\). Rewrite as \(5t^2 - 15t + 2t - 6\) and factor by grouping to get \((5t + 2)(t - 3)\).
Find factors of \(3(8) = 24\) that add to \(14\), which are \(12\) and \(2\). Factor by grouping \(3m^2 + 12m + 2m + 8\) to obtain \((3m + 2)(m + 4)\).
Find two factors of \(20(6) = 120\) that add to \(-23\), which are \(-15\) and \(-8\). Rewrite the middle term as \(-15ab - 8ab\) and factor by grouping to get \((4a - 3b)(5a - 2b)\).
Find factors of \(12(-5) = -60\) that sum to \(11\), which are \(15\) and \(-4\). Rewrite the middle term as \(15xy - 4xy\) and factor by grouping to obtain \((4x + 5y)(3x - y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-18y^3 + 15y^2 + 12y\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3y\) to get \(-3y(6y^2 - 5y - 4)\). Factoring the trinomial yields \(-3y(3y - 4)(2y + 1)\).
Find factors of \(15(-10) = -150\) that add to \(-19\), which are \(-25\) and \(6\). Rewrite the expression as \(15x^2 - 25x + 6x - 10\) and factor by grouping to obtain \((5x + 2)(3x - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(6x^3 - 21x^2 - 45x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(3x\) to get \(3x(2x^2 - 7x - 15)\). Then factor the quadratic into \((2x + 3)(x - 5)\), resulting in \(3x(2x + 3)(x - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(4y^2 - 4y - 3\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(4(-3) = -12\) and add to \(-4\), which are \(-6\) and \(2\). Grouping gives \(4y^2 - 6y + 2y - 3 = 2y(2y - 3) + 1(2y - 3) = (2y + 1)(2y - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(2m^2 + 5m - 3\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(2(-3) = -6\) and add to \(5\), which are \(6\) and \(-1\). Rewrite and factor by grouping: \(2m^2 + 6m - m - 3 = 2m(m + 3) - 1(m + 3) = (2m - 1)(m + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(6t^2 + t - 2\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(6(-2) = -12\) and add to \(1\), which are \(4\) and \(-3\). Factoring by grouping gives \(6t^2 + 4t - 3t - 2 = 2t(3t + 2) - 1(3t + 2) = (2t - 1)(3t + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(6x^2 + 7x + 2\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(6 \cdot 2 = 12\) and add to \(7\), which are \(3\) and \(4\). Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping: \(6x^2 + 3x + 4x + 2 = 3x(2x + 1) + 2(2x + 1) = (2x + 1)(3x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(3p^2 - 7p + 2\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(3(2) = 6\) and add to \(-7\), which are \(-6\) and \(-1\). Grouping gives \(3p^2 - 6p - p + 2 = 3p(p - 2) - 1(p - 2) = (3p - 1)(p - 2)\).

Find two numbers that multiply to \(15(-8) = -120\) and add to \(14\), which are \(20\) and \(-6\). Rewrite and factor by grouping: \(15a^2 + 20a - 6a - 8 = 5a(3a + 4) - 2(3a + 4) = (5a - 2)(3a + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-6x^2 + 26x - 24\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-2\) to get \(-2(3x^2 - 13x + 12)\). Factoring the remaining trinomial gives \(-2(3x - 4)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(3b^2 + 8b + 4\)
qs.s: Find two factors of \(3 \times 4 = 12\) that add to \(8\), which are \(6\) and \(2\). Grouping gives \(3b^2 + 6b + 2b + 4 = 3b(b + 2) + 2(b + 2) = (3b + 2)(b + 2)\).
Find two factors of \(3 \times 8 = 24\) that add to \(-10\), which are \(-6\) and \(-4\). Grouping gives \(3y^2 - 6y - 4y + 8 = 3y(y - 2) - 4(y - 2) = (3y - 4)(y - 2)\).
Find two factors of \(5 \times (-3) = -15\) that add to \(-14\), which are \(-15\) and \(1\). Grouping gives \(5n^2 - 15n + n - 3 = 5n(n - 3) + 1(n - 3) = (5n + 1)(n - 3)\).
Find two factors of \(4 \times 15 = 60\) that add to \(-16\), which are \(-10\) and \(-6\). Rewrite as \(4w^2 - 10w - 6w + 15 = 2w(2w - 5) - 3(2w - 5) = (2w - 3)(2w - 5)\).
Find two factors of \(15 \times (-10) = -150\) that add to \(19\), which are \(25\) and \(-6\). Grouping gives \(15p^2 + 25p - 6p - 10 = 5p(3p + 5) - 2(3p + 5) = (5p - 2)(3p + 5)\).
Find two factors of \(12 \times 20 = 240\) that add to \(-31\), which are \(-16\) and \(-15\). Grouping gives \(12m^2 - 16m - 15m + 20 = 4m(3m - 4) - 5(3m - 4) = (4m - 5)(3m - 4)\).
Find two factors of \(6 \times 10 = 60\) that add to \(-19\), which are \(-15\) and \(-4\). Grouping gives \(6x^2 - 15xy - 4xy + 10y^2 = 3x(2x - 5y) - 2y(2x - 5y) = (3x - 2y)(2x - 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(8a^2 + 2ab - 15b^2\)
qs.s: Find two factors of \(8 \times (-15) = -120\) that add to \(2\), which are \(12\) and \(-10\). Grouping gives \(8a^2 + 12ab - 10ab - 15b^2 = 4a(2a + 3b) - 5b(2a + 3b) = (4a - 5b)(2a + 3b)\).
Find two factors of \(12 \times (-5) = -60\) that add to \(-17\), which are \(-20\) and \(3\). Grouping gives \(12x^2 - 20x + 3x - 5 = 4x(3x - 5) + 1(3x - 5) = (4x + 1)(3x - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(6x^2 + 7x - 3\)
qs.s: Find two factors of \(6 \times (-3) = -18\) that add to \(7\), which are \(9\) and \(-2\). Rewrite the middle term as \(9x - 2x\) and factor by grouping to get \((2x + 3)(3x - 1)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(4y^2 - 8y - 5\)
qs.s: Find two factors of \(4 \times (-5) = -20\) that add to \(-8\), which are \(-10\) and \(2\). Factor by grouping \(4y^2 - 10y + 2y - 5\) to obtain \((2y + 1)(2y - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(2k^2 - 9k + 9\)
qs.s: Find two factors of \(2 \times 9 = 18\) that add to \(-9\), which are \(-6\) and \(-3\). Factor by grouping \(2k^2 - 6k - 3k + 9\) to get \((2k - 3)(k - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12x^2 - 23x + 10\)
qs.s: Find two factors of \(12 \times 10 = 120\) that add to \(-23\), which are \(-15\) and \(-8\). Split the middle term and factor by grouping to get \((3x - 2)(4x - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(6x^3 + 15x^2 - 9x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(3x\) to get \(3x(2x^2 + 5x - 3)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial into \((2x - 1)(x + 3)\), giving \(3x(2x - 1)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-10x^2 - 11x + 6\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(10x^2 + 11x - 6)\). The factors of \(10 \times (-6) = -60\) that sum to \(11\) are \(15\) and \(-4\), so grouping yields \(-(2x + 3)(5x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4x^3 + 22x^2 - 24x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x\) to obtain \(-2x(2x^2 - 11x + 12)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial by finding factors of \(24\) that sum to \(-11\) (\(-8\) and \(-3\)), giving \(-2x(2x - 3)(x - 4)\).

exercises.name: Factor trinomial with negative leading coefficient

qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(3a^2 + 8a - 3)\). Factoring the quadratic inside yields \(-(3a - 1)(a + 3)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to write the expression as \(-(2y^2 + 7y + 3)\). Factoring the trinomial inside gives \(-(2y + 1)(y + 3)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(5x^2 - 7x - 6)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial to get \(-(5x + 3)(x - 2)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(3x^2 - 5x - 2)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial gives \(-(3x + 1)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(-2x^2 + x + 6\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(2x^2 - x - 6)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial into \((2x + 3)(x - 2)\) to obtain \(-(2x + 3)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-6x^2 - 11xy + 10y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(6x^2 + 11xy - 10y^2)\). Find two numbers that multiply to \(-60\) and add to \(11\), which are \(15\) and \(-4\), yielding \(-(3x - 2y)(2x + 5y)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(6x^2 - 7x - 20)\). Find two factors of \(6(-20) = -120\) that add to \(-7\), which are \(8\) and \(-15\), giving \(-(3x + 4)(2x - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(-2x^2 + 5xy - 3y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to rewrite the expression as \(-(2x^2 - 5xy + 3y^2)\). Factoring the quadratic inside gives \(-(2x - 3y)(x - y)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(-2x^2 + 3xy + 5y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(2x^2 - 3xy - 5y^2)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial gives \(-(2x - 5y)(x + y)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(-5m^2 - 7mn - 2n^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(5m^2 + 7mn + 2n^2)\). Factoring the trinomial produces \(-(5m + 2n)(m + n)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(-3a^2 - 5ab + 2b^2\)
qs.s: Factoring out a negative sign gives \(-(3a^2 + 5ab - 2b^2)\). Factoring this trinomial yields \(-(3a - b)(a + 2b)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(-3x^2 - 7xy - 2y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(3x^2 + 7xy + 2y^2)\). Then, factor the trinomial into binomials to obtain \(-(3x + y)(x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-18x^4y - 3x^3y^2 + 6x^2y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3x^2y\) to leave \(-3x^2y(6x^2 + xy - 2y^2)\). Then, factor the trinomial into \(-3x^2y(2x - y)(3x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-6x^2 - 7xy + 20y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(6x^2 + 7xy - 20y^2)\). Finding factors of \(6(-20) = -120\) that add to \(7\) gives \(15\) and \(-8\), which factors as \(-(2x + 5y)(3x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4x^3y + 14x^2y^2 - 12xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial \(-2xy\) to get \(-2xy(2x^2 - 7xy + 6y^2)\). Then, factoring the quadratic trinomial gives \(-2xy(2x - 3y)(x - 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-10a^2b - 25ab^2 + 60b^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-5b\) to obtain \(-5b(2a^2 + 5ab - 12b^2)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial yields \(-5b(2a - 3b)(a + 4b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-6x^3 - 9x^2y + 15xy^2\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-3x\) to get \(-3x(2x^2 + 3xy - 5y^2)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields \(-3x(2x + 5y)(x - y)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(4x^2 - 4x - 15)\), then find factors of \(4(-15) = -60\) that add to \(-4\), which are \(-10\) and \(6\). Factoring by grouping gives \(-(2x - 5)(2x + 3)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(3x^2 + 14x - 5)\), then find factors of \(3(-5) = -15\) that sum to \(14\), which are \(15\) and \(-1\). Grouping terms results in \(-(3x - 1)(x + 5)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(3x^2 - 7x - 20)\), then find two numbers that multiply to \(3(-20) = -60\) and add to \(-7\), which are \(-12\) and \(5\). Grouping terms yields \(-(3x + 5)(x - 4)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(2x^2 - 9x + 10)\), then find factors of \(2(10) = 20\) that add to \(-9\), which are \(-4\) and \(-5\). Factoring by grouping gives \(-(2x - 5)(x - 2)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(12x^2 - 11x - 15)\), then find factors of \(12(-15) = -180\) that add to \(-11\), which are \(-20\) and \(9\). Grouping terms yields \(-(4x + 3)(3x - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4x^4 - 6x^3 + 40x^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x^2\) to leave \(-2x^2(2x^2 + 3x - 20)\), then factor the trinomial using factors of \(-40\) that add to \(3\), giving \(-2x^2(2x - 5)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-6x^3 + 15x^2 + 36x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3x\) to get \(-3x(2x^2 - 5x - 12)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial by finding factors of \(-24\) that add to \(-5\), giving \(-3x(2x + 3)(x - 4)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(6x^2 + 7xy - 20y^2)\), then find factors of \(6(-20) = -120\) that add to \(7\), which are \(15\) and \(-8\). Factoring by grouping produces \(-(3x - 4y)(2x + 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^3y - 5x^2y^2 + 12xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial factor \(-xy\) to get \(-xy(2x^2 + 5xy - 12y^2)\), then factor the resulting trinomial into \(-xy(2x - 3y)(x + 4y)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(5x^2 + 13xy - 6y^2)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial yields \(-(5x - 2y)(x + 3y)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(2x^2 + 7xy - 15y^2)\). Then factor the quadratic expression to get \(-(2x - 3y)(x + 5y)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(4a^2 - 11ab + 6b^2)\). Factoring by grouping with middle terms \(-8ab\) and \(-3ab\) gives \(-(4a - 3b)(a - 2b)\).

qs.q: Factor. \(-3x^2 + 7xy + 6y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(3x^2 - 7xy - 6y^2)\). Then factor the trinomial into \(-(3x + 2y)(x - 3y)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(2x^2 - 11xy + 12y^2)\). Then find two factors of \(24\) that add to \(-11\), which gives \(-(2x - 3y)(x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-18x^4y + 21x^3y^2 + 15x^2y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3x^2y\) to get \(-3x^2y(6x^2 - 7xy - 5y^2)\). Then factor the trinomial to obtain \(-3x^2y(2x + y)(3x - 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-12x^2 - 11xy + 15y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(12x^2 + 11xy - 15y^2)\). Find factors of \((12)(-15) = -180\) that add to \(11\), which are \(20\) and \(-9\), giving \(-(4x - 3y)(3x + 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-6x^3y + 17x^2y^2 - 5xy^3\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common monomial factor \(-xy\) to get \(-xy(6x^2 - 17xy + 5y^2)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial to obtain \(-xy(3x - y)(2x - 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-4x^4 + 14x^3y + 18x^2y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial factor \(-2x^2\) to obtain \(-2x^2(2x^2 - 7xy - 9y^2)\). Factoring the remaining trinomial produces \(-2x^2(2x - 9y)(x + y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-10a^3b - 19a^2b^2 + 15ab^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-ab\) to yield \(-ab(10a^2 + 19ab - 15b^2)\). Factoring the trinomial with factors \(25\) and \(-6\) gives \(-ab(5a - 3b)(2a + 5b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-54x^2 + 108xy - 48y^2\)
qs.s: Factoring out the greatest common factor \(-6\) leaves \(-6(9x^2 - 18xy + 8y^2)\), which factors completely into \(-6(3x - 4y)(3x - 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-20a^2 + 38ab - 12b^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-2\) to get \(-2(10a^2 - 19ab + 6b^2)\), then factor the quadratic expression to obtain \(-2(2a - 3b)(5a - 2b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-24x^2 + 44xy + 40y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-4\) to obtain \(-4(6x^2 - 11xy - 10y^2)\), then factor the trinomial into \(-4(2x - 5y)(3x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-40x^2 + 70xy - 15y^2\)
qs.s: First factor out the common factor \(-5\) to obtain \(-5(8x^2 - 14xy + 3y^2)\). Factoring the remaining trinomial yields \(-5(2x - 3y)(4x - y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-18x^2 + 33xy - 12y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3\) to get \(-3(6x^2 - 11xy + 4y^2)\). Then factor the trinomial to obtain \(-3(2x - y)(3x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-60x^2y^2 + 93xy^3 - 36y^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-3y^2\) to obtain \(-3y^2(20x^2 - 31xy + 12y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial inside gives \(-3y^2(4x - 3y)(5x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-36x^3y + 42x^2y^2 + 120xy^3\)
qs.s: First factor out the common monomial factor \(-6xy\) to get \(-6xy(6x^2 - 7xy - 20y^2)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial gives \(-6xy(2x - 5y)(3x + 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-48x^4 + 68x^3y - 24x^2y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial factor \(-4x^2\) to obtain \(-4x^2(12x^2 - 17xy + 6y^2)\), then factor the trinomial to get \(-4x^2(3x - 2y)(4x - 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-40a^3b - 90a^2b^2 + 175ab^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common monomial factor \(-5ab\) to obtain \(-5ab(8a^2 + 18ab - 35b^2)\), then factor the trinomial into \(-5ab(2a + 7b)(4a - 5b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-30x^4 + 52x^2y^2 - 16y^4\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-2\) to get \(-2(15x^4 - 26x^2y^2 + 8y^4)\), then treat the expression as quadratic in \(x^2\) and \(y^2\) to factor it as \(-2(3x^2 - 4y^2)(5x^2 - 2y^2)\).
Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3\) to get \(-3(9x^2 + 24xy + 16y^2)\), then factor the perfect square trinomial as \(-3(3x + 4y)^2\).
Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2\) to get \(-2(25x^2 + 30xy + 9y^2)\), then factor the perfect square trinomial as \(-2(5x + 3y)^2\).
Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2\) to get \(-2(16a^2 - 24ab + 9b^2)\), then factor the perfect square trinomial as \(-2(4a - 3b)^2\).
Factor out the greatest common factor \(-6\) to get \(-6(4p^2 - 12pq + 9q^2)\), then factor the perfect square trinomial as \(-6(2p - 3q)^2\).
Factor out the greatest common factor \(-7\) to get \(-7(4m^2 + 12mn + 9n^2)\), then factor the perfect square trinomial as \(-7(2m + 3n)^2\).
Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2ab\) to get \(-2ab(6a^2 + 13ab - 5b^2)\), then factor the quadratic expression to get \(-2ab(2a + 5b)(3a - b)\).
Factor out the common monomial factor \(-2x\) to obtain \(-2x(9x^4 - 30x^2y^2 + 25y^4)\), which is quadratic in form and factors into \(-2x(3x^2 - 5y^2)^2\).
Factor out the common monomial factor \(-2x^2y^2\) to obtain \(-2x^2y^2(16x^2 - 40xy + 25y^2)\), then factor the perfect square trinomial as \(-2x^2y^2(4x - 5y)^2\).
Factor out the greatest common monomial factor \(-3x\) to get \(-3x(6x^2 - 7xy - 5y^2)\), then factor the trinomial by grouping to obtain \(-3x(3x - 5y)(2x + y)\).
Factor out the greatest common monomial factor \(-3xy\) to get \(-3xy(25x^2 + 40xy + 16y^2)\), then factor the perfect square trinomial to obtain \(-3xy(5x + 4y)^2\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(10x^2 + 19x + 6)\). Finding factors of \(10 \times 6 = 60\) that sum to \(19\) gives \(15\) and \(4\), yielding \(-(2x + 3)(5x + 2)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(6x^2 + 7x + 2)\). Finding factors of \(6 \times 2 = 12\) that add to \(7\) gives \(3\) and \(4\), which factors into \(-(2x + 1)(3x + 2)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(8x^2 - 14x + 3)\). Factors of \(8 \times 3 = 24\) that sum to \(-14\) are \(-12\) and \(-2\), leading to \(-(2x - 3)(4x - 1)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(12x^2 - 11x + 2)\). Finding factors of \(12 \times 2 = 24\) that sum to \(-11\) gives \(-3\) and \(-8\), yielding \(-(3x - 2)(4x - 1)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to rewrite the expression as \(-(15x^2 + x - 2)\). Factors of \(15 \times (-2) = -30\) that add to \(1\) are \(6\) and \(-5\), giving \(-(3x - 1)(5x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-10x^4 + 19x^3 - 6x^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-x^2\) to get \(-x^2(10x^2 - 19x + 6)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial produces \(-x^2(2x - 3)(5x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-20x^3y + 34x^2y^2 - 12xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2xy\) to get \(-2xy(10x^2 - 17xy + 6y^2)\). Factoring the remaining trinomial produces \(-2xy(2x - y)(5x - 6y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-18x^2y + 15xy^2 + 12y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3y\) to obtain \(-3y(6x^2 - 5xy - 4y^2)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields \(-3y(2x + y)(3x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-24x^2 - 2x + 15\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(24x^2 + 2x - 15)\). Finding factors of \(24 \times (-15) = -360\) that add to \(2\) gives \(20\) and \(-18\), leading to \(-(4x - 3)(6x + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-12x^3 - 26x^2 - 10x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x\) to get \(-2x(6x^2 + 13x + 5)\). Factoring the trinomial in parentheses results in \(-2x(2x + 1)(3x + 5)\).
First factor out the greatest common factor, \(-5\), to get \(-5(2x^2 + xy - 6y^2)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial into \(-5(2x - 3y)(x + 2y)\).
Factor out the common factor of \(-2\) to obtain \(-2(2a^2 - 11ab + 12b^2)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial yields \(-2(2a - 3b)(a - 4b)\).
First factor out \(-2\) to get \(-2(3u^2 - 13uv + 10v^2)\). Then factor the trinomial to obtain \(-2(3u - 10v)(u - v)\).
Factor out the greatest common factor, \(-4\), yielding \(-4(3x^2 + 2xy - 5y^2)\). Factoring the quadratic expression gives \(-4(3x + 5y)(x - y)\).
Factor out the common factor of \(-3\) to get \(-3(5x^2 + 6xy - 8y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial yields \(-3(5x - 4y)(x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-18x^2 + 69xy - 60y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-3\) to get \(-3(6x^2 - 23xy + 20y^2)\). Finding two numbers that multiply to \(120\) and add to \(-23\) (\(-15\) and \(-8\)) allows factoring the trinomial into \(-3(3x - 4y)(2x - 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-12x^3y + 6x^2y^2 + 90xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor, \(-6xy\), to obtain \(-6xy(2x^2 - xy - 15y^2)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial gives \(-6xy(2x + 5y)(x - 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-24a^2 - 44ab + 40b^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-4\) to obtain \(-4(6a^2 + 11ab - 10b^2)\). Factoring the trinomial by grouping produces \(-4(3a - 2b)(2a + 5b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-10x^4y^2 - 35x^3y^3 + 20x^2y^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the monomial common factor \(-5x^2y^2\) to get \(-5x^2y^2(2x^2 + 7xy - 4y^2)\). Factoring the remaining trinomial gives \(-5x^2y^2(2x - y)(x + 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-24x^3 + 42x^2y + 90xy^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-6x\) to leave \(-6x(4x^2 - 7xy - 15y^2)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial yields \(-6x(4x + 5y)(x - 3y)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(14x^2 - 27xy + 9y^2)\). The factors of \(14 \times 9 = 126\) that sum to \(-27\) are \(-21\) and \(-6\), so the expression factors as \(-(2x - 3y)(7x - 3y)\).
Factoring out \(-1\) gives \(-(12x^2 - 25xy + 12y^2)\). Since \((-16)(-9) = 144\) and \(-16 + (-9) = -25\), the trinomial factors as \(-(3x - 4y)(4x - 3y)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(6x^2 - 17xy + 12y^2)\). Find two numbers that multiply to \(6 \times 12 = 72\) and add to \(-17\), which are \(-9\) and \(-8\), giving \(-(2x - 3y)(3x - 4y)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to rewrite the expression as \(-(10x^2 + 11xy - 6y^2)\). Two numbers that multiply to \(-60\) and add to \(11\) are \(15\) and \(-4\), yielding \(-(2x + 3y)(5x - 2y)\).
Factoring out \(-1\) yields \(-(8x^2 + 14xy - 15y^2)\). Finding factors of \(-120\) that add to \(14\) gives \(20\) and \(-6\), which factors to \(-(2x + 5y)(4x - 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-20a^3b + 14a^2b^2 + 24ab^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial factor \(-2ab\) to get \(-2ab(10a^2 - 7ab - 12b^2)\). Factoring the trinomial by grouping with \(-15\) and \(8\) gives \(-2ab(2a - 3b)(5a + 4b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-6x^3y + 26x^2y^2 - 24xy^3\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-2xy\) to get \(-2xy(3x^2 - 13xy + 12y^2)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial using factors of \(36\) that sum to \(-13\) (\(-9\) and \(-4\)), giving \(-2xy(x - 3y)(3x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-18x^2 + 33xy + 40y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(18x^2 - 33xy - 40y^2)\). Find two numbers whose product is \(18 \times (-40) = -720\) and whose sum is \(-33\), which are \(-48\) and \(15\), yielding \(-(3x - 8y)(6x + 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-12x^4 - 6x^3y + 90x^2y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial factor \(-6x^2\) to obtain \(-6x^2(2x^2 + xy - 15y^2)\). Then factor the remaining trinomial by finding factors of \(-30\) that sum to \(1\) (\(6\) and \(-5\)), resulting in \(-6x^2(x + 3y)(2x - 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-30x^4y + 55x^3y^2 + 50x^2y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common monomial factor \(-5x^2y\) to get \(-5x^2y(6x^2 - 11xy - 10y^2)\). Factor the trinomial inside the parentheses using factors of \(-60\) that sum to \(-11\) (\(-15\) and \(4\)), which gives \(-5x^2y(2x - 5y)(3x + 2y)\).
Factor out the common factor \(-3\) to get \(-3(6t^4 - 7t^2 - 5)\). Factoring the quadratic expression in \(t^2\) yields \(-3(3t^2 - 5)(2t^2 + 1)\).
Factor out \(-5\) to obtain \(-5(6a^4 + 11a^2 - 10)\). Factoring the quadratic expression in \(a^2\) with factors \(15\) and \(-4\) gives \(-5(2a^2 + 5)(3a^2 - 2)\).

First factor out \(-2\) to get \(-2(12y^4 - 17y^2 + 6)\). Then factor the trinomial in \(y^2\) using the factors of \(12 \times 6 = 72\) that sum to \(-17\) (\(-9\) and \(-8\)), which yields \(-2(4y^2 - 3)(3y^2 - 2)\).
Factor out \(-4\) to obtain \(-4(6m^4 + 7m^2 - 5)\). Factoring the trinomial inside gives \(-4(2m^2 - 1)(3m^2 + 5)\).
First factor out the greatest common factor \(-3\) to get \(-3(10x^4 - 11x^2 - 6)\). Then factor the trinomial in \(x^2\) into \((2x^2 - 3)(5x^2 + 2)\), giving \(-3(2x^2 - 3)(5x^2 + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-54x^4 - 111x^2 + 60\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-3\) to get \(-3(18x^4 + 37x^2 - 20) = -3(2x^2 + 5)(9x^2 - 4)\). Factoring the difference of squares \(9x^2 - 4\) yields \(-3(2x^2 + 5)(3x - 2)(3x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-8x^4 + 74x^2 - 18\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-2\) to get \(-2(4x^4 - 37x^2 + 9) = -2(4x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 9)\). Then factor both differences of squares to obtain \(-2(2x - 1)(2x + 1)(x - 3)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-12x^6 + 28x^4 y^2 + 80x^2 y^4\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-4x^2\) to get \(-4x^2(3x^4 - 7x^2 y^2 - 20y^4) = -4x^2(x^2 - 4y^2)(3x^2 + 5y^2)\). Finally, factor the difference of squares \(x^2 - 4y^2\) to get \(-4x^2(x - 2y)(x + 2y)(3x^2 + 5y^2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-6x^5 + 46x^3 + 72x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common monomial factor \(-2x\) to get \(-2x(3x^4 - 23x^2 - 36) = -2x(x^2 - 9)(3x^2 + 4)\). Finally, factor the difference of squares \(x^2 - 9\) into \((x - 3)(x + 3)\), giving \(-2x(x - 3)(x + 3)(3x^2 + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(-30x^5 y - 25x^3 y^3 + 30x y^5\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-5xy\) to obtain \(-5xy(6x^4 + 5x^2 y^2 - 6y^4)\). Then factor the two-variable quadratic form to get \(-5xy(2x^2 + 3y^2)(3x^2 - 2y^2)\).

exercises.name: Factor polynomial with common binomial factor

qs.q: Factor completely: \(6x^2(y + 2)^2 + 7x(y + 2)^2 - 3(y + 2)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial factor \((y + 2)^2\) to get \((y + 2)^2(6x^2 + 7x - 3)\), then factor the quadratic trinomial into \((2x + 3)(3x - 1)\).
Factor out \((w - 5)^3\) to get \((w - 5)^3(15z^2 + 11z - 12)\), then factor the quadratic as \((3z + 4)(5z - 3)\).
Factor out the common factor \((2b + 1)^4\) to get \((2b + 1)^4(10a^2 - 19a + 6)\), then factor the quadratic trinomial into \((2a - 3)(5a - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12y^2(x - 3)^3 - 5y(x - 3)^3 - 2(x - 3)^3\)
qs.s: Factor out \((x - 3)^3\) to obtain \((x - 3)^3(12y^2 - 5y - 2)\), then factor the trinomial into \((3y - 2)(4y + 1)\).
Factor out \((p - 4)^3\) to leave \((p - 4)^3(8m^2 + 14m - 15)\), which factors into \((p - 4)^3(2m + 5)(4m - 3)\).
Factor out \((y - 3)^3\) to get \((y - 3)^3[2(x + 1)^2 + 7(x + 1) - 15]\), factor the quadratic in \((x + 1)\) into \([2(x + 1) - 3][(x + 1) + 5]\), and simplify to \((y - 3)^3(2x - 1)(x + 6)\).
Factor out the GCF \(-2x(2a + 3)^3\) to get \(-2x(2a + 3)^3(12x^2 - 11x - 15)\), then factor the resulting quadratic into \((3x - 5)(4x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(6x^2(a - 2b)^2 - 17xy(a - 2b)^2 + 12y^2(a - 2b)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \((a - 2b)^2\) to obtain \((a - 2b)^2(6x^2 - 17xy + 12y^2)\), then factor the two-variable quadratic trinomial into \((2x - 3y)(3x - 4y)\).
Factor out \(-(m + 5)^2\) to obtain \(-(m + 5)^2(3x^2 - 11x + 6)\). Factoring \(3x^2 - 11x + 6\) results in \(-(3x - 2)(x - 3)(m + 5)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4x^2(p - 2)^2 - 4x(p - 2)^2 + 3(p - 2)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-(p - 2)^2\) to obtain \(-(p - 2)^2(4x^2 + 4x - 3)\). Factoring the remaining trinomial gives \(-(2x - 1)(2x + 3)(p - 2)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^2(a - 1)^2 + 5x(a - 1)^2 + 3(a - 1)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-(a - 1)^2\) to get \(-(a - 1)^2(2x^2 - 5x - 3)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields \(-(2x + 1)(x - 3)(a - 1)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-5x^2(z + 3)^2 - 7x(z + 3)^2 + 6(z + 3)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-(z + 3)^2\) to obtain \(-(z + 3)^2(5x^2 + 7x - 6)\). Factoring the remaining trinomial gives \(-(5x - 3)(x + 2)(z + 3)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2y^2(x - 4)^2 - 9y(x - 4)^2 - 4(x - 4)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-(x - 4)^2\) to get \(-(x - 4)^2(2y^2 + 9y + 4)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial gives \(-(2y + 1)(y + 4)(x - 4)^2\).

Factor out \(-(y + 3)^2\) to get \(-(y + 3)^2(2x^4 - 7x^2 - 4)\). Factoring as a quadratic in \(x^2\) gives \(-(y + 3)^2(2x^2 + 1)(x^2 - 4)\), and factoring the difference of squares gives \(-(2x^2 + 1)(x - 2)(x + 2)(y + 3)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4x^3(y - 2)^2 + 14x^2 z(y - 2)^2 + 8xz^2(y - 2)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x(y - 2)^2\) to obtain \(-2x(y - 2)^2(2x^2 - 7xz - 4z^2)\). Factoring the two-variable trinomial gives \(-2x(2x + z)(x - 4z)(y - 2)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-6x^2(a - 2b)^2 - 13xy(a - 2b)^2 + 5y^2(a - 2b)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-(a - 2b)^2\) to obtain \(-(a - 2b)^2(6x^2 + 13xy - 5y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial into \((3x - y)(2x + 5y)\) results in \(-(3x - y)(2x + 5y)(a - 2b)^2\).
Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3x(a + 1)^2\) to get \(-3x(a + 1)^2(2x^2 + 5x - 3)\). Factoring \(2x^2 + 5x - 3\) gives \((2x - 1)(x + 3)\), resulting in \(-3x(2x - 1)(x + 3)(a + 1)^2\).
Factor out \(-(2y - 1)^2\) to get \(-(2y - 1)^2(12x^2 + 7x - 10)\). Using the ac-method on \(12x^2 + 7x - 10\) yields factors \(15\) and \(-8\), giving \(-(4x + 5)(3x - 2)(2y - 1)^2\).

qs.q: Factor. \(1 + x - 72x^2\)
qs.s: Find two integers that multiply to \(-72\) and add to \(1\), which are \(9\) and \(-8\). Thus, \(1 + x - 72x^2 = (1 + 9x)(1 - 8x)\).
Find two integers that multiply to \(-60\) and add to \(-11\), which are \(-15\) and \(4\). Thus, \(1 - 11x - 60x^2 = (1 - 15x)(1 + 4x)\).
Find two integers that multiply to \(-36\) and add to \(-5\), which are \(-9\) and \(4\). Thus, \(1 - 5x - 36x^2 = (1 - 9x)(1 + 4x)\).
Find two integers that multiply to \(-48\) and add to \(-2\), which are \(-8\) and \(6\). Thus, \(1 - 2x - 48x^2 = (1 - 8x)(1 + 6x)\).
Find two integers that multiply to \(-45\) and add to \(4\), which are \(9\) and \(-5\). Thus, \(1 + 4x - 45x^2 = (1 + 9x)(1 - 5x)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(6 - 7x - 20x^2\)
qs.s: Find two numbers whose product is \(6 \times (-20) = -120\) and whose sum is \(-7\), which are \(-15\) and \(8\). Rewrite and factor by grouping: \(6 - 15x + 8x - 20x^2 = 3(2 - 5x) + 4x(2 - 5x) = (2 - 5x)(3 + 4x)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \(4 - 11x - 45x^2\)
qs.s: Find two numbers with product \(4 \times (-45) = -180\) and sum \(-11\), which are \(-20\) and \(9\). Rewrite as \(4 - 20x + 9x - 45x^2 = 4(1 - 5x) + 9x(1 - 5x) = (1 - 5x)(4 + 9x)\).

qs.q: Factor completely. \((y + 3) - 5x(y + 3) - 36x^2(y + 3)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial factor \((y + 3)\) to get \((y + 3)(1 - 5x - 36x^2)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial to obtain \((y + 3)(1 - 9x)(1 + 4x)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 - 20x^2 + 64\)
qs.s: Substituting \(u = x^2\) gives \(u^2 - 20u + 64 = (u - 4)(u - 16) = (x^2 - 4)(x^2 - 16)\). Factoring both differences of squares completely yields \((x - 2)(x + 2)(x - 4)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 - 13x^2 + 36\)
qs.s: Using the substitution \(u = x^2\), factor \(u^2 - 13u + 36\) into \((u - 4)(u - 9) = (x^2 - 4)(x^2 - 9)\). Applying the difference of squares to each binomial gives \((x - 2)(x + 2)(x - 3)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 - 5x^2 + 4\)
qs.s: Let \(u = x^2\) to rewrite the polynomial as \(u^2 - 5u + 4 = (u - 1)(u - 4) = (x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 4)\). Factoring both differences of squares gives \((x - 1)(x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(25 - 26x^2 + x^4\)
qs.s: Setting \(u = x^2\), the polynomial factors as \((u - 1)(u - 25) = (x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 25)\). Factoring each difference of squares completely results in \((x - 1)(x + 1)(x - 5)(x + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(16 - 17x^2 + x^4\)
qs.s: Rewriting in quadratic form with \(u = x^2\) gives \(u^2 - 17u + 16 = (u - 1)(u - 16) = (x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 16)\). Factoring each binomial as a difference of squares yields \((x - 1)(x + 1)(x - 4)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 - 29x^2y^2 + 100y^4\)
qs.s: Factor the two-variable quadratic form into \((x^2 - 4y^2)(x^2 - 25y^2)\). Each factor is a difference of squares, which factors completely into \((x - 2y)(x + 2y)(x - 5y)(x + 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(1 - 13x^2 + 36x^4\)
qs.s: Write the polynomial as \(36x^4 - 13x^2 + 1\) and factor the quadratic form into \((4x^2 - 1)(9x^2 - 1)\). Factoring both differences of squares gives \((2x - 1)(2x + 1)(3x - 1)(3x + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^4 - 17x^2 + 4\)
qs.s: Let \(u = x^2\) to factor \(4u^2 - 17u + 4\) as \((4u - 1)(u - 4) = (4x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 4)\). Factoring each difference of squares completely produces \((2x - 1)(2x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^5 + 50x^3 - 288x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x\) to obtain \(-2x(x^4 - 25x^2 + 144) = -2x(x^2 - 9)(x^2 - 16)\). Factoring each difference of squares completely gives \(-2x(x - 3)(x + 3)(x - 4)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(9x^4 - 40x^2 + 16\)
qs.s: Let \(u = x^2\) to factor \(9u^2 - 40u + 16\) into \((9u - 4)(u - 4) = (9x^2 - 4)(x^2 - 4)\). Factoring each difference of squares completely yields \((3x - 2)(3x + 2)(x - 2)(x + 2)\).
Factor out \((y + 5)^2\) to obtain \((y + 5)^2(15x^2 + 14x - 8)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial gives \((y + 5)^2(5x - 2)(3x + 4)\).
Factor out the common binomial factor \((x - 3)^2\) to obtain \((x - 3)^2(10y^2 - 11y - 6)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial into \((5y + 2)(2y - 3)\) to get \((x - 3)^2(5y + 2)(2y - 3)\).
Factor out \((w - 1)^2\) to get \((w - 1)^2(12u^2 - 17u + 6)\). Then factor the trinomial into \((3u - 2)(4u - 3)\), yielding \((w - 1)^2(3u - 2)(4u - 3)\).
Factor out \((k - 4)^2\) to leave \((k - 4)^2(8t^2 + 22t + 15)\). Factoring the remaining quadratic trinomial produces \((k - 4)^2(4t + 5)(2t + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(6m^2(z + 2)^2 + 7m(z + 2)^2 - 5(z + 2)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \((z + 2)^2\) to get \((z + 2)^2(6m^2 + 7m - 5)\). Factoring the trinomial yields \((z + 2)^2(2m - 1)(3m + 5)\).

Factor out the common factor \((2x - 1)^2\) to get \((2x - 1)^2(24y^2 - 46y + 15)\). With \(ac = 360 = (-36)(-10)\), the trinomial factors as \((12y - 5)(2y - 3)\), giving \((2x - 1)^2(12y - 5)(2y - 3)\).

Factor out \((x - 5)^2\) to obtain \((x - 5)^2(4y^4 - 37y^2 + 9)\), which factors in quadratic form into \((x - 5)^2(4y^2 - 1)(y^2 - 9)\). Factoring both differences of squares completely yields \((x - 5)^2(2y - 1)(2y + 1)(y - 3)(y + 3)\).

Factor out \((3w + 2)^2\) to obtain \((3w + 2)^2(20y^2 - 47y + 24)\). Using factors of \(ac = 480\) that add to \(-47\) (\(-32\) and \(-15\)), factor the quadratic into \((4y - 3)(5y - 8)\), yielding \((3w + 2)^2(4y - 3)(5y - 8)\).
First factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x(a - 4)^2\) to obtain \(-2x(a - 4)^2(6x^2 - 13x - 5)\). Then factor the trinomial into \((3x + 1)(2x - 5)\) to get \(-2x(a - 4)^2(3x + 1)(2x - 5)\).
Factor out the greatest common factor \(2b(x + 2)^2\) to leave \(2b(x + 2)^2(10a^2 + 7ab - 6b^2)\). Factoring the remaining trinomial produces \(2b(x + 2)^2(2a - b)(5a + 6b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(6x^2(x + 3)^2 - 11xy(x + 3)^2 - 10y^2(x + 3)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial factor \((x + 3)^2\) to obtain \((x + 3)^2(6x^2 - 11xy - 10y^2)\). Factoring the remaining quadratic trinomial gives \((x + 3)^2(2x - 5y)(3x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(8u^2(u + 5)^2 - 22uv(u + 5)^2 + 15v^2(u + 5)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \((u + 5)^2\) to obtain \((u + 5)^2(8u^2 - 22uv + 15v^2)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields \((u + 5)^2(2u - 3v)(4u - 5v)\).
Factor out the common factor \((p - 4)^2\) to get \((p - 4)^2(10p^2 + 29pq - 21q^2)\). Factoring the trinomial results in \((p - 4)^2(2p + 7q)(5p - 3q)\).
Factor out \((m - 1)^2\) to get \((m - 1)^2(12m^2 + 11mn - 15n^2)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial into \((m - 1)^2(3m + 5n)(4m - 3n)\).
Factor out \((2x + 1)^2\) to get \((2x + 1)^2(14x^2 - 19xy - 3y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial produces \((2x + 1)^2(2x - 3y)(7x + y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(5y^2 - 40y + 80\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(5\) to get \(5(y^2 - 8y + 16)\), then factor the perfect square trinomial to obtain \(5(y - 4)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(7n^2 + 70n + 175\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(7\) to obtain \(7(n^2 + 10n + 25)\), then factor the perfect square trinomial to get \(7(n + 5)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3m^2 + 36m + 108\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(3\) to get \(3(m^2 + 12m + 36)\), then factor the perfect square trinomial to obtain \(3(m + 6)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4p^2 - 24p + 36\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(4\) to obtain \(4(p^2 - 6p + 9)\), then factor the perfect square trinomial to get \(4(p - 3)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^2 + 28x + 98\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(2\) to get \(2(x^2 + 14x + 49)\), then recognize \(x^2 + 14x + 49\) as a perfect square trinomial to obtain \(2(x + 7)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^3 + 24x^2 - 72x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x\) to obtain \(-2x(x^2 - 12x + 36)\), then factor the perfect square trinomial to get \(-2x(x - 6)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(50x^2y - 120xy^2 + 72y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2y\) to get \(2y(25x^2 - 60xy + 36y^2)\), then factor the perfect square trinomial to obtain \(2y(5x - 6y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-18y^5 - 48y^4 - 32y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2y^3\) to obtain \(-2y^3(9y^2 + 24y + 16)\), then factor the perfect square trinomial to get \(-2y^3(3y + 4)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12x^2 - 36x + 27\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3\) to get \(3(4x^2 - 12x + 9)\), then factor the non-monic perfect square trinomial to obtain \(3(2x - 3)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3a^3b + 30a^2b^2 + 75ab^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3ab\) to get \(3ab(a^2 + 10ab + 25b^2)\), then factor the multivariable perfect square trinomial to obtain \(3ab(a + 5b)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^3 + 12x^2 + 36x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(x\) to get \(x(x^2 + 12x + 36)\). Since \(x^2 + 12x + 36\) is a perfect square trinomial, it factors as \((x + 6)^2\), giving \(x(x + 6)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^3 - 10x^2 + 25x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(x\) to obtain \(x(x^2 - 10x + 25)\). Recognize \(x^2 - 10x + 25\) as \((x - 5)^2\), yielding \(x(x - 5)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(y^3 - 20y^2 + 100y\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(y\) to get \(y(y^2 - 20y + 100)\). Factoring the perfect square trinomial gives \(y(y - 10)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(m^3 + 14m^2 + 49m\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(m\) to get \(m(m^2 + 14m + 49)\). Then factor the perfect square trinomial to obtain \(m(m + 7)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^3 - 18a^2 + 81a\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(a\) to get \(a(a^2 - 18a + 81)\). The trinomial is a perfect square \((a - 9)^2\), so the complete factorization is \(a(a - 9)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3x^4 - 24x^3y + 48x^2y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3x^2\) to get \(3x^2(x^2 - 8xy + 16y^2)\). Since \(x^2 - 8xy + 16y^2 = (x - 4y)^2\), the complete factorization is \(3x^2(x - 4y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12x^3 - 36x^2 + 27x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(3x\) to obtain \(3x(4x^2 - 12x + 9)\). The trinomial is a perfect square \((2x - 3)^2\), giving \(3x(2x - 3)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-5a^3b - 30a^2b^2 - 45ab^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-5ab\) to obtain \(-5ab(a^2 + 6ab + 9b^2)\). The trinomial factors into the square of a binomial, \((a + 3b)^2\), resulting in \(-5ab(a + 3b)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(18x^5 + 60x^4 + 50x^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(2x^3\) to get \(2x^3(9x^2 + 30x + 25)\). Recognizing \(9x^2 + 30x + 25\) as \((3x + 5)^2\), the final result is \(2x^3(3x + 5)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^2 + 20xy + 25y^2\)
qs.s: The first term is \((2x)^2\), the last term is \((5y)^2\), and the middle term is \(2(2x)(5y) = 20xy\). Therefore, this factors as \((2x + 5y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(49u^2 + 28uv + 4v^2\)
qs.s: Since \(49u^2 = (7u)^2\), \(4v^2 = (2v)^2\), and the middle term is \(2(7u)(2v) = 28uv\), this trinomial factors as \((7u + 2v)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(16m^2 - 40mn + 25n^2\)
