qs.s: Factor \(-3x^2 - x + 4 = -(3x + 4)(x - 1) = 0\) to find x-intercepts at \(x = -\frac{4}{3}\) and \(x = 1\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{4}{3} + 1}{2} = -\frac{1}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(y = p(x) = 7x - 2x^2 + 15\).
qs.s: Rewrite in standard form and factor: \(-2x^2 + 7x + 15 = -(2x + 3)(x - 5) = 0\), giving x-intercepts \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = 5\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{3}{2} + 5}{2} = \frac{7}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(y = f(x) = 2x^2 - 5x - 12\).
qs.s: Set \(f(x) = 0\) and factor: \((2x + 3)(x - 4) = 0\), giving x-intercepts at \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = 4\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{3}{2} + 4}{2} = \frac{5}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 5x - 3\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \((2x + 1)(x - 3) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = 3\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{1}{2} + 3}{2} = \frac{5}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(g(x) = 3x^2 + 8x + 4\).
qs.s: Setting \(g(x) = 0\) gives \((3x + 2)(x + 2) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\) and \(x = -2\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{2}{3} + (-2)}{2} = -\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 3x - 5\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \((2x - 5)(x + 1) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = \frac{5}{2}\) and \(x = -1\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{\frac{5}{2} + (-1)}{2} = \frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(h(x) = 3x^2 - 2x - 8\).
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) gives \((3x + 4)(x - 2) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = -\frac{4}{3}\) and \(x = 2\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{4}{3} + 2}{2} = \frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(g(x) = 2x^2 + 7x + 3\).
qs.s: Setting \(g(x) = 0\) gives \((2x + 1)(x + 3) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = -3\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{1}{2} + (-3)}{2} = -\frac{7}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = (3x - 2)(2x + 1) - (x^2 + 6x + 4)\).
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying gives \(f(x) = 5x^2 - 7x - 6 = (5x + 3)(x - 2) = 0\), yielding x-intercepts \(x = -\frac{3}{5}\) and \(x = 2\). The axis of symmetry is their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{3}{5} + 2}{2} = \frac{7}{10}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(h(x) = 6x^2 - 17x + 12\).
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) and factoring gives \((3x - 4)(2x - 3) = 0\), giving x-intercepts \(x = \frac{4}{3}\) and \(x = \frac{3}{2}\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{\frac{4}{3} + \frac{3}{2}}{2} = \frac{17}{12}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 2(x - 2)^2 - x - 13\).
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying yields \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 9x - 5 = (2x + 1)(x - 5) = 0\), which gives x-intercepts \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = 5\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{1}{2} + 5}{2} = \frac{9}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(g(x) = 12x^2 - 20x + 3\).
qs.s: Setting \(g(x) = 0\) and factoring gives \((2x - 3)(6x - 1) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = \frac{1}{6}\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{\frac{3}{2} + \frac{1}{6}}{2} = \frac{5}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -6x^2 + 11x + 10\).
qs.s: Factoring \(-(6x^2 - 11x - 10) = 0\) gives \(-(3x + 2)(2x - 5) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\) and \(x = \frac{5}{2}\). The axis of symmetry is their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{2}{3} + \frac{5}{2}}{2} = \frac{11}{12}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 8x - x^2\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \(x(8 - x) = 0\), which yields \(x\)-intercepts at \(x = 0\) and \(x = 8\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{0 + 8}{2} = 4\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -x^2 - 4x\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \(-x(x + 4) = 0\), which yields \(x\)-intercepts at \(x = 0\) and \(x = -4\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{0 + (-4)}{2} = -2\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 - 6x\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \(x(x - 6) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(x = 0\) and \(x = 6\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{0 + 6}{2} = 3\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 16 - x^2\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \(16 - x^2 = 0\), so \((4 - x)(4 + x) = 0\), which yields \(x\)-intercepts at \(x = -4\) and \(x = 4\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-4 + 4}{2} = 0\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 + 10x\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \(x(x + 10) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(x = 0\) and \(x = -10\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{0 + (-10)}{2} = -5\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 - 4x - 21\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \((x - 7)(x + 3) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(x = 7\) and \(x = -3\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{7 + (-3)}{2} = 2\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 7x - 4\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \((2x + 1)(x - 4) = 0\), yielding \(x\)-intercepts at \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = 4\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{1}{2} + 4}{2} = \frac{7}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -3x^2 + 30x - 48\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(-3\) yields \(-3(x - 2)(x - 8) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(x = 2\) and \(x = 8\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{2 + 8}{2} = 5\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 2x^2 + 12x - 32\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(2\) gives \(2(x + 8)(x - 2) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(x = -8\) and \(x = 2\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-8 + 2}{2} = -3\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -x^2 + 2x + 24\).
qs.s: Factoring gives \(-(x - 6)(x + 4) = 0\), yielding \(x\)-intercepts at \(x = 6\) and \(x = -4\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{6 + (-4)}{2} = 1\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -x^2 - 2x + 8\).
qs.s: Setting \(g(x) = 0\) gives \(-(x + 4)(x - 2) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(x = -4\) and \(x = 2\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-4 + 2}{2} = -1\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -x^2 + 4x + 5\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \(-(x - 5)(x + 1) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(x = 5\) and \(x = -1\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{5 + (-1)}{2} = 2\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(h(x) = -x^2 + 6x - 5\).
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) gives \(-(x - 5)(x - 1) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(x = 5\) and \(x = 1\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{5 + 1}{2} = 3\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(k(x) = -x^2 + 8x - 12\).
qs.s: Setting \(k(x) = 0\) gives \(-(x - 6)(x - 2) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(x = 6\) and \(x = 2\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{6 + 2}{2} = 4\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(p(x) = -x^2 - 4x + 12\).
qs.s: Setting \(p(x) = 0\) gives \(-(x + 6)(x - 2) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(x = -6\) and \(x = 2\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-6 + 2}{2} = -2\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(h(x) = -3x^2 - 10x + 8\).
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) gives \(-(3x - 2)(x + 4) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(x = \frac{2}{3}\) and \(x = -4\). The axis of symmetry is their midpoint: \(x = \frac{\frac{2}{3} + (-4)}{2} = -\frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(k(x) = -5x^2 + 2x + 16\).
qs.s: Setting \(k(x) = 0\) gives \(-(5x + 8)(x - 2) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(x = -\frac{8}{5}\) and \(x = 2\). The axis of symmetry is their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{8}{5} + 2}{2} = \frac{1}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(g(x) = (2x - 1)(5 - x) - 7\).
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying yields \(g(x) = -2x^2 + 11x - 12 = -(2x - 3)(x - 4)\). Setting \(g(x) = 0\) gives roots \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = 4\), so the axis of symmetry is \(x = \frac{\frac{3}{2} + 4}{2} = \frac{11}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(p(x) = -20x^2 - 16x - 3\).
qs.s: Setting \(p(x) = 0\) gives \(-(2x + 1)(10x + 3) = 0\), yielding intercepts \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = -\frac{3}{10}\). The axis of symmetry is their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{5}{10} + (-\frac{3}{10})}{2} = -\frac{2}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(y = q(x) = 2x^2 + 4x\).
qs.s: Setting \(2x^2 + 4x = 0\) gives \(2x(x + 2) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(0\) and \(-2\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{0 + (-2)}{2} = -1\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(y = h(x) = x^2 + 8x\).
qs.s: Setting \(x^2 + 8x = 0\) gives \(x(x + 8) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(0\) and \(-8\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{0 + (-8)}{2} = -4\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(y = g(x) = x^2 - 6x\).
qs.s: Setting \(x^2 - 6x = 0\) gives \(x(x - 6) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(0\) and \(6\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{0 + 6}{2} = 3\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(y = f(x) = x^2 + 4\).
qs.s: Since \(x^2 + 4 = 0\) has no real solutions, the parabola has its vertex at \((0, 4)\), which means the axis of symmetry is the vertical line \(x = 0\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(y = p(x) = -x^2 + 4x\).
qs.s: Setting \(-x^2 + 4x = 0\) gives \(-x(x - 4) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(0\) and \(4\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{0 + 4}{2} = 2\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(y = p(x) = -x^2 + 2x + 35\).
qs.s: Setting \(-(x^2 - 2x - 35) = 0\) factors as \(-(x - 7)(x + 5) = 0\), giving x-intercepts \(7\) and \(-5\). The axis of symmetry is the midpoint: \(x = \frac{7 + (-5)}{2} = 1\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(y = q(x) = x^2 - 5x + 6\).
qs.s: Setting \(x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0\) factors as \((x - 2)(x - 3) = 0\), giving x-intercepts \(2\) and \(3\). The axis of symmetry is the midpoint: \(x = \frac{2 + 3}{2} = \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(y = g(x) = x^2 + 10x + 9\).
qs.s: Setting \(x^2 + 10x + 9 = 0\) factors as \((x + 9)(x + 1) = 0\), giving x-intercepts \(-9\) and \(-1\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-9 + (-1)}{2} = -5\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(y = h(x) = 2x^2 - 8x - 24\).
qs.s: Setting \(2(x^2 - 4x - 12) = 0\) factors as \(2(x - 6)(x + 2) = 0\), giving x-intercepts \(6\) and \(-2\). The axis of symmetry is the midpoint: \(x = \frac{6 + (-2)}{2} = 2\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(y = f(x) = x^2 - 6x - 16\).
qs.s: Setting \(x^2 - 6x - 16 = 0\) factors as \((x - 8)(x + 2) = 0\), yielding x-intercepts \(8\) and \(-2\). The axis of symmetry is the midpoint: \(x = \frac{8 + (-2)}{2} = 3\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = k(x) = -x^2 + 8x - 7\)
qs.s: Setting \(k(x) = 0\) gives \(-(x - 7)(x - 1) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = 7\) and \(x = 1\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{7 + 1}{2} = 4\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = h(x) = -x^2 + 4x + 12\)
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) gives \(-(x - 6)(x + 2) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = 6\) and \(x = -2\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{6 + (-2)}{2} = 2\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = g(x) = -x^2 - 6x - 5\)
qs.s: Setting \(g(x) = 0\) gives \(-(x + 5)(x + 1) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = -5\) and \(x = -1\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-5 + (-1)}{2} = -3\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = p(x) = -x^2 - 4x + 21\)
qs.s: Setting \(p(x) = 0\) gives \(-(x + 7)(x - 3) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = -7\) and \(x = 3\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-7 + 3}{2} = -2\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = f(x) = -x^2 + 2x + 15\)
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \(-(x - 5)(x + 3) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = 5\) and \(x = -3\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{5 + (-3)}{2} = 1\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = g(x) = -3x^2 + 7x + 6\)
qs.s: Setting \(g(x) = 0\) gives \(-(3x + 2)(x - 3) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\) and \(x = 3\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{2}{3} + 3}{2} = \frac{7}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = p(x) = -5x^2 - 13x + 6\)
qs.s: Setting \(p(x) = 0\) gives \(-(5x - 2)(x + 3) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = \frac{2}{5}\) and \(x = -3\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{\frac{2}{5} + (-3)}{2} = -\frac{13}{10}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = k(x) = -6x^2 + 19x - 10\)
qs.s: Setting \(k(x) = 0\) gives \(-(3x - 2)(2x - 5) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = \frac{2}{3}\) and \(x = \frac{5}{2}\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{\frac{2}{3} + \frac{5}{2}}{2} = \frac{19}{12}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = f(x) = -2x^2 - 5x + 3\)
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \(-(2x - 1)(x + 3) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = -3\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{\frac{1}{2} + (-3)}{2} = -\frac{5}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = h(x) = -4x^2 + 12x + 7\)
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) gives \(-(2x + 1)(2x - 7) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = \frac{7}{2}\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{1}{2} + \frac{7}{2}}{2} = \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = g(x) = x^2 + 8x + 16\).
qs.s: Factoring the trinomial gives \(y = (x + 4)^2\). Setting \(y = 0\) gives a single x-intercept at \(x = -4\), which means the axis of symmetry is \(x = -4\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = p(x) = x^2 - 2x - 8\).
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \((x - 4)(x + 2) = 0\), so the x-intercepts are \(x = 4\) and \(x = -2\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{4 + (-2)}{2} = 1\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = f(x) = 9 - 6x + x^2\).
qs.s: Rewriting the function in standard form gives \(y = x^2 - 6x + 9 = (x - 3)^2\). Setting \(y = 0\) yields the single x-intercept at \(x = 3\), so the axis of symmetry is the line \(x = 3\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = q(x) = 12 - 8x + x^2\).
qs.s: Rewriting in standard form gives \(y = x^2 - 8x + 12 = (x - 2)(x - 6)\). The axis of symmetry passes through the midpoint of the x-intercepts \(2\) and \(6\): \(x = \frac{2 + 6}{2} = 4\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = h(x) = 25 - 10x + x^2\).
qs.s: Rearrange and factor the function as \(y = x^2 - 10x + 25 = (x - 5)^2\). Since the only x-intercept is \(x = 5\), the axis of symmetry is \(x = 5\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = g(x) = -50 + 20x - 2x^2\).
qs.s: Factor out \(-2\) to get \(y = -2(x^2 - 10x + 25) = -2(x - 5)^2\). Setting \(y = 0\) gives a single x-intercept at \(x = 5\), so the axis of symmetry is \(x = 5\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = h(x) = 4 + 8x + 3x^2\).
qs.s: Rewriting in standard form gives \(y = 3x^2 + 8x + 4 = (3x + 2)(x + 2)\). The x-intercepts are \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\) and \(x = -2\), and their midpoint gives the axis of symmetry: \(x = \frac{-\frac{2}{3} + (-2)}{2} = -\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = m(x) = 15 - 11x + 2x^2\).
qs.s: In standard form, \(y = 2x^2 - 11x + 15 = (2x - 5)(x - 3)\), which has x-intercepts at \(x = \frac{5}{2}\) and \(x = 3\). The axis of symmetry is the line halfway between them: \(x = \frac{\frac{5}{2} + 3}{2} = \frac{11}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = p(x) = 4 - x - 3x^2\).
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(-(3x^2 + x - 4) = -(3x + 4)(x - 1) = 0\), yielding x-intercepts \(x = -\frac{4}{3}\) and \(x = 1\). The axis of symmetry is the midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{4}{3} + 1}{2} = -\frac{1}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = f(x) = 9 - 12x + 4x^2\).
qs.s: In standard form, \(y = 4x^2 - 12x + 9 = (2x - 3)^2\). Setting \(y = 0\) gives the single x-intercept \(x = \frac{3}{2}\), so the axis of symmetry is \(x = \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(p(x) = x^2 + \sqrt{7}x\).
qs.s: Setting \(p(x) = 0\) yields \(x(x + \sqrt{7}) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(0\) and \(-\sqrt{7}\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{0 + (-\sqrt{7})}{2} = -\frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(g(x) = x^2 + \sqrt{10}x\).
qs.s: Setting \(g(x) = 0\) gives \(x(x + \sqrt{10}) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(0\) and \(-\sqrt{10}\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{0 + (-\sqrt{10})}{2} = -\frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 - \sqrt{6}x\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \(x(x - \sqrt{6}) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(0\) and \(\sqrt{6}\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{0 + \sqrt{6}}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(q(x) = -x^2 + \sqrt{5}x\).
qs.s: Setting \(q(x) = 0\) gives \(-x(x - \sqrt{5}) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(0\) and \(\sqrt{5}\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{0 + \sqrt{5}}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(h(x) = x^2 - \sqrt{14}x\).
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) yields \(x(x - \sqrt{14}) = 0\), which gives \(x\)-intercepts at \(0\) and \(\sqrt{14}\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{0 + \sqrt{14}}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{14}}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(h(x) = -3x^2 - x + 4\).
qs.s: Factoring \(-3x^2 - x + 4 = -(3x + 4)(x - 1) = 0\) gives \(x\)-intercepts at \(-\frac{4}{3}\) and \(1\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{4}{3} + 1}{2} = -\frac{1}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(p(x) = 4x^2 + 4x - 3\).
qs.s: Factoring \(4x^2 + 4x - 3 = (2x - 1)(2x + 3) = 0\) gives \(x\)-intercepts at \(\frac{1}{2}\) and \(-\frac{3}{2}\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{\frac{1}{2} + \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)}{2} = -\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(q(x) = 6x^2 - x - 2\).
qs.s: Factoring \(6x^2 - x - 2 = (2x + 1)(3x - 2) = 0\) gives \(x\)-intercepts at \(-\frac{1}{2}\) and \(\frac{2}{3}\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{-\frac{1}{2} + \frac{2}{3}}{2} = \frac{1}{12}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 7x + 3\).
qs.s: Factoring \(2x^2 - 7x + 3 = (2x - 1)(x - 3) = 0\) gives \(x\)-intercepts at \(\frac{1}{2}\) and \(3\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint: \(x = \frac{\frac{1}{2} + 3}{2} = \frac{7}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = r(x) = \sqrt{20}x^2 - \sqrt{2}x\)
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(\sqrt{2}x(\sqrt{10}x - 1) = 0\), giving \(x\)-intercepts at \(x = 0\) and \(x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} = \frac{\sqrt{10}}{10}\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint, \(x = \frac{0 + \frac{\sqrt{10}}{10}}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{10}}{20}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = h(x) = -\sqrt{8}x^2 + \sqrt{6}x\)
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(-\sqrt{2}x(2x - \sqrt{3}) = 0\), giving \(x\)-intercepts at \(x = 0\) and \(x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint, \(x = \frac{0 + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = f(x) = \sqrt{10}x^2 - \sqrt{5}x\)
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(\sqrt{5}x(\sqrt{2}x - 1) = 0\), which yields \(x\)-intercepts at \(x = 0\) and \(x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through the midpoint of the intercepts, \(x = \frac{0 + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = g(x) = -\sqrt{15}x^2 - \sqrt{3}x\)
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(-\sqrt{3}x(\sqrt{5}x + 1) = 0\), giving \(x\)-intercepts at \(x = 0\) and \(x = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} = -\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint, \(x = \frac{0 + \left(-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\right)}{2} = -\frac{\sqrt{5}}{10}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = p(x) = \sqrt{18}x^2 + \sqrt{3}x\)
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(\sqrt{3}x(\sqrt{6}x + 1) = 0\), which yields \(x\)-intercepts at \(x = 0\) and \(x = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} = -\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through the midpoint of the intercepts, \(x = \frac{0 + \left(-\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}\right)}{2} = -\frac{\sqrt{6}}{12}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = g(x) = 3\sqrt{2}x^2 - 10\sqrt{2}x + 8\sqrt{2}\)
qs.s: Factoring out \(\sqrt{2}\) gives \(\sqrt{2}(3x^2 - 10x + 8) = \sqrt{2}(3x - 4)(x - 2) = 0\), yielding \(x\)-intercepts at \(x = \frac{4}{3}\) and \(x = 2\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint, \(x = \frac{\frac{4}{3} + 2}{2} = \frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = q(x) = -\sqrt{8}x^2 + \sqrt{50}x + \sqrt{18}\)
qs.s: Simplifying radicals yields \(-2\sqrt{2}x^2 + 5\sqrt{2}x + 3\sqrt{2} = -\sqrt{2}(2x + 1)(x - 3) = 0\), so the \(x\)-intercepts are \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = 3\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint, \(x = \frac{-\frac{1}{2} + 3}{2} = \frac{5}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = h(x) = -6\sqrt{5}x^2 - \sqrt{5}x + 2\sqrt{5}\)
qs.s: Factoring out \(-\sqrt{5}\) gives \(-\sqrt{5}(6x^2 + x - 2) = -\sqrt{5}(2x - 1)(3x + 2) = 0\), giving \(x\)-intercepts at \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint, \(x = \frac{\frac{1}{2} + \left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)}{2} = -\frac{1}{12}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = f(x) = -2\sqrt{3}x^2 + 7\sqrt{3}x - 3\sqrt{3}\)
qs.s: Factoring out \(-\sqrt{3}\) yields \(-\sqrt{3}(2x^2 - 7x + 3) = -\sqrt{3}(2x - 1)(x - 3) = 0\), which gives \(x\)-intercepts at \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = 3\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through their midpoint, \(x = \frac{\frac{1}{2} + 3}{2} = \frac{7}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the axis of symmetry of the quadratic function: \(y = p(x) = -\sqrt{54}x^2 + \sqrt{24}x + \sqrt{6}\)
qs.s: Simplifying radicals gives \(-3\sqrt{6}x^2 + 2\sqrt{6}x + \sqrt{6} = -\sqrt{6}(3x + 1)(x - 1) = 0\), giving \(x\)-intercepts at \(x = -\frac{1}{3}\) and \(x = 1\). The axis of symmetry is the line through their midpoint, \(x = \frac{-\frac{1}{3} + 1}{2} = \frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: To graph the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 - 9\) by completing a table of values, what is the value of \(y\) when \(x = -2\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -2\) into the function: \(f(-2) = (-2)^2 - 9 = 4 - 9 = -5\).

qs.q: To graph the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 + 5\) by completing a table of values, what is the value of \(y\) when \(x = -2\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -2\) into the function: \(f(-2) = (-2)^2 + 5 = 4 + 5 = 9\).

qs.s: Substitute \(x = -3\) into the function: \(f(-3) = (-3)^2 - 1 = 9 - 1 = 8\).

qs.s: Substitute \(x = -1\) into the function: \(f(-1) = (-1)^2 - 6 = 1 - 6 = -5\).

qs.q: To graph the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 - 3\) by completing a table of values, what is the value of \(y\) when \(x = -3\)?

qs.q: To graph the quadratic function \(f(x) = -x^2 + 1\) by completing a table of values, what is the value of \(f(-3)\)?

qs.q: When completing a table of values to graph the quadratic function \(h(x) = -x^2 + 4x\), what is the value of \(y\) when \(x = -2\)?

qs.q: When completing a table of values to graph the quadratic function \(g(x) = -x^2 - 3x\), what is the value of \(y\) when \(x = -2\)?

qs.q: In a table of values used to graph the quadratic function \(p(x) = -2x^2 + 4x + 1\), the \(y\)-value at \(x = -1\) is \(a\) and the \(y\)-value at \(x = 2\) is \(b\). What is the value of \(a - b\)?

qs.s: Substitute \(x = -2\) into the function to get \(f(-2) = 3(-2)^2 - 5 = 3(4) - 5 = 12 - 5 = 7\).

qs.q: A table of values is constructed to graph the quadratic function \(h(x) = -2x^2 + 7\). What is the value of \(y\) when \(x = -2\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -2\) into the function to get \(h(-2) = -2(-2)^2 + 7 = -2(4) + 7 = -8 + 7 = -1\).

qs.q: To graph the quadratic function \(g(x) = 2x^2 - 8\) using a table of values, what is the value of \(g(-3)\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -3\) into the function to get \(g(-3) = 2(-3)^2 - 8 = 2(9) - 8 = 18 - 8 = 10\).

qs.q: In a table of values used to graph the quadratic function \(k(x) = -3x^2 + 4\), what is the value of \(y\) when \(x = -2\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -2\) into the function to get \(k(-2) = -3(-2)^2 + 4 = -3(4) + 4 = -12 + 4 = -8\).

qs.q: When completing a table of values to graph the quadratic function \(p(x) = 3x^2 - 10\), what is the value of \(p(-3)\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -3\) into the function to get \(p(-3) = 3(-3)^2 - 10 = 3(9) - 10 = 27 - 10 = 17\).

exercises.name: Identifying features of a parabola from its graph

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to find the domain and range of the function.
qs.a: Domain: all real numbers; Range: y \ge -2
d: Domain: all real numbers; Range: y \le -2
qs.s: The domain of any quadratic function is all real numbers. Since this parabola opens upward with its vertex at (-3, -2), its lowest point is y = -2, so the range is y \ge -2.

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to identify its vertex, axis of symmetry, and y-intercept.
qs.a: Vertex: (1, 4); Axis of symmetry: x = 1; y-intercept: (0, 3)
d: Vertex: (4, 1); Axis of symmetry: x = 4; y-intercept: (3, 0)
Vertex: (1, 4); Axis of symmetry: y = 1; y-intercept: (0, 3)
Vertex: (-1, 4); Axis of symmetry: x = -1; y-intercept: (0, 3)
qs.s: The highest point on the curve is the vertex at (1, 4). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line x = 1, and the curve crosses the y-axis at (0, 3).

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to find its vertex and the equation of its axis of symmetry.
qs.s: The lowest point on the parabola is the vertex at (2, -4). The vertical line passing through the vertex is the axis of symmetry, given by x = 2.

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to determine its x-intercepts and y-intercept.
qs.s: The graph crosses the x-axis at x = 2 and x = 4, giving x-intercepts of (2, 0) and (4, 0). It crosses the y-axis at y = 8, giving a y-intercept of (0, 8).

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to determine whether the function has a maximum or minimum value, and state its value and the range of the function.
qs.s: Because the parabola opens downward, its vertex at (-1, 4) represents a maximum value of 4. Consequently, the range consists of all values less than or equal to 4, or y \le 4.

qs.q: The graph of a vertically stretched quadratic function is shown below. What is the distance between its two x-intercepts, and what is the maximum value of the function?
qs.s: The x-intercepts are at (-1, 0) and (3, 0), so the distance between them is 3 - (-1) = 4. The vertex is at (1, 8), so the maximum value of the function is 8.

qs.q: For the quadratic function graphed below, calculate the sum of the x-coordinates of both x-intercepts, the y-intercept, and the maximum value of the function.
qs.s: The x-intercepts are at (0, 0) and (4, 0), giving x-coordinates of 0 and 4. The y-intercept is 0, and the maximum value at the vertex (2, 2) is 2. The sum is 0 + 4 + 0 + 2 = 6.

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to identify its vertex, domain, and range.
qs.a: Vertex: (-2, -4); Domain: all real numbers; Range: y \ge -4
d: Vertex: (-4, -2); Domain: all real numbers; Range: y \ge -4
Vertex: (-2, -4); Domain: all real numbers; Range: y \le -4
qs.s: The vertex is located at (-2, -4). The domain of any quadratic function is all real numbers, and since it opens upward from y = -4, the range is y \ge -4.

qs.q: Let the graphed parabola have vertex (h, k), axis of symmetry x = c, and y-intercept (0, b). What is the value of h + k + c + b?
qs.s: The vertex is (3, 4), which gives h = 3 and k = 4. The axis of symmetry is x = 3, so c = 3. The y-intercept is at (0, -5), so b = -5. Thus, h + k + c + b = 3 + 4 + 3 + (-5) = 5.

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to determine its axis of symmetry, y-intercept, and range.
qs.a: Axis of symmetry: x = 2; y-intercept: (0, 9); Range: y \ge -3
d: Axis of symmetry: x = 2; y-intercept: (0, 9); Range: y \le -3
Axis of symmetry: y = 2; y-intercept: (9, 0); Range: y \ge -3
Axis of symmetry: x = -2; y-intercept: (0, 9); Range: y \ge -3
qs.s: The vertex is at (2, -3), so the axis of symmetry is x = 2 and the minimum value is -3, giving a range of y \ge -3. The curve crosses the y-axis at (0, 9).

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to find its \(x\)-intercept(s) and \(y\)-intercept.
qs.s: The curve intersects the \(x\)-axis at \((2, 0)\) and \((4, 0)\), so these are the \(x\)-intercepts. It intersects the \(y\)-axis at \((0, 8)\), so \((0, 8)\) is the \(y\)-intercept.

qs.q: Determine the vertex, axis of symmetry, and range of the quadratic function shown in the graph.
qs.s: The vertex is at the peak \((2, 1)\), giving an axis of symmetry of \(x = 2\). Because the parabola opens downward, its \(y\)-values are less than or equal to \(1\), so the range is \(y \le 1\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function to identify its vertex, \(x\)-intercept(s), and minimum value.
qs.s: The parabola touches the \(x\)-axis at its vertex \((-2, 0)\), meaning there is only one \(x\)-intercept, \((-2, 0)\). Since the parabola opens upward, the minimum value is the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex, which is \(0\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to find its vertex and the equation of its axis of symmetry.
qs.s: The lowest point of the parabola is the vertex at \((2, -4)\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line passing through the vertex, given by \(x = 2\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) to determine its domain, range, and maximum or minimum value.
qs.a: Domain: all real numbers; Range: \(y \le 4\); Maximum value: \(4\)
d: Domain: all real numbers; Range: \(y \ge 4\); Minimum value: \(4\)
Domain: all real numbers; Range: \(y \le -1\); Maximum value: \(-1\)
qs.s: The parabola opens downward with vertex \((-1, 4)\). The domain of any quadratic function is all real numbers, and since the highest point has \(y\)-coordinate \(4\), the maximum value is \(4\) and the range is \(y \le 4\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) to determine its vertex, \(x\)-intercepts, \(y\)-intercept, and range.
qs.s: The vertex is at \((1, -8)\), so the parabola opens upward from a minimum value of \(-8\), making the range \(y \ge -8\). The curve crosses the \(x\)-axis at \((-1, 0)\) and \((3, 0)\), and crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, -6)\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to identify its vertex, axis of symmetry, \(x\)-intercept(s), \(y\)-intercept, and maximum value.
qs.s: The highest point is the vertex at \((3, 8)\), giving the axis of symmetry \(x = 3\) and a maximum value of \(8\). The parabola crosses the \(x\)-axis at \((1, 0)\) and \((5, 0)\), and crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, -10)\).

qs.q: Based on the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) shown below, which statement is NOT correct?
d: The maximum value of the function is \(9\).
qs.s: The vertex is \((-4, 9)\), giving an axis of symmetry of \(x = -4\) and a maximum value of \(9\). The graph crosses the \(x\)-axis at \((-7, 0)\) and \((-1, 0)\), and crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, -7)\), not \((0, -9)\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) to determine the distance between its two \(x\)-intercepts and its maximum value.
qs.s: The \(x\)-intercepts are \((0, 0)\) and \((8, 0)\), so the distance between them is \(8 - 0 = 8\). The vertex is at \((4, 8)\), which gives a maximum value of \(8\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to identify its vertex, axis of symmetry, \(x\)-intercept(s), and range.
qs.a: Vertex: \((-3, -3)\); Axis of symmetry: \(x = -3\); \(x\)-intercepts: \((-6, 0)\) and \((0, 0)\); Range: \(y \ge -3\)
d: Vertex: \((3, -3)\); Axis of symmetry: \(x = 3\); \(x\)-intercepts: \((0, 0)\) and \((6, 0)\); Range: \(y \ge -3\)
Vertex: \((-3, -3)\); Axis of symmetry: \(y = -3\); \(x\)-intercepts: \((-6, 0)\) and \((0, 0)\); Range: \(x \ge -3\)
qs.s: The vertex is at \((-3, -3)\), meaning the axis of symmetry is \(x = -3\) and the range is \(y \ge -3\). The parabola intersects the \(x\)-axis at \((-6, 0)\) and \((0, 0)\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) to determine its vertex and range.
qs.s: The lowest point of the parabola is the vertex at \((3, -1)\). Because the curve opens upward, the function takes on all values greater than or equal to \(-1\), so the range is \(y \ge -1\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function to determine its axis of symmetry, \(y\)-intercept, and minimum value.
qs.s: The vertex is at \((-1, -4)\), which gives the axis of symmetry \(x = -1\) and minimum value \(-4\). The curve crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, -3)\), which is the \(y\)-intercept.

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to identify its \(x\)-intercepts and \(y\)-intercept.
qs.s: The graph crosses the \(x\)-axis at \((-3, 0)\) and \((1, 0)\), which are the \(x\)-intercepts, and crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, 3)\), which is the \(y\)-intercept.

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) to determine its vertex, axis of symmetry, and minimum value.
qs.a: Vertex: \((2, -4)\), axis of symmetry: \(x = 2\), minimum value: \(-4\)
d: Vertex: \((-4, 2)\), axis of symmetry: \(y = 2\), minimum value: \(2\)
Vertex: \((2, -4)\), axis of symmetry: \(x = -4\), minimum value: \(2\)
Vertex: \((-2, -4)\), axis of symmetry: \(x = -2\), minimum value: \(-4\)
qs.s: The lowest point on the parabola is the vertex at \((2, -4)\). The vertical line through the vertex gives the axis of symmetry \(x = 2\), and the minimum value is the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex, which is \(-4\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function to determine its vertex, axis of symmetry, and range.
qs.s: The highest point on the parabola is the vertex at \((2, 1)\), giving the axis of symmetry \(x = 2\). Since the parabola opens downward, its maximum value is \(1\), which gives the range \(y \le 1\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function to determine its vertex, \(x\)-intercept(s), \(y\)-intercept, and maximum value.
qs.s: The parabola touches the \(x\)-axis at its vertex \((4, 0)\), making \((4, 0)\) the single \(x\)-intercept as well as the point where the maximum value of \(0\) occurs. The graph crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, -8)\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function to identify its vertex, \(x\)-intercept(s), \(y\)-intercept, and range.
qs.s: The vertex is at \((-2, 2)\), so the range is \(y \ge 2\). Because the entire curve lies strictly above the horizontal axis, there are no real \(x\)-intercepts; the \(y\)-intercept is at \((0, 4)\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function to identify its vertex, axis of symmetry, \(x\)-intercepts, and \(y\)-intercept.
qs.s: The lowest point of the curve is the vertex at \((-2, -4)\), yielding the axis of symmetry \(x = -2\). The curve intersects the \(x\)-axis at \((-6, 0)\) and \((2, 0)\), and crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, -3)\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function to determine its vertex, axis of symmetry, \(x\)-intercepts, and range.
qs.a: Vertex: \((1, 8)\), axis of symmetry: \(x = 1\), \(x\)-intercepts: \((-1, 0)\) and \((3, 0)\), range: \(y \le 8\)
d: Vertex: \((1, 8)\), axis of symmetry: \(x = 1\), \(x\)-intercepts: \((-1, 0)\) and \((3, 0)\), range: \(y \ge 8\)
Vertex: \((-1, 8)\), axis of symmetry: \(x = -1\), \(x\)-intercepts: \((-3, 0)\) and \((1, 0)\), range: \(y \le 8\)
Vertex: \((8, 1)\), axis of symmetry: \(y = 8\), \(x\)-intercepts: \((0, -1)\) and \((0, 3)\), range: \(y \le 8\)
qs.s: The parabola reaches its maximum at the vertex \((1, 8)\), giving the axis of symmetry \(x = 1\) and range \(y \le 8\). The curve intersects the \(x\)-axis at \((-1, 0)\) and \((3, 0)\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function to determine its vertex, axis of symmetry, domain, and range.
qs.a: Vertex: \((2, 8)\), axis of symmetry: \(x = 2\), domain: all real numbers, range: \(y \le 8\)
d: Vertex: \((2, 8)\), axis of symmetry: \(x = 2\), domain: \(x \le 2\), range: all real numbers
Vertex: \((-2, 8)\), axis of symmetry: \(x = -2\), domain: all real numbers, range: \(y \le 8\)
Vertex: \((2, 8)\), axis of symmetry: \(y = 8\), domain: all real numbers, range: \(y \ge 8\)
qs.s: The vertex is at \((2, 8)\), so the vertical axis of symmetry is \(x = 2\). The parabola extends infinitely horizontally (domain: all real numbers) and downward from its maximum value of \(8\) (range: \(y \le 8\)).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function below to identify its \(x\)-intercepts and \(y\)-intercept.
qs.s: The parabola crosses the \(x\)-axis at points \((2, 0)\) and \((4, 0)\), which are the \(x\)-intercepts. It crosses the vertical \(y\)-axis at \((0, 8)\), which is the \(y\)-intercept.

qs.q: The graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) is shown below. What are the domain and range of \(f(x)\)?
qs.s: The parabola continues infinitely to the left and right, so the domain is all real numbers. Since it opens upward from the minimum point at \((-2, -3)\), the range is \(y \ge -3\).

qs.q: Which set of characteristics correctly describes the parabola shown in the graph?
qs.s: The highest point on the curve is \((1, 4)\), meaning the vertex is \((1, 4)\) and the parabola opens downward. Consequently, the function has a maximum value equal to the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex, which is \(4\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola below to determine whether the function has a maximum or minimum value, and state its range.
qs.s: Because the parabola opens downward, it reaches a peak at the vertex \((-1, 4)\), giving a maximum value of \(4\). Therefore, the range is all values less than or equal to \(4\), written as \(y \le 4\).

qs.q: The graph of a quadratic function is shown below. What are the coordinates of the vertex and the equation of the axis of symmetry?
qs.s: The lowest point on the parabola is the vertex at \((2, -4)\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line passing through the vertex, which has the equation \(x = 2\).

qs.q: Determine the number of \(x\)-intercepts, the coordinates of the vertex, and the range of the quadratic function shown.
qs.s: The parabola's vertex is at \((-2, 2)\) and opens upward, so it lies entirely above the \(x\)-axis and has \(0\) \(x\)-intercepts. Its minimum value is \(2\), which makes the range \(y \ge 2\).

qs.q: The parabola shown has the vertex form equation \(f(x) = a(x - p)^2 + q\). What are the values of \(a\), \(p\), and \(q\)?
qs.s: The vertex is \((1, 8)\), so \(p = 1\) and \(q = 8\). Using the \(y\)-intercept \((0, 6)\) in \(6 = a(0 - 1)^2 + 8\), we get \(6 = a + 8\), so \(a = -2\).

qs.q: The graph of a vertically stretched quadratic function is shown below. Determine its vertex, \(x\)-intercepts, and \(y\)-intercept.
qs.s: The lowest point of the parabola is \((-1, -8)\), which gives the vertex. The curve intersects the \(x\)-axis at \((-3, 0)\) and \((1, 0)\), and crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, -6)\).

qs.q: Examine the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) below. Which of the following statements is FALSE?
qs.a: The function has a minimum value of \(-5\).
d: The range of the function is \(y \le 4\).
The zeros of the function are \(x = 1\) and \(x = 5\).
qs.s: Since the parabola opens downward, it has a maximum value of \(4\) at its vertex \((3, 4)\), but no minimum value. The value \(-5\) is actually the \(y\)-intercept, making the statement false.

qs.q: Based on the graph of the parabola below, which quadratic function in vertex form \(f(x) = a(x - p)^2 + q\) represents the curve?
qs.s: The vertex is at \((p, q) = (4, 2)\), so \(f(x) = a(x - 4)^2 + 2\). Substituting the \(y\)-intercept \((0, -6)\) gives \(-6 = a(0 - 4)^2 + 2 \implies 16a = -8 \implies a = -0.5\), yielding \(f(x) = -0.5(x - 4)^2 + 2\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to identify its \(x\)-intercept(s) and \(y\)-intercept.
qs.s: The graph crosses the \(x\)-axis at the points \((-1, 0)\) and \((3, 0)\), and it crosses the \(y\)-axis at the point \((0, -3)\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to determine its vertex, domain, and range.
qs.a: Vertex: \((-3, -1)\); Domain: all real numbers; Range: \(y \ge -1\)
d: Vertex: \((3, -1)\); Domain: all real numbers; Range: \(y \ge -1\)
Vertex: \((-3, -1)\); Domain: \(x \ge -3\); Range: all real numbers
Vertex: \((-1, -3)\); Domain: all real numbers; Range: \(y \ge -3\)
qs.s: The vertex is at \((-3, -1)\). The domain of any parabola opening vertically is all real numbers, and since it opens upward from \(y = -1\), the range is \(y \ge -1\).

qs.q: Use the given graph of the parabola to determine the coordinates of its vertex and the equation of its axis of symmetry.
qs.s: The lowest point on the parabola is the vertex at \((2, -4)\). The vertical line passing through this vertex gives the axis of symmetry, which is \(x = 2\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to determine whether the quadratic function has a maximum or minimum value (and what it is), and state its range.
qs.s: Because the parabola opens downward, its vertex at \((-1, 4)\) represents the highest point, giving a maximum value of \(4\). The range is all real values less than or equal to this peak: \(y \le 4\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to find its vertex, the axis of symmetry, and its optimal (maximum or minimum) value.
qs.a: Vertex: \((3, 1)\); Axis of symmetry: \(x = 3\); Maximum value: \(1\)
d: Vertex: \((3, 1)\); Axis of symmetry: \(y = 1\); Minimum value: \(1\)
Vertex: \((-3, 1)\); Axis of symmetry: \(x = -3\); Maximum value: \(1\)
Vertex: \((1, 3)\); Axis of symmetry: \(x = 1\); Maximum value: \(3\)
qs.s: The parabola reaches its highest point at \((3, 1)\), meaning it has a maximum value of \(1\). The vertical line through the vertex is \(x = 3\), which is the axis of symmetry.

qs.q: The graph of a vertically stretched parabola is shown. Identify its vertex, axis of symmetry, \(x\)-intercepts, and range.
qs.a: Vertex: \((2, -8)\); Axis of symmetry: \(x = 2\); \(x\)-intercepts: \((0, 0)\) and \((4, 0)\); Range: \([-8, \infty)\)
d: Vertex: \((-8, 2)\); Axis of symmetry: \(y = -8\); \(x\)-intercepts: \((0, 0)\) and \((4, 0)\); Range: \([-8, \infty)\)
Vertex: \((2, -8)\); Axis of symmetry: \(x = 2\); \(x\)-intercepts: \((-4, 0)\) and \((0, 0)\); Range: \((-\infty, -8]\)
Vertex: \((2, -8)\); Axis of symmetry: \(x = -8\); \(x\)-intercepts: \((0, 0)\) and \((4, 0)\); Range: \((-\infty, 2]\)
qs.s: The vertex is at \((2, -8)\), yielding the vertical axis of symmetry \(x = 2\). The parabola intersects the \(x\)-axis at \((0, 0)\) and \((4, 0)\), and opens upward from \(y = -8\), so its range is \([-8, \infty)\).

qs.q: A quadratic function is graphed on the grid. Find its vertex, equation of the axis of symmetry, \(x\)-intercepts, and range.
qs.a: Vertex: \((-2, 8)\); Axis of symmetry: \(x = -2\); \(x\)-intercepts: \((-4, 0)\) and \((0, 0)\); Range: \(y \le 8\)
d: Vertex: \((2, 8)\); Axis of symmetry: \(x = 2\); \(x\)-intercepts: \((-4, 0)\) and \((0, 0)\); Range: \(y \le 8\)
Vertex: \((-2, 8)\); Axis of symmetry: \(y = 8\); \(x\)-intercepts: \((-4, 0)\) and \((0, 0)\); Range: \(y \ge 8\)
Vertex: \((-2, 8)\); Axis of symmetry: \(x = -2\); \(x\)-intercepts: \((-2, 0)\) and \((4, 0)\); Range: \(y \le -2\)
qs.s: The peak is at vertex \((-2, 8)\), giving the axis of symmetry \(x = -2\). The curve passes through the origin \((0, 0)\) and \((-4, 0)\) on the \(x\)-axis, and since it opens downward from \(y = 8\), the range is \(y \le 8\).

qs.q: From the graph of the parabola, identify the vertex, \(x\)-intercept(s), \(y\)-intercept, and minimum value.
qs.s: The vertex sits directly on the \(x\)-axis at \((4, 0)\), which is also the only \(x\)-intercept. The minimum value is \(0\), and the curve intersects the \(y\)-axis at \((0, 8)\).

qs.q: The graph of a quadratic function is shown. Determine the vertex, \(y\)-intercept, non-zero \(x\)-intercept, and maximum value.
qs.s: The highest point on the curve is \((4, 8)\), giving a maximum value of \(8\). The parabola passes through \((0, 0)\), so the \(y\)-intercept is \((0, 0)\), and by symmetry, the other \(x\)-intercept is at \((8, 0)\).

qs.q: Use the given graph to determine the vertex, \(x\)-intercept(s), \(y\)-intercept, and range of the quadratic function.
d: Vertex: \((2, 3)\); \(x\)-intercepts: None; \(y\)-intercept: \((0, 7)\); Range: all real numbers
qs.s: The vertex is at \((2, 3)\) and the parabola opens upward, so it never intersects the \(x\)-axis (no \(x\)-intercepts). The \(y\)-intercept is at \((0, 7)\), and the range of values is \(y \ge 3\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) to find the coordinates of its vertex and the equation of its axis of symmetry.
qs.s: The vertex is the lowest point on the parabola at \((2, -4)\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line passing through the vertex, which has the equation \(x = 2\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) to determine its range and maximum or minimum value.
qs.s: The parabola opens downward with its peak at \((-1, 4)\), so it has a maximum value of \(4\). The range consists of all real numbers less than or equal to this maximum, \(y \le 4\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) to determine the equation of its axis of symmetry and its \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is the vertical line passing through the vertex \((2, 4)\), which is \(x = 2\). The points where the parabola intersects the \(x\)-axis are \((0, 0)\) and \((4, 0)\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) to find its \(x\)-intercept(s) and \(y\)-intercept.
qs.s: The graph crosses the \(x\)-axis at \((-1, 0)\) and \((3, 0)\), so these points are the \(x\)-intercepts. It crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, -3)\), which is the \(y\)-intercept.

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) to identify its vertex, domain, and range.
qs.a: Vertex: \((-2, -1)\); Domain: all real numbers; Range: \(y \ge -1\)
d: Vertex: \((2, -1)\); Domain: all real numbers; Range: \(y \ge -1\)
Vertex: \((-1, -2)\); Domain: all real numbers; Range: \(y \ge -2\)
qs.s: The lowest point of the parabola is the vertex at \((-2, -1)\). The function extends horizontally without bound, making its domain all real numbers, and since it opens upward from \(y = -1\), its range is \(y \ge -1\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) to find its vertex, \(x\)-intercept(s), and maximum value.
qs.s: The parabola is tangent to the \(x\)-axis at its vertex \((-2, 0)\), meaning it has exactly one \(x\)-intercept at \((-2, 0)\). Since the parabola opens downward, its maximum value is \(0\).

qs.q: Based on the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\), which of the following statements is FALSE?
d: The range of the function is \(y \le 9\).
qs.s: The graph crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, 5)\), not \((0, 9)\); the value \(9\) is the maximum \(y\)-value at the vertex \((-2, 9)\). The other three statements correctly describe the parabola.

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) to determine its \(x\)-intercept(s), \(y\)-intercept, and range.
qs.s: Because the entire parabola lies above the \(x\)-axis, it has no \(x\)-intercepts. It crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, 7)\) and opens upward from its minimum at the vertex \((2, 3)\), yielding the range \(y \ge 3\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) to determine its vertex, \(x\)-intercepts, and minimum value.
qs.s: The lowest point on the parabola is the vertex at \((-1, -8)\), which gives a minimum value of \(-8\). The curve intersects the \(x\)-axis at \((-3, 0)\) and \((1, 0)\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) to determine its vertex, axis of symmetry, \(y\)-intercept, and range.
qs.s: The vertex is at \((2, 8)\), which gives the vertical axis of symmetry \(x = 2\). The graph crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, 6)\) and opens downward from \(y = 8\), so the range is \(y \le 8\).

exercises.name: Finding a symmetric point on a parabola

qs.q: Find a third point on the quadratic function that has the indicated vertex, and whose graph passes through the given point: vertex \((4, 1)\), point \((1, 10)\)
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is \(x = 4\), and the point is \(4 - 1 = 3\) units to the left of the vertex. Moving \(3\) units to the right of the vertex gives \(x = 4 + 3 = 7\), yielding the symmetric point \((7, 10)\).

qs.q: Find a third point on the quadratic function that has the indicated vertex, and whose graph passes through the given point: vertex \((-2, 3)\), point \((1, -6)\)
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is \(x = -2\), and the point is \(1 - (-2) = 3\) units to the right of the vertex. Moving \(3\) units to the left of the vertex gives \(x = -2 - 3 = -5\), resulting in the point \((-5, -6)\).

qs.q: Find a third point on the quadratic function that has the indicated vertex, and whose graph passes through the given point: vertex \((1, 5)\), point \((4, -4)\)
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is \(x = 1\), and the point is \(4 - 1 = 3\) units to the right of the vertex. Moving \(3\) units to the left gives \(x = 1 - 3 = -2\), giving the symmetric point \((-2, -4)\).

qs.q: Find a third point on the quadratic function that has the indicated vertex, and whose graph passes through the given point: vertex \((-3, -4)\), point \((-1, 0)\)
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is \(x = -3\), and the given point is \(-1 - (-3) = 2\) units to the right of the vertex. Moving \(2\) units to the left gives \(x = -3 - 2 = -5\), so the symmetric point is \((-5, 0)\).

qs.q: Find a third point on the quadratic function that has the indicated vertex, and whose graph passes through the given point: vertex \((2, -1)\), point \((6, 15)\)
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is \(x = 2\), and the given point is \(6 - 2 = 4\) units to the right of the vertex. Moving \(4\) units to the left gives \(x = 2 - 4 = -2\), so the symmetric point with the same \(y\)-value is \((-2, 15)\).

qs.q: Find a third point on the quadratic function that has the indicated vertex, and whose graph passes through the given point: vertex \((-18, 45)\), point \((15, -64)\)
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is \(x = -18\), and the given point is \(15 - (-18) = 33\) units to the right of the vertex. Moving \(33\) units to the left gives \(x = -18 - 33 = -51\), producing the point \((-51, -64)\).

qs.q: Find a third point on the quadratic function that has the indicated vertex, and whose graph passes through the given point: vertex \((\frac{2}{3}, 5)\), point \((\frac{7}{4}, -1)\)
qs.s: The horizontal distance from the vertex \(x = \frac{2}{3}\) to the point is \(\frac{7}{4} - \frac{2}{3} = \frac{13}{12}\) to the right. Subtracting \(\frac{13}{12}\) from \(\frac{2}{3}\) gives \(x = \frac{8}{12} - \frac{13}{12} = -\frac{5}{12}\), so the symmetric point is \((-\frac{5}{12}, -1)\).

qs.q: Find a third point on the quadratic function that has the indicated vertex, and whose graph passes through the given point: vertex \((35, -28)\), point \((12, 79)\)
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is \(x = 35\), and the given point is \(35 - 12 = 23\) units to the left of the vertex. Moving \(23\) units to the right gives \(x = 35 + 23 = 58\), resulting in the point \((58, 79)\).

qs.q: Find a third point on the quadratic function that has the indicated vertex, and whose graph passes through the given point: vertex \((-\frac{5}{6}, -3)\), point \((\frac{1}{2}, 5)\)
qs.s: The horizontal distance from the vertex to the point is \(\frac{1}{2} - (-\frac{5}{6}) = \frac{3}{6} + \frac{5}{6} = \frac{8}{6}\). Moving \(\frac{8}{6}\) units to the left of the vertex gives \(x = -\frac{5}{6} - \frac{8}{6} = -\frac{13}{6}\), yielding \((-\frac{13}{6}, 5)\).

qs.q: Find a third point on the quadratic function that has the indicated vertex, and whose graph passes through the given point: vertex \((\frac{1}{2}, 3)\), point \((\frac{7}{2}, -6)\)
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is \(x = \frac{1}{2}\), and the given point is \(\frac{7}{2} - \frac{1}{2} = 3\) units to the right of the vertex. Moving \(3\) units to the left gives \(x = \frac{1}{2} - 3 = -\frac{5}{2}\), giving the symmetric point \((-\frac{5}{2}, -6)\).

qs.q: Find a third point on the quadratic function that has vertex \((-3, 1)\) and passes through the point \((-1, -7)\).
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is \(x = -3\), so the point \((-1, -7)\) is \(-1 - (-3) = 2\) units to the right. Moving \(2\) units to the left of the axis gives \(x = -3 - 2 = -5\), resulting in \((-5, -7)\).

qs.q: Find a third point on the quadratic function that has vertex \((3, 5)\) and passes through the point \((7, -3)\).
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is \(x = 3\), and the point is \(7 - 3 = 4\) units to the right of the axis. Moving \(4\) units to the left gives \(x = 3 - 4 = -1\), yielding the point \((-1, -3)\).

qs.q: Find a third point on the quadratic function that has vertex \((1, -2)\) and passes through the point \((-3, 6)\).
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is \(x = 1\), and the given point is \(1 - (-3) = 4\) units to the left. Moving \(4\) units to the right gives \(x = 1 + 4 = 5\), giving the point \((5, 6)\).
