qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = (x + 3)^2 - 25\).
qs.s: Set \(f(x) = 0\) to get \((x + 3)^2 = 25\), so \(x + 3 = \pm 5\). Solving gives \(x = 2\) or \(x = -8\), so the smaller x-intercept is \(-8\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = (x + 5)^2 - 1\).
qs.s: To find the y-intercept, evaluate \(f(0) = (0 + 5)^2 - 1 = 25 - 1 = 24\).

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -4\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 + 25\).
qs.s: Set \(f(x) = 0\) to get \(-4\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = -25\), which yields \(\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{4}\) and \(x - \frac{3}{2} = \pm \frac{5}{2}\). Solving gives \(x = 4\) or \(x = -1\), so the smaller x-intercept is \(-1\).

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = \frac{1}{3}(x + 2)^2 - 27\).
qs.s: Set \(f(x) = 0\) to get \(\frac{1}{3}(x + 2)^2 = 27\), so \((x + 2)^2 = 81\) and \(x + 2 = \pm 9\). Thus \(x = 7\) or \(x = -11\), so the smaller x-intercept is \(-11\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 3(x + 4)^2 - 75\).
qs.s: Set \(f(x) = 0\) to get \(3(x + 4)^2 = 75\), so \((x + 4)^2 = 25\) and \(x + 4 = \pm 5\). Solving gives \(x = 1\) or \(x = -9\), so the greater x-intercept is \(1\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4)^2 + 18\).
qs.s: Set \(f(x) = 0\) to get \(-\frac{1}{2}(x - 4)^2 = -18\), so \((x - 4)^2 = 36\) and \(x - 4 = \pm 6\). Solving gives \(x = 10\) or \(x = -2\), so the greater x-intercept is \(10\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2(x - 5)^2 + 32\).
Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = (x + 1)^2 - 16\).
qs.s: Set \(f(x) = 0\) to get \((x + 1)^2 = 16\), which gives \(x + 1 = \pm 4\), so \(x = 3\) or \(x = -5\). The smaller x-intercept is \(-5\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = (x + 3)^2 + 5\).
qs.s: To find the y-intercept, evaluate \(h(0) = (0 + 3)^2 + 5 = 9 + 5 = 14\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = (x - 5)^2 - 4\).
qs.s: Set \(g(x) = 0\) to get \((x - 5)^2 = 4\), which gives \(x - 5 = \pm 2\), so \(x = 7\) or \(x = 3\). The greater x-intercept is \(7\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = (x - 4)^2 + 3\).
qs.s: To find the y-intercept, evaluate \(f(0) = (0 - 4)^2 + 3 = 16 + 3 = 19\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = (x - 2)^2 - 9\).
qs.s: Set \(g(x) = 0\) to get \((x - 2)^2 = 9\), which gives \(x - 2 = \pm 3\), so \(x = 5\) or \(x = -1\). The greater x-intercept is \(5\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -4(x + 3)^2 + 64\).
qs.s: Set \(g(x) = 0\) to get \(-4(x + 3)^2 = -64\), so \((x + 3)^2 = 16\) and \(x + 3 = \pm 4\), yielding \(x = 1\) or \(x = -7\). The greater x-intercept is \(1\).

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 2\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 - 18\).
qs.s: Set \(f(x) = 0\) to get \(2(x - \frac{1}{2})^2 = 18\), so \((x - \frac{1}{2})^2 = 9\) and \(x - \frac{1}{2} = \pm 3\), giving \(x = \frac{7}{2}\) or \(x = -\frac{5}{2}\). The smaller x-intercept is \(-\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -3(x - 4)^2 + 75\).
qs.s: Set \(g(x) = 0\) to get \(-3(x - 4)^2 = -75\), so \((x - 4)^2 = 25\) and \(x - 4 = \pm 5\), yielding \(x = 9\) or \(x = -1\). The greater x-intercept is \(9\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2(x - 5)^2 + 37\).
qs.s: To find the y-intercept, evaluate \(f(0) = -2(0 - 5)^2 + 37 = -2(25) + 37 = -13\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = \frac{1}{3}(x - 6)^2 - 19\).
qs.s: To find the y-intercept, evaluate \(h(0) = \frac{1}{3}(0 - 6)^2 - 19 = \frac{1}{3}(36) - 19 = -7\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(k(x) = 2(x + 5)^2 - 18\).
qs.s: Set \(k(x) = 0\) to get \(2(x + 5)^2 = 18\), which simplifies to \((x + 5)^2 = 9\). Solving \(x + 5 = \pm 3\) gives \(x = -2\) and \(x = -8\), so the greater x-intercept is \(-2\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = 3(x + 2)^2 - 75\).
qs.s: Set \(g(x) = 0\) to get \(3(x + 2)^2 = 75\), which simplifies to \((x + 2)^2 = 25\). Solving \(x + 2 = \pm 5\) gives \(x = 3\) and \(x = -7\), so the greater x-intercept is \(3\).

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = 5(x - 1)^2 - 45\).
qs.s: Set \(h(x) = 0\) to get \(5(x - 1)^2 = 45\), so \((x - 1)^2 = 9\). Taking the square root gives \(x - 1 = \pm 3\), which yields \(x = 4\) and \(x = -2\), so the smaller x-intercept is \(-2\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 2(x - 3)^2 - 32\).
qs.s: To find the y-intercept, substitute \(x = 0\) into the function: \(f(0) = 2(0 - 3)^2 - 32 = 2(9) - 32 = -14\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(p(x) = -2(x + 4)^2 + 50\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 0\) into the function to obtain \(p(0) = -2(0 + 4)^2 + 50 = -2(16) + 50 = 18\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = -5(x - 6)^2 + 140\).
Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = \frac{2}{3}(x - 4)^2 - 24\).
qs.s: Set \(f(x) = 0\) and multiply by \(\frac{3}{2}\) to obtain \((x - 4)^2 = 36\). Solving \(x - 4 = \pm 6\) gives \(x = 10\) and \(x = -2\), so the smaller x-intercept is \(-2\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(k(x) = 3\left(x - \frac{2}{3}\right)^2 - \frac{25}{3}\).
qs.s: Set \(k(x) = 0\) to get \(\left(x - \frac{2}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{9}\), so \(x - \frac{2}{3} = \pm \frac{5}{3}\). This yields \(x = \frac{7}{3}\) and \(x = -1\), of which the greater x-intercept is \(\frac{7}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(m(x) = -3x^2 - 18x + 48\).
qs.s: Convert \(m(x)\) to standard form as \(m(x) = -3(x + 3)^2 + 75\), then solve \(-3(x + 3)^2 + 75 = 0\) to find \((x + 3)^2 = 25\). This gives \(x = -3 \pm 5\), which results in x-intercepts of \(2\) and \(-8\), with the smaller being \(-8\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = 2x^2 - 8x - 24\).
qs.s: Rewrite \(g(x)\) in standard form as \(g(x) = 2(x - 2)^2 - 32\), and set it equal to 0 to get \((x - 2)^2 = 16\). Solving \(x - 2 = \pm 4\) gives \(x = 6\) and \(x = -2\), so the greater x-intercept is \(6\).

qs.q: What is the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(p(x) = -(x - 5)^2 + 7\)?
qs.s: Set \(p(x) = 0\) to get \(-(x - 5)^2 + 7 = 0\), which simplifies to \((x - 5)^2 = 7\). Thus \(x = 5 \pm \sqrt{7}\), so the greater x-intercept is \(5 + \sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: What is the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = 2(x + 1)^2 - 18\)?
qs.s: Set \(h(x) = 0\) to get \(2(x + 1)^2 = 18\), so \((x + 1)^2 = 9\). Thus \(x + 1 = \pm 3\), giving intercepts \(x = 2\) and \(x = -4\), so the smaller x-intercept is \(-4\).

qs.q: What is the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -3(x + 2)^2 + 15\)?
qs.s: Set \(f(x) = 0\) to get \(-3(x + 2)^2 + 15 = 0\), which gives \((x + 2)^2 = 5\) and \(x = -2 \pm \sqrt{5}\). The greater x-intercept is \(-2 + \sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: What is the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(q(x) = -2(x + 3)^2 + 15\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 0\) into the function to find the y-intercept: \(q(0) = -2(0 + 3)^2 + 15 = -2(9) + 15 = -3\).

qs.q: What is the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -2(x - 4)^2 + 13\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 0\) into the function to find the y-intercept: \(g(0) = -2(0 - 4)^2 + 13 = -2(16) + 13 = -19\).

qs.q: What is the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 12x - 10\)?
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -2(x - 3)^2 + 8\). Setting \(f(x) = 0\) yields \((x - 3)^2 = 4\), so \(x = 3 \pm 2\), and the greater x-intercept is \(5\).

qs.q: What is the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = 2x^2 - 3x - 5\)?
qs.s: Complete the square to write \(h(x) = 2\left(x - \frac{3}{4}\right)^2 - \frac{49}{8}\). Setting \(h(x) = 0\) gives \(\left(x - \frac{3}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{49}{16}\), so \(x = \frac{3 \pm 7}{4}\), which yields the smaller x-intercept \(-1\).

qs.q: What is the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(k(x) = -4x^2 + 16x + 9\)?
qs.s: Rewrite in vertex form as \(k(x) = -4(x - 2)^2 + 25\). Setting \(k(x) = 0\) yields \((x - 2)^2 = \frac{25}{4}\), so \(x = 2 \pm \frac{5}{2}\), giving the greater x-intercept \(\frac{9}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = \frac{2}{3}(x - 1)^2 - 24\)?
qs.s: Set \(f(x) = 0\) to get \(\frac{2}{3}(x - 1)^2 = 24\), which simplifies to \((x - 1)^2 = 36\). Thus \(x - 1 = \pm 6\), giving intercepts \(7\) and \(-5\), so the smaller x-intercept is \(-5\).

qs.q: What is the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -3(x - 4)^2 + 14\)?
qs.s: Set \(g(x) = 0\) to obtain \(3(x - 4)^2 = 14\), so \((x - 4)^2 = \frac{14}{3}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing gives \(x = 4 \pm \frac{\sqrt{42}}{3}\), so the greater x-intercept is \(4 + \frac{\sqrt{42}}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}\left(x - \frac{1}{3}\right)^2\).
qs.s: To find the y-intercept, evaluate \(f(0) = -\frac{1}{2}\left(0 - \frac{1}{3}\right)^2 = -\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{9}\right) = -\frac{1}{18}\).

qs.q: Find the x-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -\frac{2}{3}\left(x + \frac{3}{4}\right)^2\).
qs.s: Set \(g(x) = 0\) to get \(-\frac{2}{3}\left(x + \frac{3}{4}\right)^2 = 0\), which gives \(\left(x + \frac{3}{4}\right)^2 = 0\). Solving for \(x\) yields \(x = -\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = \frac{2}{5}\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2\).
qs.s: To find the y-intercept, evaluate \(h(0) = \frac{2}{5}\left(0 - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{2}{5}\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{10}\).

qs.q: Find the x-intercept of the quadratic function \(q(x) = \frac{3}{5}\left(x - \frac{4}{3}\right)^2\).
qs.s: Set \(q(x) = 0\) to get \(\frac{3}{5}\left(x - \frac{4}{3}\right)^2 = 0\), which gives \(\left(x - \frac{4}{3}\right)^2 = 0\). Solving for \(x\) yields \(x = \frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(p(x) = -\frac{1}{4}\left(x + \frac{2}{3}\right)^2\).
qs.s: To find the y-intercept, evaluate \(p(0) = -\frac{1}{4}\left(0 + \frac{2}{3}\right)^2 = -\frac{1}{4}\left(\frac{4}{9}\right) = -\frac{1}{9}\).

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = -\frac{3}{2}\left(x + \frac{1}{3}\right)^2 + \frac{27}{8}\).
qs.s: Set \(h(x) = 0\) to get \(-\frac{3}{2}\left(x + \frac{1}{3}\right)^2 = -\frac{27}{8}\), which simplifies to \(\left(x + \frac{1}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}\). Taking the square root gives \(x + \frac{1}{3} = \pm \frac{3}{2}\), so the smaller x-intercept is \(x = -\frac{1}{3} - \frac{3}{2} = -\frac{11}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(q(x) = \frac{4}{3}\left(x - \frac{5}{4}\right)^2 - \frac{3}{4}\).
qs.s: Set \(q(x) = 0\) to get \(\frac{4}{3}\left(x - \frac{5}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{3}{4}\), which simplifies to \(\left(x - \frac{5}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{16}\). Taking the square root gives \(x - \frac{5}{4} = \pm \frac{3}{4}\), so the greater x-intercept is \(x = \frac{5}{4} + \frac{3}{4} = 2\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(p(x) = \frac{5}{6}\left(x - \frac{3}{5}\right)^2 - \frac{7}{10}\).
Find the y-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -\frac{3}{4}\left(x - \frac{2}{3}\right)^2 + \frac{5}{8}\).
qs.s: Evaluate \(f(0) = -\frac{3}{4}\left(0 - \frac{2}{3}\right)^2 + \frac{5}{8} = -\frac{3}{4}\left(\frac{4}{9}\right) + \frac{5}{8} = -\frac{1}{3} + \frac{5}{8} = \frac{7}{24}\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = \frac{2}{3}\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 - \frac{8}{3}\).
qs.s: Set \(g(x) = 0\) to get \(\frac{2}{3}\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{8}{3}\), so \(\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = 4\). Taking the square root gives \(x - \frac{1}{2} = \pm 2\), so the greater x-intercept is \(x = \frac{1}{2} + 2 = \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 + 8x\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \(x^2 + 8x = 0\), which factors as \(x(x + 8) = 0\). The roots are \(x = 0\) and \(x = -8\), so the non-zero \(x\)-intercept is \(-8\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(p(x) = x^2 - 10x\).
qs.s: Setting \(p(x) = 0\) gives \(x(x - 10) = 0\), which gives \(x = 0\) or \(x = 10\). Therefore, the non-zero \(x\)-intercept is \(10\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(k(x) = x^2 - 9x\).
qs.s: Setting \(k(x) = 0\) yields \(x(x - 9) = 0\), resulting in roots \(x = 0\) and \(x = 9\). Hence, the non-zero \(x\)-intercept is \(9\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = x^2 - 6x\).
qs.s: Setting \(g(x) = 0\) yields \(x^2 - 6x = 0\), which factors as \(x(x - 6) = 0\). Solving gives \(x = 0\) or \(x = 6\), so the non-zero \(x\)-intercept is \(6\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = x^2 + 14x\).
qs.s: Set \(h(x) = 0\) to get \(x(x + 14) = 0\), which yields \(x = 0\) and \(x = -14\). Thus, the non-zero \(x\)-intercept is \(-14\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(k(x) = -x^2 - 5x + 6\).
qs.s: Set \(k(x) = 0\) and multiply by \(-1\) to get \(x^2 + 5x - 6 = (x + 6)(x - 1) = 0\). The roots are \(x = -6\) and \(x = 1\), so the smaller \(x\)-intercept is \(-6\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = 2x^2 - 5x - 3\).
qs.s: Set \(g(x) = 0\) and factor into \((2x + 1)(x - 3) = 0\), which gives intercepts \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = 3\). The smaller \(x\)-intercept is \(-\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(p(x) = 2(x - 1)^2 - 18\).
qs.s: Set \(p(x) = 0\) to get \(2(x - 1)^2 = 18\), so \((x - 1)^2 = 9\). Taking the square root gives \(x - 1 = \pm 3\), which yields \(x = 4\) and \(x = -2\), with \(4\) being the greater intercept.

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = 3(x - 2)^2 - 5\).
qs.s: The \(y\)-intercept is found by evaluating \(h(0) = 3(0 - 2)^2 - 5 = 3(4) - 5 = 7\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 - 3x - 10\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\), factor the trinomial as \((x - 5)(x + 2) = 0\), giving \(x = 5\) and \(x = -2\). The greater \(x\)-intercept is \(5\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -x^2 - 2x + 8\).
qs.s: Setting \(g(x) = 0\) gives \(-(x^2 + 2x - 8) = -(x + 4)(x - 2) = 0\), yielding \(x = -4\) and \(x = 2\). The smaller \(x\)-intercept is \(-4\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2x^2 - 4x + 6\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \(-2(x^2 + 2x - 3) = -2(x + 3)(x - 1) = 0\), so the intercepts are \(x = -3\) and \(x = 1\). The greater \(x\)-intercept is \(1\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = -2x^2 + 8x - 6\).
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) gives \(-2(x^2 - 4x + 3) = -2(x - 1)(x - 3) = 0\), which gives roots at \(x = 1\) and \(x = 3\). The smaller \(x\)-intercept is \(1\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(k(x) = -2x^2 - 8x - 8\).
qs.s: Setting \(k(x) = 0\) yields \(-2(x^2 + 4x + 4) = -2(x + 2)^2 = 0\). Solving gives a single \(x\)-intercept at \(x = -2\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(p(x) = -3x^2 + 12x + 15\).
qs.s: Setting \(p(x) = 0\) gives \(-3(x^2 - 4x - 5) = -3(x - 5)(x + 1) = 0\), so \(x = 5\) and \(x = -1\). The greater \(x\)-intercept is \(5\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(k(x) = -4x^2 + 16x - 7\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(-4(x - 2)^2 + 9 = 0\), so \((x - 2)^2 = \frac{9}{4}\) and \(x = 2 \pm \frac{3}{2}\). The smaller \(x\)-intercept is \(2 - \frac{3}{2} = \frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(p(x) = -2x^2 + 8x - 2\).
qs.s: Completing the square yields \(-2(x - 2)^2 + 6 = 0\), so \((x - 2)^2 = 3\) and \(x = 2 \pm \sqrt{3}\). The smaller \(x\)-intercept is \(2 - \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = -x^2 + 6x - 2\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(h(x) = -(x - 3)^2 + 7 = 0\), which leads to \((x - 3)^2 = 7\) and \(x = 3 \pm \sqrt{7}\). The greater \(x\)-intercept is \(3 + \sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -2x^2 + 7x + 15\).
qs.s: Setting \(g(x) = 0\) gives \(-(2x^2 - 7x - 15) = -(2x + 3)(x - 5) = 0\), yielding roots \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = 5\). The greater \(x\)-intercept is \(5\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 5x - 2\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) and factoring yields \((3x + 1)(x - 2) = 0\), giving \(x = -\frac{1}{3}\) and \(x = 2\). The smaller \(x\)-intercept is \(-\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = \frac{1}{3}x^2 - 2x + \frac{5}{3}\).
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) gives \(\frac{1}{3}(x^2 - 6x + 5) = 0\), which factors as \(\frac{1}{3}(x - 5)(x - 1) = 0\). The \(x\)-intercepts are \(1\) and \(5\), so the greater \(x\)-intercept is \(5\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(p(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 + 2x - \frac{21}{2}\).
qs.s: Setting \(p(x) = 0\) gives \(\frac{1}{2}(x^2 + 4x - 21) = 0\), which factors as \(\frac{1}{2}(x + 7)(x - 3) = 0\). The \(x\)-intercepts are \(-7\) and \(3\), so the smaller \(x\)-intercept is \(-7\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 - 2x + \frac{5}{2}\).
qs.s: Setting \(g(x) = 0\) gives \(-\frac{1}{2}(x^2 + 4x - 5) = 0\), which factors as \(-\frac{1}{2}(x + 5)(x - 1) = 0\). The \(x\)-intercepts are \(-5\) and \(1\), so the smaller \(x\)-intercept is \(-5\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(k(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 - 4x - \frac{15}{2}\).
qs.s: Setting \(k(x) = 0\) gives \(-\frac{1}{2}(x^2 + 8x + 15) = 0\), which factors as \(-\frac{1}{2}(x + 5)(x + 3) = 0\). The \(x\)-intercepts are \(-5\) and \(-3\), so the greater \(x\)-intercept is \(-3\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 3x - \frac{7}{2}\).
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \(\frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 6x - 7) = 0\), which factors as \(\frac{1}{2}(x - 7)(x + 1) = 0\). The \(x\)-intercepts are \(-1\) and \(7\), so the greater \(x\)-intercept is \(7\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(m(x) = -\frac{1}{3}x^2 + 2x + 1\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(-\frac{1}{3}(x - 3)^2 + 4 = 0\), so \((x - 3)^2 = 12\). Solving gives \(x = 3 \pm \sqrt{12} = 3 \pm 2\sqrt{3}\), so the smaller \(x\)-intercept is \(3 - 2\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = \frac{3}{2}x^2 - 5x + \frac{7}{2}\).
qs.s: Completing the square yields \(f(x) = \frac{3}{2}\left(x - \frac{5}{3}\right)^2 - \frac{2}{3} = 0\), which gives \(\left(x - \frac{5}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{4}{9}\). Solving yields \(x = \frac{5}{3} \pm \frac{2}{3}\), giving intercepts \(1\) and \(\frac{7}{3}\), so the greater is \(\frac{7}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the distance between the two \(x\)-intercepts of the quadratic function \(h(x) = \frac{1}{4}x^2 - x - 8\).
qs.s: Writing in standard form gives \(\frac{1}{4}(x - 2)^2 - 9 = 0\), which leads to \((x - 2)^2 = 36\) and intercepts \(x = 8\) and \(x = -4\). The distance between them is \(8 - (-4) = 12\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 4x + 5\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(g(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x - 4)^2 - 3 = 0\), which simplifies to \((x - 4)^2 = 6\). Taking the square root gives \(x = 4 \pm \sqrt{6}\), so the greater \(x\)-intercept is \(4 + \sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(k(x) = \frac{3}{2}x^2 - \frac{5}{4}x - 1\).
qs.s: Completing the square yields \(\frac{3}{2}\left(x - \frac{5}{12}\right)^2 - \frac{121}{96} = 0\), so \(\left(x - \frac{5}{12}\right)^2 = \frac{121}{144}\). Taking the square root gives \(x = \frac{5}{12} \pm \frac{11}{12}\), giving intercepts \(\frac{4}{3}\) and \(-\frac{1}{2}\), so the smaller is \(-\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero x-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = 5x^2 - 8x\).
qs.s: Set \(h(x) = 0\) to get \(x(5x - 8) = 0\), which gives \(x = 0\) or \(5x - 8 = 0\). Solving \(5x - 8 = 0\) yields the non-zero x-intercept \(x = \frac{8}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero x-intercept of the quadratic function \(r(x) = 3x^2 + 11x\).
qs.s: Set \(r(x) = 0\) to get \(x(3x + 11) = 0\), which gives \(x = 0\) or \(3x + 11 = 0\). Solving \(3x + 11 = 0\) yields the non-zero x-intercept \(x = -\frac{11}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero x-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -4x^2 - 9x\).
qs.s: Set \(f(x) = 0\) to get \(-x(4x + 9) = 0\), which gives \(x = 0\) or \(4x + 9 = 0\). Solving \(4x + 9 = 0\) yields the non-zero x-intercept \(x = -\frac{9}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero x-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -2x^2 + 7x\).
qs.s: Set \(g(x) = 0\) to get \(-x(2x - 7) = 0\), which gives \(x = 0\) or \(2x - 7 = 0\). Solving \(2x - 7 = 0\) yields the non-zero x-intercept \(x = \frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero x-intercept of the quadratic function \(m(x) = -6x^2 + 5x\).
qs.s: Set \(m(x) = 0\) to get \(-x(6x - 5) = 0\), which gives \(x = 0\) or \(6x - 5 = 0\). Solving \(6x - 5 = 0\) yields the non-zero x-intercept \(x = \frac{5}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = 2\left(x - \frac{1}{4}\right)^2 - \frac{9}{8}\).
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) yields \(\left(x - \frac{1}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{16}\), so \(x - \frac{1}{4} = \pm\frac{3}{4}\). This gives intercepts \(x = 1\) and \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\), with \(-\frac{1}{2}\) being the smaller.

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 11x - 4\).
qs.s: Set \(f(x) = 0\) to get \(3x^2 - 11x - 4 = (3x + 1)(x - 4) = 0\), giving intercepts \(x = -\frac{1}{3}\) and \(x = 4\). The smaller x-intercept is \(-\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(k(x) = 4x^2 - 12x + 5\).
qs.s: Set \(k(x) = 0\) to get \((2x - 1)(2x - 5) = 0\), giving intercepts \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = \frac{5}{2}\). The greater x-intercept is \(\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -6x^2 + x + 2\).
qs.s: Set \(g(x) = 0\) to get \(-(2x + 1)(3x - 2) = 0\), which gives intercepts \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = \frac{2}{3}\). The greater x-intercept is \frac{2}{3}.

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(p(x) = (2x - 3)(x + 1) - 12\).
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying gives \(p(x) = 2x^2 - x - 15 = (2x + 5)(x - 3) = 0\). The intercepts are \(x = -\frac{5}{2}\) and \(x = 3\), so the smaller x-intercept is \(-\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(p(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 4x + \frac{11}{2}\)?
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(p(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x - 4)^2 - \frac{5}{2}\). Setting \(p(x) = 0\) yields \((x - 4)^2 = 5\), so \(x = 4 \pm \sqrt{5}\), and the smaller \(x\)-intercept is \(4 - \sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: What is the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 2x + \frac{3}{2}\)?
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 2)^2 + \frac{7}{2}\). Setting \(f(x) = 0\) yields \((x - 2)^2 = 7\), so \(x = 2 \pm \sqrt{7}\), and the greater \(x\)-intercept is \(2 + \sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: What is the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(q(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 - 4x - \frac{5}{2}\)?
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(q(x) = -\frac{1}{2}(x + 4)^2 + \frac{11}{2}\). Setting \(q(x) = 0\) yields \((x + 4)^2 = 11\), so \(x = -4 \pm \sqrt{11}\), and the greater \(x\)-intercept is \(-4 + \sqrt{11}\).

qs.q: What is the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 + 3x + \frac{5}{2}\)?
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(g(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x + 3)^2 - 2\). Setting \(g(x) = 0\) yields \((x + 3)^2 = 4\), so \(x = -3 \pm 2\), which gives the smaller \(x\)-intercept \(x = -5\).

qs.q: What is the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{3}x^2 + 2x - \frac{5}{3}\)?
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{3}(x - 3)^2 + \frac{4}{3}\). Setting \(h(x) = 0\) yields \((x - 3)^2 = 4\), so \(x = 3 \pm 2\), and the greater \(x\)-intercept is \(5\).

qs.q: What is the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(q(x) = -\frac{1}{4}x^2 - \frac{1}{6}x + \frac{2}{3}\)?
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(q(x) = -\frac{1}{4}\left(x + \frac{1}{3}\right)^2 + \frac{25}{36}\). Setting \(q(x) = 0\) yields \(\left(x + \frac{1}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{9}\), so \(x = -\frac{1}{3} \pm \frac{5}{3}\), giving the smaller \(x\)-intercept \(-2\).

qs.q: What is the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = \frac{3}{4}x^2 + \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{5}{4}\)?
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(h(x) = \frac{3}{4}\left(x + \frac{1}{3}\right)^2 - \frac{4}{3}\). Setting \(h(x) = 0\) yields \(\left(x + \frac{1}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{16}{9}\), so \(x = -\frac{1}{3} \pm \frac{4}{3}\), giving the smaller \(x\)-intercept \(-\frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: What is the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -\frac{2}{3}x^2 + \frac{2}{3}x + \frac{4}{3}\)?
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -\frac{2}{3}\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{3}{2}\). Setting \(f(x) = 0\) yields \(\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}\), so \(x = \frac{1}{2} \pm \frac{3}{2}\), and the greater \(x\)-intercept is \(2\).

qs.q: What is the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(p(x) = -\frac{1}{3}x^2 + \frac{5}{3}x - \frac{11}{12}\)?
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(p(x) = -\frac{1}{3}\left(x - \frac{5}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{7}{6}\). Setting \(p(x) = 0\) yields \(\left(x - \frac{5}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{7}{2}\), so \(x = \frac{5}{2} \pm \frac{\sqrt{14}}{2} = \frac{5 \pm \sqrt{14}}{2}\), and the greater \(x\)-intercept is \(\frac{5 + \sqrt{14}}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 - \frac{3}{2}x + \frac{1}{8}\)?
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(g(x) = -\frac{1}{2}\left(x + \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{5}{4}\). Setting \(g(x) = 0\) yields \(\left(x + \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{5}{2}\), so \(x = -\frac{3}{2} \pm \frac{\sqrt{10}}{2} = \frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{10}}{2}\), and the greater \(x\)-intercept is \(\frac{-3 + \sqrt{10}}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(q(x) = -0.4x^2 + 6\)?
qs.s: Setting \(q(x) = 0\) gives \(-0.4x^2 + 6 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 = 15\). Taking the positive square root yields \(x = \sqrt{15}\).

qs.q: What is the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -0.5x^2 + 1\)?
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \(-0.5x^2 + 1 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 = 2\). Taking the positive square root yields \(x = \sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: What is the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = -0.5x^2 + 8\)?
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) gives \(-0.5x^2 + 8 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 = 16\). Taking the positive square root yields \(x = 4\).

qs.q: What is the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -0.2x^2 + 2\)?
qs.s: Setting \(g(x) = 0\) gives \(-0.2x^2 + 2 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 = 10\). Taking the positive square root yields \(x = \sqrt{10}\).

qs.q: What is the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(p(x) = -0.5x^2 + 3\)?
qs.s: Setting \(p(x) = 0\) gives \(-0.5x^2 + 3 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 = 6\). Taking the positive square root yields \(x = \sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: What is the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(q(x) = -2x^2 + 4x + 4\)?
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(q(x) = -2(x - 1)^2 + 6\). Setting \(q(x) = 0\) gives \((x - 1)^2 = 3\), which gives \(x = 1 \pm \sqrt{3}\), so the positive \(x\)-intercept is \(1 + \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: What is the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = -0.5x^2 - x + 4\)?
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) and multiplying by \(-2\) gives \(x^2 + 2x - 8 = 0\), which factors as \((x + 4)(x - 2) = 0\). The roots are \(x = -4\) and \(x = 2\), so the positive \(x\)-intercept is \(2\).

qs.q: What is the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -x^2 + 4x + 1\)?
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(g(x) = -(x - 2)^2 + 5\). Setting \(g(x) = 0\) yields \((x - 2)^2 = 5\), which gives \(x = 2 \pm \sqrt{5}\), so the positive \(x\)-intercept is \(2 + \sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: What is the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(p(x) = -0.2x^2 + 0.8x + 1\)?
qs.s: Setting \(p(x) = 0\) and multiplying by \(-5\) yields \(x^2 - 4x - 5 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 5)(x + 1) = 0\). The roots are \(x = 5\) and \(x = -1\), so the positive \(x\)-intercept is \(5\).

qs.q: What is the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 3x + 5\)?
qs.s: Setting \(f(x) = 0\) gives \(2x^2 - 3x - 5 = 0\), which factors as \((2x - 5)(x + 1) = 0\). The roots are \(x = \frac{5}{2}\) and \(x = -1\), so the positive \(x\)-intercept is \(\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the lesser x-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = 3x^2 + 2\sqrt{2}x - 2\).
qs.s: Setting \(3x^2 + 2\sqrt{2}x - 2 = 0\), the quadratic formula yields \(x = \frac{-2\sqrt{2} \pm \sqrt{8 + 24}}{6} = \frac{-2\sqrt{2} \pm 4\sqrt{2}}{6}\). The lesser x-intercept is \(\frac{-6\sqrt{2}}{6} = -\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(p(x) = 10x^2 - 3\sqrt{5}x - 5\).
qs.s: Setting \(10x^2 - 3\sqrt{5}x - 5 = 0\), the discriminant is \(D = 45 + 200 = 245 = (7\sqrt{5})^2\), giving \(x = \frac{3\sqrt{5} \pm 7\sqrt{5}}{20}\). The greater x-intercept is \(\frac{10\sqrt{5}}{20} = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the positive x-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = 4x^2 - \sqrt{2}x - 3\).
qs.s: Setting \(4x^2 - \sqrt{2}x - 3 = 0\), the discriminant is \(D = 2 - 4(4)(-3) = 50\), giving roots \(x = \frac{\sqrt{2} \pm 5\sqrt{2}}{8}\). The positive x-intercept is \(\frac{6\sqrt{2}}{8} = \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the lesser x-intercept of the quadratic function \(q(x) = 12x^2 - 5\sqrt{3}x - 6\).
qs.s: Setting \(12x^2 - 5\sqrt{3}x - 6 = 0\), the discriminant is \(D = 75 + 288 = 363 = (11\sqrt{3})^2\), giving \(x = \frac{5\sqrt{3} \pm 11\sqrt{3}}{24}\). The lesser x-intercept is \(\frac{-6\sqrt{3}}{24} = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 2x^2 - \sqrt{3}x - 3\).
qs.s: Setting \(2x^2 - \sqrt{3}x - 3 = 0\), the quadratic formula gives \(x = \frac{\sqrt{3} \pm \sqrt{3 + 24}}{4} = \frac{\sqrt{3} \pm 3\sqrt{3}}{4}\). The greater x-intercept is \(\frac{4\sqrt{3}}{4} = \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(f(x) = \sqrt{2}x^2 - 5x + 3\sqrt{2}\).
qs.s: Setting \(\sqrt{2}x^2 - 5x + 3\sqrt{2} = 0\), the discriminant is \(D = 25 - 4(\sqrt{2})(3\sqrt{2}) = 1\), giving \(x = \frac{5 \pm 1}{2\sqrt{2}}\). The greater root is \(\frac{6}{2\sqrt{2}} = \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the lesser x-intercept of the quadratic function \(k(x) = 2\sqrt{6}x^2 + x - \sqrt{6}\).
qs.s: Setting \(2\sqrt{6}x^2 + x - \sqrt{6} = 0\), the discriminant is \(D = 1 - 4(2\sqrt{6})(-\sqrt{6}) = 49\), giving \(x = \frac{-1 \pm 7}{4\sqrt{6}}\). The lesser root simplifies to \(\frac{-8}{4\sqrt{6}} = -\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} = -\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the positive x-intercept of the quadratic function \(m(x) = (2x - \sqrt{7})^2 + \sqrt{7}x - 14\).
qs.s: Expanding and collecting terms gives \(m(x) = 4x^2 - 3\sqrt{7}x - 7\). Setting \(m(x) = 0\) yields \(x = \frac{3\sqrt{7} \pm \sqrt{63 + 112}}{8} = \frac{3\sqrt{7} \pm 5\sqrt{7}}{8}\), so the positive x-intercept is \(\frac{8\sqrt{7}}{8} = \sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(h(x) = 3\sqrt{5}x^2 - 7x - 2\sqrt{5}\).
qs.s: Setting \(3\sqrt{5}x^2 - 7x - 2\sqrt{5} = 0\), the discriminant is \(D = 49 - 4(3\sqrt{5})(-2\sqrt{5}) = 169 = 13^2\), giving \(x = \frac{7 \pm 13}{6\sqrt{5}}\). Rationalizing the greater root gives \(\frac{20}{6\sqrt{5}} = \frac{2\sqrt{5}}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the lesser x-intercept of the quadratic function \(g(x) = 2(x + \sqrt{3})^2 - \sqrt{3}x - 12\).
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying gives \(g(x) = 2x^2 + 3\sqrt{3}x - 6\). Setting this to 0 yields \(x = \frac{-3\sqrt{3} \pm \sqrt{27 + 48}}{4} = \frac{-3\sqrt{3} \pm 5\sqrt{3}}{4}\), so the lesser x-intercept is \(\frac{-8\sqrt{3}}{4} = -2\sqrt{3}\).

exercises.name: Graphing and analyzing a quadratic function

qs.q: What is the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -x^2 - 2x\)?
qs.s: Complete the square by factoring out \(-1\): \(f(x) = -(x^2 + 2x + 1) + 1 = -(x + 1)^2 + 1\). The vertex is \((-1, 1)\).

qs.q: What is the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -x^2 + 6x\)?
qs.s: Complete the square by factoring out \(-1\): \(f(x) = -(x^2 - 6x + 9) + 9 = -(x - 3)^2 + 9\). The vertex is \((3, 9)\).

qs.q: What is the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -x^2 + 10x\)?
qs.s: Complete the square by factoring out \(-1\): \(f(x) = -(x^2 - 10x + 25) + 25 = -(x - 5)^2 + 25\). The vertex is \((5, 25)\).

qs.q: What is the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 - 8x\)?
qs.s: Complete the square: \(f(x) = (x^2 - 8x + 16) - 16 = (x - 4)^2 - 16\). The vertex is \((4, -16)\).

qs.q: What is the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -x^2 + 14x - 40\)?
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) from the variable terms and complete the square: \(f(x) = -(x^2 - 14x + 49) + 49 - 40 = -(x - 7)^2 + 9\). The vertex is \((7, 9)\).

qs.q: What is the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + 7\)?
qs.s: Factor out \(3\) from the variable terms and complete the square: \(f(x) = 3(x^2 - 4x + 4) - 12 + 7 = 3(x - 2)^2 - 5\). The vertex is \((2, -5)\).

qs.q: What is the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 8x - 3\)?
qs.s: Factor out \(-2\) from the variable terms and complete the square: \(f(x) = -2(x^2 - 4x + 4) + 8 - 3 = -2(x - 2)^2 + 5\). The vertex is \((2, 5)\).

qs.q: What is the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 4x - 1\)?
qs.s: Factor out \(-\frac{1}{2}\) from the variable terms and complete the square: \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 8x + 16) + 8 - 1 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4)^2 + 7\). The vertex is \((4, 7)\).

qs.q: What is the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 6x + 5\)?
qs.s: Factor out \(2\) from the variable terms and complete the square: \(f(x) = 2(x^2 - 3x + \frac{9}{4}) - \frac{9}{2} + 5 = 2(x - \frac{3}{2})^2 + \frac{1}{2}\). The vertex is \((3/2, 1/2)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 + 6x + 2\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = (x^2 + 6x + 9) - 9 + 2 = (x + 3)^2 - 7\), so the vertex is \((-3, -7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -x^2 + 2x + 8\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -(x^2 - 2x + 1) + 1 + 8 = -(x - 1)^2 + 9\), so the vertex is \((1, 9)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -x^2 - 6x - 5\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -(x^2 + 6x + 9) + 9 - 5 = -(x + 3)^2 + 4\), so the vertex is \((-3, 4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 - 4x - 5\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = (x^2 - 4x + 4) - 4 - 5 = (x - 2)^2 - 9\), so the vertex is \((2, -9)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -x^2 - 8x - 12\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -(x^2 + 8x + 16) + 16 - 12 = -(x + 4)^2 + 4\), so the vertex is \((-4, 4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -(x - 3)(x + 1) + 2x - 4\).
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms yields \(f(x) = -x^2 + 4x - 1\), which completes to \(-(x - 2)^2 + 3\), so the vertex is \((2, 3)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 4x - 3\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(-\frac{1}{2}\) from the variable terms and completing the square yields \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 8x + 16) + 8 - 3 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4)^2 + 5\), so the vertex is \((4, 5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 6x - 1\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(-2\) and completing the square yields \(f(x) = -2\left(x^2 - 3x + \frac{9}{4}\right) + \frac{9}{2} - 1 = -2\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{7}{2}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, \frac{7}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -4x^2 + 40x - 87\).
Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 11 + 8x - 2x^2\).
qs.s: Rewriting in standard form gives \(f(x) = -2(x^2 - 4x + 4) + 8 + 11 = -2(x - 2)^2 + 19\), so the vertex is \((2, 19)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(k(x) = x^2 + 4x + 7\).
qs.s: Complete the square by writing \(k(x) = (x^2 + 4x + 4) + 7 - 4 = (x + 2)^2 + 3\). The vertex is \((h, k) = (-2, 3)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 11\).
qs.s: Complete the square by writing \(f(x) = (x^2 - 6x + 9) + 11 - 9 = (x - 3)^2 + 2\). In standard form \(f(x) = (x - h)^2 + k\), the vertex is \((h, k) = (3, 2)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(g(x) = x^2 + 8x + 12\).
qs.s: Complete the square to obtain \(g(x) = (x^2 + 8x + 16) + 12 - 16 = (x + 4)^2 - 4\). Comparing to standard form \(g(x) = (x - h)^2 + k\), the vertex is \((-4, -4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(m(x) = x^2 - 10x + 21\).
qs.s: Complete the square to get \(m(x) = (x^2 - 10x + 25) + 21 - 25 = (x - 5)^2 - 4\). Therefore, the vertex is \((5, -4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(p(x) = x^2 - 2x - 5\).
qs.s: Rewrite the function as \(p(x) = (x^2 - 2x + 1) - 5 - 1 = (x - 1)^2 - 6\). Thus, the vertex of the parabola is \((1, -6)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 12x + 11\).
qs.s: Factor 2 from the variable terms to get \(f(x) = 2(x^2 - 6x) + 11\), then complete the square: \(f(x) = 2(x^2 - 6x + 9) + 11 - 18 = 2(x - 3)^2 - 7\). The vertex is \((3, -7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(q(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 6x - 10\).
qs.s: Factor \(-\frac{1}{2}\) from the first two terms to get \(q(x) = -\frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 12x) - 10\), then complete the square: \(q(x) = -\frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 12x + 36) - 10 + 18 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 6)^2 + 8\). The vertex is \((6, 8)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -3x^2 - 12x - 5\).
qs.s: Factor \(-3\) from the \(x\)-terms to obtain \(g(x) = -3(x^2 + 4x) - 5 = -3(x^2 + 4x + 4) - 5 + 12 = -3(x + 2)^2 + 7\). The vertex is \((-2, 7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(h(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 4x + 3\).
qs.s: Factor \(\frac{1}{2}\) from the variable terms to get \(h(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 8x) + 3\), then complete the square: \(h(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 8x + 16) + 3 - 8 = \frac{1}{2}(x - 4)^2 - 5\). The vertex is \((4, -5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(p(x) = 2x^2 - 6x + 1\).
qs.s: Factor 2 from the variable terms to get \(p(x) = 2(x^2 - 3x) + 1\), then complete the square: \(p(x) = 2\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 + 1 - \frac{9}{2} = 2\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 - \frac{7}{2}\). The vertex is \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{7}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(p(x) = 2x^2 - 12x + 14\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(p(x) = 2(x^2 - 6x + 9) - 18 + 14 = 2(x - 3)^2 - 4\). Thus, the vertex is \((3, -4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(g(x) = 3x^2 + 6x - 2\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(g(x) = 3(x^2 + 2x + 1) - 3 - 2 = 3(x + 1)^2 - 5\). Thus, the vertex is \((-1, -5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 8x - 7\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -2(x^2 - 4x + 4) + 8 - 7 = -2(x - 2)^2 + 1\). Thus, the vertex is \((2, 1)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(h(x) = -3x^2 - 12x - 8\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(h(x) = -3(x^2 + 4x + 4) + 12 - 8 = -3(x + 2)^2 + 4\). Thus, the vertex is \((-2, 4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(q(x) = -4x^2 + 8x + 2\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(q(x) = -4(x^2 - 2x + 1) + 4 + 2 = -4(x - 1)^2 + 6\). Thus, the vertex is \((1, 6)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(p(x) = 3(x - 2)(x + 4) - 2x + 5\).
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying gives \(p(x) = 3x^2 + 4x - 19\). Completing the square gives \(3\left(x + \frac{2}{3}\right)^2 - \frac{4}{3} - 19 = 3\left(x + \frac{2}{3}\right)^2 - \frac{61}{3}\), so the vertex is \(\left(-\frac{2}{3}, -\frac{61}{3}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(q(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 3x - 2\).
qs.s: Factoring \(-\frac{1}{2}\) from the variable terms gives \(q(x) = -\frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 6x + 9) + \frac{9}{2} - 2 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 3)^2 + \frac{5}{2}\). Thus, the vertex is \(\left(3, \frac{5}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(h(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 3x + 4\).
qs.s: Factoring \(\frac{1}{2}\) from the variable terms gives \(h(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 6x + 9) - \frac{9}{2} + 4 = \frac{1}{2}(x - 3)^2 - \frac{1}{2}\). Thus, the vertex is \(\left(3, -\frac{1}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -2x^2 + 6x - 5\).
qs.s: Completing the square yields \(g(x) = -2\left(x^2 - 3x + \frac{9}{4}\right) + \frac{9}{2} - 5 = -2\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{2}\). Thus, the vertex is \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(k(x) = -x^2 - 4x\).
qs.s: Factor \(-1\) to get \(-(x^2 + 4x)\), then complete the square by adding and subtracting \(4\) to obtain \(-(x + 2)^2 + 4\). The vertex is \((-2, 4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(g(x) = 2x - x^2\).
qs.s: Rewrite \(g(x)\) in standard form as \(-(x^2 - 2x + 1) + 1 = -(x - 1)^2 + 1\). Thus, the vertex of the parabola is \((1, 1)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 5x - x^2\).
qs.s: Rewrite \(f(x)\) as \(-(x^2 - 5x)\) and complete the square by adding and subtracting \((5/2)^2 = 25/4\) inside to obtain \(f(x) = -\left(x - \frac{5}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{25}{4}\). Therefore, the vertex is \(\left(\frac{5}{2}, \frac{25}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(h(x) = -x^2 + 6x\).
qs.s: Factor \(-1\) from the terms to get \(-(x^2 - 6x)\), then complete the square to obtain \(-(x - 3)^2 + 9\). The vertex is \((3, 9)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(p(x) = x - x^2\).
qs.s: Rewrite \(p(x)\) as \(-(x^2 - x)\) and complete the square to get \(-\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{1}{4}\). Thus, the vertex is \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(q(x) = 2x^2 - 5x + 1\).
qs.s: Factor \(2\) from the variable terms to write \(2\left(x^2 - \frac{5}{2}x\right) + 1\), then complete the square to obtain \(2\left(x - \frac{5}{4}\right)^2 - \frac{25}{8} + 1 = 2\left(x - \frac{5}{4}\right)^2 - \frac{17}{8}\). The vertex is \(\left(\frac{5}{4}, -\frac{17}{8}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(h(x) = 2x^2 - 6x + 1\).
qs.s: Factor \(2\) from the variable terms to get \(2\left(x^2 - 3x\right) + 1\), then complete the square to obtain \(2\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 - \frac{9}{2} + 1 = 2\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 - \frac{7}{2}\). The vertex is \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{7}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2x^2 - 4x + 3\).
qs.s: Factor \(-2\) from the variable terms to get \(-2(x^2 + 2x) + 3\), then complete the square inside to obtain \(-2(x + 1)^2 + 2 + 3 = -2(x + 1)^2 + 5\). Therefore, the vertex is \((-1, 5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(p(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 4x - 1\).
qs.s: Factor \(-\frac{1}{2}\) from the variable terms to obtain \(-\frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 8x) - 1\), then complete the square to get \(-\frac{1}{2}(x - 4)^2 + 8 - 1 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4)^2 + 7\). The vertex is \((4, 7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(g(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + 7\).
qs.s: Factor \(3\) from the first two terms to get \(3(x^2 - 4x) + 7\), and complete the square to get \(3(x - 2)^2 - 12 + 7 = 3(x - 2)^2 - 5\). Hence, the vertex is \((2, -5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(r(x) = -2x^2 - 4x + 5\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(r(x) = -2(x^2 + 2x + 1) + 5 + 2 = -2(x + 1)^2 + 7\). Thus, the vertex is \((-1, 7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(h(x) = -3x^2 - 6x + 1\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(h(x) = -3(x^2 + 2x + 1) + 1 + 3 = -3(x + 1)^2 + 4\). Thus, the vertex is \((-1, 4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 12x - 10\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -2(x^2 - 6x + 9) - 10 + 18 = -2(x - 3)^2 + 8\). Thus, the vertex is \((3, 8)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(p(x) = 2x^2 - 8x - 1\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(p(x) = 2(x^2 - 4x + 4) - 1 - 8 = 2(x - 2)^2 - 9\). Thus, the vertex is \((2, -9)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(m(x) = -3x^2 + 36x - 97\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(m(x) = -3(x^2 - 12x + 36) - 97 + 108 = -3(x - 6)^2 + 11\). Thus, the vertex is \((6, 11)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(k(x) = -3x^2 + 4x + 1\).
qs.s: Factoring \(-3\) and completing the square gives \(k(x) = -3\left(x^2 - \frac{4}{3}x + \frac{4}{9}\right) + 1 + \frac{4}{3} = -3\left(x - \frac{2}{3}\right)^2 + \frac{7}{3}\). Thus, the vertex is \(\left(\frac{2}{3}, \frac{7}{3}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(h(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 6x + 11\).
qs.s: Factoring \(\frac{1}{2}\) from the variable terms and completing the square gives \(h(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 12x + 36) + 11 - 18 = \frac{1}{2}(x - 6)^2 - 7\). Thus, the vertex is \((6, -7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -2(x + 1)(x - 5) - 4x + 7\).
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms yields \(g(x) = -2x^2 + 4x + 17\). Completing the square gives \(g(x) = -2(x - 1)^2 + 19\), so the vertex is \((1, 19)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 6x - 1\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -2\left(x^2 - 3x + \frac{9}{4}\right) - 1 + \frac{9}{2} = -2\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{7}{2}\). Thus, the vertex is \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, \frac{7}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(k(x) = 3x^2 + 6x + 2\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(k(x) = 3(x^2 + 2x + 1) - 3 + 2 = 3(x + 1)^2 - 1\). Therefore, the vertex is \((-1, -1)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 8x - 3\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -2(x^2 - 4x + 4) + 8 - 3 = -2(x - 2)^2 + 5\). Therefore, the vertex is \((2, 5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(h(x) = 2x^2 - 8x + 1\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(h(x) = 2(x^2 - 4x + 4) - 8 + 1 = 2(x - 2)^2 - 7\). Therefore, the vertex is \((2, -7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(p(x) = -4x^2 + 24x - 32\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(p(x) = -4(x^2 - 6x + 9) + 36 - 32 = -4(x - 3)^2 + 4\). Therefore, the vertex is \((3, 4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2(x + 1)(x - 5) + 4x - 3\).
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms yields \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 12x + 7\). Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -2(x - 3)^2 + 25\), so the vertex is \((3, 25)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(m(x) = -2(x - 5)^2 + 8(x - 1) + 7\).
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying gives \(m(x) = -2x^2 + 28x - 51\). Completing the square gives \(m(x) = -2(x - 7)^2 + 47\), so the vertex is \((7, 47)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(p(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 6x + 11\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(\frac{1}{2}\) and completing the square gives \(p(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 12x + 36) - 18 + 11 = \frac{1}{2}(x - 6)^2 - 7\). Thus, the vertex is \((6, -7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(h(x) = -x^2 + 5x - 2\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(h(x) = -\left(x^2 - 5x + \frac{25}{4}\right) + \frac{25}{4} - 2 = -\left(x - \frac{5}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{17}{4}\). Thus, the vertex is \(\left(\frac{5}{2}, \frac{17}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the quadratic function \(g(x) = 2x^2 - 6x + 7\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(g(x) = 2\left(x^2 - 3x + \frac{9}{4}\right) - \frac{9}{2} + 7 = 2\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{5}{2}\). Thus, the vertex is \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, \frac{5}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 4x + 5\).
qs.s: Factor \(\frac{1}{2}\) from the variable terms to get \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 8x) + 5\), then complete the square to write \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x - 4)^2 - 3\). The vertex is \((4, -3)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(k(x) = -\frac{1}{3}x^2 + 4x - 7\).
qs.s: Factor \(-\frac{1}{3}\) from the variable terms to get \(k(x) = -\frac{1}{3}(x^2 - 12x) - 7\), then complete the square to write \(k(x) = -\frac{1}{3}(x - 6)^2 + 5\). The vertex is \((6, 5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(h(x) = \frac{1}{3}x^2 + 2x - 1\).
qs.s: Factor \(\frac{1}{3}\) from the variable terms to get \(h(x) = \frac{1}{3}(x^2 + 6x) - 1\), then complete the square to write \(h(x) = \frac{1}{3}(x + 3)^2 - 4\). The vertex is \((-3, -4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 - 2x + 3\).
qs.s: Factor \(-\frac{1}{2}\) from the variable terms to get \(g(x) = -\frac{1}{2}(x^2 + 4x) + 3\), then complete the square to write \(g(x) = -\frac{1}{2}(x + 2)^2 + 5\). The vertex is \((-2, 5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(p(x) = -\frac{1}{4}x^2 + 2x - 2\).
qs.s: Factor \(-\frac{1}{4}\) from the variable terms to get \(p(x) = -\frac{1}{4}(x^2 - 8x) - 2\), then complete the square to write \(p(x) = -\frac{1}{4}(x - 4)^2 + 2\). The vertex is \((4, 2)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{3}x^2 + 16x - 175\).
qs.s: Factor \(-\frac{1}{3}\) from the variable terms to write \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{3}(x^2 - 48x) - 175\), then complete the square with \(24^2 = 576\) to obtain \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{3}(x - 24)^2 + 17\). The vertex is \((24, 17)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(q(x) = -\frac{1}{3}x^2 - 3x - 2\).
qs.s: Factor \(-\frac{1}{3}\) from the variable terms to get \(q(x) = -\frac{1}{3}(x^2 + 9x) - 2\), then complete the square with \((\frac{9}{2})^2 = \frac{81}{4}\) to obtain \(q(x) = -\frac{1}{3}(x + \frac{9}{2})^2 + \frac{19}{4}\). The vertex is \((-\frac{9}{2}, \frac{19}{4})\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(g(x) = -\frac{1}{2}(x + 2)(x - 6) - x + 1\).
qs.s: Expand and simplify the function to general form \(g(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + x + 7\), then complete the square to obtain \(g(x) = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 1)^2 + \frac{15}{2}\). The vertex is \((1, \frac{15}{2})\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(p(x) = -\frac{2}{5}x^2 + 2x + 3\).
qs.s: Factor \(-\frac{2}{5}\) from the variable terms to write \(p(x) = -\frac{2}{5}(x^2 - 5x) + 3\), then complete the square with \((\frac{5}{2})^2 = \frac{25}{4}\) to obtain \(p(x) = -\frac{2}{5}(x - \frac{5}{2})^2 + \frac{11}{2}\). The vertex is \((\frac{5}{2}, \frac{11}{2})\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of \(p(x) = |2x^2 - 18|\).
qs.s: The parabola \(y = 2x^2 - 18\) has its vertex at \((0, -18)\). The absolute value reflects this point across the x-axis to \((0, 18)\).

qs.q: Find the positive x-intercept of the graph of \(h(x) = |x^2 - 16|\).
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) yields \(|x^2 - 16| = 0\), so \(x^2 = 16\) and \(x = \pm 4\). The positive x-intercept is \((4, 0)\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the axis of symmetry of the graph of \(k(x) = |x^2 - 49|\).
qs.s: The parabola \(y = x^2 - 49\) is symmetric about the y-axis, \(x = 0\). Reflecting the negative values across the x-axis preserves this line of symmetry, so the axis of symmetry is \(x = 0\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of \(f(x) = |x^2 - 9|\).
qs.s: The parabola \(y = x^2 - 9\) has its vertex at \((0, -9)\). The absolute value reflects the portion below the x-axis upward, so the vertex of the graph is \((0, 9)\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the graph of \(g(x) = |x^2 - 25|\).
qs.s: Evaluating at \(x = 0\) gives \(g(0) = |0^2 - 25| = |-25| = 25\), so the y-intercept is \((0, 25)\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the graph of \(m(x) = |-3(x + 2)^2 + 5|\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 0\) to get \(m(0) = |-3(2)^2 + 5| = |-12 + 5| = |-7| = 7\), giving the y-intercept \((0, 7)\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the axis of symmetry of the graph of \(g(x) = |2x^2 + 12x - 14|\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(2x^2 + 12x - 14 = 2(x + 3)^2 - 32\), so the axis of symmetry passes through the vertex at \(x = -3\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the graph of \(h(x) = |2x^2 - 7x - 4|\).
qs.s: Setting \(|2x^2 - 7x - 4| = 0\) gives \((2x + 1)(x - 4) = 0\), yielding roots \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = 4\). The greater x-intercept is \((4, 0)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of \(k(x) = |2x^2 - 8x - 10|\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(2x^2 - 8x - 10 = 2(x - 2)^2 - 18\), which has vertex \((2, -18)\). The absolute value reflects this point across the x-axis to \((2, 18)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of \(f(x) = |x^2 - 6x - 16|\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(x^2 - 6x - 16 = (x - 3)^2 - 25\), which has a vertex at \((3, -25)\). Applying the absolute value reflects this point across the x-axis to \((3, 25)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the function \(f(x) = |-x^2 + 4x + 5|\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(-x^2 + 4x + 5 = -(x^2 - 4x + 4) + 4 + 5 = -(x - 2)^2 + 9\). Since the maximum value \(9\) is positive, the vertex of the graph is \((2, 9)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the function \(h(x) = |-x^2 + 6x - 5|\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(-x^2 + 6x - 5 = -(x^2 - 6x + 9) + 9 - 5 = -(x - 3)^2 + 4\). Therefore, the vertex of the graph is \((3, 4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the function \(p(x) = |-x^2 - 2x + 8|\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(-x^2 - 2x + 8 = -(x^2 + 2x + 1) + 1 + 8 = -(x + 1)^2 + 9\). Therefore, the vertex of the graph is \((-1, 9)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the function \(g(x) = |-x^2 - 4x + 5|\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(-x^2 - 4x + 5 = -(x^2 + 4x + 4) + 4 + 5 = -(x + 2)^2 + 9\). Therefore, the vertex of the graph is \((-2, 9)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the function \(q(x) = |-x^2 + 8x - 12|\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(-x^2 + 8x - 12 = -(x^2 - 8x + 16) + 16 - 12 = -(x - 4)^2 + 4\). Therefore, the vertex of the graph is \((4, 4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the function \(f(x) = |-2x^2 + 8x + 10|\).
qs.s: Factoring \(-2\) from the variable terms and completing the square yields \(-2(x^2 - 4x + 4) + 8 + 10 = -2(x - 2)^2 + 18\). The vertex of the graph is \((2, 18)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the function \(g(x) = |-3x^2 - 18x - 15|\).
qs.s: Factoring \(-3\) and completing the square gives \(-3(x^2 + 6x + 9) + 27 - 15 = -3(x + 3)^2 + 12\). The vertex of the graph is \((-3, 12)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the function \(h(x) = |-x^2 + 5x - 4|\).
qs.s: Completing the square yields \(-(x^2 - 5x + \frac{25}{4}) + \frac{25}{4} - 4 = -(x - \frac{5}{2})^2 + \frac{9}{4}\). The vertex of the graph is \((\frac{5}{2}, \frac{9}{4})\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the function \(q(x) = |-2x^2 + 6x + 1|\).
qs.s: Factoring \(-2\) and completing the square yields \(-2(x^2 - 3x + \frac{9}{4}) + \frac{9}{2} + 1 = -2(x - \frac{3}{2})^2 + \frac{11}{2}\). The vertex of the graph is \((\frac{3}{2}, \frac{11}{2})\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the graph of the function \(p(x) = |-\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 4x - 2|\).
qs.s: Factoring \(-\frac{1}{2}\) from the variable terms gives \(-\frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 8x + 16) + 8 - 2 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4)^2 + 6\). The vertex of the graph is \((4, 6)\).

exercises.name: Finding the vertex with literal coefficients

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 - ax - 3\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = \left(x - \frac{a}{2}\right)^2 - 3 - \frac{a^2}{4}\). Therefore, the vertex is \(\left(\frac{a}{2}, -3 - \frac{a^2}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 + bx + 1\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = \left(x + \frac{b}{2}\right)^2 + 1 - \frac{b^2}{4}\). Therefore, the vertex is \(\left(-\frac{b}{2}, 1 - \frac{b^2}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 - kx + 9\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = \left(x - \frac{k}{2}\right)^2 + 9 - \frac{k^2}{4}\). Therefore, the vertex is \(\left(\frac{k}{2}, 9 - \frac{k^2}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 - 2mx + 7\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = (x - m)^2 + 7 - m^2\). Therefore, the vertex is \((m, 7 - m^2)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 + px - 5\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = \left(x + \frac{p}{2}\right)^2 - 5 - \frac{p^2}{4}\). Therefore, the vertex is \(\left(-\frac{p}{2}, -5 - \frac{p^2}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -3x^2 + kx - 2\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(-3\) gives \(f(x) = -3\left(x^2 - \frac{k}{3}x + \frac{k^2}{36}\right) - 2 + \frac{k^2}{12} = -3\left(x - \frac{k}{6}\right)^2 + \frac{k^2}{12} - 2\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{k}{6}, \frac{k^2}{12} - 2\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - bx + 6\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(\frac{1}{2}\) gives \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 2bx + b^2) + 6 - \frac{b^2}{2} = \frac{1}{2}(x - b)^2 + 6 - \frac{b^2}{2}\), so the vertex is \(\left(b, 6 - \frac{b^2}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 8mx + c\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(-2\) gives \(f(x) = -2(x^2 - 4mx + 4m^2) + c + 8m^2 = -2(x - 2m)^2 + 8m^2 + c\), so the vertex is \((2m, 8m^2 + c)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -x^2 + kx - 3\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(-1\) and completing the square gives \(f(x) = -\left(x - \frac{k}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{k^2}{4} - 3\). Therefore, the vertex is \(\left(\frac{k}{2}, \frac{k^2}{4} - 3\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 2x^2 + kx + 1\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(2\) gives \(f(x) = 2\left(x^2 + \frac{k}{2}x + \frac{k^2}{16}\right) + 1 - \frac{k^2}{8} = 2\left(x + \frac{k}{4}\right)^2 + 1 - \frac{k^2}{8}\), so the vertex is \(\left(-\frac{k}{4}, 1 - \frac{k^2}{8}\right)\).

exercises.name: Finding the vertex with literal coefficients

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(p(x) = x^2 - 5kx + 2k^2\).
qs.s: Completing the square yields \(p(x) = \left(x - \frac{5k}{2}\right)^2 - \frac{17k^2}{4}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{5k}{2}, -\frac{17k^2}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(h(x) = -2x^2 + 4kx + k^2\).
qs.s: Completing the square yields \(h(x) = -2(x - k)^2 + 3k^2\), so the vertex is \((k, 3k^2)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(q(x) = 3x^2 - 4kx + 2k^2\).
qs.s: Rewriting in standard form gives \(q(x) = 3\left(x - \frac{2k}{3}\right)^2 + \frac{2k^2}{3}\), which gives the vertex \(\left(\frac{2k}{3}, \frac{2k^2}{3}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 6kx + k^2\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = 2\left(x - \frac{3k}{2}\right)^2 - \frac{7k^2}{2}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{3k}{2}, -\frac{7k^2}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(g(x) = 3x^2 + 2kx - k^2\).
qs.s: Writing in standard form gives \(g(x) = 3\left(x + \frac{k}{3}\right)^2 - \frac{4k^2}{3}\), which gives the vertex \(\left(-\frac{k}{3}, -\frac{4k^2}{3}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(f(x) = -4x^2 + 7kx - 5k^2\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -4\left(x - \frac{7k}{8}\right)^2 - \frac{31k^2}{16}\), hence the vertex is \(\left(\frac{7k}{8}, -\frac{31k^2}{16}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(q(x) = -2(x - 3k)(x + k) - 5kx + 3k^2\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(q(x) = -2x^2 - kx + 9k^2 = -2\left(x + \frac{k}{4}\right)^2 + \frac{73k^2}{8}\), giving the vertex \(\left(-\frac{k}{4}, \frac{73k^2}{8}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(p(x) = 3(x - 2k)^2 - 2(x + k)^2 + k^2\).
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying yields \(p(x) = x^2 - 16kx + 11k^2 = (x - 8k)^2 - 53k^2\), which gives the vertex \((8k, -53k^2)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(g(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - \frac{3}{4}kx + 2k^2\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(\frac{1}{2}\) and completing the square yields \(g(x) = \frac{1}{2}\left(x - \frac{3k}{4}\right)^2 + \frac{55k^2}{32}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{3k}{4}, \frac{55k^2}{32}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(h(x) = (2x + 3k)(x - k) + 5kx - k^2\).
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms gives \(h(x) = 2x^2 + 6kx - 4k^2 = 2\left(x + \frac{3k}{2}\right)^2 - \frac{17k^2}{2}\), so the vertex is \(\left(-\frac{3k}{2}, -\frac{17k^2}{2}\right)\).

exercises.name: Finding the vertex with literal coefficients

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(f(x) = 2x^2 - ax + c^2\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(h = -\frac{-a}{2(2)} = \frac{a}{4}\), and substituting gives \(k = 2\left(\frac{a}{4}\right)^2 - a\left(\frac{a}{4}\right) + c^2 = c^2 - \frac{a^2}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(f(x) = 2x^2 + 3mx + n^2\).
qs.s: Writing in standard form, \(f(x) = 2\left(x + \frac{3m}{4}\right)^2 - 2\left(\frac{9m^2}{16}\right) + n^2 = 2\left(x + \frac{3m}{4}\right)^2 + n^2 - \frac{9m^2}{8}\), giving the vertex \(\left(-\frac{3m}{4}, n^2 - \frac{9m^2}{8}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(g(x) = 3x^2 + bx - c^2\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(g(x) = 3\left(x + \frac{b}{6}\right)^2 - 3\left(\frac{b^2}{36}\right) - c^2 = 3\left(x + \frac{b}{6}\right)^2 - c^2 - \frac{b^2}{12}\), so the vertex is \(\left(-\frac{b}{6}, -c^2 - \frac{b^2}{12}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(h(x) = 4x^2 - px + q^2\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{-p}{2(4)} = \frac{p}{8}\), and substituting gives \(y = 4\left(\frac{p^2}{64}\right) - \frac{p^2}{8} + q^2 = q^2 - \frac{p^2}{16}\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(p(x) = -2x^2 + kx + m^2\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(h = -\frac{k}{2(-2)} = \frac{k}{4}\), and evaluating \(p\left(\frac{k}{4}\right) = -2\left(\frac{k^2}{16}\right) + \frac{k^2}{4} + m^2 = m^2 + \frac{k^2}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(f(x) = 2(x + a)^2 - 6ax + b^2\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 2ax + 2a^2 + b^2 = 2\left(x - \frac{a}{2}\right)^2 - \frac{a^2}{2} + 2a^2 + b^2 = 2\left(x - \frac{a}{2}\right)^2 + b^2 + \frac{3a^2}{2}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{a}{2}, b^2 + \frac{3a^2}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(f(x) = -3x^2 + 4ax - 2a^2 + b^2\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(h = -\frac{4a}{2(-3)} = \frac{2a}{3}\); substituting into \(f(x)\) yields \(k = -3\left(\frac{4a^2}{9}\right) + 4a\left(\frac{2a}{3}\right) - 2a^2 + b^2 = b^2 - \frac{2a^2}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(f(x) = 2(x - a)(x + 2a) + b^2\).
qs.s: Expanding yields \(f(x) = 2x^2 + 2ax - 4a^2 + b^2\), which has vertex \(x = -\frac{2a}{2(2)} = -\frac{a}{2}\) and \(y = 2\left(-\frac{3a}{2}\right)\left(\frac{3a}{2}\right) + b^2 = b^2 - \frac{9a^2}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - \frac{a}{3}x + b^2\).
qs.s: Factoring the leading coefficient gives \(\frac{1}{2}\left(x^2 - \frac{2a}{3}x\right) + b^2 = \frac{1}{2}\left(x - \frac{a}{3}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{a^2}{9}\right) + b^2 = \frac{1}{2}\left(x - \frac{a}{3}\right)^2 + b^2 - \frac{a^2}{18}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{a}{3}, b^2 - \frac{a^2}{18}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(g(x) = -\frac{2}{3}x^2 + 2ax - a^2 + b\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(h = -\frac{2a}{2(-2/3)} = \frac{3a}{2}\), and substituting gives \(k = -\frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{9a^2}{4}\right) + 2a\left(\frac{3a}{2}\right) - a^2 + b = -\frac{3a^2}{2} + 2a^2 + b = b + \frac{a^2}{2}\).

exercises.name: Finding the vertex with literal coefficients

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(h(x) = ax^2 + 6x - a\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{6}{2a} = -\frac{3}{a}\). Evaluating \(h\left(-\frac{3}{a}\right)\) yields \(y = a\left(-\frac{3}{a}\right)^2 + 6\left(-\frac{3}{a}\right) - a = -\frac{a^2 + 9}{a}\), so the vertex is \(\left(-\frac{3}{a}, -\frac{a^2 + 9}{a}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(f(x) = cx^2 - x + c\).
qs.s: Using \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), we find \(x = -\frac{-1}{2c} = \frac{1}{2c}\). Substituting into \(f(x)\) gives \(y = c\left(\frac{1}{2c}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{2c} + c = \frac{4c^2 - 1}{4c}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{1}{2c}, \frac{4c^2 - 1}{4c}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(g(x) = px^2 + 8x + p\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{8}{2p} = -\frac{4}{p}\). Substituting into \(g(x)\) gives \(y = p\left(-\frac{4}{p}\right)^2 + 8\left(-\frac{4}{p}\right) + p = \frac{p^2 - 16}{p}\), giving the vertex \(\left(-\frac{4}{p}, \frac{p^2 - 16}{p}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(g(x) = mx^2 + 4x + m\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{4}{2m} = -\frac{2}{m}\). Substituting into \(g(x)\) yields \(y = m\left(-\frac{2}{m}\right)^2 + 4\left(-\frac{2}{m}\right) + m = \frac{m^2 - 4}{m}\), giving the vertex \(\left(-\frac{2}{m}, \frac{m^2 - 4}{m}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(f(x) = kx^2 - 5x + k\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), we have \(x = -\frac{-5}{2k} = \frac{5}{2k}\). Substituting \(x\) gives \(y = k\left(\frac{5}{2k}\right)^2 - 5\left(\frac{5}{2k}\right) + k = \frac{4k^2 - 25}{4k}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{5}{2k}, \frac{4k^2 - 25}{4k}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(f(x) = (p - 1)x^2 + 4x + (p + 1)\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{4}{2(p - 1)} = -\frac{2}{p - 1}\). Substituting into \(f(x)\) yields \(y = -\frac{4}{p - 1} + (p + 1) = \frac{p^2 - 1 - 4}{p - 1} = \frac{p^2 - 5}{p - 1}\), giving the vertex \(\left(-\frac{2}{p - 1}, \frac{p^2 - 5}{p - 1}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(g(x) = ax^2 + (a + 2)x + 1\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{a + 2}{2a}\). Substituting into \(g(x)\) gives \(y = -\frac{(a + 2)^2}{4a} + 1 = \frac{-(a^2 + 4a + 4) + 4a}{4a} = -\frac{a^2 + 4}{4a}\), so the vertex is \(\left(-\frac{a + 2}{2a}, -\frac{a^2 + 4}{4a}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(f(x) = 4kx^2 - 6x + 3k\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{-6}{2(4k)} = \frac{3}{4k}\). Substituting into \(f(x)\) gives \(y = 4k\left(\frac{3}{4k}\right)^2 - 6\left(\frac{3}{4k}\right) + 3k = -\frac{9}{4k} + 3k = \frac{12k^2 - 9}{4k}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{3}{4k}, \frac{12k^2 - 9}{4k}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(g(x) = -2mx^2 + 5x - 3m\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{5}{2(-2m)} = \frac{5}{4m}\). Substituting \(x\) gives \(y = -2m\left(\frac{5}{4m}\right)^2 + 5\left(\frac{5}{4m}\right) - 3m = \frac{25}{8m} - 3m = \frac{25 - 24m^2}{8m}\), giving vertex \(\left(\frac{5}{4m}, \frac{25 - 24m^2}{8m}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(h(x) = ax^2 - 6bx + 2a\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{-6b}{2a} = \frac{3b}{a}\). Substituting into \(h(x)\) gives \(y = a\left(\frac{3b}{a}\right)^2 - 6b\left(\frac{3b}{a}\right) + 2a = -\frac{9b^2}{a} + 2a = \frac{2a^2 - 9b^2}{a}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{3b}{a}, \frac{2a^2 - 9b^2}{a}\right)\).

exercises.name: Finding the vertex with literal coefficients

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(f(x) = kx(10 - x)\).
qs.s: Expanding and completing the square gives \(f(x) = -k(x^2 - 10x + 25) + 25k = -k(x - 5)^2 + 25k\). Thus, the vertex is \((5, 25k)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(h(x) = px(12 - x)\).
qs.s: Expanding and completing the square gives \(h(x) = -p(x^2 - 12x + 36) + 36p = -p(x - 6)^2 + 36p\). Thus, the vertex is \((6, 36p)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(r(x) = -bx(x - 4)\).
qs.s: Expanding and completing the square gives \(r(x) = -b(x^2 - 4x + 4) + 4b = -b(x - 2)^2 + 4b\). Thus, the vertex is \((2, 4b)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(g(x) = ax(x - 6)\).
qs.s: Expanding and completing the square gives \(g(x) = a(x^2 - 6x + 9) - 9a = a(x - 3)^2 - 9a\). Thus, the vertex is \((3, -9a)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(m(x) = cx(x + 8)\).
qs.s: Expanding and completing the square gives \(m(x) = c(x^2 + 8x + 16) - 16c = c(x + 4)^2 - 16c\). Thus, the vertex is \((-4, -16c)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(h(x) = -3kx(x - 8)\).
qs.s: Expanding and factoring gives \(h(x) = -3k(x^2 - 8x + 16) + 48k = -3k(x - 4)^2 + 48k\). Thus, the vertex is \((4, 48k)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(f(x) = k(x - 2)(14 - x)\).
qs.s: Expanding and completing the square gives \(f(x) = -k(x^2 - 16x + 64) + 64k - 28k = -k(x - 8)^2 + 36k\). Thus, the vertex is \((8, 36k)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(g(x) = kx(12 - x) - 11k\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(g(x) = -k(x^2 - 12x + 36) + 36k - 11k = -k(x - 6)^2 + 25k\). Thus, the vertex is \((6, 25k)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(p(x) = kx(9 - x)\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(p(x) = -k\left(x^2 - 9x + \frac{81}{4}\right) + \frac{81}{4}k = -k\left(x - \frac{9}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{81}{4}k\). Thus, the vertex is \(\left(\frac{9}{2}, \frac{81}{4}k\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of \(q(x) = 2kx(7 - x) + 5k\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(q(x) = -2k\left(x - \frac{7}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{49}{2}k + 5k = -2k\left(x - \frac{7}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{59}{2}k\). Thus, the vertex is \(\left(\frac{7}{2}, \frac{59}{2}k\right)\).

exercises.name: Finding a coefficient given extremum information

qs.q: Find \(a\) such that \(f(x) = ax^2 + 6x - 7\) has a maximum value at \(x = 5\).
qs.s: The extremum occurs at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), so \(-\frac{6}{2a} = 5\). Solving \(-\frac{3}{a} = 5\) gives \(a = -\frac{3}{5}\), which confirms a maximum since \(a < 0\).

qs.q: Find \(a\) such that \(f(x) = ax^2 + 16x + 9\) has a maximum value at \(x = 2\).
qs.s: The extremum occurs at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), so \(-\frac{16}{2a} = 2\). Solving \(-\frac{8}{a} = 2\) gives \(a = -4\), which confirms a maximum since \(a < 0\).

qs.q: Find \(a\) such that \(f(x) = ax^2 - 12x - 5\) has a minimum value at \(x = 4\).
qs.s: The extremum occurs at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), so \(-\frac{-12}{2a} = 4\). Solving \(\frac{6}{a} = 4\) gives \(a = \frac{6}{4} = \frac{3}{2}\), which confirms a minimum since \(a > 0\).

qs.q: Find \(a\) such that \(f(x) = ax^2 - 8x + 3\) has a minimum value at \(x = 2\).
qs.s: The extremum occurs at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), so \(-\frac{-8}{2a} = 2\). Solving \(\frac{4}{a} = 2\) gives \(a = 2\), which confirms a minimum since \(a > 0\).

qs.q: Find \(a\) such that \(f(x) = ax^2 - 10x + 1\) has a maximum value at \(x = -1\).
qs.s: The extremum occurs at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), so \(-\frac{-10}{2a} = -1\). Solving \(\frac{5}{a} = -1\) gives \(a = -5\), which confirms a maximum since \(a < 0\).

qs.q: Find \(a\) such that \(f(x) = ax^2 - 24x + 19\) has a minimum value of \(-17\).
qs.s: The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{-24}{2a} = \frac{12}{a}\), giving the minimum value \(f\left(\frac{12}{a}\right) = -\frac{144}{a} + 19\). Setting \(-\frac{144}{a} + 19 = -17\) gives \(-\frac{144}{a} = -36\), so \(a = 4\).

qs.q: Find \(a\) such that \(f(x) = (2a - 3)x^2 + 20x - 11\) has a maximum value at \(x = 5\).
qs.s: The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{20}{2(2a - 3)} = 5\), which simplifies to \(-\frac{10}{2a - 3} = 5\). Solving gives \(2a - 3 = -2\), so \(a = \frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Find \(a\) such that \(f(x) = ax(x - 6) + 8x - 5\) has a minimum value at \(x = 1\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(f(x) = ax^2 + (8 - 6a)x - 5\), so the vertex is at \(x = -\frac{8 - 6a}{2a} = \frac{6a - 8}{2a}\). Setting \(\frac{6a - 8}{2a} = 1\) yields \(6a - 8 = 2a\), so \(a = 2\).

qs.q: Find \(a\) such that \(f(x) = ax^2 - 4ax + 2a - 5\) has a maximum value of \(7\).
qs.s: The vertex is at \(x = -\frac{-4a}{2a} = 2\), and the maximum value is \(f(2) = 4a - 8a + 2a - 5 = -2a - 5\). Setting \(-2a - 5 = 7\) gives \(-2a = 12\), so \(a = -6\).

qs.q: Find \(a\) such that \(f(x) = ax^2 + 12x - 7\) has a maximum value of \(11\).
qs.s: The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{12}{2a} = -\frac{6}{a}\), where the value is \(f\left(-\frac{6}{a}\right) = -\frac{36}{a} - 7\). Setting \(-\frac{36}{a} - 7 = 11\) gives \(-\frac{36}{a} = 18\), so \(a = -2\).

exercises.name: Finding a coefficient given extremum information

qs.q: Find the positive value of \(b\) so that the function \(f(x) = 3x^2 + bx + 10\) has a minimum value of \(-2\).
qs.s: Completing the square yields \(f(x) = 3\left(x + \frac{b}{6}\right)^2 + 10 - \frac{b^2}{12}\), so the minimum value is \(10 - \frac{b^2}{12} = -2\). Solving \(\frac{b^2}{12} = 12\) gives \(b^2 = 144\), which gives the positive value \(b = 12\).

qs.q: Find the positive value of \(b\) so that the function \(f(x) = -2x^2 + bx - 5\) has a maximum value of \(3\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -2\left(x - \frac{b}{4}\right)^2 + \frac{b^2}{8} - 5\), so the maximum value is \(\frac{b^2}{8} - 5 = 3\). Solving \(\frac{b^2}{8} = 8\) gives \(b^2 = 64\), so \(b = 8\).

qs.q: Find the positive value of \(b\) so that the function \(f(x) = x^2 + bx + 5\) has a minimum value of \(-4\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = \left(x + \frac{b}{2}\right)^2 + 5 - \frac{b^2}{4}\), so the minimum value is \(5 - \frac{b^2}{4} = -4\). Solving \(\frac{b^2}{4} = 9\) yields \(b^2 = 36\), which gives \(b = 6\) for \(b > 0\).

qs.q: Find the positive value of \(b\) so that the function \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 + bx + 1\) has a minimum value of \(-7\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x + b)^2 + 1 - \frac{b^2}{2}\), so the minimum value is \(1 - \frac{b^2}{2} = -7\). Solving \(\frac{b^2}{2} = 8\) gives \(b^2 = 16\), which gives \(b = 4\).

qs.q: Find the negative value of \(b\) so that the function \(f(x) = -x^2 + bx - 7\) has a maximum value of \(9\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -\left(x - \frac{b}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{b^2}{4} - 7\), so the maximum value is \(\frac{b^2}{4} - 7 = 9\). Solving \(\frac{b^2}{4} = 16\) gives \(b^2 = 64\), so the negative value is \(b = -8\).

qs.q: Find the positive value of \(b\) so that the function \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{3}x^2 + bx - 5\) has a maximum value of \(7\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(-\frac{1}{3}\) and completing the square yields \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{3}\left(x - \frac{3b}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{3b^2}{4} - 5\). Setting the maximum \(\frac{3b^2}{4} - 5 = 7\) gives \(\frac{3b^2}{4} = 12\), so \(b^2 = 16\) and \(b = 4\).

qs.q: Find the positive value of \(b\) so that the function \(f(x) = 2x^2 + bx + 1\) has a minimum value of \(-\frac{17}{8}\).
qs.s: Completing the square yields \(f(x) = 2\left(x + \frac{b}{4}\right)^2 + 1 - \frac{b^2}{8}\), so the minimum value is \(1 - \frac{b^2}{8} = -\frac{17}{8}\). Solving gives \(\frac{b^2}{8} = \frac{25}{8}\), so \(b^2 = 25\) and \(b = 5\).

qs.q: Find the positive value of \(b\) so that the function \(f(x) = (x - 1)(x - 3) + bx\) has a minimum value of \(-6\).
qs.s: Expanding and collecting like terms gives \(f(x) = x^2 + (b - 4)x + 3\). Completing the square gives a minimum value of \(3 - \frac{(b - 4)^2}{4} = -6\), so \((b - 4)^2 = 36\), which gives \(b - 4 = 6\) and \(b = 10\).

qs.q: Find the positive value of \(b\) so that the function \(f(x) = 2(x - 1)^2 - (x + 3)^2 + bx\) has a minimum value of \(-43\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(f(x) = 2(x^2 - 2x + 1) - (x^2 + 6x + 9) + bx = x^2 + (b - 10)x - 7\). Completing the square gives the minimum value \(-7 - \frac{(b - 10)^2}{4} = -43\), so \((b - 10)^2 = 144\), which yields \(b = 10 + 12 = 22\).

qs.q: Find the value of \(a\) so that the function \(f(x) = ax^2 - 12x + 7\) has a maximum value of \(16\).
qs.s: Completing the square yields \(f(x) = a\left(x - \frac{6}{a}\right)^2 + 7 - \frac{36}{a}\). Setting the maximum value \(7 - \frac{36}{a} = 16\) gives \(-\frac{36}{a} = 9\), which simplifies to \(a = -4\) (consistent with \(a < 0\) for a maximum).

exercises.name: Finding a coefficient given extremum information

qs.q: Find \(c\) so that the function \(f(x) = 0.2x^2 - 6x + c\) has a minimum value of \(15\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = 0.2(x - 15)^2 - 45 + c\), so the minimum value is \(c - 45\). Setting \(c - 45 = 15\) yields \(c = 60\).

qs.q: Find \(c\) so that the function \(f(x) = 0.25x^2 + 3x + c\) has a minimum value of \(-4.5\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = 0.25(x + 6)^2 - 9 + c\), so the minimum value is \(c - 9\). Setting \(c - 9 = -4.5\) yields \(c = 4.5\).

qs.q: Find \(c\) so that the function \(f(x) = 0.5x^2 - 7x + c\) has a minimum value of \(-18.5\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = 0.5(x - 7)^2 - 24.5 + c\), so the minimum value is \(c - 24.5\). Setting \(c - 24.5 = -18.5\) yields \(c = 6\).

qs.q: Find \(c\) so that the function \(f(x) = -0.5x^2 + 4x + c\) has a maximum value of \(11\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -0.5(x - 4)^2 + 8 + c\), so the maximum value is \(c + 8\). Setting \(c + 8 = 11\) yields \(c = 3\).

qs.q: Find \(c\) so that the function \(f(x) = -0.1x^2 - 5x + c\) has a maximum value of \(75.5\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -0.1(x + 25)^2 + 62.5 + c\), so the maximum value is \(c + 62.5\). Setting \(c + 62.5 = 75.5\) yields \(c = 13\).

qs.q: Find \(c\) so that the function \(f(x) = 2(x + 3)^2 - (x - 1)^2 + 4x + c\) has a minimum value of \(-15\).
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying yields \(f(x) = x^2 + 18x + 17 + c = (x + 9)^2 - 64 + c\). Setting the minimum value \(c - 64 = -15\) gives \(c = 49\).

qs.q: Find \(c\) so that the function \(f(x) = -0.05x^2 + 14x + c\) has a maximum value of \(1020\).
qs.s: Completing the square gives \(f(x) = -0.05(x - 140)^2 + 980 + c\), so the maximum value is \(c + 980\). Setting \(c + 980 = 1020\) yields \(c = 40\).

qs.q: Find \(c\) so that the function \(f(x) = -2(x - 2)(x + 4) - 8x + c\) has a maximum value of \(10\).
qs.s: Expanding and collecting like terms gives \(f(x) = -2x^2 - 12x + 16 + c = -2(x + 3)^2 + 34 + c\). Setting the maximum value \(c + 34 = 10\) yields \(c = -24\).

qs.q: Find \(c\) so that the function \(f(x) = 3(x - 1)(x + 5) - 6x + c\) has a minimum value of \(-10\).
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying gives \(f(x) = 3x^2 + 6x - 15 + c = 3(x + 1)^2 - 18 + c\). Setting the minimum value \(c - 18 = -10\) gives \(c = 8\).

qs.q: Find \(c\) so that the function \(f(x) = \frac{2}{5}x^2 - 3x + c\) has a minimum value of \(\frac{7}{8}\).
qs.s: Completing the square yields \(f(x) = \frac{2}{5}\left(x - \frac{15}{4}\right)^2 - \frac{45}{8} + c\). Setting the minimum value \(c - \frac{45}{8} = \frac{7}{8}\) gives \(c = \frac{52}{8} = \frac{13}{2}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. For a quadratic function in general form, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) with \(a \neq 0\), the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is given by the formula \(x =\) ________.
qs.s: By completing the square on the general form \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is found to be \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\).
