qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The graph of a quadratic function in general form, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), opens downward if and only if ________.
qs.s: The direction of opening of a parabola is determined solely by the sign of the leading coefficient \(a\), opening downward when \(a < 0\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. In the general form of a quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), the real coefficient \(a\) must satisfy ________.
qs.s: If \(a = 0\), the quadratic term vanishes and the function becomes linear, so \(a \neq 0\) is required for the function to be quadratic.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) intersects the \(y\)-axis at the point ________.
qs.s: Evaluating the function at \(x = 0\) gives \(f(0) = a(0)^2 + b(0) + c = c\), which corresponds to the \(y\)-intercept \((0, c)\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. In terms of the coefficients \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\), the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex of \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) is given by ________.
qs.s: Substituting the vertex \(x\)-coordinate \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) simplifies to the vertex \(y\)-coordinate \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the quadratic function \(f(x) = 3x^2 + bx + 5\) with \(b > 0\) has a minimum value of \(2\), then \(b =\) ________.
qs.s: The minimum value is the vertex \(y\)-coordinate \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = 5 - \frac{b^2}{12}\). Setting \(5 - \frac{b^2}{12} = 2\) gives \(b^2 = 36\), so \(b = 6\) since \(b > 0\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The quadratic function \(f(x) = 0.2x^2 + 6x + c\) has a minimum value of \(-38\) when \(c =\) ________.
qs.s: The minimum value equals \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = c - \frac{6^2}{4(0.2)} = c - 45\). Setting \(c - 45 = -38\) yields \(c = 7\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 - 12x + 7\) has a maximum value at \(x = -2\) when \(a =\) ________.
qs.s: The maximum occurs at the vertex \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-12}{2a} = \frac{6}{a}\). Setting \(\frac{6}{a} = -2\) gives \(a = -3\), with \(a < 0\) confirming a maximum.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. For any non-zero real number \(k\), the axis of symmetry of the parabola \(f(x) = kx(10 - x)\) is the line ________.
qs.s: Writing the function in general form gives \(f(x) = -kx^2 + 10kx\), so \(a = -k\) and \(b = 10k\). The axis of symmetry is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{10k}{2(-k)} = 5\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. In terms of the non-zero parameter \(k\), the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex of \(g(x) = 3x^2 + 2kx + k^2\) is ________.
qs.s: Using the vertex formula \(y = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) with \(a = 3\), \(b = 2k\), and \(c = k^2\), we calculate \(k^2 - \frac{(2k)^2}{4(3)} = k^2 - \frac{4k^2}{12} = \frac{2k^2}{3}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola \(y = x^2 + 6x + 10\) is \(x =\) ________.
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through the vertex, given by \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{6}{2(1)} = -3\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The \(y\)-intercept of the parabola \(y = -2x^2 + 5x - 7\) is \((0,\) ________\()\).
qs.s: Substituting \(x = 0\) into \(y = -2x^2 + 5x - 7\) gives \(y = -7\), so the \(y\)-intercept is \((0, -7)\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex of \(y = 3x^2 + bx + c\) is ________.
qs.s: Using the vertex formula \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\) with \(a = 3\), the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(-\frac{b}{2(3)} = -\frac{b}{6}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. In the vertex formula for \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\), the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(c -\) ________.
qs.s: From the vertex formula derived by completing the square, the vertex is \(\left(-\frac{b}{2a}, c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right)\), so the blank is filled by \(\frac{b^2}{4a}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex of \(y = x^2 - 8x + 15\) is ________.
qs.s: Using the vertex formula \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\) with \(a = 1\) and \(b = -8\), the \(x\)-coordinate is \(-\frac{-8}{2(1)} = 4\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the quadratic function \(f(x) = 0.1x^2 + 6x + c\) has a minimum value of \(-75\), then \(c =\) ________.
qs.s: The minimum value occurs at the vertex where \(y = c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = c - \frac{6^2}{4(0.1)} = c - 90\). Setting \(c - 90 = -75\) gives \(c = 15\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex of \(y = -\frac{2}{3}x^2 + 4x - 1\) is ________.
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{4}{2(-2/3)} = 3\). Evaluating the function at \(x = 3\) gives \(y = -\frac{2}{3}(3)^2 + 4(3) - 1 = -6 + 12 - 1 = 5\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex of \(y = 2x^2 + kx + k^2\) is ________.
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{k}{2(2)} = -\frac{k}{4}\). Substituting this gives \(y = 2\left(-\frac{k}{4}\right)^2 + k\left(-\frac{k}{4}\right) + k^2 = \frac{k^2}{8} - \frac{k^2}{4} + k^2 = \frac{7k^2}{8}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the parabola \(y = ax^2 + 12x - 5\) has its axis of symmetry at \(x = -2\), then \(a =\) ________.
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is given by \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), so \(-\frac{12}{2a} = -2\). Simplifying gives \(-\frac{6}{a} = -2\), which yields \(a = 3\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex of \(y = kx(8 - x)\) is ________.
qs.s: Expanding gives \(y = -kx^2 + 8kx\), so the vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{8k}{2(-k)} = 4\). Substituting \(x = 4\) yields \(y = k(4)(8 - 4) = 16k\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The coordinates of the y-intercept of the parabola \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) are ________.
qs.s: Evaluating the quadratic equation at \(x = 0\) gives \(y = a(0)^2 + b(0) + c = c\), so the y-intercept is \((0, c)\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The y-coordinate of the vertex of the parabola \(y = ax^2 + bx\) is ________.
qs.s: Using the vertex formula \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) with constant term \(c = 0\), the y-coordinate is \(0 - \frac{b^2}{4a} = -\frac{b^2}{4a}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) is ________.
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is the vertical line passing through the vertex, so its equation is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The x-coordinate of the vertex of \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) is ________.
qs.s: For a quadratic function in general form \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\), the x-coordinate of the vertex is given by \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. Expressed as a single fraction with denominator \(4a\), the y-coordinate of the vertex of \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) is ________.
qs.s: Finding a common denominator for the vertex formula gives \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = \frac{4ac}{4a} - \frac{b^2}{4a} = \frac{4ac - b^2}{4a}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the parabola \(y = ax^2 + 8x - 3\) has a maximum value of \(5\), then $a = $ ________.
qs.s: The maximum value is the y-coordinate of the vertex, so \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = 5\). Substituting \(b = 8\) and \(c = -3\) gives \(-3 - \frac{64}{4a} = 5\), which simplifies to \(-\frac{16}{a} = 8\), so \(a = -2\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the parabola \(y = 3x^2 - 12x + c\) has a minimum value of \(-7\), then $c = $ ________.
qs.s: The minimum value is the y-coordinate of the vertex, \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = c - \frac{(-12)^2}{4(3)} = c - 12\). Setting \(c - 12 = -7\) yields \(c = 5\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. In terms of \(k\), the y-coordinate of the vertex of the parabola \(y = 2x^2 + kx + k^2\) is ________.
qs.s: Using the vertex formula \(y = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) with \(a = 2\), \(b = k\), and \(c = k^2\), we obtain \(y = k^2 - \frac{k^2}{4(2)} = k^2 - \frac{k^2}{8} = \frac{7k^2}{8}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. For \(p \neq 0\), the y-coordinate of the vertex of the parabola \(y = px^2 - 6x + p\) expressed as a single fraction is ________.
qs.s: With \(a = p\), \(b = -6\), and \(c = p\), the y-coordinate of the vertex is \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = p - \frac{(-6)^2}{4p} = p - \frac{9}{p} = \frac{p^2 - 9}{p}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. For \(k \neq 0\), the y-coordinate of the vertex of the parabola \(y = kx(12 - x)\) is ________.
qs.s: Expanding gives \(y = -kx^2 + 12kx\), so \(a = -k\), \(b = 12k\), and \(c = 0\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{12k}{2(-k)} = 6\), giving \(y = k(6)(12 - 6) = 36k\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex of the parabola \(y = 2x^2 + 8x - 1\) is ________.
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is given by \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{8}{2(2)} = -2\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The \(y\)-intercept of the parabola \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) is the point ________.
qs.s: Substituting \(x = 0\) into \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) gives \(y = c\), so the \(y\)-intercept is \((0, c)\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The axis of symmetry of the parabola \(y = x^2 - 4x + 5\) is the line ________.
qs.s: Using the formula \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\) with \(a = 1\) and \(b = -4\), we find the axis of symmetry is \(x = -\frac{-4}{2(1)} = 2\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The axis of symmetry of the parabola \(y = ax^2 - bx + c\) is the line ________.
qs.s: Using the axis of symmetry formula \(x = -\frac{B}{2A}\) with \(A = a\) and \(B = -b\) yields \(x = -\frac{-b}{2a} = \frac{b}{2a}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The axis of symmetry of the parabola \(y = ax^2 + c\) is the line ________.
qs.s: Since the linear coefficient is \(b = 0\), the axis of symmetry is \(x = -\frac{0}{2a}\), which simplifies to \(x = 0\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The axis of symmetry of the quadratic function \(y = 2x(6 - x) + 5\) is the line ________.
qs.s: Expanding gives the general form \(y = -2x^2 + 12x + 5\), where \(a = -2\) and \(b = 12\). The axis of symmetry is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{12}{2(-2)} = 3\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. For any non-zero constant \(k\), the axis of symmetry of the parabola \(y = 3x^2 - 12kx + k^2\) is the line ________.
qs.s: With coefficients \(a = 3\) and \(b = -12k\), the axis of symmetry is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-12k}{2(3)} = 2k\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. For any non-zero constant \(k\), the axis of symmetry of the parabola \(y = kx(10 - x) - 3\) is the line ________.
qs.s: Expanding yields \(y = -kx^2 + 10kx - 3\) with \(a = -k\) and \(b = 10k\). The axis of symmetry is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{10k}{2(-k)} = 5\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the axis of symmetry of the parabola \(y = ax^2 + 12x - 7\) is \(x = -2\), then $a = $ ________.
qs.s: Setting the axis of symmetry formula \(-\frac{12}{2a} = -2\) gives \(-\frac{6}{a} = -2\), which solves to \(a = 3\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex of the parabola \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 6x - 10\) is ________.
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{6}{2(-1/2)} = 6\). Substituting \(x = 6\) yields \(y = -\frac{1}{2}(6)^2 + 6(6) - 10 = -18 + 36 - 10 = 8\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The vertical line that divides a parabola into two symmetrical halves is called the ________.
qs.s: By definition, the axis of symmetry is the vertical line passing through the vertex that divides the parabola into two congruent, mirror-image halves.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) intersects the \(y\)-axis at the point \((0,\) ________).
qs.s: Evaluating the function at \(x = 0\) gives \(f(0) = a(0)^2 + b(0) + c = c\), which gives the \(y\)-intercept \((0, c)\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If a parabola opens upward, the \(y\)-coordinate of its vertex represents the ________ value of the function.
qs.s: Since an upward-opening parabola reaches its lowest point at the vertex, the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex is the function's minimum value.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. For a quadratic function in general form \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), the parabola opens downward when the leading coefficient \(a\) is ________.
qs.s: The sign of \(a\) dictates the direction of opening; when \(a < 0\) (negative), the parabola opens downward.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. For any quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is given by the formula $x = $ ________.
qs.s: Derived from completing the square of the general form \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), the vertex formula gives the \(x\)-coordinate as \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 18x + 23\) is ________.
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{-18}{2(3)} = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) gives \(y = 3(3)^2 - 18(3) + 23 = -4\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 - 6x + c\) has a minimum value of \(-2\) when $c = $ ________.
qs.s: The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{-6}{2(1)} = 3\), and setting \(f(3) = (3)^2 - 6(3) + c = -2\) gives \(-9 + c = -2\), so \(c = 7\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The maximum value of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 12x - 11\) is ________.
qs.s: The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{12}{2(-2)} = 3\). Evaluating \(f(3) = -2(3)^2 + 12(3) - 11 = 7\) yields the maximum value.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the axis of symmetry of the parabola \(f(x) = -2x^2 + bx + 7\) is the line \(x = 5\), then $b = $ ________.
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\). Setting \(5 = -\frac{b}{2(-2)} = \frac{b}{4}\) gives \(b = 20\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 + 8x - 5\) achieves its maximum value at \(x = 4\) when $a = $ ________.
qs.s: A maximum occurs at the vertex where \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), so \(4 = -\frac{8}{2a} = -\frac{4}{a}\), which gives \(a = -1\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) occurs at the point \((0, \underline{\quad})\).
qs.s: Evaluating \(f(0) = a(0)^2 + b(0) + c = c\), so the graph crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, c)\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) is given by $x = $ ________.
qs.s: By the vertex formula derived from completing the square, the axis of symmetry and the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The axis of symmetry of the parabola \(f(x) = a(x - h)^2 + k\) is the vertical line given by the equation $x = $ ________.
qs.s: The vertex is at \((h, k)\), and the axis of symmetry is the vertical line passing through it, given by \(x = h\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If a parabola opens downward, the function attains its ________ value at the vertex.
qs.s: Since \(a < 0\), the parabola opens downward and the vertex represents the highest point, which is the maximum value of the function.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the leading coefficient \(a\) in \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) is positive, the parabola opens ________.
qs.s: When the leading coefficient \(a\) is positive, the parabola opens upward, with the vertex as its lowest point.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The quadratic function \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 12x - 11\) attains its maximum value at $y = $ ________.
Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the parabola \(f(x) = ax^2 + 16x - 9\) has its axis of symmetry at \(x = -4\), then $a = $ ________.
qs.s: Using \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), we set \(-4 = -\frac{16}{2a}\), which simplifies to \(-4 = -\frac{8}{a}\), yielding \(a = 2\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. In terms of \(k\), the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = x^2 + kx + 9\) is ________.
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{k}{2}\). Substituting this into the function yields \(f\left(-\frac{k}{2}\right) = \left(-\frac{k}{2}\right)^2 + k\left(-\frac{k}{2}\right) + 9 = 9 - \frac{k^2}{4}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The quadratic function \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + c\) has a minimum value of \(-5\) when $c = $ ________.
qs.s: The minimum is at \(x = -\frac{-12}{2(3)} = 2\). Substituting gives \(f(2) = 3(2)^2 - 12(2) + c = -12 + c = -5\), so \(c = 7\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The axis of symmetry of the parabola \(f(x) = -\frac{3}{4}x^2 + 6x - 5\) is the vertical line $x = $ ________.
qs.s: Using the axis of symmetry formula \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), we have \(x = -\frac{6}{2\left(-\frac{3}{4}\right)} = -\frac{6}{-\frac{3}{2}} = 4\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) opens upward when the leading coefficient \(a\) is ________.
qs.s: A parabola opens upward if and only if its leading coefficient \(a\) is greater than zero, meaning \(a\) is positive.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The turning point where a parabola reaches its highest or lowest point is called the ________.
qs.s: The vertex of a parabola is the point where the curve turns, representing either the minimum or maximum value.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the leading coefficient \(a\) of a quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) is negative, the vertex represents the ________ value of the function.
qs.s: When \(a < 0\), the parabola opens downward, which means the vertex is the highest point and represents the maximum value.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. For a quadratic function in general form \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), the \(y\)-coordinate of the \(y\)-intercept is ________.
qs.s: Setting \(x = 0\) in \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) yields \(f(0) = c\), so the \(y\)-intercept is located at \((0, c)\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The vertical line that passes through the vertex and divides a parabola into two symmetric halves is called the axis of ________.
qs.s: The vertical line passing through the vertex that divides the parabola into mirror-image halves is defined as the axis of symmetry.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. In the vertex formula for the quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex expressed in terms of \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) is ________.
qs.s: Completing the square yields \(f(x) = a\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\), so the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. For any quadratic function in general form \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \neq 0\)), the equation of the axis of symmetry is ________.
qs.s: By completing the square on the general form, the axis of symmetry is the vertical line through the vertex given by \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 12kx + 5\) in terms of \(k\) is ________.
qs.s: Using the vertex formula \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), we have \(x = -\frac{-12k}{2(3)} = \frac{12k}{6} = 2k\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The parabola defined by \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 8x - 11\) attains its maximum value at the vertex with coordinates ________.
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{8}{2(-2)} = 2\), and substituting gives \(f(2) = -2(2)^2 + 8(2) - 11 = -3\), so the vertex is \((2, -3)\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The axis of symmetry for the parabola \(f(x) = -\frac{3}{4}x^2 + 6x - 7\) is the vertical line with equation ________.
qs.s: Using \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), we get \(x = -\frac{6}{2\left(-\frac{3}{4}\right)} = -\frac{6}{-\frac{3}{2}} = 4\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement: If the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) is located at \((4, -7)\) and \(a < 0\), then the graph has ________ \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: The vertex \((4, -7)\) is below the \(x\)-axis, and since \(a < 0\), the parabola opens downward and never crosses the \(x\)-axis, resulting in 0 \(x\)-intercepts.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement: If the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) is located at \((6, 0)\) with \(a \neq 0\), then the graph has ________ \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: Because the vertex has a \(y\)-coordinate of 0, it lies directly on the \(x\)-axis, meaning the parabola touches the \(x\)-axis at exactly 1 point.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement: If a quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) has a minimum value of \(5\), then the graph of \(f(x)\) has ________ \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: A minimum value means the parabola opens upward (\(a > 0\)). Since the lowest \(y\)-value is \(5 > 0\), the entire graph stays strictly above the \(x\)-axis and has 0 \(x\)-intercepts.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement: If the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) is located at \((-3, -2)\) and \(a > 0\), then the graph has ________ \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: The vertex \((-3, -2)\) lies below the \(x\)-axis, and because \(a > 0\), the parabola opens upward and must cross the \(x\)-axis at two points, giving 2 \(x\)-intercepts.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement: If a quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) has a maximum value of \(8\), then the graph of \(f(x)\) has ________ \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: A maximum value indicates that the parabola opens downward (\(a < 0\)). Because the maximum \(y\)-value is positive (\(8 > 0\)), the graph extends downward across the \(x\)-axis, yielding 2 \(x\)-intercepts.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement: If the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 6x + c\) lies on the line \(y = -4\), then $c = $ ________.
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{-6}{2(1/2)} = 6\). Substituting into \(f(x)\) gives \(f(6) = \frac{1}{2}(36) - 6(6) + c = -18 + c = -4\), so \(c = 14\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement: If the parabola \(f(x) = -2x^2 + bx - 5\) has its axis of symmetry at \(x = -3\), then the maximum value of \(f(x)\) is ________.
qs.s: From the axis of symmetry formula \(x = -\frac{b}{2(-2)} = -3\), we find \(b = -12\). The maximum value occurs at the vertex: \(f(-3) = -2(-3)^2 - 12(-3) - 5 = -18 + 36 - 5 = 13\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement: The parabola \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + k\) has its vertex on the \(x\)-axis when $k = $ ________.
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{-12}{2(3)} = 2\). For the vertex to lie on the \(x\)-axis, \(f(2) = 3(2)^2 - 12(2) + k = -12 + k = 0\), which gives \(k = 12\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement: If the quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 + 8x - 3\) reaches a maximum value of \(5\), then $a = $ ________.
qs.s: The maximum value is the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex: \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = -3 - \frac{64}{4a} = 5\). Solving \(-\frac{16}{a} = 8\) yields \(a = -2\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement: The graph of the parabola \(f(x) = -x^2 + 6x + (k - 4)\) has no \(x\)-intercepts if and only if $k < $ ________.
qs.s: Because \(a = -1 < 0\), the parabola opens downward and has no \(x\)-intercepts when its vertex is below the \(x\)-axis. The vertex occurs at \(x = 3\) with \(y = f(3) = k + 5\), so setting \(k + 5 < 0\) gives \(k < -5\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the vertex of the graph of \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) lies on the \(x\)-axis, and \(a \neq 0\), then the graph of \(f(x)\) has ________ \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: When the vertex of a parabola lies directly on the \(x\)-axis, the graph touches the \(x\)-axis only at that single point. Therefore, the graph has exactly 1 \(x\)-intercept.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the vertex of the graph of \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) is above the \(x\)-axis, and \(a > 0\), then the graph of \(f(x)\) has ________ \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: Since \(a > 0\), the parabola opens upward. Because its vertex is already above the \(x\)-axis, the graph curves away from the \(x\)-axis and has 0 \(x\)-intercepts.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the vertex of the graph of \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) is at \((3, -4)\), and \(a > 0\), then the graph of \(f(x)\) has ________ \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: The vertex \((3, -4)\) lies below the \(x\)-axis because its \(y\)-coordinate is negative. Since \(a > 0\), the parabola opens upward and crosses the \(x\)-axis twice, giving 2 \(x\)-intercepts.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the vertex of the graph of \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) is below the \(x\)-axis, and \(a > 0\), then the graph of \(f(x)\) has ________ \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: Since \(a > 0\), the parabola opens upward. Because its vertex is below the \(x\)-axis, the graph must cross the \(x\)-axis twice, resulting in 2 \(x\)-intercepts.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The graph of \(f(x) = 0.4x^2 - 4x + 13\) has ________ \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: The vertex is located at \(x = -\frac{-4}{2(0.4)} = 5\) with \(y = 0.4(5)^2 - 4(5) + 13 = 3\). Since the vertex is above the \(x\)-axis and the parabola opens upward (\(a = 0.4 > 0\)), the graph has 0 \(x\)-intercepts.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The graph of \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 5x - 11\) has ________ \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: The vertex is located at \(x = -\frac{5}{2(-1/2)} = 5\) with \(y = -\frac{1}{2}(5)^2 + 5(5) - 11 = 1.5\). Since the vertex is above the \(x\)-axis and the parabola opens downward (\(a = -\frac{1}{2} < 0\)), the graph has 2 \(x\)-intercepts.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The graph of \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 12x + 13\) has ________ \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: The vertex is located at \(x = -\frac{-12}{2(2)} = 3\) with \(y = 2(3)^2 - 12(3) + 13 = -5\). Since the vertex is below the \(x\)-axis and the parabola opens upward (\(a = 2 > 0\)), the graph has 2 \(x\)-intercepts.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The graph of \(f(x) = -x^2 + 8x - 19\) has ________ \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, the vertex is at \(x = -\frac{8}{2(-1)} = 4\) with \(y = -(4)^2 + 8(4) - 19 = -3\). Since the vertex is below the \(x\)-axis and the parabola opens downward (\(a = -1 < 0\)), the graph has 0 \(x\)-intercepts.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The graph of \(f(x) = -3x^2 + 18x - 27\) has ________ \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: The vertex is located at \(x = -\frac{18}{2(-3)} = 3\) with \(y = -3(3)^2 + 18(3) - 27 = 0\). Since the vertex lies directly on the \(x\)-axis, the graph has exactly 1 \(x\)-intercept.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. For the quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) with \(a < 0\), the maximum value of the function is ________.
qs.s: Since \(a < 0\), the parabola opens downward and reaches its maximum value at the vertex, which is the \(y\)-coordinate \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the graph of \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) has \(a > 0\) and \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} > 0\), then the graph has ________ \(x\)-intercept(s).
qs.s: Since \(a > 0\), the parabola opens upward, and since the minimum value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is strictly positive, the graph lies entirely above the \(x\)-axis and has 0 \(x\)-intercepts.

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) is the point ________.
qs.s: Evaluating the function at \(x = 0\) gives \(f(0) = a(0)^2 + b(0) + c = c\), so the coordinates of the \(y\)-intercept are \((0, c)\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. For any quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) with \(a \neq 0\), the equation of its axis of symmetry is \(x =\) ________.
qs.s: The axis of symmetry is the vertical line passing through the vertex \(\left(-\frac{b}{2a}, c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right)\), which has equation \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = 2x^2 + kx + k^2\) is ________.
qs.s: Using the vertex formula \(y = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) with \(a = 2\), \(b = k\), and \(c = k^2\), we calculate \(y = k^2 - \frac{k^2}{4(2)} = k^2 - \frac{k^2}{8} = \frac{7}{8}k^2\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. The quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 + 4x - 4\) has a maximum value at \(x = 6\) when \(a =\) ________.
qs.s: The maximum value occurs on the axis of symmetry, \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{4}{2a} = -\frac{2}{a}\). Setting \(-\frac{2}{a} = 6\) yields \(a = -\frac{2}{6} = -\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the quadratic function \(f(x) = 2x^2 + bx - 3\) has a minimum value of \(-5\) and \(b > 0\), then \(b =\) ________.
qs.s: The minimum value is \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = -3 - \frac{b^2}{8} = -5\). Solving gives \(\frac{b^2}{8} = 2\), which means \(b^2 = 16\), so \(b = 4\) since \(b > 0\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the graph of \(f(x) = kx^2 - 6x + 3\) (\(k \neq 0\)) has exactly one \(x\)-intercept, then \(k =\) ________.
qs.s: A parabola has exactly one \(x\)-intercept when the \(y\)-coordinate of its vertex is zero: \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = 3 - \frac{(-6)^2}{4k} = 3 - \frac{9}{k} = 0\). Solving gives \(\frac{9}{k} = 3\), so \(k = 3\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank to make a true statement. If the quadratic function \(f(x) = -x^2 + kx - 9\) has a maximum value of \(7\) and \(k > 0\), then \(k =\) ________.
qs.s: The maximum value is \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = -9 - \frac{k^2}{4(-1)} = -9 + \frac{k^2}{4} = 7\). Solving gives \(\frac{k^2}{4} = 16\), so \(k^2 = 64\), which yields \(k = 8\) since \(k > 0\).

qs.q: Write a quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = 2, b = 5, c = -7\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = 2\), \(b = 5\), and \(c = -7\) into the general form \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\). This yields \(f(x) = 2x^2 + 5x - 7\).

qs.q: Write a quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = 5, b = -6, c = 1\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = 5\), \(b = -6\), and \(c = 1\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) to get \(f(x) = 5x^2 - 6x + 1\).

qs.q: Write a quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = 1, b = -3, c = 9\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = 1\), \(b = -3\), and \(c = 9\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\). Writing \(1x^2\) simply as \(x^2\) gives \(f(x) = x^2 - 3x + 9\).

qs.q: Write a quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -4, b = -1, c = -8\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = -4\), \(b = -1\), and \(c = -8\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\). Writing the middle term \(-1x\) as \(-x\) yields \(f(x) = -4x^2 - x - 8\).

qs.q: Write a quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -1, b = 4, c = -3\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = -1\), \(b = 4\), and \(c = -3\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\). Writing \(-1x^2\) in standard form as \(-x^2\), we obtain \(f(x) = -x^2 + 4x - 3\).

qs.q: Write a quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -\frac{5}{8}, b = -\frac{1}{6}, c = \frac{7}{12}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = -\frac{5}{8}\), \(b = -\frac{1}{6}\), and \(c = \frac{7}{12}\) directly into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) to obtain \(f(x) = -\frac{5}{8}x^2 - \frac{1}{6}x + \frac{7}{12}\).

qs.q: Write a quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), where the coefficients are given by \(a = -\frac{8}{12}\), \(b = \frac{3}{5} + \frac{7}{5}\), and \(c = -\frac{9}{6}\).
qs.s: Simplify the coefficients to lowest terms: \(a = -\frac{2}{3}\), \(b = \frac{10}{5} = 2\), and \(c = -\frac{3}{2}\). Substituting these into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) gives \(f(x) = -\frac{2}{3}x^2 + 2x - \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Write a quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), where the coefficients are given by \(a = 2(-5) + 3\), \(b = (-3)^2 - 10\), and \(c = -4(-6) - 17\).
qs.s: Evaluate each coefficient first: \(a = -10 + 3 = -7\), \(b = 9 - 10 = -1\), and \(c = 24 - 17 = 7\). Substituting these into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) yields \(f(x) = -7x^2 - x + 7\).

qs.q: Write a quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -\frac{2}{5}, b = 0, c = \frac{7}{3}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = -\frac{2}{5}\), \(b = 0\), and \(c = \frac{7}{3}\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\). Since \(b = 0\), the linear term \(0x\) is omitted, resulting in \(f(x) = -\frac{2}{5}x^2 + \frac{7}{3}\).

qs.q: Write a quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(b = -35, c = 72, a = -14\).
qs.s: Identify the coefficient of \(x^2\) as \(a = -14\), the coefficient of \(x\) as \(b = -35\), and the constant term as \(c = 72\). Substituting these into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) gives \(f(x) = -14x^2 - 35x + 72\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = \frac{1}{4}, b = -5, c = 3\).
qs.s: Substitute the coefficients \(a = \frac{1}{4}\), \(b = -5\), and \(c = 3\) directly into the general form \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) to obtain \(f(x) = \frac{1}{4}x^2 - 5x + 3\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -\frac{2}{3}, b = 6, c = -1\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = -\frac{2}{3}\), \(b = 6\), and \(c = -1\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), giving \(f(x) = -\frac{2}{3}x^2 + 6x - 1\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -\frac{1}{6}, b = 4, c = 9\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = -\frac{1}{6}\), \(b = 4\), and \(c = 9\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) to obtain \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{6}x^2 + 4x + 9\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -\frac{5}{2}, b = -7, c = 8\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = -\frac{5}{2}\), \(b = -7\), and \(c = 8\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) to get \(f(x) = -\frac{5}{2}x^2 - 7x + 8\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = \frac{3}{5}, b = -2, c = -4\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = \frac{3}{5}\), \(b = -2\), and \(c = -4\) into the general form to get \(f(x) = \frac{3}{5}x^2 - 2x - 4\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -\frac{5}{6} \div \frac{5}{2}\), \(b = \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{3}{4}\), and \(c = 1 - 2\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)\).
qs.s: Compute the coefficients: \(a = -\frac{5}{6} \cdot \frac{2}{5} = -\frac{1}{3}\), \(b = \frac{1}{4} + \frac{3}{4} = 1\), and \(c = 1 - \frac{8}{3} = -\frac{5}{3}\). Substituting these values yields \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{3}x^2 + x - \frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = \frac{1}{3} - \frac{5}{6}\), \(b = -\frac{3}{4} + \frac{1}{2}\), and \(c = 2 - \frac{7}{3}\).
qs.s: Evaluate each coefficient: \(a = \frac{2}{6} - \frac{5}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}\), \(b = -\frac{3}{4} + \frac{2}{4} = -\frac{1}{4}\), and \(c = \frac{6}{3} - \frac{7}{3} = -\frac{1}{3}\). Substituting these values into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) gives \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 - \frac{1}{4}x - \frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), in terms of the constant \(k\), given the values of coefficients: \(a = -k\), \(b = 3k\), and \(c = -2k^2\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = -k\), \(b = 3k\), and \(c = -2k^2\) into general form to get \(f(x) = -kx^2 + 3kx - 2k^2\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = (-2)^2 - 7\), \(b = -\frac{2}{3} \cdot \frac{9}{8}\), and \(c = \frac{5}{6} - \frac{7}{4}\).
Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients in simplest form: \(a = -\frac{36}{48}\), \(b = \frac{45}{60}\), and \(c = -\frac{70}{28}\).
qs.s: Simplify the fractions: \(a = -\frac{3}{4}\), \(b = \frac{3}{4}\), and \(c = -\frac{5}{2}\). Substituting into general form gives \(f(x) = -\frac{3}{4}x^2 + \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = 1, b = -6, c = -8\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = 1\), \(b = -6\), and \(c = -8\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) to obtain \(f(x) = x^2 - 6x - 8\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = 3, b = 0, c = -5\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = 3\), \(b = 0\), and \(c = -5\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) to obtain \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 5\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -1, b = 7, c = 0\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = -1\), \(b = 7\), and \(c = 0\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) to obtain \(f(x) = -x^2 + 7x\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = 5, b = -4, c = 2\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = 5\), \(b = -4\), and \(c = 2\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) to obtain \(f(x) = 5x^2 - 4x + 2\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -4, b = -1, c = 6\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = -4\), \(b = -1\), and \(c = 6\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) to obtain \(f(x) = -4x^2 - x + 6\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), whose coefficients are given by \(a = \frac{1}{4} - \frac{5}{6}\), \(b = -\frac{2}{3} \cdot \frac{9}{4}\), and \(c = 0\).
qs.s: Simplify each coefficient: \(a = \frac{3}{12} - \frac{10}{12} = -\frac{7}{12}\), \(b = -\frac{18}{12} = -\frac{3}{2}\), and \(c = 0\). Substituting these values into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) gives \(f(x) = -\frac{7}{12}x^2 - \frac{3}{2}x\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), whose coefficients are given by \(a = 2(-4) + 1\), \(b = (-3)^2 - 5\), and \(c = 11 - 4(5)\).
qs.s: Calculate each coefficient first: \(a = -8 + 1 = -7\), \(b = 9 - 5 = 4\), and \(c = 11 - 20 = -9\). Substituting these into the general form yields \(f(x) = -7x^2 + 4x - 9\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -15, b = 180, c = -450\).
Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = 2, b = -\sqrt{3}, c = -7\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = 2\), \(b = -\sqrt{3}\), and \(c = -7\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) to get \(f(x) = 2x^2 - \sqrt{3}x - 7\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -\frac{5}{6}, b = \frac{3}{4}, c = -\frac{7}{10}\).
qs.s: Substitute the fractional coefficients \(a = -\frac{5}{6}\), \(b = \frac{3}{4}\), and \(c = -\frac{7}{10}\) directly into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) to get \(f(x) = -\frac{5}{6}x^2 + \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{7}{10}\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -\frac{5}{4}, b = 0, c = \frac{2}{3}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = -\frac{5}{4}\), \(b = 0\), and \(c = \frac{2}{3}\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\). Omitting the zero linear term gives \(f(x) = -\frac{5}{4}x^2 + \frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = \frac{5}{6}, b = 0, c = -\frac{1}{2}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = \frac{5}{6}\), \(b = 0\), and \(c = -\frac{1}{2}\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\). Since \(b = 0\), the linear term is omitted, yielding \(f(x) = \frac{5}{6}x^2 - \frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = \frac{1}{4}, b = -5, c = 0\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = \frac{1}{4}\), \(b = -5\), and \(c = 0\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\). Since \(c = 0\), the constant term is omitted, giving \(f(x) = \frac{1}{4}x^2 - 5x\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -1, b = -\frac{4}{3}, c = 7\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a = -1\), \(b = -\frac{4}{3}\), and \(c = 7\) into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\). In simplest form, the coefficient \(-1\) is written as a negative sign, giving \(f(x) = -x^2 - \frac{4}{3}x + 7\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = \frac{1}{3} - \frac{5}{6}\), \(b = -\frac{3}{4} + 2\), and \(c = \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 + \frac{9}{8}\).
qs.s: First calculate the coefficients: \(a = \frac{2}{6} - \frac{5}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}\), \(b = -\frac{3}{4} + \frac{8}{4} = \frac{5}{4}\), and \(c = -\frac{1}{8} + \frac{9}{8} = 1\). Substituting these into \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) gives \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + \frac{5}{4}x + 1\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -15 + 4^2 - 3\), \(b = \frac{3}{8} - \frac{7}{12} + \frac{5}{6}\), and \(c = -24 \div (-3) - 13\).
qs.s: Evaluate each coefficient: \(a = -15 + 16 - 3 = -2\), \(b = \frac{9 - 14 + 20}{24} = \frac{15}{24} = \frac{5}{8}\), and \(c = 8 - 13 = -5\). This gives the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2x^2 + \frac{5}{8}x - 5\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = \frac{5}{12} - \frac{7}{6}\), \(b = 4\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) - 2\), and \(c = \frac{7}{2} - \frac{5}{3}\).
qs.s: Evaluate each coefficient: \(a = \frac{5 - 14}{12} = -\frac{3}{4}\), \(b = 2 - 2 = 0\), and \(c = \frac{21 - 10}{6} = \frac{11}{6}\). Since \(b = 0\), omitting the linear term yields \(f(x) = -\frac{3}{4}x^2 + \frac{11}{6}\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), with the given values of coefficients: \(a = -\frac{4}{9} \cdot \frac{3}{8}\), \(b = \frac{5}{6} \div \left(-\frac{5}{12}\right)\), and \(c = 7 - 3 \cdot \frac{8}{3}\).
qs.s: Simplify each coefficient: \(a = -\frac{12}{72} = -\frac{1}{6}\), \(b = \frac{5}{6} \cdot \left(-\frac{12}{5}\right) = -2\), and \(c = 7 - 8 = -1\). Substituting these values gives \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{6}x^2 - 2x - 1\).

qs.q: Write a two-variable quadratic function, \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), given that the coefficients satisfy \(a = -\frac{2}{5}\), \(b = 5a + 3\), and \(c = -2b - \frac{1}{2}\).
qs.s: Calculate the coefficients in sequence: \(a = -\frac{2}{5}\), \(b = 5\left(-\frac{2}{5}\right) + 3 = 1\), and \(c = -2(1) - \frac{1}{2} = -\frac{5}{2}\). Writing the function with \(b = 1\) in simplest form yields \(f(x) = -\frac{2}{5}x^2 + x - \frac{5}{2}\).

exercises.name: Find the vertex of a parabola

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = x^2 - 9\).
qs.s: For \(f(x) = x^2 - 9\), the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{0}{2(1)} = 0\). Substituting \(x = 0\) gives \(f(0) = 0^2 - 9 = -9\), so the vertex is \((0, -9)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = -x^2 + 4\).
qs.s: For \(h(x) = -x^2 + 4\), the \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{0}{2(-1)} = 0\). Evaluating at \(x = 0\) gives \(h(0) = -(0)^2 + 4 = 4\), so the vertex is \((0, 4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(k(x) = x^2 - 25\).
qs.s: For \(k(x) = x^2 - 25\), the \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{0}{2(1)} = 0\). Evaluating at \(x = 0\) gives \(k(0) = 0^2 - 25 = -25\), so the vertex is \((0, -25)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = -x^2 - 3\).
qs.s: For \(p(x) = -x^2 - 3\), the \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{0}{2(-1)} = 0\). Evaluating at \(x = 0\) yields \(p(0) = -(0)^2 - 3 = -3\), so the vertex is \((0, -3)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = x^2 + 7\).
qs.s: For \(g(x) = x^2 + 7\), the \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{0}{2(1)} = 0\). Substituting \(x = 0\) yields \(g(0) = 0^2 + 7 = 7\), so the vertex is \((0, 7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(k(x) = -3x^2 + 18x - 20\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{18}{2(-3)} = 3\). Substituting into the function gives \(k(3) = -3(3)^2 + 18(3) - 20 = 7\), so the vertex is \((3, 7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(m(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 4x + 6\).
qs.s: Using \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-4}{2(1/2)} = 4\), we evaluate \(m(4) = \frac{1}{2}(4)^2 - 4(4) + 6 = -2\). Therefore, the vertex is \((4, -2)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = -x^2 + 4x + 1\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{4}{2(-1)} = 2\). Evaluating \(g(2) = -(2)^2 + 4(2) + 1 = 5\), the vertex is \((2, 5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = 2x^2 - 8x + 3\).
qs.s: Using \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-8}{2(2)} = 2\), we find the \(y\)-coordinate by calculating \(h(2) = 2(2)^2 - 8(2) + 3 = -5\). Thus, the vertex is \((2, -5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 5\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-6}{2(1)} = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) gives \(f(3) = 3^2 - 6(3) + 5 = -4\), so the vertex is \((3, -4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = -2x^2 + 8\).
Find the vertex of the parabola \(k(x) = -x^2 - 7\).
Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = -x^2 + 5\).
qs.s: For \(f(x) = -x^2 + 5\), \(a = -1\), \(b = 0\), and \(c = 5\). The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{0}{2(-1)} = 0\), and \(f(0) = 5\), giving the vertex \((0, 5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = 3x^2 - 6\).
Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = 2x^2 - 12x + 10\).
Find the vertex of the parabola \(m(x) = -3x^2 - 6x + 4\).
qs.s: For \(m(x) = -3x^2 - 6x + 4\), the \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{-6}{2(-3)} = -1\). Evaluating at \(x = -1\) yields \(m(-1) = -3(-1)^2 - 6(-1) + 4 = 7\), so the vertex is \((-1, 7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(q(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 4x + 3\).
qs.s: For \(q(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 4x + 3\), the \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{-4}{2(1/2)} = 4\). Substituting \(x = 4\) yields \(q(4) = \frac{1}{2}(4)^2 - 4(4) + 3 = -5\), so the vertex is \((4, -5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = x^2 - 8x + 16\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{-8}{2(1)} = 4\). Substituting \(x = 4\) yields \(h(4) = (4)^2 - 8(4) + 16 = 0\), so the vertex is \((4, 0)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(k(x) = x^2 - 10x + 28\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{-10}{2(1)} = 5\). Evaluating the function gives \(k(5) = (5)^2 - 10(5) + 28 = 3\), so the vertex is \((5, 3)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(j(x) = x^2 + 2x - 5\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{2}{2(1)} = -1\). Evaluating the function gives \(j(-1) = (-1)^2 + 2(-1) - 5 = -6\), so the vertex is \((-1, -6)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 1\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{-4}{2(1)} = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) gives \(f(2) = (2)^2 - 4(2) + 1 = -3\), so the vertex is \((2, -3)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = x^2 + 6x + 11\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{6}{2(1)} = -3\). Evaluating the function gives \(g(-3) = (-3)^2 + 6(-3) + 11 = 2\), so the vertex is \((-3, 2)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 24x + 41\).
qs.s: Using \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), we find \(x = -\frac{-24}{2(3)} = 4\). Substituting \(x = 4\) yields \(f(4) = 3(4)^2 - 24(4) + 41 = -7\), so the vertex is \((4, -7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(k(x) = -2x^2 + 5x + 3\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{5}{2(-2)} = \frac{5}{4}\). Evaluating the function gives \(k\left(\frac{5}{4}\right) = -2\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)^2 + 5\left(\frac{5}{4}\right) + 3 = \frac{49}{8}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{5}{4}, \frac{49}{8}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 6x - 10\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{6}{2(-1/2)} = 6\). Substituting \(x = 6\) gives \(g(6) = -\frac{1}{2}(6)^2 + 6(6) - 10 = 8\), so the vertex is \((6, 8)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = -x^2 + 5x - 2\).
qs.s: Using \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), we obtain \(x = -\frac{5}{2(-1)} = \frac{5}{2}\). Substituting gives \(p\left(\frac{5}{2}\right) = -\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^2 + 5\left(\frac{5}{2}\right) - 2 = \frac{17}{4}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{5}{2}, \frac{17}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = 2x^2 + 6x - 1\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{6}{2(2)} = -\frac{3}{2}\). Substituting this gives \(h\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right) = 2\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 + 6\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right) - 1 = -\frac{11}{2}\), so the vertex is \(\left(-\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{11}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = x^2 + 10x + 21\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{10}{2(1)} = -5\). Evaluating \(p(-5) = (-5)^2 + 10(-5) + 21 = -4\) gives the vertex \((-5, -4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(q(x) = x^2 - 2x - 11\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{-2}{2(1)} = 1\). Evaluating \(q(1) = 1^2 - 2(1) - 11 = -12\) gives the vertex \((1, -12)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = x^2 + 8x + 7\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{8}{2(1)} = -4\). Evaluating \(f(-4) = (-4)^2 + 8(-4) + 7 = -9\) gives the vertex \((-4, -9)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = x^2 - 6x + 4\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{-6}{2(1)} = 3\). Evaluating \(h(3) = 3^2 - 6(3) + 4 = -5\) gives the vertex \((3, -5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 4x + 3\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{-4}{2(1/2)} = 4\). Substituting \(x = 4\) yields \(y = \frac{1}{2}(4)^2 - 4(4) + 3 = -5\), so the vertex is \((4, -5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = -3x^2 + 12x - 5\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{12}{2(-3)} = 2\). Evaluating \(h(2) = -3(2)^2 + 12(2) - 5 = 7\) gives the vertex \((2, 7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(q(x) = 2x^2 - 6x + 1\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{-6}{2(2)} = \frac{3}{2}\). Substituting \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) yields \(y = 2\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 - 6\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) + 1 = -\frac{7}{2}\), so the vertex is \((3/2, -7/2)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = -x^2 + 5x - 2\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{5}{2(-1)} = \frac{5}{2}\). Substituting this into the function gives \(y = -\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^2 + 5\left(\frac{5}{2}\right) - 2 = \frac{17}{4}\), so the vertex is \((5/2, 17/4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = -\frac{1}{3}x^2 + 2x + 1\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{2}{2(-1/3)} = 3\). Evaluating \(p(3) = -\frac{1}{3}(3)^2 + 2(3) + 1 = 4\) gives the vertex \((3, 4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = 2x^2 - 20x + 47\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{-20}{2(2)} = 5\). Evaluating the function gives \(p(5) = 2(5)^2 - 20(5) + 47 = -3\), so the vertex is \((5, -3)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = -3x^2 - 6x + 4\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{-6}{2(-3)} = -1\). Evaluating the function gives \(g(-1) = -3(-1)^2 - 6(-1) + 4 = 7\), so the vertex is \((-1, 7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 12x + 11\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{-12}{2(2)} = 3\). Evaluating the function gives \(f(3) = 2(3)^2 - 12(3) + 11 = -7\), so the vertex is \((3, -7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(k(x) = -4x^2 + 16x - 11\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{16}{2(-4)} = 2\). Evaluating the function gives \(k(2) = -4(2)^2 + 16(2) - 11 = 5\), so the vertex is \((2, 5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = 4x^2 + 16x - 5\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{16}{2(4)} = -2\). Evaluating the function gives \(h(-2) = 4(-2)^2 + 16(-2) - 5 = -21\), so the vertex is \((-2, -21)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(m(x) = -\frac{2}{3}x^2 + 3x - 1\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{3}{2(-2/3)} = \frac{9}{4}\). Substituting \(x = \frac{9}{4}\) gives \(m\left(\frac{9}{4}\right) = -\frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^2 + 3\left(\frac{9}{4}\right) - 1 = \frac{19}{8}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{9}{4}, \frac{19}{8}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = -6x^2 + 84x - 275\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{84}{2(-6)} = 7\). Substituting \(x = 7\) gives \(h(7) = -6(7)^2 + 84(7) - 275 = 19\), so the vertex is \((7, 19)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = -\frac{1}{3}x^2 + 4x - 7\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{4}{2(-1/3)} = 6\). Substituting \(x = 6\) gives \(g(6) = -\frac{1}{3}(6)^2 + 4(6) - 7 = 5\), so the vertex is \((6, 5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(k(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 3x + \frac{1}{4}\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{-3}{2(1/2)} = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) gives \(k(3) = \frac{1}{2}(3)^2 - 3(3) + \frac{1}{4} = -\frac{17}{4}\), so the vertex is \(\left(3, -\frac{17}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 6x + 1\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{-6}{2(2)} = \frac{3}{2}\). Substituting \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) gives \(f\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) = 2\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 - 6\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) + 1 = -\frac{7}{2}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{7}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = \frac{1}{4}x^2 - 2x - 3\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-2}{2(1/4)} = 4\). Evaluating \(p(4) = \frac{1}{4}(4)^2 - 2(4) - 3 = -7\), so the vertex is \((4, -7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(m(x) = -\frac{1}{4}x^2 + x + 2\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{1}{2(-1/4)} = 2\). Evaluating \(m(2) = -\frac{1}{4}(2)^2 + (2) + 2 = 3\), so the vertex is \((2, 3)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = \frac{1}{3}x^2 - 2x + 1\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-2}{2(1/3)} = 3\). Evaluating \(h(3) = \frac{1}{3}(3)^2 - 2(3) + 1 = -2\), so the vertex is \((3, -2)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 4x + 3\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-4}{2(1/2)} = 4\). Evaluating \(f(4) = \frac{1}{2}(4)^2 - 4(4) + 3 = -5\), so the vertex is \((4, -5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 2x + 5\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{2}{2(-1/2)} = 2\). Evaluating \(g(2) = -\frac{1}{2}(2)^2 + 2(2) + 5 = 7\), so the vertex is \((2, 7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 14x + 75\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{-14}{2(1/2)} = 14\). Evaluating \(h(14) = \frac{1}{2}(14)^2 - 14(14) + 75 = -23\), so the vertex is \((14, -23)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(q(x) = 0.4x^2 + 2x - 5\).
Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + \frac{3}{4}x + \frac{5}{8}\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{3/4}{2(-1/2)} = \frac{3}{4}\). Evaluating \(p\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) = -\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2 + \frac{3}{4}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) + \frac{5}{8} = \frac{29}{32}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{3}{4}, \frac{29}{32}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = 3x^2 - 8x + 9 - x^2 + 2x - 1\).
qs.s: Combining like terms gives \(g(x) = 2x^2 - 6x + 8\). Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{-6}{2(2)} = \frac{3}{2}\), and substituting gives \(g\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) = \frac{7}{2}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, \frac{7}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{3}x^2 + 3x - 4\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{3}{2(-1/3)} = \frac{9}{2}\). Evaluating \(f\left(\frac{9}{2}\right) = -\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{9}{2}\right)^2 + 3\left(\frac{9}{2}\right) - 4 = \frac{11}{4}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{9}{2}, \frac{11}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = -3x^2 + 6x - 7\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, the \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{6}{2(-3)} = 1\). Substituting \(x = 1\) gives \(p(1) = -3(1)^2 + 6(1) - 7 = -4\), so the vertex is \((1, -4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(m(x) = 2x^2 + 8x + 3\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, the \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{8}{2(2)} = -2\). Substituting \(x = -2\) gives \(m(-2) = 2(-2)^2 + 8(-2) + 3 = -5\), so the vertex is \((-2, -5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = -4x^2 + 16x - 13\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, the \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{16}{2(-4)} = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) gives \(h(2) = -4(2)^2 + 16(2) - 13 = 3\), so the vertex is \((2, 3)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = -2x^2 - 8x - 5\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, the \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-8}{2(-2)} = -2\). Substituting \(x = -2\) gives \(f(-2) = -2(-2)^2 - 8(-2) - 5 = 3\), so the vertex is \((-2, 3)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + 7\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, the \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-12}{2(3)} = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) gives \(g(2) = 3(2)^2 - 12(2) + 7 = -5\), so the vertex is \((2, -5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = -\frac{3}{4}x^2 + 6x - 7\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, the \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{6}{2\left(-\frac{3}{4}\right)} = 4\). Substituting \(x = 4\) into the function gives \(f(4) = -\frac{3}{4}(16) + 6(4) - 7 = 5\), so the vertex is \((4, 5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(k(x) = -2x^2 + 40x - 163\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, the \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{40}{2(-2)} = 10\). Substituting \(x = 10\) into the equation gives \(k(10) = -2(100) + 40(10) - 163 = 37\), so the vertex is \((10, 37)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = 10x - 2x^2 + 6x - 25\).
qs.s: Combine like terms to write the function in general form as \(h(x) = -2x^2 + 16x - 25\). Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{16}{2(-2)} = 4\), and substituting yields \(h(4) = -2(16) + 16(4) - 25 = 7\), giving vertex \((4, 7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = 3x^2 - 5x + 4\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, the \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{-5}{2(3)} = \frac{5}{6}\). Substituting \(x = \frac{5}{6}\) gives \(g\left(\frac{5}{6}\right) = 3\left(\frac{25}{36}\right) - 5\left(\frac{5}{6}\right) + 4 = \frac{23}{12}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{5}{6}, \frac{23}{12}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + \frac{3}{2}x - 2\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{3/2}{2(-1/2)} = \frac{3}{2}\). Substituting gives \(p\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) = -\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{9}{4}\right) + \frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) - 2 = -\frac{7}{8}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{7}{8}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = -3x^2 - 18x - 23\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{-18}{2(-3)} = -3\). Evaluating gives \(p(-3) = -3(-3)^2 - 18(-3) - 23 = 4\), so the vertex is \((-3, 4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + 7\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{-12}{2(3)} = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) gives \(f(2) = 3(2)^2 - 12(2) + 7 = -5\), so the vertex is \((2, -5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = -2x^2 + 8x - 5\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{8}{2(-2)} = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) gives \(g(2) = -2(2)^2 + 8(2) - 5 = 3\), so the vertex is \((2, 3)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = 2x^2 + 12x + 13\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{12}{2(2)} = -3\). Substituting \(x = -3\) yields \(h(-3) = 2(-3)^2 + 12(-3) + 13 = -5\), giving the vertex \((-3, -5)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(k(x) = 3x^2 + 6x - 1\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{6}{2(3)} = -1\). Substituting \(x = -1\) into the function gives \(k(-1) = 3(-1)^2 + 6(-1) - 1 = -4\), so the vertex is \((-1, -4)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = 3x(x - 4) - 2x + 7\).
qs.s: Expanding the expression gives \(p(x) = 3x^2 - 14x + 7\). The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{-14}{2(3)} = \frac{7}{3}\), and substituting gives \(p\left(\frac{7}{3}\right) = -\frac{28}{3}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{7}{3}, -\frac{28}{3}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = -\frac{1}{4}x^2 + \frac{2}{3}x + 1\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{2/3}{2(-1/4)} = \frac{4}{3}\). Evaluating gives \(g\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) = -\frac{1}{4}\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)^2 + \frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) + 1 = \frac{13}{9}\), giving the vertex \(\left(\frac{4}{3}, \frac{13}{9}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = -4x^2 + 72x - 311\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{72}{2(-4)} = 9\). Evaluating gives \(h(9) = -4(9)^2 + 72(9) - 311 = 13\), so the vertex is \((9, 13)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 5x + 1\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{-5}{2(2)} = \frac{5}{4}\). Substituting into \(f(x)\) yields \(f\left(\frac{5}{4}\right) = 2\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)^2 - 5\left(\frac{5}{4}\right) + 1 = -\frac{17}{8}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{5}{4}, -\frac{17}{8}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(r(x) = 0.2x^2 - 1.6x + 5.8\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{-1.6}{2(0.2)} = 4\). Substituting \(x = 4\) into \(r(x)\) gives \(r(4) = 0.2(4)^2 - 1.6(4) + 5.8 = 2.6\), so the vertex is \((4, 2.6)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = -2x^2 + 5x - 1\).
qs.s: The x-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{5}{2(-2)} = \frac{5}{4}\), and substituting gives \(y = -2\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)^2 + 5\left(\frac{5}{4}\right) - 1 = \frac{17}{8}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{5}{4}, \frac{17}{8}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = 2x^2 + 3x - 2\).
qs.s: The x-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{3}{2(2)} = -\frac{3}{4}\), and substituting gives \(y = 2\left(-\frac{3}{4}\right)^2 + 3\left(-\frac{3}{4}\right) - 2 = -\frac{25}{8}\), so the vertex is \(\left(-\frac{3}{4}, -\frac{25}{8}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = 4x^2 - 6x + 1\).
qs.s: The x-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-6}{2(4)} = \frac{3}{4}\), and substituting gives \(y = 4\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2 - 6\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) + 1 = -\frac{5}{4}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{3}{4}, -\frac{5}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(k(x) = -3x^2 + 6x - 5\).
qs.s: The x-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{6}{2(-3)} = 1\), and substituting gives \(y = -3(1)^2 + 6(1) - 5 = -2\), so the vertex is \((1, -2)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1\).
qs.s: The x-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{-4}{2(3)} = \frac{2}{3}\), and substituting gives \(y = 3\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 - 4\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) + 1 = -\frac{1}{3}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{2}{3}, -\frac{1}{3}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = -(x - 4)^2 + 6x - 7\).
qs.s: Expanding and collecting like terms yields \(h(x) = -x^2 + 14x - 23\). The x-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{14}{2(-1)} = 7\), and evaluating gives \(y = -(7)^2 + 14(7) - 23 = 26\), so the vertex is \((7, 26)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = 0.4x^2 - 2x + 1.5\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{-2}{2(0.4)} = 2.5\). Substituting into \(p(x)\) gives \(y = 0.4(2.5)^2 - 2(2.5) + 1.5 = -1\), so the vertex is \((2.5, -1)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = (2x + 1)(x - 3) + 4x - 5\).
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying gives \(f(x) = 2x^2 - x - 8\). The vertex has \(x = -\frac{-1}{2(2)} = \frac{1}{4}\) and \(y = 2\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{1}{4}\right) - 8 = -\frac{65}{8}\), giving \(\left(\frac{1}{4}, -\frac{65}{8}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + \frac{2}{3}x + 1\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{2/3}{2(-1/2)} = \frac{2}{3}\). Substituting into \(g(x)\) gives \(y = -\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 + \frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) + 1 = \frac{11}{9}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{2}{3}, \frac{11}{9}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(m(x) = 5x^2 - 8x + 11\).
qs.s: Using \(a = 5\) and \(b = -8\), the x-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{-8}{2(5)} = \frac{4}{5}\). Evaluating gives \(y = 5\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^2 - 8\left(\frac{4}{5}\right) + 11 = \frac{39}{5}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{4}{5}, \frac{39}{5}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(q(x) = -\frac{1}{3}x^2 + x + 2\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{1}{2(-1/3)} = \frac{3}{2}\). Substituting gives \(q\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) = -\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{3}{2} + 2 = \frac{11}{4}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, \frac{11}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{4}x^2 + 3x - 2\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{3}{2(-1/4)} = 6\). Evaluating at \(x = 6\) gives \(h(6) = -\frac{1}{4}(6)^2 + 3(6) - 2 = 7\), so the vertex is \((6, 7)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 + 3x - 1\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{3}{2(1/2)} = -3\). Substituting into the function gives \(p(-3) = \frac{1}{2}(-3)^2 + 3(-3) - 1 = -\frac{11}{2}\), so the vertex is \(\left(-3, -\frac{11}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 5x - 3\).
qs.s: Using the vertex formula, \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{5}{2(-1/2)} = 5\). Substituting \(x = 5\) gives \(f(5) = -\frac{1}{2}(5)^2 + 5(5) - 3 = \frac{19}{2}\), so the vertex is \(\left(5, \frac{19}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(p(x) = \frac{2}{5}x^2 - 3x + \frac{7}{4}\).
qs.s: We find \(x = -\frac{-3}{2(2/5)} = \frac{15}{4}\). Substituting gives \(p\left(\frac{15}{4}\right) = \frac{2}{5}\left(\frac{225}{16}\right) - 3\left(\frac{15}{4}\right) + \frac{7}{4} = -\frac{31}{8}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{15}{4}, -\frac{31}{8}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(g(x) = -\frac{1}{6}x^2 + 7x - 45\).
Find the vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = -\frac{3}{4}x^2 + \frac{2}{3}x + \frac{1}{2}\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{2/3}{2(-3/4)} = \frac{4}{9}\). Evaluating at \(x = \frac{4}{9}\) gives \(f\left(\frac{4}{9}\right) = -\frac{3}{4}\left(\frac{16}{81}\right) + \frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{4}{9}\right) + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{35}{54}\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{4}{9}, \frac{35}{54}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(k(x) = -\frac{2}{3}x^2 - \frac{5}{2}x + 1\).
qs.s: The \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = -\frac{-5/2}{2(-2/3)} = -\frac{15}{8}\). Evaluating the function gives \(k\left(-\frac{15}{8}\right) = -\frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{225}{64}\right) - \frac{5}{2}\left(-\frac{15}{8}\right) + 1 = \frac{107}{32}\), so the vertex is \(\left(-\frac{15}{8}, \frac{107}{32}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(h(x) = 2(x - 3)(x + 5) - 3(x^2 - 2x + 1)\).
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms yields \(h(x) = -x^2 + 10x - 33\). Then \(x = -\frac{10}{2(-1)} = 5\), and substituting gives \(h(5) = -(5)^2 + 10(5) - 33 = -8\), so the vertex is \((5, -8)\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 5x + 4\).
qs.s: Since \(a = 3 > 0\), the parabola opens upward and has a minimum value at \(x = -\frac{-5}{2(3)} = \frac{5}{6}\). The minimum value is \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = 4 - \frac{25}{4(3)} = 4 - \frac{25}{12} = \frac{23}{12}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 3x + 5\).
qs.s: Since \(a = -2 < 0\), the parabola opens downward and has a maximum value at \(x = -\frac{3}{2(-2)} = \frac{3}{4}\). The maximum value is \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = 5 - \frac{9}{4(-2)} = 5 + \frac{9}{8} = \frac{49}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -3x^2 - 4x + 2\).
qs.s: Since \(a = -3 < 0\), the function has a maximum value at \(x = -\frac{-4}{2(-3)} = -\frac{2}{3}\). The maximum value is \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = 2 - \frac{16}{4(-3)} = 2 + \frac{4}{3} = \frac{10}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 2x^2 + 5x - 1\).
qs.s: Since \(a = 2 > 0\), the parabola opens upward and has a minimum value at \(x = -\frac{5}{2(2)} = -\frac{5}{4}\). Substituting \(x = -\frac{5}{4}\) gives \(f\left(-\frac{5}{4}\right) = 2\left(-\frac{5}{4}\right)^2 + 5\left(-\frac{5}{4}\right) - 1 = -\frac{33}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the quadratic function \(f(x) = 4x^2 - 6x + 5\).
qs.s: Since \(a = 4 > 0\), the parabola has a minimum value at \(x = -\frac{-6}{2(4)} = \frac{3}{4}\). The minimum value is \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = 5 - \frac{36}{4(4)} = 5 - \frac{9}{4} = \frac{11}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the function \(f(x) = (3x - 2)(x + 1) - (x - 3)^2\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(f(x) = (3x^2 + x - 2) - (x^2 - 6x + 9) = 2x^2 + 7x - 11\). Since \(a = 2 > 0\), it has a minimum value of \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = -11 - \frac{49}{4(2)} = -11 - \frac{49}{8} = -\frac{137}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the quadratic function \(f(x) = \frac{3}{4}x^2 - 5x + 6\).
qs.s: Since \(a = \frac{3}{4} > 0\), the function has a minimum value at \(x = -\frac{-5}{2(3/4)} = \frac{10}{3}\). The minimum value is \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = 6 - \frac{25}{4(3/4)} = 6 - \frac{25}{3} = -\frac{7}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the quadratic function \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + \frac{5}{3}x - 2\).
qs.s: Since \(a = -\frac{1}{2} < 0\), the function has a maximum value at \(x = -\frac{5/3}{2(-1/2)} = \frac{5}{3}\). The maximum value is \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = -2 - \frac{25/9}{4(-1/2)} = -2 + \frac{25}{18} = -\frac{11}{18}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the function \(f(x) = (2x - 1)(x + 4) - 3x(x - 2)\).
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying yields \(f(x) = (2x^2 + 7x - 4) - (3x^2 - 6x) = -x^2 + 13x - 4\). Since \(a = -1 < 0\), the function has a maximum value of \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = -4 - \frac{169}{4(-1)} = \frac{153}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the function \(f(x) = 5 - 2(x + 2)(3x - 1)\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(f(x) = 5 - 2(3x^2 + 5x - 2) = -6x^2 - 10x + 9\). Since \(a = -6 < 0\), it has a maximum value of \(c - \frac{b^2}{4a} = 9 - \frac{100}{4(-6)} = 9 + \frac{25}{6} = \frac{79}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = x^2 + 6x + 5\).
qs.s: Since \(a = 1 > 0\), the parabola opens upward and has a minimum value. The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{6}{2(1)} = -3\), giving a minimum value of \(f(-3) = (-3)^2 + 6(-3) + 5 = -4\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = -x^2 + 6x - 2\).
qs.s: Since \(a = -1 < 0\), the parabola opens downward and has a maximum value. The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{6}{2(-1)} = 3\), giving a maximum value of \(f(3) = -(3)^2 + 6(3) - 2 = 7\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 4x + 3\).
qs.s: Since \(a = \frac{1}{2} > 0\), the parabola opens upward and has a minimum value. The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{-4}{2(1/2)} = 4\), so the minimum value is \(f(4) = \frac{1}{2}(4)^2 - 4(4) + 3 = -5\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 8x + 1\).
qs.s: Since \(a = 2 > 0\), the parabola opens upward and has a minimum value. The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{-8}{2(2)} = 2\), so the minimum value is \(f(2) = 2(2)^2 - 8(2) + 1 = -7\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 - 2x + 6\).
qs.s: Since \(a = -\frac{1}{2} < 0\), the parabola opens downward and has a maximum value. The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{-2}{2(-1/2)} = -2\), giving a maximum value of \(f(-2) = -\frac{1}{2}(-2)^2 - 2(-2) + 6 = 8\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = 15 - 2x(x + 4)\).
qs.s: Rewriting in standard form gives \(f(x) = -2x^2 - 8x + 15\). Since \(a = -2 < 0\), the parabola has a maximum value at \(x = -\frac{-8}{2(-2)} = -2\), which gives \(f(-2) = 15 - 2(-2)(2) = 23\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = 4x^2 - 40x + 117\).
qs.s: Since \(a = 4 > 0\), the parabola opens upward and has a minimum value. The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{-40}{2(4)} = 5\), giving \(f(5) = 4(25) - 40(5) + 117 = 17\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{4}x^2 + 3x - \frac{7}{2}\).
qs.s: Since \(a = -\frac{1}{4} < 0\), the parabola has a maximum value at \(x = -\frac{3}{2(-1/4)} = 6\). Evaluating at \(x = 6\) yields \(f(6) = -\frac{1}{4}(36) + 3(6) - \frac{7}{2} = 9 - \frac{7}{2} = \frac{11}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = 3(x - 2)(x + 4) + 5\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(f(x) = 3(x^2 + 2x - 8) + 5 = 3x^2 + 6x - 19\). Since \(a = 3 > 0\), the parabola has a minimum value at \(x = -\frac{6}{2(3)} = -1\), which is \(f(-1) = 3(-3)(3) + 5 = -22\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 6x - 1\).
qs.s: Since \(a = -2 < 0\), the parabola has a maximum value at \(x = -\frac{6}{2(-2)} = \frac{3}{2}\). Substituting gives \(f\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) = -2\left(\frac{9}{4}\right) + 6\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) - 1 = -\frac{9}{2} + 8 = \frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = 4x^2 + 16x + 9\).
qs.s: Since \(a = 4 > 0\), the parabola opens upward and has a minimum value. The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{16}{2(4)} = -2\), so the minimum value is \(f(-2) = 4(-2)^2 + 16(-2) + 9 = -7\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = -x^2 - 6x - 4\).
qs.s: Since \(a = -1 < 0\), the parabola opens downward and has a maximum value. The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{-6}{2(-1)} = -3\), so the maximum value is \(f(-3) = -(-3)^2 - 6(-3) - 4 = 5\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 8x + 11\).
qs.s: Since \(a = 2 > 0\), the parabola opens upward and has a minimum value. The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{-8}{2(2)} = 2\), yielding a minimum value of \(f(2) = 2(2)^2 - 8(2) + 11 = 3\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + 7\).
qs.s: Since \(a = 3 > 0\), the parabola opens upward and has a minimum value. The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{-12}{2(3)} = 2\), so the minimum value is \(f(2) = 3(2)^2 - 12(2) + 7 = -5\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = -4x^2 + 48x - 119\).
qs.s: Since \(a = -4 < 0\), the parabola opens downward and has a maximum value. The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{48}{2(-4)} = 6\), so the maximum value is \(f(6) = -4(36) + 48(6) - 119 = 25\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = -2(x - 1)(x + 5) + 6x - 7\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(f(x) = -2(x^2 + 4x - 5) + 6x - 7 = -2x^2 - 2x + 3\). Since \(a = -2 < 0\), the function has a maximum at \(x = -\frac{-2}{2(-2)} = -\frac{1}{2}\), giving \(f\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = -2\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) - 2\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) + 3 = \frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = -(2x - 1)^2 + 8x + 5\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(f(x) = -(4x^2 - 4x + 1) + 8x + 5 = -4x^2 + 12x + 4\). Since \(a = -4 < 0\), the function has a maximum at \(x = -\frac{12}{2(-4)} = \frac{3}{2}\), giving a maximum value of \(f\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) = -4\left(\frac{9}{4}\right) + 12\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) + 4 = 13\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = \frac{1}{3}x^2 - 4x + 17\).
qs.s: Since \(a = \frac{1}{3} > 0\), the parabola opens upward and has a minimum value. The vertex is at \(x = -\frac{-4}{2(1/3)} = 6\), giving a minimum value of \(f(6) = \frac{1}{3}(36) - 4(6) + 17 = 5\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 2x\).
qs.s: Since \(a = 3 > 0\), the parabola opens upward and has a minimum value at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = \frac{1}{3}\). Substituting gives \(f\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) = 3\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^2 - 2\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) = -\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 5x\).
qs.s: Since \(a = 2 > 0\), the parabola opens upward and has a minimum value at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = \frac{5}{4}\). Substituting gives \(f\left(\frac{5}{4}\right) = 2\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)^2 - 5\left(\frac{5}{4}\right) = -\frac{25}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = -5x^2 + 4x\).
qs.s: Since \(a = -5 < 0\), the parabola opens downward and has a maximum value at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = \frac{2}{5}\). Substituting gives \(f\left(\frac{2}{5}\right) = -5\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^2 + 4\left(\frac{2}{5}\right) = \frac{4}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = -2x^2 + 3x\).
qs.s: Since \(a = -2 < 0\), the parabola opens downward and has a maximum value at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = \frac{3}{4}\). Substituting gives \(f\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) = -2\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2 + 3\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) = \frac{9}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = 2x^2 + x\).
qs.s: Since \(a = 2 > 0\), the parabola opens upward and has a minimum value at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{1}{4}\). Substituting gives \(f\left(-\frac{1}{4}\right) = 2\left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)^2 + \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right) = -\frac{1}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + \frac{3}{2}x - 1\).
qs.s: Since \(a = -\frac{1}{2} < 0\), the maximum occurs at \(x = -\frac{3/2}{2(-1/2)} = \frac{3}{2}\). Substituting gives \(f\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) = -\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) - 1 = \frac{1}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = (2x + 3)(x - 5)\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 7x - 15\), which opens upward and has a minimum at \(x = -\frac{-7}{2(2)} = \frac{7}{4}\). Evaluating gives \(f\left(\frac{7}{4}\right) = \left(2\cdot\frac{7}{4}+3\right)\left(\frac{7}{4}-5\right) = -\frac{169}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = \frac{2}{3}x^2 - 3x + 1\).
qs.s: Since \(a = \frac{2}{3} > 0\), the minimum occurs at \(x = -\frac{-3}{2(2/3)} = \frac{9}{4}\). Substituting gives \(f\left(\frac{9}{4}\right) = \frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^2 - 3\left(\frac{9}{4}\right) + 1 = -\frac{19}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the maximum or minimum value of the parabola \(f(x) = 1 - 2x(3x + 4)\).
