qs.s: The maximum height occurs at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{2.4}{2(-0.02)} = 60\text{ feet}\). Evaluating the function at \(x = 60\) yields \(h(60) = -0.02(60)^2 + 2.4(60) + 8 = -72 + 144 + 8 = 80\text{ feet}\).

qs.q: A golf ball is hit from an elevated tee box. Its flight path is modeled by the function \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{80} x^2 + \frac{3}{2} x + 5\), where \(h(x)\) is the height in yards and \(x\) is the horizontal distance in yards from the tee. What is the maximum height reached by the ball?
qs.s: The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{3/2}{2(-1/80)} = 60\text{ yards}\). Substituting \(x = 60\) gives \(h(60) = -\frac{1}{80}(60)^2 + \frac{3}{2}(60) + 5 = -45 + 90 + 5 = 50\text{ yards}\).

qs.q: A firework is launched from a platform 10 feet above the ground. Its path is modeled by \(h(x) = -\frac{3}{400} x^2 + 3x + 10\), where \(h(x)\) is the height in feet and \(x\) is the horizontal distance in feet. What is the maximum height reached by the firework?
qs.s: The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{3}{2(-3/400)} = 200\text{ feet}\). Substituting \(x = 200\) gives a maximum height of \(h(200) = -\frac{3}{400}(200)^2 + 3(200) + 10 = -300 + 600 + 10 = 310\text{ feet}\).

qs.q: An arrow is shot from an elevated platform. Its trajectory is modeled by \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{120} x^2 + x + 15\), where \(h(x)\) is the height in feet and \(x\) is the horizontal distance in feet. What is the maximum height reached by the arrow?
qs.s: The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{1}{2(-1/120)} = 60\text{ feet}\). Substituting \(x = 60\) gives a maximum height of \(h(60) = -\frac{1}{120}(60)^2 + 60 + 15 = -30 + 60 + 15 = 45\text{ feet}\).

qs.q: A flare is fired from the deck of a ship. Its height \(h(x)\) in meters is modeled by \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{250} x^2 + \frac{4}{5} x + 24\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance in meters from the ship. What is the maximum height reached by the flare?
qs.s: The peak horizontal distance is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{4/5}{2(-1/250)} = 100\text{ meters}\). Evaluating at \(x = 100\) gives \(h(100) = -\frac{1}{250}(100)^2 + \frac{4}{5}(100) + 24 = -40 + 80 + 24 = 64\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: Water sprayed from a garden hose at ground level follows a path given by \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{20} x^2 + 2x\), where \(h(x)\) is the height in feet and \(x\) is the horizontal distance in feet from the nozzle. How far horizontally does the stream of water travel before hitting the ground?
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) gives \(x\left(-\frac{1}{20}x + 2\right) = 0\). Solving for the non-zero root yields \(-\frac{1}{20}x + 2 = 0\), so \(x = 40\) feet.

qs.q: A kickball is kicked upwards from ground level across a playground. Its height \(h(x)\) in feet is given by \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{50} x^2 + x\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance traveled in feet. How far did the kickball travel horizontally before landing?
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) yields \(x\left(-\frac{1}{50}x + 1\right) = 0\). For \(x > 0\), solving \(-\frac{1}{50}x + 1 = 0\) gives \(x = 50\) feet.

qs.q: A soccer ball is kicked from ground level. Its height \(h(x)\) in meters is modeled by \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{30} x^2 + x\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance the ball traveled in meters. How far did the soccer ball travel horizontally before hitting the ground?
qs.s: Set \(h(x) = 0\) to find when the ball lands: \(x\left(-\frac{1}{30}x + 1\right) = 0\). Since the landing point has \(x > 0\), \(-\frac{1}{30}x + 1 = 0\) gives \(x = 30\) meters.

qs.q: A tennis ball is launched from ground level by a training machine. Its height \(s(x)\) in feet is given by \(s(x) = -\frac{1}{80} x^2 + x\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance traveled in feet. How far did the tennis ball travel horizontally when it hit the ground?
qs.s: Set \(s(x) = 0\) to get \(x\left(-\frac{1}{80}x + 1\right) = 0\). Discarding the launch point \(x = 0\), we have \(-\frac{1}{80}x + 1 = 0\), which gives \(x = 80\) feet.

qs.q: A golf ball is struck from ground level. Its height \(h(x)\) in yards is given by the function \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{100} x^2 + 2x\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance the ball traveled in yards. How far did the golf ball travel horizontally before hitting the ground?
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) gives \(x\left(-\frac{1}{100}x + 2\right) = 0\). Since \(x > 0\), solving \(-\frac{1}{100}x + 2 = 0\) yields \(x = 200\) yards.

qs.q: A golfer hits a golf ball from ground level toward an elevated green that is 15 feet above the ground. The height \(h(x)\) of the ball in feet is modeled by \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{80} x^2 + x\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance in feet. As the ball is descending, it lands on the green. What horizontal distance did the ball travel before landing?
qs.s: Set \(h(x) = 15\), which rearranges to \(x^2 - 80x + 1200 = 0\) or \((x - 20)(x - 60) = 0\). Since the ball lands while descending, we select the larger root, \(x = 60\) feet.

qs.q: An archer shoots an arrow from ground level. Its height \(h(x)\) in feet is given by the function \(h(x) = -\frac{2}{375} x^2 + \frac{4}{5} x\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance traveled in feet. How far did the arrow travel horizontally before hitting the ground?
qs.s: Set \(h(x) = 0\) to get \(x\left(-\frac{2}{375}x + \frac{4}{5}\right) = 0\). Solving \(-\frac{2}{375}x + \frac{4}{5} = 0\) gives \(x = \frac{4}{5} \cdot \frac{375}{2} = 150\) feet.

qs.q: A stunt motorcycle launches off a 30-foot-high ramp. Its height \(h(x)\) in feet above the ground is given by \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{90} x^2 + \frac{2}{3} x + 30\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance in feet from the end of the ramp. How far did the motorcycle travel horizontally before landing on the ground?
qs.s: Setting \(h(x) = 0\) and multiplying by \(-90\) gives \(x^2 - 60x - 2700 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x - 90)(x + 30) = 0\), so the motorcycle traveled \(90\) feet horizontally.

qs.q: A football is thrown from an elevated platform 24 feet above the ground. Its height \(h(x)\) in feet is given by \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{100} x^2 + x + 24\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance in feet from the platform. How far did the football travel horizontally before hitting the ground?
qs.s: Set \(h(x) = 0\) and multiply by \(-100\) to obtain \(x^2 - 100x - 2400 = 0\). Factoring as \((x - 120)(x + 20) = 0\) and taking the positive root gives \(x = 120\) feet.

qs.q: An emergency flare is fired from the top of a 60-foot sea cliff. Its height \(h(x)\) in feet above the water is given by \(h(x) = -\frac{1}{200} x^2 + \frac{7}{10} x + 60\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance in feet from the launch site. How far did the flare travel horizontally before splashing into the water?
qs.s: Set \(h(x) = 0\) and multiply by \(-200\) to get \(x^2 - 140x - 12000 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 200)(x + 60) = 0\), so the positive distance is \(x = 200\) feet.

exercises.name: Revenue and income optimization from quadratic model

qs.q: A manufacturer of headphones has found that the revenue \(R\) (in dollars) from sales is a function of the unit price \(p\) (in dollars) that it charges: \(R = -2p^2 + 600p\). What unit price \(p\) should be charged to maximize revenue?
qs.s: The quadratic function \(R = -2p^2 + 600p\) reaches its maximum at the vertex \(p = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{600}{2(-2)} = 150\). Therefore, a unit price of $150 should be charged to maximize revenue.

qs.q: An electronics company determines that the daily revenue \(R\) (in dollars) from selling portable speakers is given by \(R = -\frac{1}{4}p^2 + 100p\), where \(p\) is the unit price in dollars. What is the maximum daily revenue?
qs.s: The maximum occurs at the vertex \(p = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{100}{2(-1/4)} = 200\). Substituting \(p = 200\) yields the maximum revenue $R = -\frac{1}{4}(200)^2 + 100(200) = $10,000.

qs.q: A software developer determines that the daily revenue \(R\) (in dollars) from sales of a mobile app is given by \(R = -5p^2 + 150p\), where \(p\) is the price in dollars charged per download. What unit price \(p\) should be charged to maximize daily revenue?
qs.s: The maximum revenue occurs at the vertex \(p = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{150}{2(-5)} = 15\). Therefore, the developer should charge $15 per download to maximize revenue.

qs.q: A local bakery finds that its weekly revenue \(R\) (in dollars) from selling custom cakes is given by \(R = -p^2 + 80p\), where \(p\) is the price in dollars charged per cake. What price \(p\) should be charged to maximize the weekly revenue?
qs.s: The maximum revenue occurs at the vertex \(p = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{80}{2(-1)} = 40\). Thus, a price of $40 per cake maximizes weekly revenue.

qs.q: A clothing retailer finds that the revenue \(R\) (in dollars) from selling a line of winter coats is given by \(R = -\frac{1}{2}p^2 + 120p\), where \(p\) is the price in dollars per coat. What is the maximum revenue?
qs.s: The vertex occurs at \(p = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{120}{2(-1/2)} = 120\). Substituting \(p = 120\) gives the maximum revenue $R = -\frac{1}{2}(120)^2 + 120(120) = $7,200.

qs.q: An online education platform determines that the net revenue \(R\) (in dollars) from a professional certificate program depends on the enrollment fee \(p\) (in dollars) according to \(R(p) = -\frac{2}{5}p^2 + 240p - 11000\). What is the maximum net revenue the platform can earn?

A market research analyst determines that the daily demand \(q\) for a specialty appliance is related to its price \(p\) (in dollars) by the equation \(q = 500 - 2p\). Since revenue is defined as \(R = p \cdot q\), what is the maximum daily revenue?
qs.s: The revenue function is \(R(p) = -2p^2 + 500p\), which has its vertex at \(p = -\frac{500}{2(-2)} = 125\). The maximum revenue is $R(125) = 125(500 - 2(125)) = 125(250) = $31,250.

qs.q: An industrial machinery company models its monthly revenue \(R\) (in dollars) as a function of the number of machines sold, \(x\), by the quadratic function \(R(x) = -2x^2 + 1800x - 50000\). What is the maximum monthly revenue the company can achieve?

A community theater finds that at a ticket price of $30, it sells 500 tickets per show. For each $1 increase in ticket price, 10 fewer tickets are sold. The revenue per show is given by \(R(x) = (30 + x)(500 - 10x)\), where \(x\) is the number of $1 increases. What is the maximum revenue per show?
qs.s: Expanding yields \(R(x) = -10x^2 + 200x + 15000\), which has its maximum at \(x = -\frac{200}{2(-10)} = 10\). Substituting \(x = 10\) into \(R(x)\) gives $(30 + 10)(500 - 100) = (40)(400) = $16,000.

qs.q: A gym currently has 600 members who each pay a monthly fee of $40. Management estimates that for each $2 increase in the monthly fee, 10 members will leave. The monthly income \(I\) (in dollars) is modeled by \(I(x) = (40 + 2x)(600 - 10x)\), where \(x\) is the number of $2 increases. What monthly fee should the gym charge to maximize its income?
qs.s: Expanding gives \(I(x) = -20x^2 + 800x + 24000\), which reaches its maximum at \(x = -\frac{800}{2(-20)} = 20\). The optimal monthly fee is $40 + 2(20) = $80.

qs.q: A homeowner has \(80\text{ m}\) of fencing to create a rectangular garden along the straight exterior wall of a house. If no fence is needed along the wall, what is the largest area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: With width \(x\) perpendicular to the wall, the length is \(80 - 2x\). The area is \(A(x) = x(80 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 80x\), which reaches its maximum at \(x = 20\text{ m}\), yielding an area of \(20 \times 40 = 800\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A park ranger has \(1600\text{ m}\) of fencing to build a rectangular enclosure that borders a straight cliff face. No fencing is required along the cliff. What is the largest area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: If the two sides perpendicular to the cliff each have length \(x\), the remaining side has length \(1600 - 2x\). The area function \(A(x) = -2x^2 + 1600x\) reaches its vertex at \(x = 400\text{ m}\), producing a maximum area of \(400 \times 800 = 320,000\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A rancher has \(3000\text{ m}\) of fencing to enclose a rectangular pasture along a straight canal. If the canal acts as a natural barrier needing no fencing, what is the maximum area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: Let \(x\) represent the width perpendicular to the canal, so the length is \(3000 - 2x\). The area is \(A(x) = 3000x - 2x^2\), which reaches a maximum at the vertex \(x = 750\text{ m}\), giving an area of \(750 \times 1500 = 1,125,000\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A farmer has \(1200\text{ m}\) of fencing to enclose a rectangular pasture bordering a straight river. No fencing is needed along the riverbank. What is the largest area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the width perpendicular to the river, so the length parallel to the river is \(1200 - 2x\). The area function \(A(x) = x(1200 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 1200x\) has its vertex at \(x = 300\text{ m}\), giving a maximum area of \(300 \times 600 = 180,000\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: Lifeguards use \(400\text{ m}\) of rope to enclose a rectangular swimming area along a straight shoreline. If no rope is needed along the shore, what is the maximum area of the swimming enclosure?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the width extending from the shore, so the length along the shore is \(400 - 2x\). The area is \(A(x) = x(400 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 400x\), which is maximized at \(x = 100\text{ m}\), giving a maximum area of \(100 \times 200 = 20,000\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: An open-topped rain gutter with a rectangular cross-section is made by bending up the two long edges of a flat metal strip that is \(60\text{ cm}\) wide. What is the maximum cross-sectional area of the gutter?
qs.s: If the two sides are bent up by \(x\text{ cm}\) each, the base width is \(60 - 2x\text{ cm}\). The cross-sectional area is \(A(x) = x(60 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 60x\), which reaches its maximum at \(x = 15\text{ cm}\), giving an area of \(15 \times 30 = 450\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A rancher wants to enclose a rectangular feedlot bordering a straight river, divided into two equal corrals by a fence perpendicular to the river. No fencing is needed along the river. If \(4800\text{ m}\) of fencing is available in total, what is the maximum total area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the length of each of the 3 fences perpendicular to the river, so the length parallel to the river is \(4800 - 3x\). The total area \(A(x) = x(4800 - 3x) = -3x^2 + 4800x\) has its vertex at \(x = 800\text{ m}\), yielding a maximum area of \(800 \times 2400 = 1,920,000\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage yard is to be enclosed on all four sides. The fencing for the side facing the street costs \(\$40\) per metre, while the fencing for the remaining three sides costs \(\$20\) per metre. If the total budget for fencing is \(\$14,400\), what is the maximum area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: Let \(y\) be the length of the side facing the street and \(x\) be the perpendicular depth. The cost is \(40y + 20y + 2(20x) = 60y + 40x = 14,400\), which simplifies to \(2x = 720 - 3y\), so \(A(y) = y(360 - 1.5y) = -1.5y^2 + 360y\). The vertex is at \(y = 120\text{ m}\), which gives \(x = 180\text{ m}\) and a maximum area of \(120 \times 180 = 21,600\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A farmer has \(3600\text{ m}\) of fencing to build a rectangular enclosure on open ground, divided into three identical adjacent pens by two interior dividing fences parallel to the ends. What is the maximum total area of the enclosure?
qs.s: With 4 parallel fence sections of width \(x\) and 2 boundary sections of length \(y\), the constraint is \(4x + 2y = 3600\), or \(y = 1800 - 2x\). The total area \(A(x) = x(1800 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 1800x\) is maximized at \(x = 450\text{ m}\), giving \(450 \times 900 = 405,000\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A rectangular watering trough of length \(4\text{ m}\) is constructed from a flat metal sheet of width \(1.2\text{ m}\) by turning up the two long edges at right angles. What is the maximum volume of the trough, in cubic metres?
qs.s: If the edges are bent up by \(x\text{ m}\), the base is \(1.2 - 2x\text{ m}\), giving a cross-sectional area of \(A(x) = x(1.2 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 1.2x\). The vertex occurs at \(x = 0.3\text{ m}\), so the maximum cross-sectional area is \(0.3 \times 0.6 = 0.18\text{ m}^2\), and the maximum volume is \(0.18 \times 4 = 0.72\text{ m}^3\).

exercises.name: Rectangular area optimization with fixed perimeter

qs.q: A homeowner has 56 m of fencing to build a rectangular patio enclosure. What is the maximum area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: With width \(x\) m, the length is \(28 - x\) m, which yields the area function \(A(x) = -x^2 + 28x\). The maximum is at the vertex \(x = -28 / (2(-1)) = 14\), so the maximum area is \(14 \times 14 = 196\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A gardener has 40 m of fencing to enclose a rectangular garden. What is the maximum area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: Letting the width be \(x\) m, the length is \(20 - x\) m, so the area function is \(A(x) = x(20 - x) = -x^2 + 20x\). The vertex is at \(x = -20 / (2(-1)) = 10\), giving a maximum area of \(10 \times 10 = 100\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A rectangular dog run is to be enclosed using 64 m of fencing. What is the maximum area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: With width \(x\) m, the length is \(32 - x\) m, giving the quadratic area model \(A(x) = -x^2 + 32x\). The vertex is at \(x = -32 / (2(-1)) = 16\), giving a maximum area of \(16 \times 16 = 256\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A wire of length 48 cm is bent into the shape of a rectangle. What is the maximum area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: The length of the rectangle is \(24 - x\) cm for width \(x\) cm, giving the area function \(A(x) = -x^2 + 24x\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -24 / (2(-1)) = 12\), producing a maximum area of \(12 \times 12 = 144\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the maximum area of a rectangle that can be constructed with a perimeter of 28 cm.
qs.s: Letting the width be \(x\) cm, the length is \(14 - x\) cm, giving the area function \(A(x) = x(14 - x) = -x^2 + 14x\). The maximum occurs at the vertex \(x = -14 / (2(-1)) = 7\), yielding a maximum area of \(7 \times 7 = 49\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A zoo keeper has 360 m of fencing to build a rectangular enclosure divided into three equal adjacent pens by two interior fences parallel to the width. What is the maximum total area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: With four width segments of length \(x\) m, the length is \((360 - 4x)/2 = 180 - 2x\), giving \(A(x) = -2x^2 + 180x\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -180 / (2(-2)) = 45\text{ m}\), giving a maximum area of \(45(90) = 4050\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A landscaper has 70 m of fencing to enclose a rectangular garden. What is the maximum area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: With width \(x\) m, the length is \(35 - x\) m, so the area is modeled by \(A(x) = -x^2 + 35x\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -35 / (2(-1)) = 17.5\text{ m}\), giving a maximum area of \(17.5 \times 17.5 = 306.25\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A rancher has 180 m of fencing to construct a rectangular corral divided into two equal pens by an interior fence parallel to one of the sides. What is the maximum total area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: With three sections of fence of length \(x\) m, the corral's length is \((180 - 3x)/2 = 90 - 1.5x\), giving \(A(x) = -1.5x^2 + 90x\). The vertex is at \(x = -90 / (2(-1.5)) = 30\text{ m}\), giving a maximum area of \(30(45) = 1350\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A farmer has 160 m of fencing to enclose a rectangular pasture along a straight river, where no fencing is needed along the river bank. What is the maximum area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: With width \(x\) perpendicular to the river, the length is \(160 - 2x\), giving the area function \(A(x) = x(160 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 160x\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -160 / (2(-2)) = 40\text{ m}\), so the maximum area is \(40(80) = 3200\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A rectangular garden is to be enclosed against an existing straight brick wall (no fencing needed along the wall) and divided into two sections by an interior fence perpendicular to the wall. If 120 m of fencing is used in total, what is the maximum area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: With three perpendicular fence segments of length \(x\) m, the side parallel to the wall is \(120 - 3x\), giving \(A(x) = -3x^2 + 120x\). The vertex is at \(x = -120 / (2(-3)) = 20\text{ m}\), resulting in a maximum area of \(20(60) = 1200\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: What is the larger of two numbers that differ by 12 if their product is a minimum?
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(x + 12\). The product \(P(x) = x^2 + 12x\) reaches its minimum at \(x = -6\), so the larger number is \(-6 + 12 = 6\).

qs.q: What is the minimum product of two numbers that differ by 14?
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(x + 14\). The product \(P(x) = x^2 + 14x\) has its vertex at \(x = -7\), giving a minimum product of \((-7)(7) = -49\).

qs.q: What is the minimum product of two numbers that differ by 6?
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(x + 6\). The product \(P(x) = x^2 + 6x\) reaches its minimum value at \(x = -3\), yielding \((-3)(3) = -9\).

qs.q: What is the minimum product of two numbers that differ by 10?
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(x + 10\). The product \(P(x) = x(x + 10) = x^2 + 10x\) has its vertex at \(x = -5\), giving a minimum product of \((-5)(5) = -25\).

qs.q: What is the smaller of two numbers that differ by 16 if their product is minimized?
qs.s: Let the smaller number be \(x\), so the larger number is \(x + 16\). The product \(P(x) = x(x + 16) = x^2 + 16x\) is minimized at the vertex \(x = -8\).

qs.q: The sum of a number and twice another number is 40. What is the maximum product of the two numbers?
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(y\) with \(x + 2y = 40\), so the product is \(P(y) = y(40 - 2y) = -2y^2 + 40y\). The vertex occurs at \(y = 10\), giving \(x = 20\) and a maximum product of \(20 \times 10 = 200\).

qs.q: Two numbers differ by 10. What is the minimum possible value of the sum of their squares?
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(x + 10\). The sum of their squares is \(S(x) = x^2 + (x + 10)^2 = 2x^2 + 20x + 100\), which has its minimum at \(x = -5\), giving \(S(-5) = 2(-5)^2 + 20(-5) + 100 = 50\).

qs.q: Two numbers differ by 12. What is the minimum product of the smaller number and three times the larger number?
qs.s: Let the smaller number be \(x\), so the larger number is \(x + 12\). The product is \(P(x) = x \cdot 3(x + 12) = 3x^2 + 36x\), which reaches its minimum at \(x = -6\), giving \(P(-6) = 3(-6)^2 + 36(-6) = -108\).

qs.q: Two numbers differ by 8. What is the minimum value of the sum of the square of the larger number and three times the square of the smaller number?
qs.s: Let the smaller number be \(x\), so the larger number is \(x + 8\). The expression is \(E(x) = (x + 8)^2 + 3x^2 = 4x^2 + 16x + 64\), which has its vertex at \(x = -2\), yielding a minimum value of \(4(-2)^2 + 16(-2) + 64 = 48\).

qs.q: What is the minimum product of two numbers that differ by 9?
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(x + 9\). The product \(P(x) = x(x + 9) = x^2 + 9x\) reaches its minimum at the vertex \(x = -\frac{9}{2}\), giving a minimum product of \(\left(-\frac{9}{2}\right)\left(\frac{9}{2}\right) = -\frac{81}{4}\).

exercises.name: Projectile motion: maximum height and position

qs.q: A flare is launched from a boat 4 m above the water. Its height, \(h\), in metres above the water is modeled by \(h = -0.01x^2 + 1.2x + 4\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the boat in metres. How far horizontally from the boat is the flare when it reaches its maximum height?
qs.s: The horizontal distance at the maximum height is the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex, \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{1.2}{2(-0.01)} = 60\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An arrow is shot from an elevated platform 15 m above the ground. Its height, \(h\), in metres above the ground is given by \(h = -0.05x^2 + 3x + 15\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the platform in metres. What is the maximum height reached by the arrow?
qs.s: The arrow reaches its peak at \(x = -\frac{3}{2(-0.05)} = 30\text{ m}\). Substituting \(x = 30\) gives the maximum height \(h = -0.05(30)^2 + 3(30) + 15 = 60\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A soccer ball is kicked from the ground. Its height, \(h\), in metres is modeled by \(h = -0.04x^2 + 1.6x\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance in metres. What is the maximum height reached by the soccer ball?
qs.s: The ball reaches its maximum height when \(x = -\frac{1.6}{2(-0.04)} = 20\text{ m}\). Evaluating the height gives \(h = -0.04(20)^2 + 1.6(20) = 16\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A golf ball is hit from the ground. Its height, \(h\), in metres above the ground is given by \(h = -0.02x^2 + 2x\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance travelled in metres. How far has the golf ball travelled horizontally when it reaches its maximum height?
qs.s: The maximum height occurs at the vertex where \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{2}{2(-0.02)} = 50\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A tennis ball is hit from an initial height of 2.5 m. Its height, \(h\), in metres above the court is given by \(h = -0.02x^2 + 0.4x + 2.5\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance travelled in metres. How far has the ball travelled horizontally when it reaches its maximum height?
qs.s: The horizontal distance at the vertex is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{0.4}{2(-0.02)} = 10\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A model rocket is launched from a platform 55 m above the ground. Its height, \(h\), in metres is given by \(h = -\frac{1}{80}x^2 + \frac{3}{2}x + 55\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the platform in metres. What is the maximum height reached by the rocket?

An artillery shell follows a path given by \(h = -\frac{3}{200}x^2 + \frac{9}{10}x + 48\), where \(h\) is the height in metres and \(x\) is the horizontal distance in metres. What is the maximum height reached by the artillery shell?
qs.s: The maximum height occurs at \(x = -\frac{9/10}{2(-3/200)} = 30\text{ m}\). Substituting \(x = 30\) into the equation yields \(h = -\frac{3}{200}(900) + \frac{9}{10}(30) + 48 = -13.5 + 27 + 48 = 61.5\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Two catapults launch stones along parabolic trajectories. Catapult 1 launches a stone modeled by \(h_1 = -0.01x^2 + 1.4x + 15\), and Catapult 2 launches a stone modeled by \(h_2 = -0.02x^2 + 2x + 20\), where \(h\) and \(x\) are measured in metres. What is the positive difference between the maximum heights reached by the two stones?
qs.s: Catapult 1 peaks at \(x = 70\text{ m}\) with \(h_1(70) = 64\text{ m}\), while Catapult 2 peaks at \(x = 50\text{ m}\) with \(h_2(50) = 70\text{ m}\). The positive difference between their maximum heights is \(70 - 64 = 6\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Two fireworks are launched from the ground. The height of Firework A is given by \(h_A = -0.02x^2 + 2.4x + 30\) and the height of Firework B is given by \(h_B = -0.01x^2 + 1.6x + 20\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance in metres. How much farther horizontally from its launch point is Firework B than Firework A when each reaches its maximum height?
qs.s: Firework A reaches maximum height at \(x = -\frac{2.4}{2(-0.02)} = 60\text{ m}\) and Firework B at \(x = -\frac{1.6}{2(-0.01)} = 80\text{ m}\), so the difference is \(80 - 60 = 20\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A test missile is fired from an underground silo. Its height, \(h\), in metres relative to ground level is modeled by \(h = -0.004x^2 + 3.2x - 40\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance in metres from the silo. What is the maximum height above ground level reached by the missile?
qs.s: The horizontal distance at the peak is \(x = -\frac{3.2}{2(-0.004)} = 400\text{ m}\). Substituting \(x = 400\) gives \(h = -0.004(160000) + 3.2(400) - 40 = -640 + 1280 - 40 = 600\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An arrow is shot from an observation tower 20 m above the ground. The height, \(h\), of the arrow above the ground in metres is given by \(h = -0.05x^2 + 3x + 20\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the tower in metres. Find the maximum height reached by the arrow.
qs.s: The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{3}{2(-0.05)} = 30\text{ m}\). Substituting into the formula gives \(h = -0.05(30)^2 + 3(30) + 20 = 65\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A soccer ball is kicked from the top of an embankment 12 m above a field. The height, \(h\), of the ball above the field in metres is modeled by \(h = -0.04x^2 + 1.6x + 12\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the embankment in metres. Find the maximum height reached by the soccer ball.
qs.s: The maximum height occurs at \(x = -\frac{1.6}{2(-0.04)} = 20\text{ m}\). Evaluating the height yields \(h = -0.04(20)^2 + 1.6(20) + 12 = 28\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A flare is launched from a ship's deck 25 m above the water. Its height, \(h\), in metres above the water is given by \(h = -0.002x^2 + 0.6x + 25\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the launch point in metres. Find the horizontal distance from the ship at which the flare reaches its maximum height.
qs.s: The horizontal distance at the vertex is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{0.6}{2(-0.002)} = 150\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A firework is launched from a platform 40 m above the ground. The height, \(h\), of the firework above the ground in metres is given by \(h = -0.02x^2 + 2x + 40\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the platform in metres. Find the maximum height reached by the firework.
qs.s: The maximum height occurs at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{2}{2(-0.02)} = 50\text{ m}\). Substituting \(x = 50\) into the equation gives \(h = -0.02(50)^2 + 2(50) + 40 = 90\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A golf ball is hit from an elevated tee 15 m above the fairway. The height, \(h\), of the ball above the fairway in metres is given by \(h = -0.01x^2 + 0.8x + 15\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the tee in metres. Find the horizontal distance at which the golf ball reaches its maximum height.
qs.s: The horizontal distance at the maximum height is the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex, which is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{0.8}{2(-0.01)} = 40\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An artillery shell is fired from a hilltop 80 m above a plain. Its path is modeled by \(h = -\frac{1}{250}x^2 + \frac{6}{5}x + 80\), where \(h\) is the height in metres and \(x\) is the horizontal distance in metres from the launch point. Find the horizontal distance at which the shell reaches its maximum height.
qs.s: The horizontal distance at the peak is given by \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{6/5}{2(-1/250)} = \frac{6}{5} \times 125 = 150\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A stunt motorcycle jumps off an elevated ramp. The height, \(h\), in metres above the ground is modeled by \(h = 15 + 1.9x - 0.05x(x - 2)\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance in metres from the edge of the ramp. Find the maximum height reached by the motorcycle.
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying yields \(h = -0.05x^2 + 2x + 15\). The maximum occurs at \(x = -\frac{2}{2(-0.05)} = 20\text{ m}\), giving \(h = -0.05(20)^2 + 2(20) + 15 = 35\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A catapult launches a boulder from the top of a 75 m cliff. The height, \(h\), of the boulder above the ground is given by \(h = -0.0125x^2 + 1.5x + 75\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the base of the cliff in metres. How many metres above the top of the cliff does the boulder reach at its peak?
qs.s: The peak occurs at \(x = -\frac{1.5}{2(-0.0125)} = 60\text{ m}\), reaching a total height of \(h = -0.0125(60)^2 + 1.5(60) + 75 = 120\text{ m}\). Subtracting the 75 m cliff height gives \(120 - 75 = 45\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A sounding rocket is launched from a cliff 120 m above the ground. Its height, \(h\), in metres is given by \(h = -0.05x^2 + 14x + 120\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance in metres from the launch site. Find the maximum height reached by the rocket.

A flare is fired from an offshore platform 175 m above the water. Its trajectory is modeled by \(h = -\frac{1}{450}x^2 + \frac{4}{3}x + 175\), where \(h\) is the height above the water and \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the platform, both in metres. Find the maximum height of the flare above the water.
qs.s: The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{4/3}{2(-1/450)} = \frac{4}{3} \times 225 = 300\text{ m}\). Substituting \(x = 300\) into the equation yields \(h = -\frac{1}{450}(300)^2 + \frac{4}{3}(300) + 175 = -200 + 400 + 175 = 375\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A flare is launched from a rescue boat deck 15 m above the water. The height, \(h\), of the flare above the water is given by \(h = -0.05x^2 + x + 15\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the boat in metres. How far from the boat will the flare land in the water?
qs.s: Setting \(h = 0\) gives \(-0.05x^2 + x + 15 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 20x - 300 = 0\). Factoring as \((x - 30)(x + 10) = 0\) yields the positive distance \(x = 30\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A golf ball is hit from an elevated tee 10 m above the fairway. The height, \(h\), of the ball above the fairway is given by \(h = -0.02x^2 + 0.8x + 10\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the tee in metres. How far from the base of the tee will the ball land on the fairway?
qs.s: Setting \(h = 0\) gives \(-0.02x^2 + 0.8x + 10 = 0\), which multiplies by \(-50\) to give \(x^2 - 40x - 500 = 0\). Factoring as \((x - 50)(x + 10) = 0\) gives the positive solution \(x = 50\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A catapult launches a boulder from a fortress wall 35 m above the surrounding field. The height, \(h\), of the boulder above the field is given by \(h = -0.05x^2 + 3x + 35\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the wall in metres. How far from the base of the fortress wall will the boulder strike the field?
qs.s: Setting \(h = 0\) gives \(-0.05x^2 + 3x + 35 = 0\), which multiplies by \(-20\) to become \(x^2 - 60x - 700 = 0\). Factoring as \((x - 70)(x + 10) = 0\) gives the positive distance \(x = 70\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An arrow is shot from an archery platform 16 m above the ground. The height, \(h\), of the arrow above the ground is given by \(h = -0.01x^2 + 0.6x + 16\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the platform in metres. How far from the base of the platform will the arrow hit the ground?
qs.s: Setting \(h = 0\) yields \(-0.01x^2 + 0.6x + 16 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 60x - 1600 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 80)(x + 20) = 0\), so the positive solution is \(x = 80\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A water cannon shoots a stream of water from the top of an 18 m high embankment. The height, \(h\), of the water stream above the ground is given by \(h = -0.005x^2 + 0.45x + 18\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the embankment in metres. How far from the base of the embankment will the stream of water hit the ground?
qs.s: Setting \(h = 0\) gives \(-0.005x^2 + 0.45x + 18 = 0\), which multiplies by \(-200\) to give \(x^2 - 90x - 3600 = 0\). Factoring as \((x - 120)(x + 30) = 0\) yields \(x = 120\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A model rocket is launched from a hilltop platform. Its height, \(h\), in metres above the surrounding ground is given by \(h = -0.04(x - 150)^2 + 1600\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the platform in metres. How far horizontally from the platform will the rocket hit the ground?
qs.s: Setting \(h = 0\) gives \(0.04(x - 150)^2 = 1600\), so \((x - 150)^2 = 40000\). Taking the positive square root gives \(x - 150 = 200\), which results in \(x = 350\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A flare is fired from a cliff 50 m above the sea. Its height, \(h\), in metres above the water is given by \(h = -0.02x^2 + 2x + 50\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the base of the cliff in metres. How far from the base of the cliff will the flare land in the water?
qs.s: Setting \(h = 0\) and dividing by \(-0.02\) yields \(x^2 - 100x - 2500 = 0\). Applying the quadratic formula gives \(x = \frac{100 \pm \sqrt{10000 + 10000}}{2} = 50 \pm 50\sqrt{2}\), which yields the positive root \((50 + 50\sqrt{2})\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An aircraft releases an emergency supply container from an altitude of 120 m. The height, \(h\), of the container above the ground in metres is given by \(h = 120 + 1.2x - 0.002x(x + 100)\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance traveled in metres. How far horizontally from the release point will the container land on the ground?
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms gives \(h = -0.002x^2 + x + 120\). Setting \(h = 0\) and multiplying by \(-500\) gives \(x^2 - 500x - 60000 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 600)(x + 100) = 0\), yielding \(x = 600\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A stunt car is launched off an elevated track 60 m above the ground. Its trajectory is described by \(h = -\frac{1}{180}(x - 60)^2 + 80\), where \(h\) is the height above the ground in metres and \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the end of the track in metres. How far horizontally from the end of the track will the car land on the ground?
qs.s: Setting \(h = 0\) gives \(\frac{1}{180}(x - 60)^2 = 80\), so \((x - 60)^2 = 14400\). Taking the positive square root gives \(x - 60 = 120\), which results in \(x = 180\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A coastal defense cannon fires a shell from a cliff 160 m above the ocean. The height, \(h\), of the shell above the ocean is modeled by \(h = -\frac{1}{500}x^2 + \frac{7}{5}x + 160\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance from the cliff in metres. How far from the base of the cliff will the shell land in the water?
qs.s: Setting \(h = 0\) gives \(-\frac{1}{500}x^2 + \frac{7}{5}x + 160 = 0\), which multiplies by \(-500\) to give \(x^2 - 700x - 80000 = 0\). Factoring as \((x - 800)(x + 100) = 0\) yields the positive root \(x = 800\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A youth sports camp charges $50 per registration and enrolls 60 children. For each $1 increase in the fee, enrollment drops by 1 child. What registration fee will maximize the camp's revenue?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $1 increases. Revenue is \(R(x) = (50 + x)(60 - x) = -x^2 + 10x + 3000\), which reaches its maximum at \(x = -\frac{10}{2(-1)} = 5\), giving an optimal fee of \(50 + 5 = \$55\).

qs.q: The student council charges $8 per ticket for the annual school dance, with an average attendance of 160 students. For each $1 increase in ticket price, attendance decreases by 10 students. What ticket price should they set to maximize revenue?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $1 increases. Revenue is given by \(R(x) = (8 + x)(160 - 10x) = -10x^2 + 80x + 1280\), with the vertex at \(x = -\frac{80}{2(-10)} = 4\), so the optimal price is \(8 + 4 = \$12\).

qs.q: A city tour bus company charges $20 per seat and averages 100 passengers per day. For each $1 increase in ticket price, the company loses 2 passengers per day. What price should the company charge per ticket to maximize revenue?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $1 increases. Revenue is \(R(x) = (20 + x)(100 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 60x + 2000\), which has its maximum at the vertex \(x = -\frac{60}{2(-2)} = 15\), giving an optimal price of \(20 + 15 = \$35\).

qs.q: An art gallery charges $14 for admission and averages 120 visitors per day. For each $1 increase in the admission price, the gallery loses 4 visitors per day. What price should the gallery charge to maximize revenue?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $1 increases. Revenue is \(R(x) = (14 + x)(120 - 4x) = -4x^2 + 64x + 1680\), with the vertex at \(x = -\frac{64}{2(-4)} = 8\), yielding an optimal price of \(14 + 8 = \$22\).

qs.q: A community choir charges $12 per ticket and regularly attracts 120 attendees. For each $1 increase in ticket price, attendance drops by 6 people. What ticket price will maximize revenue?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $1 increases. Revenue is \(R(x) = (12 + x)(120 - 6x) = -6x^2 + 48x + 1440\), which reaches its maximum at \(x = -\frac{48}{2(-6)} = 4\), so the optimal ticket price is \(12 + 4 = \$16\).

qs.q: A comedy club charges $20 for admission and averages 150 guests per night. For each $2 increase in ticket price, attendance decreases by 5 people. What is the maximum revenue the club can generate?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $2 increases, giving revenue \(R(x) = (20 + 2x)(150 - 5x) = -10x^2 + 200x + 3000\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{200}{2(-10)} = 10\), so the maximum revenue is \(R(10) = (40)(100) = \$4000\).

qs.q: A bakery sells 200 artisanal loaves of bread each day at $6.00 each. For each $0.50 increase in price, the bakery sells 10 fewer loaves per day. What is the maximum daily revenue the bakery can achieve?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $0.50 increases, giving revenue \(R(x) = (6 + 0.5x)(200 - 10x) = -5x^2 + 40x + 1200\). The vertex is at \(x = -\frac{40}{2(-5)} = 4\), giving a maximum revenue of \(R(4) = (8)(160) = \$1280\).

qs.q: A 600-seat theater is \(\frac{2}{3}\) full when charging $30 per ticket. For every $3 increase in ticket price, attendance decreases by 20 people. What ticket price will maximize the theater's revenue?
qs.s: The initial attendance is \(\frac{2}{3} \times 600 = 400\) people. Letting \(x\) be the number of $3 increases, revenue is \(R(x) = (30 + 3x)(400 - 20x) = -60x^2 + 600x + 12000\), with the vertex at \(x = -\frac{600}{2(-60)} = 5\), giving an optimal price of \(30 + 3(5) = \$45\).

qs.q: A charity gala charges $100 per plate and attracts 400 guests. For each $5 increase in ticket price, 10 fewer guests attend. How many guests will attend the gala when revenue is maximized?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $5 increases, so revenue is \(R(x) = (100 + 5x)(400 - 10x) = -50x^2 + 1000x + 40000\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{1000}{2(-50)} = 10\), resulting in \(400 - 10(10) = 300\) guests attending.

qs.q: A fitness gym currently charges $80 per month and has 300 members. A market survey shows that for each $5 decrease in the monthly membership fee, the gym will gain 30 new members. What monthly fee should the gym charge to maximize revenue?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $5 price reductions, so revenue is \(R(x) = (80 - 5x)(300 + 30x) = -150x^2 + 900x + 24000\). The vertex is at \(x = -\frac{900}{2(-150)} = 3\), giving an optimal monthly fee of \(80 - 5(3) = \$65\).

exercises.name: Revenue and income optimization from quadratic model

qs.q: A retailer can sell \(x\) lawnmowers at a price of \((480 - x)\) dollars each. How many lawnmowers must be sold to maximize revenue?
qs.s: Revenue is modeled by \(R(x) = x(480 - x) = -x^2 + 480x\), and the maximum occurs at the vertex \(x = -\frac{480}{2(-1)} = 240\).

qs.q: A store can sell \(x\) digital cameras at a price of \((500 - x)\) dollars each. What is the maximum revenue the store can achieve?
qs.s: Revenue is given by \(R(x) = x(500 - x) = -x^2 + 500x\), which is maximized at \(x = -\frac{500}{2(-1)} = 250\). The maximum revenue is \(R(250) = 250(500 - 250) = \$62,500\).

qs.q: An artisan sells \(x\) handmade leather bags at a price of \((360 - x)\) dollars each. How many bags must be sold to maximize income?
qs.s: Income is modeled by \(I(x) = x(360 - x) = -x^2 + 360x\), which reaches its maximum at the vertex \(x = -\frac{360}{2(-1)} = 180\).

qs.q: A manufacturer can sell \(x\) electric scooters at a price of \((600 - x)\) dollars each. How many scooters must be sold to maximize revenue?
qs.s: The revenue function is \(R(x) = x(600 - x) = -x^2 + 600x\), which reaches its maximum at the vertex \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{600}{2(-1)} = 300\).

qs.q: A company can sell \(x\) smartphones at a price of \((900 - x)\) dollars each. What is the maximum income the company can earn?
qs.s: Income is given by \(I(x) = x(900 - x) = -x^2 + 900x\), with its vertex at \(x = -\frac{900}{2(-1)} = 450\). Thus, the maximum income is \(I(450) = 450(900 - 450) = \$202,500\).

qs.q: A manufacturer can sell \(x\) electric generators at a price of \((2000 - 5x)\) dollars each. What is the maximum revenue that the manufacturer can obtain?
qs.s: Revenue is \(R(x) = x(2000 - 5x) = -5x^2 + 2000x\), which reaches its maximum at \(x = -\frac{2000}{2(-5)} = 200\). The maximum revenue is \(R(200) = 200(2000 - 5(200)) = \$200,000\).

qs.q: A manufacturer determines that \(x\) espresso machines can be sold at a price of \((1500 - 3x)\) dollars each. What price should the manufacturer set for each espresso machine to maximize total revenue?
qs.s: Revenue is \(R(x) = -3x^2 + 1500x\), which is maximized when \(x = -\frac{1500}{2(-3)} = 250\) machines are sold. Substituting \(x = 250\) into the price formula gives a price of \(1500 - 3(250) = \$750\).

qs.q: A bus tour company charges $60 per ticket and averages 200 passengers per week. Market research shows that for every $3 increase in ticket price, the company will lose 5 passengers. What ticket price should the company charge to maximize weekly revenue?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $3 increases; revenue is \(R(x) = (60 + 3x)(200 - 5x) = -15x^2 + 300x + 12000\). The vertex is at \(x = -\frac{300}{2(-15)} = 10\), so the optimal ticket price is \(60 + 3(10) = \$90\).

qs.q: A stadium currently charges $40 per ticket and sells an average of 3,000 tickets per game. Management finds that for each $2 decrease in ticket price, an additional 300 tickets will be sold. How many tickets must be sold to maximize revenue per game?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $2 price decreases; revenue is \(R(x) = (40 - 2x)(3000 + 300x) = -600x^2 + 6000x + 120000\). The vertex is at \(x = -\frac{6000}{2(-600)} = 5\), so the optimal number of tickets sold is \(3000 + 300(5) = 4,500\).

qs.q: An art gallery sells prints for $40 each and currently sells 120 prints per month. The gallery owner estimates that for each $2 increase in price, 4 fewer prints will be sold. What is the maximum monthly revenue the gallery can achieve?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $2 price increases; revenue is \(R(x) = (40 + 2x)(120 - 4x) = -8x^2 + 80x + 4800\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{80}{2(-8)} = 5\), giving a maximum revenue of \((40 + 2(5))(120 - 4(5)) = 50 \times 100 = \$5,000\).

qs.q: A 32 cm wide strip of aluminum is bent into a rectangular rain gutter by folding up the edges on both sides at right angles. How deep must the gutter be to maximize the amount of water it can carry?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the depth in centimeters, giving a base of \(32 - 2x\) and cross-sectional area \(A(x) = x(32 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 32x\). The maximum occurs at the vertex \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{32}{2(-2)} = 8\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A 24-inch wide sheet of copper is bent into a rectangular trough by turning up the sides at right angles. How high must the sides be to maximize the trough's volume?
qs.s: With side height \(x\), the base width is \(24 - 2x\), giving cross-sectional area \(A(x) = x(24 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 24x\). The maximum volume occurs at the vertex \(x = -\frac{24}{2(-2)} = 6\text{ inches}\).

qs.q: A gardener bends a 40 cm wide piece of galvanized sheet metal into a rectangular trough with an open top. What side height will maximize the volume of the trough?
qs.s: Letting \(x\) be the height of the sides, the cross-sectional area is \(A(x) = x(40 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 40x\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{40}{2(-2)} = 10\text{ cm}\), which maximizes the volume.

qs.q: A tin sheet with a width of 36 cm is bent upwards at right angles on both sides to form a rectangular water chute. What height of the sides maximizes the chute's carrying capacity?
qs.s: Letting \(x\) be the height, the cross-sectional area is \(A(x) = x(36 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 36x\). The maximum carrying capacity occurs at the vertex \(x = -\frac{36}{2(-2)} = 9\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A strip of plastic 28 cm wide is folded along two parallel lines to create a rectangular feeding trough. How high must the trough be to maximize its cross-sectional area?
qs.s: If the height is \(x\), the base is \(28 - 2x\) and the area is \(A(x) = x(28 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 28x\). The area reaches its maximum at the vertex \(x = -\frac{28}{2(-2)} = 7\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rancher has 240 meters of fencing to build a rectangular corral along a straight river bank, requiring no fence along the water. The corral is divided into two equal pens by an interior fence perpendicular to the river bank. What is the maximum total area of the corral?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the length of each of the 3 fences perpendicular to the river, so the side parallel to the river is \(240 - 3x\). The total area is \(A(x) = x(240 - 3x) = -3x^2 + 240x\), which reaches its maximum at \(x = -\frac{240}{2(-3)} = 40\text{ m}\), yielding \(40(240 - 120) = 4800\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A farmer uses 400 meters of fencing to build a rectangular pasture against a barn wall, requiring no fencing along the wall. The pasture is divided into three separate grazing pens by two interior fences perpendicular to the barn wall. To maximize the total area, what must be the length of the fence parallel to the barn wall?
qs.s: With 4 fence sections of length \(x\) perpendicular to the wall, the parallel side has length \(y = 400 - 4x\). The area \(A(x) = x(400 - 4x) = -4x^2 + 400x\) is maximized at \(x = -\frac{400}{2(-4)} = 50\text{ m}\), giving a parallel side length of \(y = 400 - 4(50) = 200\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A 64 cm wide sheet of metal is bent into a rectangular trough with an open top by folding up both sides at right angles. What is the maximum cross-sectional area of the trough?
qs.s: The cross-sectional area is \(A(x) = x(64 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 64x\), which reaches its maximum at \(x = -\frac{64}{2(-2)} = 16\text{ cm}\). Substituting \(x = 16\) gives the maximum area \(A(16) = 16(64 - 32) = 512\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A 50 cm wide, 4-meter-long sheet of galvanized steel is bent into a rectangular water trough by turning up two sides of equal height at right angles. What is the maximum volume of the trough in liters? (\(1\text{ L} = 1000\text{ cm}^3\))
qs.s: The cross-sectional area \(A(x) = x(50 - 2x)\) is maximized at \(x = \frac{50}{4} = 12.5\text{ cm}\), giving \(A = 12.5(25) = 312.5\text{ cm}^2\). With length \(400\text{ cm}\), the maximum volume is \(312.5 \times 400 = 125{,}000\text{ cm}^3 = 125\text{ L}\).

qs.q: A rectangular garden is enclosed on all four sides and divided into two equal plots by an interior fence parallel to one of the sides. If 120 meters of fencing is used in total, what is the maximum total area that can be enclosed?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the length of the 3 parallel fence segments, so the other 2 sides each measure \(\frac{120 - 3x}{2} = 60 - 1.5x\). The area \(A(x) = x(60 - 1.5x) = -1.5x^2 + 60x\) has its vertex at \(x = -\frac{60}{2(-1.5)} = 20\text{ m}\), yielding a maximum area of \(20(60 - 30) = 600\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: The sum of two numbers is 12, and the sum of their squares is a minimum. What is the minimum sum of their squares?
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(12 - x\), so the sum of squares is \(S(x) = x^2 + (12 - x)^2 = 2x^2 - 24x + 144\). The vertex is at \(x = 24 / 4 = 6\), giving a minimum sum of \(6^2 + 6^2 = 72\).

qs.q: The difference between two numbers is 8, and the sum of their squares is a minimum. What is the smaller number?
qs.s: Let the smaller number be \(y\), so the larger is \(y + 8\); their sum of squares is \(S(y) = y^2 + (y + 8)^2 = 2y^2 + 16y + 64\). The minimum occurs at the vertex \(y = -16 / (2 \cdot 2) = -4\).

qs.q: The sum of two numbers is 20, and the sum of their squares is a minimum. What is the minimum sum of their squares?
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(20 - x\); their sum of squares is \(S(x) = x^2 + (20 - x)^2 = 2x^2 - 40x + 400\). The vertex is at \(x = 40 / 4 = 10\), giving a minimum sum of \(10^2 + 10^2 = 200\).

qs.q: The sum of two integers is 16, and the sum of their squares is a minimum. What is the value of each integer?
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(16 - x\); the sum of squares is \(S(x) = x^2 + (16 - x)^2 = 2x^2 - 32x + 256\). The minimum occurs at the vertex \(x = -(-32) / (2 \cdot 2) = 8\), so each integer is 8.

qs.q: The difference between two numbers is 6, and the sum of their squares is a minimum. What is the minimum sum of their squares?
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(y\) and \(y + 6\), giving \(S(y) = y^2 + (y + 6)^2 = 2y^2 + 12y + 36\). The vertex is at \(y = -12 / 4 = -3\), yielding the numbers \(-3\) and \(3\), with a minimum sum of squares of \((-3)^2 + 3^2 = 18\).

qs.q: Two positive numbers \(x\) and \(y\) satisfy \(2x + y = 40\). What is the maximum possible value of their product \(xy\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 40 - 2x\) into the product to obtain \(P(x) = x(40 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 40x\). The maximum occurs at the vertex \(x = -40 / (2 \cdot (-2)) = 10\), so \(y = 20\) and the maximum product is \(10 \times 20 = 200\).

qs.q: Two numbers \(x\) and \(y\) satisfy \(x - 2y = 12\). What is the minimum possible value of their product \(xy\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 2y + 12\) into the product to get \(P(y) = y(2y + 12) = 2y^2 + 12y\). The minimum occurs at the vertex \(y = -12 / 4 = -3\), giving \(x = 6\) and a minimum product of \(6 \times (-3) = -18\).

qs.q: The sum of two numbers \(x\) and \(y\) is 12. What is the minimum possible value of \(x^2 + 2y^2\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 12 - y\) into the expression to get \(E(y) = (12 - y)^2 + 2y^2 = 3y^2 - 24y + 144\). The minimum is at \(y = 24 / 6 = 4\), which gives \(x = 8\) and a minimum value of \(8^2 + 2(4^2) = 96\).

qs.q: Two numbers \(x\) and \(y\) have a sum of 10. What is the minimum possible value of \(2x^2 + 3y^2\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 10 - x\) to get \(E(x) = 2x^2 + 3(10 - x)^2 = 5x^2 - 60x + 300\). The vertex is at \(x = 60 / 10 = 6\), giving \(y = 4\) and a minimum value of \(2(6^2) + 3(4^2) = 72 + 48 = 120\).

qs.q: Two positive numbers \(x\) and \(y\) satisfy \(2x + 3y = 60\). What is the maximum possible value of their product \(xy\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 30 - 1.5y\) into the product to get \(P(y) = y(30 - 1.5y) = -1.5y^2 + 30y\). The maximum occurs at \(y = -30 / (2 \cdot (-1.5)) = 10\), so \(x = 15\) and the maximum product is \(15 \times 10 = 150\).

qs.q: A parabolic greenhouse frame has a span of 16 m and a maximum height of 6 m. What is the height of the frame at a point 4 m from the centre?
qs.s: Modeling the frame as \(y = 6 - ax^2\) with roots at \(x = \pm 8\) gives \(a = \frac{6}{8^2} = \frac{3}{32}\). At \(x = 4\), \(y = 6 - \frac{3}{32}(4^2) = 4.5\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A parabolic arch for an overpass has a span of 60 m and a maximum height of 18 m. What is the height of the arch at a point 20 m from the centre?
qs.s: Using the model \(y = 18 - ax^2\) with \(y = 0\) at \(x = 30\), we find \(a = \frac{18}{30^2} = 0.02\). At \(x = 20\), the height is \(y = 18 - 0.02(20^2) = 10\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A parabolic arch has a span of 40 m and a maximum height of 20 m. What is the height of the arch at a point 10 m from the centre?
qs.s: With the peak at \((0, 20)\), the parabola is modeled by \(y = 20 - ax^2\). Since \(y = 0\) at \(x = 20\), \(a = \frac{20}{20^2} = 0.05\), so at \(x = 10\), \(y = 20 - 0.05(10^2) = 15\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A parabolic tunnel entrance has a span of 30 m and a maximum height of 9 m. What is the height of the tunnel at a point 5 m from the centre?
qs.s: Placing the vertex at \((0, 9)\), the equation is \(y = 9 - ax^2\). Since \(y = 0\) at \(x = 15\), \(a = \frac{9}{15^2} = 0.04\), and at \(x = 5\), \(y = 9 - 0.04(5^2) = 8\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An entrance to an exhibition hall is shaped like a parabolic arch with a span of 20 m and a maximum height of 8 m. What is the height of the arch at a point 5 m from the centre?
qs.s: The equation is \(y = 8 - ax^2\) with roots at \(x = \pm 10\), which gives \(a = \frac{8}{10^2} = 0.08\). At \(x = 5\), the height is \(y = 8 - 0.08(5^2) = 6\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A parabolic roof of a warehouse is supported by two vertical walls that are 6 m high. The parabolic roof has a span of 40 m between the walls and reaches a maximum height of 10 m above the tops of the walls. What is the total height from the ground to the roof at a point 12 m from the centre of the building?
qs.s: The height of the roof above the walls is \(h(x) = 10 - ax^2\), where \(h(20) = 0\) gives \(a = \frac{10}{20^2} = 0.025\). At \(x = 12\), \(h(12) = 10 - 0.025(12^2) = 6.4\text{ m}\), so the total height from the ground is \(6 + 6.4 = 12.4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A parabolic arch has a span of 50 m and a maximum height of 25 m. At what horizontal distance from either base of the arch is the height of the arch equal to 16 m?
qs.s: The arch is modeled by \(y = 25 - ax^2\), where \(a = \frac{25}{25^2} = \frac{1}{25}\). Setting \(y = 16\) gives \(16 = 25 - \frac{1}{25}x^2 \implies x = 15\text{ m}\) from the centre, which is \(25 - 15 = 10\text{ m}\) from the base.

qs.q: A parabolic tunnel has a span of 40 m at ground level and a maximum ceiling height of 16 m at its centre. A rectangular truck with a width of 10 m and a height of 11 m drives along the centre of the tunnel. What is the vertical clearance between the top of the truck and the ceiling of the tunnel?
qs.s: The tunnel ceiling is modeled by \(y = 16 - ax^2\), where \(a = \frac{16}{20^2} = 0.04\). At the edge of the truck (\(x = 5\)), the ceiling height is \(y = 16 - 0.04(5^2) = 15\text{ m}\), giving a clearance of \(15 - 11 = 4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A parabolic arch has a span of 48 m and a maximum height of 18 m. What is the horizontal width of the arch at a height of 10 m above the ground?
qs.s: The arch is modeled by \(y = 18 - ax^2\), where \(y = 0\) at \(x = 24\), giving \(a = \frac{18}{24^2} = \frac{1}{32}\). Setting \(y = 10\) yields \(10 = 18 - \frac{1}{32}x^2 \implies x = 16\text{ m}\), so the total width is \(2 \times 16 = 32\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The main cable of a suspension bridge hangs in the shape of a parabola between two towers that are 120 m apart and 30 m tall. The lowest point of the cable is 6 m above the roadway. What is the height of the cable above the roadway at a point 30 m horizontally from the centre of the bridge?
qs.s: With the vertex at \((0, 6)\), the cable is modeled by \(y = ax^2 + 6\). Since \(y = 30\) at the tower where \(x = 60\), \(a = \frac{30 - 6}{60^2} = \frac{1}{150}\), so at \(x = 30\), \(y = \frac{1}{150}(30^2) + 6 = 12\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rancher has \(1800\text{ m}\) of fencing to build two adjacent rectangular corrals with a shared dividing fence. What length of the shared fence will maximize the total enclosed area?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the length of the shared fence; the perimeter equation is \(3x + 2y = 1800\), so \(y = 900 - 1.5x\). The area function \(A(x) = -1.5x^2 + 900x\) has its vertex at \(x = -\frac{900}{2(-1.5)} = 300\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A landscaper has \(960\text{ m}\) of fencing to enclose two adjacent rectangular garden plots sharing a common border. What length of the common border produces the maximum total enclosed area?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the length of the common border; then \(3x + 2y = 960\), so \(y = 480 - 1.5x\). The area \(A(x) = -1.5x^2 + 480x\) is maximized at \(x = -\frac{480}{2(-1.5)} = 160\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A horse trainer has \(1500\text{ m}\) of fencing to build two adjacent rectangular paddocks sharing a common fence line. What is the maximum total area that can be enclosed, in square meters?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the length of the dividing fence; the constraint is \(3x + 2y = 1500\), giving \(y = 750 - 1.5x\). Maximizing \(A(x) = -1.5x^2 + 750x\) yields \(x = 250\text{ m}\) and \(y = 375\text{ m}\), for a maximum total area of \(250 \times 375 = 93\,750\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A farmer has \(600\text{ m}\) of fencing to enclose two adjacent rectangular pens that share a common dividing fence. What is the maximum total area that can be enclosed, in square meters?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the length of the shared fence, so \(3x + 2y = 600\), giving \(y = 300 - 1.5x\). The total area \(A(x) = x(300 - 1.5x) = -1.5x^2 + 300x\) reaches its maximum at \(x = -\frac{300}{2(-1.5)} = 100\text{ m}\), giving a maximum area of \(100 \times 150 = 15\,000\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: An animal shelter has \(360\text{ m}\) of wire fencing to construct two adjacent rectangular dog runs of equal size sharing a common partition. What is the maximum total area that can be enclosed, in square meters?
qs.s: With \(x\) as the partition length, \(3x + 2y = 360\), so \(y = 180 - 1.5x\). The area is \(A(x) = -1.5x^2 + 180x\), which reaches its maximum at \(x = 60\text{ m}\), yielding a maximum total area of \(60 \times 90 = 5400\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A farmer uses a long exterior barn wall as one side of an enclosure. Fencing is used for the remaining sides to create two adjacent rectangular pens of equal size, requiring three fences perpendicular to the wall and one fence parallel to the wall. If the farmer has \(600\text{ m}\) of fencing, what is the maximum total area that can be enclosed, in square meters?
qs.s: Since the barn wall replaces one parallel side, the constraint is \(3x + y = 600\), giving \(y = 600 - 3x\). The area function \(A(x) = -3x^2 + 600x\) has its vertex at \(x = -\frac{600}{2(-3)} = 100\text{ m}\), for a maximum area of \(100 \times 300 = 30\,000\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A flat strip of sheet metal \(60\text{ cm}\) wide is bent into a rectangular rain gutter by turning up two equal vertical sides of height \(x\text{ cm}\) at right angles. What is the maximum cross-sectional area of the gutter, in square centimeters?
qs.s: Turning up two edges of height \(x\) leaves a base of \(60 - 2x\), so the cross-sectional area is \(A(x) = x(60 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 60x\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{60}{2(-2)} = 15\text{ cm}\), giving a maximum area of \(15 \times 30 = 450\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A trough of length \(300\text{ cm}\) is constructed from a rectangular sheet of metal \(100\text{ cm}\) wide by bending up the two long edges of width \(x\text{ cm}\) at right angles. What is the maximum volume of the trough, in cubic centimeters?
qs.s: The cross-sectional area is \(A(x) = x(100 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 100x\), which reaches its maximum at \(x = 25\text{ cm}\) with an area of \(25 \times 50 = 1250\text{ cm}^2\). Multiplying by the length gives a maximum volume of \(1250 \times 300 = 375\,000\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A rancher has \(2400\text{ m}\) of fencing to build three adjacent, identical rectangular corrals in a single row, separated by two interior dividing fences. What is the maximum total area that can be enclosed, in square meters?
qs.s: The enclosure has 4 cross fences of length \(x\) and 2 longitudinal sides of length \(y\), so \(4x + 2y = 2400\) or \(y = 1200 - 2x\). The total area \(A(x) = -2x^2 + 1200x\) is maximized at \(x = 300\text{ m}\), giving a maximum area of \(300 \times 600 = 180\,000\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A rancher has \(2000\text{ m}\) of fencing to build four adjacent, identical rectangular corrals arranged in a single row, separated by three interior dividing fences. What is the maximum area of each individual corral, in square meters?
qs.s: With 5 cross fences and 2 outer sides, \(5x + 2y = 2000\), so \(y = 1000 - 2.5x\). The total area \(A(x) = -2.5x^2 + 1000x\) is maximized at \(x = 200\text{ m}\) with \(y = 500\text{ m}\), producing a total area of \(100\,000\text{ m}^2\); dividing by 4 gives \(25\,000\text{ m}^2\) per corral.

qs.q: A fitness studio charges its members $300 per year for up to 40 members. For each member enrolled beyond 40, the yearly membership cost is reduced by $3 for all members. What total number of members would generate the maximum revenue for the studio?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of additional members; the revenue function is \(R(x) = (40 + x)(300 - 3x) = -3x^2 + 180x + 12000\), which reaches its maximum at \(x = -\frac{180}{2(-3)} = 30\). Thus, the total number of members is \(40 + 30 = 70\).

qs.q: A tour bus company charges $80 per ticket for a charter group of 30 passengers. For each additional passenger beyond 30, the price of each ticket is reduced by $1 for everyone. What total number of passengers will maximize the revenue from the charter?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of additional passengers; the revenue function is \(R(x) = (30 + x)(80 - x) = -x^2 + 50x + 2400\), which reaches its vertex at \(x = -\frac{50}{2(-1)} = 25\). The total number of passengers is \(30 + 25 = 55\).

qs.q: A community rowing club charges an annual fee of $240 per member for up to 80 members. For each member who joins beyond 80, the fee for each member decreases by $2. What total number of members will produce the maximum annual revenue for the club?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of members over 80; the revenue function is \(R(x) = (80 + x)(240 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 80x + 19200\), whose vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{80}{2(-2)} = 20\). Therefore, the total number of members is \(80 + 20 = 100\).

qs.q: A summer camp charges a registration fee of $160 per child for 50 children. For each child registered beyond 50, the registration fee is decreased by $2 for all children. What total number of children will produce the maximum revenue for the camp?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of children beyond 50; the revenue is \(R(x) = (50 + x)(160 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 60x + 8000\), which has a maximum at \(x = -\frac{60}{2(-2)} = 15\). The total number of children is \(50 + 15 = 65\).

qs.q: A martial arts club charges an annual fee of $120 per person for 50 members. For each additional member beyond 50, the annual fee is decreased by $1 for all members. What total number of members will produce the maximum annual revenue for the club?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of members beyond 50; the revenue function is \(R(x) = (50 + x)(120 - x) = -x^2 + 70x + 6000\), which has its vertex at \(x = -\frac{70}{2(-1)} = 35\). The total number of members is \(50 + 35 = 85\).

qs.q: A community theater sells all 500 tickets for a musical when the ticket price is $20. A survey indicates that for each $2 increase in ticket price, 25 fewer tickets will be sold. What ticket price will maximize the theater's revenue?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $2 price increases; revenue is \(R(x) = (20 + 2x)(500 - 25x) = -50x^2 + 500x + 10000\), with its maximum at \(x = -\frac{500}{2(-50)} = 5\). The optimal ticket price is \(20 + 2(5) = \$30\).

qs.q: An airline charter service charges $450 per seat for a flight with 80 passengers. For each additional passenger beyond 80, the price per seat for all passengers is reduced by $1.50. What total number of passengers will produce the maximum revenue for the charter service?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of additional passengers; the revenue is \(R(x) = (80 + x)(450 - 1.5x) = -1.5x^2 + 330x + 36000\), which reaches a maximum at \(x = -\frac{330}{2(-1.5)} = 110\). The total number of passengers is \(80 + 110 = 190\).

qs.q: An executive tennis club currently charges 120 members an annual fee of $400 each. For each additional member over 120, the annual fee is reduced by $2 for all members. What is the maximum annual revenue the club can generate?
qs.s: With \(x\) additional members, the revenue is \(R(x) = (120 + x)(400 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 160x + 48000\), which peaks at \(x = -\frac{160}{2(-2)} = 40\). Evaluating revenue at \(x = 40\) gives \((120 + 40)(400 - 80) = 160 \times 320 = \$51,200\).

qs.q: A 300-unit storage facility is fully rented when the monthly fee is $120 per unit. For each $10 increase in the monthly fee, 15 units become vacant. How many units should be rented to maximize the facility's monthly revenue?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $10 price increases; the revenue is \(R(x) = (300 - 15x)(120 + 10x) = -150x^2 + 1200x + 36000\), which has its maximum at \(x = -\frac{1200}{2(-150)} = 4\). The number of rented units that maximizes revenue is \(300 - 15(4) = 240\).

qs.q: A ski resort sells season passes to 200 skiers at $600 each. Market research shows that for each $15 increase in the pass price, 4 fewer skiers will purchase a pass. What is the maximum total revenue the resort can generate from season pass sales?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $15 price increases; revenue is \(R(x) = (600 + 15x)(200 - 4x) = -60x^2 + 600x + 120000\), which reaches its maximum at \(x = -\frac{600}{2(-60)} = 5\). The maximum revenue is \(R(5) = (600 + 75)(200 - 20) = 675 \times 180 = \$121,500\).

qs.q: A bakery sells specialty cakes for $20 each and averages 120 sales per month. For each $1 increase in price, the bakery expects to sell 2 fewer cakes per month. Find the price that will maximize the monthly revenue.
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $1 increases, so revenue is \(R(x) = (20 + x)(120 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 80x + 2400\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{80}{2(-2)} = 20\), giving a price of \(20 + 20 = \$40\).

qs.q: A school club sells custom water bottles for $8 each and averages 80 sales per week. For each $1 increase in price, sales decrease by 5 bottles per week. Find the price that will maximize weekly revenue.
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $1 increases, giving revenue \(R(x) = (8 + x)(80 - 5x) = -5x^2 + 40x + 640\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{40}{2(-5)} = 4\), so the optimal price is \(8 + 4 = \$12\).

qs.q: A community theater sells tickets to a play for $12 each, averaging 80 attendees per performance. For each $1 increase in ticket price, attendance decreases by 4 people. Find the ticket price that will maximize revenue per show.
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $1 increases, giving revenue \(R(x) = (12 + x)(80 - 4x) = -4x^2 + 32x + 960\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{32}{2(-4)} = 4\), making the optimal ticket price \(12 + 4 = \$16\).

qs.q: An online educator sells a study guide for $15 and averages 210 downloads per month. For each $1 increase in price, downloads decrease by 10 per month. Find the price that will maximize monthly revenue.
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $1 increases, giving revenue \(R(x) = (15 + x)(210 - 10x) = -10x^2 + 60x + 3150\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{60}{2(-10)} = 3\), so the revenue-maximizing price is \(15 + 3 = \$18\).

qs.q: A fitness center sells monthly passes for $25 each and currently sells 70 passes per month. For each $1 increase in pass price, the center expects to sell 2 fewer passes. Find the pass price that will maximize monthly revenue.
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $1 increases, giving revenue \(R(x) = (25 + x)(70 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 20x + 1750\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{20}{2(-2)} = 5\), giving an optimal pass price of \(25 + 5 = \$30\).

qs.q: A 60-passenger tour bus is \(\frac{5}{6}\) full when the ticket price is $30. For each $2 increase in ticket price, 2 fewer passengers take the tour. Find the ticket price that will maximize total revenue.
qs.s: The initial number of passengers is \(\frac{5}{6} \times 60 = 50\). With \(x\) price increases of \(2, R(x) = (30 + 2x)(50 - 2x) = -4x^2 + 40x + 1500\), which reaches its maximum at \(x = -\frac{40}{2(-4)} = 5\), giving a price of \(30 + 2(5) = \$40\).

qs.q: A sports arena has 6,000 season pass holders when the pass is priced at $500. A survey shows that for every $20 decrease in price, 400 additional passes will be sold. Find the pass price that will maximize revenue.
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $20 price reductions, giving \(R(x) = (500 - 20x)(6000 + 400x) = -8000x^2 + 80000x + 3000000\). The vertex is at \(x = -\frac{80000}{2(-8000)} = 5\), so the optimal price is \(500 - 20(5) = \$400\).

qs.q: An electronics company sells 1,200 tablets per month when priced at $200 each. For each $10 increase in price, sales drop by 30 units. Find the number of tablets sold per month that maximizes total revenue.
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $10 price increases, so \(R(x) = (200 + 10x)(1200 - 30x) = -300x^2 + 6000x + 240000\). The vertex occurs at \(x = -\frac{6000}{2(-300)} = 10\), so the number of units sold is \(1200 - 30(10) = 900\).

qs.q: A cafeteria sells 160 sandwiches per day when priced at $6.00 each. For each $0.50 increase in price, sales decrease by 8 sandwiches. Find the maximum daily revenue the cafeteria can achieve.
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $0.50 increases, so \(R(x) = (6 + 0.5x)(160 - 8x) = -4x^2 + 32x + 960\). The vertex is at \(x = -\frac{32}{2(-4)} = 4\), giving a maximum revenue of \((6 + 2)(160 - 32) = 8 \times 128 = \$1,024\).

qs.q: A concert promoter currently sells all 500 tickets for a performance when tickets are priced at $40 each. For each $5 increase in ticket price, 25 fewer tickets will be sold. Find the maximum total revenue that can be generated.
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of $5 increases, so \(R(x) = (40 + 5x)(500 - 25x) = -125x^2 + 1500x + 20000\). The maximum occurs at \(x = -\frac{1500}{2(-125)} = 6\), yielding a maximum revenue of \((40 + 30)(500 - 150) = 70 \times 350 = \$24,500\).

qs.q: Runner A is 10 km north of an intersection and is jogging south toward it at 8 km/h. At the same time, Runner B leaves the intersection, jogging east at 6 km/h. What is the minimum distance between the two runners?
qs.s: The square of the distance is \(D^2(t) = (10 - 8t)^2 + (6t)^2 = 100t^2 - 160t + 100\). The vertex occurs at \(t = \frac{160}{2(100)} = 0.8\text{ h}\), giving a minimum distance of \(\sqrt{(3.6)^2 + (4.8)^2} = 6\text{ km}\).

qs.q: Car A is 20 miles north of an intersection, traveling south at 30 mph. At the same moment, Car B leaves the intersection, traveling east at 30 mph. What is the minimum distance between the two cars?
qs.s: The square of the distance is \(D^2(t) = (20 - 30t)^2 + (30t)^2 = 1800t^2 - 1200t + 400\). The vertex is at \(t = \frac{1200}{2(1800)} = \frac{1}{3}\text{ h}\), giving a minimum distance of \(\sqrt{10^2 + 10^2} = 10\sqrt{2}\text{ miles}\).

qs.q: Cyclist A is 25 km south of an intersection and rides north toward it at 15 km/h. At the same time, Cyclist B leaves the intersection, riding west at 20 km/h. What is the minimum distance between the two cyclists?
qs.s: The square of the distance is \(D^2(t) = (15t - 25)^2 + (20t)^2 = 625t^2 - 750t + 625\). The vertex is at \(t = \frac{750}{2(625)} = 0.6\text{ h}\), yielding a minimum distance of \(\sqrt{(-16)^2 + 12^2} = 20\text{ km}\).

qs.q: Boat A is 50 km west of Boat B. Boat A travels east at 12 km/h, while Boat B travels south at 16 km/h. After how many hours will the distance between the two boats be at a minimum?
qs.s: The square of the distance is \(D^2(t) = (12t - 50)^2 + (16t)^2 = 400t^2 - 1200t + 2500\). The minimum occurs at the vertex \(t = -\frac{b}{2a} = \frac{1200}{2(400)} = 1.5\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: Ship A is 50 nautical miles west of Ship B. Ship A is heading east at 6 knots, and Ship B is heading south at 8 knots. At what time (in hours) will the two ships be closest to each other?
qs.s: The square of the distance is \(D^2(t) = (6t - 50)^2 + (8t)^2 = 100t^2 - 600t + 2500\). The vertex gives the time of minimum distance as \(t = \frac{600}{2(100)} = 3\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: Ship A is 80 nautical miles west of Ship B. At 9:00 AM, Ship A sets sail east at 16 knots, while Ship B sets sail north at 12 knots. At what time will the two ships be closest to each other?
qs.s: The square of the distance is \(D^2(t) = (16t - 80)^2 + (12t)^2 = 400t^2 - 2560t + 6400\), with vertex at \(t = \frac{2560}{2(400)} = 3.2\text{ hours}\) (3 hours 12 minutes). Adding this to 9:00 AM gives 12:12 PM.

qs.q: Airplane A leaves an airport flying east at 120 km/h. At the same time, Airplane B is 150 km north of the airport and flies south at 160 km/h. What is the minimum distance between the two airplanes?
qs.s: The square of the distance is \(D^2(t) = (120t)^2 + (150 - 160t)^2 = 40000t^2 - 48000t + 22500\). The vertex occurs at \(t = \frac{48000}{2(40000)} = 0.6\text{ h}\), resulting in a minimum distance of \(\sqrt{72^2 + 54^2} = 90\text{ km}\).

qs.q: Ship A is 100 km west of Ship B. Ship A heads east at 24 km/h, while Ship B heads south at 18 km/h. How far has Ship A traveled when the distance between the two ships is at a minimum?
qs.s: The square of the distance is \(D^2(t) = (24t - 100)^2 + (18t)^2 = 900t^2 - 4800t + 10000\), minimized at \(t = \frac{4800}{2(900)} = \frac{8}{3}\text{ h}\). Ship A has traveled \(24 \times \frac{8}{3} = 64\text{ km}\).

qs.q: Car A is 60 km west of an intersection and travels east at 40 km/h. At the same time, Car B is 80 km north of the intersection and travels south at 30 km/h. What is the minimum distance between the two cars?
qs.s: The square of the distance is \(D^2(t) = (40t - 60)^2 + (80 - 30t)^2 = 2500t^2 - 9600t + 10000\). The vertex is at \(t = \frac{9600}{2(2500)} = 1.92\text{ h}\), giving a minimum distance of \(\sqrt{(16.8)^2 + (22.4)^2} = 28\text{ km}\).

qs.q: Ship A is 50 nautical miles south of a port and sails north at 30 knots. At the same time, Ship B is 70 nautical miles east of the port and sails west at 40 knots. After how many hours will the distance between the two ships be at a minimum?
qs.s: The square of the distance is \(D^2(t) = (30t - 50)^2 + (70 - 40t)^2 = 2500t^2 - 8600t + 7400\). The minimum occurs at \(t = \frac{8600}{2(2500)} = 1.72\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: A rectangular pen is built against a barn wall that is 100 ft long (no fence along the barn). The side parallel to the barn can be at most 100 ft. There are 240 ft of fencing. Use the figure (x = each side perpendicular to the barn, L = side parallel to the barn). What is the maximum area of the pen?
qs.s: 2x + L = 240 gives A = x(240 - 2x), which peaks at x = 60 with L = 120, but L can be at most 100. So L = 100, x = 70 and A = 70 x 100 = 7000 sq ft.

qs.q: A club builds a rectangular corral against the side of a barn, so no fence is needed along the barn wall. The barn wall is 50 ft long, so the side parallel to the barn can be at most 50 ft. The club has 200 ft of fencing. Use the figure (x = each side perpendicular to the barn, L = side parallel to the barn). What is the maximum area of the corral?
qs.s: 2x + L = 200 gives A = x(200 - 2x), which peaks at x = 50 with L = 100, but L can be at most 50. So L = 50, x = 75 and A = 75 x 50 = 3750 sq ft.

qs.q: A rectangular paddock is built against a barn wall that is 120 ft long (no fence along the barn). The side parallel to the barn can be at most 120 ft. There are 200 ft of fencing. Use the figure (x = each side perpendicular to the barn, L = side parallel to the barn). What is the maximum area of the paddock?
qs.s: 2x + L = 200 gives A = x(200 - 2x), which peaks at x = 50 with L = 100. Since 100 is at most 120, the limit does not apply and A = 50 x 100 = 5000 sq ft.

qs.q: A rectangular garden is fenced against a barn wall that is 40 ft long (no fence along the barn). The side parallel to the barn can be at most 40 ft. There are 140 ft of fencing. Use the figure (x = each side perpendicular to the barn, L = side parallel to the barn). What is the maximum area of the garden?
qs.s: 2x + L = 140 gives A = x(140 - 2x), which peaks at x = 35 with L = 70, but L can be at most 40. So L = 40, x = 50 and A = 50 x 40 = 2000 sq ft.

qs.q: A farmer encloses a rectangular field against a barn wall that is 80 ft long (no fence along the barn). The side parallel to the barn can be at most 80 ft. There are 400 ft of fencing. Use the figure (x = each side perpendicular to the barn, L = side parallel to the barn). What value of x gives the maximum area?
qs.s: 2x + L = 400 gives A = x(400 - 2x), which peaks at x = 100 with L = 200, but L can be at most 80. So L = 80 and x = (400 - 80)/2 = 160 ft.

qs.q: A horse arena is built against a barn wall that is 150 ft long (no fence along the barn). The side parallel to the barn can be at most 150 ft. There are 420 ft of fencing. Use the figure (x = each side perpendicular to the barn, L = side parallel to the barn). What is the maximum area of the arena?
qs.s: 2x + L = 420 gives A = x(420 - 2x), which peaks at x = 105 with L = 210 (too long). So L = 150, x = 135 and A = 135 x 150 = 20250 sq ft.

qs.q: A corral is built against a barn wall that is 90 ft long (no fence along the barn) and is split into two equal pens by one dividing fence parallel to the sides perpendicular to the barn. There are 480 ft of fencing in total, and L can be at most 90 ft. Use the figure (x = length of each fence perpendicular to the barn, L = length along the barn). What is the maximum total area?
qs.s: Three fences of length x plus L use all the fence: 3x + L = 480, so A = x(480 - 3x), which peaks at x = 80 with L = 240 (too long). So L = 90, x = 130 and A = 130 x 90 = 11700 sq ft.
