qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(x^2 - 2x - 15 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 5)(x + 3) = 0\). The roots are \(x = 5\) and \(x = -3\), so the greater x-intercept is 5.

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = 3x(x - 3) - 2(x + 2)\).
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms gives \(y = 3x^2 - 11x - 4\). Setting \(y = 0\) and factoring yields \((3x + 1)(x - 4) = 0\), so the roots are \(x = -1/3\) and \(x = 4\), making the smaller x-intercept -1/3.

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = x^2 - 4x - 96\).
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(x^2 - 4x - 96 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 12)(x + 8) = 0\). The roots are \(x = 12\) and \(x = -8\), so the greater x-intercept is 12.

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = (2x + 1)(x - 4) + 7\).
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying gives \(y = 2x^2 - 7x + 3\). Setting \(y = 0\) and factoring gives \((2x - 1)(x - 3) = 0\), yielding roots \(x = 1/2\) and \(x = 3\), so the smaller x-intercept is 1/2.

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -2x^2 + 3x + 14\).
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(-2x^2 + 3x + 14 = 0\), or \(2x^2 - 3x - 14 = 0\), which factors as \((2x - 7)(x + 2) = 0\). The roots are \(x = 7/2\) and \(x = -2\), so the greater x-intercept is 7/2.

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = 6x^2 - x - 12\).
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(6x^2 - x - 12 = 0\), which factors as \((2x - 3)(3x + 4) = 0\). The roots are \(x = 3/2\) and \(x = -4/3\), so the greater x-intercept is 3/2.

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept for the quadratic equation \(y = x^2 + 5x + 6\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(x^2 + 5x + 6 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 2)(x + 3) = 0\), so \(x = -2\) or \(x = -3\), making the greater x-intercept \(-2\).

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept for the quadratic equation \(y = x^2 - 7x + 10\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(x^2 - 7x + 10 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 2)(x - 5) = 0\), so \(x = 2\) or \(x = 5\), making the smaller x-intercept \(2\).

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept for the quadratic equation \(y = x^2 - 2x - 15\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(x^2 - 2x - 15 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 5)(x + 3) = 0\), so \(x = 5\) or \(x = -3\), making the smaller x-intercept \(-3\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept for the quadratic equation \(y = x^2 - x - 12\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(x^2 - x - 12 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x + 3) = 0\), so \(x = 4\) or \(x = -3\), making the greater x-intercept \(4\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept for the quadratic equation \(y = x^2 - 4x - 21\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(x^2 - 4x - 21 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 7)(x + 3) = 0\), so \(x = 7\) or \(x = -3\), making the greater x-intercept \(7\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept for the quadratic equation \(y = (2x - 3)(x + 1) - 7\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) and expand to get \(2x^2 - x - 10 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x - 5)(x + 2) = 0\), so \(x = \frac{5}{2}\) or \(x = -2\), making the greater x-intercept \(\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept for the quadratic equation \(y = 3x(x + 1) - (x + 8)\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) and simplify to get \(3x^2 + 2x - 8 = 0\). Factoring gives \((3x - 4)(x + 2) = 0\), so \(x = \frac{4}{3}\) or \(x = -2\), making the greater x-intercept \(\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept for the quadratic equation \(y = 3x^2 - 10x - 8\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(3x^2 - 10x - 8 = 0\). Factoring gives \((3x + 2)(x - 4) = 0\), so \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\) or \(x = 4\), making the smaller x-intercept \(-\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept for the quadratic equation \(y = -3x^2 + 9x + 30\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(-3x^2 + 9x + 30 = 0\), and divide by \(-3\) to get \(x^2 - 3x - 10 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 5)(x + 2) = 0\), so \(x = 5\) or \(x = -2\), making the greater x-intercept \(5\).

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept for the quadratic equation \(y = 2x^2 - 9x + 4\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(2x^2 - 9x + 4 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x - 1)(x - 4) = 0\), so \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) or \(x = 4\), making the smaller x-intercept \(\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -x^2 + 36\).
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercepts, set \(y = 0\): \(-x^2 + 36 = 0\), which gives \(x^2 = 36\), so \(x = 6\) or \(x = -6\). The greater \(x\)-intercept is \(6\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -x^2 + 9\).
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercepts, set \(y = 0\): \(-x^2 + 9 = 0\), which gives \(x^2 = 9\), so \(x = 3\) or \(x = -3\). The greater \(x\)-intercept is \(3\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -x^2 + 25\).
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercepts, set \(y = 0\): \(-x^2 + 25 = 0\), which gives \(x^2 = 25\), so \(x = 5\) or \(x = -5\). The greater \(x\)-intercept is \(5\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -x^2 + 64\).
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercepts, set \(y = 0\): \(-x^2 + 64 = 0\), which gives \(x^2 = 64\), so \(x = 8\) or \(x = -8\). The greater \(x\)-intercept is \(8\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -x^2 + 16\).
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercepts, set \(y = 0\): \(-x^2 + 16 = 0\), which gives \(x^2 = 16\), so \(x = 4\) or \(x = -4\). The greater \(x\)-intercept is \(4\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -x^2 + 8x - 12\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(-x^2 + 8x - 12 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 8x + 12 = 0\) or \((x - 6)(x - 2) = 0\). The roots are \(x = 6\) and \(x = 2\), so the greater \(x\)-intercept is \(6\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -6x^2 + 7x + 3\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(6x^2 - 7x - 3 = 0\), which factors as \((3x + 1)(2x - 3) = 0\). The roots are \(x = -\frac{1}{3}\) and \(x = \frac{3}{2}\), so the greater \(x\)-intercept is \frac{3}{2}.

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -2x^2 - 6x + 20\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) and divide by \(-2\) to get \(x^2 + 3x - 10 = 0\), which factors as \((x + 5)(x - 2) = 0\). The roots are \(x = -5\) and \(x = 2\), so the greater \(x\)-intercept is \(2\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -2x^2 - x + 15\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(2x^2 + x - 15 = 0\), which factors as \((2x - 5)(x + 3) = 0\). The roots are \(x = \frac{5}{2}\) and \(x = -3\), so the greater \(x\)-intercept is \frac{5}{2}.

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 - 3x - 4\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) and multiply by \(-2\) to obtain \(x^2 + 6x + 8 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x + 4)(x + 2) = 0\), giving intercepts \(x = -4\) and \(x = -2\), so the greater x-intercept is \(-2\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - x - 4\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to obtain \(\frac{1}{2}x^2 - x - 4 = 0\), then multiply by \(2\) to get \(x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x + 2) = 0\), which yields \(x = 4\) and \(x = -2\), so the greater x-intercept is \(4\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 - 2x + 6\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) and multiply by \(-2\) to get \(x^2 + 4x - 12 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x + 6)(x - 2) = 0\), giving intercepts \(x = -6\) and \(x = 2\), so the greater x-intercept is \(2\).

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x^2 + x + 6\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) and multiply by \(-3\) to get \(x^2 - 3x - 18 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 6)(x + 3) = 0\), so the intercepts are \(x = 6\) and \(x = -3\), with \(-3\) being the smaller x-intercept.

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = \frac{1}{3}x^2 - 3x + 6\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) and multiply by \(3\) to get \(x^2 - 9x + 18 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 3)(x - 6) = 0\), so the intercepts are \(x = 3\) and \(x = 6\), and the smaller x-intercept is \(3\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = \frac{1}{2}(x + 2)^2 - \frac{1}{3}x - \frac{10}{3}\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(y = \frac{1}{2}(x^2 + 4x + 4) - \frac{1}{3}x - \frac{10}{3} = \frac{1}{2}x^2 + \frac{5}{3}x - \frac{4}{3}\). Setting \(y = 0\) and multiplying by \(6\) yields \(3x^2 + 10x - 8 = (3x - 2)(x + 4) = 0\), so the greater x-intercept is \(\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = \frac{1}{3}x(x + 2) - \frac{5}{6}x - \frac{5}{2}\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(y = \frac{1}{3}x^2 + \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{5}{6}x - \frac{5}{2} = \frac{1}{3}x^2 - \frac{1}{6}x - \frac{5}{2}\). Setting \(y = 0\) and multiplying by \(6\) results in \(2x^2 - x - 15 = (2x + 5)(x - 3) = 0\), so the greater x-intercept is \(3\).

qs.q: Find the greater x-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = \frac{2}{5}x^2 - \frac{7}{10}x - 3\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) and multiply by \(10\) to clear denominators, giving \(4x^2 - 7x - 30 = 0\). Factoring by grouping yields \((4x - 15)(x + 2) = 0\), which gives roots \(x = \frac{15}{4}\) and \(x = -2\), so the greater x-intercept is \(\frac{15}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -\frac{3}{2}x^2 + \frac{5}{4}x + 1\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) and multiply by \(-4\) to obtain \(6x^2 - 5x - 4 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x + 1)(3x - 4) = 0\), yielding intercepts \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = \frac{4}{3}\), so the smaller x-intercept is \(-\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the smaller x-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + \frac{7}{24}x + \frac{5}{12}\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) and multiply by \(-24\) to obtain \(12x^2 - 7x - 10 = 0\). Factoring gives \((3x + 2)(4x - 5) = 0\), which yields intercepts \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\) and \(x = \frac{5}{4}\), so the smaller x-intercept is \(-\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = 2x^2 + 7x + 3\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(2x^2 + 7x + 3 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x + 1)(x + 3) = 0\), which gives \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = -3\), so the greater intercept is \(-\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = 3x^2 - 7x + 2\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(3x^2 - 7x + 2 = 0\). Factoring gives \((3x - 1)(x - 2) = 0\), giving \(x = \frac{1}{3}\) and \(x = 2\), so the smaller intercept is \(\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = 3x^2 + 5x - 2\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(3x^2 + 5x - 2 = 0\). Factoring gives \((3x - 1)(x + 2) = 0\), which yields roots \(x = \frac{1}{3}\) and \(x = -2\), so the smaller intercept is \(-2\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = 2x^2 - 3x - 2\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(2x^2 - 3x - 2 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x + 1)(x - 2) = 0\), so \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) or \(x = 2\), with the greater intercept being \(2\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = 2x^2 + 3x - 5\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(2x^2 + 3x - 5 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x + 5)(x - 1) = 0\), so \(x = -\frac{5}{2}\) or \(x = 1\), with the greater intercept being \(1\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = (2x + 1)(x + 2) + 2x - 17\).
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms gives \(y = 2x^2 + 7x - 15\). Setting \(y = 0\) and factoring yields \((2x - 3)(x + 5) = 0\), which gives \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = -5\), so the greater intercept is \(\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = 2x(4x - 1) - 5(x + 3) - 3\).
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying gives \(y = 8x^2 - 7x - 18\). Setting \(y = 0\) and factoring gives \((8x + 9)(x - 2) = 0\), so \(x = -\frac{9}{8}\) or \(x = 2\), with the greater intercept being \(2\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = (3x - 1)^2 - (x + 5)^2\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(y = (9x^2 - 6x + 1) - (x^2 + 10x + 25) = 8x^2 - 16x - 24\). Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(8(x - 3)(x + 1) = 0\), yielding roots \(x = 3\) and \(x = -1\), so the smaller intercept is \(-1\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -6x^2 + 9x + 42\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) and divide by the common factor \(-3\) to get \(2x^2 - 3x - 14 = 0\). Factoring yields \((2x - 7)(x + 2) = 0\), so \(x = \frac{7}{2}\) and \(x = -2\), with the smaller intercept being \(-2\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = 6x^2 - 19x + 10\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(6x^2 - 19x + 10 = 0\). Factoring by grouping gives \((3x - 2)(2x - 5) = 0\), giving \(x = \frac{2}{3}\) and \(x = \frac{5}{2}\), so the greater intercept is \(\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -\frac{1}{5}x^2 + 5\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(-\frac{1}{5}(x^2 - 25) = 0\), which factors as \(-\frac{1}{5}(x - 5)(x + 5) = 0\). Setting the factors to zero gives \(x = 5\) or \(x = -5\), so the positive \(x\)-intercept is \(5\).

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -\frac{1}{4}x^2 + 4\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(-\frac{1}{4}(x^2 - 16) = 0\), which factors as \(-\frac{1}{4}(x - 4)(x + 4) = 0\). Solving gives \(x = 4\) or \(x = -4\), so the positive \(x\)-intercept is \(4\).

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 2\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(-\frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 4) = 0\), which factors as \(-\frac{1}{2}(x - 2)(x + 2) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 2\) or \(x = -2\), so the positive \(x\)-intercept is \(2\).

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -\frac{1}{8}x^2 + 8\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(-\frac{1}{8}(x^2 - 64) = 0\), which factors as \(-\frac{1}{8}(x - 8)(x + 8) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 8\) or \(x = -8\), so the positive \(x\)-intercept is \(8\).

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -\frac{1}{6}x^2 + 6\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(-\frac{1}{6}(x^2 - 36) = 0\), which factors as \(-\frac{1}{6}(x - 6)(x + 6) = 0\). Solving yields \(x = 6\) or \(x = -6\), so the positive \(x\)-intercept is \(6\).

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = 6x^2 - x - 2\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) and factor the trinomial into \((3x - 2)(2x + 1) = 0\). Solving each factor gives \(x = \frac{2}{3}\) or \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\), so the positive \(x\)-intercept is \(\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = (x - 1)(x - 3) - 24\).
qs.s: Expand to get \(y = x^2 - 4x + 3 - 24 = x^2 - 4x - 21\), then set \(y = 0\) and factor as \((x - 7)(x + 3) = 0\). Setting the factors to zero gives \(x = 7\) or \(x = -3\), so the positive \(x\)-intercept is \(7\).

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x^2 - x + 6\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) and factor out \(-\frac{1}{3}\) to get \(-\frac{1}{3}(x^2 + 3x - 18) = 0\), which factors as \(-\frac{1}{3}(x + 6)(x - 3) = 0\). Solving the factors gives \(x = -6\) or \(x = 3\), so the positive \(x\)-intercept is \(3\).

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = -\frac{2}{3}x^2 + 54\).
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(-\frac{2}{3}x^2 + 54 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 = 54 \cdot \frac{3}{2} = 81\). Factoring as \(-\frac{2}{3}(x - 9)(x + 9) = 0\) yields \(x = 9\) or \(x = -9\), so the positive \(x\)-intercept is \(9\).

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-intercept of the quadratic function \(y = 2x^2 - 3x - 14\).
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) and factor the quadratic expression to get \((2x - 7)(x + 2) = 0\). Solving each factor yields \(x = \frac{7}{2}\) or \(x = -2\), so the positive \(x\)-intercept is \(\frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution to the equation \(7x(6x + 5) = 0\).
qs.s: Using the zero factor property, set \(7x = 0\) or \(6x + 5 = 0\). Solving the second equation gives \(6x = -5\), so \(x = -\frac{5}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution to the equation \(5x(3x + 7) = 0\).
qs.s: Setting each factor to zero gives \(5x = 0\) or \(3x + 7 = 0\). Solving the non-zero factor yields \(3x = -7\), so \(x = -\frac{7}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution to the equation \(3x(2x - 5) = 0\).
qs.s: By the zero factor property, either \(3x = 0\) or \(2x - 5 = 0\). Solving \(2x - 5 = 0\) gives \(2x = 5\), so \(x = \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution to the equation \(2x(7x - 4) = 0\).
qs.s: Set each factor equal to zero: \(2x = 0\) or \(7x - 4 = 0\). Solving \(7x - 4 = 0\) gives \(7x = 4\), so \(x = \frac{4}{7}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution to the equation \(4x(5x - 3) = 0\).
qs.s: Applying the zero factor property gives \(4x = 0\) or \(5x - 3 = 0\). Solving \(5x - 3 = 0\) results in \(5x = 3\), so \(x = \frac{3}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the greater solution to the equation \(2x(3x + 1) = (3x + 1)^2\).
qs.s: Subtract \((3x + 1)^2\) to get \(2x(3x + 1) - (3x + 1)^2 = 0\), then factor out \((3x + 1)\) to obtain \((3x + 1)(-x - 1) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = -\frac{1}{3}\) and \(x = -1\), so the greater solution is \(-\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \(3x(x + 1) = x(x + 2) + 15\).
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(3x^2 + 3x = x^2 + 2x + 15\), which rearranges to \(2x^2 + x - 15 = 0\). Factoring yields \((2x - 5)(x + 3) = 0\), so the positive solution is \(x = \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the greatest solution to the equation \(2x^3 - 5x^2 - 12x = 0\)?
qs.s: Factor out the common term \(x\) to get \(x(2x^2 - 5x - 12) = 0\), which factors further into \(x(2x + 3)(x - 4) = 0\). The roots are \(x = 0\), \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\), and \(x = 4\), so the greatest solution is \(4\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \(2x(4x + 7) = 15\).
qs.s: Expand and set the equation to zero: \(8x^2 + 14x - 15 = 0\). Factoring gives \((4x - 3)(2x + 5) = 0\), which yields \(x = \frac{3}{4}\) or \(x = -\frac{5}{2}\), so the positive solution is \(\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the greater solution to the equation \(4x(2x - 1) = x(2x + 1) + 4\).
qs.s: Expand both sides to get \(8x^2 - 4x = 2x^2 + x + 4\), then rearrange to \(6x^2 - 5x - 4 = 0\). Factoring gives \((3x - 4)(2x + 1) = 0\), so the roots are \(x = \frac{4}{3}\) and \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\), with \(\frac{4}{3}\) being the greater solution.

qs.q: What is the smaller solution to the equation \((4x - \frac{1}{2})(x - \frac{1}{5}) = 0\)?
qs.s: Setting each factor to zero gives \(4x - \frac{1}{2} = 0 \implies x = \frac{1}{8}\) or \(x - \frac{1}{5} = 0 \implies x = \frac{1}{5}\). Since \(\frac{1}{8} = \frac{5}{40} < \frac{8}{40} = \frac{1}{5}\), the smaller solution is \(\frac{1}{8}\).

qs.q: What is the greater solution to the equation \((x + \frac{1}{3})(2x - \frac{3}{4}) = 0\)?
qs.s: Applying the zero factor property gives \(x + \frac{1}{3} = 0 \implies x = -\frac{1}{3}\) or \(2x - \frac{3}{4} = 0 \implies x = \frac{3}{8}\). Since \(\frac{3}{8} > -\frac{1}{3}\), the greater solution is \(\frac{3}{8}\).

qs.q: What is the smaller solution to the equation \((x - \frac{1}{2})(3x - \frac{1}{4}) = 0\)?
qs.s: Setting each factor equal to zero yields \(x - \frac{1}{2} = 0 \implies x = \frac{1}{2}\) or \(3x - \frac{1}{4} = 0 \implies x = \frac{1}{12}\). Comparing the two roots, the smaller solution is \(\frac{1}{12}\).

qs.q: What is the greater solution to the equation \((x - \frac{1}{4})(2x - \frac{1}{3}) = 0\)?
qs.s: Setting each factor equal to zero gives \(x - \frac{1}{4} = 0 \implies x = \frac{1}{4}\) or \(2x - \frac{1}{3} = 0 \implies x = \frac{1}{6}\). Since \(\frac{1}{4} > \frac{1}{6}\), the greater solution is \(\frac{1}{4}\).

qs.q: What is the greater solution to the equation \((x - \frac{2}{3})(2x - \frac{1}{2}) = 0\)?
qs.s: By the zero factor property, \(x - \frac{2}{3} = 0 \implies x = \frac{2}{3}\) or \(2x - \frac{1}{2} = 0 \implies x = \frac{1}{4}\). Since \(\frac{2}{3} = \frac{8}{12} > \frac{3}{12} = \frac{1}{4}\), the greater solution is \(\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: What is the greatest solution to the equation \((2x + \frac{1}{2})(3x - \frac{1}{4})(4x - \frac{2}{3}) = 0\)?
qs.s: Setting each factor to zero yields the roots \(x = -\frac{1}{4}\), \(x = \frac{1}{12}\), and \(x = \frac{2}{12} = \frac{1}{6}\). Comparing these values, the greatest solution is \(\frac{1}{6}\).

qs.q: What is the smaller solution to the equation \((2x - 1)(x - \frac{1}{3}) = \frac{2}{3}\)?
qs.s: Expanding and moving all terms to one side gives \(2x^2 - \frac{5}{3}x - \frac{1}{3} = 0\), which multiplies by \(3\) to \(6x^2 - 5x - 1 = 0\). Factoring gives \((6x + 1)(x - 1) = 0\), yielding solutions \(x = -\frac{1}{6}\) and \(x = 1\), of which \(-\frac{1}{6}\) is smaller.

qs.q: What is the greater solution to the equation \((\frac{2}{3}x - \frac{1}{2})(\frac{3}{5}x + \frac{1}{4}) = 0\)?
qs.s: Setting each factor to zero gives \(\frac{2}{3}x = \frac{1}{2} \implies x = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{3}{2} = \frac{3}{4}\), or \(\frac{3}{5}x = -\frac{1}{4} \implies x = -\frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{5}{3} = -\frac{5}{12}\). The greater solution is \(\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: What is the smaller solution to the equation \((3x - \frac{1}{2})(2x + 1) - (3x - \frac{1}{2})(x + 4) = 0\)?
qs.s: Factor out the common term to get \((3x - \frac{1}{2})[(2x + 1) - (x + 4)] = (3x - \frac{1}{2})(x - 3) = 0\). By the zero factor property, \(x = \frac{1}{6}\) or \(x = 3\), so the smaller solution is \(\frac{1}{6}\).

qs.q: What is the greater solution to the equation \(6x^2 - \frac{7}{2}x = -\frac{1}{2}\)?
qs.s: Write in standard form \(6x^2 - \frac{7}{2}x + \frac{1}{2} = 0\) and multiply by \(2\) to obtain \(12x^2 - 7x + 1 = 0\). Factoring gives \((3x - 1)(4x - 1) = 0\), so \(x = \frac{1}{3}\) or \(x = \frac{1}{4}\), with the greater solution being \(\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \((3x - 2)(3x - 2) = 0\).
qs.s: By the zero factor property, set \(3x - 2 = 0\). Solving for \(x\) gives \(3x = 2\), which simplifies to \(x = \frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \((5w - 2)(5w - 2) = 0\).
qs.s: Using the zero factor property, set \(5w - 2 = 0\). Adding \(2\) to both sides and dividing by \(5\) results in \(w = \frac{2}{5}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \((4a + 3)(4a + 3) = 0\).
qs.s: Set the repeated factor equal to zero: \(4a + 3 = 0\). Subtracting \(3\) and dividing by \(4\) yields \(a = -\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \((2k + 5)(2k + 5) = 0\).
qs.s: Setting the factor equal to zero gives \(2k + 5 = 0\). Subtracting \(5\) and dividing by \(2\) gives \(k = -\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \((3m + 4)(3m + 4) = 0\).
qs.s: Set the factor equal to zero: \(3m + 4 = 0\). Solving for \(m\) gives \(3m = -4\), so \(m = -\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation: \(6x^2 - 11x = 10\).
qs.s: Write the equation as \(6x^2 - 11x - 10 = 0\) and factor it into \((3x + 2)(2x - 5) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\) and \(x = \frac{5}{2}\), so the positive solution is \(\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the greater solution to the equation: \((4x - 1)(x - 1) = x(x + 3) + 4\).
qs.s: Expand both sides to obtain \(4x^2 - 5x + 1 = x^2 + 3x + 4\), which simplifies to \(3x^2 - 8x - 3 = 0\). Factoring gives \((3x + 1)(x - 3) = 0\), resulting in solutions \(x = -\frac{1}{3}\) and \(x = 3\), so the greater solution is \(3\).

qs.q: Find the smaller solution to the equation: \((2x - 1)^2 = 7x + 4\).
qs.s: Expanding the left side yields \(4x^2 - 4x + 1 = 7x + 4\), which rearranges to \(4x^2 - 11x - 3 = 0\). Factoring produces \((4x + 1)(x - 3) = 0\), giving solutions \(x = -\frac{1}{4}\) and \(x = 3\), with \(-\frac{1}{4}\) being the smaller solution.

qs.q: Find the greater solution to the equation: \((x - 1)(2x + 5) = 4\).
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging into standard form gives \(2x^2 + 3x - 9 = 0\), which factors as \((2x - 3)(x + 3) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = -3\), so the greater solution is \(\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(36x^2 + 49 = 84x\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in standard form as \(36x^2 - 84x + 49 = 0\), which factors as \((6x - 7)^2 = 0\). Setting \(6x - 7 = 0\) yields \(x = \frac{7}{6}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its greater solution: \((0.1k + 2)(0.5k - 7) = 0\).
qs.s: Setting each factor equal to zero gives \(0.1k + 2 = 0 \implies k = -20\) and \(0.5k - 7 = 0 \implies k = 14\). The greater solution is \(14\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its negative solution: \((0.25w + 3)(0.2w - 4) = 0\).
qs.s: Set each factor to zero to obtain \(0.25w + 3 = 0 \implies w = -12\) and \(0.2w - 4 = 0 \implies w = 20\). The negative solution is \(-12\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its lesser solution: \((0.2m + 3)(0.75m - 6) = 0\).
qs.s: Setting each factor to zero yields \(0.2m + 3 = 0 \implies m = -15\) and \(0.75m - 6 = 0 \implies m = 8\). Therefore, the lesser solution is \(-15\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its greater solution: \((0.5x - 1)(0.25x + 2) = 0\).
qs.s: Setting each factor to zero gives \(0.5x - 1 = 0 \implies x = 2\) and \(0.25x + 2 = 0 \implies x = -8\). Comparing the roots, the greater solution is \(2\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its positive solution: \((0.25t - 1)(0.5t + 3) = 0\).
qs.s: Set each factor to zero to find \(0.25t - 1 = 0 \implies t = 4\) and \(0.5t + 3 = 0 \implies t = -6\). Thus, the positive solution is \(4\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its positive solution: \(0.25x^2 - x = 3\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(0.25x^2 - x - 3 = 0\) and multiply by \(4\) to obtain \(x^2 - 4x - 12 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x - 6)(x + 2) = 0\), which gives \(x = 6\) and \(x = -2\), so the positive solution is \(6\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its greater solution: \((0.25x - 2)(2x + 1) = (0.25x - 2)(x + 4)\).
qs.s: Rearrange to \((0.25x - 2)(2x + 1) - (0.25x - 2)(x + 4) = 0\) and factor out the common term to get \((0.25x - 2)(x - 3) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero yields \(x = 8\) and \(x = 3\), so the greater solution is \(8\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its greater solution: \(0.2x^2 - 0.7x = 1.5\).
qs.s: Set the equation to zero as \(0.2x^2 - 0.7x - 1.5 = 0\) and multiply by \(10\) to get \(2x^2 - 7x - 15 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x + 3)(x - 5) = 0\), yielding solutions \(x = -1.5\) and \(x = 5\), of which \(5\) is the greater.

qs.q: Solve the equation for its greatest solution: \((0.5x - 4)(0.2x + 3)(0.1x - 1) = 0\).
qs.s: Applying the zero factor property yields \(0.5x - 4 = 0 \implies x = 8\), \(0.2x + 3 = 0 \implies x = -15\), and \(0.1x - 1 = 0 \implies x = 10\). Among the solutions \(8, -15,\) and \(10\), the greatest solution is \(10\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its positive solution: \((0.5x - 1)(x + 3) = 3\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(0.5x^2 + 0.5x - 3 = 3\), which simplifies to \(0.5x^2 + 0.5x - 6 = 0\), or \(x^2 + x - 12 = 0\) after multiplying by \(2\). Factoring into \((x + 4)(x - 3) = 0\) gives solutions \(x = -4\) and \(x = 3\), so the positive solution is \(3\).

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring: \(x^2 = 49\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(x^2 - 49 = 0\) and factor as \((x - 7)(x + 7) = 0\). Applying the zero factor property gives \(x - 7 = 0\) or \(x + 7 = 0\), which yields \(x = \pm 7\).

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring: \(a^2 = 36\).
qs.s: Subtract 36 from both sides to get \(a^2 - 36 = 0\), then factor as \((a - 6)(a + 6) = 0\). By the zero factor property, \(a = \pm 6\).

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring: \(m^2 = 121\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(m^2 - 121 = 0\) and factor as \((m - 11)(m + 11) = 0\). Using the zero factor property, \(m - 11 = 0\) or \(m + 11 = 0\), so \(m = \pm 11\).

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring: \(y^2 = 100\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(y^2 - 100 = 0\) and factor the difference of squares as \((y - 10)(y + 10) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(y = \pm 10\).

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring: \(w^2 = 64\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(w^2 - 64 = 0\) and factor as \((w - 8)(w + 8) = 0\). Setting each factor equal to zero gives \(w = \pm 8\).

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring: \(4x^2 = 169\).
qs.s: Subtract 169 to obtain \(4x^2 - 169 = 0\) and factor as \((2x - 13)(2x + 13) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(2x = 13\) or \(2x = -13\), so \(x = \pm \frac{13}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring: \((3x - 2)^2 = 49\).
qs.s: Subtract 49 to write \(((3x - 2) - 7)((3x - 2) + 7) = 0\), which simplifies to \((3x - 9)(3x + 5) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero yields \(x = 3\) or \(x = -\frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring: \((x - 3)(x + 3) = 40\).
qs.s: Expand the left side to get \(x^2 - 9 = 40\), then subtract 40 to set the equation to zero: \(x^2 - 49 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 7)(x + 7) = 0\), so \(x = \pm 7\).

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring: \(5x^2 - 27 = 2x^2 + 48\).
qs.s: Rearrange all terms to one side to get \(3x^2 - 75 = 0\), then factor out the greatest common factor to get \(3(x^2 - 25) = 3(x - 5)(x + 5) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero yields \(x = \pm 5\).

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring: \((x + 5)^2 = 64\).
qs.s: Rewrite as \((x + 5)^2 - 64 = 0\) and factor the difference of squares as \(((x + 5) - 8)((x + 5) + 8) = (x - 3)(x + 13) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 3\) or \(x = -13\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(x^2 = 6x\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(x^2 - 6x = 0\) and factor out the common term to get \(x(x - 6) = 0\). By the zero factor property, the solutions are \(x = 0\) or \(x = 6\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(m^2 = -5m\)
qs.s: Add \(5m\) to both sides to obtain \(m^2 + 5m = 0\), which factors as \(m(m + 5) = 0\). Applying the zero factor property yields \(m = 0\) or \(m = -5\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(w^2 = -3w\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(w^2 + 3w = 0\) and factor out \(w\) to obtain \(w(w + 3) = 0\). By the zero factor property, the solutions are \(w = 0\) or \(w = -3\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(7t = t^2\)
qs.s: Subtract \(7t\) from both sides to obtain \(t^2 - 7t = 0\), then factor as \(t(t - 7) = 0\). Setting each factor equal to zero gives \(t = 0\) or \(t = 7\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(y^2 = -y\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(y^2 + y = 0\) and factor out \(y\) to get \(y(y + 1) = 0\). Setting each factor equal to zero gives \(y = 0\) or \(y = -1\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(x^2 - 3x = 10\)
qs.s: Subtract 10 from both sides to write the equation in standard form as \(x^2 - 3x - 10 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 5)(x + 2) = 0\). By the zero factor property, the solutions are \(x = 5\) or \(x = -2\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \((k - 3)^2 = 3k - 5\)
qs.s: Expand the left side to get \(k^2 - 6k + 9 = 3k - 5\) and subtract \(3k - 5\) to obtain \(k^2 - 9k + 14 = 0\). Factoring yields \((k - 2)(k - 7) = 0\), so the solutions are \(k = 2\) or \(k = 7\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(y(y + 4) = 21\)
qs.s: Expand the left side and subtract 21 to get \(y^2 + 4y - 21 = 0\), then factor into \((y + 7)(y - 3) = 0\). Setting each factor equal to zero gives \(y = -7\) or \(y = 3\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(2m^2 + 5m = 12\)
qs.s: Subtract 12 to write the equation as \(2m^2 + 5m - 12 = 0\), which factors into \((2m - 3)(m + 4) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero yields \(m = \frac{3}{2}\) or \(m = -4\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(3x^2 = 5x\)
qs.s: Rearrange the equation to \(3x^2 - 5x = 0\) and factor out \(x\) to get \(x(3x - 5) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 0\) or \(3x - 5 = 0\), which yields \(x = 0\) or \(x = \frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: What is the non-integer solution to the equation \((x - 6)(x + 2)(3x - 4) = 0\)?
qs.s: Setting each factor equal to zero yields the solutions \(x = 6\), \(x = -2\), and \(3x - 4 = 0 \implies x = \frac{4}{3}\). Thus, the only non-integer solution is \(\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: What is the greatest solution to the equation \((x - 3)(x + 5)(2x - 1) = 0\)?
qs.s: Set each factor equal to zero: \(x - 3 = 0 \implies x = 3\), \(x + 5 = 0 \implies x = -5\), and \(2x - 1 = 0 \implies x = \frac{1}{2}\). Comparing these values, the greatest solution is \(3\).

qs.q: What is the greatest solution to the equation \((x + 4)(x - 2)(2x - 7) = 0\)?
qs.s: Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = -4\), \(x = 2\), and \(2x - 7 = 0 \implies x = \frac{7}{2}\). Comparing \(-4 < 2 < \frac{7}{2}\), the greatest solution is \(\frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the smallest solution to the equation \((x - 5)(x + 2)(2x + 1) = 0\)?
qs.s: Applying the zero factor property yields \(x = 5\), \(x = -2\), and \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\). Comparing the values, \(-2 < -\frac{1}{2} < 5\), so the smallest solution is \(-2\).

qs.q: What is the smallest solution to the equation \((x - 1)(x - 4)(2x + 5) = 0\)?
qs.s: Set each factor to zero to obtain \(x = 1\), \(x = 4\), and \(2x + 5 = 0 \implies x = -\frac{5}{2}\). Since \(-\frac{5}{2} < 1 < 4\), the smallest solution is \(-\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the greatest solution to the equation \((2x - 3)(x^2 - 5x - 14) = 0\)?
qs.s: Factor the quadratic to obtain \((2x - 3)(x - 7)(x + 2) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero yields \(x = \frac{3}{2}\), \(x = 7\), and \(x = -2\), so the greatest solution is \(7\).

qs.q: What is the smallest solution to the equation \((x - 6)(2x + 1)(3x + 7)(x - 2) = 0\)?
qs.s: Applying the zero factor property gives \(x = 6\), \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\), \(x = -\frac{7}{3}\), and \(x = 2\). Comparing these values, \(-\frac{7}{3} < -\frac{1}{2} < 2 < 6\), so the smallest solution is \(-\frac{7}{3}\).

qs.q: What is the sum of all solutions to the equation \((2x - 3)(x + 4)(3x + 1) = 0\)?
qs.s: Setting each factor to zero gives the solutions \(x = \frac{3}{2}\), \(x = -4\), and \(x = -\frac{1}{3}\). Finding a common denominator to add them gives \(\frac{9}{6} - \frac{24}{6} - \frac{2}{6} = -\frac{17}{6}\).

qs.q: What is the smallest solution to the equation \(2x^3 - x^2 - 15x = 0\)?
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(x\) to get \(x(2x^2 - x - 15) = x(2x + 5)(x - 3) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero yields \(x = 0\), \(x = -\frac{5}{2}\), and \(x = 3\), so the smallest solution is \(-\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the greatest solution to the equation \((x + 4)(6x^2 - 7x - 3) = 0\)?
qs.s: Factor the quadratic factor to obtain \((x + 4)(3x + 1)(2x - 3) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = -4\), \(x = -\frac{1}{3}\), and \(x = \frac{3}{2}\), so the greatest solution is \(\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the non-zero solution to the equation \(x(x - 3)(x - 3) = 0\)?
qs.s: Setting each factor equal to zero gives \(x = 0\) or \(x - 3 = 0\), yielding solutions \(x = 0\) and \(x = 3\). Thus, the non-zero solution is \(3\).

qs.q: What is the least solution to the equation \(x(x + 6)(x + 6) = 0\)?
qs.s: Applying the zero factor property yields \(x = 0\) and \(x = -6\). The least solution is \(-6\).

qs.q: What is the greatest solution to the equation \(x(x + 4)(x + 4) = 0\)?
qs.s: By the zero factor property, \(x = 0\) or \(x + 4 = 0\), which gives solutions \(x = 0\) and \(x = -4\). Between these two values, the greatest solution is \(0\).

qs.q: What is the least solution to the equation \(x(x - 8)(x - 8) = 0\)?
qs.s: Setting each factor to zero yields \(x = 0\) and \(x = 8\). Therefore, the least solution is \(0\).

qs.q: What is the greatest solution to the equation \(x(x - 5)(x - 5) = 0\)?
qs.s: Applying the zero factor property gives \(x = 0\) or \(x - 5 = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = 0\) and \(x = 5\). The greatest solution is \(5\).

qs.q: What is the least solution to the equation \(x^3 + 36x = -12x^2\)?
qs.s: Rearrange the equation to \(x^3 + 12x^2 + 36x = 0\) and factor out \(x\) to get \(x(x + 6)^2 = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 0\) and \(x = -6\), so the least solution is \(-6\).

qs.q: What is the least solution to the equation \(x^3 - 2x^2 - 15x = 0\)?
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) gives \(x(x^2 - 2x - 15) = 0\), which factors into \(x(x - 5)(x + 3) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = 0\), \(x = 5\), and \(x = -3\), so the least solution is \(-3\).

qs.q: What is the greatest solution to the equation \(4x^3 - 20x^2 + 25x = 0\)?
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) yields \(x(4x^2 - 20x + 25) = 0\), which factors as \(x(2x - 5)^2 = 0\). Setting the factors to zero gives \(x = 0\) and \(x = \frac{5}{2}\), so the greatest solution is \(\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the greatest solution to the equation \(x^3 - 14x^2 + 49x = 0\)?
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) gives \(x(x^2 - 14x + 49) = 0\), which factors as \(x(x - 7)^2 = 0\). By the zero factor property, the solutions are \(x = 0\) and \(x = 7\), so the greatest solution is \(7\).

qs.q: What is the least solution to the equation \(2x^3 - 5x^2 = 12x\)?
qs.s: Rearranging gives \(2x^3 - 5x^2 - 12x = 0\), which factors as \(x(2x + 3)(x - 4) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero yields \(x = 0\), \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\), and \(x = 4\), so the least solution is \(-\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution to the equation \(x^2 = -9x\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(x^2 + 9x = 0\) and factor as \(x(x + 9) = 0\). By the zero factor property, the solutions are \(x = 0\) and \(x = -9\), so the non-zero solution is \(-9\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution to the equation \(x^2 = -5x\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(x^2 + 5x = 0\) and factor to get \(x(x + 5) = 0\). By the zero factor property, \(x = 0\) or \(x = -5\), so the non-zero solution is \(-5\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution to the equation \(x^2 = 8x\).
qs.s: Subtract \(8x\) from both sides to get \(x^2 - 8x = 0\), which factors as \(x(x - 8) = 0\). The zero factor property gives \(x = 0\) or \(x = 8\), so the non-zero solution is \(8\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution to the equation \(x^2 = -7x\).
qs.s: Add \(7x\) to both sides to obtain \(x^2 + 7x = 0\), which factors into \(x(x + 7) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 0\) or \(x = -7\), so the non-zero solution is \(-7\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution to the equation \(x^2 = 4x\).
qs.s: Rearrange the equation to \(x^2 - 4x = 0\) and factor out \(x\) to get \(x(x - 4) = 0\). Applying the zero factor property gives \(x = 0\) or \(x = 4\), so the non-zero solution is \(4\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \(x^2 - 4x = 21\).
qs.s: Subtract 21 from both sides to obtain \(x^2 - 4x - 21 = 0\), which factors into \((x - 7)(x + 3) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero yields \(x = 7\) or \(x = -3\), so the positive solution is \(7\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution to the equation \(3x^2 = 7x\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(3x^2 - 7x = 0\) and factor out \(x\) to get \(x(3x - 7) = 0\). Setting the non-zero factor to zero gives \(3x - 7 = 0\), so \(x = \frac{7}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \((x - 2)(x + 5) = 8\).
qs.s: Expand the left side to get \(x^2 + 3x - 10 = 8\), then subtract 8 to obtain \(x^2 + 3x - 18 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 6)(x - 3) = 0\), so the positive solution is \(x = 3\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \(2x^2 + 7x = 15\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(2x^2 + 7x - 15 = 0\) and factor it as \((2x - 3)(x + 5) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) or \(x = -5\), so the positive solution is \(\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \(3x^2 - 4x + 1 = x^2 + 2x + 9\).
qs.s: Collect all terms on one side to get \(2x^2 - 6x - 8 = 0\), then divide by 2 to obtain \(x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x + 1) = 0\), so the positive solution is \(x = 4\).

qs.q: Solve the equation over the real numbers: \(x^2 + 9 = 0\).
qs.s: Subtracting 9 from both sides gives \(x^2 = -9\). Since the square of any real number is non-negative, the equation has no real solution.

qs.q: Solve the equation over the real numbers: \(x^2 + 4 = 0\).
qs.s: Subtracting 4 from both sides gives \(x^2 = -4\). Since the square of any real number cannot be negative, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve the equation over the real numbers: \(x^2 + 16 = 0\).
qs.s: Subtracting 16 from both sides yields \(x^2 = -16\). Because the square of any real number cannot be negative, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve the equation over the real numbers: \(x^2 + 49 = 0\).
qs.s: Subtracting 49 from both sides yields \(x^2 = -49\). Since the square of a real number cannot be negative, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve the equation over the real numbers: \(x^2 + 25 = 0\).
qs.s: Subtracting 25 from both sides gives \(x^2 = -25\). Since no real number squared equals a negative number, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve the equation over the real numbers: \(2(x - 4)(x + 4) + 11 = -93\).
qs.s: Expanding the left side gives \(2(x^2 - 16) + 11 = -93\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 - 21 = -93\) and then \(2x^2 = -72\). Dividing by 2 yields \(x^2 = -36\), which has no real solution since the square of any real number cannot be negative.

qs.q: Solve the equation over the real numbers: \((x - 7)(x + 7) + 3(x + 4) = 3x - 181\).
qs.s: Expanding the left side gives \(x^2 - 49 + 3x + 12 = 3x - 181\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 3x - 37 = 3x - 181\). Subtracting \(3x\) and adding 37 yields \(x^2 = -144\), which has no real solution because the square of any real number is non-negative.

qs.q: Solve the equation over the real numbers: \(\frac{x^2 + 20}{4} = \frac{x^2 - 20}{6}\).
qs.s: Cross-multiplying gives \(6(x^2 + 20) = 4(x^2 - 20)\), which simplifies to \(6x^2 + 120 = 4x^2 - 80\), or \(2x^2 = -200\). Dividing by 2 yields \(x^2 = -100\), which has no real solution because a real number squared cannot be negative.

qs.q: Solve the equation over the real numbers: \((x + 5)^2 - 10x = -56\).
qs.s: Expanding the left side yields \(x^2 + 10x + 25 - 10x = -56\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 25 = -56\) or \(x^2 = -81\). Because the square of a real number is always non-negative, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve the equation over the real numbers: \(3(x^2 + 8) = x^2 - 104\).
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(3x^2 + 24 = x^2 - 104\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 = -128\) and then \(x^2 = -64\). Since the square of any real number cannot be negative, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring. What is the positive solution to \(x^2 = 4\)?
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(x^2 - 4 = 0\) and factor as \((x - 2)(x + 2) = 0\). Setting the positive factor to zero gives \(x = 2\).

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring. What is the positive solution to \(w^2 = 49\)?
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(w^2 - 49 = 0\) and factor as \((w - 7)(w + 7) = 0\). Setting the factors equal to zero gives \(w = 7\) and \(w = -7\), so the positive solution is 7.

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring. What is the negative solution to \(m^2 = 9\)?
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(m^2 - 9 = 0\) and factor as \((m - 3)(m + 3) = 0\). Setting \(m + 3 = 0\) yields the negative solution \(m = -3\).

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring. What is the smaller solution to \(t^2 = 25\)?
qs.s: Subtract 25 from both sides to obtain \(t^2 - 25 = 0\), which factors into \((t - 5)(t + 5) = 0\). The roots are \(t = 5\) and \(t = -5\), making the smaller solution \(-5\).

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring. What is the greater solution to \(k^2 = 16\)?
qs.s: Subtract 16 from both sides to get \(k^2 - 16 = 0\), which factors as \((k - 4)(k + 4) = 0\). The roots are \(k = 4\) and \(k = -4\), so the greater solution is 4.

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring: \(x^2 - 3x = 28\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Write the equation in standard form as \(x^2 - 3x - 28 = 0\), then factor to get \((x - 7)(x + 4) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = 7\) and \(x = -4\), so the greater solution is 7.

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring: \(\frac{x}{x - 3} - \frac{2}{x + 2} = \frac{10}{x^2 - x - 6}\). What is the valid solution?
qs.s: Multiply both sides by \((x - 3)(x + 2)\) to obtain \(x(x + 2) - 2(x - 3) = 10\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 4 = 0\), or \((x - 2)(x + 2) = 0\). Since \(x = -2\) makes the denominator zero, it must be rejected as extraneous, leaving \(x = 2\) as the only valid solution.

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring: \(2x^2 + 7x = 15\). What is the positive solution?
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in general form as \(2x^2 + 7x - 15 = 0\), then factor by grouping to obtain \((2x - 3)(x + 5) = 0\). Setting \(2x - 3 = 0\) yields the positive solution \(x = 3/2\).

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring: \((x + 2)(x - 3) = 14\). What is the positive solution?
qs.s: Expand the left side to get \(x^2 - x - 6 = 14\), then subtract 14 to obtain \(x^2 - x - 20 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 5)(x + 4) = 0\), so the positive solution is \(x = 5\).

qs.q: Solve the equation by factoring: \(4x^2 = 81\). What is the positive solution?
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(4x^2 - 81 = 0\) and factor as the difference of squares \((2x - 9)(2x + 9) = 0\). Setting \(2x - 9 = 0\) gives the positive solution \(x = 9/2\).

qs.q: Solve the equation \(7p^2 = p\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Rearrange to \(7p^2 - p = 0\) and factor out \(p\) to get \(p(7p - 1) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero yields \(p = 0\) or \(p = \frac{1}{7}\), so the greater solution is \frac{1}{7}.

qs.q: Solve the equation \(4w^2 = 3w\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Subtract \(3w\) from both sides to get \(4w^2 - 3w = 0\), which factors as \(w(4w - 3) = 0\). The solutions are \(w = 0\) and \(w = \frac{3}{4}\), making \frac{3}{4} the greater solution.

qs.q: Solve the equation \(3x^2 = x\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Rearrange the equation to \(3x^2 - x = 0\) and factor out \(x\) to get \(x(3x - 1) = 0\). By the zero factor property, the solutions are \(x = 0\) and \(x = \frac{1}{3}\), so the greater solution is \frac{1}{3}.

qs.q: Solve the equation \(5t^2 = 2t\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Subtract \(2t\) from both sides to obtain \(5t^2 - 2t = 0\), then factor as \(t(5t - 2) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(t = 0\) or \(t = \frac{2}{5}\), so the greater solution is \frac{2}{5}.

qs.q: Solve the equation \(6m^2 = m\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(6m^2 - m = 0\) and factor to obtain \(m(6m - 1) = 0\). The roots are \(m = 0\) and \(m = \frac{1}{6}\), so the greater solution is \frac{1}{6}.

qs.q: Solve the equation \((2m + 1)(m - 4) = -7\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Expand the product to get \(2m^2 - 7m - 4 = -7\), then add \(7\) to both sides to form \(2m^2 - 7m + 3 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2m - 1)(m - 3) = 0\), which yields \(m = \frac{1}{2}\) or \(m = 3\), so the greater solution is 3.

qs.q: Solve the equation \((2k - 1)^2 = k + 7\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Expand the square on the left to get \(4k^2 - 4k + 1 = k + 7\), then collect all terms on one side to get \(4k^2 - 5k - 6 = 0\). Factoring gives \((4k + 3)(k - 2) = 0\), which yields \(k = -\frac{3}{4}\) or \(k = 2\), so the greater solution is 2.

qs.q: Solve the equation \(2w(3w - 2) = 3w + 20\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Expand and rearrange the equation to standard form \(6w^2 - 7w - 20 = 0\), then factor as \((3w + 4)(2w - 5) = 0\). The roots are \(w = -\frac{4}{3}\) and \(w = \frac{5}{2}\), so the greater solution is \frac{5}{2}.

qs.q: Solve the equation \(2x^2 + 5x = 12\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Write the equation in standard form as \(2x^2 + 5x - 12 = 0\) and factor it as \((2x - 3)(x + 4) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) or \(x = -4\), so the greater solution is \frac{3}{2}.

qs.q: Solve the equation \(y(2y - 5) = 12\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Expand the left side to get \(2y^2 - 5y = 12\), then subtract \(12\) to obtain \(2y^2 - 5y - 12 = 0\). Factoring yields \((2y + 3)(y - 4) = 0\), giving solutions \(y = -\frac{3}{2}\) and \(y = 4\), so the greater solution is 4.

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution of the equation \(2x^2 - 5x = 0\).
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(x\) to get \(x(2x - 5) = 0\). Setting the factor \(2x - 5 = 0\) gives \(x = \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution of the equation \(7x^2 - 2x = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) gives \(x(7x - 2) = 0\). Solving \(7x - 2 = 0\) gives the non-zero root \(x = \frac{2}{7}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution of the equation \(3x^2 + 8x = 0\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in factored form as \(x(3x + 8) = 0\). Setting \(3x + 8 = 0\) gives \(x = -\frac{8}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution of the equation \(5x^2 - 4x = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring gives \(x(5x - 4) = 0\). Setting the non-zero factor \(5x - 4 = 0\) yields \(x = \frac{4}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero solution of the equation \(4x^2 + 3x = 0\).
qs.s: Factor the expression as \(x(4x + 3) = 0\). By the zero factor property, \(4x + 3 = 0\) yields the non-zero solution \(x = -\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution of the equation \((2x - 1)^2 = x + 7\).
qs.s: Expand the left side to obtain \(4x^2 - 4x + 1 = x + 7\), then simplify to \(4x^2 - 5x - 6 = 0\). Factoring gives \((4x + 3)(x - 2) = 0\), which yields \(x = -\frac{3}{4}\) or \(x = 2\), so the positive solution is \(2\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution of the equation \((x - 2)(x + 3) = 14\).
qs.s: Expand and subtract \(14\) to write the equation in standard form as \(x^2 + x - 20 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x + 5) = 0\), which yields \(x = 4\) or \(x = -5\), so the positive solution is \(4\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution of the equation \(3x(x - 1) = 2x + 8\).
qs.s: Expand to get \(3x^2 - 3x = 2x + 8\), then rearrange to \(3x^2 - 5x - 8 = 0\). Factoring yields \((3x - 8)(x + 1) = 0\), giving the positive solution \(x = \frac{8}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the greatest solution of the equation \(x^3 - 3x^2 - 10x = 0\).
qs.s: Factor out \(x\) to get \(x(x^2 - 3x - 10) = 0\), then factor the quadratic to obtain \(x(x - 5)(x + 2) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = 0\), \(x = 5\), and \(x = -2\), of which \(5\) is the greatest.

qs.q: Find the positive solution of the equation \(2x^2 + 5x = 12\).
qs.s: Subtract \(12\) to obtain \(2x^2 + 5x - 12 = 0\), which factors as \((2x - 3)(x + 4) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) or \(x = -4\), so the positive solution is \(\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the non-zero solution to the equation \(\frac{4}{3}x^2 = 8x\)?
qs.s: Subtract \(8x\) to obtain \(\frac{4}{3}x^2 - 8x = 0\) and factor out \(x\) to get \(x(\frac{4}{3}x - 8) = 0\). Setting the factor \(\frac{4}{3}x - 8 = 0\) gives \(x = 8 \cdot \frac{3}{4} = 6\).

qs.q: What is the non-zero solution to the equation \(\frac{5}{6}x^2 = 15x\)?
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(\frac{5}{6}x^2 - 15x = 0\) and factor out \(x\) to obtain \(x(\frac{5}{6}x - 15) = 0\). Setting the non-zero factor to zero gives \(x = 15 \cdot \frac{6}{5} = 18\).

qs.q: What is the non-zero solution to the equation \(\frac{2}{5}x^2 = 8x\)?
qs.s: Subtract \(8x\) from both sides to get \(\frac{2}{5}x^2 - 8x = 0\), then factor as \(x(\frac{2}{5}x - 8) = 0\). Setting \(\frac{2}{5}x - 8 = 0\) gives \(x = 8 \cdot \frac{5}{2} = 20\).

qs.q: What is the non-zero solution to the equation \(\frac{3}{4}x^2 = 9x\)?
qs.s: Rearrange the equation to \(\frac{3}{4}x^2 - 9x = 0\) and factor to obtain \(x(\frac{3}{4}x - 9) = 0\). Setting \(\frac{3}{4}x - 9 = 0\) yields \(x = 9 \cdot \frac{4}{3} = 12\).

qs.q: What is the non-zero solution to the equation \(\frac{3}{5}x^2 = 6x\)?
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(\frac{3}{5}x^2 - 6x = 0\) and factor out \(x\) to get \(x(\frac{3}{5}x - 6) = 0\). Setting the non-zero factor to zero gives \(\frac{3}{5}x = 6\), which simplifies to \(x = 6 \cdot \frac{5}{3} = 10\).

qs.q: What is the positive solution to the equation \(\frac{2}{3}x^2 - \frac{5}{3}x = 4\)?
qs.s: Multiply the entire equation by \(3\) to clear denominators, giving \(2x^2 - 5x - 12 = 0\). Factoring yields \((2x + 3)(x - 4) = 0\), which gives roots \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = 4\), so the positive solution is \(4\).

qs.q: What is the greatest solution to the equation \(\frac{3}{4}x^3 = 12x\)?
qs.s: Rearrange as \(\frac{3}{4}x^3 - 12x = 0\) and factor out \(\frac{3}{4}x\) to obtain \(\frac{3}{4}x(x^2 - 16) = 0\), which factors further into \(\frac{3}{4}x(x - 4)(x + 4) = 0\). The roots are \(-4\), \(0\), and \(4\), so the greatest solution is \(4\).

qs.q: What is the negative solution to the equation \(\frac{1}{2}x^2 + \frac{1}{6}x = \frac{5}{3}\)?
qs.s: Multiply through by the LCD of \(6\) to get \(3x^2 + x - 10 = 0\), which factors as \((3x - 5)(x + 2) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = \frac{5}{3}\) and \(x = -2\), so the negative solution is \(-2\).

qs.q: What is the greater solution to the equation \(\frac{1}{2}x(2x - 3) = 8x - 12\)?
qs.s: Multiply both sides by \(2\) to obtain \(x(2x - 3) = 16x - 24\), which expands and rearranges to \(2x^2 - 19x + 24 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x - 3)(x - 8) = 0\), producing solutions \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = 8\), the greater of which is \(8\).

qs.q: What is the positive solution to the equation \(\frac{5}{3}x^2 + \frac{11}{6}x = 1\)?
qs.s: Multiply by \(6\) to clear denominators, resulting in \(10x^2 + 11x - 6 = 0\). Factoring produces \((5x - 2)(2x + 3) = 0\), giving solutions \(x = \frac{2}{5}\) and \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\), so the positive solution is \(\frac{2}{5}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(\frac{x^2(2x - 5)}{x} = 0\).
qs.s: The numerator equals zero when \(x = 0\) or \(2x - 5 = 0\), giving \(x = \frac{5}{2}\). The restriction \(x \neq 0\) eliminates \(x = 0\), so \(x = \frac{5}{2}\) is the unique solution.

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(\frac{(x - 3)^2(x + 5)}{x - 3} = 0\).
qs.s: Setting the numerator to zero gives \(x = 3\) or \(x = -5\). Since the denominator cannot be zero (\(x \neq 3\)), \(x = 3\) is extraneous, leaving \(x = -5\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(\frac{3x^2(x - 6)}{x} = 0\).
qs.s: The numerator factors give potential roots \(x = 0\) and \(x = 6\). The denominator requires \(x \neq 0\), so \(x = 0\) is an extraneous solution, leaving \(x = 6\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(\frac{x^2(x + 4)}{x} = 0\).
qs.s: Setting the numerator to zero yields \(x = 0\) or \(x = -4\). Since the denominator requires \(x \neq 0\), the root \(x = 0\) is rejected, leaving \(x = -4\) as the only solution.

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(\frac{x^2(x - 7)}{x} = 0\).
qs.s: Setting the numerator equal to zero gives \(x^2(x - 7) = 0\), so \(x = 0\) or \(x = 7\). Because the denominator cannot be zero (\(x \neq 0\)), \(x = 0\) is extraneous, leaving \(x = 7\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(\frac{x^3 - 16x}{x^2 + 4x} = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring the numerator gives \(x(x - 4)(x + 4) = 0\), yielding roots \(x = 0, 4, -4\). The denominator factors as \(x(x + 4) \neq 0\), which excludes \(x = 0\) and \(x = -4\), leaving \(x = 4\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(\frac{x^3 - 4x^2 - x + 4}{x^2 - 5x + 4} = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring by grouping gives \((x^2 - 1)(x - 4) = (x - 1)(x + 1)(x - 4) = 0\), so \(x = 1, -1, 4\). The denominator factors as \((x - 1)(x - 4) \neq 0\), rejecting \(x = 1\) and \(x = 4\), which leaves \(x = -1\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(\frac{4x^3 - x}{2x^2 - x} = 0\).
qs.s: The numerator factors as \(x(2x - 1)(2x + 1) = 0\), giving \(x = 0, \frac{1}{2}, -\frac{1}{2}\). The denominator factors as \(x(2x - 1) \neq 0\), which rejects \(x = 0\) and \(x = \frac{1}{2}\), leaving \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(\frac{x^3 - 3x^2 - 10x}{x^2 - 5x} = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring the numerator yields \(x(x - 5)(x + 2) = 0\), giving \(x = 0, 5, -2\). Because the denominator is \(x(x - 5) \neq 0\), both \(x = 0\) and \(x = 5\) are extraneous, leaving \(x = -2\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(\frac{2x^3 - x^2 - 18x + 9}{2x^2 + 5x - 3} = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring the numerator by grouping yields \((x - 3)(x + 3)(2x - 1) = 0\), giving \(x = 3, -3, \frac{1}{2}\). The denominator factors as \((2x - 1)(x + 3) \neq 0\), eliminating \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = -3\), so the only solution is \(x = 3\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \(x^2 = 10\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(x^2 - 10 = 0\), which factors as \((x - \sqrt{10})(x + \sqrt{10}) = 0\). By the zero factor property, the positive solution is \(x = \sqrt{10}\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \(x^2 = 7\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(x^2 - 7 = 0\), which factors as \((x - \sqrt{7})(x + \sqrt{7}) = 0\). By the zero factor property, the positive solution is \(x = \sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Find the negative solution to the equation \(x^2 = 11\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(x^2 - 11 = 0\), which factors as \((x - \sqrt{11})(x + \sqrt{11}) = 0\). By the zero factor property, the negative solution is \(x = -\sqrt{11}\).

qs.q: Find the negative solution to the equation \(x^2 = 2\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(x^2 - 2 = 0\), which factors as \((x - \sqrt{2})(x + \sqrt{2}) = 0\). By the zero factor property, the negative solution is \(x = -\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \(x^2 = 5\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(x^2 - 5 = 0\), which factors as \((x - \sqrt{5})(x + \sqrt{5}) = 0\). By the zero factor property, the positive solution is \(x = \sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \(2x^2 - 5 = 19\).
qs.s: Subtract 19 to get \(2x^2 - 24 = 0\), then factor as \(2(x^2 - 12) = 2(x - \sqrt{12})(x + \sqrt{12}) = 0\). By the zero factor property, the positive solution is \(x = \sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Find the negative solution to the equation \(3(x^2 - 2) = x^2 + 10\).
qs.s: Expand and collect all terms on one side to get \(2x^2 - 16 = 0\), which factors as \(2(x - \sqrt{8})(x + \sqrt{8}) = 0\). By the zero factor property, the negative solution is \(x = -\sqrt{8} = -2\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \(5x^2 - 14 = x^2 + 58\).
qs.s: Subtract \(x^2 + 58\) from both sides to get \(4x^2 - 72 = 0\), which factors as \(4(x - \sqrt{18})(x + \sqrt{18}) = 0\). Setting the first factor to zero gives the positive solution \(x = \sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Find the negative solution to the equation \(\frac{3}{4}x^2 - 2 = 13\).
qs.s: Subtract 13 to obtain \(\frac{3}{4}x^2 - 15 = 0\), which factors as \(\frac{3}{4}(x^2 - 20) = \frac{3}{4}(x - \sqrt{20})(x + \sqrt{20}) = 0\). Setting the second factor to zero gives the negative solution \(x = -\sqrt{20} = -2\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \(4x^2 - 5 = 10\).
qs.s: Subtract 10 to obtain \(4x^2 - 15 = 0\), which factors as \((2x - \sqrt{15})(2x + \sqrt{15}) = 0\). Setting the first factor to zero gives the positive solution \(x = \frac{\sqrt{15}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its negative solution: \(x^2 - 2x - 15 = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring gives \((x - 5)(x + 3) = 0\), which yields solutions \(x = 5\) and \(x = -3\). The negative solution is \(-3\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its smaller solution: \(x^2 + 8x + 15 = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring gives \((x + 3)(x + 5) = 0\), which yields \(x = -3\) and \(x = -5\). The smaller solution is \(-5\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its positive solution: \(x^2 + 4x - 12 = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring gives \((x + 6)(x - 2) = 0\), yielding solutions \(x = -6\) and \(x = 2\). The positive solution is \(2\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its smaller solution: \(x^2 - 9x + 20 = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x - 5) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = 4\) and \(x = 5\). The smaller solution is \(4\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its greater solution: \(x^2 + 7x + 12 = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring gives \((x + 3)(x + 4) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = -3\) and \(x = -4\). The greater solution is \(-3\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(\frac{x}{x - 4} - \frac{1}{x + 2} = \frac{24}{x^2 - 2x - 8}\).
qs.s: Multiplying by the LCD \((x - 4)(x + 2)\) for \(x \neq 4, -2\) yields \(x(x + 2) - (x - 4) = 24\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + x - 20 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 5)(x - 4) = 0\), and rejecting the extraneous solution \(x = 4\) leaves the single solution \(x = -5\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its positive solution: \(2x^2 + 5x = 12\).
qs.s: Rewriting in standard form gives \(2x^2 + 5x - 12 = 0\), which factors as \((2x - 3)(x + 4) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) or \(x = -4\), so the positive solution is \frac{3}{2}.

qs.q: Solve the equation for its positive solution: \((x - 1)(x + 4) = 14\).
qs.s: Expanding the left side yields \(x^2 + 3x - 4 = 14\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 3x - 18 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 6)(x - 3) = 0\), so the positive solution is \(3\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its greatest solution: \(x^3 - 4x^2 - 12x = 0\).
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(x\) to get \(x(x^2 - 4x - 12) = 0\), which factors further into \(x(x - 6)(x + 2) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = 0\), \(x = 6\), and \(x = -2\), so the greatest solution is \(6\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its smaller solution: \(3x^2 - 11x = 4\).
qs.s: Subtract \(4\) to get standard form \(3x^2 - 11x - 4 = 0\), which factors into \((3x + 1)(x - 4) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = -\frac{1}{3}\) and \(x = 4\), so the smaller solution is -\frac{1}{3}.

qs.q: Find the smaller solution to the equation \(x^2 - 8x + 15 = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring gives \((x - 3)(x - 5) = 0\), which produces solutions \(x = 3\) and \(x = 5\). The smaller solution is \(3\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \(x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x + 2) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = 4\) and \(x = -2\). Thus, the positive solution is \(4\).

qs.q: Find the smaller solution to the equation \(x^2 + 7x + 10 = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring the quadratic gives \((x + 5)(x + 2) = 0\), which yields solutions \(x = -5\) and \(x = -2\). The smaller solution is \(-5\).

qs.q: Find the greater solution to the equation \(x^2 - 8x + 12 = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring the quadratic gives \((x - 6)(x - 2) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = 6\) and \(x = 2\). The greater solution is \(6\).

qs.q: Find the negative solution to the equation \(x^2 + 4x - 21 = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring gives \((x + 7)(x - 3) = 0\), yielding solutions \(x = -7\) and \(x = 3\). The negative solution is \(-7\).

qs.q: Find the greater solution to the equation \(2x(x - 1) = 3x + 12\).
qs.s: Expanding and moving all terms to one side yields \(2x^2 - 5x - 12 = 0\), which factors into \((2x + 3)(x - 4) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = 4\), so the greater solution is \(4\).

qs.q: Find the greatest solution to the equation \(x^3 - 2x^2 - 15x = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring out the greatest common factor gives \(x(x^2 - 2x - 15) = 0\), which factors further into \(x(x - 5)(x + 3) = 0\). The roots are \(x = 0\), \(x = 5\), and \(x = -3\), making \(5\) the greatest solution.

qs.q: Solve the equation for \(x\): \(\frac{x}{x - 3} + \frac{1}{x + 1} = \frac{12}{x^2 - 2x - 3}\).
qs.s: Multiplying both sides by \((x - 3)(x + 1)\) simplifies to \(x^2 + 2x - 15 = 0\), or \((x + 5)(x - 3) = 0\). The value \(x = 3\) is extraneous because it causes division by zero, leaving \(x = -5\) as the only valid solution.

qs.q: Find the smaller solution to the equation \(6x^2 - 13x = 5\).
qs.s: In standard form, the equation is \(6x^2 - 13x - 5 = 0\), which factors into \((3x + 1)(2x - 5) = 0\). Solving gives \(x = -\frac{1}{3}\) and \(x = \frac{5}{2}\), so the smaller solution is \(-\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its positive solution: \(w^2 - w - 30 = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring the equation gives \((w - 6)(w + 5) = 0\), which yields \(w = 6\) or \(w = -5\). Therefore, the positive solution is \(6\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its negative solution: \(y^2 - 2y - 15 = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring the equation gives \((y - 5)(y + 3) = 0\), which yields \(y = 5\) or \(y = -3\). Therefore, the negative solution is \(-3\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its positive solution: \(x^2 + x - 20 = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring the equation gives \((x + 5)(x - 4) = 0\), which yields \(x = -5\) or \(x = 4\). Therefore, the positive solution is \(4\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its greater solution: \(m^2 - 3m - 28 = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring the equation gives \((m - 7)(m + 4) = 0\), which yields \(m = 7\) or \(m = -4\). The greater solution is \(7\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its smaller solution: \(k^2 + 4k - 21 = 0\).
qs.s: Factoring the equation gives \((k + 7)(k - 3) = 0\), which yields \(k = -7\) or \(k = 3\). The smaller solution is \(-7\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its positive solution: \(3x(2x - 1) = 4x + 20\).
qs.s: Expanding and collecting like terms gives \(6x^2 - 7x - 20 = 0\), which factors into \((3x + 4)(2x - 5) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero yields \(x = -\frac{4}{3}\) or \(x = \frac{5}{2}\), so the positive solution is \(\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its negative solution: \(3x^2 - 11x = 20\).
qs.s: Rearranging into standard form gives \(3x^2 - 11x - 20 = 0\), which factors as \((3x + 4)(x - 5) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero yields \(x = -\frac{4}{3}\) or \(x = 5\), so the negative solution is \(-\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation: \(\frac{x}{x-2} + \frac{3}{x+5} = \frac{14}{x^2+3x-10}\).
qs.s: Multiplying by the LCD \((x-2)(x+5)\) gives \(x(x+5) + 3(x-2) = 14\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 8x - 20 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x+10)(x-2) = 0\), but \(x = 2\) is extraneous since it makes a denominator zero, leaving \(-10\) as the solution.

qs.q: Solve the equation for its greater solution: \((2x + 1)(x + 1) = 13 - 2x\).
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging into standard form gives \(2x^2 + 5x - 12 = 0\), which factors as \((2x - 3)(x + 4) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero yields \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) or \(x = -4\), so the greater solution is \frac{3}{2}.

qs.q:
Solve the equation. What is the smaller solution?
\(m^2 - 7m = -12\)
qs.s: Rearrange the equation to \(m^2 - 7m + 12 = 0\), which factors into \((m - 3)(m - 4) = 0\). Solving for \(m\) gives \(m = 3\) or \(m = 4\), so the smaller solution is \(3\).

qs.q:
Solve the equation. What is the greater solution?
\(n^2 + 10n = -21\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(n^2 + 10n + 21 = 0\), which factors into \((n + 3)(n + 7) = 0\). Solving gives \(n = -3\) or \(n = -7\), so the greater solution is \(-3\).

qs.q:
Solve the equation. What is the smaller solution?
\(p^2 + 5p = 14\)
qs.s: Write the equation in standard form as \(p^2 + 5p - 14 = 0\) and factor to get \((p + 7)(p - 2) = 0\). The solutions are \(p = -7\) and \(p = 2\), so the smaller solution is \(-7\).

qs.q:
Solve the equation. What is the greater solution?
\(x^2 + 6x = -8\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in standard form as \(x^2 + 6x + 8 = 0\), which factors as \((x + 2)(x + 4) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero yields \(x = -2\) or \(x = -4\), so the greater solution is \(-2\).

qs.q:
Solve the equation. What is the positive solution?
\(k^2 - 2k = 15\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(k^2 - 2k - 15 = 0\), then factor as \((k - 5)(k + 3) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(k = 5\) or \(k = -3\), so the positive solution is \(5\).

qs.q:
Solve the equation. What is the smaller solution?
\((x - 1)(x + 4) = 14\)
qs.s: Expand the left side to get \(x^2 + 3x - 4 = 14\), then subtract \(14\) to obtain \(x^2 + 3x - 18 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x + 6)(x - 3) = 0\), giving solutions \(x = -6\) and \(x = 3\), so the smaller solution is \(-6\).

qs.q:
Solve the equation. What is the greater solution?
\(3x(x - 4) = x + 10\)
qs.s: Expand the left side to obtain \(3x^2 - 12x = x + 10\), and rearrange to standard form \(3x^2 - 13x - 10 = 0\). Factoring gives \((3x + 2)(x - 5) = 0\), yielding solutions \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\) and \(x = 5\), so the greater solution is \(5\).

qs.q:
Solve the equation. What is the greater solution?
\(6x^2 - 7x = 3\)
qs.s: Write the equation in standard form as \(6x^2 - 7x - 3 = 0\), then factor by grouping to get \((3x + 1)(2x - 3) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = -\frac{1}{3}\) and \(x = \frac{3}{2}\), so the greater solution is \(\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the equation. What is the smaller solution?
\(2x^2 - x = 15\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in standard form as \(2x^2 - x - 15 = 0\), then factor as \((2x + 5)(x - 3) = 0\). Setting each factor equal to zero gives \(x = -\frac{5}{2}\) or \(x = 3\), so the smaller solution is \(-\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the equation for \(x\):
\(\frac{x}{x - 4} - \frac{1}{x + 2} = \frac{24}{x^2 - 2x - 8}\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by \((x - 4)(x + 2)\) for \(x \neq 4, -2\) to get \(x(x + 2) - (x - 4) = 24\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + x - 20 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 5)(x - 4) = 0\), and rejecting the extraneous root \(x = 4\) leaves the single solution \(x = -5\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its greater solution: \(m(m - 8) = -15\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in standard form as \(m^2 - 8m + 15 = 0\), which factors as \((m - 3)(m - 5) = 0\). The solutions are \(m = 3\) and \(m = 5\), so the greater solution is \(5\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its smaller solution: \(p(p + 6) = -8\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in standard form as \(p^2 + 6p + 8 = 0\), which factors as \((p + 2)(p + 4) = 0\). The solutions are \(p = -4\) and \(p = -2\), so the smaller solution is \(-4\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its greater solution: \(y(y + 5) = -6\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in standard form as \(y^2 + 5y + 6 = 0\), which factors as \((y + 2)(y + 3) = 0\). The solutions are \(y = -3\) and \(y = -2\), so the greater solution is \(-2\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its smaller solution: \(w(w - 6) = -8\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in standard form as \(w^2 - 6w + 8 = 0\), which factors as \((w - 2)(w - 4) = 0\). The solutions are \(w = 2\) and \(w = 4\), so the smaller solution is \(2\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its greater solution: \(x(x - 7) = -10\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in standard form as \(x^2 - 7x + 10 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 2)(x - 5) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = 2\) and \(x = 5\), so the greater solution is \(5\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its greater solution: \((3w + 1)(w + 3) = 11\)
qs.s: Expand the left side to get \(3w^2 + 10w + 3 = 11\), then subtract \(11\) to obtain \(3w^2 + 10w - 8 = 0\). Factoring gives \((3w - 2)(w + 4) = 0\), so the solutions are \(w = \frac{2}{3}\) and \(w = -4\), making the greater solution \(\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its greater solution: \(x(2x + 5) = 12\)
qs.s: Expand and set the equation to zero to obtain \(2x^2 + 5x - 12 = 0\), which factors as \((2x - 3)(x + 4) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = -4\), so the greater solution is \(\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its smaller solution: \(n(n - 5) = 84\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(n^2 - 5n - 84 = 0\), which factors as \((n - 12)(n + 7) = 0\). The solutions are \(n = 12\) and \(n = -7\), so the smaller solution is \(-7\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its smaller solution: \((y - 2)(y + 5) = 18\)
qs.s: Expand the left side to get \(y^2 + 3y - 10 = 18\), then subtract \(18\) to get \(y^2 + 3y - 28 = 0\). Factoring gives \((y + 7)(y - 4) = 0\), giving solutions \(y = -7\) and \(y = 4\), so the smaller solution is \(-7\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for its greater solution: \(2m(m - 3) = m + 15\)
qs.s: Expand to get \(2m^2 - 6m = m + 15\) and collect all terms on one side to get \(2m^2 - 7m - 15 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2m + 3)(m - 5) = 0\), so the solutions are \(m = -\frac{3}{2}\) and \(m = 5\), making the greater solution \(5\).

qs.q: Find the smaller solution to the equation \(w(4w - 19) = -12\).
qs.s: Rearranging the equation yields \(4w^2 - 19w + 12 = 0\), which factors as \((4w - 3)(w - 4) = 0\). The solutions are \(w = \frac{3}{4}\) and \(w = 4\), so the smaller solution is \(\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \(m(5m + 13) = 6\).
qs.s: Rewriting in standard form gives \(5m^2 + 13m - 6 = 0\), which factors as \((5m - 2)(m + 3) = 0\). The solutions are \(m = \frac{2}{5}\) and \(m = -3\), so the positive solution is \(\frac{2}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the smaller solution to the equation \(y(3y + 1) = 14\).
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging gives \(3y^2 + y - 14 = 0\), which factors into \((3y + 7)(y - 2) = 0\). Thus, \(y = -\frac{7}{3}\) or \(y = 2\), so the smaller solution is \(-\frac{7}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the greater solution to the equation \(k(3k - 11) = -6\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(3k^2 - 11k + 6 = 0\), which factors into \((3k - 2)(k - 3) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(k = \frac{2}{3}\) or \(k = 3\), so the greater solution is \(3\).

qs.q: Find the greater solution to the equation \(x(2x - 5) = 12\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(2x^2 - 5x - 12 = 0\), which factors as \((2x + 3)(x - 4) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero yields \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\) or \(x = 4\), so the greater solution is \(4\).

qs.q: Find the greater solution to the equation \(y(8y + 2) = 15\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(8y^2 + 2y - 15 = 0\), which factors as \((4y - 5)(2y + 3) = 0\). Solving gives \(y = \frac{5}{4}\) or \(y = -\frac{3}{2}\), so the greater solution is \(\frac{5}{4}\).

qs.q: Solve the equation for \(x\): \(\frac{x}{x - 3} - \frac{1}{x + 2} = \frac{15}{x^2 - x - 6}\).
qs.s: Multiplying by \((x - 3)(x + 2)\) gives \(x(x + 2) - (x - 3) = 15\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + x - 12 = 0\), or \((x + 4)(x - 3) = 0\). Rejecting the extraneous solution \(x = 3\) leaves \(x = -4\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \(2x(2x - 3) = (x - 2)^2 + 4\).
qs.s: Expanding both sides yields \(4x^2 - 6x = x^2 - 4x + 8\), which simplifies to \(3x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0\). Factoring gives \((3x + 4)(x - 2) = 0\), so \(x = -\frac{4}{3}\) or \(x = 2\), making \(2\) the positive solution.

qs.q: Solve the equation for \(x\): \(\frac{2x}{x - 1} - \frac{3}{x + 4} = \frac{10}{x^2 + 3x - 4}\).
qs.s: Multiplying by \((x - 1)(x + 4)\) gives \(2x(x + 4) - 3(x - 1) = 10\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 + 5x - 7 = 0\), or \((2x + 7)(x - 1) = 0\). Rejecting the extraneous solution \(x = 1\) gives \(x = -\frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the smaller solution to the equation \((3x + 1)(x - 2) = (x - 3)(x + 1) + 10\).
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(3x^2 - 5x - 2 = x^2 - 2x + 7\), which rearranges to \(2x^2 - 3x - 9 = 0\). Factoring yields \((2x + 3)(x - 3) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = 3\), with smaller solution \(-\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the smaller solution to the equation \((x + 7)(x - 2) = 10\)?
qs.s: Expanding the equation gives \(x^2 + 5x - 14 = 10\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 5x - 24 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 8)(x - 3) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = -8\) and \(x = 3\), with the smaller solution being \(-8\).

qs.q: Find the greater solution to the equation \((x + 13)(x - 2) = -44\).
qs.s: Expanding the left side yields \(x^2 + 11x - 26 = -44\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 11x + 18 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 2)(x + 9) = 0\), giving solutions \(x = -2\) and \(x = -9\), so the greater solution is \(-2\).

qs.q: What is the smaller solution to the equation \((x - 15)(x + 3) = -65\)?
qs.s: Expanding the left side gives \(x^2 - 12x - 45 = -65\), which rearranges to \(x^2 - 12x + 20 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 2)(x - 10) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = 2\) and \(x = 10\), and the smaller solution is \(2\).

qs.q: Find the greater solution to the equation \((x - 8)(x + 2) = -21\).
qs.s: Expanding the left side gives \(x^2 - 6x - 16 = -21\), which rearranges to \(x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x - 1)(x - 5) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = 1\) and \(x = 5\), with the greater solution being \(5\).

qs.q: Find the positive solution to the equation \((x - 5)(x + 2) = 18\).
qs.s: Expanding the left side yields \(x^2 - 3x - 10 = 18\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 3x - 28 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 7)(x + 4) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = 7\) and \(x = -4\), with the positive solution being \(7\).

qs.q: Find the greater solution to the equation \((3x - 2)(2x + 3) = -2\).
qs.s: Expanding the left side yields \(6x^2 + 5x - 6 = -2\), which rearranges to \(6x^2 + 5x - 4 = 0\). Factoring produces \((2x - 1)(3x + 4) = 0\), giving solutions \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = -\frac{4}{3}\), so the greater solution is \(\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the smaller solution to the equation \((x - 2)(x + 1) = 3x + 19\)?
qs.s: Expanding the left side gives \(x^2 - x - 2 = 3x + 19\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 4x - 21 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 7)(x + 3) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = 7\) and \(x = -3\), with the smaller solution being \(-3\).

qs.q: Find the greater solution to the equation \((x - 20)(x + 3) = 140\).
qs.s: Expanding the equation yields \(x^2 - 17x - 60 = 140\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 17x - 200 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x - 25)(x + 8) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = 25\) and \(x = -8\), and the greater solution is \(25\).

qs.q: What is the greater solution to the equation \((3x + 1)(x + 2) = x^2 + 17\)?
qs.s: Expanding the left side gives \(3x^2 + 7x + 2 = x^2 + 17\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 + 7x - 15 = 0\). Factoring yields \((2x - 3)(x + 5) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = -5\), and the greater solution is \(\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the smaller solution to the equation \((2x + 5)(x - 2) = -7\)?
qs.s: Expanding the equation gives \(2x^2 + x - 10 = -7\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 + x - 3 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x + 3)(x - 1) = 0\), yielding roots \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = 1\), so the smaller solution is \(-\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the positive solution to the equation \((x + 4)(x + 1) = 3x + 19\)?
qs.s: Expanding and moving all terms to one side yields \(x^2 + 2x - 15 = 0\), which factors as \((x + 5)(x - 3) = 0\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = -5\) or \(x = 3\), so the positive solution is \(3\).

qs.q: What is the greater solution to the equation \((x + 3)(x - 5) = 2x + 6\)?
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(x^2 - 2x - 15 = 2x + 6\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 4x - 21 = 0\). Factoring as \((x - 7)(x + 3) = 0\) gives \(x = 7\) or \(x = -3\), so the greater solution is \(7\).

qs.q: What is the smaller solution to the equation \((x - 1)(x + 3) = 4x + 5\)?
qs.s: Expanding gives \(x^2 + 2x - 3 = 4x + 5\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x + 2) = 0\), so \(x = 4\) or \(x = -2\), with \(-2\) being the smaller solution.

qs.q: What is the greater solution to the equation \((x - 4)(x + 2) = 3x - 12\)?
qs.s: Expanding and setting the equation to zero gives \(x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0\), which factors into \((x - 4)(x - 1) = 0\). The roots are \(x = 4\) and \(x = 1\), so the greater solution is \(4\).

qs.q: What is the smaller solution to the equation \((x + 2)(x + 1) = 14 - x\)?
qs.s: Expanding gives \(x^2 + 3x + 2 = 14 - x\), which rearranges to \(x^2 + 4x - 12 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x + 6)(x - 2) = 0\), giving solutions \(x = -6\) and \(x = 2\), so the smaller solution is \(-6\).

qs.q: What is the positive solution to the equation \((2x - 5)^2 = (x - 3)^2 + 21\)?
qs.s: Expanding both squares gives \(4x^2 - 20x + 25 = x^2 - 6x + 30\), which rearranges to \(3x^2 - 14x - 5 = 0\). Factoring gives \((3x + 1)(x - 5) = 0\), yielding solutions \(x = -1/3\) and \(x = 5\), so the positive solution is \(5\).

qs.q: What is the greater solution to the equation \((2x - 1)(2x + 3) = (x + 1)(x + 2) + 5\)?
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(4x^2 + 4x - 3 = x^2 + 3x + 7\), which simplifies to \(3x^2 + x - 10 = 0\). Factoring as \((3x - 5)(x + 2) = 0\) gives solutions \(x = 5/3\) and \(x = -2\), so the greater solution is \(5/3\).

qs.q: What is the smaller solution to the equation \((3x - 1)(x - 2) = x^2 + 6\)?
qs.s: Expanding gives \(3x^2 - 7x + 2 = x^2 + 6\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 - 7x - 4 = 0\). Factoring yields \((2x + 1)(x - 4) = 0\), giving solutions \(x = -1/2\) and \(x = 4\), so the smaller solution is \(-1/2\).

qs.q: Solve the equation \(\frac{x}{x - 3} - \frac{1}{x + 3} = \frac{18}{x^2 - 9}\).
qs.s: Multiplying by the common denominator \((x - 3)(x + 3)\) gives \(x(x + 3) - (x - 3) = 18\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 2x - 15 = 0\) and factors as \((x + 5)(x - 3) = 0\). We reject \(x = 3\) because it makes the denominator zero, leaving \(x = -5\) as the only valid solution.
