qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \(m(m + 1) = 1\)
qs.s: Expand to get \(m^2 + m = 1\), then add \((1/2)^2 = 1/4\) to both sides to obtain \((m + 1/2)^2 = 5/4\). Taking the square root gives \(m + 1/2 = \pm\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\), so \(m = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \(w(w + 7) = -3\)

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \(y(y - 5) = 3\)
qs.s: Expand to get \(y^2 - 5y = 3\), then add \((-5/2)^2 = 25/4\) to both sides to obtain \((y - 5/2)^2 = 37/4\). Taking the square root gives \(y - 5/2 = \pm\frac{\sqrt{37}}{2}\), so \(y = \frac{5 \pm \sqrt{37}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \(x(x + 3) = 1\)
qs.s: Expand to get \(x^2 + 3x = 1\), then add \((3/2)^2 = 9/4\) to both sides to get \((x + 3/2)^2 = 13/4\). Taking the square root yields \(x + 3/2 = \pm\frac{\sqrt{13}}{2}\), so \(x = \frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{13}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \(t(t - 1) = 4\)
qs.s: Expand to get \(t^2 - t = 4\), then add \((-1/2)^2 = 1/4\) to both sides to get \((t - 1/2)^2 = 17/4\). Taking the square root gives \(t - 1/2 = \pm\frac{\sqrt{17}}{2}\), so \(t = \frac{1 \pm \sqrt{17}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \((x - 2)(x + 5) = 2x + 1\)
qs.s: Expand and rearrange \((x - 2)(x + 5) = 2x + 1\) into \(x^2 + x = 11\), then add \((1/2)^2 = 1/4\) to both sides to get \((x + 1/2)^2 = 45/4\). Taking the square root and simplifying \(\sqrt{45} = 3\sqrt{5}\) gives \(x + 1/2 = \pm\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2}\), so \(x = \frac{-1 \pm 3\sqrt{5}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \((3 - x)(x + 5) = 4\)
qs.s: Expand \((3 - x)(x + 5) = 4\) to \(-x^2 - 2x + 15 = 4\), rearrange and divide by \(-1\) to get \(x^2 + 2x = 11\). Adding \(1\) to both sides gives \((x + 1)^2 = 12\), and taking the square root with \(\sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}\) yields \(x = -1 \pm 2\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \(5 - w(w - 7) = 2w + 1\)
qs.s: Expand \(5 - w(w - 7) = 2w + 1\) to \(-w^2 + 5w = -4\), then divide by \(-1\) to get \(w^2 - 5w = 4\). Completing the square gives \((w - 5/2)^2 = 4 + 25/4 = 41/4\), so \(w = \frac{5 \pm \sqrt{41}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \((z - 1)(z + 8) = 2z + 11\)
qs.s: Expand \((z - 1)(z + 8) = 2z + 11\) and collect terms on the left to obtain \(z^2 + 5z = 19\). Completing the square gives \((z + 5/2)^2 = 19 + 25/4 = 101/4\), which results in \(z = \frac{-5 \pm \sqrt{101}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \((x - 3)(x + 4) = 3x + 35\)
qs.s: Expand and collect like terms to write \((x - 3)(x + 4) = 3x + 35\) as \(x^2 - 2x = 47\). Adding \(1\) to both sides yields \((x - 1)^2 = 48\), which gives \(x - 1 = \pm 4\sqrt{3}\) or \(x = 1 \pm 4\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \(x(5 - x) = 2\)
qs.s: Expanding and multiplying by \(-1\) gives \(x^2 - 5x = -2\). Adding \((-\frac{5}{2})^2 = \frac{25}{4}\) to both sides yields \((x - \frac{5}{2})^2 = \frac{17}{4}\), so \(x = \frac{5 \pm \sqrt{17}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \(x(1 - x) = 3\)
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging gives \(x^2 - x = -3\). Completing the square produces \((x - \frac{1}{2})^2 = -\frac{11}{4}\), which has no real solution because the square of a real number cannot be negative.

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \(x(4 - x) = 1\)
qs.s: Expanding and multiplying by \(-1\) gives \(x^2 - 4x = -1\). Adding \((-2)^2 = 4\) to both sides results in \((x - 2)^2 = 3\), so \(x = 2 \pm \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \((x - 3)(x - 1) = 2(x + 1)\)
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(x^2 - 4x + 3 = 2x + 2\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 6x = -1\). Completing the square gives \((x - 3)^2 = 8\), so \(x = 3 \pm \sqrt{8} = 3 \pm 2\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \((x + 2)(x - 5) = 2x - 3\)
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging terms gives \(x^2 - 5x = 7\). Adding \((-\frac{5}{2})^2 = \frac{25}{4}\) to both sides yields \((x - \frac{5}{2})^2 = \frac{53}{4}\), so \(x = \frac{5 \pm \sqrt{53}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \(x(8 - x) = 2x - 1\)
qs.s: Expanding and collecting all variable terms on the left yields \(x^2 - 6x = 1\). Adding \((-3)^2 = 9\) to both sides produces \((x - 3)^2 = 10\), so \(x = 3 \pm \sqrt{10}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \(x(14 - x) = 17\)
qs.s: Expanding and dividing by \(-1\) yields \(x^2 - 14x = -17\). Adding \((-7)^2 = 49\) to both sides gives \((x - 7)^2 = 32\), so \(x = 7 \pm \sqrt{32} = 7 \pm 4\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible. \((1 - x)(x + 5) = 2\)
qs.s: Expanding the left side gives \(-x^2 - 4x + 5 = 2\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 4x = 3\). Adding \(2^2 = 4\) to both sides gives \((x + 2)^2 = 7\), so \(x = -2 \pm \sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \(x(x - 6) = -7\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \(x^2 - 6x = -7\). Adding \((-3)^2 = 9\) to both sides results in \((x - 3)^2 = 2\), yielding \(x = 3 \pm \sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \(x(6 - x) = 2\)
qs.s: Rewriting the equation in standard form gives \(x^2 - 6x = -2\). Adding \(3^2 = 9\) to both sides gives \((x - 3)^2 = 7\), which solves to \(x = 3 \pm \sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \(x(2 - x) = -4\)
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging yields \(x^2 - 2x = 4\). Completing the square by adding \(1\) to both sides gives \((x - 1)^2 = 5\), so \(x = 1 \pm \sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \(x(x + 4) = 2\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \(x^2 + 4x = 2\). Adding \(2^2 = 4\) to both sides produces \((x + 2)^2 = 6\), so \(x = -2 \pm \sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \(x(4 - x) = 1\)
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging gives \(x^2 - 4x = -1\). Completing the square gives \((x - 2)^2 = 3\), so \(x = 2 \pm \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \((x - 2)(x - 8) = 2x + 7\)
qs.s: Expanding yields \(x^2 - 10x + 16 = 2x + 7\), which rearranges to \(x^2 - 12x = -9\). Adding \(36\) to both sides gives \((x - 6)^2 = 27\), so \(x = 6 \pm \sqrt{27} = 6 \pm 3\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \((4 - x)(x + 2) = 2(1 - x)\)
qs.s: Expanding yields \(-x^2 + 2x + 8 = 2 - 2x\), which rearranges to \(x^2 - 4x = 6\). Adding \(4\) to both sides gives \((x - 2)^2 = 10\), so \(x = 2 \pm \sqrt{10}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \((x - 1)(x + 7) = 2x + 1\)
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(x^2 + 6x - 7 = 2x + 1\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 4x = 8\). Completing the square produces \((x + 2)^2 = 12\), so \(x = -2 \pm \sqrt{12} = -2 \pm 2\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \((x - 5)^2 = 2x + 13\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \(x^2 - 10x + 25 = 2x + 13\), which rearranges to \(x^2 - 12x = -12\). Adding \(36\) to both sides gives \((x - 6)^2 = 24\), so \(x = 6 \pm 2\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \(x(10 - x) = 2(x - 2)\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \(10x - x^2 = 2x - 4\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 8x = 4\). Completing the square results in \((x - 4)^2 = 20\), giving \(x = 4 \pm \sqrt{20} = 4 \pm 2\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible.
\((1 - x)(x + 4) = 1\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \(-x^2 - 3x + 4 = 1\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 3x = 3\). Completing the square by adding \(9/4\) gives \((x + 3/2)^2 = 21/4\), leading to \(x = \frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{21}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible.
\((4 - x)(x + 2) = 3\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \(-x^2 + 2x + 8 = 3\), which rearranges to \(x^2 - 2x = 5\). Adding \(1\) to both sides gives \((x - 1)^2 = 6\), so \(x = 1 \pm \sqrt{6}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible.
\((3 - x)(x + 1) = 1\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \(-x^2 + 2x + 3 = 1\), which rearranges to \(x^2 - 2x = 2\). Completing the square yields \((x - 1)^2 = 3\), so \(x = 1 \pm \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible.
\((x - 1)(x + 5) = 2\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \(x^2 + 4x - 5 = 2\), which rearranges to \(x^2 + 4x = 7\). Adding \(4\) to both sides gives \((x + 2)^2 = 11\), so \(x = -2 \pm \sqrt{11}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible.
\((2 - x)(x + 3) = -2\)
qs.s: Expanding yields \(-x^2 - x + 6 = -2\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + x = 8\). Adding \((1/2)^2 = 1/4\) gives \((x + 1/2)^2 = 33/4\), so \(x = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{33}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible.
\((2x - 1)(x + 3) - (x + 2)^2 = 6\)
qs.s: Expanding yields \((2x^2 + 5x - 3) - (x^2 + 4x + 4) = 6\), simplifying to \(x^2 + x = 13\). Adding \(1/4\) gives \((x + 1/2)^2 = 53/4\), so \(x = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{53}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible.
\(\frac{(x + 2)(x - 4)}{2} = 1 - 2x\)
qs.s: Multiplying by \(2\) and expanding gives \(x^2 - 2x - 8 = 2 - 4x\), which rearranges to \(x^2 + 2x = 10\). Adding \(1\) gives \((x + 1)^2 = 11\), so \(x = -1 \pm \sqrt{11}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible.
\((2 - x)(x + 6) = 2x - 33\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \(-x^2 - 4x + 12 = 2x - 33\), which rearranges to \(x^2 + 6x = 45\). Adding \(9\) gives \((x + 3)^2 = 54\), so \(x = -3 \pm \sqrt{54} = -3 \pm 3\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible.
\((x + 1)^2 + (x - 2)^2 = x^2 + 17\)
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms yields \(2x^2 - 2x + 5 = x^2 + 17\), which rearranges to \(x^2 - 2x = 12\). Completing the square gives \((x - 1)^2 = 13\), so \(x = 1 \pm \sqrt{13}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers when possible.
\((x - 4)(x + 2) = 4(x - 3) + 7\)
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(x^2 - 2x - 8 = 4x - 5\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 6x = 3\). Adding \(9\) gives \((x - 3)^2 = 12\), so \(x = 3 \pm \sqrt{12} = 3 \pm 2\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x^2 + 6x - 1 = 0\)
qs.s: Divide all terms by 3 to obtain \(x^2 + 2x = \frac{1}{3}\), then add \(1^2 = 1\) to both sides to form \((x + 1)^2 = \frac{4}{3}\). Taking the square root of both sides gives \(x + 1 = \pm \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} = \pm \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\), so \(x = -1 \pm \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x^2 + 4x - 7 = 0\)
qs.s: Divide by 2 to get \(x^2 + 2x = \frac{7}{2}\), then add \(1^2 = 1\) to both sides to obtain \((x + 1)^2 = \frac{9}{2}\). Taking the square root gives \(x + 1 = \pm \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} = \pm \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\), so \(x = -1 \pm \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x^2 + 12x + 2 = 0\)
qs.s: Divide by 3 to get \(x^2 + 4x = -\frac{2}{3}\), then complete the square by adding \(2^2 = 4\) to both sides, yielding \((x + 2)^2 = \frac{10}{3}\). Taking the square root produces \(x + 2 = \pm \frac{\sqrt{30}}{3}\), giving \(x = -2 \pm \frac{\sqrt{30}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x^2 - 4x - 5 = 0\)
qs.s: Divide all terms by 2 to get \(x^2 - 2x = \frac{5}{2}\), then complete the square by adding \((-1)^2 = 1\) to both sides to get \((x - 1)^2 = \frac{7}{2}\). Applying the square root property gives \(x - 1 = \pm \sqrt{\frac{7}{2}} = \pm \frac{\sqrt{14}}{2}\), which simplifies to \(x = 1 \pm \frac{\sqrt{14}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x^2 - 8x + 3 = 0\)
qs.s: Divide by 2 to write the equation as \(x^2 - 4x = -\frac{3}{2}\), then add \((-2)^2 = 4\) to both sides to obtain \((x - 2)^2 = \frac{5}{2}\). Taking the square root gives \(x - 2 = \pm \frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}\), which results in \(x = 2 \pm \frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x(x - 3) = x + 5\)
qs.s: Expand and rearrange to \(3x^2 - 10x = 5\), then divide by 3 to get \(x^2 - \frac{10}{3}x = \frac{5}{3}\). Adding \(\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{9}\) gives \(\left(x - \frac{5}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{40}{9}\), so \(x = \frac{5}{3} \pm \frac{2\sqrt{10}}{3} = \frac{5 \pm 2\sqrt{10}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x(x + 3) = 3\)
qs.s: Expand to \(2x^2 + 6x = 3\) and divide by 2 to obtain \(x^2 + 3x = \frac{3}{2}\). Adding \(\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}\) to both sides yields \(\left(x + \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{15}{4}\), which gives \(x = -\frac{3}{2} \pm \frac{\sqrt{15}}{2} = \frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{15}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(-2x^2 + 6x + 5 = 0\)
qs.s: Divide all terms by \(-2\) to obtain \(x^2 - 3x = \frac{5}{2}\), then complete the square by adding \(\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}\) to both sides to get \(\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{19}{4}\). Applying the square root property yields \(x = \frac{3}{2} \pm \frac{\sqrt{19}}{2} = \frac{3 \pm \sqrt{19}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x(x - 2) = 2x + 1\)
qs.s: Expand to \(3x^2 - 6x = 2x + 1\), rearrange to \(3x^2 - 8x = 1\), and divide by 3 to obtain \(x^2 - \frac{8}{3}x = \frac{1}{3}\). Completing the square by adding \(\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{16}{9}\) yields \(\left(x - \frac{4}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{19}{9}\), so \(x = \frac{4}{3} \pm \frac{\sqrt{19}}{3} = \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{19}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \((2x - 1)(x + 3) = 2\)
qs.s: Expand to \(2x^2 + 5x - 3 = 2\), rearrange to \(2x^2 + 5x = 5\), and divide by 2 to get \(x^2 + \frac{5}{2}x = \frac{5}{2}\). Adding \(\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{16}\) gives \(\left(x + \frac{5}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{65}{16}\), which results in \(x = -\frac{5}{4} \pm \frac{\sqrt{65}}{4} = \frac{-5 \pm \sqrt{65}}{4}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x^2 - 3x = 3\)
qs.s: Divide by \(2\) to obtain \(x^2 - \frac{3}{2}x = \frac{3}{2}\), then add \(\left(-\frac{3}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{16}\) to both sides to get \(\left(x - \frac{3}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{33}{16}\). Taking the square root and isolating \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{3 \pm \sqrt{33}}{4}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x^2 + 3x = 1\)
qs.s: Divide by \(2\) to get \(x^2 + \frac{3}{2}x = \frac{1}{2}\), then add \(\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{16}\) to both sides to obtain \(\left(x + \frac{3}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{17}{16}\). Taking the square root and solving for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{17}}{4}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x^2 - x = 3\)
qs.s: Divide by \(3\) to get \(x^2 - \frac{1}{3}x = 1\), then add \(\left(-\frac{1}{6}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{36}\) to both sides to get \(\left(x - \frac{1}{6}\right)^2 = \frac{37}{36}\). Taking the square root gives \(x = \frac{1 \pm \sqrt{37}}{6}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x^2 + 5x = 2\)
qs.s: Divide each term by \(2\) to obtain \(x^2 + \frac{5}{2}x = 1\), then add \(\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{16}\) to both sides to get \(\left(x + \frac{5}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{41}{16}\). Taking the square root yields \(x = \frac{-5 \pm \sqrt{41}}{4}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x^2 + 2x = 4\)
qs.s: Divide by \(3\) to get \(x^2 + \frac{2}{3}x = \frac{4}{3}\), then add \(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{9}\) to both sides to obtain \(\left(x + \frac{1}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{13}{9}\). Taking the square root gives \(x = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{13}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x(x - 1) = 2x + 1\)
qs.s: Expand and rearrange the equation to get \(3x^2 - 5x = 1\), then divide by \(3\) to obtain \(x^2 - \frac{5}{3}x = \frac{1}{3}\). Completing the square by adding \(\left(-\frac{5}{6}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{36}\) gives \(\left(x - \frac{5}{6}\right)^2 = \frac{37}{36}\), so \(x = \frac{5 \pm \sqrt{37}}{6}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(4x^2 + 1 = 2x(x - 3) + 8\)
qs.s: Expand and collect like terms to get \(2x^2 + 6x = 7\), then divide by \(2\) to obtain \(x^2 + 3x = \frac{7}{2}\). Adding \(\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}\) to both sides gives \(\left(x + \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{23}{4}\), so \(x = \frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{23}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \((x + 2)(5x - 1) = 7\)
qs.s: Expand and rearrange to \(5x^2 + 9x = 9\), then divide by \(5\) to obtain \(x^2 + \frac{9}{5}x = \frac{9}{5}\). Add \(\left(\frac{9}{10}\right)^2 = \frac{81}{100}\) to both sides to get \(\left(x + \frac{9}{10}\right)^2 = \frac{261}{100}\), and taking the square root gives \(x = \frac{-9 \pm 3\sqrt{29}}{10}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x(4 - x) = 2\)
qs.s: Expand and write as \(-3x^2 + 12x = 2\), then divide by \(-3\) to get \(x^2 - 4x = -\frac{2}{3}\). Complete the square by adding \((-2)^2 = 4\) to get \((x - 2)^2 = \frac{10}{3}\), and rationalizing the square root yields \(x = \frac{6 \pm \sqrt{30}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(5 - 2x^2 = 4x\)
qs.s: Rearrange to \(-2x^2 - 4x = -5\) and divide by \(-2\) to get \(x^2 + 2x = \frac{5}{2}\). Add \(1^2 = 1\) to both sides to get \((x + 1)^2 = \frac{7}{2}\), and taking the square root gives \(x + 1 = \pm\frac{\sqrt{14}}{2}\), which simplifies to \(x = \frac{-2 \pm \sqrt{14}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(5x^2 + 7x = 1\)
qs.s: Divide by 5 to obtain \(x^2 + \frac{7}{5}x = \frac{1}{5}\), then add \(\left(\frac{7}{10}\right)^2 = \frac{49}{100}\) to both sides to get \(\left(x + \frac{7}{10}\right)^2 = \frac{69}{100}\). Taking the square root gives \(x + \frac{7}{10} = \pm \frac{\sqrt{69}}{10}\), so \(x = \frac{-7 \pm \sqrt{69}}{10}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x^2 - 5x = 1\)
qs.s: Divide by 3 to get \(x^2 - \frac{5}{3}x = \frac{1}{3}\), then add \(\left(-\frac{5}{6}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{36}\) to both sides to obtain \(\left(x - \frac{5}{6}\right)^2 = \frac{37}{36}\). Taking the square root gives \(x - \frac{5}{6} = \pm \frac{\sqrt{37}}{6}\), so \(x = \frac{5 \pm \sqrt{37}}{6}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(4x^2 - 3x = 2\)
qs.s: Divide by 4 to get \(x^2 - \frac{3}{4}x = \frac{1}{2}\), then add \(\left(-\frac{3}{8}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{64}\) to both sides to obtain \(\left(x - \frac{3}{8}\right)^2 = \frac{41}{64}\). Taking the square root gives \(x - \frac{3}{8} = \pm \frac{\sqrt{41}}{8}\), so \(x = \frac{3 \pm \sqrt{41}}{8}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(6x^2 - 8x = 5\)
qs.s: Dividing by 6 gives \(x^2 - \frac{4}{3}x = \frac{5}{6}\), and adding \(\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{4}{9}\) to both sides gives \(\left(x - \frac{2}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{23}{18}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing gives \(x = \frac{2}{3} \pm \frac{\sqrt{46}}{6} = \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{46}}{6}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(5x^2 - 2x + 3 = 4x + 6\)
qs.s: Rearranging terms gives \(5x^2 - 6x = 3\), and dividing by 5 yields \(x^2 - \frac{6}{5}x = \frac{3}{5}\). Adding \(\left(-\frac{3}{5}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{25}\) to both sides produces \(\left(x - \frac{3}{5}\right)^2 = \frac{24}{25}\), so \(x = \frac{3 \pm \sqrt{24}}{5} = \frac{3 \pm 2\sqrt{6}}{5}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x(x - 2) = 2\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \(3x^2 - 6x = 2\), and dividing by 3 yields \(x^2 - 2x = \frac{2}{3}\). Adding \((-1)^2 = 1\) to both sides gives \((x - 1)^2 = \frac{5}{3}\), which leads to \(x = 1 \pm \sqrt{\frac{5}{3}} = \frac{3 \pm \sqrt{15}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(\displaystyle 3x^2 + 2x = 2\)
qs.s: Divide each term by 3 to get \(x^2 + \frac{2}{3}x = \frac{2}{3}\), then add \((\frac{1}{3})^2 = \frac{1}{9}\) to both sides to get \((x + \frac{1}{3})^2 = \frac{7}{9}\), yielding \(x = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{7}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(\displaystyle 2x^2 - 5x = 1\)
qs.s: Divide by 2 to obtain \(x^2 - \frac{5}{2}x = \frac{1}{2}\), then complete the square by adding \((-\frac{5}{4})^2 = \frac{25}{16}\) to both sides to get \((x - \frac{5}{4})^2 = \frac{33}{16}\), giving \(x = \frac{5 \pm \sqrt{33}}{4}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(\displaystyle 3x^2 - 4x = 1\)
qs.s: Divide by 3 to get \(x^2 - \frac{4}{3}x = \frac{1}{3}\), then add \((-\frac{2}{3})^2 = \frac{4}{9}\) to both sides to get \((x - \frac{2}{3})^2 = \frac{7}{9}\), which simplifies to \(x = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{7}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(\displaystyle 5x^2 + 3x = 1\)
qs.s: Divide by 5 to get \(x^2 + \frac{3}{5}x = \frac{1}{5}\), then add \((\frac{3}{10})^2 = \frac{9}{100}\) to both sides to yield \((x + \frac{3}{10})^2 = \frac{29}{100}\), giving \(x = \frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{29}}{10}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(\displaystyle -4x^2 + 12x + 1 = 0\)
qs.s: Subtract 1 and divide all terms by \(-4\) to get \(x^2 - 3x = \frac{1}{4}\). Add \((-\frac{3}{2})^2 = \frac{9}{4}\) to both sides to get \((x - \frac{3}{2})^2 = \frac{10}{4}\), so \(x = \frac{3 \pm \sqrt{10}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(\displaystyle (2x + 3)^2 = 3x + 14\)
qs.s: Expand to \(4x^2 + 12x + 9 = 3x + 14\), rearrange to \(4x^2 + 9x = 5\), and divide by 4 to get \(x^2 + \frac{9}{4}x = \frac{5}{4}\). Adding \((\frac{9}{8})^2 = \frac{81}{64}\) to both sides gives \((x + \frac{9}{8})^2 = \frac{161}{64}\), yielding \(x = \frac{-9 \pm \sqrt{161}}{8}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(\displaystyle (2x - 1)(x + 2) = 5\)
qs.s: Expand to get \(2x^2 + 3x - 2 = 5\), isolate the variable terms as \(2x^2 + 3x = 7\), and divide by 2 to get \(x^2 + \frac{3}{2}x = \frac{7}{2}\). Adding \((\frac{3}{4})^2 = \frac{9}{16}\) to both sides gives \((x + \frac{3}{4})^2 = \frac{65}{16}\), so \(x = \frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{65}}{4}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(\displaystyle x(3x - 5) = 2x + 1\)
qs.s: Expand and collect like terms to get \(3x^2 - 7x = 1\), then divide by 3 to reach \(x^2 - \frac{7}{3}x = \frac{1}{3}\). Complete the square by adding \((-\frac{7}{6})^2 = \frac{49}{36}\) to both sides to get \((x - \frac{7}{6})^2 = \frac{61}{36}\), resulting in \(x = \frac{7 \pm \sqrt{61}}{6}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(\displaystyle 6x^2 - 4x - 1 = 0\)
qs.s: Add 1 and divide by 6 to obtain \(x^2 - \frac{2}{3}x = \frac{1}{6}\), then add \((-\frac{1}{3})^2 = \frac{1}{9}\) to both sides to get \((x - \frac{1}{3})^2 = \frac{5}{18}\); simplifying \(\sqrt{\frac{5}{18}} = \frac{\sqrt{10}}{6}\) gives \(x = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{10}}{6}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x^2 = -7x - 2\)
qs.s: Divide by \(2\) to write \(x^2 + \frac{7}{2}x = -1\), then add \(\left(\frac{7}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{49}{16}\) to both sides to obtain \(\left(x + \frac{7}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{33}{16}\). Taking the square root of both sides leads to \(x = \frac{-7 \pm \sqrt{33}}{4}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x^2 = 4x + 3\)
qs.s: Rearrange to \(x^2 - \frac{4}{3}x = 1\) and add \(\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{4}{9}\) to both sides to get \(\left(x - \frac{2}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{13}{9}\). Taking the square root gives \(x - \frac{2}{3} = \pm\frac{\sqrt{13}}{3}\), so \(x = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{13}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x^2 = -10x - 4\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equation as \(x^2 + \frac{10}{3}x = -\frac{4}{3}\) and add \(\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{9}\) to both sides to get \(\left(x + \frac{5}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{13}{9}\). Taking the square root gives \(x + \frac{5}{3} = \pm\frac{\sqrt{13}}{3}\), so \(x = \frac{-5 \pm \sqrt{13}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(5x^2 = -4x + 2\)
qs.s: Divide by \(5\) to obtain \(x^2 + \frac{4}{5}x = \frac{2}{5}\), then complete the square by adding \(\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^2 = \frac{4}{25}\) to both sides. This yields \(\left(x + \frac{2}{5}\right)^2 = \frac{14}{25}\), which gives \(x = \frac{-2 \pm \sqrt{14}}{5}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x(3x - 4) = 1\)
qs.s: Expand to \(6x^2 - 8x = 1\) and divide by \(6\) to get \(x^2 - \frac{4}{3}x = \frac{1}{6}\). Adding \(\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{4}{9}\) to both sides gives \(\left(x - \frac{2}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{11}{18}\), so \(x = \frac{2}{3} \pm \frac{\sqrt{22}}{6} = \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{22}}{6}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x(x - 3) = 1 - 2x\)
qs.s: Expand and collect like terms to get \(2x^2 - 4x = 1\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 2x = \frac{1}{2}\). Completing the square gives \((x - 1)^2 = \frac{3}{2}\), and taking the square root yields \(x = 1 \pm \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2} = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{6}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x(x + 1) = 5 - x\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \(3x^2 + 3x = 5 - x\), which rearranges to \(x^2 + \frac{4}{3}x = \frac{5}{3}\). Adding \(\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{4}{9}\) to both sides produces \(\left(x + \frac{2}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{19}{9}\), so \(x = \frac{-2 \pm \sqrt{19}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2 - 3x^2 = 5x - 2\)
qs.s: Rearranging to standard form gives \(3x^2 + 5x = 4\), or \(x^2 + \frac{5}{3}x = \frac{4}{3}\). Adding \(\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{36}\) to both sides yields \(\left(x + \frac{5}{6}\right)^2 = \frac{73}{36}\), which simplifies to \(x = \frac{-5 \pm \sqrt{73}}{6}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(5x^2 = 10x + 2\)
qs.s: Divide each term by \(5\) to obtain \(x^2 - 2x = \frac{2}{5}\), then add \(1\) to both sides to form \((x - 1)^2 = \frac{7}{5}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing yields \(x = 1 \pm \frac{\sqrt{35}}{5}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x^2 = 6x + 5\)
qs.s: Divide by \(3\) to obtain \(x^2 - 2x = \frac{5}{3}\), then add \(1\) to both sides to write \((x - 1)^2 = \frac{8}{3}\). Taking the square root and simplifying \(\sqrt{\frac{8}{3}} = \frac{2\sqrt{6}}{3}\) yields \(x = 1 \pm \frac{2\sqrt{6}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x^2 = 4x + 3\)
qs.s: Divide by \(2\) to obtain \(x^2 - 2x = \frac{3}{2}\), then complete the square by adding \(1\) to both sides to get \((x - 1)^2 = \frac{5}{2}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing the denominator yields \(x = 1 \pm \frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x^2 = 12x + 1\)
qs.s: Divide by \(3\) to get \(x^2 - 4x = \frac{1}{3}\), then add \(4\) to both sides to obtain \((x - 2)^2 = \frac{13}{3}\). Applying the square root property and rationalizing gives \(x = 2 \pm \frac{\sqrt{39}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x^2 = -4x + 5\)
qs.s: Rearrange and divide by \(2\) to get \(x^2 + 2x = \frac{5}{2}\), then add \(1\) to both sides to find \((x + 1)^2 = \frac{7}{2}\). Solving for \(x\) and rationalizing the denominator gives \(x = -1 \pm \frac{\sqrt{14}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \((2x - 1)(x + 2) = 1\)
qs.s: Expand to \(2x^2 + 3x - 2 = 1\) and rearrange to \(2x^2 + 3x = 3\). Dividing by \(2\) gives \(x^2 + \frac{3}{2}x = \frac{3}{2}\), and adding \((\frac{3}{4})^2 = \frac{9}{16}\) gives \((x + \frac{3}{4})^2 = \frac{33}{16}\), giving \(x = \frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{33}}{4}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x(x - 2) = x + 1\)
qs.s: Expand and collect terms as \(3x^2 - 7x = 1\), then divide by \(3\) to get \(x^2 - \frac{7}{3}x = \frac{1}{3}\). Adding \((\frac{7}{6})^2 = \frac{49}{36}\) to both sides yields \((x - \frac{7}{6})^2 = \frac{61}{36}\), which simplifies to \(x = \frac{7 \pm \sqrt{61}}{6}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(4 - 2x^2 = 12x - 1\)
qs.s: Rearrange to \(-2x^2 - 12x = -5\) and divide by \(-2\) to obtain \(x^2 + 6x = \frac{5}{2}\). Adding \(9\) to both sides gives \((x + 3)^2 = \frac{23}{2}\), and taking the square root followed by rationalizing yields \(x = -3 \pm \frac{\sqrt{46}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x(x - 1) = 4x + 5\)
qs.s: Expand to \(2x^2 - 2x = 4x + 5\) and rearrange to \(2x^2 - 6x = 5\). Dividing by \(2\) and completing the square by adding \((\frac{3}{2})^2 = \frac{9}{4}\) gives \((x - \frac{3}{2})^2 = \frac{19}{4}\), so \(x = \frac{3 \pm \sqrt{19}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2(x - 1)^2 = 3x + 5\)
qs.s: Expand to \(2x^2 - 4x + 2 = 3x + 5\) and rearrange to \(2x^2 - 7x = 3\). Dividing by \(2\) and completing the square by adding \((\frac{7}{4})^2 = \frac{49}{16}\) to both sides produces \((x - \frac{7}{4})^2 = \frac{73}{16}\), giving \(x = \frac{7 \pm \sqrt{73}}{4}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x^2 + 2\sqrt{6}x = -2\)
qs.s: Dividing by 3 gives \(x^2 + \frac{2\sqrt{6}}{3}x = -\frac{2}{3}\). Adding \(\left(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{2}{3}\) to both sides gives \(\left(x + \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\right)^2 = 0\), so \(x = -\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x^2 - 2\sqrt{10}x = -5\)
qs.s: Dividing by 2 gives \(x^2 - \sqrt{10}x = -\frac{5}{2}\). Adding \(\left(-\frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{5}{2}\) to both sides gives \(\left(x - \frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}\right)^2 = 0\), so \(x = \frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x^2 - 2\sqrt{3}x = -1\)
qs.s: Dividing by 3 gives \(x^2 - \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}x = -\frac{1}{3}\). Adding \(\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{3}\) to both sides gives \(\left(x - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)^2 = 0\), so \(x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(5x^2 - 2\sqrt{5}x = -1\)
qs.s: Dividing by 5 gives \(x^2 - \frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}x = -\frac{1}{5}\). Adding \(\left(-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{5}\) to both sides yields \(\left(x - \frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\right)^2 = 0\), so \(x = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x^2 + 2\sqrt{6}x = -3\)
qs.s: Dividing by 2 gives \(x^2 + \sqrt{6}x = -\frac{3}{2}\). Adding \(\left(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{3}{2}\) to both sides yields \(\left(x + \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\right)^2 = 0\), so \(x = -\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x(2x - \sqrt{5}) = 2\sqrt{5}x + 3\)
qs.s: Expanding and collecting like terms yields \(4x^2 - 4\sqrt{5}x = 3\), and dividing by 4 gives \(x^2 - \sqrt{5}x = \frac{3}{4}\). Adding \(\frac{5}{4}\) to both sides yields \(\left(x - \frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\right)^2 = 2\), which gives \(x = \frac{\sqrt{5} \pm 2\sqrt{2}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x(x + 2\sqrt{2}) = 1\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \(3x^2 + 6\sqrt{2}x = 1\), and dividing by 3 gives \(x^2 + 2\sqrt{2}x = \frac{1}{3}\). Adding 2 to both sides produces \((x + \sqrt{2})^2 = \frac{7}{3}\), leading to \(x = -\sqrt{2} \pm \frac{\sqrt{21}}{3} = \frac{-3\sqrt{2} \pm \sqrt{21}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(5 - 2x(x - 2\sqrt{2}) = 1\)
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging gives \(-2x^2 + 4\sqrt{2}x = -4\), and dividing by \(-2\) gives \(x^2 - 2\sqrt{2}x = 2\). Adding 2 to both sides gives \((x - \sqrt{2})^2 = 4\), which simplifies to \(x = \sqrt{2} \pm 2\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(\frac{3}{2}x^2 - \sqrt{3}x = 2\)
qs.s: Multiplying by \(\frac{2}{3}\) gives \(x^2 - \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}x = \frac{4}{3}\). Adding \(\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{3}\) to both sides yields \(\left(x - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{5}{3}\), which gives \(x = \frac{\sqrt{3} \pm \sqrt{15}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x(x - \sqrt{3}) = 2\sqrt{3}x + 1\)
qs.s: Rearranging yields \(2x^2 - 4\sqrt{3}x = 1\), and dividing by 2 gives \(x^2 - 2\sqrt{3}x = \frac{1}{2}\). Adding 3 to both sides yields \((x - \sqrt{3})^2 = \frac{7}{2}\), so \(x = \sqrt{3} \pm \frac{\sqrt{14}}{2} = \frac{2\sqrt{3} \pm \sqrt{14}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x^2 - 6x - 2 = 0\)
qs.s: Dividing by 3 gives \(x^2 - 2x = \frac{2}{3}\), and adding \((-1)^2 = 1\) yields \((x - 1)^2 = \frac{5}{3}\). Taking the square root gives \(x - 1 = \pm\frac{\sqrt{15}}{3}\), so \(x = 1 \pm \frac{\sqrt{15}}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(-2x^2 - 12x - 7 = 0\)
qs.s: Dividing by \(-2\) gives \(x^2 + 6x = -\frac{7}{2}\), and adding \(3^2 = 9\) yields \((x + 3)^2 = \frac{11}{2}\). Taking the square root gives \(x + 3 = \pm\frac{\sqrt{22}}{2}\), so \(x = -3 \pm \frac{\sqrt{22}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(5x^2 + 10x - 1 = 0\)
qs.s: Dividing by 5 gives \(x^2 + 2x = \frac{1}{5}\), and adding \(1^2 = 1\) yields \((x + 1)^2 = \frac{6}{5}\). Taking the square root gives \(x + 1 = \pm\frac{\sqrt{30}}{5}\), so \(x = -1 \pm \frac{\sqrt{30}}{5}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(3x^2 - 9x - 2 = 0\)
qs.s: Dividing by 3 gives \(x^2 - 3x = \frac{2}{3}\), and adding \(\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}\) gives \(\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{35}{12}\). Taking the square root gives \(x - \frac{3}{2} = \pm\frac{\sqrt{105}}{6}\), which simplifies to \(x = \frac{9 \pm \sqrt{105}}{6}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(-2x^2 + 7x + 3 = 0\)
qs.s: Dividing by \(-2\) gives \(x^2 - \frac{7}{2}x = \frac{3}{2}\), and adding \(\left(-\frac{7}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{49}{16}\) yields \(\left(x - \frac{7}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{73}{16}\). Taking the square root gives \(x - \frac{7}{4} = \pm\frac{\sqrt{73}}{4}\), so \(x = \frac{7 \pm \sqrt{73}}{4}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(5x^2 - 15x - 7 = 0\)
qs.s: Dividing by 5 gives \(x^2 - 3x = \frac{7}{5}\), and adding \(\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}\) yields \(\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{73}{20}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing gives \(x - \frac{3}{2} = \pm\frac{\sqrt{365}}{10}\), so \(x = \frac{15 \pm \sqrt{365}}{10}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers. \(2x(x - 5) = 3 - 4x\)
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging gives \(2x^2 - 6x - 3 = 0\), so dividing by 2 yields \(x^2 - 3x = \frac{3}{2}\). Adding \(\frac{9}{4}\) gives \(\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{15}{4}\), leading to \(x = \frac{3 \pm \sqrt{15}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(9x^2 - 12x - 23 = 0\)
qs.s: Dividing by \(9\) gives \(x^2 - \frac{4}{3}x = \frac{23}{9}\), and completing the square by adding \((-\frac{2}{3})^2 = \frac{4}{9}\) gives \((x - \frac{2}{3})^2 = 3\). Taking the square root yields \(x = \frac{2}{3} \pm \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(-9x^2 + 24x + 2 = 0\)
qs.s: Dividing by \(-9\) yields \(x^2 - \frac{8}{3}x = \frac{2}{9}\), and adding \((-\frac{4}{3})^2 = \frac{16}{9}\) results in \((x - \frac{4}{3})^2 = 2\). Solving for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{4}{3} \pm \sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(-4x^2 + 4x + 7 = 0\)
qs.s: Dividing by \(-4\) gives \(x^2 - x = \frac{7}{4}\), and adding \((-\frac{1}{2})^2 = \frac{1}{4}\) to both sides yields \((x - \frac{1}{2})^2 = 2\). Taking the square root gives \(x = \frac{1}{2} \pm \sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(-9x^2 - 6x + 17 = 0\)
qs.s: Dividing by \(-9\) produces \(x^2 + \frac{2}{3}x = \frac{17}{9}\), and adding \((\frac{1}{3})^2 = \frac{1}{9}\) yields \((x + \frac{1}{3})^2 = 2\). Taking the square root gives \(x = -\frac{1}{3} \pm \sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(-4x^2 + 12x + 11 = 0\)
qs.s: Dividing by \(-4\) gives \(x^2 - 3x = \frac{11}{4}\), and adding \((-\frac{3}{2})^2 = \frac{9}{4}\) gives \((x - \frac{3}{2})^2 = 5\). Thus, \(x = \frac{3}{2} \pm \sqrt{5}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(5x(4 - x) = 13\)
qs.s: Rearranging gives \(-5x^2 + 20x = 13\), so \(x^2 - 4x = -\frac{13}{5}\). Completing the square by adding \((-2)^2 = 4\) yields \((x - 2)^2 = \frac{7}{5}\), which gives \(x = 2 \pm \frac{\sqrt{35}}{5} = \frac{10 \pm \sqrt{35}}{5}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(x(7 - 2x) = x - 3\)
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging gives \(-2x^2 + 6x = -3\), so \(x^2 - 3x = \frac{3}{2}\). Adding \((-\frac{3}{2})^2 = \frac{9}{4}\) yields \((x - \frac{3}{2})^2 = \frac{15}{4}\), resulting in \(x = \frac{3 \pm \sqrt{15}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(3x(x - 2) = 2 - 4x\)
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging gives \(3x^2 - 2x = 2\), which becomes \(x^2 - \frac{2}{3}x = \frac{2}{3}\). Adding \((-\frac{1}{3})^2 = \frac{1}{9}\) gives \((x - \frac{1}{3})^2 = \frac{7}{9}\), so \(x = \frac{1 \pm \sqrt{7}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square. Use exact answers.
\(12x^2 - 12x - 5 = 0\)
qs.s: Dividing by \(12\) gives \(x^2 - x = \frac{5}{12}\), and adding \((-\frac{1}{2})^2 = \frac{3}{12}\) gives \((x - \frac{1}{2})^2 = \frac{2}{3}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing yields \(x = \frac{1}{2} \pm \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3} = \frac{3 \pm 2\sqrt{6}}{6}\).

qs.q:

\((2x - 3)^2 = 2(x + 5)\)
Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \(-4x^2 + 4x + 35 = 0\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Dividing by \(-4\) gives \(x^2 - x = \frac{35}{4}\), and adding \(\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{4}\) to both sides yields \(\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = 9\). Taking square roots gives \(x - \frac{1}{2} = \pm 3\), so the solutions are \(x = \frac{7}{2}\) and \(x = -\frac{5}{2}\), with the greater being \(\frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \(-4x^2 + 12x + 55 = 0\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Dividing by \(-4\) gives \(x^2 - 3x = \frac{55}{4}\), and adding \(\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}\) to both sides results in \(\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = 16\). Taking square roots gives \(x - \frac{3}{2} = \pm 4\), so \(x = \frac{11}{2}\) or \(x = -\frac{5}{2}\), giving the greater solution \(\frac{11}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \(-4x^2 + 8x + 45 = 0\). What is the smaller solution?
qs.s: Dividing by \(-4\) gives \(x^2 - 2x = \frac{45}{4}\), and adding \((-1)^2 = 1\) to both sides results in \((x - 1)^2 = \frac{49}{4}\). Taking square roots gives \(x - 1 = \pm \frac{7}{2}\), which yields \(x = \frac{9}{2}\) or \(x = -\frac{5}{2}\), with the smaller solution being \(-\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \(-4x^2 - 4x + 63 = 0\). What is the smaller solution?
qs.s: Dividing by \(-4\) gives \(x^2 + x = \frac{63}{4}\), and adding \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{4}\) to both sides yields \(\left(x + \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = 16\). Taking square roots gives \(x + \frac{1}{2} = \pm 4\), so \(x = \frac{7}{2}\) or \(x = -\frac{9}{2}\), with the smaller solution being \(-\frac{9}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \(-4x^2 - 12x + 27 = 0\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Dividing by \(-4\) gives \(x^2 + 3x = \frac{27}{4}\), and adding \(\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}\) gives \(\left(x + \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = 9\). Taking square roots gives \(x + \frac{3}{2} = \pm 3\), which gives \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) or \(x = -\frac{9}{2}\), with the greater solution being \(\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \(2x(5 - 2x) = 3 - 6x\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging into standard form gives \(-4x^2 + 16x - 3 = 0\), or \(x^2 - 4x = -\frac{3}{4}\). Adding \((-2)^2 = 4\) gives \((x - 2)^2 = \frac{13}{4}\), so \(x = 2 \pm \frac{\sqrt{13}}{2} = \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{13}}{2}\), with the greater solution being \(\frac{4 + \sqrt{13}}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \((x + 2)^2 - 3x^2 = 5x + 1\). What is the smaller solution?
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying gives \(-2x^2 - x + 3 = 0\), which becomes \(x^2 + \frac{1}{2}x = \frac{3}{2}\). Adding \(\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{16}\) gives \(\left(x + \frac{1}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{16}\), leading to \(x = -\frac{1}{4} \pm \frac{5}{4}\), which yields \(1\) and \(-\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \((2x + 1)^2 - (x - 3)^2 = 24\). What is the positive solution?
qs.s: Expanding and collecting like terms yields \(3x^2 + 10x - 32 = 0\), so \(x^2 + \frac{10}{3}x = \frac{32}{3}\). Adding \(\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{9}\) gives \(\left(x + \frac{5}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{121}{9}\), so \(x + \frac{5}{3} = \pm \frac{11}{3}\), which gives \(x = 2\) or \(x = -\frac{16}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \(-3x(2x - 1) = -4x - 3\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Expanding and moving all terms to one side gives \(-6x^2 + 7x + 3 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - \frac{7}{6}x = \frac{1}{2}\). Adding \(\left(-\frac{7}{12}\right)^2 = \frac{49}{144}\) yields \(\left(x - \frac{7}{12}\right)^2 = \frac{121}{144}\), so \(x = \frac{7}{12} \pm \frac{11}{12}\), giving solutions \(\frac{3}{2}\) and \(-\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Solve the quadratic equation by completing the square: \(2x(2 - x) = x^2 - 2\). What is the greater solution?
qs.s: Rearranging gives \(-3x^2 + 4x + 2 = 0\), so dividing by \(-3\) gives \(x^2 - \frac{4}{3}x = \frac{2}{3}\). Adding \(\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{4}{9}\) gives \(\left(x - \frac{2}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{10}{9}\), which yields \(x = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{10}}{3}\), with the greater solution being \(\frac{2 + \sqrt{10}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. Leave the answer in radical form.
\(\displaystyle \frac{-(2) \pm \sqrt{2^2 - 4(1)(-5)}}{2 \cdot 1}\)
qs.s: Evaluate under the radical: \(2^2 - 4(1)(-5) = 4 + 20 = 24\), so \(\sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6}\). Then simplify \(\frac{-2 \pm 2\sqrt{6}}{2} = -1 \pm \sqrt{6}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. Leave the answer in radical form.
\(\displaystyle \frac{-(-2) \pm \sqrt{(-2)^2 - 4(1)(-7)}}{2 \cdot 1}\)
qs.s: Evaluate under the radical: \((-2)^2 - 4(1)(-7) = 4 + 28 = 32\), so \(\sqrt{32} = 4\sqrt{2}\). Then simplify \(\frac{2 \pm 4\sqrt{2}}{2} = 1 \pm 2\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:

qs.s: Evaluate under the radical: \((-6)^2 - 4(1)(7) = 36 - 28 = 8\), so \(\sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2}\). Then simplify \(\frac{6 \pm 2\sqrt{2}}{2} = 3 \pm \sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:

qs.s: Evaluate under the radical: \((-4)^2 - 4(1)(-1) = 16 + 4 = 20\), so \(\sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}\). Then simplify \(\frac{4 \pm 2\sqrt{5}}{2} = 2 \pm \sqrt{5}\).

qs.q:

\(\displaystyle \frac{-(4) \pm \sqrt{4^2 - 4(1)(-3)}}{2 \cdot 1}\)
qs.s: Evaluate under the radical: \(4^2 - 4(1)(-3) = 16 + 12 = 28\), so \(\sqrt{28} = 2\sqrt{7}\). Then simplify \(\frac{-4 \pm 2\sqrt{7}}{2} = -2 \pm \sqrt{7}\).

qs.q:

qs.s: Evaluate under the radical: \((-8)^2 - 4(6)(-2) = 64 + 48 = 112\), so \(\sqrt{112} = 4\sqrt{7}\). Then divide the numerator and denominator by \(4\): \(\frac{8 \pm 4\sqrt{7}}{12} = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{7}}{3}\).

qs.q:

\(\displaystyle \frac{-(-6) \pm \sqrt{(-6)^2 - 4(2)(1)}}{2 \cdot 2}\)
qs.s: Evaluate under the radical: \((-6)^2 - 4(2)(1) = 36 - 8 = 28\), so \(\sqrt{28} = 2\sqrt{7}\). Then divide the numerator and denominator by \(2\): \(\frac{6 \pm 2\sqrt{7}}{4} = \frac{3 \pm \sqrt{7}}{2}\).

qs.q:

qs.s: Evaluate under the radical: \((-6)^2 - 4(4)(-3) = 36 + 48 = 84\), so \(\sqrt{84} = 2\sqrt{21}\). Then divide the numerator and denominator by \(2\): \(\frac{6 \pm 2\sqrt{21}}{8} = \frac{3 \pm \sqrt{21}}{4}\).

qs.q:

\(\displaystyle \frac{-(6) \pm \sqrt{6^2 - 4(3)(-2)}}{2 \cdot 3}\)
qs.s: Evaluate under the radical: \(6^2 - 4(3)(-2) = 36 + 24 = 60\), so \(\sqrt{60} = 2\sqrt{15}\). Then divide the numerator and denominator by \(2\): \(\frac{-6 \pm 2\sqrt{15}}{6} = \frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{15}}{3}\).

qs.q:

\(\displaystyle \frac{-(-4) \pm \sqrt{(-4)^2 - 4(2)(-7)}}{2 \cdot 2}\)

qs.q: Simplify the expression and leave the answer in simplest radical form: \(\frac{-(-3) \pm \sqrt{(-3)^2 - 4(-1)(5)}}{2(-1)}\)
qs.s: Evaluating under the radical gives \((-3)^2 - 4(-1)(5) = 9 + 20 = 29\). Dividing \(3 \pm \sqrt{29}\) by \(-2\) yields \(\frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{29}}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression and leave the answer in simplest radical form: \(\frac{-(-5) \pm \sqrt{(-5)^2 - 4(-1)(2)}}{2(-1)}\)
qs.s: Simplify the numerator to \(5 \pm \sqrt{25 + 8} = 5 \pm \sqrt{33}\). Dividing by \(2(-1) = -2\) gives \(\frac{5 \pm \sqrt{33}}{-2} = \frac{-5 \pm \sqrt{33}}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression and leave the answer in simplest radical form: \(\frac{-(-5) \pm \sqrt{(-5)^2 - 4(-2)(-1)}}{2(-2)}\)
qs.s: The expression under the radical is \(25 - 8 = 17\), giving \(\frac{5 \pm \sqrt{17}}{-4}\). Factoring the negative sign out of the denominator yields \(\frac{-5 \pm \sqrt{17}}{4}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression and leave the answer in simplest radical form: \(\frac{-(-1) \pm \sqrt{(-1)^2 - 4(-3)(1)}}{2(-3)}\)
qs.s: The numerator simplifies to \(1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 12} = 1 \pm \sqrt{13}\) and the denominator is \(-6\). Distributing the negative sign from the denominator yields \(\frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{13}}{6}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression and leave the answer in simplest radical form: \(\frac{-(-3) \pm \sqrt{(-3)^2 - 4(-2)(1)}}{2(-2)}\)
qs.s: Evaluating the numerator gives \(-(-3) = 3\) and \((-3)^2 - 4(-2)(1) = 9 + 8 = 17\). Dividing \(3 \pm \sqrt{17}\) by \(2(-2) = -4\) and transferring the negative sign yields \(\frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{17}}{4}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression and leave the answer in simplest radical form: \(\frac{-(-8) \pm \sqrt{(-8)^2 - 4(2)(-3)}}{2(2)}\)
qs.s: Evaluate the discriminant to get \(64 + 24 = 88\), so \(\sqrt{88} = 2\sqrt{22}\). Dividing \(\frac{8 \pm 2\sqrt{22}}{4}\) by the common factor \(2\) gives \(\frac{4 \pm \sqrt{22}}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression and leave the answer in simplest radical form: \(\frac{-(-6) \pm \sqrt{(-6)^2 - 4(-3)(1)}}{2(-3)}\)
qs.s: Simplify the radical to get \(\frac{6 \pm \sqrt{48}}{-6} = \frac{6 \pm 4\sqrt{3}}{-6}\). Dividing both numerator and denominator by \(-2\) gives \(\frac{-3 \pm 2\sqrt{3}}{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression and leave the answer in simplest radical form: \(\frac{-(-10) \pm \sqrt{(-10)^2 - 4(-4)(1)}}{2(-4)}\)
qs.s: Under the radical, \((-10)^2 - 4(-4)(1) = 116\), which simplifies to \(\sqrt{116} = 2\sqrt{29}\). Simplifying \(\frac{10 \pm 2\sqrt{29}}{-8}\) by dividing numerator and denominator by \(-2\) yields \(\frac{-5 \pm \sqrt{29}}{4}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression and leave the answer in simplest radical form: \(\frac{-(-4) \pm \sqrt{(-4)^2 - 4(-2)(1)}}{2(-2)}\)
qs.s: The expression becomes \(\frac{4 \pm \sqrt{24}}{-4} = \frac{4 \pm 2\sqrt{6}}{-4}\). Factoring out \(2\) from the numerator and canceling with \(-4\) gives \(\frac{-2 \pm \sqrt{6}}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression and leave the answer in simplest radical form: \(\frac{-(-6) \pm \sqrt{(-6)^2 - 4(-6)(3)}}{2(-6)}\)
qs.s: The discriminant is \(36 + 72 = 108\), so \(\sqrt{108} = 6\sqrt{3}\). Dividing both terms of the numerator and the denominator by \(-6\) gives \(\frac{6 \pm 6\sqrt{3}}{-12} = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{3}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression using the \(-\) sign. Leave your answer in simplest radical form:
\(\displaystyle \frac{-(-4) \pm \sqrt{(-4)^2 - 4(\sqrt{5})(-\sqrt{5})}}{2\sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: The radicand simplifies to \((-4)^2 - 4(-5) = 16 + 20 = 36\), so \(\sqrt{36} = 6\). Evaluating with the \(-\) sign gives \(\frac{4 - 6}{2\sqrt{5}} = \frac{-2}{2\sqrt{5}} = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} = -\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression using the \(+\) sign. Leave your answer in simplest radical form:
\(\displaystyle \frac{-(-8) \pm \sqrt{(-8)^2 - 4(\sqrt{3})(-3\sqrt{3})}}{2\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: The radicand simplifies to \((-8)^2 - 4(-9) = 64 + 36 = 100\), so \(\sqrt{100} = 10\). Evaluating with the \(+\) sign gives \(\frac{8 + 10}{2\sqrt{3}} = \frac{18}{2\sqrt{3}} = \frac{9}{\sqrt{3}} = 3\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression using the \(+\) sign. Leave your answer in simplest radical form:
\(\displaystyle \frac{-(-1) \pm \sqrt{(-1)^2 - 4(\sqrt{2})(-\sqrt{2})}}{2\sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: The radicand simplifies to \((-1)^2 - 4(-2) = 1 + 8 = 9\), so \(\sqrt{9} = 3\). Evaluating with the \(+\) sign gives \(\frac{1 + 3}{2\sqrt{2}} = \frac{4}{2\sqrt{2}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression using the \(-\) sign. Leave your answer in simplest radical form:
\(\displaystyle \frac{-(-1) \pm \sqrt{(-1)^2 - 4(\sqrt{2})(-3\sqrt{2})}}{2\sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: The radicand simplifies to \((-1)^2 - 4(-6) = 1 + 24 = 25\), so \(\sqrt{25} = 5\). Evaluating with the \(-\) sign gives \(\frac{1 - 5}{2\sqrt{2}} = \frac{-4}{2\sqrt{2}} = \frac{-2}{\sqrt{2}} = -\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression using the \(+\) sign. Leave your answer in simplest radical form:
\(\displaystyle \frac{-(-6) \pm \sqrt{(-6)^2 - 4(\sqrt{7})(-\sqrt{7})}}{2\sqrt{7}}\)
qs.s: The radicand simplifies to \((-6)^2 - 4(-7) = 36 + 28 = 64\), so \(\sqrt{64} = 8\). Evaluating with the \(+\) sign gives \(\frac{6 + 8}{2\sqrt{7}} = \frac{14}{2\sqrt{7}} = \frac{7}{\sqrt{7}} = \sqrt{7}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression using the \(+\) sign. Leave your answer in simplest radical form:
\(\displaystyle \frac{-(-2) \pm \sqrt{(-2)^2 - 4(2\sqrt{5})(-\sqrt{5})}}{2(2\sqrt{5})}\)
qs.s: The radicand simplifies to \(4 - 4(-10) = 44\), so \(\sqrt{44} = 2\sqrt{11}\). Taking the \(+\) sign gives \(\frac{2 + 2\sqrt{11}}{4\sqrt{5}} = \frac{1 + \sqrt{11}}{2\sqrt{5}} = \frac{(1 + \sqrt{11})\sqrt{5}}{2(5)} = \frac{\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{55}}{10}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression using the \(+\) sign. Leave your answer in simplest radical form:
\(\displaystyle \frac{-(-2\sqrt{3}) \pm \sqrt{(-2\sqrt{3})^2 - 4(\sqrt{2})(-\sqrt{2})}}{2\sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: The radicand simplifies to \(12 - 4(-2) = 20\), so \(\sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}\). Taking the \(+\) sign gives \(\frac{2\sqrt{3} + 2\sqrt{5}}{2\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{5})\sqrt{2}}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{10}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression using the \(-\) sign. Leave your answer in simplest radical form:
\(\displaystyle \frac{-(-4) \pm \sqrt{(-4)^2 - 4(\sqrt{3})(-2\sqrt{3})}}{2\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: The radicand simplifies to \(16 - 4(-6) = 40\), so \(\sqrt{40} = 2\sqrt{10}\). Taking the \(-\) sign gives \(\frac{4 - 2\sqrt{10}}{2\sqrt{3}} = \frac{2 - \sqrt{10}}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{(2 - \sqrt{10})\sqrt{3}}{3} = \frac{2\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{30}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression using the \(-\) sign. Leave your answer in simplest radical form:
\(\displaystyle \frac{-(-3\sqrt{2}) \pm \sqrt{(-3\sqrt{2})^2 - 4(\sqrt{6})(-\sqrt{6})}}{2\sqrt{6}}\)
qs.s: The radicand simplifies to \(18 - 4(-6) = 42\). Taking the \(-\) sign and multiplying numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{6}\) yields \(\frac{(3\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{42})\sqrt{6}}{2(6)} = \frac{3\sqrt{12} - \sqrt{252}}{12} = \frac{6\sqrt{3} - 6\sqrt{7}}{12} = \frac{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{7}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression using the \(+\) sign. Leave your answer in simplest radical form:
\(\displaystyle \frac{-(-6) \pm \sqrt{(-6)^2 - 4(3\sqrt{2})(-\sqrt{2})}}{2(3\sqrt{2})}\)
qs.s: The radicand simplifies to \(36 - 4(-6) = 60\), so \(\sqrt{60} = 2\sqrt{15}\). Taking the \(+\) sign gives \(\frac{6 + 2\sqrt{15}}{6\sqrt{2}} = \frac{3 + \sqrt{15}}{3\sqrt{2}} = \frac{(3 + \sqrt{15})\sqrt{2}}{3(2)} = \frac{3\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{30}}{6}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. Leave answers in radical form.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{3} \pm \sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^2 - 4(2)(-3)}}{2 \cdot 2}\)
qs.s: Evaluate the radicand: \((\sqrt{3})^2 - 4(2)(-3) = 3 + 24 = 27\), so \(\sqrt{27} = 3\sqrt{3}\). Then \(\frac{\sqrt{3} \pm 3\sqrt{3}}{4}\) gives \(\frac{4\sqrt{3}}{4} = \sqrt{3}\) and \(\frac{-2\sqrt{3}}{4} = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. Leave answers in radical form.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{5} \pm \sqrt{(\sqrt{5})^2 - 4(2)(-5)}}{2 \cdot 2}\)
qs.s: Evaluate the radicand: \((\sqrt{5})^2 - 4(2)(-5) = 5 + 40 = 45\), so \(\sqrt{45} = 3\sqrt{5}\). Then \(\frac{\sqrt{5} \pm 3\sqrt{5}}{4}\) simplifies to \(\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{4} = \sqrt{5}\) and \(\frac{-2\sqrt{5}}{4} = -\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. Leave answers in radical form.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{2} \pm \sqrt{(\sqrt{2})^2 - 4(1)(-4)}}{2 \cdot 1}\)
qs.s: Evaluate the radicand: \((\sqrt{2})^2 - 4(1)(-4) = 2 + 16 = 18\), so \(\sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}\). Then \(\frac{\sqrt{2} \pm 3\sqrt{2}}{2}\) yields \(\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{2} = 2\sqrt{2}\) and \(\frac{-2\sqrt{2}}{2} = -\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. Leave answers in radical form.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{3} \pm \sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^2 - 4(3)(-2)}}{2 \cdot 3}\)
qs.s: Evaluate the radicand: \((\sqrt{3})^2 - 4(3)(-2) = 3 + 24 = 27\), so \(\sqrt{27} = 3\sqrt{3}\). Then \(\frac{\sqrt{3} \pm 3\sqrt{3}}{6}\) reduces to \(\frac{4\sqrt{3}}{6} = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\) and \(\frac{-2\sqrt{3}}{6} = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. Leave answers in radical form.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{3} \pm \sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^2 - 4(1)(-6)}}{2 \cdot 1}\)
qs.s: Evaluate the radicand: \((\sqrt{3})^2 - 4(1)(-6) = 3 + 24 = 27\), which gives \(\sqrt{27} = 3\sqrt{3}\). Then \(\frac{\sqrt{3} \pm 3\sqrt{3}}{2}\) gives \(\frac{4\sqrt{3}}{2} = 2\sqrt{3}\) and \(\frac{-2\sqrt{3}}{2} = -\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. Leave answers in radical form.
\(\displaystyle \frac{-2\sqrt{6} \pm \sqrt{(-2\sqrt{6})^2 - 4(3)(-6)}}{2 \cdot 3}\)
qs.s: Compute the radicand: \((-2\sqrt{6})^2 - 4(3)(-6) = 24 + 72 = 96\), so \(\sqrt{96} = 4\sqrt{6}\). Then \(\frac{-2\sqrt{6} \pm 4\sqrt{6}}{6}\) simplifies to \(\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\) and \(\frac{-6\sqrt{6}}{6} = -\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. Leave answers in radical form.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2\sqrt{2} \pm \sqrt{(2\sqrt{2})^2 - 4(3)(-2)}}{2 \cdot 3}\)
qs.s: Compute the radicand: \((2\sqrt{2})^2 - 4(3)(-2) = 8 + 24 = 32\), so \(\sqrt{32} = 4\sqrt{2}\). Then \(\frac{2\sqrt{2} \pm 4\sqrt{2}}{6}\) yields \(\frac{6\sqrt{2}}{6} = \sqrt{2}\) and \(\frac{-2\sqrt{2}}{6} = -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. Leave answers in radical form.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2\sqrt{5} \pm \sqrt{(2\sqrt{5})^2 - 4(3)(-5)}}{2 \cdot 3}\)
qs.s: Compute the radicand: \((2\sqrt{5})^2 - 4(3)(-5) = 20 + 60 = 80\), so \(\sqrt{80} = 4\sqrt{5}\). Then \(\frac{2\sqrt{5} \pm 4\sqrt{5}}{6}\) yields \(\frac{6\sqrt{5}}{6} = \sqrt{5}\) and \(\frac{-2\sqrt{5}}{6} = -\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. Leave answers in radical form.
\(\displaystyle \frac{3\sqrt{3} \pm \sqrt{(3\sqrt{3})^2 - 4(2)(-6)}}{2 \cdot 2}\)
qs.s: Compute the radicand: \((3\sqrt{3})^2 - 4(2)(-6) = 27 + 48 = 75\), so \(\sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3}\). Then \(\frac{3\sqrt{3} \pm 5\sqrt{3}}{4}\) gives \(\frac{8\sqrt{3}}{4} = 2\sqrt{3}\) and \(\frac{-2\sqrt{3}}{4} = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. Leave answers in radical form.
\(\displaystyle \frac{5\sqrt{2} \pm \sqrt{(5\sqrt{2})^2 - 4(2)(6)}}{2 \cdot 2}\)
qs.s: Compute the radicand: \((5\sqrt{2})^2 - 4(2)(6) = 50 - 48 = 2\), so the radical is \(\sqrt{2}\). Then \(\frac{5\sqrt{2} \pm \sqrt{2}}{4}\) yields \(\frac{6\sqrt{2}}{4} = \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\) and \(\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{4} = \sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
