qs.s: Setting the discriminant to zero gives \((k + 2)^2 - 4(k)(2) = k^2 + 4k + 4 - 8k = k^2 - 4k + 4 = 0\). Factoring \((k - 2)^2 = 0\) gives the unique solution \(k = 2\).

qs.q:
Determine the larger value of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions.
\(x^2 - kx + 3k = 8\); one real solution
qs.s: Writing in standard form gives \(x^2 - kx + (3k - 8) = 0\), so the discriminant is \((-k)^2 - 4(1)(3k - 8) = k^2 - 12k + 32 = 0\). Factoring \((k - 8)(k - 4) = 0\) gives roots \(4\) and \(8\), so the larger value is \(8\).

qs.q:
Determine the positive value of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions.
\(x^2 + kx + 2k + 5 = 0\); one real solution
qs.s: Setting the discriminant to zero gives \(k^2 - 4(1)(2k + 5) = k^2 - 8k - 20 = 0\). Factoring as \((k - 10)(k + 2) = 0\) gives the positive value \(k = 10\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(kx^2 + 2x + k = 0\); two real solutions.
qs.s: For two real solutions, the discriminant must be positive: \(b^2 - 4ac = 2^2 - 4(k)(k) = 4 - 4k^2 > 0\), which gives \(k^2 < 1\), or \(-1 < k < 1\). Since the equation is quadratic, the leading coefficient cannot be zero, so \(k \neq 0\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(kx^2 + 3x + k = 0\); two real solutions.
qs.s: For two real solutions, \(b^2 - 4ac = 3^2 - 4(k)(k) = 9 - 4k^2 > 0\), which yields \(k^2 < \frac{9}{4}\), or \(-\frac{3}{2} < k < \frac{3}{2}\). Because the \(x^2\) coefficient cannot be zero, \(k \neq 0\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(kx^2 + 6x + k = 0\); two real solutions.
qs.s: Setting the discriminant greater than zero gives \(6^2 - 4(k)(k) = 36 - 4k^2 > 0\), so \(k^2 < 9\), meaning \(-3 < k < 3\). We also require \(k \neq 0\) for the equation to remain quadratic.

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(2kx^2 + 5x + 2k = 0\); two real solutions.
qs.s: Setting \(b^2 - 4ac > 0\) gives \(5^2 - 4(2k)(2k) = 25 - 16k^2 > 0\), so \(k^2 < \frac{25}{16}\), which means \(-\frac{5}{4} < k < \frac{5}{4}\). Since the leading coefficient \(2k \neq 0\), \(k \neq 0\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(kx^2 - 4x + k = 0\); two real solutions.
qs.s: For two real solutions, \(b^2 - 4ac = (-4)^2 - 4(k)(k) = 16 - 4k^2 > 0\), which simplifies to \(k^2 < 4\), or \(-2 < k < 2\). The leading coefficient cannot be zero, so \(k \neq 0\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(2x(x + k) = -(3k + 8)\); two real solutions.
qs.s: Rearranging into standard form yields \(2x^2 + 2kx + (3k + 8) = 0\). Setting \(b^2 - 4ac = (2k)^2 - 4(2)(3k + 8) = 4(k^2 - 6k - 16) > 0\) gives \((k - 8)(k + 2) > 0\), so \(k < -2\) or \(k > 8\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x(x + k) = 4x - k + 1\); two real solutions.
qs.s: Rearranging to standard form gives \(x^2 + (k - 4)x + (k - 1) = 0\). Setting \(b^2 - 4ac = (k - 4)^2 - 4(1)(k - 1) = k^2 - 12k + 20 > 0\) yields \((k - 2)(k - 10) > 0\), so \(k < 2\) or \(k > 10\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \((k - 1)x^2 + 6x + k = 1\); two real solutions.
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in standard form as \((k - 1)x^2 + 6x + (k - 1) = 0\). For two real solutions, \(b^2 - 4ac = 36 - 4(k - 1)^2 > 0\), giving \((k - 1)^2 < 9\), which leads to \(-2 < k < 4\) with \(k \neq 1\) since the leading coefficient cannot be zero.

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x(x + k + 2) = 2 - 3k\); two real solutions.
qs.s: Write the equation as \(x^2 + (k + 2)x + (3k - 2) = 0\). For two real solutions, \(b^2 - 4ac = (k + 2)^2 - 4(1)(3k - 2) = k^2 - 8k + 12 > 0\), which factors as \((k - 2)(k - 6) > 0\), so \(k < 2\) or \(k > 6\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \((k + 2)x^2 + 6x + k = -2\); two real solutions.
qs.s: In standard form, \((k + 2)x^2 + 6x + (k + 2) = 0\), so \(b^2 - 4ac = 36 - 4(k + 2)^2 > 0 \implies (k + 2)^2 < 9\), which gives \(-5 < k < 1\) with \(k \neq -2\) so the leading coefficient is non-zero.

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(kx^2 + 4x + k = 0\); no real solutions.
qs.s: For the equation to have no real solutions, the discriminant must be negative: \(b^2 - 4ac = 4^2 - 4(k)(k) = 16 - 4k^2 < 0\). Solving \(4k^2 > 16\) gives \(k^2 > 4\), which means \(k < -2\text{ or }k > 2\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(kx^2 + 3x + k = 0\); no real solutions.
qs.s: For no real solutions, the discriminant is negative: \(3^2 - 4(k)(k) = 9 - 4k^2 < 0\). This leads to \(k^2 > \frac{9}{4}\), so \(k < -\frac{3}{2}\text{ or }k > \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(2x^2 + kx + 8 = 0\); no real solutions.
qs.s: The equation has no real solutions when \(b^2 - 4ac < 0\), which yields \(k^2 - 4(2)(8) = k^2 - 64 < 0\). Thus, \(-8 < k < 8\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(4x^2 + kx + 1 = 0\); no real solutions.
qs.s: Setting the discriminant negative gives \(b^2 - 4ac = k^2 - 4(4)(1) = k^2 - 16 < 0\). Solving \(k^2 < 16\) gives \(-4 < k < 4\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x^2 + kx + 9 = 0\); no real solutions.
qs.s: For no real solutions, set the discriminant less than zero: \(b^2 - 4ac = k^2 - 4(1)(9) = k^2 - 36 < 0\). Solving \(k^2 < 36\) gives \(-6 < k < 6\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \((k - 1)x^2 + 6x + k - 1 = 0\); no real solutions.
qs.s: For no real solutions, \(b^2 - 4ac = 6^2 - 4(k - 1)^2 < 0\), which simplifies to \((k - 1)^2 > 9\). This means \(k - 1 < -3\text{ or }k - 1 > 3\), yielding \(k < -2\text{ or }k > 4\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(\frac{1}{2}x^2 + kx + k + 4 = 0\); no real solutions.
qs.s: The discriminant is \(k^2 - 4\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)(k + 4) = k^2 - 2k - 8\). Requiring \(k^2 - 2k - 8 < 0\) gives \((k - 4)(k + 2) < 0\), so \(-2 < k < 4\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x(x + 2k) = -3k - 4\); no real solutions.
qs.s: Writing in standard form gives \(x^2 + 2kx + (3k + 4) = 0\). Setting \(b^2 - 4ac < 0\) yields \((2k)^2 - 4(1)(3k + 4) = 4(k^2 - 3k - 4) < 0\), which factors as \(4(k - 4)(k + 1) < 0\), giving \(-1 < k < 4\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x^2 + (k + 1)x + 2k = 1\); no real solutions.
qs.s: Rearranging to standard form gives \(x^2 + (k + 1)x + (2k - 1) = 0\). Setting \(b^2 - 4ac < 0\) yields \((k + 1)^2 - 4(1)(2k - 1) = k^2 - 6k + 5 < 0\), which factors as \((k - 1)(k - 5) < 0\), giving \(1 < k < 5\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x^2 + (k - 1)x + k + 2 = 0\); no real solutions.
qs.s: The discriminant must be negative: \((k - 1)^2 - 4(1)(k + 2) = k^2 - 6k - 7 < 0\). Factoring gives \((k - 7)(k + 1) < 0\), which yields \(-1 < k < 7\).

qs.q: Determine the negative value of \(k\) so that the equation \(x^2 - kx + 16 = 0\) has one real solution.
qs.s: Setting the discriminant to zero yields \((-k)^2 - 4(1)(16) = 0\), which simplifies to \(k^2 = 64\). Since \(k < 0\), we obtain \(k = -8\).

qs.q: Determine the positive value of \(k\) so that the equation \(x^2 + kx + 49 = 0\) has one real solution.
qs.s: The equation has one real solution when the discriminant is zero: \(k^2 - 4(1)(49) = 0\), so \(k^2 = 196\). Since \(k > 0\), we find \(k = 14\).

qs.q: Determine the negative value of \(k\) so that the equation \(x^2 + kx + 36 = 0\) has one real solution.
qs.s: For one real solution, the discriminant must be zero: \(k^2 - 4(1)(36) = 0\), giving \(k^2 = 144\). Choosing the negative root gives \(k = -12\).

qs.q: Determine the positive value of \(k\) so that the equation \(x^2 - kx + 9 = 0\) has one real solution.
qs.s: For the equation to have one real solution, the discriminant must be zero: \((-k)^2 - 4(1)(9) = 0\), which gives \(k^2 = 36\). Since \(k > 0\), we have \(k = 6\).

qs.q: Determine the positive value of \(k\) so that the equation \(x^2 + kx + 25 = 0\) has one real solution.
qs.s: Setting the discriminant to zero gives \(k^2 - 4(1)(25) = 0\), so \(k^2 = 100\). Taking the positive square root gives \(k = 10\).

qs.q: Determine the positive value of \(k\) so that the equation \(3x^2 + k(x + 1) + 9 = 0\) has one real solution.
qs.s: In standard form, the equation is \(3x^2 + kx + (k + 9) = 0\), so its discriminant is \(k^2 - 4(3)(k + 9) = k^2 - 12k - 108 = 0\). Factoring gives \((k - 18)(k + 6) = 0\), so the positive value is \(k = 18\).

qs.q: Determine the positive value of \(k\) so that the equation \(x^2 + (k - 2)x + 2k + 1 = 0\) has one real solution.
qs.s: Setting the discriminant to zero gives \((k - 2)^2 - 4(1)(2k + 1) = 0\), which simplifies to \(k^2 - 12k = 0\). Factoring gives \(k(k - 12) = 0\), so the positive solution is \(k = 12\).

qs.q: Determine the positive value of \(k\) so that the equation \(x^2 + kx + k + 8 = 0\) has one real solution.
qs.s: Setting the discriminant to zero gives \(k^2 - 4(1)(k + 8) = 0\), which simplifies to \(k^2 - 4k - 32 = 0\). Factoring as \((k - 8)(k + 4) = 0\) gives the positive value \(k = 8\).

qs.q: Determine the positive value of \(k\) so that the equation \(2x^2 + kx = -(k + 16)\) has one real solution.
qs.s: Rearranging into standard form gives \(2x^2 + kx + (k + 16) = 0\). Setting the discriminant to zero yields \(k^2 - 4(2)(k + 16) = k^2 - 8k - 128 = 0\), which factors as \((k - 16)(k + 8) = 0\), giving \(k = 16\).

qs.q: Determine the negative value of \(k\) so that the equation \(x^2 - 2kx + 3k + 10 = 0\) has one real solution.
qs.s: The discriminant must be zero: \((-2k)^2 - 4(1)(3k + 10) = 4k^2 - 12k - 40 = 0\). Dividing by 4 yields \(k^2 - 3k - 10 = (k - 5)(k + 2) = 0\), so the negative value is \(k = -2\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x^2 - kx + 25 = 0\); two real solutions
qs.s: The discriminant is \(b^2 - 4ac = (-k)^2 - 4(1)(25) = k^2 - 100\). For two real solutions, \(k^2 - 100 > 0\), which gives \(k < -10\) or \(k > 10\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(2x^2 + kx + 8 = 0\); two real solutions
qs.s: The discriminant is \(b^2 - 4ac = k^2 - 4(2)(8) = k^2 - 64\). For two real solutions, \(k^2 - 64 > 0\), which gives \(k < -8\) or \(k > 8\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x^2 + kx + 49 = 0\); two real solutions
qs.s: The discriminant is \(b^2 - 4ac = k^2 - 4(1)(49) = k^2 - 196\). For two real solutions, \(k^2 - 196 > 0\), which gives \(k < -14\) or \(k > 14\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x^2 - kx = -36\); two real solutions
qs.s: Rearranging gives \(x^2 - kx + 36 = 0\), so the discriminant is \(b^2 - 4ac = (-k)^2 - 4(1)(36) = k^2 - 144\). Setting \(k^2 - 144 > 0\) yields \(k < -12\) or \(k > 12\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x^2 + kx + 1 = 0\); two real solutions
qs.s: The discriminant is \(b^2 - 4ac = k^2 - 4(1)(1) = k^2 - 4\). For two real solutions, \(k^2 - 4 > 0\), which gives \(k < -2\) or \(k > 2\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x(x - 2k) + 3k + 4 = 0\); two real solutions
qs.s: Expanding gives \(x^2 - 2kx + (3k + 4) = 0\), with discriminant \(b^2 - 4ac = (-2k)^2 - 4(1)(3k + 4) = 4(k^2 - 3k - 4)\). Setting \(4(k - 4)(k + 1) > 0\) yields \(k < -1\) or \(k > 4\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(2x(x + k) = -(k + 4)\); two real solutions
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging gives \(2x^2 + 2kx + (k + 4) = 0\), with discriminant \(b^2 - 4ac = (2k)^2 - 4(2)(k + 4) = 4(k^2 - 2k - 8)\). Setting \(4(k - 4)(k + 2) > 0\) yields \(k < -2\) or \(k > 4\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(\frac{1}{2}x^2 - kx + 5k = 12\); two real solutions
Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x^2 + kx + k = -3\); two real solutions
qs.s: Rearranging into standard form gives \(x^2 + kx + (k + 3) = 0\), with discriminant \(b^2 - 4ac = k^2 - 4(1)(k + 3) = k^2 - 4k - 12\). Setting \((k - 6)(k + 2) > 0\) yields \(k < -2\) or \(k > 6\).

qs.q: Determine the values of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x(x + 2k) = 5 - 6k\); two real solutions
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging gives \(x^2 + 2kx + (6k - 5) = 0\), with discriminant \(b^2 - 4ac = (2k)^2 - 4(1)(6k - 5) = 4(k^2 - 6k + 5)\). Setting \(4(k - 1)(k - 5) > 0\) yields \(k < 1\) or \(k > 5\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(y^2 - ky + 1 = 0\); no real solutions.
qs.s: For no real solutions, the discriminant must be negative: \((-k)^2 - 4(1)(1) = k^2 - 4 < 0\). Solving \(k^2 < 4\) gives \(-2 < k < 2\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x^2 - kx + 16 = 0\); no real solutions.
qs.s: For no real solutions, the discriminant must satisfy \(b^2 - 4ac < 0\), giving \((-k)^2 - 4(1)(16) = k^2 - 64 < 0\). Solving this inequality yields \(-8 < k < 8\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x^2 + kx + 36 = 0\); no real solutions.
qs.s: To have no real solutions, the discriminant must satisfy \(b^2 - 4ac < 0\), which gives \(k^2 - 4(1)(36) = k^2 - 144 < 0\). Solving gives \(-12 < k < 12\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x^2 + kx + 9 = 0\); no real solutions.
qs.s: For the equation to have no real solutions, the discriminant must be negative: \(b^2 - 4ac = k^2 - 4(1)(9) = k^2 - 36 < 0\). Solving \(k^2 < 36\) gives \(-6 < k < 6\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x^2 + kx + 25 = 0\); no real solutions.
qs.s: Setting the discriminant less than zero gives \(k^2 - 4(1)(25) = k^2 - 100 < 0\). Solving \(k^2 < 100\) produces \(-10 < k < 10\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x^2 + 2kx + 3k = -4\); no real solutions.
qs.s: Rewrite in standard form as \(x^2 + 2kx + (3k + 4) = 0\). For no real solutions, set \(b^2 - 4ac = (2k)^2 - 4(1)(3k + 4) = 4k^2 - 12k - 16 < 0\), which simplifies to \(k^2 - 3k - 4 < 0\); factoring \((k - 4)(k + 1) < 0\) gives \(-1 < k < 4\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x(2x + k) = -18\); no real solutions.
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in standard form as \(2x^2 + kx + 18 = 0\). For no real solutions, set \(b^2 - 4ac = k^2 - 4(2)(18) = k^2 - 144 < 0\), which gives \(-12 < k < 12\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(4x^2 + kx = -25\); no real solutions.
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in standard form as \(4x^2 + kx + 25 = 0\). For no real solutions, set \(b^2 - 4ac = k^2 - 4(4)(25) = k^2 - 400 < 0\), yielding \(-20 < k < 20\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x^2 - kx + 6 = 0\); no real solutions.
qs.s: The condition for no real solutions is \(b^2 - 4ac < 0\), so \((-k)^2 - 4(1)(6) = k^2 - 24 < 0\). Thus \(k^2 < 24\), giving \(-\sqrt{24} < k < \sqrt{24}\), which simplifies to \(-2\sqrt{6} < k < 2\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(k\) so that the equation has the indicated number of solutions: \(x^2 + kx + k + 3 = 0\); no real solutions.
qs.s: For no real solutions, set \(b^2 - 4ac = k^2 - 4(1)(k + 3) < 0\), giving \(k^2 - 4k - 12 < 0\). Factoring as \((k - 6)(k + 2) < 0\) yields \(-2 < k < 6\).

qs.q: Find the smaller of two consecutive odd whole numbers such that the sum of their squares is 74.
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(x + 2\). Solving \(x^2 + (x + 2)^2 = 74\) gives \(2x^2 + 4x - 70 = 0\), or \(x^2 + 2x - 35 = 0\), which factors as \((x + 7)(x - 5) = 0\), giving the smaller number \(x = 5\).

qs.q: Find the larger of two consecutive odd whole numbers such that the sum of their squares is 202.
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(x + 2\). Setting \(x^2 + (x + 2)^2 = 202\) gives \(2x^2 + 4x - 198 = 0\), or \(x^2 + 2x - 99 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 11)(x - 9) = 0\), so \(x = 9\), which makes the larger number \(x + 2 = 11\).

qs.q: Find the smaller of two consecutive positive integers such that the sum of their squares is 85.
qs.s: Let the integers be \(x\) and \(x + 1\). Solving \(x^2 + (x + 1)^2 = 85\) gives \(2x^2 + 2x - 84 = 0\), or \(x^2 + x - 42 = 0\), which factors as \((x + 7)(x - 6) = 0\). Rejecting the negative root gives the smaller integer \(x = 6\).

qs.q: Find the larger of two consecutive even whole numbers such that the sum of their squares is 100.
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(x + 2\). Solving \(x^2 + (x + 2)^2 = 100\) gives \(2x^2 + 4x - 96 = 0\), or \(x^2 + 2x - 48 = 0\), so \((x + 8)(x - 6) = 0\). Since \(x = 6\), the larger number is \(x + 2 = 8\).

qs.q: Find the smaller of two consecutive even whole numbers such that the sum of their squares is 164.
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(x + 2\). Expanding \(x^2 + (x + 2)^2 = 164\) yields \(2x^2 + 4x - 160 = 0\), or \(x^2 + 2x - 80 = 0\). Factoring as \((x + 10)(x - 8) = 0\) gives the smaller number \(x = 8\).

qs.q: The sum of the square of the smaller and twice the square of the larger of two consecutive positive even integers is 264. Find the smaller of the two integers.
qs.s: Let the integers be \(x\) and \(x + 2\). Setting \(x^2 + 2(x + 2)^2 = 264\) yields \(3x^2 + 8x - 256 = 0\), which factors as \((3x + 32)(x - 8) = 0\). Rejecting the negative value gives the smaller integer \(x = 8\).

qs.q: Find the smallest of three consecutive positive integers such that the sum of their squares is 509.
qs.s: Let the integers be \(x\), \(x + 1\), and \(x + 2\). Expanding \(x^2 + (x + 1)^2 + (x + 2)^2 = 509\) simplifies to \(3x^2 + 6x - 504 = 0\), or \(x^2 + 2x - 168 = 0\). Factoring as \((x + 14)(x - 12) = 0\) yields the smallest integer \(x = 12\).

qs.q: The sum of the squares of two consecutive positive integers is 57 more than their product. Find the larger integer.
qs.s: Let the integers be \(x\) and \(x + 1\). Setting \(x^2 + (x + 1)^2 = x(x + 1) + 57\) simplifies to \(x^2 + x - 56 = 0\), which factors as \((x + 8)(x - 7) = 0\). Since \(x = 7\), the larger integer is \(x + 1 = 8\).

qs.q: Find the largest of three consecutive positive odd integers such that the sum of their squares is 251.
qs.s: Let the integers be \(x\), \(x + 2\), and \(x + 4\). The equation \(x^2 + (x + 2)^2 + (x + 4)^2 = 251\) simplifies to \(3x^2 + 12x - 231 = 0\), or \(x^2 + 4x - 77 = 0\), factoring into \((x + 11)(x - 7) = 0\). With \(x = 7\), the largest integer is \(x + 4 = 11\).

qs.q: Find the larger of two consecutive odd whole numbers such that the sum of their squares is 1154.
qs.s: Let the numbers be \(x\) and \(x + 2\). Solving \(x^2 + (x + 2)^2 = 1154\) leads to \(2x^2 + 4x - 1150 = 0\), or \(x^2 + 2x - 575 = 0\), which factors as \((x + 25)(x - 23) = 0\). The smaller number is \(x = 23\), so the larger number is \(x + 2 = 25\).

qs.q: The sum of a number and 8 times its reciprocal is 6. What is the smaller number that has this property?
qs.s: Setting up the equation \(x + \frac{8}{x} = 6\) yields \(x^2 - 6x + 8 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 2)(x - 4) = 0\), so the solutions are 2 and 4, and the smaller number is 2.

qs.q: The sum of a number and 12 times its reciprocal is 7. What is the smaller number that has this property?
qs.s: Multiplying \(x + \frac{12}{x} = 7\) by \(x\) gives \(x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0\), which factors into \((x - 3)(x - 4) = 0\). The numbers are 3 and 4, so the smaller number is 3.

qs.q: The sum of a number and twice its reciprocal is \(-3\). What is the smaller number that has this property?
qs.s: Multiplying \(x + \frac{2}{x} = -3\) by \(x\) gives \(x^2 + 3x + 2 = 0\), which factors into \((x + 1)(x + 2) = 0\). The roots are \(-1\) and \(-2\), so the smaller number is \(-2\).

qs.q: The sum of a number and 6 times its reciprocal is 5. What is the greater number that has this property?
qs.s: The equation \(x + \frac{6}{x} = 5\) simplifies to \(x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0\). Factoring into \((x - 2)(x - 3) = 0\) yields solutions 2 and 3, so the greater number is 3.

qs.q: The sum of a number and 5 times its reciprocal is 6. What is the greater number that has this property?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number, so \(x + \frac{5}{x} = 6\). Multiplying by \(x\) gives \(x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 1)(x - 5) = 0\), giving solutions 1 and 5, where the greater number is 5.

qs.q: The difference between twice a number and 5 times its reciprocal is 9. What is the negative number that has this property?
qs.s: The equation is \(2x - \frac{5}{x} = 9\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 - 9x - 5 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x + 1)(x - 5) = 0\), so the negative solution is \(-\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: A positive number exceeds 3 times its reciprocal by \(\frac{11}{2}\). What is the number?
qs.s: The relation gives \(x - \frac{3}{x} = \frac{11}{2}\), which becomes \(2x^2 - 11x - 6 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x + 1)(x - 6) = 0\), and since the number is positive, \(x = 6\).

qs.q: The sum of three times a number and 4 times its reciprocal is 8. What is the smaller number that has this property?
qs.s: Multiplying \(3x + \frac{4}{x} = 8\) by \(x\) gives \(3x^2 - 8x + 4 = 0\), which factors as \((3x - 2)(x - 2) = 0\). The roots are \(\frac{2}{3}\) and \(2\), so the smaller number is \(\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: The sum of twice a number and 5 times its reciprocal is 11. What is the smaller number that has this property?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number, so \(2x + \frac{5}{x} = 11\), which multiplies out to \(2x^2 - 11x + 5 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x - 1)(x - 5) = 0\), so \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) or \(x = 5\), and the smaller number is \(\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: The sum of a number and 12 times its reciprocal is \(\frac{19}{2}\). What is the smaller number that has this property?
qs.s: Setting \(x + \frac{12}{x} = \frac{19}{2}\) and multiplying by \(2x\) yields \(2x^2 - 19x + 24 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x - 3)(x - 8) = 0\), so \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) or \(x = 8\), making \(\frac{3}{2}\) the smaller number.

qs.q: The length and width of a rectangular photograph are \(2\text{ in}\) by \(3\text{ in}\). How much must be added equally to the length and width to double the area?
qs.s: The equation is \((2 + x)(3 + x) = 2(2 \times 3) = 12\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 5x - 6 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 6)(x - 1) = 0\), so \(x = 1\text{ in}\).

qs.q: The length and width of a rectangular banner are \(6\text{ ft}\) by \(9\text{ ft}\). How much must be added equally to the length and width to double the area?
qs.s: Setting \((6 + x)(9 + x) = 2(6 \times 9) = 108\) gives \(x^2 + 15x - 54 = 0\). Factoring as \((x + 18)(x - 3) = 0\), we find \(x = 3\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: The length and width of a rectangular metal plate are \(10\text{ cm}\) by \(15\text{ cm}\). How much must be added equally to the length and width to double the area?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the amount added to each dimension. Solving \((10 + x)(15 + x) = 2(10 \times 15) = 300\) gives \(x^2 + 25x - 150 = 0\), which factors as \((x + 30)(x - 5) = 0\), so \(x = 5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The length and width of a rectangular rug are \(8\text{ ft}\) by \(12\text{ ft}\). How much must be added equally to the length and width to double the area?
qs.s: Setting \((8 + x)(12 + x) = 2(8 \times 12) = 192\) yields \(x^2 + 20x - 96 = 0\). Factoring as \((x + 24)(x - 4) = 0\) gives the positive solution \(x = 4\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: The length and width of a rectangular garden plot are \(3\text{ m}\) by \(10\text{ m}\). How much must be added equally to the length and width to double the area?
qs.s: Setting \((3 + x)(10 + x) = 2(3 \times 10) = 60\) gives \(x^2 + 13x - 30 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x + 15)(x - 2) = 0\), so \(x = 2\text{ m}\) must be added.

qs.q: The length and width of a rectangular athletic field are \(14\text{ m}\) by \(15\text{ m}\). An equal amount is added to both the length and width to double the area of the field. What is the new perimeter of the field?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the amount added; then \((14 + x)(15 + x) = 2(14 \times 15) = 420\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 29x - 210 = 0\), giving \((x + 35)(x - 6) = 0\) so \(x = 6\text{ m}\). The new dimensions are \(20\text{ m}\) and \(21\text{ m}\), so the new perimeter is \(2(20 + 21) = 82\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular swimming pool measures \(6\text{ m}\) by \(20\text{ m}\). A concrete walkway of uniform width surrounds the pool. If the walkway doubles the total area, what is the width of the walkway?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the width of the walkway; the total area is \((6 + 2x)(20 + 2x) = 2(6 \times 20) = 240\), which simplifies to \(4x^2 + 52x - 120 = 0\), or \(x^2 + 13x - 30 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 15)(x - 2) = 0\), so \(x = 2\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular garden plot measures \(5\text{ m}\) by \(7\text{ m}\). A uniform dirt path is constructed around the entire perimeter of the garden. If the area of the path alone is \(45\text{ m}^2\), what is the width of the path?
qs.s: The total area including the path is \((5 + 2x)(7 + 2x) = (5 \times 7) + 45 = 80\), which simplifies to \(4x^2 + 24x - 45 = 0\). Factoring yields \((2x - 3)(2x + 15) = 0\), so the positive solution is \(x = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular garden measures \(12\text{ m}\) by \(18\text{ m}\). A paved walkway of uniform width is built around the outside of the garden. If the area of the walkway alone is \(136\text{ m}^2\), what is the length of the outer boundary of the walkway (the larger dimension)?
qs.s: The total area is \((12 + 2x)(18 + 2x) = (12 \times 18) + 136 = 352\), which simplifies to \(4x^2 + 60x - 136 = 0\) or \(x^2 + 15x - 34 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 17)(x - 2) = 0\), so \(x = 2\text{ m}\), and the larger outer dimension is \(18 + 2(2) = 22\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Two trains leave a station at the same time on tracks that cross at a right angle. After one hour, they are 130 km apart. If one train travels 70 km/h faster than the other, what is the speed of the slower train?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the speed of the slower train. By the Pythagorean theorem, \(x^2 + (x + 70)^2 = 130^2\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 70x - 6000 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 50)(x + 120) = 0\), so the speed of the slower train is 50 km/h.

qs.q: Two small planes leave an airfield at the same time, flying along perpendicular paths. After one hour, the planes are 250 km apart. If one plane travels 170 km/h faster than the other, what is the speed of the slower plane?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the speed of the slower plane. By the Pythagorean theorem, \(x^2 + (x + 170)^2 = 250^2\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 170x - 16800 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 70)(x + 240) = 0\), so the speed of the slower plane is 70 km/h.

qs.q: Two runners start from the same point at the same time, running in perpendicular directions. After one hour, they are 15 km apart. If one runner runs 3 km/h faster than the other, what is the speed of the slower runner?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the speed of the slower runner. By the Pythagorean theorem, \(x^2 + (x + 3)^2 = 15^2\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 3x - 108 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 9)(x + 12) = 0\), so the slower runner's speed is 9 km/h.

qs.q: Two cars leave an intersection at the same time, traveling on perpendicular roads. After one hour, the cars are 100 km apart. If one car travels 20 km/h faster than the other, what is the speed of the slower car?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the speed of the slower car. By the Pythagorean theorem, \(x^2 + (x + 20)^2 = 100^2\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 20x - 4800 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 60)(x + 80) = 0\), so the speed of the slower car is 60 km/h.

qs.q: Two cargo ships leave a port at the same time, traveling at right angles to each other. After one hour, the ships are 50 km apart. If one ship travels 10 km/h faster than the other, what is the speed of the slower ship?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the speed of the slower ship. Using the Pythagorean theorem, \(x^2 + (x + 10)^2 = 50^2\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 10x - 1200 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 30)(x + 40) = 0\), so the speed of the slower ship is 30 km/h.

qs.q: A boat leaves a dock traveling south. One hour later, a second boat leaves the same dock traveling west at a speed 10 km/h faster than the first boat. Two hours after the second boat departs, the boats are 50 km apart. What is the speed of the first boat?
qs.s: The first boat travels for 3 hours and the second for 2 hours, giving \((3x)^2 + [2(x + 10)]^2 = 50^2\), which simplifies to \(13x^2 + 80x - 2100 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x - 10)(13x + 210) = 0\), so the speed of the first boat is 10 km/h.

qs.q: Two planes depart from an airport at the same time, traveling along perpendicular flight paths. After 1.5 hours, the planes are 750 km apart. If one plane flies 100 km/h faster than the other, what is the speed of the faster plane?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the slower plane's speed; then \((1.5x)^2 + [1.5(x + 100)]^2 = 750^2\), which reduces to \(x^2 + 100x - 120000 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 300)(x + 400) = 0\), so the faster plane's speed is \(300 + 100 = 400\) km/h.

qs.q: A freight train leaves a junction traveling north. Thirty minutes later, a passenger train leaves the same junction traveling west at a speed 55 km/h faster than the freight train. Two hours after the freight train departed, the two trains are 130 km apart. What is the speed of the freight train?
qs.s: The freight train travels for 2 hours and the passenger train for 1.5 hours, giving \((2x)^2 + [1.5(x + 55)]^2 = 130^2\), which simplifies to \(5x^2 + 198x - 8075 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x - 25)(5x + 323) = 0\), so the speed of the freight train is 25 km/h.

qs.q: Two runners leave a park entrance at the same time, running along paths that meet at a right angle. One runner runs 2 km/h faster than the other. After 45 minutes, the straight-line distance between them is 7.5 km. What is the speed of the slower runner?
qs.s: Since 45 minutes is \(\frac{3}{4}\) hour, the distance equation is \((\frac{3}{4}x)^2 + [\frac{3}{4}(x + 2)]^2 = 7.5^2\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 2x - 48 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 6)(x + 8) = 0\), so the speed of the slower runner is 6 km/h.

qs.q: Two planes leave an airport at the same time, one flying due north and the other flying due west. After 2 hours, the planes are 1300 km apart. If the northbound plane travels 130 km/h slower than the westbound plane, how far has the northbound plane traveled?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the speed of the northbound plane; then \((2x)^2 + [2(x + 130)]^2 = 1300^2\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 130x - 202800 = 0\) with positive root \(x = 390\) km/h. Thus, the northbound plane traveled \(390\text{ km/h} \times 2\text{ h} = 780\) km.

qs.q: A kayaker takes 2 hours longer to paddle 16 km up a river than to return 16 km down the river. If the kayaker paddles at 6 km/h in still water, what is the speed of the current?
qs.s: Let \(c\) be the speed of the current. Solving \(\frac{16}{6-c} - \frac{16}{6+c} = 2\) leads to \(c^2 + 16c - 36 = 0\), which factors as \((c+18)(c-2) = 0\), giving \(c = 2\) km/h.

qs.q: A riverboat takes 1 hour longer to go 60 km upstream than to return 60 km downstream. If the riverboat travels at 25 km/h in still water, what is the speed of the current?
qs.s: Let \(c\) be the speed of the current. Solving \(\frac{60}{25-c} - \frac{60}{25+c} = 1\) leads to \(c^2 + 120c - 625 = 0\), which factors as \((c+125)(c-5) = 0\), giving \(c = 5\) km/h.

qs.q: A motorboat takes 1 hour longer to go 15 km up a river than to go down the river. If the motorboat travels at 8 km/h in still water, what is the speed of the current?
qs.s: Let \(c\) be the speed of the current. Solving \(\frac{15}{8-c} - \frac{15}{8+c} = 1\) leads to \(c^2 + 30c - 64 = 0\), which factors as \((c+32)(c-2) = 0\), giving \(c = 2\) km/h.

qs.q: A canoeist takes 1 hour longer to paddle 24 km up a river than to paddle 24 km down the river. If the canoeist paddles at 7 km/h in still water, what is the speed of the current?
qs.s: Let \(c\) be the speed of the current. Solving \(\frac{24}{7-c} - \frac{24}{7+c} = 1\) leads to \(c^2 + 48c - 49 = 0\), which factors as \((c+49)(c-1) = 0\), giving \(c = 1\) km/h.

qs.q: A boat takes 1 hour longer to travel 16 km up a river than to travel 16 km down the river. If the boat's speed in still water is 12 km/h, what is the speed of the current?
qs.s: Let \(c\) be the speed of the current. Solving \(\frac{16}{12-c} - \frac{16}{12+c} = 1\) leads to \(c^2 + 32c - 144 = 0\), which factors as \((c+36)(c-4) = 0\), giving \(c = 4\) km/h.

qs.q: An airplane flies 720 km to a destination with a tailwind and returns 720 km against the same wind. The entire round trip takes 7 hours. If the wind blows at a constant speed of 30 km/h, what is the airspeed of the plane in calm air?
qs.s: Let \(v\) be the plane's airspeed in calm air. Solving \(\frac{720}{v+30} + \frac{720}{v-30} = 7\) yields \(7v^2 - 1440v - 6300 = 0\), which factors as \((v-210)(7v+30) = 0\), giving \(v = 210\) km/h.

qs.q: A motorboat travels 48 km upstream and then returns 48 km downstream. The entire round trip takes 5 hours. If the speed of the river current is 4 km/h, what is the speed of the motorboat in still water?
qs.s: Let \(v\) be the boat's speed in still water. Solving \(\frac{48}{v-4} + \frac{48}{v+4} = 5\) gives \(5v^2 - 96v - 80 = 0\), which factors as \((v-20)(5v+4) = 0\), yielding \(v = 20\) km/h.

qs.q: A boat takes 1 hour and 20 minutes longer to travel 14 km up a river than to return 14 km down the river. If the boat travels at 10 km/h in still water, what is the speed of the current?
qs.s: Converting 1 hr 20 min to \(\frac{4}{3}\) hours, we solve \(\frac{14}{10-c} - \frac{14}{10+c} = \frac{4}{3}\), which simplifies to \(c^2 + 21c - 100 = 0\) and factors as \((c-4)(c+25) = 0\), giving \(c = 4\) km/h.

qs.q: A boat travels 32 km upstream and then 24 km downstream, taking a total of 6 hours for the entire trip. If the river current flows at 2 km/h, what is the speed of the boat in still water?
qs.s: Let \(v\) be the boat's speed in still water. Solving \(\frac{32}{v-2} + \frac{24}{v+2} = 6\) simplifies to \(3v^2 - 28v - 20 = 0\), which factors as \((v-10)(3v+2) = 0\), giving \(v = 10\) km/h.

qs.q: A motorboat takes 45 minutes longer to travel 20 km upstream than to return 20 km downstream. If the boat travels at 13 km/h in still water, what is the speed of the current?
qs.s: Converting 45 minutes to \(\frac{3}{4}\) hour, we solve \(\frac{20}{13-c} - \frac{20}{13+c} = \frac{3}{4}\), which simplifies to \(3c^2 + 160c - 507 = 0\) and factors as \((c-3)(3c+169) = 0\), giving \(c = 3\) km/h.

exercises.name: 3D box surface area and volume problems

qs.q: The total surface area of a square-based box with a height of 8 cm is 210 cm². Find the length of the base of the box.
qs.s: The total surface area equation is \(2x^2 + 4(8)x = 210\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 16x - 105 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 5)(x + 21) = 0\), so the base length is \(5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The total surface area of a square-based box with a height of 10 cm is 312 cm². Find the length of the base of the box.
qs.s: The surface area equation is \(2x^2 + 4(10)x = 312\), which reduces to \(x^2 + 20x - 156 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 6)(x + 26) = 0\), yielding a base length of \(6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The total surface area of a box with a square base and a height of 5 cm is 288 cm². Find the length of the base of the box.
qs.s: The equation for the surface area is \(2x^2 + 4(5)x = 288\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 10x - 144 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 8)(x + 18) = 0\), so the base length is \(8\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The total surface area of a square-based box with a height of 7 cm is 144 cm². Find the length of the base of the box.
qs.s: Setting up the surface area equation gives \(2x^2 + 4(7)x = 144\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 14x - 72 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x - 4)(x + 18) = 0\), so the base length is \(4\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The total surface area of a square-based box with a height of 4 cm is 306 cm². Find the length of the base of the box.
qs.s: The total surface area equation is \(2x^2 + 4(4)x = 306\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 8x - 153 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 9)(x + 17) = 0\), so the base length is \(9\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open-top box with a square base has a height of 10 cm and an outside surface area of 825 cm². Find the volume of the box.
qs.s: For an open-top box, the surface area is \(x^2 + 4(10)x = 825\), which simplifies to \((x - 15)(x + 55) = 0\), giving \(x = 15\text{ cm}\). The volume is then \(V = 15^2 \times 10 = 2250\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage box with a height of 8 m has a length that is 5 m longer than its width. If the volume of the box is 400 m³, find the length of the box.
qs.s: The volume equation is \(8w(w + 5) = 400\), which simplifies to \(w^2 + 5w - 50 = 0\) and factors to \((w - 5)(w + 10) = 0\), giving width \(w = 5\text{ m}\). Thus, the length is \(5 + 5 = 10\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A closed rectangular box has a height of 6 cm. The length of its base is 4 cm greater than its width. If the total surface area of the box is 370 cm², find the width of the base.
qs.s: The surface area is \(2w(w + 4) + 2(6)w + 2(6)(w + 4) = 370\), which simplifies to \(w^2 + 16w - 161 = 0\). Factoring gives \((w - 7)(w + 23) = 0\), so the width of the base is \(7\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open-top storage bin has a rectangular base whose length is twice its width. The height of the bin is 5 m. If the total outside surface area (base and four sides) is 152 m², find the width of the bin.
qs.s: The surface area is \(2w^2 + 2(5)w + 2(5)(2w) = 152\), which reduces to \(w^2 + 15w - 76 = 0\). Factoring gives \((w - 4)(w + 19) = 0\), so the width of the bin is \(4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The height of a closed box with a square base is 3 cm less than the side length of its base. If the total surface area of the box is 480 cm², find the height of the box.
qs.s: The total surface area is \(2x^2 + 4x(x - 3) = 480\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 2x - 80 = 0\) and factors to \((x - 10)(x + 8) = 0\), giving base length \(x = 10\text{ cm}\). Therefore, the height is \(10 - 3 = 7\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Tom takes 3 hours to paint a fence alone, and Huck takes 6 hours to paint the same fence alone. How long does it take them to paint the fence together?
qs.s: Working together, their combined rate is \(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{2}\) of the fence per hour. Solving \(\frac{1}{t} = \frac{1}{2}\) gives \(t = 2\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: David takes 5 hours to detail a car alone, and Sarah takes 3 hours to do the same job alone. How long does it take them to detail the car together?
qs.s: Their combined rate is \(\frac{1}{5} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{8}{15}\) of the job per hour. Solving \(\frac{1}{t} = \frac{8}{15}\) yields \(t = \frac{15}{8}\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: Elena takes 6 hours to tile a kitchen floor alone, and Marco takes 9 hours to tile the same floor alone. How long does it take them to tile the floor together?
qs.s: Their combined rate is \(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{9} = \frac{5}{18}\) of the floor per hour. Solving \(\frac{1}{t} = \frac{5}{18}\) gives \(t = \frac{18}{5}\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: Brian takes 4 hours to clean an office alone, and Kevin takes 12 hours to do the same job alone. How long does it take them to clean the office together?
qs.s: Their combined rate is \(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}\) of the office per hour. Solving \(\frac{1}{t} = \frac{1}{3}\) yields \(t = 3\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: Carlos takes 2 hours to mow a lawn alone, and Julia takes 5 hours to mow the same lawn alone. How long does it take them to mow the lawn together?
qs.s: Their combined rate is \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{5} = \frac{7}{10}\) of the lawn per hour. Solving \(\frac{1}{t} = \frac{7}{10}\) gives \(t = \frac{10}{7}\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: A large pipe can fill a storage tank 8 hours faster than a small pipe. Working together, both pipes can fill the tank in 3 hours. How long does it take the large pipe to fill the tank alone?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the large pipe's time; then \(\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{x+8} = \frac{1}{3}\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 2x - 24 = 0\). Factoring as \((x - 4)(x + 6) = 0\) yields \(x = 4\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: Marcus takes 5 hours longer than Liam to paint a room alone. Working together, they can paint the room in 6 hours. How long does it take Liam to paint the room alone?
qs.s: Letting \(x\) be Liam's time, \(\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{x+5} = \frac{1}{6}\) leads to \(x^2 - 7x - 30 = 0\). Factoring as \((x - 10)(x + 3) = 0\) gives \(x = 10\text{ hours}\) after rejecting the negative root.

qs.q: Working alone, Ken can assemble a playset in 6 hours, Lisa can assemble it in 8 hours, and Mark can assemble it in 12 hours. How long does it take them to assemble the playset working together?
qs.s: The combined rate of all three workers is \(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{9}{24} = \frac{3}{8}\) per hour. Solving \(\frac{1}{t} = \frac{3}{8}\) gives \(t = \frac{8}{3}\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: Priya can write a software program in 6 hours, and Daniel can write the same program in 9 hours. Priya works alone for 2 hours, and then Daniel joins her to finish the program. How many hours do they work together to complete the remaining work?
qs.s: Priya completes \(2\left(\frac{1}{6}\right) = \frac{1}{3}\) of the job alone, leaving \(\frac{2}{3}\). Working together at a rate of \(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{9} = \frac{5}{18}\) per hour, the time needed is \(\frac{2/3}{5/18} = \frac{12}{5}\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: An experienced roofer can shingle a roof in 9 hours, while an apprentice takes 18 hours. After working together for 4 hours, the apprentice leaves, and the experienced roofer finishes the job alone. How many additional hours does it take the experienced roofer to finish the job alone?
qs.s: Working together, their rate is \(\frac{1}{9} + \frac{1}{18} = \frac{1}{6}\), completing \(4\left(\frac{1}{6}\right) = \frac{2}{3}\) of the job in 4 hours. The roofer finishes the remaining \(\frac{1}{3}\) alone at a rate of \(\frac{1}{9}\) per hour in \(\frac{1/3}{1/9} = 3\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: An animal shelter uses 108 m of fencing to enclose two adjacent rectangular runs separated by a shared partition fence. If the total area is 432 m², what is the smaller possible length of the shared partition fence?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the partition length, so \(3x + 2y = 108\) gives \(y = 54 - 1.5x\). The equation \(x(54 - 1.5x) = 432\) simplifies to \(x^2 - 36x + 288 = 0\), factoring into \((x - 12)(x - 24) = 0\), so the smaller possible length is 12 m.

qs.q: A rancher uses 90 m of fencing to enclose two adjacent rectangular corrals that share a common dividing fence. If the total area enclosed is 300 m², what is the larger possible length of the shared dividing fence?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the length of the shared fence, so \(3x + 2y = 90\) gives \(y = 45 - 1.5x\). Substituting into \(x(45 - 1.5x) = 300\) yields \(x^2 - 30x + 200 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 10)(x - 20) = 0\), giving a larger length of 20 m.

qs.q: A community garden uses 150 m of fencing to enclose two adjacent rectangular plots separated by a dividing fence. If the total area of the two plots is 900 m², what is the smaller possible length of the shared dividing fence?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the length of the dividing fence, giving \(3x + 2y = 150\), or \(y = 75 - 1.5x\). Setting up the area equation \(x(75 - 1.5x) = 900\) leads to \(x^2 - 50x + 600 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 20)(x - 30) = 0\), so the smaller possible length is 20 m.

qs.q: A dog daycare facility uses 180 m of fencing to create two adjacent rectangular play areas that share a common fence. If the total enclosed area is 1200 m², what is the larger possible length of the shared fence?
qs.s: Letting \(x\) be the shared fence length, \(3x + 2y = 180\) gives \(y = 90 - 1.5x\). Substituting into \(x(90 - 1.5x) = 1200\) produces \(x^2 - 60x + 800 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 20)(x - 40) = 0\), so the larger possible length is 40 m.

qs.q: A farmer uses 120 m of fencing to build two adjacent identical rectangular pens sharing a common side. If the total enclosed area is 450 m², what is the smaller possible length of the shared dividing fence?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the length of the dividing fence, so \(3x + 2y = 120\) gives \(y = 60 - 1.5x\). The area equation \(x(60 - 1.5x) = 450\) simplifies to \(x^2 - 40x + 300 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 10)(x - 30) = 0\), giving a smaller length of 10 m.

qs.q: A kennel uses 250 m of fencing to enclose four adjacent rectangular dog runs in a row, using three internal dividing fences parallel to the ends. If the total enclosed area of all four runs combined is 1500 m², what is the larger possible length of each dividing fence?
qs.s: Using 5 sections of length \(x\) gives \(5x + 2y = 250\), so \(y = 125 - 2.5x\). The area equation \(x(125 - 2.5x) = 1500\) simplifies to \(x^2 - 50x + 600 = 0\), factoring as \((x - 20)(x - 30) = 0\), which gives a larger length of 30 m.

qs.q: A farmer uses 160 m of fencing to divide a pasture into three adjacent rectangular corrals of equal size by placing two internal dividing fences parallel to the ends. If the total enclosed area is 750 m², what is the larger possible length of each dividing fence?
qs.s: With 4 fences of length \(x\), the total perimeter gives \(4x + 2y = 160\), so \(y = 80 - 2x\). Substituting into \(x(80 - 2x) = 750\) gives \(x^2 - 40x + 375 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 15)(x - 25) = 0\), making the larger length 25 m.

qs.q: A rancher uses 161 m of fencing to construct two adjacent rectangular corrals against a long stone wall, so no fencing is needed along the wall. The shared dividing fence is perpendicular to the wall, and a 4 m opening is left unfenced for a gate along the outer side parallel to the wall. If the total enclosed area is 2100 m², find the shorter possible length of the shared dividing fence.
qs.s: The perimeter relation is \(3x + (y - 4) = 161\), so \(y = 165 - 3x\). Substituting into \(x(165 - 3x) = 2100\) simplifies to \(x^2 - 55x + 700 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 20)(x - 35) = 0\), so the shorter length is 20 m.

qs.q: A ranch uses 220 m of fencing to enclose two adjacent rectangular corrals that share a common dividing fence. If the total area enclosed is 2000 m², what is the larger possible length of the shared fence?
qs.s: The fencing constraint is \(3x + 2y = 220\), so \(y = 110 - 1.5x\). Setting \(x(110 - 1.5x) = 2000\) yields \(3x^2 - 220x + 4000 = 0\), which factors as \((3x - 100)(x - 40) = 0\), giving a larger length of 40 m.

qs.q: A rancher uses 234 m of fencing to enclose two adjacent rectangular corrals that share a common dividing fence. Two 3-meter-wide gate openings along the exterior boundary require no fencing. If the total enclosed area is 2250 m², what is the larger possible length of the shared dividing fence?
qs.s: Accounting for the two gates gives \(3x + 2y - 2(3) = 234\), so \(y = 120 - 1.5x\). The area equation \(x(120 - 1.5x) = 2250\) reduces to \(x^2 - 80x + 1500 = 0\), which factors into \((x - 30)(x - 50) = 0\), giving a larger length of 50 m.

exercises.name: 3D box surface area and volume problems

qs.q: From each corner of a square piece of cardboard, a square with sides of 3 cm is removed. The edges are then turned up to form an open box. If the box is to hold 300 cm³, what is the side length of the original piece of cardboard?
qs.s: The volume of the box is given by \(3(x - 6)^2 = 300\), which simplifies to \((x - 6)^2 = 100\). Solving for the positive length gives \(x - 6 = 10\), so \(x = 16\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: From each corner of a square piece of cardboard, a square with sides of 2 in is cut out. The edges are folded up to create an open box. If the box has a volume of 128 in³, what is the side length of the original piece of cardboard?
qs.s: Setting up the volume equation gives \(2(x - 4)^2 = 128\), so \((x - 4)^2 = 64\). Taking the positive root gives \(x - 4 = 8\), so \(x = 12\text{ in}\).

qs.q: An open box is made by cutting a square with sides of 4 cm from each corner of a square piece of cardboard and turning up the sides. If the box holds 400 cm³, what is the side length of the original piece of cardboard?
qs.s: The volume is given by \(4(x - 8)^2 = 400\), which simplifies to \((x - 8)^2 = 100\). Solving for the positive length yields \(x - 8 = 10\), so \(x = 18\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: From each corner of a square piece of tin, a square with sides of 2 cm is removed. The sides are folded up to form an open box with a volume of 72 cm³. What is the side length of the original piece of tin?
qs.s: The box has volume \(2(x - 4)^2 = 72\), so \((x - 4)^2 = 36\). Since length must be positive, \(x - 4 = 6\), giving \(x = 10\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: From each corner of a square piece of sheet metal, a square with sides of 5 cm is cut out. The sides are folded up to form an open rectangular box. If the volume of the box is 500 cm³, what is the side length of the original piece of sheet metal?
qs.s: The volume equation is \(5(x - 10)^2 = 500\), so \((x - 10)^2 = 100\). Taking the positive square root gives \(x - 10 = 10\), which yields \(x = 20\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open rectangular storage box has a square base and a height of 4 cm. If the total exterior surface area of the box (the base and four sides) is 105 cm², what is the side length of the base?
qs.s: The exterior surface area is \(x^2 + 4(4x) = 105\), which gives \(x^2 + 16x - 105 = 0\). Factoring as \((x + 21)(x - 5) = 0\) yields the positive root \(x = 5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular piece of cardboard is 4 cm longer than it is wide. From each corner, a square with sides of 2 cm is cut out, and the edges are turned up to form an open box. If the volume of the box is 192 cm³, what is the width of the original piece of cardboard?
qs.s: Let the width be \(w\); the base has dimensions \((w - 4)\) and \(w\), so \(2w(w - 4) = 192\), or \(w^2 - 4w - 96 = 0\). Factoring as \((w - 12)(w + 8) = 0\) gives the positive solution \(w = 12\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A closed rectangular box with a square base has a height of 6 cm. If the total surface area of the box is 128 cm², what is the side length of its base?
qs.s: The total surface area of the closed box is \(2x^2 + 4(6x) = 128\), which reduces to \(x^2 + 12x - 64 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 16)(x - 4) = 0\), so the positive side length is \(x = 4\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular piece of cardboard is 6 cm longer than it is wide. A square with sides of 2 cm is cut from each corner, and the edges are turned up to form an open box. If the box has a volume of 320 cm³, find the length of the original piece of cardboard.
qs.s: Let the width be \(w\); the volume is \(2(w - 4)(w + 2) = 320\), which simplifies to \(w^2 - 2w - 168 = 0\), giving \((w - 14)(w + 12) = 0\) so \(w = 14\text{ cm}\). The original length is \(w + 6 = 20\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular sheet of metal is twice as long as it is wide. Squares with sides of 3 cm are removed from each corner, and the sides are folded up to make an open box. If the box has a volume of 324 cm³, what is the width of the original sheet of metal?
qs.s: Let the width be \(w\); the volume is \(3(w - 6)(2w - 6) = 324\), which simplifies to \((w - 6)(w - 3) = 54\) or \(w^2 - 9w - 36 = 0\). Factoring \((w - 12)(w + 3) = 0\) yields \(w = 12\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular plot of land has an area of 126 m². If the width is increased by 1 m and the length is decreased by 3 m, the area stays the same. Find the original width of the plot.
qs.s: The equation \((w+1)(l-3) = 126\) simplifies to \(l = 3w + 3\). Substituting into \(lw = 126\) gives \(w^2 + w - 42 = 0\), which factors as \((w+7)(w-6) = 0\), so the original width is \(6\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular swimming pool has an area of 200 m². If the width is increased by 2 m and the length is decreased by 5 m, the area remains the same. Find the original length of the pool.
qs.s: The relation \((w+2)(l-5) = 200\) simplifies to \(2l - 5w = 10\), so \(l = \frac{5w+10}{2}\). Substituting into \(lw = 200\) gives \(w^2 + 2w - 80 = 0\), which yields \(w = 8\text{ m}\) and an original length of \(l = 200 / 8 = 25\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular garden has an area of 60 m². If the width is increased by 1 m and the length is decreased by 2 m, the area stays the same. Find the original length of the garden.
qs.s: Let \(w\) and \(l\) be the original width and length; then \((w+1)(l-2) = 60\) simplifies to \(l = 2w + 2\). Substituting this into \(lw = 60\) yields \(w^2 + w - 30 = 0\), which factors to give \(w = 5\text{ m}\) and length \(l = 60 / 5 = 12\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular patio has an area of 96 m². If the width is increased by 2 m and the length is decreased by 4 m, the area remains unchanged. Find the original width of the patio.
qs.s: From \((w+2)(l-4) = 96\), we obtain \(l = 2w + 4\). Substituting into \(lw = 96\) gives \(w^2 + 2w - 48 = 0\), which factors as \((w+8)(w-6) = 0\), giving an original width of \(w = 6\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular billboard has an area of 108 m². If the width is increased by 3 m and the length is decreased by 3 m, the area stays the same. Find the original length of the billboard.
qs.s: Expanding \((w+3)(l-3) = 108\) gives \(l = w + 3\). Substituting into \(lw = 108\) yields \(w^2 + 3w - 108 = 0\), which factors as \((w+12)(w-9) = 0\), so \(w = 9\text{ m}\) and the original length is \(l = 9 + 3 = 12\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular workshop has an area of 130 m². If its width is increased by 3 m and its length is decreased by 2 m, the area increases by 13 m². Find the perimeter of the original workshop.
qs.s: The equation \((w+3)(l-2) = 143\) simplifies to \(3l - 2w = 19\), so \(l = \frac{2w+19}{3}\). Substituting into \(lw = 130\) produces \(2w^2 + 19w - 390 = 0\), which factors as \((2w+39)(w-10)=0\), giving \(w = 10\text{ m}\), \(l = 13\text{ m}\), and perimeter \(2(10 + 13) = 46\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular park has an area of 180 m². If the width is increased by 4 m and the length is decreased by 3 m, the area increases by 30 m². Find the original length of the park.
qs.s: Expanding \((w+4)(l-3) = 210\) with \(lw = 180\) gives \(4l - 3w = 42\), so \(l = \frac{3w+42}{4}\). Substituting into \(lw = 180\) yields \(w^2 + 14w - 240 = 0\), which factors to \((w+24)(w-10)=0\), giving \(w = 10\text{ m}\) and original length \(l = 18\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular sports field has an area of 360 m². If the width is increased by 5 m and the length is decreased by 4 m, the area increases by 40 m². Find the original length of the field.
qs.s: Expanding \((w+5)(l-4) = 400\) gives \(5l - 4w = 60\), so \(l = \frac{4w+60}{5}\). Substituting into \(lw = 360\) yields \(w^2 + 15w - 450 = 0\), factoring as \((w+30)(w-15)=0\), giving \(w = 15\text{ m}\) and original length \(l = 360 / 15 = 24\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular courtyard has an area of 90 m². If its width is increased by 1 m and its length is decreased by 2 m, its area increases by 1 m². Find the original width of the courtyard.
qs.s: The relation \((w+1)(l-2) = 91\) simplifies to \(l = 2w + 3\). Substituting into \(lw = 90\) yields the quadratic \(2w^2 + 3w - 90 = 0\), which factors as \((2w+15)(w-6)=0\), giving an original width of \(w = 6\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage room has an area of 66 m². If the width is increased by 2 m and the length is decreased by 3 m, the area decreases by 2 m². Find the perimeter of the original room.
qs.s: From \((w+2)(l-3) = 64\), we get \(2l - 3w = 4\), so \(l = \frac{3w+4}{2}\); substituting into \(lw = 66\) produces \(3w^2 + 4w - 132 = 0\), which yields \(w = 6\text{ m}\) and \(l = 11\text{ m}\). Thus, the original perimeter is \(2(11 + 6) = 34\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Carlos travels 180 km by car. If he reduces his speed by 15 km/h, the journey takes 1 hour longer. What was his original speed?
qs.s: The equation is \(\frac{180}{v - 15} - \frac{180}{v} = 1\), which simplifies to \(v^2 - 15v - 2700 = 0\). Factoring gives \((v - 60)(v + 45) = 0\), so \(v = 60\) km/h.

qs.q: Maya drives 240 km. If she increases her speed by 20 km/h, the trip takes 1 hour less. Find Maya's original speed.
qs.s: The equation is \(\frac{240}{v} - \frac{240}{v + 20} = 1\), which simplifies to \(v^2 + 20v - 4800 = 0\). Factoring gives \((v + 80)(v - 60) = 0\), so \(v = 60\) km/h.

qs.q: A tour bus travels 360 km. If the driver increases the speed by 15 km/h, the journey takes 2 hours less. Find the original speed of the bus.
qs.s: Setting up the equation \(\frac{360}{v} - \frac{360}{v + 15} = 2\) leads to \(v^2 + 15v - 2700 = 0\). Factoring gives \((v + 60)(v - 45) = 0\), so \(v = 45\) km/h.

qs.q: A cyclist travels 120 km. If she increases her average speed by 10 km/h, the ride takes 1 hour less. Find her original speed.
qs.s: The equation is \(\frac{120}{v} - \frac{120}{v + 10} = 1\), which simplifies to \(v^2 + 10v - 1200 = 0\). Factoring yields \((v + 40)(v - 30) = 0\), so \(v = 30\) km/h.

qs.q: A delivery truck travels 400 km. If the driver increases the speed by 10 km/h, the trip takes 2 hours less. What was the truck's original speed?
qs.s: Setting up the time difference gives \(\frac{400}{v} - \frac{400}{v + 10} = 2\), which simplifies to \(v^2 + 10v - 2000 = 0\). Factoring gives \((v + 50)(v - 40) = 0\), so \(v = 40\) km/h.

qs.q: Sophia drove 225 km to visit a client. On her return trip along the same route, she decreased her speed by 15 km/h, causing the trip to take 45 minutes longer. What was her speed on the way to the client?
qs.s: Converting 45 minutes to \(\frac{3}{4}\) hour gives \(\frac{225}{v - 15} - \frac{225}{v} = \frac{3}{4}\), which simplifies to \(v^2 - 15v - 4500 = 0\). Factoring gives \((v - 75)(v + 60) = 0\), so her original speed was 75 km/h.

qs.q: An airplane flies 1500 km at a constant speed. If the pilot increases the average speed by 100 km/h, the flight takes 30 minutes less. What was the airplane's original speed?
qs.s: Convert 30 minutes to \(\frac{1}{2}\) hour to get \(\frac{1500}{v} - \frac{1500}{v + 100} = \frac{1}{2}\), which simplifies to \(v^2 + 100v - 300000 = 0\). Factoring gives \((v + 600)(v - 500) = 0\), so \(v = 500\) km/h.

qs.q: A motorist drives 120 km to a conference. On the return trip along the same route, she increases her speed by 20 km/h. If the total driving time for the round trip is 5 hours, what was her speed on the trip to the conference?
qs.s: Set up the total time equation \(\frac{120}{v} + \frac{120}{v + 20} = 5\), which simplifies to \(v^2 - 28v - 480 = 0\). Factoring gives \((v - 40)(v + 12) = 0\), so the speed on the outbound trip was 40 km/h.

qs.q: A driver travels a total of 270 km. She drives the first 120 km at a constant speed and then increases her speed by 15 km/h for the remaining 150 km. If the entire trip takes 4 hours, what was her initial speed?
qs.s: The total time equation is \(\frac{120}{v} + \frac{150}{v + 15} = 4\), which simplifies to \(2v^2 - 105v - 900 = 0\). Factoring yields \((2v + 15)(v - 60) = 0\), giving an initial speed of 60 km/h.

qs.q: An express train travels 280 km. If its speed is increased by 10 km/h, the trip takes 30 minutes less. How many hours did the trip take at the original speed?
qs.s: From \(\frac{280}{v} - \frac{280}{v + 10} = \frac{1}{2}\), we obtain \(v^2 + 10v - 5600 = 0\), giving \(v = 70\) km/h. The original time taken was \(\frac{280}{70} = 4\) hours.

qs.q: A circular pond is surrounded by a wooden deck of uniform width. The radius of the entire structure including the deck is \(11\text{ m}\), and the area of the deck is \(85\pi\text{ m}^2\). Find the width of the deck.
qs.s: The deck's area equation is \(\pi[11^2 - (11 - w)^2] = 85\pi\), which simplifies to \(w^2 - 22w + 85 = 0\). Factoring gives \((w - 5)(w - 17) = 0\), so the width must be \(5\text{ m}\) as \(w < 11\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A circular flower garden is surrounded by a gravel path of uniform width. The radius of the entire garden area, including the path, is \(9\text{ m}\). If the area of the path is \(45\pi\text{ m}^2\), find the width of the path.
qs.s: The equation for the path's area is \(\pi[9^2 - (9 - w)^2] = 45\pi\), which simplifies to \(w^2 - 18w + 45 = 0\). Factoring yields \((w - 3)(w - 15) = 0\), so \(w = 3\text{ m}\) because the width cannot exceed the total radius of \(9\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A circular swimming pool is surrounded by a tiled walkway of uniform width. If the radius of the entire pool area including the walkway is \(10\text{ m}\) and the area of the walkway is \(64\pi\text{ m}^2\), find the width of the walkway.
qs.s: Let \(w\) be the width of the walkway; the area equation is \(\pi[10^2 - (10 - w)^2] = 64\pi\), which simplifies to \(w^2 - 20w + 64 = 0\). Factoring gives \((w - 4)(w - 16) = 0\), and since \(w < 10\text{ m}\), the width is \(4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A circular fountain is surrounded by a decorative stone border of uniform width. The radius of the entire installation, including the border, is \(7\text{ m}\). If the area of the stone border is \(13\pi\text{ m}^2\), find the width of the border.
qs.s: The border area is \(\pi[7^2 - (7 - w)^2] = 13\pi\), simplifying to \(w^2 - 14w + 13 = 0\). Factoring gives \((w - 1)(w - 13) = 0\), and rejecting \(w = 13\text{ m}\) (since \(w < 7\text{ m}\)) leaves \(w = 1\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A circular patio with a radius of \(5\text{ m}\) is surrounded by a grass border of uniform width. If the area of the grass border is \(24\pi\text{ m}^2\), find the width of the border.
qs.s: With an inner radius of \(5\text{ m}\), the border area is \(\pi[(5 + w)^2 - 5^2] = 24\pi\), which simplifies to \(w^2 + 10w - 24 = 0\). Factoring gives \((w - 2)(w + 12) = 0\), and rejecting the negative root gives \(w = 2\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A circular wading pool has a diameter of \(24\text{ m}\) and is surrounded by a concrete deck of uniform width. If the area of the deck is \(\frac{9}{16}\) of the area of the pool, find the width of the deck.
qs.s: The radius of the pool is \(12\text{ m}\) and its area is \(144\pi\text{ m}^2\), so the deck area is \(\frac{9}{16}(144\pi) = 81\pi\text{ m}^2\). Solving \(\pi[(12 + w)^2 - 12^2] = 81\pi\) gives \(w^2 + 24w - 81 = 0\), which factors as \((w - 3)(w + 27) = 0\), yielding \(w = 3\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A circular running track of uniform width surrounds a grass sports field. The diameter of the entire facility, including the field and the track, is \(60\text{ m}\). If the track has an area of \(275\pi\text{ m}^2\), find the width of the track.
qs.s: The outer radius is \(60 / 2 = 30\text{ m}\), so the track area is \(\pi[30^2 - (30 - w)^2] = 275\pi\), giving \(w^2 - 60w + 275 = 0\). Factoring gives \((w - 5)(w - 55) = 0\), and since \(w < 30\text{ m}\), the width is \(5\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A circular skating rink is surrounded by a rubber safety border of uniform width. The radius of the entire rink including the border is \(8\text{ m}\), and the area of the border is \(21.75\pi\text{ m}^2\). Find the width of the border.
qs.s: The area equation is \(\pi[8^2 - (8 - w)^2] = 21.75\pi\), leading to \(w^2 - 16w + 21.75 = 0\) or \(4w^2 - 64w + 87 = 0\). Factoring as \((2w - 3)(2w - 29) = 0\) gives \(w = 1.5\text{ m}\) (rejecting \(w = 14.5\text{ m}\) since \(w < 8\text{ m}\)).

qs.q: A circular plaza has a diameter of \(20\text{ m}\) and is surrounded by a decorative brick border of uniform width. If the area of the brick border is \(56.25\pi\text{ m}^2\), find the width of the border.
qs.s: The plaza radius is \(10\text{ m}\), so \(\pi[(10 + w)^2 - 10^2] = 56.25\pi\) simplifies to \(4w^2 + 80w - 225 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2w - 5)(2w + 45) = 0\), which gives \(w = 2.5\text{ m}\) after rejecting the negative root.

qs.q: A circular pond has a radius of \(12\text{ m}\) and is surrounded by a stone pathway of uniform width. If the area of the pathway is \(\frac{7}{9}\) of the area of the pond, find the width of the pathway.
qs.s: The pond area is \(\pi(12^2) = 144\pi\text{ m}^2\), so the pathway area is \(\frac{7}{9}(144\pi) = 112\pi\text{ m}^2\). Setting \(\pi[(12 + w)^2 - 12^2] = 112\pi\) yields \(w^2 + 24w - 112 = 0\), which factors as \((w - 4)(w + 28) = 0\), giving \(w = 4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A mason and his apprentice can build a stone retaining wall in 10 hours. Working alone, the mason can build the wall in 15 hours. How long would it take the apprentice to build the wall alone?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the time in hours for the apprentice alone. Solving \(\frac{1}{15} + \frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{10}\) gives \(\frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{10} - \frac{1}{15} = \frac{1}{30}\), so \(x = 30\) hours.

qs.q: A gardener and his assistant can prune all the trees in an orchard in 3 days. Working alone, the gardener can prune the orchard in 4 days. How many days would it take the assistant to do the job alone?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the number of days for the assistant alone. From \(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{3}\), we get \(\frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{12}\), so \(x = 12\) days.

qs.q: An experienced painter and an apprentice can paint a room in 6 hours. Working alone, the painter can do the job in 10 hours. How long would it take the apprentice to paint the room alone?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the time in hours for the apprentice to paint the room alone. Setting up the equation \(\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{6}\), we subtract to get \(\frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{10} = \frac{1}{15}\), so \(x = 15\) hours.

qs.q: Two printing machines working together can complete a print run in 6 minutes. The newer machine can complete the run alone in 9 minutes. How long would it take the older machine to complete the print run alone?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the time in minutes for the older machine alone. From \(\frac{1}{9} + \frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{6}\), we have \(\frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{9} = \frac{1}{18}\), so \(x = 18\) minutes.

qs.q: Two inlet pipes can fill a water tank in 8 hours when open together. The first pipe alone can fill the tank in 12 hours. How long would it take the second pipe to fill the tank alone?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the time in hours for the second pipe alone. Solving \(\frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{8}\) gives \(\frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{8} - \frac{1}{12} = \frac{1}{24}\), which means \(x = 24\) hours.

qs.q: Rita can paint a fence alone in 10 hours, and Sam can paint it alone in 15 hours. Rita begins the job alone and works for 5 hours, after which Sam joins her to help. How many hours do Rita and Sam work together to finish painting the fence?
qs.s: In 5 hours, Rita completes \(5 \times \frac{1}{10} = \frac{1}{2}\) of the fence, leaving \(\frac{1}{2}\) unfinished. Together their combined rate is \(\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{15} = \frac{1}{6}\) per hour, so they finish the remaining half in \(\frac{1/2}{1/6} = 3\) hours.

qs.q: Working alone, an experienced roofer can shingle a roof in 9 hours less time than an apprentice. When they work together, they can shingle the roof in 6 hours. How many hours would it take the apprentice to shingle the roof working alone?
qs.s: Let \(t\) be the apprentice's alone time; then the roofer takes \(t - 9\) hours. Solving \(\frac{1}{t-9} + \frac{1}{t} = \frac{1}{6}\) yields \(t^2 - 21t + 54 = 0\), which factors as \((t - 18)(t - 3) = 0\), so \(t = 18\) hours because \(t > 9\).

qs.q: A standard pump takes 5 hours longer to drain a reservoir than a high-capacity pump. When both pumps operate together, they can drain the reservoir in 6 hours. How many hours would it take the high-capacity pump to drain the reservoir alone?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the time for the high-capacity pump alone; then the standard pump takes \(x + 5\) hours. Solving \(\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{x+5} = \frac{1}{6}\) leads to \(x^2 - 7x - 30 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 10)(x + 3) = 0\), giving \(x = 10\) hours.

qs.q: Working alone, a master technician takes 3 hours less than an apprentice to overhaul an engine. Working together, they can finish the overhaul in 2 hours. How many hours does it take the master technician to overhaul the engine alone?
qs.s: Let \(m\) be the master technician's alone time; then the apprentice takes \(m + 3\) hours. The equation \(\frac{1}{m} + \frac{1}{m+3} = \frac{1}{2}\) simplifies to \(m^2 - m - 6 = 0\), which factors as \((m - 3)(m + 2) = 0\), giving \(m = 3\) hours.

qs.q: Three pipes, A, B, and C, can fill a cistern in 2 hours when working together. Working alone, pipe A can fill it in 4 hours, and pipe B can fill it in 6 hours. How many hours would it take pipe C to fill the cistern working alone?
qs.s: The combined rate equation is \(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{2}\). Solving for \(x\) gives \(\frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{12}\), so \(x = 12\) hours.

qs.q: A river has a current of 1 km/h. Maya paddles her canoe 12 km downstream and then heads back upstream to her starting point. If the round trip takes 5 hours, what is Maya's paddling speed in still water?
qs.s: Setting up \(\frac{12}{v+1} + \frac{12}{v-1} = 5\) simplifies to \(5v^2 - 24v - 5 = 0\). Factoring as \((5v + 1)(v - 5) = 0\) gives a paddling speed of 5 km/h in still water.

qs.q: The current of a river is 2 km/h. A kayaker travels downstream a distance of 15 km and then returns upstream to the starting point. If the total trip took 4 hours, what is the kayaker's paddling rate in still water?
qs.s: Setting up the equation \(\frac{15}{v+2} + \frac{15}{v-2} = 4\) simplifies to \(2v^2 - 15v - 8 = 0\). Factoring as \((2v + 1)(v - 8) = 0\) gives a rate of 8 km/h in still water.

qs.q: The current of a stream flows at 2 km/h. Liam rows a boat 24 km downstream and then paddles back upstream to his starting dock. If the entire trip takes 5 hours, what is Liam's rowing rate in still water?
qs.s: The equation \(\frac{24}{v+2} + \frac{24}{v-2} = 5\) simplifies to \(5v^2 - 48v - 20 = 0\). Factoring as \((5v + 2)(v - 10) = 0\) gives a still-water speed of 10 km/h.

qs.q: The rate of a river's current is 2 km/h. A motorboat travels 8 km downstream and then returns upstream to where it started. If the total trip took 3 hours, what is the boat's speed in still water?
qs.s: Setting up the time equation \(\frac{8}{v+2} + \frac{8}{v-2} = 3\) simplifies to \(3v^2 - 16v - 12 = 0\). Factoring as \((3v + 2)(v - 6) = 0\) gives a still-water speed of 6 km/h.

qs.q: The speed of a river current is 3 km/h. A canoeist paddles 20 km downstream and then returns upstream to the starting point. If the entire journey takes 7 hours, what is the canoeist's paddling rate in still water?
qs.s: Setting up \(\frac{20}{v+3} + \frac{20}{v-3} = 7\) yields \(7v^2 - 40v - 63 = 0\). Factoring as \((7v + 9)(v - 7) = 0\) gives 7 km/h in still water.

qs.q: An airplane flies 400 km with a tailwind of 20 km/h and then returns the same 400 km against the headwind. If the round trip takes 4 hours and 30 minutes, what is the plane's speed in still air?
qs.s: Convert 4 hours 30 minutes to \(\frac{9}{2}\) hours, giving \(\frac{400}{v+20} + \frac{400}{v-20} = \frac{9}{2}\). This simplifies to \(9v^2 - 1600v - 3600 = 0\), which factors as \((9v + 20)(v - 180) = 0\), yielding 180 km/h.

qs.q: A kayaker paddles 36 km downstream on a river with a current of 3 km/h. She then turns around and paddles 12 km back upstream to reach a campsite. If the total paddling time is 5 hours, what is her paddling speed in still water?
qs.s: Set up the equation \(\frac{36}{v+3} + \frac{12}{v-3} = 5\), which simplifies to \(5v^2 - 48v + 27 = 0\). Factoring as \((v - 9)(5v - 3) = 0\) and noting \(v > 3\) gives a speed of 9 km/h.

qs.q: The current in a river flows at 5 km/h. A motorboat travels 25 km downstream and then returns 25 km upstream to its starting dock. If the total trip took 3 hours and 45 minutes, what is the speed of the motorboat in still water?
qs.s: Convert 3 hours 45 minutes to \(\frac{15}{4}\) hours, so \(\frac{25}{v+5} + \frac{25}{v-5} = \frac{15}{4}\). This simplifies to \(3v^2 - 40v - 75 = 0\), which factors as \((3v + 5)(v - 15) = 0\), giving 15 km/h.

qs.q: A tour boat travels 40 km downstream on a river with a current of 6 km/h, and then returns 40 km upstream to its starting point. If the entire round trip takes 5 hours, what was the boat's speed while traveling downstream?
qs.s: The equation \(\frac{40}{v+6} + \frac{40}{v-6} = 5\) simplifies to \(v^2 - 16v - 36 = 0\), giving a still-water speed of \(v = 18\) km/h. Thus, the downstream speed is \(18 + 6 = 24\) km/h.

qs.q: A motorboat's speed in still water is 15 km/h. It travels 36 km upstream and returns 36 km downstream. If the return trip downstream takes 1 hour less than the upstream trip, what is the speed of the current?
qs.s: Setting up the time difference gives \(\frac{36}{15-c} - \frac{36}{15+c} = 1\), which simplifies to \(c^2 + 72c - 225 = 0\). Factoring as \((c+75)(c-3) = 0\) gives a current speed of 3 km/h.

qs.q: A rectangular garden is 5 m wide and 9 m long. A paved path of uniform width is constructed around the outer edge of the garden. If the area of the path is 120 m², what is the width of the path?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the width of the path. The equation is \((2x + 5)(2x + 9) - 45 = 120\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 7x - 30 = 0\); factoring gives \((x - 3)(x + 10) = 0\), so the path is 3 m wide.

qs.q: A rectangular swimming pool measures 6 m by 10 m. A concrete walkway of uniform width is built around the perimeter of the pool. If the area of the walkway is 80 m², how wide is the walkway?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the width of the walkway. The equation is \((2x + 6)(2x + 10) - 60 = 80\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 8x - 20 = 0\); factoring gives \((x - 2)(x + 10) = 0\), so the walkway is 2 m wide.

qs.q: A rectangular wooden deck measures 6 m by 8 m. A brick patio of uniform width is built completely around the deck. If the area of the brick patio is 240 m², what is the width of the patio?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the width of the patio. The equation is \((2x + 6)(2x + 8) - 48 = 240\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 7x - 60 = 0\); factoring gives \((x - 5)(x + 12) = 0\), so the patio is 5 m wide.

qs.q: A rectangular photograph measuring 9 cm by 13 cm is surrounded by a matting border of uniform width. If the area of the matting border is 48 cm², what is the width of the border?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the width of the border. The equation is \((2x + 9)(2x + 13) - 117 = 48\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 11x - 12 = 0\); factoring gives \((x - 1)(x + 12) = 0\), so the border is 1 cm wide.

qs.q: A landscaper surrounds a 7 m by 11 m rectangular lawn with a gravel border of uniform width. If the area of the gravel border is 208 m², how wide is the border?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the width of the border. The equation is \((2x + 7)(2x + 11) - 77 = 208\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 9x - 52 = 0\); factoring gives \((x - 4)(x + 13) = 0\), so the border is 4 m wide.

qs.q: A rectangular swimming pool measures 10 m by 20 m. A homeowner hires a contractor to build a concrete patio of uniform width around the pool. The contractor charges $40 per square meter of concrete, and the total cost for the patio is $7000. What is the width of the patio?
qs.s: The patio area is \(7000 / 40 = 175\) m². The equation \((2x + 10)(2x + 20) - 200 = 175\) simplifies to \(4x^2 + 60x - 175 = 0\); factoring gives \((2x - 5)(2x + 35) = 0\), so \(x = 2.5\) m.

qs.q: A rectangular community park measures 40 m by 60 m. A walking path of uniform width is constructed along the inside perimeter of the park, leaving a central grass area of 1836 m². What is the width of the walking path?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the width of the path. The equation for the inner dimensions is \((40 - 2x)(60 - 2x) = 1836\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 50x + 141 = 0\); factoring gives \((x - 3)(x - 47) = 0\), and rejecting the extraneous root yields 3 m.

qs.q: A rectangular sports field measures 15 m by 25 m. A gravel safety border of uniform width is built around the outside of the field. If the area of the border is 129 m², what is the width of the border?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the border width. The equation is \((2x + 15)(2x + 25) - 375 = 129\), which simplifies to \(4x^2 + 80x - 129 = 0\); factoring gives \((2x - 3)(2x + 43) = 0\), so \(x = 1.5\) m.

qs.q: A rectangular park lawn measures 30 m by 40 m. Two perpendicular paved walkways of uniform width cross through the center of the lawn, one parallel to the length and one parallel to the width. If the remaining grass area is 936 m², what is the width of the walkways?
qs.s: Pushing the four grass sections together gives a rectangle of dimensions \((30 - x)\) by \((40 - x)\). Setting \((30 - x)(40 - x) = 936\) simplifies to \(x^2 - 70x + 264 = 0\), which factors into \((x - 4)(x - 66) = 0\), yielding a width of 4 m.

qs.q: A rectangular patio is 8 m wide and 12 m long, and one of its 12 m sides is flush against the back wall of a house. A flower border of uniform width is planted along the other three sides. If the area of the flower border is 64 m², what is the width of the border?
qs.s: Because the border is only along three sides, the new dimensions are \((12 + 2x)\) and \((8 + x)\). The equation \((12 + 2x)(8 + x) - 96 = 64\) simplifies to \(x^2 + 14x - 32 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 2)(x + 16) = 0\), giving a width of 2 m.

qs.q: A rectangular swimming pool measures 10 m by 20 m. A concrete deck of uniform width is built around the outside of the pool. If the area of the deck alone is 136 m², what is the width of the deck?
qs.s: The total area of the pool and deck combined is \(10 \times 20 + 136 = 336\text{ m}^2\). Solving \((10 + 2x)(20 + 2x) = 336\) simplifies to \(x^2 + 15x - 34 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 2)(x + 17) = 0\), so the width of the deck is \(2\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A groundskeeper wants to mow two-thirds of a rectangular athletic field measuring 60 m by 90 m by mowing a strip of uniform width around the outside of the field. How wide of a strip must be mowed?
qs.s: The unmowed center has an area of \(\frac{1}{3} \times (60 \times 90) = 1800\text{ m}^2\). Setting \((60 - 2x)(90 - 2x) = 1800\) simplifies to \(x^2 - 75x + 900 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 15)(x - 60) = 0\), giving a width of \(15\text{ m}\) (since \(x < 30\)).

qs.q: A sports field measures 80 m by 100 m. A groundskeeper wants to mow two-fifths of the field by mowing a strip of uniform width around the outside edge. How wide should the strip be?
qs.s: Mowing two-fifths leaves three-fifths of the field unmowed, so the inner area is \(\frac{3}{5} \times (80 \times 100) = 4800\text{ m}^2\). Solving \((80 - 2x)(100 - 2x) = 4800\) simplifies to \(x^2 - 90x + 800 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 10)(x - 80) = 0\), giving a width of \(10\text{ m}\) (since \(x < 40\)).
