qs.s: Expanding and substituting gives \(3x + 2(x^2 - 4x + 4) - 7 = 4\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 - 5x - 3 = 0\) with solutions \(x = 3\) and \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\). For the larger \(x\)-value, \(x = 3\), substituting into the linear equation gives \(y = 4 - 3(3) = -5\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 - 6x + 1\)
\(2x - y = -4\)
qs.s: Substituting \(y = 2x + 4\) into the quadratic equation gives \(2x + 4 = x^2 - 6x + 1\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 8x - 3 = 0\). By the quadratic formula, \(x = \frac{8 \pm \sqrt{76}}{2} = 4 \pm \sqrt{19}\), so the greater solution is \(4 + \sqrt{19}\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value of the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 + 4x - 3\)
\(x - y = -7\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = x + 7\) into the quadratic equation to get \(x + 7 = x^2 + 4x - 3\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 3x - 10 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 5)(x - 2) = 0\), so \(x = -5\) or \(x = 2\), and the greater value is \(2\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value of the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 - 5x + 2\)
\(x - y = 3\)
qs.s: Rewrite the second equation as \(y = x - 3\) and substitute it into the first equation to obtain \(x - 3 = x^2 - 5x + 2\), which gives \(x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 1)(x - 5) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = 1\) and \(x = 5\), the greater of which is \(5\).

qs.q:
Find the smaller \(x\)-value of the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 + 2\)
\(x - y = -4\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = x + 4\) into the quadratic equation to get \(x + 4 = x^2 + 2\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - x - 2 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 2)(x + 1) = 0\), so the \(x\)-values are \(2\) and \(-1\), and the smaller value is \(-1\).

qs.q:
Find the smaller \(x\)-value of the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 + x - 7\)
\(2x - y = -5\)
qs.s: Rearrange the linear equation to \(y = 2x + 5\) and substitute into the quadratic equation to get \(2x + 5 = x^2 + x - 7\), or \(x^2 - x - 12 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x - 4)(x + 3) = 0\), so \(x = 4\) or \(x = -3\), and the smaller value is \(-3\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value of the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 + 4x - 4\)
\(x + y = 2\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2 - x\) into the quadratic equation to obtain \(2 - x = x^2 + 4x - 4\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 5x - 6 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 6)(x - 1) = 0\), yielding solutions \(x = -6\) and \(x = 1\), where the greater value is \(1\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value of the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(2x^2 - 2x - y = 8\)
\(3x - y = 5\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 3x - 5\) into the first equation to get \(2x^2 - 2x - (3x - 5) = 8\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 - 5x - 3 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x + 1)(x - 3) = 0\), so \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) or \(x = 3\), and the greater value is \(3\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value of the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = 2x^2 - 3x - 1\)
\(x - y = -3\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = x + 3\) into the quadratic equation to get \(x + 3 = 2x^2 - 3x - 1\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 - 4x - 4 = 0\), or \(x^2 - 2x - 2 = 0\). Applying the quadratic formula yields \(x = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{12}}{2} = 1 \pm \sqrt{3}\), so the greater value is \(1 + \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is the real solution to the system of equations with \(x > 0\), what is the value of \(y\)?
\(y = \frac{1}{3}x^2 + x - 2\)
\(2x - 3y = -6\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(3\) to get \(3y = x^2 + 3x - 6\), then substitute into \(2x - 3y = -6\) to get \(x^2 + x - 12 = 0\), giving \((x + 4)(x - 3) = 0\). Since \(x > 0\), we have \(x = 3\), and substituting into the linear equation yields \(2(3) - 3y = -6\), so \(y = 4\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value of the real solutions to the system of equations:
\((x - 1)(x + 4) - y = 14\)
\(5x - y = -6\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 5x + 6\) into the first equation to obtain \((x^2 + 3x - 4) - (5x + 6) = 14\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 2x - 24 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 6)(x + 4) = 0\), yielding \(x = 6\) or \(x = -4\), so the greater value is \(6\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(y\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = -(x - 2)^2 + 7\)
\(x + y = 7\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 7 - x\) into the first equation to get \(7 - x = -(x^2 - 4x + 4) + 7\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0\), giving \(x = 1\) or \(x = 4\). Substituting these into \(y = 7 - x\) gives solutions \((1, 6)\) and \((4, 3)\), so the greater \(y\)-value is \(6\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:

\(xy = 8\)
\(y = 2x - 6\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x - 6\) into \(xy = 8\) to obtain \(x(2x - 6) = 8\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 - 6x - 8 = 0\), or \(x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x + 1) = 0\), so the solutions for \(x\) are \(4\) and \(-1\), of which \(4\) is the greater value.

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:

\(xy = 20\)
\(y = 2x - 6\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x - 6\) into \(xy = 20\) to get \(2x^2 - 6x - 20 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 3x - 10 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 5)(x + 2) = 0\), so the roots are \(x = 5\) and \(x = -2\), and the greater value is \(5\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations:

\(xy = 18\)
\(y = 3x + 3\)

with \(x > 0\), what is the value of \(y\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 3x + 3\) into \(xy = 18\) to get \(3x^2 + 3x - 18 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + x - 6 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 3)(x - 2) = 0\), so the positive \(x\)-value is \(x = 2\), yielding \(y = 3(2) + 3 = 9\).

qs.q:
Find the smaller \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:

\(xy = 6\)
\(y = -2x + 8\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = -2x + 8\) into \(xy = 6\) to get \(-2x^2 + 8x - 6 = 0\), which divides by \(-2\) to give \(x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 1)(x - 3) = 0\), so the smaller \(x\)-value is \(1\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(y\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:

\(xy = -12\)
\(y = 2x + 10\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x + 10\) into \(xy = -12\) to obtain \(2x^2 + 10x + 12 = 0\), or \(x^2 + 5x + 6 = 0\), which factors as \((x + 2)(x + 3) = 0\). The solutions are \((-2, 6)\) and \((-3, 4)\), so the greater \(y\)-value is \(6\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:

\(xy = 60\)
\(2x - y = 19\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x - 19\) into \(xy = 60\) to obtain \(2x^2 - 19x - 60 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x + 5)(x - 12) = 0\), yielding \(x = 12\) and \(x = -\frac{5}{2}\), so the greater value is \(12\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations:

\(4x - 3y = 5\)
\(xy = 2\)

with \(x < 0\), what is the value of \(y\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(y = \frac{4x - 5}{3}\) into \(xy = 2\) to get \(4x^2 - 5x - 6 = 0\), which factors as \((4x + 3)(x - 2) = 0\). For \(x < 0\), \(x = -\frac{3}{4}\), and substituting this back gives \(y = \frac{4(-3/4) - 5}{3} = -\frac{8}{3}\).

qs.q:
Find the smaller \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:

\(2x + 3y = 19\)
\(xy = 14\)
qs.s: Solve the linear equation for \(y = \frac{19 - 2x}{3}\) and substitute into \(xy = 14\) to get \(2x^2 - 19x + 42 = 0\). Factoring yields \((2x - 7)(x - 6) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = \frac{7}{2}\) and \(x = 6\), with \(\frac{7}{2}\) being the smaller value.

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations:

\(x(y - 1) = 12\)
\(3x - y = 4\)

with \(x > 0\), what is the value of \(x + y\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 3x - 4\) into \(x(y - 1) = 12\) to obtain \(x(3x - 5) = 12\), which simplifies to \(3x^2 - 5x - 12 = 0\). Factoring gives \((3x + 4)(x - 3) = 0\), so \(x = 3\), \(y = 3(3) - 4 = 5\), and \(x + y = 3 + 5 = 8\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:

\(xy = 2\)
\(2x - y = -2\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x + 2\) into \(xy = 2\) to get \(2x^2 + 2x - 2 = 0\), which reduces to \(x^2 + x - 1 = 0\). Applying the quadratic formula gives \(x = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(\frac{-1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Find the greatest value of \(x\) among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(xy = 6\)
\(y = 3x - 7\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 3x - 7\) into \(xy = 6\) to get \(x(3x - 7) = 6\), or \(3x^2 - 7x - 6 = 0\). Factoring gives \((3x + 2)(x - 3) = 0\), so \(x = 3\) or \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\), and the greatest value is 3.

qs.q:
Find the greatest value of \(x\) among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(xy = -4\)
\(y = x - 5\)
qs.s: Substituting \(y = x - 5\) into \(xy = -4\) gives \(x(x - 5) = -4\), or \(x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x - 1) = 0\), so \(x = 4\) or \(x = 1\), with the greatest value being 4.

qs.q:
Find the greatest value of \(x\) among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(xy = -3\)
\(y = 2x + 5\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x + 5\) into \(xy = -3\) to obtain \(x(2x + 5) = -3\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 + 5x + 3 = 0\) and factors as \((2x + 3)(x + 1) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = -1\) and \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\), and since \(-1 > -\frac{3}{2}\), the greatest value is -1.

qs.q:
Find the greatest value of \(x\) among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(xy = 12\)
\(y = x + 4\)
qs.s: Substituting \(y = x + 4\) into \(xy = 12\) yields \(x(x + 4) = 12\), which rearranges to \(x^2 + 4x - 12 = 0\). Factoring as \((x + 6)(x - 2) = 0\) gives \(x = 2\) or \(x = -6\), so the greatest value is 2.

qs.q:
Find the greatest value of \(x\) among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(xy = 2\)
\(y = 2x + 3\)
qs.s: Substituting \(y = 2x + 3\) into \(xy = 2\) gives \(x(2x + 3) = 2\), which rearranges to \(2x^2 + 3x - 2 = 0\) and factors into \((2x - 1)(x + 2) = 0\). Thus, \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) or \(x = -2\), so the greatest value of \(x\) is \frac{1}{2}.

qs.q:
Find the greatest value of \(x + y\) among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(xy = -6\)
\(2x + y = 1\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 1 - 2x\) into \(xy = -6\) to get \(2x^2 - x - 6 = 0\), which factors as \((2x + 3)(x - 2) = 0\), giving solutions \((-\frac{3}{2}, 4)\) and \((2, -3)\). Computing the sum of coordinates for each gives \(-\frac{3}{2} + 4 = \frac{5}{2}\) and \(2 + (-3) = -1\), so the greatest value is \frac{5}{2}.

qs.q:
Find the greatest value of \(x\) among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(xy = 2\)
\(2x - y = -1\)
qs.s: Rewrite the linear equation as \(y = 2x + 1\) and substitute into \(xy = 2\) to get \(2x^2 + x - 2 = 0\). Applying the quadratic formula gives \(x = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1^2 - 4(2)(-2)}}{4} = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{17}}{4}\), so the greatest value is \frac{-1 + \sqrt{17}}{4}.

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is the real solution to the system of equations with \(x > 0\), what is the value of \(x + y\)?
\(xy = 2\)
\(2x - 3y = 1\)
qs.s: Isolating \(y\) gives \(y = \frac{2x - 1}{3}\), and substituting into \(xy = 2\) yields \(2x^2 - x - 6 = 0\), which factors as \((2x + 3)(x - 2) = 0\). Since \(x > 0\), we have \(x = 2\), which gives \(y = \frac{2(2) - 1}{3} = 1\), so \(x + y = 2 + 1 = 3\).

qs.q:
Find the greatest value of \(x\) among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(xy = 15\)
\(3x + 2y = 19\)
qs.s: Solving the linear equation for \(y\) gives \(y = \frac{19 - 3x}{2}\), and substituting into \(xy = 15\) yields \(3x^2 - 19x + 30 = 0\). Factoring gives \((3x - 10)(x - 3) = 0\), which gives \(x = \frac{10}{3}\) or \(x = 3\), so the greatest value of \(x\) is \frac{10}{3}.

qs.q:
Find the greatest value of \(y\) among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(\frac{6}{x} + 2y = 7\)
\(x + y = 4\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 4 - x\) into the first equation to get \(\frac{6}{x} + 2(4 - x) = 7\), which multiplies by \(x\) to become \(2x^2 - x - 6 = 0\) with roots \(x = 2\) and \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\). The corresponding \(y\)-values are \(4 - 2 = 2\) and \(4 - \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right) = \frac{11}{2}\), so the greatest value is \frac{11}{2}.
Setting \(2x^2 = x^2 + 4x\) yields \(x^2 - 4x = 0\), which factors as \(x(x - 4) = 0\). The solutions have \(x = 0\) and \(x = 4\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(4\).
Setting \(x^2 = 2x^2 - 3x\) gives \(x^2 - 3x = 0\), which factors as \(x(x - 3) = 0\). The real solutions have \(x = 0\) and \(x = 3\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(3\).
Setting \(3x^2 = 2x^2 + 5x\) gives \(x^2 - 5x = 0\), which factors as \(x(x - 5) = 0\). The real solutions have \(x = 0\) and \(x = 5\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(5\).
Equating the two equations gives \(3x^2 = x^2 + 4x\), which rearranges to \(2x^2 - 4x = 0\), or \(2x(x - 2) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = 0\) and \(x = 2\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(2\).

Equating the expressions for \(y\) gives \(x^2 = 3x^2 + 4x\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 + 4x = 0\), or \(2x(x + 2) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = -2\) and \(x = 0\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(0\).

Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\) to produce \(3x^2 = 3x + 6\), or \(3x^2 - 3x - 6 = 0\). Dividing by \(3\) gives \(x^2 - x - 2 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 2)(x + 1) = 0\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(2\).

Expanding the first equation gives \(y = x^2 - 4x - 3\), and setting it equal to the second gives \(2x^2 - 8x - 24 = 0\). Dividing by \(2\) produces \(x^2 - 4x - 12 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 6)(x + 2) = 0\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(6\).

Setting the two expressions equal gives \(x^2 - 2x + 3 = 2x^2 - 5x - 1\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x + 1) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = -1\) and \(x = 4\), making \(4\) the greater \(x\)-value.
Setting \(3x^2 - 4x - 1 = x^2 + 3x - 4\) gives \(2x^2 - 7x + 3 = 0\). Factoring yields \((2x - 1)(x - 3) = 0\), giving \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = 3\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(3\).

Subtracting the first equation from the second eliminates \(y\) to yield \(x^2 - 3x = 10\), or \(x^2 - 3x - 10 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 5)(x + 2) = 0\), so \(x = 5\) or \(x = -2\), with \(5\) being the greater \(x\)-value.

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2\)
\(y = 32 - x^2\)
qs.s: Equating the expressions gives \(x^2 = 32 - x^2\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 = 32\), so \(x^2 = 16\) and \(x = \pm 4\). Therefore, the greater \(x\)-value is \(4\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 + 5\)
\(y = 55 - x^2\)
qs.s: Equating gives \(x^2 + 5 = 55 - x^2\), so \(2x^2 = 50\), meaning \(x^2 = 25\) and \(x = \pm 5\). Thus, the greater \(x\)-value is \(5\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 + 3\)
\(y = 21 - x^2\)
qs.s: Setting \(x^2 + 3 = 21 - x^2\) yields \(2x^2 = 18\), so \(x^2 = 9\) and \(x = \pm 3\). The greater \(x\)-value is \(3\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = 3x^2\)
\(y = 4 - x^2\)
qs.s: Setting \(3x^2 = 4 - x^2\) gives \(4x^2 = 4\), so \(x^2 = 1\) and \(x = \pm 1\). The greater \(x\)-value is \(1\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2\)
\(y = 8 - x^2\)
qs.s: Setting \(x^2 = 8 - x^2\) gives \(2x^2 = 8\), so \(x^2 = 4\) and \(x = \pm 2\). Thus, the greater \(x\)-value is \(2\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(2x^2 - 5x - y = 1\)
\(x^2 - 3x + y = 2\)
qs.s: Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\) to give \(3x^2 - 8x - 3 = 0\), which factors into \((3x + 1)(x - 3) = 0\). This gives \(x = 3\) and \(x = -\frac{1}{3}\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(3\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 - 2x - 3\)
\(y = -x^2 + 4x + 5\)
qs.s: Setting \(x^2 - 2x - 3 = -x^2 + 4x + 5\) simplifies to \(2x^2 - 6x - 8 = 0\), or \(x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x + 1) = 0\), so \(x = 4\) and \(x = -1\), making the greater \(x\)-value \(4\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 - 3x - 4\)
\(y = -x^2 + 5x + 6\)
qs.s: Equating the equations gives \(x^2 - 3x - 4 = -x^2 + 5x + 6\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 - 8x - 10 = 0\), or \(x^2 - 4x - 5 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 5)(x + 1) = 0\), so the solutions are \(x = 5\) and \(x = -1\), with the greater \(x\)-value being \(5\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(x^2 - y = 2\)
\(x^2 + 3x + y = 12\)
qs.s: Substituting \(y = x^2 - 2\) into the second equation yields \(2x^2 + 3x - 14 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 2)(2x + 7) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = 2\) and \(x = -\frac{7}{2}\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(2\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = 2x^2 - x - 8\)
\(y = x^2 + 3x + 4\)
qs.s: Setting \(2x^2 - x - 8 = x^2 + 3x + 4\) rearranges to \(x^2 - 4x - 12 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 6)(x + 2) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = 6\) and \(x = -2\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(6\).

qs.q:
Find the real solution \((x, y)\) of the system of equations:
\(y = 2x^2\)
\(xy = 16\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x^2\) into \(xy = 16\) to get \(2x^3 = 16\), which simplifies to \(x^3 = 8\) and \(x = 2\). Then \(y = 2(2)^2 = 8\), giving the solution \((2, 8)\).

qs.q:
Find the real solution \((x, y)\) of the system of equations:
\(y = 3x^2\)
\(xy = -24\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 3x^2\) into \(xy = -24\) to obtain \(3x^3 = -24\), so \(x^3 = -8\) and \(x = -2\). Then \(y = 3(-2)^2 = 12\), yielding the solution \((-2, 12)\).

qs.q:
Find the real solution \((x, y)\) of the system of equations:
\(y = \frac{1}{4}x^2\)
\(xy = -16\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = \frac{1}{4}x^2\) into \(xy = -16\) to get \(\frac{1}{4}x^3 = -16\), which gives \(x^3 = -64\) and \(x = -4\). Then \(y = \frac{1}{4}(-4)^2 = 4\), resulting in the solution \((-4, 4)\).

qs.q:
Find the real solution \((x, y)\) of the system of equations:
\(y = \frac{1}{3}x^2\)
\(xy = 9\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = \frac{1}{3}x^2\) into \(xy = 9\) to get \(\frac{1}{3}x^3 = 9\), which gives \(x^3 = 27\) and \(x = 3\). Then \(y = \frac{1}{3}(3)^2 = 3\), giving the solution \((3, 3)\).

qs.q:
Find the real solution \((x, y)\) of the system of equations:
\(x = \frac{1}{2}y^2\)
\(xy = 32\)
qs.s: Substitute \(x = \frac{1}{2}y^2\) into \(xy = 32\) to get \(\frac{1}{2}y^3 = 32\), so \(y^3 = 64\) and \(y = 4\). Then \(x = \frac{1}{2}(4)^2 = 8\), giving the solution \((8, 4)\).

qs.q:
Find the real solution \((x, y)\) of the system of equations:
\(x = \frac{1}{4}(y - 3)^2\)
\(xy - 3x = 16\)
qs.s: Factor the second equation as \(x(y - 3) = 16\) and substitute \(x = \frac{1}{4}(y - 3)^2\) to get \(\frac{1}{4}(y - 3)^3 = 16\), so \((y - 3)^3 = 64\) and \(y = 7\). Then \(x = \frac{1}{4}(7 - 3)^2 = 4\), resulting in the solution \((4, 7)\).

qs.q:
Find the real solution \((x, y)\) of the system of equations:
\(y = -2(x + 1)^2\)
\(xy + y = -16\)
qs.s: Factor the second equation as \(y(x + 1) = -16\) and substitute \(y = -2(x + 1)^2\) to get \(-2(x + 1)^3 = -16\), so \((x + 1)^3 = 8\) and \(x = 1\). Substituting \(x = 1\) gives \(y = -2(1 + 1)^2 = -8\), yielding the solution \((1, -8)\).

qs.q:
Find the real solution \((x, y)\) of the system of equations:
\(y = \frac{1}{3}(2x - 1)^2\)
\(2xy - y = 9\)
qs.s: Factor the second equation as \(y(2x - 1) = 9\) and substitute \(y\) to obtain \(\frac{1}{3}(2x - 1)^3 = 9\), which leads to \((2x - 1)^3 = 27\) and \(x = 2\). Then \(y = \frac{1}{3}(2(2) - 1)^2 = 3\), giving the solution \((2, 3)\).

qs.q:
Find the real solution \((x, y)\) of the system of equations:
\(y = \frac{1}{2}(x - 1)^2\)
\(xy - y = 4\)
qs.s: Factor the second equation as \(y(x - 1) = 4\) and substitute \(y = \frac{1}{2}(x - 1)^2\) to obtain \(\frac{1}{2}(x - 1)^3 = 4\), which simplifies to \((x - 1)^3 = 8\) and \(x = 3\). Then \(y = \frac{1}{2}(3 - 1)^2 = 2\), so the solution is \((3, 2)\).

qs.q:
Find the real solution \((x, y)\) of the system of equations:
\(y = \frac{2}{3}x^2\)
\(xy = 144\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = \frac{2}{3}x^2\) into \(xy = 144\) to obtain \(\frac{2}{3}x^3 = 144\), which simplifies to \(x^3 = 216\) and \(x = 6\). Then \(y = \frac{2}{3}(6)^2 = 24\), giving the solution \((6, 24)\).

qs.q:
Find all real solutions of the system of equations:
\(y = -x^2\)
\(y = 2x^2 - 6x\)
qs.s: Equating the expressions gives \(-x^2 = 2x^2 - 6x\), which simplifies to \(3x^2 - 6x = 0\), so \(3x(x - 2) = 0\). Thus \(x = 0\) or \(x = 2\), yielding the solutions \((0, 0)\) and \((2, -4)\).

qs.q:
Find all real solutions of the system of equations:
\(y = x^2\)
\(y = 2x^2 - 5x\)
qs.s: Equating the two expressions for \(y\) gives \(x^2 = 2x^2 - 5x\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 5x = 0\), so \(x(x - 5) = 0\). Substituting \(x = 0\) and \(x = 5\) into \(y = x^2\) yields the solutions \((0, 0)\) and \((5, 25)\).

qs.q:
Find all real solutions of the system of equations:
\(y = 3x^2\)
\(y = 2x^2 + 7x\)
qs.s: Setting \(3x^2 = 2x^2 + 7x\) yields \(x^2 - 7x = 0\), so \(x(x - 7) = 0\), giving \(x = 0\) and \(x = 7\). Substituting these into \(y = 3x^2\) gives \((0, 0)\) and \((7, 147)\).

qs.q:
Find all real solutions of the system of equations:
\(y = x^2\)
\(y = 4x^2 + 9x\)
qs.s: Setting \(x^2 = 4x^2 + 9x\) leads to \(3x^2 + 9x = 0\), or \(3x(x + 3) = 0\), giving \(x = 0\) and \(x = -3\). Substituting these into \(y = x^2\) produces the solutions \((0, 0)\) and \((-3, 9)\).

qs.q:
Find all real solutions of the system of equations:
\(y = 2x^2\)
\(y = x^2 + 6x\)
qs.s: Setting \(2x^2 = x^2 + 6x\) gives \(x^2 - 6x = 0\), which factors as \(x(x - 6) = 0\), giving \(x = 0\) or \(x = 6\). Substituting into \(y = 2x^2\) gives \((0, 0)\) and \((6, 72)\).

qs.q:
Find all real solutions of the system of equations:
\(y = 2x^2 + 3x + 7\)
\(y = x^2 - x + 1\)
qs.s: Equating the two equations gives \(2x^2 + 3x + 7 = x^2 - x + 1\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 4x + 6 = 0\). Since the discriminant is \(4^2 - 4(1)(6) = -8 < 0\), there are no real solutions.

qs.q:
Find all real solutions of the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 - 2x + 1\)
\(y = 3x^2 - 9x + 4\)
qs.s: Setting \(3x^2 - 9x + 4 = x^2 - 2x + 1\) yields \(2x^2 - 7x + 3 = 0\), which factors as \((2x - 1)(x - 3) = 0\). Substituting \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = 3\) into \(y = x^2 - 2x + 1\) produces \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{4}\right)\) and \((3, 4)\).

qs.q:
Find all real solutions of the system of equations:
\(y = -x^2 + 4x - 1\)
\(y = x^2 - 8x + 17\)
qs.s: Equating the expressions gives \(x^2 - 8x + 17 = -x^2 + 4x - 1\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 - 12x + 18 = 0\), or \(2(x - 3)^2 = 0\). The single root is \(x = 3\), and substituting into either equation gives \(y = 2\), so the unique solution is \((3, 2)\).

qs.q:
Find all real solutions of the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 + x - 2\)
\(y = 2x^2 - 4x + 2\)
qs.s: Equating the expressions gives \(2x^2 - 4x + 2 = x^2 + x - 2\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0\) and factors as \((x - 1)(x - 4) = 0\). Substituting \(x = 1\) and \(x = 4\) into \(y = x^2 + x - 2\) produces the solutions \((1, 0)\) and \((4, 18)\).

qs.q:
Find all real solutions of the system of equations:
\(x^2 - y = 5\)
\(2x^2 - 3x - y = 9\)
qs.s: From the first equation, \(y = x^2 - 5\); substituting this into the second equation gives \(2x^2 - 3x - (x^2 - 5) = 9\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0\) or \((x - 4)(x + 1) = 0\). Substituting \(x = -1\) and \(x = 4\) into \(y = x^2 - 5\) yields \((-1, -4)\) and \((4, 11)\).

qs.q:
Find the \(y\)-value of the real solution with \(x > 0\) for the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 - 4\)
\(y = 2x^2 - x - 10\)
qs.s: Setting the equations equal gives \(x^2 - 4 = 2x^2 - x - 10\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - x - 6 = 0\) and factors into \((x - 3)(x + 2) = 0\). For the positive solution \(x = 3\), substituting into the first equation gives \(y = 3^2 - 4 = 5\).

qs.q:
Find the \(y\)-value of the real solution with \(x > 0\) for the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 + 2x + 1\)
\(y = 2x^2 + x - 1\)
qs.s: Equating the expressions for \(y\) gives \(x^2 + 2x + 1 = 2x^2 + x - 1\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - x - 2 = 0\) and factors as \((x - 2)(x + 1) = 0\). Substituting the positive root \(x = 2\) into the first equation yields \(y = 2^2 + 2(2) + 1 = 9\).

qs.q:
Find the \(y\)-value of the real solution with \(x > 0\) for the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 - x - 2\)
\(y = 2x^2 - 4x - 6\)
qs.s: Equating the two equations gives \(x^2 - x - 2 = 2x^2 - 4x - 6\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0\) and factors as \((x - 4)(x + 1) = 0\). Taking the positive solution \(x = 4\), we find \(y = 4^2 - 4 - 2 = 10\).

qs.q:
Find the \(y\)-value of the real solution with \(x > 0\) for the system of equations:
\(y = -x^2 + 3x + 4\)
\(y = x^2 - x - 2\)
qs.s: Equating the expressions gives \(-x^2 + 3x + 4 = x^2 - x - 2\), which rearranges to \(2x^2 - 4x - 6 = 0\) and factors as \(2(x - 3)(x + 1) = 0\). Using the positive solution \(x = 3\), we find \(y = 3^2 - 3 - 2 = 4\).

qs.q:
Find the \(y\)-value of the real solution with \(x > 0\) for the system of equations:
\(y = 2x^2 + 3x - 1\)
\(y = x^2 + 2x + 5\)
qs.s: Setting the equations equal gives \(2x^2 + 3x - 1 = x^2 + 2x + 5\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + x - 6 = 0\) and factors as \((x + 3)(x - 2) = 0\). Substituting the positive root \(x = 2\) into the second equation yields \(y = 2^2 + 2(2) + 5 = 13\).

qs.q:
Find the \(y\)-value of the real solution with \(x > 0\) for the system of equations:
\(y - x^2 = 3(x + 5)\)
\(y - 2x^2 = 2x + 3\)
qs.s: Rewriting in terms of \(y\) gives \(y = x^2 + 3x + 15\) and \(y = 2x^2 + 2x + 3\), which equate to \(x^2 - x - 12 = 0\) and factor into \((x - 4)(x + 3) = 0\). Substituting the positive root \(x = 4\) gives \(y = 4^2 + 3(4) + 15 = 43\).

qs.q:
Find the \(y\)-value of the real solution with \(x > 0\) for the system of equations:
\(y = 3x^2 + 4x - 1\)
\(y = x^2 - x + 2\)
qs.s: Equating the equations yields \(2x^2 + 5x - 3 = 0\), which factors into \((2x - 1)(x + 3) = 0\). Substituting the positive root \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) into the second equation produces \(y = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{2} + 2 = \frac{7}{4}\).

qs.q:
Find the \(y\)-value of the real solution with \(x > 0\) for the system of equations:
\(y = (x - 1)^2 + 4x - 1\)
\(y = 2(x + 1)^2 - 3x - 8\)
qs.s: Expanding both equations gives \(y = x^2 + 2x\) and \(y = 2x^2 + x - 6\), which set equal simplify to \(x^2 - x - 6 = 0\) with factors \((x - 3)(x + 2) = 0\). Substituting the positive root \(x = 3\) into \(y = x^2 + 2x\) yields \(y = 3^2 + 2(3) = 15\).

qs.q:
What is the sum of the \(y\)-values of all real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = 2x^2 - 4x + 1\)
\(y = x^2 + x - 5\)
qs.s: Equating the two expressions gives \(x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 2)(x - 3) = 0\) to give \(x = 2\) and \(x = 3\). Substituting these into \(y = x^2 + x - 5\) yields \(y_1 = 1\) and \(y_2 = 7\), so the sum of the \(y\)-values is \(1 + 7 = 8\).

qs.q:
Find the \(y\)-value of the real solution with \(x > 0\) for the system of equations:
\(2x^2 - 3x - y = 5\)
\(x^2 + 2x - y = -1\)
qs.s: Subtracting the second equation from the first eliminates \(y\) to produce \(x^2 - 5x - 6 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 6)(x + 1) = 0\). Using the positive root \(x = 6\) in \(y = x^2 + 2x + 1\) gives \(y = 6^2 + 2(6) + 1 = 49\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 - 2x + 3\)
\(y = 2x^2 + x - 7\)
qs.s: Equating the expressions gives \(2x^2 + x - 7 = x^2 - 2x + 3\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 3x - 10 = 0\). Factoring as \((x + 5)(x - 2) = 0\) gives \(x = -5\) or \(x = 2\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(2\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 + x - 2\)
\(y = 2x^2 - 5x + 3\)
qs.s: Setting \(2x^2 - 5x + 3 = x^2 + x - 2\) leads to \(x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0\). Factoring as \((x - 5)(x - 1) = 0\) gives \(x = 5\) or \(x = 1\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(5\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 + 2x - 1\)
\(y = 2x^2 + x - 7\)
qs.s: Equating the expressions gives \(2x^2 + x - 7 = x^2 + 2x - 1\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - x - 6 = 0\). Factoring as \((x - 3)(x + 2) = 0\) yields \(x = 3\) or \(x = -2\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(3\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 + x + 2\)
\(y = 2x^2 + 3x - 1\)
qs.s: Equating the expressions gives \(2x^2 + 3x - 1 = x^2 + x + 2\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 2x - 3 = 0\). Factoring as \((x + 3)(x - 1) = 0\) gives \(x = -3\) or \(x = 1\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(1\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(x^2 + 2x - y + 3 = 0\)
\(3x^2 - x - y - 2 = 0\)
qs.s: Solving each equation for \(y\) gives \(y = x^2 + 2x + 3\) and \(y = 3x^2 - x - 2\). Setting them equal yields \(2x^2 - 3x - 5 = 0\), which factors as \((2x - 5)(x + 1) = 0\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y - 2x^2 + 4x = 1\)
\(x^2 + 2x - y = -4\)
qs.s: Isolating \(y\) in both equations gives \(y = 2x^2 - 4x + 1\) and \(y = x^2 + 2x + 4\), which equate to \(x^2 - 6x - 3 = 0\). Using the quadratic formula yields \(x = \frac{6 \pm \sqrt{48}}{2} = 3 \pm 2\sqrt{3}\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(3 + 2\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = 3(x - 1)^2 + x - 13\)
\(y = x^2 + 8x + 14\)
qs.s: Expanding the first equation gives \(y = 3x^2 - 5x - 10\), and equating it to the second gives \(2x^2 - 13x - 24 = 0\). Factoring as \((2x + 3)(x - 8) = 0\) gives \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\) or \(x = 8\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(8\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y - 4x = x(x - 2) + 9\)
\(2x^2 - y = 3x + 5\)
qs.s: Rewriting the equations for \(y\) yields \(y = x^2 + 2x + 9\) and \(y = 2x^2 - 3x - 5\). Equating them gives \(x^2 - 5x - 14 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 7)(x + 2) = 0\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(7\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(2y - x^2 + 2x = -6\)
\(2y + x^2 - 6x = 18\)
qs.s: Expressing \(2y\) from both equations gives \(x^2 - 2x - 6 = -x^2 + 6x + 18\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 4x - 12 = 0\). Factoring as \((x - 6)(x + 2) = 0\) gives \(x = 6\) or \(x = -2\), so the greater \(x\)-value is \(6\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 + 2\)
\(y = 2x^2 - x - 4\)
qs.s: Equating the two expressions for \(y\) gives \(2x^2 - x - 4 = x^2 + 2\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - x - 6 = (x - 3)(x + 2) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = 3\) and \(x = -2\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is \(3\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 - 2\)
\(y = 2x^2 - 4x - 7\)
qs.s: Equating the expressions yields \(2x^2 - 4x - 7 = x^2 - 2\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 4x - 5 = (x - 5)(x + 1) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = 5\) and \(x = -1\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is \(5\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 + 4\)
\(y = 2x^2 + x - 2\)
qs.s: Setting the two equations equal gives \(2x^2 + x - 2 = x^2 + 4\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + x - 6 = (x + 3)(x - 2) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = -3\) and \(x = 2\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is \(2\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 - 3\)
\(y = 2x^2 + 3x - 7\)
qs.s: Setting the two equations equal gives \(2x^2 + 3x - 7 = x^2 - 3\), which rearranges to \(x^2 + 3x - 4 = (x + 4)(x - 1) = 0\). The roots are \(x = -4\) and \(x = 1\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is \(1\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = x^2 + 3\)
\(y = 2x^2 - 2x - 5\)
qs.s: Equating the two equations gives \(2x^2 - 2x - 5 = x^2 + 3\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 2x - 8 = (x - 4)(x + 2) = 0\). The roots are \(x = 4\) and \(x = -2\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is \(4\).

qs.q:
Find the \(y\)-coordinate of the real solution with the greater \(x\)-coordinate to the system of equations:
\(2x^2 - x - y = 1\)
\(x^2 + 2x + y = 13\)
qs.s: Adding the equations eliminates \(y\) to give \(3x^2 + x - 14 = (3x + 7)(x - 2) = 0\), yielding \(x = 2\) and \(x = -\frac{7}{3}\). Substituting the greater \(x\)-coordinate, \(x = 2\), into \(2x^2 - x - y = 1\) gives \(2(2)^2 - 2 - y = 1\), which solves to \(y = 5\).

qs.q:
Find the \(y\)-coordinate of the real solution with \(x > 0\) to the system of equations:
\(y - 5 = 2(x - 1)^2\)
\(y + 3x = x^2 + 19\)
qs.s: Expanding and isolating \(y\) yields \(y = 2x^2 - 4x + 7\) and \(y = x^2 - 3x + 19\), which equate to \(x^2 - x - 12 = (x - 4)(x + 3) = 0\). For the positive solution \(x = 4\), substituting into the first equation gives \(y = 2(4 - 1)^2 + 5 = 23\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y = 2(x - 3)^2 - 5\)
\(y = 6 - (x - 1)^2\)
qs.s: Expanding both equations gives \(y = 2x^2 - 12x + 13\) and \(y = -x^2 + 2x + 5\), which equate to \(3x^2 - 14x + 8 = (3x - 2)(x - 4) = 0\). The roots are \(x = \frac{2}{3}\) and \(x = 4\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is \(4\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is the real solution to the system of equations with \(x > 0\), find the value of \(x + y\):
\(3x^2 + 5x - 2y = 4\)
\(2x^2 - 6x + y = 5\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(y = -2x^2 + 6x + 5\), and substituting into the first yields \(7x^2 - 7x - 14 = 7(x - 2)(x + 1) = 0\). Since \(x > 0\), \(x = 2\), which gives \(y = -2(2)^2 + 6(2) + 5 = 9\), so \(x + y = 2 + 9 = 11\).

qs.q:
Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate among the real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y - x^2 = x + 2\)
\(y - 2x^2 = -3x + 1\)
qs.s: Equating the two expressions for \(y\) gives \(x^2 + x + 2 = 2x^2 - 3x + 1\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 4x - 1 = 0\). Applying the quadratic formula gives \(x = \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{20}}{2} = 2 \pm \sqrt{5}\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is \(2 + \sqrt{5}\).

qs.q:
Find the greatest \(x\)-value among all real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y - x^2 = 0\)
\(3x^2 - 5x - y = 3\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = x^2\) into the second equation to get \(2x^2 - 5x - 3 = 0\), which factors as \((2x + 1)(x - 3) = 0\). The solutions for \(x\) are \(-\frac{1}{2}\) and \(3\), so the greatest \(x\)-value is \(3\).

qs.q:
Find the greatest \(x\)-value among all real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y - x^2 = 0\)
\(x^2 + 4x + y = 6\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = x^2\) into the second equation to obtain \(2x^2 + 4x - 6 = 0\), which simplifies to \((x + 3)(x - 1) = 0\). The solutions for \(x\) are \(-3\) and \(1\), so the greatest \(x\)-value is \(1\).

qs.q:
Find the greatest \(y\)-value among all real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y - x^2 = 0\)
\(2x^2 + x - y = 6\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = x^2\) into the second equation to get \(x^2 + x - 6 = 0\), which factors as \((x + 3)(x - 2) = 0\), giving \(x = -3\) and \(x = 2\). Substituting back into \(y = x^2\) gives \(y = 9\) and \(y = 4\), so the greatest \(y\)-value is \(9\).

qs.q:
Find the greatest \(x\)-value among all real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y - 2x^2 = 0\)
\(x^2 + 5x + y = 2\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x^2\) into the second equation to obtain \(3x^2 + 5x - 2 = 0\), which factors into \((3x - 1)(x + 2) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = \frac{1}{3}\) and \(x = -2\), so the greatest \(x\)-value is \(\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q:
Find the smallest \(x\)-value among all real solutions to the system of equations:
\(x^2 - y = 0\)
\(x^2 - 6x + y = 8\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = x^2\) into the second equation to get \(2x^2 - 6x - 8 = 0\), or \(x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x + 1) = 0\), so \(x = 4\) or \(x = -1\), with the smallest value being \(-1\).

qs.q:
Find the greatest \(y\)-value among all real solutions to the system of equations:
\(x^2 - 3x - y + 5 = 0\)
\(x^2 - x + y - 21 = 0\)
qs.s: Isolate \(y\) from the first equation to get \(y = x^2 - 3x + 5\), and substitute it into the second equation to obtain \(2x^2 - 4x - 16 = 0\), which simplifies to \((x - 4)(x + 2) = 0\). Substituting \(x = 4\) and \(x = -2\) into \(y = x^2 - 3x + 5\) yields \(y = 9\) and \(y = 15\), respectively, so the greatest \(y\)-value is \(15\).

qs.q:
Find the greatest \(x\)-value among all real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y - 3x^2 = 0\)
\(x^2 + 8x - y = 4\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 3x^2\) into the second equation to get \(-2x^2 + 8x - 4 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 4x + 2 = 0\). Applying the quadratic formula yields \(x = \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{8}}{2} = 2 \pm \sqrt{2}\), so the greatest \(x\)-value is \(2 + \sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Find the greatest \(x\)-value among all real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y - 5 = 2(x - 1)^2\)
\(x^2 + x + y = 25\)
qs.s: Expanding the first equation yields \(y = 2x^2 - 4x + 7\), and substituting this into the second equation gives \(3x^2 - 3x - 18 = 0\). Dividing by \(3\) gives \(x^2 - x - 6 = (x - 3)(x + 2) = 0\), so \(x = 3\) or \(x = -2\), with the greatest \(x\)-value being \(3\).

qs.q:
Find the greatest \(x\)-value among all real solutions to the system of equations:
\(y + 11 = (x + 2)(x - 4)\)
\(2x^2 - 3x - y = 39\)
qs.s: Expand and isolate \(y\) in the first equation to find \(y = x^2 - 2x - 19\), and substitute it into the second equation to get \(x^2 - x - 20 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 5)(x + 4) = 0\), which yields \(x = 5\) and \(x = -4\), so the greatest \(x\)-value is \(5\).

qs.q:
Find the greatest \(y\)-value among all real solutions to the system of equations:
\(2x^2 - 3x - y = 1\)
\(3x^2 + x - 2y = 8\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x^2 - 3x - 1\) into the second equation to obtain \(-x^2 + 7x - 6 = 0\), which factors as \(-(x - 6)(x - 1) = 0\). Evaluating \(y = 2x^2 - 3x - 1\) at \(x = 1\) and \(x = 6\) gives \(y = -2\) and \(y = 53\), respectively, so the greatest \(y\)-value is \(53\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations with \(x > 0\), what is the value of \(y\)?

\(x^2 - 4x - y - 1 = 0\)
\(x^2 - x + y - 2 = 0\)
qs.s: Adding the equations eliminates \(y\) to produce \(2x^2 - 5x - 3 = (2x + 1)(x - 3) = 0\), yielding positive solution \(x = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) into the first equation gives \(3^2 - 4(3) - y - 1 = 0\), which yields \(y = -4\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations with \(x > 0\), what is the value of \(y\)?

\(x^2 + 4x - y - 5 = 0\)
\(x^2 - 2x + y - 7 = 0\)
qs.s: Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\) to give \(2x^2 + 2x - 12 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + x - 6 = 0\) with roots \(x = 2\) and \(x = -3\). For \(x = 2\), substituting into the first equation yields \(2^2 + 4(2) - y - 5 = 0\), so \(y = 7\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations with \(x < 0\), what is the value of \(y\)?

\(x^2 - x - y - 6 = 0\)
\(x^2 + 5x + y - 10 = 0\)
qs.s: Adding both equations gives \(2x^2 + 4x - 16 = 0\), or \(x^2 + 2x - 8 = (x + 4)(x - 2) = 0\), giving \(x = -4\) for \(x < 0\). Substituting \(x = -4\) into the first equation gives \((-4)^2 - (-4) - y - 6 = 0\), so \(y = 14\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations with \(x > 1\), what is the value of \(y\)?

\(x^2 - 5x + y + 1 = 0\)
\(x^2 - x - y + 3 = 0\)
qs.s: Adding the two equations gives \(2x^2 - 6x + 4 = 0\), or \(x^2 - 3x + 2 = (x - 1)(x - 2) = 0\), so \(x = 2\) when \(x > 1\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into the second equation gives \(2^2 - 2 - y + 3 = 0\), which solves to \(y = 5\).

qs.q:
What is the largest \(x\)-value among all real solutions to the system of equations?

\(x^2 + 5x - y + 2 = 0\)
\(x^2 + x + y - 10 = 0\)
qs.s: Adding the equations eliminates \(y\), resulting in \(2x^2 + 6x - 8 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 3x - 4 = (x + 4)(x - 1) = 0\). The solutions for \(x\) are \(x = -4\) and \(x = 1\), so the largest \(x\)-value is 1.

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations with \(x > 0\), what is the value of \(y\)?

\(x^2 - 2x + y - 5 = 0\)
\(x^2 - 3x - 2y + 4 = 0\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 2 and adding it to the second equation eliminates \(y\) to give \(3x^2 - 7x - 6 = (3x + 2)(x - 3) = 0\), so \(x = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) into the first equation yields \(3^2 - 2(3) + y - 5 = 0\), which gives \(y = 2\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations with \(x > 0\), what is the value of \(y\)?

\(x^2 + 3x - 3y - 1 = 0\)
\(x^2 - 7x + 2y - 16 = 0\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 2 and the second by 3, then adding them gives \(5x^2 - 15x - 50 = 0\), or \((x - 5)(x + 2) = 0\), so \(x = 5\). Substituting \(x = 5\) into the first equation gives \(5^2 + 3(5) - 3y - 1 = 0\), which solves to \(3y = 39\), so \(y = 13\).

qs.q:
Find the positive \(x\)-value among the real solutions to the system of equations.

\(2x^2 - y = 0\)
\(x^2 - 6x - y + 4 = 0\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x^2\) into the second equation to get \(x^2 - 6x - 2x^2 + 4 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 6x - 4 = 0\). Applying the quadratic formula gives \(x = \frac{-6 \pm \sqrt{36 - 4(1)(-4)}}{2} = -3 \pm \sqrt{13}\), so the positive solution is \(-3 + \sqrt{13}\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations with \(x > 0\), what is the value of \(y\)?

\(3x^2 + x - y - 10 = 0\)
\(2x^2 - 8x + y + 4 = 0\)
qs.s: Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\) to give \(5x^2 - 7x - 6 = (5x + 3)(x - 2) = 0\), which gives the positive root \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into the first equation yields \(3(2)^2 + 2 - y - 10 = 0\), so \(y = 4\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations with \(x > 0\), what is the value of \(y\)?

\((x + 1)^2 - y = 4\)
\(x(x + 4) + y = 17\)
qs.s: Expanding both equations gives \(x^2 + 2x - y - 3 = 0\) and \(x^2 + 4x + y - 17 = 0\); adding them yields \(2x^2 + 6x - 20 = 0\), or \((x + 5)(x - 2) = 0\). For \(x = 2\), substitute into the first equation to find \((2 + 1)^2 - y = 4\), which gives \(y = 5\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations where \(x\) is an integer, what is the value of \(x + y\)?

\(3x^2 + y = 13\)
\(y - 2x^2 + 4x = 1\)
qs.s: Substituting \(y = 13 - 3x^2\) into the second equation gives \(5x^2 - 4x - 12 = 0\), which factors as \((5x + 6)(x - 2) = 0\). The integer root is \(x = 2\), which gives \(y = 13 - 3(2)^2 = 1\), so \(x + y = 2 + 1 = 3\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations with \(x < 0\), what is the value of \(y\)?

\(x^2 + y = 5\)
\(2x^2 - y - 3x = 1\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 5 - x^2\) into the second equation to get \(3x^2 - 3x - 6 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - x - 2 = 0\) and gives \(x = -1\) for \(x < 0\). Substituting \(x = -1\) gives \(y = 5 - (-1)^2 = 4\).

qs.q:
Find the sum of all real \(x\)-values that satisfy the system of equations:

\(x^2 - y = -4\)
\(2x^2 - y - 3x = 0\)
qs.s: Substituting \(y = x^2 + 4\) into the second equation gives \(x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 4)(x + 1) = 0\). The solutions are \(x = 4\) and \(x = -1\), giving a sum of \(4 + (-1) = 3\).

qs.q:
Find the maximum value of \(y\) among all real solutions \((x, y)\) of the system of equations:

\(2x^2 + y = 8\)
\(y + x^2 - 2x = 5\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 8 - 2x^2\) into the second equation to obtain \(x^2 + 2x - 3 = 0\), which gives \(x = 1\) and \(x = -3\). The corresponding \(y\)-values are \(y = 8 - 2(1)^2 = 6\) and \(y = 8 - 2(-3)^2 = -10\), so the maximum value is \(6\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations with \(x > 0\), what is the value of \(y\)?

\(x^2 + y = 7\)
\(y - 2x^2 + 3x = 1\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 7 - x^2\) into the second equation to get \(-3x^2 + 3x + 6 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - x - 2 = 0\) with positive root \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) back into the first equation yields \(y = 7 - 2^2 = 3\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations with \(x > 0\), what is the value of \(y\)?

\(2x^2 - 5x + 2y = 11\)
\(3x^2 + 5x - 2y = 9\)
qs.s: Adding the two equations eliminates the linear terms to give \(5x^2 = 20\), so \(x = 2\) for \(x > 0\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into the first equation yields \(8 - 10 + 2y = 11\), which gives \(2y = 13\) and \(y = \frac{13}{2}\).

qs.q:
What is the unique \(y\)-value shared by all real solutions to the system of equations?

\(y = 2(x - 1)^2 - 3\)
\(x^2 - 2x + y = 5\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(x^2 - 2x = 5 - y\), and expanding the first equation gives \(y = 2(x^2 - 2x) - 1\). Substituting yields \(y = 2(5 - y) - 1\), which simplifies to \(3y = 9\), or \(y = 3\).

qs.q:
Find the sum of the \(y\)-coordinates of all real solutions to the system of equations:

\(y - 3x^2 = 0\)
\(2x^2 + 8x - y = -7\)
qs.s: Substituting \(y = 3x^2\) into the second equation gives \(x^2 - 8x - 7 = 0\), where the roots satisfy \(x_1 + x_2 = 8\) and \(x^2 = 8x + 7\). Each \(y\)-value is \(3x^2 = 24x + 21\), so the sum of the \(y\)-coordinates is \(24(x_1 + x_2) + 42 = 24(8) + 42 = 234\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations with integer coordinates, what is the value of \(x - y\)?

\(\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 3x - y = 2\)
\(\frac{1}{4}x^2 - x + y = 2\)
qs.s: Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\) to give \(\frac{3}{4}x^2 + 2x = 4\), or \(3x^2 + 8x - 16 = 0\), whose integer solution is \(x = -4\). Substituting \(x = -4\) into either equation yields \(y = -6\), so \(x - y = -4 - (-6) = 2\).

qs.q:
If \((x, y)\) is a real solution to the system of equations with \(x > 0\), what is the value of \(y\)?

\(4x^2 - 3x - y = -7\)
\(2x^2 + 4x - y = -22\)
qs.s: Subtracting the second equation from the first gives \(2x^2 - 7x - 15 = 0\), which factors as \((2x + 3)(x - 5) = 0\), giving \(x = 5\) for \(x > 0\). Substituting \(x = 5\) into the first equation yields \(y = 4(5)^2 - 3(5) + 7 = 92\).

exercises.name: Find points of intersection with axes or lines

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = x^2 - 2x - 1\) and the x-axis that has the greater x-coordinate.
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(x^2 - 2x - 1 = 0\), which solves to \(x = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{(-2)^2 - 4(1)(-1)}}{2} = 1 \pm \sqrt{2}\). Thus, the point with the greater x-coordinate is \((1 + \sqrt{2}, 0)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = x^2 + 4x + 1\) and the x-axis that has the smaller x-coordinate.
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) yields \(x^2 + 4x + 1 = 0\). Applying the quadratic formula gives \(x = \frac{-4 \pm \sqrt{4^2 - 4(1)(1)}}{2} = -2 \pm \sqrt{3}\), so the point with the smaller x-coordinate is \((-2 - \sqrt{3}, 0)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = x^2 - 6x + 7\) and the x-axis that has the greater x-coordinate.
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(x^2 - 6x + 7 = 0\). By the quadratic formula, \(x = \frac{6 \pm \sqrt{(-6)^2 - 4(1)(7)}}{2} = 3 \pm \sqrt{2}\), so the intersection point with the greater x-coordinate is \((3 + \sqrt{2}, 0)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = x^2 + 6x + 3\) and the x-axis that has the greater x-coordinate.
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) yields \(x^2 + 6x + 3 = 0\), giving \(x = \frac{-6 \pm \sqrt{6^2 - 4(1)(3)}}{2} = -3 \pm \sqrt{6}\). The intersection point with the greater x-coordinate is \((-3 + \sqrt{6}, 0)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = x^2 - 8x + 10\) and the x-axis that has the smaller x-coordinate.
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(x^2 - 8x + 10 = 0\). Using the quadratic formula, \(x = \frac{8 \pm \sqrt{(-8)^2 - 4(1)(10)}}{2} = 4 \pm \sqrt{6}\), so the point with the smaller x-coordinate is \((4 - \sqrt{6}, 0)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - 3x + 1\) and the line \(x - y = 3\) that has the greater x-coordinate.
qs.s: Set \(\frac{1}{2}x^2 - 3x + 1 = x - 3\) and multiply by 2 to get \(x^2 - 8x + 8 = 0\), yielding \(x = \frac{8 \pm \sqrt{32}}{2} = 4 \pm 2\sqrt{2}\). Substituting \(x = 4 + 2\sqrt{2}\) into \(y = x - 3\) gives \(y = 1 + 2\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = -x^2 + 5x - 2\) and the line \(x + y = 4\) that has the greater x-coordinate.
qs.s: Equating \(-x^2 + 5x - 2 = 4 - x\) gives \(x^2 - 6x + 6 = 0\), so \(x = 3 \pm \sqrt{3}\). For the greater x-coordinate \(x = 3 + \sqrt{3}\), substituting into \(y = 4 - x\) gives \(y = 4 - (3 + \sqrt{3}) = 1 - \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = (x - 2)^2 - 7\) and the line \(2x - y = 1\) that has the smaller x-coordinate.
qs.s: Expanding the parabola gives \(y = x^2 - 4x - 3\). Setting it equal to \(y = 2x - 1\) gives \(x^2 - 6x - 2 = 0\), so \(x = 3 \pm \sqrt{11}\); substituting \(x = 3 - \sqrt{11}\) into \(y = 2x - 1\) produces \(y = 5 - 2\sqrt{11}\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = 2x^2 - 4x - 3\) and the line \(2x - y = -1\) that has the smaller x-coordinate.
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x + 1\) into the quadratic equation to get \(2x^2 - 6x - 4 = 0\), or \(x^2 - 3x - 2 = 0\), which yields \(x = \frac{3 \pm \sqrt{17}}{2}\). Substituting the smaller root into \(y = 2x + 1\) gives \(y = 4 - \sqrt{17}\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = x^2 - 4x + 1\) and the line \(y = 2x - 3\) that has the greater x-coordinate.
qs.s: Setting \(x^2 - 4x + 1 = 2x - 3\) gives \(x^2 - 6x + 4 = 0\), so \(x = \frac{6 \pm \sqrt{20}}{2} = 3 \pm \sqrt{5}\). For \(x = 3 + \sqrt{5}\), \(y = 2(3 + \sqrt{5}) - 3 = 3 + 2\sqrt{5}\), giving the point \((3 + \sqrt{5}, 3 + 2\sqrt{5})\).

exercises.name: Find points of intersection with axes or lines

qs.q: Find the non-zero \(x\)-coordinate of the point of intersection of the parabola \(6x^2 + \frac{1}{5}x + y = 0\) and the \(x\)-axis.
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 0\) into the equation to get \(6x^2 + \frac{1}{5}x = 0\), which factors into \(x\left(6x + \frac{1}{5}\right) = 0\). The non-zero root is \(x = -\frac{1}{30}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero \(x\)-coordinate of the point of intersection of the parabola \(5x^2 - \frac{1}{3}x + y = 0\) and the \(x\)-axis.
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(5x^2 - \frac{1}{3}x = 0\), or \(x\left(5x - \frac{1}{3}\right) = 0\). The non-zero solution is \(5x = \frac{1}{3}\), which gives \(x = \frac{1}{15}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero \(x\)-coordinate of the point of intersection of the parabola \(3x^2 - \frac{1}{4}x - y = 0\) and the \(x\)-axis.
qs.s: Along the \(x\)-axis, \(y = 0\), so \(3x^2 - \frac{1}{4}x = 0 \implies x\left(3x - \frac{1}{4}\right) = 0\). Solving \(3x - \frac{1}{4} = 0\) gives \(x = \frac{1}{12}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero \(x\)-coordinate of the point of intersection of the parabola \(2x^2 - \frac{1}{7}x + y = 0\) and the \(x\)-axis.
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(2x^2 - \frac{1}{7}x = 0\), so \(x\left(2x - \frac{1}{7}\right) = 0\). For the non-zero intersection, \(2x = \frac{1}{7}\), so \(x = \frac{1}{14}\).

qs.q: Find the non-zero \(x\)-coordinate of the point of intersection of the parabola \(2x^2 + \frac{1}{4}x + y = 0\) and the \(x\)-axis.
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 0\) to get \(2x^2 + \frac{1}{4}x = 0\), which factors as \(x\left(2x + \frac{1}{4}\right) = 0\). Setting \(2x + \frac{1}{4} = 0\) yields \(x = -\frac{1}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(3x^2 - \frac{2}{3}x - y = 2\) and the line \(y = \frac{1}{3}x + 2\).
qs.s: Substituting \(y = \frac{1}{3}x + 2\) gives \(3x^2 - \frac{2}{3}x - \left(\frac{1}{3}x + 2\right) = 2\), which simplifies to \(3x^2 - x - 4 = 0\). Factoring as \((3x - 4)(x + 1) = 0\) gives the roots \(x = \frac{4}{3}\) and \(x = -1\), so the greater value is \(\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(2x^2 - \frac{3}{2}x + y = 5\) and the line \(x + 2y = 2\).
qs.s: From the linear equation, \(y = 1 - \frac{1}{2}x\). Substituting into the parabola yields \(2x^2 - \frac{3}{2}x + 1 - \frac{1}{2}x = 5\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 - 2x - 4 = 0\), or \((x - 2)(x + 1) = 0\), giving the greater root \(x = 2\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-coordinate of the point of intersection of the parabola \(3x^2 + \frac{1}{3}x + y = 0\) and the line \(7x + 3y = 1\).
qs.s: Substitute \(y = \frac{1 - 7x}{3}\) into the parabola equation to get \(3x^2 + \frac{1}{3}x + \frac{1 - 7x}{3} = 0\). Multiplying by \(3\) yields \(9x^2 - 6x + 1 = 0\), which factors as \((3x - 1)^2 = 0\), so \(x = \frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(2x^2 + \frac{5}{2}x + y = 0\) and the line \(y = -3\).
qs.s: Substitute \(y = -3\) to get \(2x^2 + \frac{5}{2}x - 3 = 0\), and multiply by \(2\) to obtain \(4x^2 + 5x - 6 = 0\). Factoring gives \((4x - 3)(x + 2) = 0\), so the positive solution is \(x = \frac{3}{4}\).

exercises.name: Find points of intersection with axes or lines

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = 91x^2 + 47x + 382\) and the \(y\)-axis.
qs.s: Setting \(x = 0\) gives \(y = 91(0)^2 + 47(0) + 382 = 382\). Therefore, the point of intersection is \((0, 382)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = -62x^2 + 83x - 149\) and the \(y\)-axis.
qs.s: To find the intersection with the \(y\)-axis, substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation: \(y = -62(0)^2 + 83(0) - 149 = -149\). Thus, the point of intersection is \((0, -149)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = 48x^2 - 19x + 235\) and the \(y\)-axis.
qs.s: To find the intersection with the \(y\)-axis, substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation: \(y = 48(0)^2 - 19(0) + 235 = 235\). Thus, the point of intersection is \((0, 235)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = 34x^2 - 76x - 415\) and the \(y\)-axis.
qs.s: Setting \(x = 0\) gives \(y = 34(0)^2 - 76(0) - 415 = -415\). Therefore, the point of intersection is \((0, -415)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = -85x^2 - 29x + 563\) and the \(y\)-axis.
qs.s: Setting \(x = 0\) gives \(y = -85(0)^2 - 29(0) + 563 = 563\). Therefore, the point of intersection is \((0, 563)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = -\frac{3}{4}(x + 8)^2 + 131\) and the \(y\)-axis.
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation: \(y = -\frac{3}{4}(0 + 8)^2 + 131 = -\frac{3}{4}(64) + 131 = -48 + 131 = 83\). Thus, the point of intersection is \((0, 83)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(3y - 14x = 2(x + 5)^2 + 94\) and the \(y\)-axis.
qs.s: Set \(x = 0\) to get \(3y - 0 = 2(0 + 5)^2 + 94 = 2(25) + 94 = 144\). Dividing by \(3\) yields \(y = 48\), so the point of intersection is \((0, 48)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = 5(x - 3)^2 - 2(x + 4)^2 + 89\) and the \(y\)-axis.
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation: \(y = 5(-3)^2 - 2(4)^2 + 89 = 5(9) - 2(16) + 89 = 45 - 32 + 89 = 102\). Thus, the point of intersection is \((0, 102)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = 3(2x - 5)(3x + 8)\) and the \(y\)-axis.
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation: \(y = 3(2(0) - 5)(3(0) + 8) = 3(-5)(8) = -120\). Thus, the point of intersection is \((0, -120)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = -4(x - 6)^2 + 185\) and the \(y\)-axis.
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation: \(y = -4(0 - 6)^2 + 185 = -4(36) + 185 = -144 + 185 = 41\). Thus, the point of intersection is \((0, 41)\).

exercises.name: Find points of intersection with axes or lines

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-coordinate among the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = -0.004x^2\) and the line \(y = -40\).
qs.s: Setting \(-0.004x^2 = -40\) yields \(x^2 = \frac{-40}{-0.004} = 10000\), which gives \(x = \pm 100\). The smaller \(x\)-coordinate is \(-100\).

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = -0.002x^2\) and the line \(y = -5\).
qs.s: Equating the expressions gives \(-0.002x^2 = -5\), which simplifies to \(x^2 = \frac{-5}{-0.002} = 2500\). Taking the positive square root yields \(x = 50\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate among the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = -0.005x^2\) and the line \(y = -18\).
qs.s: Setting \(-0.005x^2 = -18\) leads to \(x^2 = \frac{-18}{-0.005} = 3600\). Solving for \(x\) gives \(x = \pm 60\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is 60.

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = -0.001x^2\) and the line \(y = -8\).
qs.s: Setting \(-0.001x^2 = -8\) gives \(x^2 = \frac{-8}{-0.001} = 8000\). The positive solution is \(x = \sqrt{8000} = \sqrt{1600 \times 5} = 40\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = -0.005x^2\) and the line \(y = -10\).
qs.s: Solving \(-0.005x^2 = -10\) gives \(x^2 = \frac{-10}{-0.005} = 2000\). Taking the positive square root produces \(x = \sqrt{2000} = \sqrt{400 \times 5} = 20\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = -0.2(x - 4)^2 + 5\) and the \(x\)-axis.
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(-0.2(x - 4)^2 + 5 = 0\), which simplifies to \((x - 4)^2 = 25\). Solving gives \(x - 4 = \pm 5\), resulting in \(x = 9\) or \(x = -1\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is 9.

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 0.5x^2 - 3x - 2\) and the line \(y = 6\).
qs.s: Setting \(0.5x^2 - 3x - 2 = 6\) gives \(0.5x^2 - 3x - 8 = 0\), or \(x^2 - 6x - 16 = 0\). Factoring as \((x - 8)(x + 2) = 0\) yields the positive root \(x = 8\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 2x^2 - 5x + 1\) and the line \(x + y = 7\).
qs.s: Substituting \(y = 7 - x\) into the quadratic equation yields \(2x^2 - 5x + 1 = 7 - x\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 - 4x - 6 = 0\) or \(x^2 - 2x - 3 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 3)(x + 1) = 0\), so the greater solution is \(x = 3\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-coordinate of the intersection point of the parabola \(y = x^2 - 4x + 1\) and the line \(y = 2x - 4\) that has the greater \(x\)-coordinate.
qs.s: Equating the two gives \(x^2 - 4x + 1 = 2x - 4\), which rearranges to \(x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0\) and factors into \((x - 1)(x - 5) = 0\). The greater \(x\)-coordinate is \(x = 5\), and substituting into the line gives \(y = 2(5) - 4 = 6\).

qs.q: Find the positive \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = -0.01x^2 + 25\) and the line \(y = x + 1\).
qs.s: Setting \(-0.01x^2 + 25 = x + 1\) gives \(0.01x^2 + x - 24 = 0\), which scales to \(x^2 + 100x - 2400 = 0\). Factoring as \((x + 120)(x - 20) = 0\) gives the positive solution \(x = 20\).

exercises.name: Find points of intersection with axes or lines

qs.q: Find all points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 0.005x^2\) and the line \(y = 8\).
qs.s: Set \(0.005x^2 = 8\), which simplifies to \(x^2 = \frac{8}{0.005} = 1600\). Taking the square root yields \(x = \pm 40\), giving the intersection points \((-40, 8)\) and \((40, 8)\).

qs.q: Find all points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 0.02x^2\) and the line \(y = 18\).
qs.s: Setting \(0.02x^2 = 18\) gives \(x^2 = \frac{18}{0.02} = 900\). Taking the square root gives \(x = \pm 30\), so the points of intersection are \((-30, 18)\) and \((30, 18)\).

qs.q: Find all points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 0.0001x^2\) and the line \(y = 9\).
qs.s: Setting \(0.0001x^2 = 9\) gives \(x^2 = \frac{9}{0.0001} = 90000\). Taking the square root yields \(x = \pm 300\), so the intersection points are \((-300, 9)\) and \((300, 9)\).

qs.q: Find all points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 0.0004x^2\) and the line \(y = 1\).
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 1\) into the equation to get \(0.0004x^2 = 1\), which gives \(x^2 = \frac{1}{0.0004} = 2500\). Taking the square root gives \(x = \pm 50\), so the points of intersection are \((-50, 1)\) and \((50, 1)\).

qs.q: Find all points of intersection of the parabola \(y = -0.002x^2\) and the line \(y = -5\).
qs.s: Set \(-0.002x^2 = -5\), which simplifies to \(x^2 = \frac{-5}{-0.002} = 2500\). Taking the square root gives \(x = \pm 50\), so the points of intersection are \((-50, -5)\) and \((50, -5)\).

qs.q: Find all points of intersection of the parabola \(y = x^2 - 4x - 5\) and the line \(y = 7\).
qs.s: Set \(x^2 - 4x - 5 = 7\), which rearranges to \(x^2 - 4x - 12 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 6)(x + 2) = 0\), so \(x = -2\) or \(x = 6\), giving the points of intersection \((-2, 7)\) and \((6, 7)\).

qs.q: Find all points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 2x^2 - 3x + 1\) and the line \(x - y = -1\).
qs.s: Isolate \(y\) in the line equation to get \(y = x + 1\), then substitute into the parabola equation: \(x + 1 = 2x^2 - 3x + 1\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 - 4x = 0\). Factoring gives \(2x(x - 2) = 0\), yielding \(x = 0\) (\(y = 1\)) and \(x = 2\) (\(y = 3\)), so the points are \((0, 1)\) and \((2, 3)\).

qs.q: Find all points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 0.005(x + 10)^2 + 2\) and the line \(y = 4\).
qs.s: Subtract 2 to obtain \(0.005(x + 10)^2 = 2\), which gives \((x + 10)^2 = \frac{2}{0.005} = 400\). Taking the square root gives \(x + 10 = \pm 20\), yielding \(x = 10\) and \(x = -30\), so the points are \((-30, 4)\) and \((10, 4)\).

qs.q: Find all points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 2x^2 + 5x - 12\) and the \(x\)-axis.
qs.s: The \(x\)-axis has equation \(y = 0\), so solve \(2x^2 + 5x - 12 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x - 3)(x + 4) = 0\), so \(x = -4\) and \(x = \frac{3}{2}\), giving the points \((-4, 0)\) and \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, 0\right)\).

qs.q: Find all points of intersection of the parabola \(y = x^2 - 2x - 8\) and the line \(y = x + 2\).
qs.s: Equating \(x^2 - 2x - 8 = x + 2\) gives \(x^2 - 3x - 10 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 5)(x + 2) = 0\), so \(x = -2\) or \(x = 5\). Substituting these values into \(y = x + 2\) yields the points \((-2, 0)\) and \((5, 7)\).

exercises.name: Find points of intersection with axes or lines

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 0.5x^2 - 1.5x + 1\) and the line \(y = 3\).
qs.s: Equating the expressions gives \(0.5x^2 - 1.5x + 1 = 3\), or \(0.5x^2 - 1.5x - 2 = 0\). Multiplying by \(2\) gives \(x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 4)(x + 1) = 0\), so the smaller \(x\)-coordinate is \(-1\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = -x^2 + 2x + 8\) and the \(x\)-axis.
qs.s: The \(x\)-axis is the line \(y = 0\), so solve \(-x^2 + 2x + 8 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x + 2) = 0\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is \(4\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = x^2 - 6x + 4\) and the line \(y = -1\).
qs.s: Set \(x^2 - 6x + 4 = -1\), which rearranges to \(x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 1)(x - 5) = 0\), yielding \(x = 1\) and \(x = 5\), of which the smaller is \(1\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = -2x^2 + 4x + 1\) and the line \(y = -5\).
qs.s: Set \(-2x^2 + 4x + 1 = -5\), which simplifies to \(-2x^2 + 4x + 6 = 0\). Dividing by \(-2\) gives \(x^2 - 2x - 3 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 3)(x + 1) = 0\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is \(3\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = -0.1x^2 + 0.9x + 0.6\) and the line \(y = 2\).
qs.s: Set \(-0.1x^2 + 0.9x + 0.6 = 2\), which rearranges to \(-0.1x^2 + 0.9x - 1.4 = 0\). Multiplying by \(-10\) yields \(x^2 - 9x + 14 = 0\), or \((x - 2)(x - 7) = 0\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is \(7\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = \frac{1}{2}(x - 2)^2 - 5\) and the line \(x + y = 1\).
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 1 - x\) into the parabola's equation: \(1 - x = \frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 4x + 4) - 5\). Multiplying through by \(2\) and simplifying yields \(x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0\), or \((x - 4)(x + 2) = 0\), so the smaller \(x\)-coordinate is \(-2\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = x^2 - 4x + 1\) and the line \(y = 2x - 2\).
qs.s: Equating the equations gives \(x^2 - 4x + 1 = 2x - 2\), which rearranges to \(x^2 - 6x + 3 = 0\). By the quadratic formula, \(x = \frac{6 \pm \sqrt{36 - 12}}{2} = 3 \pm \sqrt{6}\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is \(3 + \sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(y\)-coordinate among the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = x^2 - 3x - 9\) and the line \(2x - y = 3\).
qs.s: Rewrite the line as \(y = 2x - 3\) and equate to obtain \(x^2 - 3x - 9 = 2x - 3\), or \(x^2 - 5x - 6 = 0\), giving \(x = 6\) and \(x = -1\). Substituting these into \(y = 2x - 3\) yields \(y = 9\) and \(y = -5\), so the greater \(y\)-coordinate is \(9\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 2x^2 - 2x - 16\) and the line \(3x - y = 4\).
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 3x - 4\) into the quadratic equation to get \(2x^2 - 2x - 16 = 3x - 4\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 - 5x - 12 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x + 3)(x - 4) = 0\), which yields \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = 4\), so the smaller \(x\)-coordinate is \(-\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the smaller \(y\)-coordinate among the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 2x^2 - 7x - 5\) and the line \(3x + y = 1\).
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 1 - 3x\) into the parabola equation to get \(2x^2 - 7x - 5 = 1 - 3x\), which simplifies to \(2x^2 - 4x - 6 = 0\), or \((x - 3)(x + 1) = 0\). For \(x = 3\), \(y = 1 - 3(3) = -8\), and for \(x = -1\), \(y = 1 - 3(-1) = 4\), so the smaller \(y\)-coordinate is \(-8\).

exercises.name: Find points of intersection with axes or lines

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 0.1x^2 + 0.3x - 1.6\) and the line \(y = 1.2\).
qs.s: Equating \(0.1x^2 + 0.3x - 1.6 = 1.2\) gives \(0.1x^2 + 0.3x - 2.8 = 0\), which multiplies by 10 to \(x^2 + 3x - 28 = 0\). Factoring into \((x + 7)(x - 4) = 0\) gives \(x = 4\) and \(x = -7\), so the greater value is 4.

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 0.5x^2 - 1.5x - 5\) and the line \(y = 4\).
qs.s: Setting \(0.5x^2 - 1.5x - 5 = 4\) yields \(0.5x^2 - 1.5x - 9 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 3x - 18 = 0\). Factoring as \((x - 6)(x + 3) = 0\) gives \(x = 6\) and \(x = -3\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is 6.

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = -0.5x^2 - x + 5.5\) and the line \(y = 1.5\).
qs.s: Setting \(-0.5x^2 - x + 5.5 = 1.5\) gives \(-0.5x^2 - x + 4 = 0\), which multiplies by \(-2\) to produce \(x^2 + 2x - 8 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x + 4)(x - 2) = 0\), yielding solutions \(x = 2\) and \(x = -4\), with \(-4\) being the smaller.

qs.q: Find the smaller \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = -0.2x^2 + 0.8x + 3.4\) and the line \(y = 1\).
qs.s: Setting \(-0.2x^2 + 0.8x + 3.4 = 1\) gives \(-0.2x^2 + 0.8x + 2.4 = 0\), which multiplies by \(-5\) to \(x^2 - 4x - 12 = 0\). Factoring into \((x - 6)(x + 2) = 0\) gives solutions \(x = 6\) and \(x = -2\), so the smaller \(x\)-coordinate is \(-2\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 0.25x^2 - x - 8\) and the \(x\)-axis.
qs.s: Since the \(x\)-axis is the line \(y = 0\), set \(0.25x^2 - x - 8 = 0\) and multiply by 4 to get \(x^2 - 4x - 32 = 0\). Factoring as \((x - 8)(x + 4) = 0\) yields \(x = 8\) and \(x = -4\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is 8.

qs.q: Find the smaller \(y\)-coordinate among the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = -2x^2 + 12x - 11\) and the line \(2x + y = 9\).
qs.s: Substituting \(y = -2x + 9\) into the parabola gives \(-2x^2 + 14x - 20 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 7x + 10 = 0\) with roots \(x = 2\) and \(x = 5\). The corresponding \(y\)-values are \(y(2) = 5\) and \(y(5) = -1\), making \(-1\) the smaller \(y\)-coordinate.

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 2x^2 - 5x + 1\) and the line \(3x - y = -7\).
qs.s: Rearrange the line equation to \(y = 3x + 7\) and set it equal to the parabola to obtain \(2x^2 - 8x - 6 = 0\), or \(x^2 - 4x - 3 = 0\). Applying the quadratic formula yields \(x = \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{16 - 4(1)(-3)}}{2} = 2 \pm \sqrt{7}\), so the greater \(x\)-coordinate is \(2 + \sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = \frac{1}{4}x^2 - x - 3\) and the line \(x - 2y = 8\).
qs.s: Isolating \(y\) gives \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 4\); setting \(\frac{1}{4}x^2 - x - 3 = \frac{1}{2}x - 4\) and clearing denominators gives \(x^2 - 6x + 4 = 0\). By the quadratic formula, \(x = \frac{6 \pm \sqrt{36 - 16}}{2} = 3 \pm \sqrt{5}\), giving the greater \(x\)-coordinate \(3 + \sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-coordinate of the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = (x - 3)^2 - 4\) and the line \(x + y = 19\) that lies in the first quadrant.
qs.s: Expand the parabola to \(y = x^2 - 6x + 5\) and substitute \(y = 19 - x\) to get \(x^2 - 5x - 14 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 7)(x + 2) = 0\). The first-quadrant point requires \(x > 0\), so \(x = 7\), yielding \(y = 19 - 7 = 12\).

qs.q: Find the greater \(x\)-coordinate of the points of intersection of the parabola \(y = 3x^2 - 10x - 7\) and the line \(2x - y = -5\).
qs.s: Rewriting the line as \(y = 2x + 5\) and equating gives \(3x^2 - 12x - 12 = 0\), or \(x^2 - 4x - 4 = 0\). The quadratic formula yields \(x = \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{16 - 4(1)(-4)}}{2} = \frac{4 \pm 4\sqrt{2}}{2} = 2 \pm 2\sqrt{2}\), with the greater value being \(2 + 2\sqrt{2}\).

exercises.name: Find points of intersection with axes or lines

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = x^2 + 2x - 8\) and the line \(3x - y = 6\) that has the smaller x-coordinate.
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 3x - 6\) into the parabola equation to obtain \(3x - 6 = x^2 + 2x - 8\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - x - 2 = 0\) and factors as \((x - 2)(x + 1) = 0\). The smaller root is \(x = -1\), and substituting into the line gives \(y = 3(-1) - 6 = -9\), giving \((-1, -9)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = x^2 - 4x + 2\) and the line \(2x - y = 7\).
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x - 7\) into the parabola equation to get \(2x - 7 = x^2 - 4x + 2\), which rearranges to \(x^2 - 6x + 9 = 0\) or \((x - 3)^2 = 0\). The single solution is \(x = 3\), giving \(y = 2(3) - 7 = -1\), so the point of intersection is \((3, -1)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = -x^2 + 4x + 3\) and the line \(x - y = 1\) that lies in the third quadrant.
qs.s: Substitute \(y = x - 1\) into \(y = -x^2 + 4x + 3\) to get \(x - 1 = -x^2 + 4x + 3\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0\) with roots \(x = 4\) and \(x = -1\). The third-quadrant point requires both coordinates to be negative, so choosing \(x = -1\) gives \(y = -1 - 1 = -2\), resulting in \((-1, -2)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = x^2 - x - 5\) and the line \(2x - y = 1\) that has the greater x-coordinate.
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x - 1\) into the parabola equation to get \(2x - 1 = x^2 - x - 5\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0\) and factors as \((x - 4)(x + 1) = 0\). Using the greater root \(x = 4\) in the linear equation gives \(y = 2(4) - 1 = 7\), yielding \((4, 7)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = -x^2 - 3x + 5\) and the line \(x + y = 2\) that lies in the first quadrant.
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2 - x\) into the quadratic equation to obtain \(2 - x = -x^2 - 3x + 5\), which simplifies to \(x^2 + 2x - 3 = 0\) with roots \(x = 1\) and \(x = -3\). The first-quadrant point requires \(x > 0\), so \(x = 1\) gives \(y = 2 - 1 = 1\), corresponding to \((1, 1)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = x^2 - 4x + 3\) and the line \(x + 3y = 3\) that has the smaller x-coordinate.
qs.s: Substituting the parabola equation into the line gives \(x + 3(x^2 - 4x + 3) = 3\), which simplifies to \(3x^2 - 11x + 6 = 0\) and factors as \((3x - 2)(x - 3) = 0\). The smaller root is \(x = \frac{2}{3}\), and substituting into the line gives \(3y = 3 - \frac{2}{3} = \frac{7}{3}\), so \(y = \frac{7}{9}\), yielding \((\frac{2}{3}, \frac{7}{9})\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - x - 4\) and the line \(3x - 2y = 2\) that lies in the first quadrant.
qs.s: Substitute \(y = \frac{3}{2}x - 1\) into the quadratic equation and clear denominators to get \(x^2 - 5x - 6 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 6)(x + 1) = 0\). The first-quadrant solution requires positive coordinates, so \(x = 6\), giving \(y = \frac{3}{2}(6) - 1 = 8\), which is \((6, 8)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = 2(x - 2)^2 - 5\) and the line \(4x - y = 7\) that has the greater x-coordinate.
qs.s: Expanding the parabola yields \(y = 2x^2 - 8x + 3\), and substituting \(y = 4x - 7\) gives \(2x^2 - 12x + 10 = 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0\) with roots \(x = 1\) and \(x = 5\). The greater value \(x = 5\) gives \(y = 4(5) - 7 = 13\), so the point of intersection is \((5, 13)\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(y = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 2)^2 + 6\) and the line \(x + 2y = 8\) that has the greater x-coordinate.
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 4 - \frac{1}{2}x\) into the parabola equation and multiply by 2 to obtain \(8 - x = -(x - 2)^2 + 12\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 5x = 0\) with solutions \(x = 0\) and \(x = 5\). Using the greater root \(x = 5\) in the linear equation gives \(2y = 8 - 5 = 3\), so \(y = \frac{3}{2}\), yielding \((5, \frac{3}{2})\).

qs.q: Find the point of intersection of the parabola \(3x^2 - 2y = 6\) and the line \(2x - y = 1\) that lies in the first quadrant.
qs.s: From the line, \(y = 2x - 1\); substituting into the parabola equation gives \(3x^2 - 2(2x - 1) = 6\), which rearranges to \(3x^2 - 4x - 4 = 0\) and factors as \((3x + 2)(x - 2) = 0\). The first-quadrant point requires \(x > 0\), so \(x = 2\), yielding \(y = 2(2) - 1 = 3\), giving \((2, 3)\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank. The graph of the linear inequality \(2x + y \ge 4\) is a _____ that includes the boundary line and all points on one side of it.
qs.s: A straight boundary line divides the coordinate plane into two regions, each called a half-plane.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. When graphing the inequality \(3x + 2y < 12\), substituting the coordinates of the origin \((0, 0)\) into the inequality serves as a _____ to determine which region to shade.
qs.s: A point not on the boundary line, such as \((0, 0)\), is called a test point and is used to determine which side of the boundary line satisfies the inequality.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. The equation \(y = 4\) is the _____ when graphing the inequality \(2y \le 8\).
qs.s: The equation formed by replacing the inequality symbol with an equals sign represents the boundary line that separates the coordinate plane into two half-planes.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. When graphing the inequality \(y \le -2x + 5\), the boundary line is drawn as a _____ line because points on the line satisfy the inequality.
qs.s: Inequalities that include equality (\(\le\) or \(\ge\)) use a solid boundary line because points on the line are included in the solution set.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. When graphing the linear inequality \(x - 3y > 6\), the boundary line is drawn as a _____ line because points on the line are not included in the solution set.
qs.s: Inequalities with strict inequality symbols (\(<\) or \(>\)) use a dashed boundary line to show that points on the line do not satisfy the inequality.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. When graphing the inequality \(5(2x - 3) - 3(4y + 2) < 3(x + 5) - 12y - 1\), the boundary line is a vertical line with the equation \(x = \underline{\quad}\).
qs.s: Setting the two expressions equal gives \(10x - 12y - 21 = 3x - 12y + 14\). Adding \(12y\) to both sides eliminates \(y\), leaving \(7x = 35\), so the boundary line is \(x = 5\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank. When graphing the linear inequality \(5(x - 2y) + 14 > 2(4x - y) - 1\), the slope of the boundary line is \(m = \underline{\quad}\).
qs.s: The boundary line equation is \(5(x - 2y) + 14 = 2(4x - y) - 1\), which expands to \(5x - 10y + 14 = 8x - 2y - 1\). Rearranging into slope-intercept form gives \(-8y = 3x - 15\), or \(y = -\frac{3}{8}x + \frac{15}{8}\), so the slope is \(-\frac{3}{8}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank. When graphing the inequality \(3(x - 2) + 2(4y + 1) \le 3x - 3(y - 6)\), the boundary line is a horizontal line with the equation \(y = \underline{\quad}\).
qs.s: Setting the expressions equal gives \(3x + 8y - 4 = 3x - 3y + 18\). Subtracting \(3x\) from both sides leaves \(8y - 4 = -3y + 18\), which simplifies to \(11y = 22\), or \(y = 2\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank. When graphing the inequality \(3(2x - 3y) - 2(x + 4y - 6) < 5x - 5\), the y-intercept of the boundary line is \((0, \underline{\quad})\).
qs.s: The boundary line equation is \(3(2x - 3y) - 2(x + 4y - 6) = 5x - 5\). Setting \(x = 0\) gives \(3(-3y) - 2(4y - 6) = -5\), which simplifies to \(-17y + 12 = -5\), or \(-17y = -17\), yielding \(y = 1\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank. The boundary line for the inequality \(3(2x - 1) - 4(y + 2) \le 2x - 7\) has the equation \(y = \underline{\quad}\).
qs.s: Replacing \(\le\) with \(=\) gives \(3(2x - 1) - 4(y + 2) = 2x - 7\). Expanding and simplifying yields \(6x - 4y - 11 = 2x - 7\), which simplifies to \(-4y = -4x + 4\), or \(y = x - 1\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In graphing the inequality \(-4x - 2y < 8\), the shaded solution would be _____ the boundary line.
qs.s: Adding \(4x\) gives \(-2y < 4x + 8\), and dividing by \(-2\) reverses the inequality to \(y > -2x - 4\). Since \(y\) is greater than the expression, the shaded solution is above the boundary line.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In graphing the inequality \(4x + 3y < 9\), the shaded solution would be _____ the boundary line.
qs.s: Subtracting \(4x\) gives \(3y < -4x + 9\), and dividing by \(3\) gives \(y < -\frac{4}{3}x + 3\). Since the inequality simplifies to \(y\) being less than the expression, the shaded solution is below the boundary line.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In graphing the inequality \(-2x < 10\), the shaded solution would be _____ the boundary line.
qs.s: Dividing both sides by \(-2\) reverses the inequality to yield \(x > -5\). Because the boundary line \(x = -5\) is vertical, the inequality \(x > -5\) represents the half-plane to the right of the boundary line.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In graphing the inequality \(3x - 5y > 15\), the shaded solution would be _____ the boundary line.
qs.s: Subtracting \(3x\) gives \(-5y > -3x + 15\), and dividing by \(-5\) reverses the inequality to \(y < \frac{3}{5}x - 3\). Since \(y\) is less than the expression, the shaded solution is below the boundary line.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In graphing the inequality \(2x - y < 7\), the shaded solution would be _____ the boundary line.
qs.s: Subtracting \(2x\) gives \(-y < -2x + 7\), and dividing by \(-1\) reverses the inequality symbol to yield \(y > 2x - 7\). Since \(y\) is greater than the expression, the shaded solution is above the boundary line.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In graphing the inequality \(2(4x - 3y) - 5(x + 2y) > 17 - 4(x - y)\), the shaded solution would be _____ the boundary line.
