qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(3x - 16y > -4x + 4y + 17\), which rearranges to \(-20y > -7x + 17\). Dividing by \(-20\) reverses the inequality to \(y < \frac{7}{20}x - \frac{17}{20}\), so the shaded solution is below the boundary line.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In graphing the inequality \(4(x - 2y) + 3(3x + y) > 5(x - y) - 24\), the shaded solution would be _____ the boundary line.
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(13x - 5y > 5x - 5y - 24\), and adding \(5y\) eliminates the \(y\)-terms to leave \(8x > -24\), or \(x > -3\). Since the boundary line \(x = -3\) is vertical, the solution is the region to the right of the boundary line.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In graphing the inequality \(\frac{x - 3y}{4} - \frac{2x + y}{6} < 1\), the shaded solution would be _____ the boundary line.
qs.s: Multiplying by the common denominator \(12\) yields \(3(x - 3y) - 2(2x + y) < 12\), which simplifies to \(-11y < x + 12\). Dividing by \(-11\) reverses the inequality to \(y > -\frac{1}{11}x - \frac{12}{11}\), meaning the shaded solution is above the boundary line.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In graphing the inequality \(3(2x - 5y) + 4x > 2(x - y) + 18\), the shaded solution would be _____ the boundary line.
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms yields \(-13y > -8x + 18\), which simplifies to \(y < \frac{8}{13}x - \frac{18}{13}\) after dividing by \(-13\) and reversing the inequality symbol. Because \(y\) is less than the expression, the shaded solution is below the boundary line.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In graphing the inequality \(15(3x - 2y) - 40 > 25(x - 3y) + 110\), the shaded solution would be _____ the boundary line.
qs.s: Distributing and collecting terms gives \(45y > -20x + 150\), which simplifies to \(y > -\frac{4}{9}x + \frac{10}{3}\) upon dividing by positive \(45\). Because the inequality simplifies to \(y\) being greater than the expression, the shaded solution is above the boundary line.

qs.q: Fill in the blanks. When graphing \(5x - 3y \le 15\), the boundary line is a _____ line and the shaded region is _____ the line.
qs.s: The symbol \(\le\) indicates a solid boundary line. Rearranging gives \(-3y \le -5x + 15\), and dividing by \(-3\) reverses the inequality to \(y \ge \frac{5}{3}x - 5\), so the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Fill in the blanks. When graphing \(3x + y < 5\), the boundary line is a _____ line and the shaded region is _____ the line.
qs.s: Since the inequality uses \(<\), the boundary line is dashed. Subtracting \(3x\) from both sides gives \(y < -3x + 5\), indicating that the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Fill in the blanks. When graphing \(3x - 2y < 6\), the boundary line is a _____ line and the shaded region is _____ the line.
qs.s: The strict inequality \(<\) means the boundary line is dashed. Rewriting in slope-intercept form gives \(-2y < -3x + 6\), and dividing by \(-2\) reverses the inequality to \(y > \frac{3}{2}x - 3\), so the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Fill in the blanks. When graphing \(x + 2y \le 8\), the boundary line is a _____ line and the shaded region is _____ the line.
qs.s: The inequality includes equality with \(\le\), so the boundary line is solid. Solving for \(y\) gives \(2y \le -x + 8\), or \(y \le -\frac{1}{2}x + 4\), which means the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Fill in the blanks. When graphing \(2x - y \ge 4\), the boundary line is a _____ line and the shaded region is _____ the line.
qs.s: Because the inequality includes \(\ge\), the boundary line is solid. Dividing \(-y \ge -2x + 4\) by \(-1\) flips the inequality to \(y \le 2x - 4\), meaning the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Fill in the blanks. When graphing \(\frac{3x + 2y}{5} - \frac{x + 4y}{2} > 3\), the boundary line is a _____ line and the shaded region is _____ the line.
qs.s: Multiplying by \(10\) gives \(2(3x + 2y) - 5(x + 4y) > 30\), which simplifies to \(x - 16y > 30\). Dividing \(-16y > -x + 30\) by \(-16\) reverses the inequality to \(y < \frac{1}{16}x - \frac{15}{8}\), so the boundary line is dashed and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Fill in the blanks. When graphing \(\frac{2x + 3y}{4} - \frac{5x + 7y}{6} \ge 2\), the boundary line is a _____ line and the shaded region is _____ the line.
qs.s: Multiplying by \(12\) produces \(3(2x + 3y) - 2(5x + 7y) \ge 24\), which simplifies to \(-4x - 5y \ge 24\). Dividing \(-5y \ge 4x + 24\) by \(-5\) reverses the inequality to \(y \le -\frac{4}{5}x - \frac{24}{5}\), indicating a solid boundary line with shading below the line.

qs.q: Fill in the blanks. When graphing \(3(3x + 2y - 4) - 4(x - y + 1) \le 2(x + 7y) - 6\), the boundary line is a _____ line and the shaded region is _____ the line.
qs.s: Simplifying both sides gives \(5x + 10y - 16 \le 2x + 14y - 6\), which rearranges to \(-4y \le -3x + 10\). Dividing by \(-4\) reverses the inequality to \(y \ge \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{5}{2}\), meaning the boundary line is solid and the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Fill in the blanks. When graphing \(4(x - 2y) + 9 \ge 2(5x - y) - 3\), the boundary line is a _____ line and the shaded region is _____ the line.
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(4x - 8y + 9 \ge 10x - 2y - 3\), which simplifies to \(-6y \ge 6x - 12\). Dividing by \(-6\) flips the inequality to \(y \le -x + 2\), so the boundary line is solid and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Fill in the blanks. When graphing \(5(2x - y + 3) - 3(x + 2y) < 2(x - 5y) + 27\), the boundary line is a _____ line and the shaded region is _____ the line.
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms yields \(7x - 11y + 15 < 2x - 10y + 27\), which simplifies to \(-y < -5x + 12\). Dividing by \(-1\) reverses the inequality to \(y > 5x - 12\), indicating a dashed boundary line with shading above the line.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. The boundary line in \(5x - 2y > 10\) would be a _____ line.
qs.s: Because the inequality uses a strict inequality symbol (\(>\)), points on the boundary line are not included in the solution set, so the boundary line is drawn as a dashed line.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. When selecting a test point to determine which side of a boundary line to shade, the point must not lie _____ the boundary line.
qs.s: Rule 2 for graphing linear inequalities states that a test point may be chosen anywhere in the plane as long as it does not lie directly on the boundary line itself.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. When graphing the linear inequality \(y > 3x - 4\), the solution region is shaded _____ the boundary line.
qs.s: Since the inequality is in slope-intercept form with \(y > 3x - 4\), the \(y\)-values are greater than those on the line, so the region above the boundary line is shaded.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. The graph of a linear inequality in two variables is a region of the coordinate plane called a _____.
qs.s: By definition, the graph of a linear inequality in two variables is a half-plane bounded by a straight line.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. The boundary line in \(4x + 3y \le 12\) would be a _____ line.
qs.s: Because the inequality includes equality (\(\le\)), points on the boundary line are included in the solution set, so the boundary line is drawn as a solid line.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. After simplifying \(6(x - 2y) + 5 \le 4(3 - 3y) - 2x + 1\), the boundary line is vertical, and the solution region is the _____ half-plane.
qs.s: The \(y\)-terms cancel when simplified to yield \(8x \le 8\) or \(x \le 1\). Since \(x\) is less than or equal to \(1\), the solution set forms the left half-plane.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. After rewriting \(4(x - 3y) + 7 \le 2(5 - y) - 6x\) in slope-intercept form, the solution region is shaded _____ the boundary line.
qs.s: Simplifying gives \(-10y \le -10x + 3\), and dividing by \(-10\) inverts the inequality to \(y \ge x - \frac{3}{10}\), which indicates shading above the boundary line.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. After simplifying \(4(3x - 2y) - 3(4x + y - 2) < 28\), the boundary line is horizontal, and the solution region is the _____ half-plane.
qs.s: The \(x\)-terms cancel to leave \(-11y < 22\), and dividing by \(-11\) inverts the inequality to \(y > -2\), which represents the upper half-plane.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. After rewriting \(3(2x - 5y) - 4(x - 2y + 3) > 14\) in slope-intercept form, the solution region is shaded _____ the boundary line.
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms yields \(-7y > -2x + 26\), and dividing by \(-7\) inverts the inequality to \(y < \frac{2}{7}x - \frac{26}{7}\), which indicates shading below the boundary line.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. When graphing the inequality \(3(3x - 2y + 4) - 2(x + 5y - 1) > 5\), the shaded solution region _____ the test point \((0, 0)\).
qs.s: Substituting \((0, 0)\) into the expression yields \(3(4) - 2(-1) = 14\), and because \(14 > 5\) is a true statement, the shaded region contains the test point \((0, 0)\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank. For a system of linear inequalities, the region containing all ordered pairs that satisfy every inequality at the same time is called the _____ region.
qs.s: The set of all points that satisfy all inequalities in a system simultaneously forms the solution region.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. When using a test point to graph a linear inequality, if the test point makes the inequality true, shade the side of the boundary line that _____ the test point.
qs.s: If the test point satisfies the inequality, the entire half-plane containing that test point represents solutions and must be shaded.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. When graphing a linear inequality with the symbol \(\le\) or \(\ge\), the boundary line is drawn as a _____ line.
qs.s: A solid line is used when the inequality includes equality (\(\le\) or \(\ge\)) because the points on the boundary line are part of the solution.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. The graph of a linear inequality in two variables is a region called a _____ -plane.
qs.s: A straight boundary line divides the two-dimensional coordinate plane into two regions, each known as a half-plane.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. When graphing a linear inequality with a strict inequality symbol (\(<\) or \(>\)), the boundary line is drawn as a _____ line.
qs.s: A dashed line is used for strict inequalities (\(<\) or \(>\)) to show that points on the boundary line are not included in the solution set.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. To graph the boundary line for the inequality \(3(2x - 5) - 4(y + 2) < 7\), simplifying it into the standard form \(6x - 4y = c\) yields \(c = \_\_\_\_\).
qs.s: Expanding the expression gives \(6x - 15 - 4y - 8 = 7\), which simplifies to \(6x - 4y - 23 = 7\); adding 23 to both sides results in \(6x - 4y = 30\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In the system of linear inequalities given by \(4x - 9y < 36\), \(2x + 5y \ge -10\), \(y > -4\), and \(3x + y < 15\), exactly _____ of the boundary lines must be drawn as dashed lines.
qs.s: Inequalities with strict inequality symbols (\(<\) and \(>\)) use dashed boundary lines; since \(4x - 9y < 36\), \(y > -4\), and \(3x + y < 15\) are strict, exactly 3 lines are dashed.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. For the system of linear inequalities \(3x + 2y \ge 26\) and \(x - 2y < -10\), the intersection point of the two boundary lines, \((\_\_\_\_, 7)\), cannot be used as a test point for either inequality.
qs.s: The intersection point lies on the boundary line \(x - 2y = -10\). Substituting \(y = 7\) gives \(x - 2(7) = -10\), so \(x - 14 = -10\), which yields \(x = 4\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank. When choosing a test point to determine the shaded region for the linear inequality \(7x - 4y > 28\), the point \((8, \_\_\_\_)\) cannot be used because it lies directly on the boundary line.
qs.s: Points on the boundary line satisfy \(7x - 4y = 28\). Substituting \(x = 8\) gives \(7(8) - 4y = 28\), so \(56 - 4y = 28\), which yields \(y = 7\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank. When rewriting the linear inequality \(5x - 8y \le -72\) in slope-intercept form to determine which half-plane to shade, the inequality becomes \(y \ge \frac{5}{8}x + \_\_\_\_\), indicating that the region above the boundary line is shaded.
qs.s: Subtracting \(5x\) gives \(-8y \le -5x - 72\), and dividing by \(-8\) reverses the inequality symbol to yield \(y \ge \frac{5}{8}x + 9\).

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(3x - 4y > 12\), which boundary line and shaded region correctly represent the solution?
qs.a: The region below the dashed boundary line
d: The region above the dashed boundary line
The region below the solid boundary line
The region above the solid boundary line
qs.s: Dividing \(-4y > -3x + 12\) by \(-4\) reverses the inequality sign to give \(y < \frac{3}{4}x - 3\). The boundary line is dashed because the inequality is strict, and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(4x - 3y \le 12\), which boundary line and shaded region correctly represent the solution?
qs.a: The region above the solid boundary line
d: The region below the solid boundary line
The region above the dashed boundary line
The region below the dashed boundary line
qs.s: Rearranging gives \(-3y \le -4x + 12\), which simplifies to \(y \ge \frac{4}{3}x - 4\) upon dividing by \(-3\) and reversing the inequality. The boundary line is solid due to the non-strict inequality, and shading is above the line.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(x + 3y > 6\), which boundary line and shaded region correctly represent the solution?
qs.a: The region above the dashed boundary line
d: The region below the dashed boundary line
The region above the solid boundary line
The region below the solid boundary line
qs.s: Rewriting in slope-intercept form gives \(y > -\frac{1}{3}x + 2\). Because the inequality is strict (\(>\)), the boundary line is dashed, and the solution region lies above the boundary line.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(3x + y \le 6\), which boundary line and shaded region correctly represent the solution?
qs.a: The region below the solid boundary line
d: The region above the solid boundary line
The region below the dashed boundary line
The region above the dashed boundary line
qs.s: Rewriting the inequality gives \(y \le -3x + 6\). Because equality is included (\(\le\)), the boundary line is solid, and since \(y\) is less than or equal to the expression, the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(x - 2y < 4\), which boundary line and shaded region correctly represent the solution?
qs.a: The region above the dashed boundary line
d: The region below the dashed boundary line
The region above the solid boundary line
The region below the solid boundary line
qs.s: Isolating \(y\) yields \(-2y < -x + 4\), which becomes \(y > \frac{1}{2}x - 2\) after dividing by \(-2\) and reversing the inequality sign. Since the inequality is strict (\(<\)), the boundary line is dashed and the region above it is shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(3(x - 2y) + 4 \ge 5(x - y) - 6\), which boundary line and shaded region correctly represent the solution?
qs.a: The region below the solid boundary line
d: The region above the solid boundary line
The region below the dashed boundary line
The region above the dashed boundary line
qs.s: Expanding gives \(3x - 6y + 4 \ge 5x - 5y - 6\), which simplifies to \(-y \ge 2x - 10\). Dividing by \(-1\) reverses the inequality to \(y \le -2x + 10\), so the solution is shaded below the solid boundary line.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(\frac{x + 2}{3} - \frac{2y - 1}{4} > \frac{5}{6}\), which boundary line and shaded region correctly represent the solution?
qs.a: The region below the dashed boundary line
d: The region above the dashed boundary line
The region below the solid boundary line
The region above the solid boundary line
qs.s: Multiplying by the LCD of 12 gives \(4(x + 2) - 3(2y - 1) > 10\), simplifying to \(-6y > -4x - 1\). Dividing by \(-6\) flips the inequality to \(y < \frac{2}{3}x + \frac{1}{6}\), requiring a dashed boundary line with shading below.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(5(2x - 3y + 4) \le 2(4x - 6y) + 14\), which boundary line and shaded region correctly represent the solution?
qs.a: The region above the solid boundary line
d: The region below the solid boundary line
The region above the dashed boundary line
The region below the dashed boundary line
qs.s: Expanding yields \(10x - 15y + 20 \le 8x - 12y + 14\), which simplifies to \(-3y \le -2x - 6\). Dividing by \(-3\) reverses the inequality to \(y \ge \frac{2}{3}x + 2\), meaning the boundary line is solid and the solution region is above it.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(2(x - 3y) - 3(x + 1) < 5 - 2y\), which boundary line and shaded region correctly represent the solution?
qs.a: The region above the dashed boundary line
d: The region below the dashed boundary line
The region above the solid boundary line
The region below the solid boundary line
qs.s: Expanding both sides yields \(2x - 6y - 3x - 3 < 5 - 2y\), which reduces to \(-4y < x + 8\). Dividing by \(-4\) reverses the inequality to \(y > -\frac{1}{4}x - 2\), so the boundary line is dashed with shading above.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(\frac{3x - 5}{2} - \frac{y + 4}{5} \ge x - 1\), which boundary line and shaded region correctly represent the solution?
qs.a: The region below the solid boundary line
d: The region above the solid boundary line
The region below the dashed boundary line
The region above the dashed boundary line
qs.s: Multiplying by the LCD of 10 gives \(5(3x - 5) - 2(y + 4) \ge 10(x - 1)\), which simplifies to \(-2y \ge -5x + 23\). Dividing by \(-2\) reverses the inequality to \(y \le \frac{5}{2}x - \frac{23}{2}\), indicating a solid boundary line with shading below.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(3x - y \ge 6\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region below the solid line \(y = 3x - 6\)
d: The region above the solid line \(y = 3x - 6\)
The region below the dashed line \(y = 3x - 6\)
The region above the dashed line \(y = 3x - 6\)
qs.s: Rewriting the inequality in slope-intercept form gives \(-y \ge -3x + 6\), which becomes \(y \le 3x - 6\) after reversing the inequality sign when dividing by \(-1\). Because of the '\(\le\)' sign, the boundary line is solid and the shaded solution region is below the line.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(x - 2y \le 6\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region above the solid line \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 3\)
d: The region below the solid line \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 3\)
The region above the dashed line \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 3\)
The region below the dashed line \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 3\)
qs.s: Rewriting in slope-intercept form gives \(-2y \le -x + 6\), which becomes \(y \ge \frac{1}{2}x - 3\) when dividing by \(-2\) and reversing the inequality symbol. Because the inequality includes equality (\(\ge\)), the boundary line is solid and the solution region lies above the line.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(4x + y > -2\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region above the dashed line \(y = -4x - 2\)
d: The region below the dashed line \(y = -4x - 2\)
The region above the solid line \(y = -4x - 2\)
The region below the solid line \(y = -4x - 2\)
qs.s: Subtracting \(4x\) from both sides gives \(y > -4x - 2\). The strict inequality (\(>\)) indicates a dashed boundary line, and \(y\) being greater means the shaded region is above the line.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(3x - 4y > 12\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region below the dashed line \(y = \frac{3}{4}x - 3\)
d: The region above the dashed line \(y = \frac{3}{4}x - 3\)
The region below the solid line \(y = \frac{3}{4}x - 3\)
The region above the solid line \(y = \frac{3}{4}x - 3\)
qs.s: Subtracting \(3x\) yields \(-4y > -3x + 12\), and dividing by \(-4\) reverses the inequality to \(y < \frac{3}{4}x - 3\). The boundary line is dashed due to '\(<\)', and the solution region is below the line.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(x + 2y < 4\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region below the dashed line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2\)
d: The region above the dashed line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2\)
The region below the solid line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2\)
The region above the solid line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2\)
qs.s: Isolating \(y\) gives \(2y < -x + 4\), or \(y < -\frac{1}{2}x + 2\). Since the inequality is strict (\(<\)), the boundary line is dashed and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(\frac{3x + y}{2} - \frac{x + 4y}{3} \ge 5\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region below the solid line \(y = \frac{7}{5}x - 6\)
d: The region above the solid line \(y = \frac{7}{5}x - 6\)
The region below the dashed line \(y = \frac{7}{5}x - 6\)
The region above the dashed line \(y = \frac{7}{5}x - 6\)
qs.s: Multiplying the entire inequality by 6 clears the denominators to yield \(3(3x + y) - 2(x + 4y) \ge 30\), which simplifies to \(7x - 5y \ge 30\), or \(-5y \ge -7x + 30\). Dividing by \(-5\) gives \(y \le \frac{7}{5}x - 6\), so the boundary line is solid and the shaded region is below.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(4(x - y) - 3 > 7x - y + 6\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region below the dashed line \(y = -x - 3\)
d: The region above the dashed line \(y = -x - 3\)
The region below the solid line \(y = -x - 3\)
The region above the solid line \(y = -x - 3\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \(4x - 4y - 3 > 7x - y + 6\), which simplifies to \(-3y > 3x + 9\). Dividing by \(-3\) reverses the inequality to \(y < -x - 3\), indicating a dashed boundary line with shading below.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(-3(x + 2y - 5) \ge 2(2x - y + 1) + 5\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region below the solid line \(y = -\frac{7}{4}x + 2\)
d: The region above the solid line \(y = -\frac{7}{4}x + 2\)
The region below the dashed line \(y = -\frac{7}{4}x + 2\)
The region above the dashed line \(y = -\frac{7}{4}x + 2\)
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(-3x - 6y + 15 \ge 4x - 2y + 7\), which simplifies to \(-4y \ge 7x - 8\). Dividing by \(-4\) reverses the inequality to \(y \le -\frac{7}{4}x + 2\), requiring a solid boundary line with shading below.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(5(2x - 3y + 4) - 2(x - y) < 4(x - 2y) + 45\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region above the dashed line \(y = \frac{4}{5}x - 5\)
d: The region below the dashed line \(y = \frac{4}{5}x - 5\)
The region above the solid line \(y = \frac{4}{5}x - 5\)
The region below the solid line \(y = \frac{4}{5}x - 5\)
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms yields \(8x - 13y + 20 < 4x - 8y + 45\), which simplifies to \(-5y < -4x + 25\). Dividing by \(-5\) flips the inequality to \(y > \frac{4}{5}x - 5\), meaning the line is dashed and the region above it is shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(\frac{x - 2y}{4} - \frac{2x - y}{6} \le 1\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region above the solid line \(y = -\frac{1}{4}x - 3\)
d: The region below the solid line \(y = -\frac{1}{4}x - 3\)
The region above the dashed line \(y = -\frac{1}{4}x - 3\)
The region below the dashed line \(y = -\frac{1}{4}x - 3\)
qs.s: Multiplying by the LCD 12 yields \(3(x - 2y) - 2(2x - y) \le 12\), which simplifies to \(-x - 4y \le 12\), or \(-4y \le x + 12\). Dividing by \(-4\) gives \(y \ge -\frac{1}{4}x - 3\), which represents the region above the solid boundary line.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(4x - 5y < 20\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region above the dashed boundary line \(4x - 5y = 20\)
d: The region below the dashed boundary line \(4x - 5y = 20\)
The region above the solid boundary line \(4x - 5y = 20\)
The region below the solid boundary line \(4x - 5y = 20\)
qs.s: Solving for \(y\) yields \(-5y < -4x + 20\), which reverses to \(y > \frac{4}{5}x - 4\) upon dividing by \(-5\). The strict inequality \(<\) means the boundary line is dashed, and \(y >\) indicates shading above the line.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(x - 4y \le -8\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region above the solid boundary line \(x - 4y = -8\)
d: The region below the solid boundary line \(x - 4y = -8\)
The region above the dashed boundary line \(x - 4y = -8\)
The region below the dashed boundary line \(x - 4y = -8\)
qs.s: Isolating \(y\) gives \(-4y \le -x - 8\), and dividing by \(-4\) reverses the inequality to \(y \ge \frac{1}{4}x + 2\). The non-strict inequality \(\le\) means the boundary line is solid, and \(y \ge\) indicates shading above the line.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(-5x - 2y > 10\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region below the dashed boundary line \(-5x - 2y = 10\)
d: The region above the dashed boundary line \(-5x - 2y = 10\)
The region below the solid boundary line \(-5x - 2y = 10\)
The region above the solid boundary line \(-5x - 2y = 10\)
qs.s: Rearranging the inequality gives \(-2y > 5x + 10\), so dividing by \(-2\) reverses the inequality to \(y < -\frac{5}{2}x - 5\). The strict inequality \(>\) requires a dashed boundary line, and \(y <\) indicates shading below the line.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(3x - 2y \ge -6\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region below the solid boundary line \(3x - 2y = -6\)
d: The region above the solid boundary line \(3x - 2y = -6\)
The region below the dashed boundary line \(3x - 2y = -6\)
The region above the dashed boundary line \(3x - 2y = -6\)
qs.s: Isolating \(y\) gives \(-2y \ge -3x - 6\), which simplifies to \(y \le \frac{3}{2}x + 3\) after dividing by \(-2\) and reversing the inequality symbol. Since the inequality is \(\ge\), the boundary line is solid, and \(y \le\) indicates shading below the line.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(2x + 3y \ge 6\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region above the solid boundary line \(2x + 3y = 6\)
d: The region below the solid boundary line \(2x + 3y = 6\)
The region above the dashed boundary line \(2x + 3y = 6\)
The region below the dashed boundary line \(2x + 3y = 6\)
qs.s: Rewriting \(2x + 3y \ge 6\) in slope-intercept form gives \(y \ge -\frac{2}{3}x + 2\). Because the inequality includes \(\ge\), the boundary line \(2x + 3y = 6\) is solid, and since \(y\) is greater than or equal to the expression, the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(3(2x - 5y + 4) - 2(x - 3y) < 18\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region above the dashed boundary line \(4x - 9y = 6\)
d: The region below the dashed boundary line \(4x - 9y = 6\)
The region above the solid boundary line \(4x - 9y = 6\)
The region below the solid boundary line \(4x - 9y = 6\)
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms yields \(4x - 9y + 12 < 18\), which simplifies to \(4x - 9y < 6\), or \(y > \frac{4}{9}x - \frac{2}{3}\). Because the inequality is strict, the boundary line \(4x - 9y = 6\) is dashed, and \(y >\) means shading above the line.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(15x - 8(2y - 5) \le 3(x + 4y) - 80\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region above the solid boundary line \(3x - 7y = -30\)
d: The region below the solid boundary line \(3x - 7y = -30\)
The region above the dashed boundary line \(3x - 7y = -30\)
The region below the dashed boundary line \(3x - 7y = -30\)
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(15x - 16y + 40 \le 3x + 12y - 80\), which simplifies to \(12x - 28y \le -120\), or \(3x - 7y \le -30\). Solving for \(y\) gives \(y \ge \frac{3}{7}x + \frac{30}{7}\), meaning the region above the solid boundary line is shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(\frac{x - 3y}{5} - \frac{2x - y}{2} > 3\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region below the dashed boundary line \(8x + y = -30\)
d: The region above the dashed boundary line \(8x + y = -30\)
The region below the solid boundary line \(8x + y = -30\)
The region above the solid boundary line \(8x + y = -30\)
qs.s: Multiplying by 10 yields \(2(x - 3y) - 5(2x - y) > 30\), which expands to \(-8x - y > 30\), or \(y < -8x - 30\). Since the inequality is strict, the boundary line \(8x + y = -30\) is dashed, and \(y <\) indicates shading below the line.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(\frac{3x - 2}{4} - \frac{y + 1}{6} \ge \frac{5}{12}\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region below the solid boundary line \(9x - 2y = 13\)
d: The region above the solid boundary line \(9x - 2y = 13\)
The region below the dashed boundary line \(9x - 2y = 13\)
The region above the dashed boundary line \(9x - 2y = 13\)
qs.s: Multiplying the entire inequality by 12 clears denominators to give \(3(3x - 2) - 2(y + 1) \ge 5\), which simplifies to \(9x - 2y \ge 13\), or \(y \le \frac{9}{2}x - \frac{13}{2}\). The boundary line is solid because of \(\ge\), and \(y \le\) indicates shading below the line.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(7(2x - y + 3) - 4(x - 3y - 2) \ge 5(x + 2y) + 49\), which region should be shaded?
qs.a: The region below the solid boundary line \(x - y = 4\)
d: The region above the solid boundary line \(x - y = 4\)
The region below the dashed boundary line \(x - y = 4\)
The region above the dashed boundary line \(x - y = 4\)
qs.s: Expanding and collecting like terms yields \(10x + 5y + 29 \ge 5x + 10y + 49\), which simplifies to \(5x - 5y \ge 20\), or \(x - y \ge 4\). Solving for \(y\) gives \(y \le x - 4\), so the region below the solid boundary line \(x - y = 4\) is shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(y - 3x \le 0\), which region should be shaded?
qs.s: Adding \(3x\) to both sides gives \(y \le 3x\). Since \(y\) is less than or equal to \(3x\), the region below the boundary line \(y = 3x\) should be shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(-2y \le x\), which region should be shaded?
qs.s: Dividing both sides by \(-2\) reverses the inequality symbol, yielding \(y \ge -\frac{1}{2}x\). Therefore, the region above the boundary line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x\) should be shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(x > 4y\), which region should be shaded?
qs.s: Rewriting \(x > 4y\) in slope-intercept form gives \(y < \frac{1}{4}x\). Because \(y\) is less than \(\frac{1}{4}x\), the region below the boundary line \(y = \frac{1}{4}x\) should be shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(3x < 2y\), which region should be shaded?
qs.s: Solving for \(y\) yields \(y > \frac{3}{2}x\). Since \(y\) is strictly greater than \(\frac{3}{2}x\), the region above the boundary line \(y = \frac{3}{2}x\) should be shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(x + 3y > 0\), which region should be shaded?
qs.s: Subtracting \(x\) gives \(3y > -x\), and dividing by \(3\) gives \(y > -\frac{1}{3}x\). Since \(y\) is greater than \(-\frac{1}{3}x\), the region above the boundary line \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x\) should be shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(5(x - y) - 2 \le 2(x + y) + 12\), which region should be shaded?
qs.s: Expanding yields \(5x - 5y - 2 \le 2x + 2y + 12\), which simplifies to \(-7y \le -3x + 14\). Dividing by \(-7\) reverses the inequality to \(y \ge \frac{3}{7}x - 2\), so the region above the boundary line \(y = \frac{3}{7}x - 2\) should be shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{2}y \ge 3\), which region should be shaded?
qs.s: Subtracting \(\frac{3}{4}x\) gives \(-\frac{1}{2}y \ge -\frac{3}{4}x + 3\), and multiplying by \(-2\) reverses the inequality to \(y \le \frac{3}{2}x - 6\). Therefore, shade the region below the boundary line \(y = \frac{3}{2}x - 6\).

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(2(x - 4) - 5y > 3x + 7\), which region should be shaded?
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging terms gives \(-5y > x + 15\), and dividing by \(-5\) reverses the inequality symbol to \(y < -\frac{1}{5}x - 3\). Thus, the region below the boundary line \(y = -\frac{1}{5}x - 3\) should be shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(7x - 4(y + 3) < 2x + 8\), which region should be shaded?
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying gives \(-4y < -5x + 20\), and dividing by \(-4\) reverses the inequality to \(y > \frac{5}{4}x - 5\). Hence, the region above the boundary line \(y = \frac{5}{4}x - 5\) must be shaded.

qs.q: To complete the graph of the linear inequality \(4x - 3y \le 12\), which region should be shaded?
