Solid line \(y = -x + 5\), shaded below the line
qs.s: Subtracting \(x\) gives \(-y \ge -x + 5\), and dividing by \(-1\) reverses the inequality to \(y \le x - 5\). Thus, the boundary line is solid and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the inequality \(2x + y \le 4\) on the coordinate plane?
qs.a: Solid line \(y = -2x + 4\), shaded below the line
d: Solid line \(y = -2x + 4\), shaded above the line
Dashed line \(y = -2x + 4\), shaded below the line
Solid line \(y = 2x + 4\), shaded below the line
qs.s: Subtracting \(2x\) from both sides gives \(y \le -2x + 4\). The boundary line is solid because the inequality includes \(\le\), and the half-plane below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the inequality \(-3x + y < 2\) on the coordinate plane?
qs.a: Dashed line \(y = 3x + 2\), shaded below the line
d: Dashed line \(y = 3x + 2\), shaded above the line
Solid line \(y = 3x + 2\), shaded below the line
Dashed line \(y = -3x + 2\), shaded below the line
qs.s: Adding \(3x\) to both sides gives \(y < 3x + 2\). Because the inequality is strict (\(<\)), the boundary line is dashed and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the inequality \(5x + y \ge -5\) on the coordinate plane?
qs.a: Solid line \(y = -5x - 5\), shaded above the line
d: Solid line \(y = -5x - 5\), shaded below the line
Dashed line \(y = -5x - 5\), shaded above the line
Solid line \(y = 5x - 5\), shaded above the line
qs.s: Subtracting \(5x\) gives \(y \ge -5x - 5\). Equality is included (\(\ge\)), so the boundary line is solid, and the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the inequality \(3x - 4(y + 2) \ge 11x - 32\) on the coordinate plane?
qs.a: Solid line \(y = -2x + 6\), shaded below the line
d: Solid line \(y = -2x + 6\), shaded above the line
Dashed line \(y = -2x + 6\), shaded below the line
Solid line \(y = -2x - 6\), shaded below the line
qs.s: Expanding yields \(3x - 4y - 8 \ge 11x - 32\), so \(-4y \ge 8x - 24\). Dividing by \(-4\) reverses the inequality to \(y \le -2x + 6\), giving a solid boundary line shaded below.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the inequality \(5(y - 1) - 3x > 2(y + 5) + 6x\) on the coordinate plane?
qs.a: Dashed line \(y = 3x + 5\), shaded above the line
d: Dashed line \(y = 3x + 5\), shaded below the line
Solid line \(y = 3x + 5\), shaded above the line
Dashed line \(y = x + 5\), shaded above the line
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(5y - 5 - 3x > 2y + 10 + 6x\), which simplifies to \(3y > 9x + 15\), or \(y > 3x + 5\). The boundary line is dashed and the region above is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the inequality \(-2(3x - y) + 7x < 4(y - 2) + 2\) on the coordinate plane?
qs.a: Dashed line \(y = \frac{1}{2}x + 3\), shaded above the line
d: Dashed line \(y = \frac{1}{2}x + 3\), shaded below the line
Solid line \(y = \frac{1}{2}x + 3\), shaded above the line
Dashed line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 3\), shaded above the line
qs.s: Expanding yields \(-6x + 2y + 7x < 4y - 8 + 2\), simplifying to \(x + 2y < 4y - 6\) and \(-2y < -x - 6\). Dividing by \(-2\) gives \(y > \frac{1}{2}x + 3\), which represents a dashed boundary line shaded above.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the inequality \(4(x + 3) - 6y \le 2x + 30\) on the coordinate plane?
qs.a: Solid line \(y = \frac{1}{3}x - 3\), shaded above the line
d: Solid line \(y = \frac{1}{3}x - 3\), shaded below the line
Dashed line \(y = \frac{1}{3}x - 3\), shaded above the line
Solid line \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x - 3\), shaded above the line
qs.s: Expanding gives \(4x + 12 - 6y \le 2x + 30\), which simplifies to \(-6y \le -2x + 18\). Dividing by \(-6\) reverses the inequality to \(y \ge \frac{1}{3}x - 3\), resulting in a solid boundary line with shading above.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the inequality \(\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{2}y \le 3\) on the coordinate plane?
qs.a: Solid line \(y = \frac{3}{2}x - 6\), shaded above the line
d: Solid line \(y = \frac{3}{2}x - 6\), shaded below the line
Dashed line \(y = \frac{3}{2}x - 6\), shaded above the line
Solid line \(y = -\frac{3}{2}x - 6\), shaded above the line
qs.s: Multiplying through by 4 gives \(3x - 2y \le 12\), which leads to \(-2y \le -3x + 12\). Dividing by \(-2\) reverses the sign to \(y \ge \frac{3}{2}x - 6\), indicating a solid line shaded above.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the linear inequality \(4x - y < 2\)?
qs.a: Dashed line \(y = 4x - 2\), shaded above the line
d: Dashed line \(y = 4x - 2\), shaded below the line
Solid line \(y = 4x - 2\), shaded above the line
Dashed line \(y = -4x + 2\), shaded above the line
qs.s: Subtracting \(4x\) gives \(-y < -4x + 2\), and dividing by \(-1\) reverses the inequality to \(y > 4x - 2\). Thus, the boundary line \(y = 4x - 2\) is dashed and the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the linear inequality \(x + 2y \le 4\)?
qs.a: Solid line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2\), shaded below the line
d: Solid line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2\), shaded above the line
Dashed line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2\), shaded below the line
Solid line \(y = -x + 2\), shaded below the line
qs.s: Subtracting \(x\) and dividing by \(2\) gives \(y \le -\frac{1}{2}x + 2\). Since the inequality includes equality, the boundary line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2\) is solid, and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the linear inequality \(x - 3y \ge 6\)?
qs.a: Solid line \(y = \frac{1}{3}x - 2\), shaded below the line
d: Solid line \(y = \frac{1}{3}x - 2\), shaded above the line
Dashed line \(y = \frac{1}{3}x - 2\), shaded below the line
Solid line \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x + 2\), shaded below the line
qs.s: Subtracting \(x\) gives \(-3y \ge -x + 6\), and dividing by \(-3\) reverses the inequality to \(y \le \frac{1}{3}x - 2\). The boundary line \(y = \frac{1}{3}x - 2\) is solid and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the linear inequality \(5x + y > -2\)?
qs.a: Dashed line \(y = -5x - 2\), shaded above the line
d: Dashed line \(y = -5x - 2\), shaded below the line
Solid line \(y = -5x - 2\), shaded above the line
Dashed line \(y = 5x - 2\), shaded above the line
qs.s: Subtracting \(5x\) isolates \(y\) to give \(y > -5x - 2\). Because the inequality is strict, the boundary line \(y = -5x - 2\) is dashed, and the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the linear inequality \(3x - y > 6\)?
qs.a: Dashed line \(y = 3x - 6\), shaded below the line
d: Dashed line \(y = 3x - 6\), shaded above the line
Solid line \(y = 3x - 6\), shaded below the line
Dashed line \(y = -3x + 6\), shaded below the line
qs.s: Rewriting in slope-intercept form gives \(-y > -3x + 6\), which simplifies to \(y < 3x - 6\) after reversing the inequality when dividing by \(-1\). Because the inequality is strict, the boundary line \(y = 3x - 6\) is dashed, and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the inequality \(\frac{3x - 2}{4} - \frac{y}{2} > x - 1\)?
qs.a: Dashed line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 1\), shaded below the line
d: Dashed line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 1\), shaded above the line
Solid line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 1\), shaded below the line
Dashed line \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 1\), shaded below the line
qs.s: Multiplying the entire inequality by \(4\) yields \(3x - 2 - 2y > 4x - 4\), which rearranges to \(-2y > x - 2\). Dividing by \(-2\) reverses the inequality to \(y < -\frac{1}{2}x + 1\), so the boundary line is dashed and shaded below.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the inequality \(\frac{x + 3}{3} - \frac{2y - 1}{4} \ge \frac{x}{2}\)?
qs.a: Solid line \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{5}{2}\), shaded below the line
d: Solid line \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{5}{2}\), shaded above the line
Dashed line \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{5}{2}\), shaded below the line
Solid line \(y = \frac{1}{3}x - \frac{5}{2}\), shaded below the line
qs.s: Multiplying through by \(12\) gives \(4(x + 3) - 3(2y - 1) \ge 6x\), which simplifies to \(4x - 6y + 15 \ge 6x\) or \(-6y \ge 2x - 15\). Dividing by \(-6\) flips the inequality to \(y \le -\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{5}{2}\), meaning a solid boundary line shaded below.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the inequality \(2(x - 3) - 3(y - 1) \le x - y + 1\)?
qs.a: Solid line \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 2\), shaded above the line
d: Solid line \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 2\), shaded below the line
Dashed line \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 2\), shaded above the line
Solid line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2\), shaded above the line
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(2x - 3y - 3 \le x - y + 1\), which simplifies to \(-2y \le -x + 4\). Dividing by \(-2\) reverses the inequality to \(y \ge \frac{1}{2}x - 2\), so the boundary line is solid and shaded above.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the inequality \(4(2x - y) - 3(x - 2y + 1) \le 11\)?
qs.a: Solid line \(y = -\frac{5}{2}x + 7\), shaded below the line
d: Solid line \(y = -\frac{5}{2}x + 7\), shaded above the line
Dashed line \(y = -\frac{5}{2}x + 7\), shaded below the line
Solid line \(y = \frac{5}{2}x + 7\), shaded below the line
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms yields \(5x + 2y - 3 \le 11\), which simplifies to \(2y \le -5x + 14\). Dividing by \(2\) gives \(y \le -\frac{5}{2}x + 7\), producing a solid boundary line shaded below.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the inequality \(5(x - 2y) - 2(3x - y + 4) < 3(x - 2) - 6\)?
qs.a: Dashed line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + \frac{1}{2}\), shaded above the line
d: Dashed line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + \frac{1}{2}\), shaded below the line
Solid line \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + \frac{1}{2}\), shaded above the line
Dashed line \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{1}{2}\), shaded above the line
qs.s: Expanding and collecting terms gives \(-x - 8y - 8 < 3x - 12\), which simplifies to \(-8y < 4x - 4\). Dividing by \(-8\) reverses the inequality to \(y > -\frac{1}{2}x + \frac{1}{2}\), so the boundary line is dashed and shaded above.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the linear inequality \(\frac{2}{3}x - 0.5y < 2\)?
qs.s: Subtracting \(\frac{2}{3}x\) gives \(-\frac{1}{2}y < -\frac{2}{3}x + 2\). Multiplying by \(-2\) reverses the inequality to \(y > \frac{4}{3}x - 4\), representing a dashed boundary line shaded above.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the linear inequality \(0.8x - \frac{1}{2}y \le 2\)?
qs.s: Isolating \(y\) gives \(-\frac{1}{2}y \le -\frac{4}{5}x + 2\). Multiplying by \(-2\) reverses the inequality to \(y \ge \frac{8}{5}x - 4\), which corresponds to a solid boundary line shaded above.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the linear inequality \(0.5x - \frac{3}{4}y \ge 3\)?
qs.s: Subtracting \(0.5x\) gives \(-\frac{3}{4}y \ge -\frac{1}{2}x + 3\). Multiplying by \(-\frac{4}{3}\) reverses the inequality sign to \(y \le \frac{2}{3}x - 4\), which is represented by a solid boundary line shaded below.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the linear inequality \(\frac{1}{2}x + 0.6y < 3\)?
qs.s: Subtracting \(\frac{1}{2}x\) yields \(\frac{3}{5}y < -\frac{1}{2}x + 3\). Multiplying by \(\frac{5}{3}\) gives \(y < -\frac{5}{6}x + 5\), which is represented by a dashed boundary line shaded below.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the linear inequality \(0.6x + \frac{4}{5}y \le 2\)?
qs.s: Subtracting \(0.6x = \frac{3}{5}x\) gives \(\frac{4}{5}y \le -\frac{3}{5}x + 2\). Multiplying by \(\frac{5}{4}\) yields \(y \le -\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{5}{2}\), which is represented by a solid boundary line shaded below.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the linear inequality \(\frac{1}{6}(2x - 9y) - 0.75x \ge 2 - \frac{4}{3}(y + 1)\)?
qs.s: Expanding and grouping terms leads to \(-\frac{1}{6}y \ge \frac{5}{12}x + \frac{2}{3}\). Multiplying by \(-6\) flips the inequality to \(y \le -\frac{5}{2}x - 4\), corresponding to a solid boundary line shaded below.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the linear inequality \(\frac{2}{3}(y - 3) + 0.4x < \frac{5}{6}y - 1.2x + 4\)?
qs.s: Expanding and collecting like terms yields \(-\frac{1}{6}y < -\frac{8}{5}x + 6\). Multiplying by \(-6\) flips the inequality sign to \(y > \frac{48}{5}x - 36\), which corresponds to a dashed line shaded above.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the linear inequality \(0.6(x - 5) - \frac{3}{8}y \ge \frac{1}{4}(x + 2) - 1\)?
qs.s: Expanding gives \(\frac{3}{5}x - 3 - \frac{3}{8}y \ge \frac{1}{4}x - \frac{1}{2}\), which rearranges to \(-\frac{3}{8}y \ge -\frac{7}{20}x + \frac{5}{2}\). Multiplying by \(-\frac{8}{3}\) reverses the inequality to \(y \le \frac{14}{15}x - \frac{20}{3}\), represented by a solid boundary line shaded below.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the linear inequality \(1.5(4 - 2x) + \frac{5}{2}y \le \frac{1}{3}(6y - 9) + 0.8x\)?
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(6 - 3x + \frac{5}{2}y \le 2y - 3 + \frac{4}{5}x\), which simplifies to \(\frac{1}{2}y \le \frac{19}{5}x - 9\). Multiplying by 2 gives \(y \le \frac{38}{5}x - 18\), representing a solid line shaded below.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the linear inequality \(\frac{3x - 2y}{4} - \frac{x + y}{3} > 0.5\)?
qs.s: Multiplying the inequality by 12 yields \(3(3x - 2y) - 4(x + y) > 6\), which simplifies to \(5x - 10y > 6\). Dividing by \(-10\) flips the inequality to \(y < \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{3}{5}\), represented by a dashed line shaded below.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the boundary line and shaded region for the graph of \(\frac{1}{2}x - \frac{1}{2}y \ge 1\)?
qs.s: Multiplying by \(2\) gives \(x - y \ge 2\), which yields \(-y \ge -x + 2\); dividing by \(-1\) reverses the inequality to \(y \le x - 2\). Because equality is included, the boundary line is solid, and \(y \le\) indicates shading below the line.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the boundary line and shaded region for the graph of \(\frac{1}{4}x + \frac{3}{4}y < 3\)?
qs.s: Multiplying the inequality by \(4\) gives \(x + 3y < 12\), which rearranges to \(y < -\frac{1}{3}x + 4\). The strict inequality indicates a dashed boundary line, and \(y <\) means the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the boundary line and shaded region for the graph of \(\frac{2}{5}x + \frac{1}{5}y \le 2\)?
qs.s: Multiplying by \(5\) gives \(2x + y \le 10\), which solves to \(y \le -2x + 10\). The non-strict inequality \(\le\) corresponds to a solid boundary line with the half-plane below shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the boundary line and shaded region for the graph of \(\frac{2}{3}x - \frac{1}{3}y > 1\)?
qs.s: Multiplying by \(3\) yields \(2x - y > 3\), or \(-y > -2x + 3\), which inverts to \(y < 2x - 3\) when dividing by \(-1\). The strict inequality requires a dashed boundary line, and \(y <\) dictates shading below the line.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the boundary line and shaded region for the graph of \(\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{1}{4}y > -1\)?
qs.s: Multiplying by \(4\) gives \(3x + y > -4\), which simplifies to \(y > -3x - 4\). Since the inequality is strict, the boundary line is dashed and the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the boundary line and shaded region for the graph of \(\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{2}{3}y \le \frac{5}{6}\)?
qs.s: Multiplying by the LCD \(12\) gives \(9x - 8y \le 10\), so \(-8y \le -9x + 10\). Dividing by \(-8\) reverses the inequality to \(y \ge \frac{9}{8}x - \frac{5}{4}\), which represents a solid boundary line shaded above.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the boundary line and shaded region for the graph of \(\frac{1}{2}(x - 6) + \frac{1}{3}y > \frac{2}{3}x - 1\)?
qs.s: Multiplying the entire inequality by \(6\) yields \(3(x - 6) + 2y > 4x - 6\), which simplifies to \(3x - 18 + 2y > 4x - 6\), or \(2y > x + 12\). Dividing by \(2\) gives \(y > \frac{1}{2}x + 6\), giving a dashed boundary line shaded above.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the boundary line and shaded region for the graph of \(\frac{x + 2}{3} - \frac{y - 1}{4} \ge 2\)?
qs.s: Multiplying by \(12\) gives \(4(x + 2) - 3(y - 1) \ge 24\), which simplifies to \(4x - 3y + 11 \ge 24\), or \(-3y \ge -4x + 13\). Dividing by \(-3\) reverses the inequality to \(y \le \frac{4}{3}x - \frac{13}{3}\), resulting in a solid boundary line shaded below.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the boundary line and shaded region for the graph of \(\frac{2}{5}x - \frac{1}{2}(y + 4) < \frac{1}{10}x - \frac{3}{5}y\)?
qs.s: Multiplying by \(10\) clears fractions to give \(4x - 5(y + 4) < x - 6y\), which expands to \(4x - 5y - 20 < x - 6y\). Adding \(6y\) and isolating \(y\) yields \(y < -3x + 20\), meaning the boundary line is dashed and shaded below.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the boundary line and shaded region for the graph of \(\frac{5}{6}x - \frac{3}{4}y + 2 \ge \frac{1}{3}x + \frac{1}{2}\)?
qs.s: Multiplying by the LCD \(12\) gives \(10x - 9y + 24 \ge 4x + 6\), which rearranges to \(-9y \ge -6x - 18\). Dividing by \(-9\) reverses the inequality to \(y \le \frac{2}{3}x + 2\), which defines a solid boundary line with the half-plane below shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the linear inequality \(y \ge \frac{5}{2}x - 4\)?
qs.s: The inequality symbol \(\ge\) means the boundary line \(y = \frac{5}{2}x - 4\) is solid. Because \(y\) is greater than or equal to the expression, the solution region is shaded above the line.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the linear inequality \(y > \frac{1}{3}x - 5\)?
qs.s: The strict inequality \(>\) means the boundary line \(y = \frac{1}{3}x - 5\) is drawn as a dashed line. Since \(y\) is greater than the expression, the half-plane above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the linear inequality \(y \ge -\frac{2}{3}x + 1\)?
qs.s: The inequality includes equality (\(\ge\)), so the boundary line \(y = -\frac{2}{3}x + 1\) is solid. With \(y\) greater than or equal to the linear expression, the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the linear inequality \(y < \frac{3}{4}x - 2\)?
qs.s: Since the inequality symbol is \(<\), the boundary line \(y = \frac{3}{4}x - 2\) is dashed. Because \(y\) is less than the expression, the region below the boundary line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the linear inequality \(y \le -\frac{4}{5}x + 3\)?
qs.s: Because the inequality includes \(\le\), the boundary line \(y = -\frac{4}{5}x + 3\) is solid. Since \(y\) is less than or equal to the expression, the region below the boundary line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the linear inequality \(5x - 2(y + 3) > 4\)?
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying gives \(5x - 2y > 10\), which rearranges to \(-2y > -5x + 10\) and flips to \(y < \frac{5}{2}x - 5\) when divided by \(-2\). Therefore, the boundary line is dashed and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the linear inequality \(-2x - 4y \ge 8\)?
qs.s: Adding \(2x\) gives \(-4y \ge 2x + 8\), and dividing by \(-4\) reverses the inequality to \(y \le -\frac{1}{2}x - 2\). Because the inequality is \(\le\), the boundary line is solid and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the linear inequality \(4x - 3y \le 12\)?
qs.s: Subtracting \(4x\) yields \(-3y \le -4x + 12\), and dividing by \(-3\) flips the inequality to \(y \ge \frac{4}{3}x - 4\). Since the inequality includes \(\ge\), the boundary line is solid and the region above it is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the linear inequality \(\frac{1}{3}x - \frac{1}{2}y \ge 1\)?
qs.s: Multiplying the inequality by \(6\) gives \(2x - 3y \ge 6\), which rearranges to \(-3y \ge -2x + 6\) and flips to \(y \le \frac{2}{3}x - 2\) upon dividing by \(-3\). Thus, the boundary line is solid and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following correctly describes the graph of the linear inequality \(3x - 5y < 15\)?
qs.s: Subtracting \(3x\) gives \(-5y < -3x + 15\), and dividing by \(-5\) reverses the inequality to \(y > \frac{3}{5}x - 3\). The inequality is strict (\(>\)), so the boundary line is dashed and the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the linear inequality \(y > -\frac{3}{5}x - 2\)?
qs.a: Dashed boundary line with slope \(-\frac{3}{5}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -2)\), shaded above
d: Dashed boundary line with slope \(-\frac{3}{5}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -2)\), shaded below
Solid boundary line with slope \(-\frac{3}{5}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -2)\), shaded above
Dashed boundary line with slope \(\frac{3}{5}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -2)\), shaded above
qs.s: The strict inequality \(>\) means the boundary line is dashed with slope \(-\frac{3}{5}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -2)\), and the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the linear inequality \(y \le -\frac{4}{3}x + 3\)?
qs.a: Solid boundary line with slope \(-\frac{4}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 3)\), shaded below
d: Solid boundary line with slope \(-\frac{4}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 3)\), shaded above
Dashed boundary line with slope \(-\frac{4}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 3)\), shaded below
Solid boundary line with slope \(-\frac{3}{4}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 3)\), shaded below
qs.s: The symbol \(\le\) means the boundary line is solid with slope \(-\frac{4}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 3)\), and values of \(y\) less than or equal to the line are shaded below.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the linear inequality \(y \ge \frac{3}{4}x - 5\)?
qs.a: Solid boundary line with slope \(\frac{3}{4}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -5)\), shaded above
d: Solid boundary line with slope \(\frac{3}{4}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -5)\), shaded below
Dashed boundary line with slope \(\frac{3}{4}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -5)\), shaded above
Solid boundary line with slope \(\frac{4}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -5)\), shaded above
qs.s: The inequality includes \(\ge\), so the boundary line \(y = \frac{3}{4}x - 5\) is solid with slope \(\frac{3}{4}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -5)\), and the half-plane above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the linear inequality \(y < -\frac{2}{3}x + 4\)?
qs.a: Dashed boundary line with slope \(-\frac{2}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 4)\), shaded below
d: Dashed boundary line with slope \(-\frac{2}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 4)\), shaded above
Solid boundary line with slope \(-\frac{2}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 4)\), shaded below
Dashed boundary line with slope \(-\frac{3}{2}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 4)\), shaded below
qs.s: Because the inequality is strict (\(<\)), the boundary line \(y = -\frac{2}{3}x + 4\) is dashed with slope \(-\frac{2}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 4)\), and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the linear inequality \(y \le \frac{1}{2}x + 1\)?
qs.a: Solid boundary line with slope \(\frac{1}{2}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 1)\), shaded below
d: Solid boundary line with slope \(\frac{1}{2}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 1)\), shaded above
Dashed boundary line with slope \(\frac{1}{2}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 1)\), shaded below
Solid boundary line with slope \(2\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 1)\), shaded below
qs.s: The inequality symbol \(\le\) indicates a solid boundary line \(y = \frac{1}{2}x + 1\) with slope \(\frac{1}{2}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 1)\), with the region below the line shaded.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the linear inequality \(4(x - 2) - 6y \le -2\)?
qs.a: Solid boundary line with slope \(\frac{2}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -1)\), shaded above
d: Solid boundary line with slope \(\frac{2}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -1)\), shaded below
Dashed boundary line with slope \(\frac{2}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -1)\), shaded above
Solid boundary line with slope \(\frac{3}{2}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -1)\), shaded above
qs.s: Expanding yields \(4x - 8 - 6y \le -2\), which simplifies to \(-6y \le -4x + 6\). Dividing by \(-6\) flips the inequality to \(y \ge \frac{2}{3}x - 1\), giving a solid boundary line with slope \(\frac{2}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -1)\), shaded above.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the linear inequality \(3x - 5y \le 15\)?
qs.a: Solid boundary line with slope \(\frac{3}{5}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -3)\), shaded above
d: Solid boundary line with slope \(\frac{3}{5}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -3)\), shaded below
Dashed boundary line with slope \(\frac{3}{5}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -3)\), shaded above
Solid boundary line with slope \(-\frac{3}{5}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -3)\), shaded above
qs.s: Rewriting in slope-intercept form gives \(-5y \le -3x + 15\); dividing by \(-5\) reverses the inequality to \(y \ge \frac{3}{5}x - 3\). Thus, the graph has a solid boundary line with slope \(\frac{3}{5}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -3)\), shaded above the line.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the linear inequality \(-2x - 7y \ge 14\)?
qs.a: Solid boundary line with slope \(-\frac{2}{7}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -2)\), shaded below
d: Solid boundary line with slope \(-\frac{2}{7}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -2)\), shaded above
Dashed boundary line with slope \(-\frac{2}{7}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -2)\), shaded below
Solid boundary line with slope \frac{2}{7} and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -2)\), shaded below
qs.s: Adding \(2x\) gives \(-7y \ge 2x + 14\); dividing by \(-7\) inverts the inequality to \(y \le -\frac{2}{7}x - 2\). The boundary line is solid with slope \(-\frac{2}{7}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -2)\), shaded below.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the linear inequality \(5x + 6y - 18 \le 0\)?
qs.a: Solid boundary line with slope \(-\frac{5}{6}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 3)\), shaded below
d: Solid boundary line with slope \(-\frac{5}{6}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 3)\), shaded above
Dashed boundary line with slope \(-\frac{5}{6}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 3)\), shaded below
Solid boundary line with slope \(-\frac{6}{5}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 3)\), shaded below
qs.s: Rearranging gives \(6y \le -5x + 18\), and dividing by \(6\) gives \(y \le -\frac{5}{6}x + 3\). Since equality is included, the boundary line is solid with slope \(-\frac{5}{6}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, 3)\), shaded below.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the linear inequality \(4x - 3y > 12\)?
qs.a: Dashed boundary line with slope \(\frac{4}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -4)\), shaded below
d: Dashed boundary line with slope \(\frac{4}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -4)\), shaded above
Solid boundary line with slope \(\frac{4}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -4)\), shaded below
Dashed boundary line with slope \(\frac{3}{4}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -4)\), shaded below
qs.s: Subtracting \(4x\) yields \(-3y > -4x + 12\), and dividing by \(-3\) reverses the inequality symbol to \(y < \frac{4}{3}x - 4\). This gives a dashed boundary line with slope \(\frac{4}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -4)\), shaded below the line.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the inequality \(y \le -4\) in the coordinate plane?
d: A solid line \(x = -4\), shaded to the left
qs.s: The boundary line is the horizontal line \(y = -4\), drawn solid because equality is included (\(\le\)). Since \(y\) is less than or equal to \(-4\), the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the inequality \(x \ge 4\) in the coordinate plane?
qs.a: A solid line \(x = 4\), shaded to the right
d: A dashed line \(x = 4\), shaded to the right
A solid line \(x = 4\), shaded to the left
qs.s: The inequality \(x \ge 4\) has a boundary line at \(x = 4\), which is drawn solid because equality is included. Since \(x\) is greater than or equal to \(4\), the half-plane to the right of the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the inequality \(x > -2\) in the coordinate plane?
qs.a: A dashed line \(x = -2\), shaded to the right
d: A solid line \(x = -2\), shaded to the right
A dashed line \(x = -2\), shaded to the left
qs.s: The boundary line is \(x = -2\), which is drawn dashed because the inequality is strict (\(>\)). Since \(x\) is greater than \(-2\), the half-plane to the right of the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the inequality \(y < -1\) in the coordinate plane?
d: A dashed line \(x = -1\), shaded to the left
qs.s: The boundary line is the horizontal line \(y = -1\), drawn dashed because the inequality is strict (\(<\)). Because \(y\) is less than \(-1\), the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the inequality \(y \ge 3\) in the coordinate plane?
d: A solid line \(x = 3\), shaded to the right
qs.s: The boundary line is the horizontal line \(y = 3\), drawn solid because equality is included (\(\ge\)). Because \(y\) is greater than or equal to \(3\), the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the inequality \(2(x - 2) - y \le 3\) in the coordinate plane?
qs.s: Expanding gives \(2x - 4 - y \le 3\), which simplifies to \(-y \le -2x + 7\), and dividing by \(-1\) reverses the inequality to \(y \ge 2x - 7\). The boundary line is solid, and the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the inequality \(3(x + 1) \ge 5y - 7\) in the coordinate plane?
qs.s: Expanding yields \(3x + 3 \ge 5y - 7\), which simplifies to \(5y \le 3x + 10\) or \(y \le \frac{3}{5}x + 2\). The boundary line is solid because equality is included, and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the inequality \(5x - 4y > x - 8\) in the coordinate plane?
qs.a: A dashed line \(y = x + 2\), shaded below
d: A dashed line \(y = x + 2\), shaded above
A solid line \(y = x + 2\), shaded below
qs.s: Subtracting \(x\) gives \(4x - 4y > -8\), which becomes \(-4y > -4x - 8\), and dividing by \(-4\) reverses the inequality to \(y < x + 2\). The boundary line is dashed, and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the inequality \(2x - 3y \ge 6\) in the coordinate plane?
qs.s: Subtracting \(2x\) gives \(-3y \ge -2x + 6\), and dividing by \(-3\) reverses the inequality to \(y \le \frac{2}{3}x - 2\). The boundary line is solid because equality is included, and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which description correctly represents the graph of the inequality \(4x + 3y < 12\) in the coordinate plane?
qs.s: Subtracting \(4x\) and dividing by \(3\) gives \(y < -\frac{4}{3}x + 4\). The boundary line is dashed because the inequality is strict (\(<\)), and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the inequality \(y < 4\) on a coordinate plane?
d: Dashed line \(x = 4\), shaded to the left
qs.s: The inequality \(y < 4\) has a strict inequality, so the boundary is a dashed horizontal line at \(y = 4\). Since \(y\) is less than \(4\), the half-plane below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the inequality \(y \le -2\) on a coordinate plane?
d: Solid line \(x = -2\), shaded to the left
qs.s: The inequality \(y \le -2\) includes equality, so the boundary is a solid horizontal line at \(y = -2\). Since \(y\) is less than or equal to \(-2\), the half-plane below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the inequality \(y > -5\) on a coordinate plane?
d: Dashed line \(x = -5\), shaded to the right
qs.s: The inequality \(y > -5\) is strict, so the boundary is a dashed horizontal line at \(y = -5\). Since \(y\) is greater than \(-5\), the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the inequality \(y \ge 0\) on a coordinate plane?
d: Solid line \(x = 0\), shaded to the right
qs.s: The boundary line for \(y \ge 0\) is the solid line \(y = 0\) (the x-axis) because equality is included. Since \(y\) is greater than or equal to \(0\), the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the inequality \(y \ge 1\) on a coordinate plane?
d: Solid line \(x = 1\), shaded to the right
qs.s: The inequality \(y \ge 1\) includes equality, so the boundary is a solid horizontal line at \(y = 1\). Since \(y\) is greater than or equal to \(1\), the half-plane above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the inequality \(3x - y < 4\) on a coordinate plane?
qs.s: Subtracting \(3x\) gives \(-y < -3x + 4\), and dividing by \(-1\) reverses the inequality to \(y > 3x - 4\). Since the inequality is strict, the boundary is a dashed line and the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the inequality \(4x - 5y > 10\) on a coordinate plane?
qs.s: Subtracting \(4x\) gives \(-5y > -4x + 10\), and dividing by \(-5\) reverses the inequality to \(y < \frac{4}{5}x - 2\). The boundary is a dashed line because the inequality is strict, and the half-plane below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the inequality \(2x + y \le 6\) on a coordinate plane?
qs.s: Subtracting \(2x\) from both sides gives \(y \le -2x + 6\). The boundary is a solid line because equality is included, and the half-plane below the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the inequality \(3x + 2y \ge -6\) on a coordinate plane?
qs.s: Rearranging gives \(2y \ge -3x - 6\), which simplifies to \(y \ge -\frac{3}{2}x - 3\). The boundary line is solid because equality is included, and the region above the line is shaded.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the graph of the inequality \(x - 3y \ge 9\) on a coordinate plane?
qs.s: Subtracting \(x\) gives \(-3y \ge -x + 9\), and dividing by \(-3\) reverses the inequality to \(y \le \frac{1}{3}x - 3\). The boundary is a solid line, and the region below the line is shaded.

qs.q:
The boundary lines of the system of linear inequalities divide the coordinate plane into four regions labeled A, B, C, and D. Which region represents the solution set of the system?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} -x + y \le 3 \\ 2x + y \le 0 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing the point \((-1, -2)\) in Region D gives \(-(-1) + (-2) = -1 \le 3\) and \(2(-1) + (-2) = -4 \le 0\), which makes both statements true.

qs.q:
The boundary lines of the system of linear inequalities divide the coordinate plane into four regions labeled A, B, C, and D. Which region represents the solution set of the system?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x - 2y \ge 2 \\ x + 2y \le -2 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing the point \((0, -4)\) in Region C yields \(0 - 2(-4) = 8 \ge 2\) and \(0 + 2(-4) = -8 \le -2\), satisfying both inequalities.

qs.q:
The boundary lines of the system of linear inequalities divide the coordinate plane into four regions labeled A, B, C, and D. Which region represents the solution set of the system?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x - y \ge 1 \\ x + 2y \le 4 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing the point \((2, -2)\) in Region B gives \(2 - (-2) = 4 \ge 1\) and \(2 + 2(-2) = -2 \le 4\), satisfying both inequalities.

qs.q:
The boundary lines of the system of linear inequalities divide the coordinate plane into four regions labeled A, B, C, and D. Which region represents the solution set of the system?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x + y \ge 2 \\ x - y \le 4 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing the point \((3, 2)\) located in Region A gives \(3 + 2 = 5 \ge 2\) and \(3 - 2 = 1 \le 4\), satisfying both inequalities.

qs.q:
The boundary lines of the system of linear inequalities divide the coordinate plane into four regions labeled A, B, C, and D. Which region represents the solution set of the system?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} 2x - y \le 2 \\ x + y \ge 1 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing the point \((1, 3)\) located in Region B gives \(2(1) - 3 = -1 \le 2\) and \(1 + 3 = 4 \ge 1\), which satisfies both inequalities.

qs.q: Which system of linear inequalities is represented by the shaded region in the graph?
qs.s: The dashed line \(x - 2y = 2\) represents the strict inequality \(x - 2y < 2\), and the solid line \(2x + y = 4\) represents \(2x + y \le 4\); testing \((0,0)\) satisfies both conditions.

qs.q:
The coordinate plane shows the boundary lines of the three linear inequalities:
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x - y \ge -1 \\ x + y \le 5 \\ y \ge 1 \end{cases}\)
Which labeled region represents the solution set of this system?
qs.s: The solution set is the triangular region bounded by the three lines; testing the point \((2, 2)\) inside Region A satisfies \(2 - 2 \ge -1\), \(2 + 2 \le 5\), and \(2 \ge 1\).

qs.q:
The coordinate plane shows the boundary lines of the system of linear inequalities:
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x \ge -2 \\ y \le 2 \\ x - y \le -1 \end{cases}\)
Which labeled region represents the solution set of this system?
qs.s: The boundary lines \(x = -2\), \(y = 2\), and \(y = x + 1\) intersect at \((-2, 2)\), \((1, 2)\), and \((-2, -1)\), enclosing Region C; testing \((-1, 1)\) satisfies all three inequalities.

qs.q:
Use the graph to determine which labeled region represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities:
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x - 2y \le -2 \\ x + y \le 4 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing the point \((-2, 2)\) in Region B gives \(-2 - 2(2) = -6 \le -2\) and \(-2 + 2 = 0 \le 4\), both of which are true. Hence, Region B is the correct solution region.

qs.q:
Use the graph to determine which labeled region represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities:
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} 2x + y \le 3 \\ x - y \ge -3 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing the origin \((0, 0)\) in Region C yields \(2(0) + 0 = 0 \le 3\) and \(0 - 0 = 0 \ge -3\), satisfying both inequalities. Thus, the solution set is Region C.

qs.q:
Use the graph to determine which labeled region represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities:
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} 3x - 2y \ge 6 \\ x + y \ge -3 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing the test point \((3.5, -3)\) in Region D gives \(3(3.5) - 2(-3) = 16.5 \ge 6\) and \(3.5 + (-3) = 0.5 \ge -3\), which satisfies both inequalities. Therefore, Region D is the solution set.

qs.q:
Use the graph to determine which labeled region represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities:
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x + y \ge 2 \\ 2x - y \le 1 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing the point \((0, 3.5)\) in Region A gives \(0 + 3.5 = 3.5 \ge 2\) and \(2(0) - 3.5 = -3.5 \le 1\), both of which are true. Therefore, Region A is the solution set.

qs.q:
Use the graph to determine which labeled region represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities:
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} 2x + 3y \ge 6 \\ 2x - y \le -2 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing \((0, 4.5)\) in Region A yields \(2(0) + 3(4.5) = 13.5 \ge 6\) and \(2(0) - 4.5 = -4.5 \le -2\), satisfying both inequalities. Thus, Region A corresponds to the solution set.

qs.q: Which system of linear inequalities defines the shaded polygonal region shown in the graph?
qs.s: The region lies in the first quadrant where \(x \ge 0\) and \(y \ge 0\), and is bounded below the lines \(x + 2y = 6\) and \(2x + y = 6\). Testing the point \((1, 1)\) confirms that \(1 + 2(1) = 3 \le 6\) and \(2(1) + 1 = 3 \le 6\).

qs.q:
Use the graph to determine which labeled region represents the solution set of the system of three linear inequalities:
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x + y \ge 2 \\ x - y \le 2 \\ x \ge -1 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing the point \((0, 3.5)\) in Region C yields \(0 + 3.5 = 3.5 \ge 2\), \(0 - 3.5 = -3.5 \le 2\), and \(0 \ge -1\), all of which are true. Thus, Region C satisfies all three inequalities.

qs.q: Which system of linear inequalities defines the shaded triangular region shown in the graph?
qs.s: The boundary lines are \(y = 1\), the line through \((1, 1)\) and \((2, 4)\) which is \(3x - y = 2\), and the line through \((2, 4)\) and \((5, 1)\) which is \(x + y = 6\). Testing an interior point like \((2, 2)\) satisfies \(y \ge 1\), \(3(2) - 2 = 4 \ge 2\), and \(2 + 2 = 4 \le 6\).

qs.q:
Use the graph to determine which labeled region represents the solution set of the system of three linear inequalities:
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x + 2y \le 4 \\ 2x - y \ge -2 \\ x - y \ge 1 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing the point \((2, -2)\) in Region D gives \(2 + 2(-2) = -2 \le 4\), \(2(2) - (-2) = 6 \ge -2\), and \(2 - (-2) = 4 \ge 1\), which satisfies all three inequalities simultaneously.

qs.q:
Use the graph to determine which labeled region represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities:
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x - 2y \le -4 \\ 3x - y \le 3 \\ 2x + y \ge -3 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing the point \((0, 3)\) in Region B gives \(0 - 2(3) = -6 \le -4\), \(3(0) - 3 = -3 \le 3\), and \(2(0) + 3 = 3 \ge -3\). Since all three inequalities hold true, Region B is the solution set.

qs.q:
Which labeled region in the graph represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x - y \ge -3 \\ 2x + y \ge 0 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: The system requires \(y \le x + 3\) (below the line \(x - y = -3\)) and \(y \ge -2x\) (above the line \(2x + y = 0\)). Testing point \((2, 1)\) in Region B satisfies both \(2 - 1 = 1 \ge -3\) and \(2(2) + 1 = 5 \ge 0\).

qs.q:
Which labeled region in the graph represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x - y \ge 1 \\ x + 2y \le 4 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Rewriting the inequalities gives \(y \le x - 1\) and \(y \le -\frac{1}{2}x + 2\), which is the region lying below both lines. Testing point \((3, -2)\) in Region C yields \(3 - (-2) = 5 \ge 1\) and \(3 + 2(-2) = -1 \le 4\), both of which are true.

qs.q:
Which labeled region in the graph represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x - 2y \ge 2 \\ x + y \le -1 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: The system represents the region below \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 1\) and below \(y = -x - 1\). Testing \((0, -4)\) in Region C gives \(0 - 2(-4) = 8 \ge 2\) and \(0 + (-4) = -4 \le -1\), confirming it is the correct region.

qs.q:
Which labeled region in the graph represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} 2x + 3y \le 6 \\ 2x - y \le -2 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: In slope-intercept form, the system is \(y \le -\frac{2}{3}x + 2\) and \(y \ge 2x + 2\). Testing \((-3, 2)\) in Region D yields \(2(-3) + 3(2) = 0 \le 6\) and \(2(-3) - 2 = -8 \le -2\), satisfying both conditions.

qs.q:
Which labeled region in the graph represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x + y \ge 2 \\ x - y \le -2 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Rewriting the system gives \(y \ge -x + 2\) and \(y \ge x + 2\), which corresponds to the region above both boundary lines. Testing the test point \((0, 4)\) in Region A satisfies both \(0 + 4 \ge 2\) and \(0 - 4 \le -2\).

qs.q:
Which labeled region in the graph represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} 3x - 4y > -6 \\ 3x + 2y \le 12 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Rewriting yields \(y < \frac{3}{4}x + 1.5\) (below the dashed line) and \(y \le -\frac{3}{2}x + 6\) (below the solid line). Testing the origin \((0, 0)\) in Region C yields \(0 > -6\) and \(0 \le 12\), both of which are true.

qs.q: Use the graph to identify the system of linear inequalities whose solution set is the shaded triangular region.
qs.s: The region is bounded to the right of the vertical line \(x = -1\) (\(x \ge -1\)), below the horizontal line \(y = 3\) (\(y \le 3\)), and above the line \(y = x - 1\), which rearranges to \(x - y \le 1\). Testing \((0, 1)\) inside the triangle satisfies all three inequalities.

qs.q: Use the graph to identify the system of linear inequalities that defines the shaded feasible region.
qs.s: The region is restricted to the first quadrant (\(x \ge 0, y \ge 0\)) and lies under both boundary lines \(2x + y = 6\) (intercepts \((3, 0)\) and \((0, 6)\)) and \(x + 2y = 6\) (intercepts \((6, 0)\) and \((0, 3)\)), requiring \(\le\) for both linear inequalities.

qs.q:
Which labeled region in the graph represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} -x + y > 1 \\ 2x + y < 4 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: The system represents points strictly above the dashed line \(y = x + 1\) and strictly below the dashed line \(y = -2x + 4\). Testing point \((-2, 2)\) in Region D yields \(-(-2) + 2 = 4 > 1\) and \(2(-2) + 2 = -2 < 4\), satisfying both inequalities.

qs.q:
Which labeled region in the graph represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} 2x + y < 2 \\ x - 3y \ge -6 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: The dashed boundary line is \(2x + y = 2\) and the solid boundary line is \(x - 3y = -6\). The system requires \(y < -2x + 2\) and \(y \le \frac{1}{3}x + 2\); testing point \((-2, -1)\) in Region C satisfies both \(2(-2) + (-1) = -5 < 2\) and \(-2 - 3(-1) = 1 \ge -6\).

qs.q:
Which labeled region (A, B, C, or D) represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x - y \le 1 \\ x + 2y \le 4 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing the origin \((0, 0)\) in Region C gives \(0 - 0 = 0 \le 1\) and \(0 + 2(0) = 0 \le 4\), satisfying both inequalities. Thus, Region C is the correct solution set.

qs.q:
Which labeled region (A, B, C, or D) represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x + y \ge 2 \\ x - y \le -2 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing a point in Region A, such as \((0, 4)\), gives \(0 + 4 = 4 \ge 2\) and \(0 - 4 = -4 \le -2\), both of which are true. Therefore, Region A is the correct solution set.

qs.q:
Which labeled region (A, B, C, or D) represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} 2x - y \le 2 \\ x + y \ge 1 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing a point in Region B, such as \((0, 3)\), satisfies both \(2(0) - 3 = -3 \le 2\) and \(0 + 3 = 3 \ge 1\). Hence, Region B represents the solution set.

qs.q:
Which labeled region (A, B, C, or D) represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x - 2y \ge 2 \\ 2x + y \ge -1 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing a test point in Region A, such as \((3, -1)\), gives \(3 - 2(-1) = 5 \ge 2\) and \(2(3) + (-1) = 5 \ge -1\), both of which are true. Thus, Region A is the solution region.

qs.q:
Which labeled region (A, B, C, or D) represents the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} 3x - y \ge -3 \\ x + y \le -1 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: Testing a point in Region D, such as \((-1, -3)\), gives \(3(-1) - (-3) = 0 \ge -3\) and \(-1 + (-3) = -4 \le -1\), satisfying both inequalities. Therefore, Region D represents the solution set.

qs.q:

qs.q:

qs.q:

qs.q:

qs.q:

qs.q:

qs.q:
Use the given graph to determine which labeled region represents the solution set to the system of three linear inequalities:
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x + y \le 3 \\ x - y \ge -1 \\ y \ge -1 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: The boundary lines \(x + y = 3\), \(x - y = -1\), and \(y = -1\) enclose the triangular Region C. Testing \((1, 0)\) inside Region C gives \(1 + 0 = 1 \le 3\), \(1 - 0 = 1 \ge -1\), and \(0 \ge -1\), satisfying all three inequalities.

qs.q:
Use the given graph to determine which labeled region represents the solution set to the system of three linear inequalities:
\(\displaystyle \begin{cases} x \ge -2 \\ y \le 2 \\ x - y \le -1 \end{cases}\)
qs.s: The vertical boundary is \(x = -2\), the horizontal boundary is \(y = 2\), and the oblique boundary is \(x - y = -1\). Testing \((-1.2, 1.2)\) in Region D yields \(-1.2 \ge -2\), \(1.2 \le 2\), and \(-1.2 - 1.2 = -2.4 \le -1\), satisfying all three inequalities.

qs.q:
Which labeled region in the given graph represents the solution set to the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} 2x - y &\ge -3 \\ x + 2y &\le 1 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: The boundary lines are \(2x - y = -3\) and \(x + 2y = 1\). Testing the point \((0.5, -2.5)\) in Region C gives \(2(0.5) - (-2.5) = 3.5 \ge -3\) and \(0.5 + 2(-2.5) = -4.5 \le 1\), both of which are true, so Region C is the solution set.

qs.q:
Which labeled region in the given graph represents the solution set to the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} 2x - y &\le 1 \\ x + y &\ge 2 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: The boundary lines are \(2x - y = 1\) and \(x + y = 2\). Testing the point \((-0.5, 3.5)\) in Region A gives \(2(-0.5) - 3.5 = -4.5 \le 1\) and \(-0.5 + 3.5 = 3 \ge 2\), both of which are true, so Region A is the solution set.

qs.q:
Which labeled region in the given graph represents the solution set to the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} x - 2y &\le 2 \\ x + y &\le -1 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: The boundary lines are \(x - 2y = 2\) and \(x + y = -1\). Testing the point \((-3.5, -1)\) in Region D gives \(-3.5 - 2(-1) = -1.5 \le 2\) and \(-3.5 + (-1) = -4.5 \le -1\), both of which are true, so Region D is the solution set.

qs.q:
Which labeled region in the given graph represents the solution set to the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} x + y &\ge 2 \\ x - 2y &\ge -4 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: The boundary lines are \(x + y = 2\) and \(x - 2y = -4\). Testing the point \((3.5, 0.5)\) in Region B gives \(3.5 + 0.5 = 4 \ge 2\) and \(3.5 - 2(0.5) = 2.5 \ge -4\), both of which are true, so Region B is the solution set.

qs.q:
Which labeled region in the given graph represents the solution set to the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} 2x + y &\ge 4 \\ x - y &\ge 2 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: The boundary lines are \(2x + y = 4\) and \(x - y = 2\). Testing the point \((4.5, 0)\) in Region B gives \(2(4.5) + 0 = 9 \ge 4\) and \(4.5 - 0 = 4.5 \ge 2\), both of which are true, so Region B is the solution set.

qs.q:
Which labeled region in the graph represents the solution set to the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} x &\ge -1 \\ y &\le 3 \\ x - y &\le 1 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: The boundary lines are the vertical line \(x = -1\), the horizontal line \(y = 3\), and the oblique line \(x - y = 1\). Testing the interior point \((0.5, 1.5)\) in Region A gives \(0.5 \ge -1\), \(1.5 \le 3\), and \(0.5 - 1.5 = -1 \le 1\), satisfying all three inequalities.

qs.q:

qs.q:
Which labeled region in the graph represents the solution set to the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} x + y &\ge 2 \\ x - y &\le 2 \\ x &\ge -1 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: The boundary lines are \(x + y = 2\), \(x - y = 2\), and \(x = -1\). Testing \((1, 3.5)\) in Region C yields \(1 + 3.5 = 4.5 \ge 2\), \(1 - 3.5 = -2.5 \le 2\), and \(1 \ge -1\), all of which hold.

qs.q: Which system of linear inequalities represents the shaded region shown in the graph?
qs.s: The region is bounded by the vertical line \(x = -1\) and the horizontal line \(y = 3\). The shaded area lies to the right of \(x = -1\) (\(x \ge -1\)) and below \(y = 3\) (\(y \le 3\)).

qs.q: Which system of linear inequalities represents the shaded rectangular region in the graph?

qs.s: The shaded region is bounded by the vertical lines \(x = -2\) and \(x = 3\). Since the shading includes all points whose \(x\)-coordinates lie between these two lines, the inequality is \(-2 \le x \le 3\).

qs.s: The horizontal boundary lines are \(y = 1\) and \(y = 5\). Since the region between these lines is shaded, the corresponding inequality is \(1 \le y \le 5\).

qs.q: Which system of linear inequalities represents the shaded region in the graph?

qs.s: The region lies in the first quadrant (\(x \ge 0, y \ge 0\)), below the horizontal line \(y = 4\) (\(y \le 4\)), and below the slanted boundary through \((0, 6)\) and \((6, 0)\) (\(x + y \le 6\)).

qs.q: The coordinate plane in the figure is divided into four regions by the solid lines \(x = 2\) and \(y = -1\). Which region represents the solution to the system of linear inequalities \(\begin{cases} x \ge 2 \\ y \le -1 \end{cases}\)?
qs.s: The inequality \(x \ge 2\) corresponds to points on or to the right of the vertical line \(x = 2\). The inequality \(y \le -1\) corresponds to points on or below the horizontal line \(y = -1\). The intersection of these two half-planes is Region C.

qs.s: The shaded rectangular region is bounded horizontally between \(x = -4\) and \(x = 2\), and vertically between \(y = 1\) and \(y = 5\). Since all boundary lines are solid, the inequalities include their endpoints, giving \(-4 \le x \le 2\) and \(1 \le y \le 5\).

qs.s: The region lies above the horizontal line \(y = -1\), giving \(y \ge -1\). The left slanted boundary passes through \((0, 1)\) with slope \(1\) (\(y = x + 1\)) and is shaded below, giving \(y \le x + 1\). qs.q: The lines \(y = x + 1\) and \(y = -x + 3\) are graphed in the figure, dividing the plane into four regions labeled Region A, Region B, Region C, and Region D. Which region represents the solution to the system \(\begin{cases} y \ge x + 1 \\ y \le -x + 3 \end{cases}\)?
qs.s: The inequality \(y \ge x + 1\) corresponds to the half-plane on or above the line \(y = x + 1\), while \(y \le -x + 3\) corresponds to the half-plane on or below the line \(y = -x + 3\). The intersection of these two regions is the left sector, labeled Region D.

\[3y \le -x + 6\]

Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\[y < -2x\]
\[2y \ge x - 6\]

Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?

\[2y < x + 4\]

Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?

\[2y > x - 4\]

Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?

Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\[3(x - y) + 4 \ge x - 2\]
\[2x - 5y < 3(y + 2) - 10\]

Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\[3(x - 2y) + 7 \ge 2(x - y) + 1\]
\[\frac{2x - y}{3} < x - 1\]

Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?

\[4 - (3x + y) > 2(x - y) - 6\]
qs.s: The inequalities simplify to \(y \le -3x + 8\) and \(y > 5x - 10\); substituting \((1, 2)\) gives \(2 \le 5\) and \(2 > -5\), which are both true.

Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?

\[5 - 2(x - y) > 3x + 1\]

qs.q:

\(2x + 3y \ge 6\)

Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?

\(2x + y > -1\)

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(2x - 3y < 6\)
\(x + 2y \ge -2\)
qs.s: Substituting \((1, 1)\) gives \(2(1) - 3(1) = -1 < 6\) and \(1 + 2(1) = 3 \ge -2\), satisfying both inequalities. The point \((3, 0)\) lies on the dashed line \(2x - 3y = 6\) and is not in the solution set.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(2x + y < 5\)
\(x - y \ge 1\)
qs.s: Substituting \((2, -1)\) into the system yields \(2(2) + (-1) = 3 < 5\) and \(2 - (-1) = 3 \ge 1\), which satisfies both inequalities. The point \((3, -1)\) lies on the dashed boundary \(2x + y = 5\) and is not included in the solution set.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(3x + y \le 3\)
\(x - 2y < 4\)
qs.s: Testing \((0, 0)\) gives \(3(0) + 0 = 0 \le 3\) and \(0 - 2(0) = 0 < 4\), so it satisfies both inequalities. The point \((0, -2)\) lies on the dashed boundary \(x - 2y = 4\) and cannot be included.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(5 - 2(x + y) \ge 3 - x\)
\(3(x - 2y) - 4y > 12\)
qs.s: Simplifying both inequalities yields \(x + 2y \le 2\) and \(3x - 10y > 12\); substituting \((4, -2)\) gives \(4 + 2(-2) = 0 \le 2\) and \(3(4) - 10(-2) = 32 > 12\). The point \((-6, -3)\) lies on the dashed boundary \(3x - 10y = 12\) and is excluded.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(2x - y \le 4\)
\(x + 3y \ge -3\)
\(x - y > -2\)
qs.s: Substituting \((1, 0)\) satisfies all three inequalities: \(2(1) - 0 = 2 \le 4\), \(1 + 3(0) = 1 \ge -3\), and \(1 - 0 = 1 > -2\). The point \((0, 2)\) lies on the dashed boundary \(x - y = -2\) and is not included.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(x + y \le 6\)
\(3x - y \ge 2\)
\(x - 2y < 2\)
qs.s: Substituting \((2, 2)\) satisfies all three inequalities: \(2 + 2 = 4 \le 6\), \(3(2) - 2 = 4 \ge 2\), and \(2 - 2(2) = -2 < 2\). The point \((2, 0)\) lies on the dashed boundary \(x - 2y = 2\) and is not in the solution set.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\frac{x}{3} - \frac{y}{2} > 1\)
\(\frac{x}{2} + \frac{y}{4} \le 3\)
qs.s: Clearing denominators gives \(2x - 3y > 6\) and \(2x + y \le 12\); substituting \((6, -1)\) yields \(2(6) - 3(-1) = 15 > 6\) and \(2(6) + (-1) = 11 \le 12\). The point \((3, 0)\) is on the dashed line \(2x - 3y = 6\) and fails the strict inequality.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(2(x - 2y) + 5 > 3(x - 1)\)
\(4(x + 1) - 3(y - 2) \le 18\)
qs.s: Simplifying the inequalities gives \(x + 4y < 8\) and \(4x - 3y \le 8\); substituting \((1, 1)\) yields \(1 + 4 = 5 < 8\) and \(4 - 3 = 1 \le 8\). The point \((0, 2)\) lies on the dashed line \(x + 4y = 8\) and fails the strict inequality.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(x + y \le 4\)
\(x + y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Substitute \((1, 1)\) into both inequalities: \(1 + 1 = 2 \le 4\) and \(1 + 1 = 2 \ge 0\), so \((1, 1)\) satisfies the system.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(x - y \le 3\)
\(x - y \ge -1\)
qs.s: Substitute \((1, 0)\) into both inequalities: \(1 - 0 = 1 \le 3\) and \(1 - 0 = 1 \ge -1\), both of which are true.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(2x - y \le 3\)
\(2x - y \ge -2\)
qs.s: Substitute \((0, 1)\) into both inequalities: \(2(0) - 1 = -1 \le 3\) and \(2(0) - 1 = -1 \ge -2\), both of which are true.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(x - y \ge 1\)
\(x + y \le 3\)
qs.s: Substitute \((2, 0)\) into both inequalities: \(2 - 0 = 2 \ge 1\) and \(2 + 0 = 2 \le 3\), both of which are true.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(2x + y \le 4\)
\(x - y \le 2\)
qs.s: Substitute \((0, 0)\) into both inequalities: \(2(0) + 0 = 0 \le 4\) and \(0 - 0 = 0 \le 2\), both of which are true.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(x + y \le 5\)
\(2x - y \ge 1\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Substitute \((2, 1)\) into all three inequalities: \(2 + 1 = 3 \le 5\), \(2(2) - 1 = 3 \ge 1\), and \(1 \ge 0\), all of which hold true.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(x - 2y \le 2\)
\(x + y \ge -1\)
\(x \le 4\)
qs.s: Substitute \((3, 2)\) into all three inequalities: \(3 - 2(2) = -1 \le 2\), \(3 + 2 = 5 \ge -1\), and \(3 \le 4\), all of which are satisfied.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(2(x + y) - 3x \le 1\)
\(3(x - y) + 4y > 5\)
qs.s: Simplifying gives \(-x + 2y \le 1\) and \(3x + y > 5\). Substituting \((3, 0)\) gives \(-3 + 0 = -3 \le 1\) and \(3(3) + 0 = 9 > 5\), both of which are true.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(3x - 2y < 6\)
\(x + 3y \ge 9\)
qs.s: Substitute \((0, 4)\) into both inequalities: \(3(0) - 2(4) = -8 < 6\) and \(0 + 3(4) = 12 \ge 9\), both of which are true. Note that \((4, 3)\) lies on the dashed boundary line \(3x - 2y = 6\) and is not included.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(-2x + y < 1\)
\(3x - 4y \ge 12\)
qs.s: Substitute \((4, -2)\) into both inequalities: \(-2(4) + (-2) = -10 < 1\) and \(3(4) - 4(-2) = 20 \ge 12\), both of which are true. The point \((-4, -7)\) lies on the dashed boundary line \(-2x + y = 1\) and is not included.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle y > x - 3\)
\(\displaystyle y \le -x + 1\)
qs.s: Substitute \((0, -1)\) into the system: \(-1 > 0 - 3 = -3\) is true, and \(-1 \le -0 + 1 = 1\) is true. Note that \((1, -2)\) lies on the dashed boundary line \(y = x - 3\) and is not a solution.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle y \ge x - 2\)
\(\displaystyle y \le -x + 2\)
qs.s: Substitute \((0, 0)\) into both inequalities: \(0 \ge 0 - 2 = -2\) is true, and \(0 \le -0 + 2 = 2\) is true. Since \((0, 0)\) satisfies both inequalities, it lies in the solution set.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle y \le -x + 4\)
\(\displaystyle y \le x + 2\)
qs.s: Substitute \((1, 0)\) into both inequalities: \(0 \le -1 + 4 = 3\) is true, and \(0 \le 1 + 2 = 3\) is true. Therefore, \((1, 0)\) lies in the solution region.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle y \ge x + 1\)
\(\displaystyle y \ge -x - 3\)
qs.s: Substitute \((-2, 2)\) into both inequalities: \(2 \ge -2 + 1 = -1\) is true, and \(2 \ge -(-2) - 3 = -1\) is true. Thus, \((-2, 2)\) satisfies the system.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle y \le x + 3\)
\(\displaystyle y \ge -x - 1\)
qs.s: Substitute \((0, 1)\) into both inequalities: \(1 \le 0 + 3 = 3\) is true, and \(1 \ge -0 - 1 = -1\) is true. The other options fail at least one of the inequalities.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle 2x - 3y \ge 6\)
\(\displaystyle x + 2y < 4\)
qs.s: Substitute \((0, -3)\) into both inequalities: \(2(0) - 3(-3) = 9 \ge 6\) is true, and \(0 + 2(-3) = -6 < 4\) is true. Point \((4, 0)\) lies on the dashed boundary line \(x + 2y = 4\) and is not included.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle 5x - 2y \ge 10\)
\(\displaystyle -3x + 4y \ge 12\)
qs.s: Testing \((6, 8)\) yields \(5(6) - 2(8) = 14 \ge 10\) (true) and \(-3(6) + 4(8) = 14 \ge 12\) (true). In contrast, testing \((0, 0)\) gives \(0 \ge 10\) (false) and \(0 \ge 12\) (false).

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle -4x + 3y < 9\)
\(\displaystyle 3x + 2y \ge 12\)
qs.s: Substituting \((4, 2)\) gives \(-4(4) + 3(2) = -10 < 9\) (true) and \(3(4) + 2(2) = 16 \ge 12\) (true). The point \((3, 7)\) gives \(-4(3) + 3(7) = 9\), which does not satisfy the strict inequality \(< 9\).

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle 3x - 4y > 12\)
\(\displaystyle 2x + 5y \ge 10\)
qs.s: Testing \((6, 1)\) gives \(3(6) - 4(1) = 14 > 12\) (true) and \(2(6) + 5(1) = 17 \ge 10\) (true). Each of the other options fails at least one inequality, such as \((5, -1)\) which gives \(2(5) + 5(-1) = 5 \ge 10\) (false).

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle 2(x - 2) - 3y \ge 1\)
\(\displaystyle 3(x + 1) + 2y < 11\)
qs.s: Simplifying gives \(2x - 3y \ge 5\) and \(3x + 2y < 8\). Testing \((3, -2)\) gives \(2(3) - 3(-2) = 12 \ge 5\) (true) and \(3(3) + 2(-2) = 5 < 8\) (true).

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(3x + 2y < 12\)
\(x - y \le 2\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Substituting \((1, 3)\) gives \(3(1) + 2(3) = 9 < 12\), \(1 - 3 = -2 \le 2\), \(1 \ge 0\), and \(3 \ge 0\), so all inequalities are satisfied. Points on dashed boundaries such as \((2, 3)\) are not included in the solution set.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(2x + 3y \le 18\)
\(x - 2y < 2\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Substituting \((2, 2)\) gives \(2(2) + 3(2) = 10 \le 18\), \(2 - 2(2) = -2 < 2\), \(2 \ge 0\), and \(2 \ge 0\), satisfying the entire system. The point \((4, 1)\) lies on the dashed boundary line \(x - 2y = 2\) and is therefore excluded.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(x + 2y < 8\)
\(3x - y \le 6\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Substituting \((1, 2)\) into the system yields \(1 + 2(2) = 5 < 8\), \(3(1) - 2 = 1 \le 6\), \(1 \ge 0\), and \(2 \ge 0\), which are all true statements. The point \((2, 3)\) lies on the dashed boundary \(x + 2y = 8\) and is not a solution.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(3x + 4y \le 24\)
\(2x - y > 2\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Substituting \((3, 1)\) gives \(3(3) + 4(1) = 13 \le 24\), \(2(3) - 1 = 5 > 2\), \(3 \ge 0\), and \(1 \ge 0\), which are all satisfied. The point \((2, 2)\) lies on the dashed boundary line \(2x - y = 2\) and is therefore not in the solution set.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(2x + y \le 6\)
\(x - 3y > -6\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Substituting \((1, 1)\) gives \(2(1) + 1 = 3 \le 6\), \(1 - 3(1) = -2 > -6\), \(1 \ge 0\), and \(1 \ge 0\), satisfying all conditions. The point \((0, 2)\) lies on the dashed boundary line \(x - 3y = -6\) and is not included.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(2(x + 2y) - x < 16\)
\(3(x - y) + 5y \le 18\)
\(x + y \ge 3\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Simplifying the first two inequalities yields \(x + 4y < 16\) and \(3x + 2y \le 18\). Testing \((3, 2)\) gives \(3 + 4(2) = 11 < 16\), \(3(3) + 2(2) = 13 \le 18\), \(3 + 2 = 5 \ge 3\), and non-negative coordinates, satisfying all five conditions.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(7x + 6y < 42\)
\(3x - 2y \le 6\)
\(x - 4y > -12\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Substituting \((2, 1)\) yields \(7(2) + 6(1) = 20 < 42\), \(3(2) - 2(1) = 4 \le 6\), \(2 - 4(1) = -2 > -12\), and \(2, 1 \ge 0\), satisfying all conditions. The point \((0, 3)\) is on the dashed line \(x - 4y = -12\) and is not a solution.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\frac{x}{3} + \frac{y}{2} < 4\)
\(2(x - 1) - 3(y + 1) \ge -5\)
\(x - y \le 3\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Simplifying yields \(2x + 3y < 24\), \(2x - 3y \ge 0\), and \(x - y \le 3\). Substituting \((4, 2)\) gives \(2(4) + 3(2) = 14 < 24\), \(2(4) - 3(2) = 2 \ge 0\), \(4 - 2 = 2 \le 3\), and non-negative coordinates, so all conditions hold.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(5x + 8y \le 80\)
\(3x - 4y > 12\)
\(x + 2y \ge 10\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Substituting \((8, 2)\) gives \(5(8) + 8(2) = 56 \le 80\), \(3(8) - 4(2) = 16 > 12\), \(8 + 2(2) = 12 \ge 10\), and \(8, 2 \ge 0\), which satisfies all inequalities. The point \((8, 3)\) lies on the dashed boundary line \(3x - 4y = 12\) and is excluded.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(4(x - 1) + 3y < 2(y + 8)\)
\(5x - 2(y - 3) \ge x + 14\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Simplifying the inequalities gives \(4x + y < 20\) and \(2x - y \ge 4\). Testing \((3, 0)\) gives \(4(3) + 0 = 12 < 20\), \(2(3) - 0 = 6 \ge 4\), \(3 \ge 0\), and \(0 \ge 0\), so all constraints are satisfied.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(x + y \ge -1\)
\(x + y \le 3\)
\(-3 \le x \le 0\)
qs.s: Substituting \((-1, 1)\), we find \(x + y = -1 + 1 = 0\), which satisfies \(-1 \le 0 \le 3\), and \(x = -1\) satisfies \(-3 \le -1 \le 0\). Hence, \((-1, 1)\) lies in the solution set.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(y - x \ge 1\)
\(y - x \le 4\)
\(-2 \le x \le 1\)
qs.s: Testing \((0, 2)\), we get \(y - x = 2 - 0 = 2\), which satisfies \(1 \le 2 \le 4\), and \(x = 0\) satisfies \(-2 \le 0 \le 1\). Thus, \((0, 2)\) is in the solution set.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(x - y \ge -2\)
\(x - y \le 2\)
\(1 \le y \le 4\)
qs.s: Testing \((1, 2)\), we have \(x - y = 1 - 2 = -1\), which satisfies \(-2 \le -1 \le 2\), and \(y = 2\) satisfies \(1 \le 2 \le 4\). Therefore, \((1, 2)\) is in the solution set.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(2x - y \ge 1\)
\(2x - y \le 4\)
\(1 \le x \le 3\)
qs.s: Testing \((2, 2)\), we have \(2(2) - 2 = 2\), which satisfies \(1 \le 2 \le 4\), and \(x = 2\) satisfies \(1 \le 2 \le 3\). Thus, \((2, 2)\) is in the solution set.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(x + y \ge 2\)
\(x + y \le 5\)
\(0 \le x \le 3\)
qs.s: Substituting \((2, 1)\) gives \(2 + 1 = 3\), which satisfies \(2 \le 3 \le 5\), and \(0 \le 2 \le 3\) is also true. Thus, \((2, 1)\) lies in the solution set.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(-4 < 3x - 2y \le 8\)
\(-2 \le 2x + y \le 7\)
\(x \ge 0\)
qs.s: Evaluating \((1, 3)\), we have \(3(1) - 2(3) = -3\), which satisfies \(-4 < -3 \le 8\), \(2(1) + 3 = 5\), which satisfies \(-2 \le 5 \le 7\), and \(x = 1 \ge 0\). The point \((0, 2)\) lies on the dashed boundary line \(3x - 2y = -4\) and is not a solution.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(3x - 4y \ge -12\)
\(x + 2y < 8\)
\(x \ge -2\)
\(y \ge -1\)
qs.s: Substituting \((1, 1)\), we get \(3(1) - 4(1) = -1 \ge -12\), \(1 + 2(1) = 3 < 8\), \(1 \ge -2\), and \(1 \ge -1\), all of which are true. The point \((2, 3)\) lies on the dashed boundary line \(x + 2y = 8\) and thus does not satisfy the strict inequality.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(-6 \le 2x - 5y \le 10\)
\(-3 \le x + y \le 4\)
qs.s: Testing \((3, 0)\), we find \(2(3) - 5(0) = 6\), which satisfies \(-6 \le 6 \le 10\), and \(3 + 0 = 3\), which satisfies \(-3 \le 3 \le 4\). Therefore, \((3, 0)\) is in the solution set.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(4x - 3y \le 12\)
\(x + 3y \ge -3\)
\(y - 2x < 4\)
\(x \le 2\)
qs.s: For \((1, -1)\), we have \(4(1) - 3(-1) = 7 \le 12\), \(1 + 3(-1) = -2 \ge -3\), \(-1 - 2(1) = -3 < 4\), and \(1 \le 2\), satisfying all conditions. The point \((0, 4)\) lies on the dashed boundary line \(y - 2x = 4\) and is therefore excluded.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(2x + 3y > 6\)
\(2x + 3y \le 18\)
\(-1 \le x \le 4\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Substituting \((2, 2)\) gives \(2(2) + 3(2) = 10\), which satisfies \(6 < 10 \le 18\), and both \(-1 \le 2 \le 4\) and \(2 \ge 0\) hold. Note that \((3, 0)\) lies on the dashed boundary line \(2x + 3y = 6\) and is therefore not included.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle x - y \ge -1\)
\(\displaystyle 2x + y \le 4\)
\(\displaystyle x \ge 0\)
qs.s: Substituting \((1, 1)\) produces \(1 - 1 = 0 \ge -1\), \(2(1) + 1 = 3 \le 4\), and \(1 \ge 0\), which are all true statements. The distractors each lie outside the shaded solution region.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle 2x + y \ge -1\)
\(\displaystyle x - y \ge -2\)
\(\displaystyle y \le 3\)
qs.s: Testing \((0, 1)\) gives \(2(0) + 1 = 1 \ge -1\), \(0 - 1 = -1 \ge -2\), and \(1 \le 3\), which are all true. Each distractor fails at least one of the inequalities.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle x + 2y \ge 2\)
\(\displaystyle x - y \le 2\)
\(\displaystyle y \le 2\)
qs.s: Testing \((2, 1)\) yields \(2 + 2(1) = 4 \ge 2\), \(2 - 1 = 1 \le 2\), and \(1 \le 2\), satisfying all three inequalities. The remaining options violate at least one boundary constraint.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle x + y \le 2\)
\(\displaystyle x - 2y \le 2\)
\(\displaystyle x \ge -2\)
qs.s: Substituting \((0, 0)\) gives \(0 + 0 = 0 \le 2\), \(0 - 2(0) = 0 \le 2\), and \(0 \ge -2\), satisfying all three conditions. The other points fail one of the three inequalities.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle x - y \le 1\)
\(\displaystyle x + y \le 3\)
\(\displaystyle y \ge -1\)
qs.s: Substituting \((1, 0)\) into each inequality yields \(1 - 0 = 1 \le 1\), \(1 + 0 = 1 \le 3\), and \(0 \ge -1\), all of which are true. The other options each violate at least one of the inequalities.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle 2(x + 1) - y \le 5\)
\(\displaystyle x + 3(y - 1) \ge 1\)
\(\displaystyle 3x - 2y < 6\)
qs.s: Simplifying gives \(2x - y \le 3\), \(x + 3y \ge 4\), and \(3x - 2y < 6\). Testing \((1, 2)\) satisfies all three inequalities, while \((0, 0)\), \((3, 2)\), and \((4, 0)\) each fail to satisfy the entire system.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle 3(x - 1) + 2y \le 11\)
\(\displaystyle 2(x + y) \ge y - 1\)
\(\displaystyle x - 3y \le 3\)
\(\displaystyle x \ge 1\)
qs.s: Simplifying the expressions yields \(3x + 2y \le 14\), \(2x + y \ge -1\), \(x - 3y \le 3\), and \(x \ge 1\). Testing \((2, 2)\) satisfies all four inequalities, whereas each distractor violates at least one constraint.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle 2x - 3y < 6\)
\(\displaystyle 3x + 2y \ge 6\)
\(\displaystyle y - x \le 2\)
qs.s: Testing \((3, 1)\) gives \(2(3) - 3(1) = 3 < 6\), \(3(3) + 2(1) = 11 \ge 6\), and \(1 - 3 = -2 \le 2\). The point \((3, 0)\) is excluded because it lies on the dashed boundary line \(2x - 3y = 6\) of the strict inequality.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle 4x - 5y \le 10\)
\(\displaystyle 5x + 3y \ge 15\)
\(\displaystyle x - 2y \ge -6\)
\(\displaystyle y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Substituting \((3, 2)\) produces \(4(3) - 5(2) = 2 \le 10\), \(5(3) + 3(2) = 21 \ge 15\), \(3 - 2(2) = -1 \ge -6\), and \(2 \ge 0\), which are all true. The other points each fail one of the inequalities.

qs.q:
Which ordered pair is in the solution set of the system of linear inequalities?
\(\displaystyle 2(x - y) + x \le 6\)
\(\displaystyle 3(x + y) - y \le 12\)
\(\displaystyle x - 4y \le 4\)
\(\displaystyle y \ge -1\)
qs.s: Simplifying the system gives \(3x - 2y \le 6\), \(3x + 2y \le 12\), \(x - 4y \le 4\), and \(y \ge -1\). Substituting \((0, 2)\) satisfies all four inequalities, while the distractors fail one or more conditions.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(x - y \le 2\)
\(x + 2y \ge 4\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: The point \((2, 2)\) satisfies \(2 - 2 = 0 \le 2\), \(2 + 2(2) = 6 \ge 4\), \(2 \ge 0\), and \(2 \ge 0\). The other points fail to satisfy all inequalities in the system.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(2x + y \le 6\)
\(x - 2y \ge 2\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \le 0\)
qs.s: Substituting \((2, -1)\) yields \(2(2) + (-1) = 3 \le 6\), \(2 - 2(-1) = 4 \ge 2\), \(2 \ge 0\), and \(-1 \le 0\), satisfying all conditions. The other points each violate at least one inequality.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(x + y \le 5\)
\(x - y \ge 1\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Substituting \((3, 1)\) into the system gives \(3 + 1 = 4 \le 5\), \(3 - 1 = 2 \ge 1\), \(3 \ge 0\), and \(1 \ge 0\), all of which are true. The other points each violate at least one inequality.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(x - y \ge -5\)
\(2x + y \ge -2\)
\(x \le 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: The ordered pair \((-1, 2)\) satisfies \(-1 - 2 = -3 \ge -5\), \(2(-1) + 2 = 0 \ge -2\), \(-1 \le 0\), and \(2 \ge 0\). The other options violate one or more conditions in the system.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(x + 2y \le 6\)
\(2x - y \le 4\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Substituting \((1, 1)\) gives \(1 + 2(1) = 3 \le 6\), \(2(1) - 1 = 1 \le 4\), \(1 \ge 0\), and \(1 \ge 0\), which are all true. Each distractor fails at least one inequality.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(4(x - 1) - y \le 2x + 3y + 2\)
\(3(x + y) - 5 \ge x - y + 7\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Simplifying the inequalities gives \(x - 2y \le 3\) and \(x + 2y \ge 6\); testing \((4, 2)\) gives \(4 - 2(2) = 0 \le 3\) and \(4 + 2(2) = 8 \ge 6\), which are both true along with \(4 \ge 0\) and \(2 \ge 0\). The other points fail one or more inequalities.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(2x + 3y \le 18\)
\(3x - 2y \le 12\)
\(x + y \ge 3\)
\(x \ge 1\)
\(y \ge 1\)
qs.s: Substituting \((3, 2)\) satisfies all five inequalities: \(2(3) + 3(2) = 12 \le 18\), \(3(3) - 2(2) = 5 \le 12\), \(3 + 2 = 5 \ge 3\), \(3 \ge 1\), and \(2 \ge 1\). Each distractor violates at least one constraint in the system.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(x + y \le 7\)
\(2x - y \le 5\)
\(x - 2y \le 2\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Testing \((2, 3)\) satisfies all five inequalities: \(2 + 3 \le 7\), \(2(2) - 3 = 1 \le 5\), \(2 - 2(3) = -4 \le 2\), \(2 \ge 0\), and \(3 \ge 0\). Each incorrect option fails at least one of the five constraints.

qs.q:
Which of the following ordered pairs lies in the solution region of the system of linear inequalities?
\(3(x + y) - 2x \le 8\)
\(2(2x - y) + 3y \ge 7\)
\(x \ge 0\)
\(y \ge 0\)
