Change to simplest radical form: \(-3\sqrt[4]{405}\)
Change to simplest radical form: \(4\sqrt[3]{-250}\)
Change to simplest radical form: \(-2\sqrt[3]{3456}\)
Change to simplest radical form: \(-6\sqrt[3]{\frac{16}{27}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the radical as \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{8 \cdot 2}}{\sqrt[3]{27}} = \frac{2\sqrt[3]{2}}{3}\). Multiplying by \(-6\) gives \(-6 \cdot \frac{2\sqrt[3]{2}}{3} = -4\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{2}{15}\sqrt[3]{-135}\)
qs.s: Factor \(-135\) as \(-27 \cdot 5\), which gives \(\sqrt[3]{-135} = -3\sqrt[3]{5}\). Multiplying by \(\frac{2}{15}\) yields \(\frac{2}{15}(-3\sqrt[3]{5}) = -\frac{2}{5}\sqrt[3]{5}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{3}{4}\sqrt[3]{-40}\)
qs.s: Factor \(-40\) as \(-8 \cdot 5\), so \(\sqrt[3]{-40} = -2\sqrt[3]{5}\). Multiplying by \(\frac{3}{4}\) gives \(\frac{3}{4}(-2\sqrt[3]{5}) = -\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[3]{5}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{5}{8}\sqrt[3]{-16}\)
Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{7}{9}\sqrt[3]{-54}\)
qs.s: Factor \(-54\) as \(-27 \cdot 2\), giving \(\sqrt[3]{-54} = -3\sqrt[3]{2}\). Multiplying by \(\frac{7}{9}\) gives \(\frac{7}{9}(-3\sqrt[3]{2}) = -\frac{7}{3}\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{7}{16}\sqrt[3]{-128}\)
qs.s: Factor \(-128\) as \(-64 \cdot 2\), so \(\sqrt[3]{-128} = -4\sqrt[3]{2}\). Multiplying by \(\frac{7}{16}\) results in \(\frac{7}{16}(-4\sqrt[3]{2}) = -\frac{7}{4}\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{9}{4}\sqrt[3]{-\frac{16}{27}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the radical as \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{-16}}{\sqrt[3]{27}} = \frac{-2\sqrt[3]{2}}{3}\). Multiplying by \(\frac{9}{4}\) yields \(\frac{9}{4}\left(-\frac{2\sqrt[3]{2}}{3}\right) = -\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(-\frac{5}{18}\sqrt[3]{-432}\)
Change to simplest radical form: \(-\frac{4}{21}\sqrt[3]{-686}\)
Change to simplest radical form: \(-\frac{4}{15}\sqrt[3]{-\frac{250}{64}}\)
qs.s: Evaluate the radical as \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{-250}}{\sqrt[3]{64}} = \frac{-5\sqrt[3]{2}}{4}\). Then \(-\frac{4}{15}\left(-\frac{5\sqrt[3]{2}}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{7}{6}\sqrt[5]{-192}\)
Change to simplest radical form: \(-\frac{4}{5}\sqrt[3]{375}\)
Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{135}\)
qs.s: Factor \(135\) as \(27 \cdot 5 = 3^3 \cdot 5\), so \(\sqrt[3]{135} = 3\sqrt[3]{5}\). Multiplying by \(\frac{2}{3}\) gives \(\frac{2}{3}(3\sqrt[3]{5}) = 2\sqrt[3]{5}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(-\frac{3}{4}\sqrt[3]{128}\)
qs.s: Factor \(128\) as \(64 \cdot 2 = 4^3 \cdot 2\), so \(\sqrt[3]{128} = 4\sqrt[3]{2}\). Multiplying by \(-\frac{3}{4}\) gives \(-\frac{3}{4}(4\sqrt[3]{2}) = -3\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{7}{2}\sqrt[3]{56}\)
qs.s: Factor \(56\) as \(8 \cdot 7 = 2^3 \cdot 7\), so \(\sqrt[3]{56} = 2\sqrt[3]{7}\). Multiplying by \(\frac{7}{2}\) gives \(\frac{7}{2}(2\sqrt[3]{7}) = 7\sqrt[3]{7}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(-\frac{5}{3}\sqrt[3]{108}\)
qs.s: Factor \(108\) as \(27 \cdot 4 = 3^3 \cdot 4\), so \(\sqrt[3]{108} = 3\sqrt[3]{4}\). Multiplying by \(-\frac{5}{3}\) gives \(-\frac{5}{3}(3\sqrt[3]{4}) = -5\sqrt[3]{4}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(-\frac{3}{7}\sqrt[3]{-1372}\)
Change to simplest radical form: \(-\frac{5}{8}\sqrt[3]{432}\)
Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{4}{3}\sqrt[3]{135} - \frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{40}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(\frac{4}{3}\sqrt[3]{27 \cdot 5} = \frac{4}{3}(3\sqrt[3]{5}) = 4\sqrt[3]{5}\) and \(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{8 \cdot 5} = \frac{1}{2}(2\sqrt[3]{5}) = \sqrt[3]{5}\). Subtracting gives \(4\sqrt[3]{5} - \sqrt[3]{5} = 3\sqrt[3]{5}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(-\frac{5}{6}\sqrt[4]{567}\)
qs.s: Factor \(567\) as \(81 \cdot 7 = 3^4 \cdot 7\), so \(\sqrt[4]{567} = 3\sqrt[4]{7}\). Multiplying by \(-\frac{5}{6}\) gives \(-\frac{5}{6}(3\sqrt[4]{7}) = -\frac{5}{2}\sqrt[4]{7}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(-\frac{5}{2}\sqrt[3]{\frac{54}{125}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the radical as \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{54}{125}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{27 \cdot 2}}{\sqrt[3]{125}} = \frac{3\sqrt[3]{2}}{5}\). Multiplying by \(-\frac{5}{2}\) gives \(-\frac{5}{2} \cdot \frac{3\sqrt[3]{2}}{5} = -\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form. \(\sqrt[4]{48}\)
qs.s: Factor 48 as \(16 \times 3 = 2^4 \times 3\). Then \(\sqrt[4]{48} = \sqrt[4]{2^4 \cdot 3} = 2\sqrt[4]{3}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form. \(\sqrt[4]{80}\)
qs.s: Factor 80 as \(16 \times 5 = 2^4 \times 5\). Then \(\sqrt[4]{80} = \sqrt[4]{2^4 \cdot 5} = 2\sqrt[4]{5}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form. \(\sqrt[4]{112}\)
qs.s: Factor 112 as \(16 \times 7 = 2^4 \times 7\). Then \(\sqrt[4]{112} = \sqrt[4]{2^4 \cdot 7} = 2\sqrt[4]{7}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form. \(\sqrt[4]{405}\)
qs.s: Factor 405 as \(81 \times 5 = 3^4 \times 5\). Then \(\sqrt[4]{405} = \sqrt[4]{3^4 \cdot 5} = 3\sqrt[4]{5}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form. \(\sqrt[4]{243}\)
qs.s: Factor 243 as \(81 \times 3 = 3^4 \times 3\). Then \(\sqrt[4]{243} = \sqrt[4]{3^4 \cdot 3} = 3\sqrt[4]{3}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form. \(\sqrt[4]{2592}\)
qs.s: Factor 2592 into prime factors as \(2^5 \times 3^4 = (2 \cdot 3)^4 \times 2 = 6^4 \times 2\). Thus, \(\sqrt[4]{2592} = \sqrt[4]{6^4 \cdot 2} = 6\sqrt[4]{2}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form. \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{32}{625}}\)
qs.s: Apply the quotient rule to obtain \(\frac{\sqrt[4]{32}}{\sqrt[4]{625}}\). Since \(32 = 16 \times 2 = 2^4 \times 2\) and \(625 = 5^4\), this simplifies to \(\frac{2\sqrt[4]{2}}{5}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form. \(-2\sqrt[4]{1250}\)
qs.s: Factor 1250 as \(625 \times 2 = 5^4 \times 2\), so \(\sqrt[4]{1250} = 5\sqrt[4]{2}\). Multiplying by \(-2\) gives \(-2(5\sqrt[4]{2}) = -10\sqrt[4]{2}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form. \(5\sqrt[4]{512}\)
qs.s: Factor 512 as \(256 \times 2 = 4^4 \times 2\), which gives \(\sqrt[4]{512} = 4\sqrt[4]{2}\). Multiplying by the outside coefficient yields \(5 \times 4\sqrt[4]{2} = 20\sqrt[4]{2}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{3}{4}\sqrt[4]{512}\)
qs.s: Factor \(512 = 4^4 \cdot 2\), so \(\sqrt[4]{512} = 4\sqrt[4]{2}\). Multiplying by the coefficient gives \(\frac{3}{4} \cdot 4\sqrt[4]{2} = 3\sqrt[4]{2}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{4}{3}\sqrt[4]{162}\)
qs.s: Factor \(162 = 3^4 \cdot 2\), so \(\sqrt[4]{162} = 3\sqrt[4]{2}\). Multiplying by the coefficient gives \(\frac{4}{3} \cdot 3\sqrt[4]{2} = 4\sqrt[4]{2}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{2}{5}\sqrt[4]{1875}\)
qs.s: Factor \(1875 = 5^4 \cdot 3\), so \(\sqrt[4]{1875} = 5\sqrt[4]{3}\). Multiplying by the coefficient gives \(\frac{2}{5} \cdot 5\sqrt[4]{3} = 2\sqrt[4]{3}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{5}{6}\sqrt[4]{2592}\)
qs.s: Factor \(2592 = 6^4 \cdot 2\), so \(\sqrt[4]{2592} = 6\sqrt[4]{2}\). Multiplying by the coefficient gives \(\frac{5}{6} \cdot 6\sqrt[4]{2} = 5\sqrt[4]{2}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[4]{\frac{162}{625}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the radical quotient as \(\frac{\sqrt[4]{81 \cdot 2}}{\sqrt[4]{625}} = \frac{3\sqrt[4]{2}}{5}\). Multiplying by the coefficient gives \(\frac{2}{3} \cdot \frac{3\sqrt[4]{2}}{5} = \frac{2\sqrt[4]{2}}{5}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{5}{6}\sqrt[4]{\frac{405}{16}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the radical to get \(\frac{\sqrt[4]{81 \cdot 5}}{\sqrt[4]{16}} = \frac{3\sqrt[4]{5}}{2}\). Multiplying by \(\frac{5}{6}\) gives \(\frac{5}{6} \cdot \frac{3\sqrt[4]{5}}{2} = \frac{5\sqrt[4]{5}}{4}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\left(\frac{3}{4}\sqrt[3]{24}\right)\left(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{36}\right)\)
qs.s: Multiply the coefficients \(\frac{3}{4} \cdot \frac{2}{3} = \frac{1}{2}\) and the radicals \(\sqrt[3]{24 \cdot 36} = \sqrt[3]{216 \cdot 4} = 6\sqrt[3]{4}\). Multiplying together gives \(\frac{1}{2} \cdot 6\sqrt[3]{4} = 3\sqrt[3]{4}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{3}{10}\sqrt[4]{320000}\)
qs.s: Factor \(320000 = 20^4 \cdot 2\), so \(\sqrt[4]{320000} = 20\sqrt[4]{2}\). Multiplying by the coefficient gives \(\frac{3}{10} \cdot 20\sqrt[4]{2} = 6\sqrt[4]{2}\).

qs.q: Change to simplest radical form: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[4]{48} \cdot \sqrt[4]{54}\)
qs.s: Multiply under the radical to get \(\sqrt[4]{48 \cdot 54} = \sqrt[4]{16 \cdot 81 \cdot 2} = 6\sqrt[4]{2}\). Then multiply by the coefficient: \(\frac{2}{3} \cdot 6\sqrt[4]{2} = 4\sqrt[4]{2}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{p^3 q^6}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the radicand as \(p^2 \cdot p \cdot q^6 = (p q^3)^2 \cdot p\). Taking the square root results in \(p q^3 \sqrt{p}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{m^3 n^4}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \(m^2 \cdot m \cdot n^4 = (m n^2)^2 \cdot m\). Extracting the perfect square factors gives \(m n^2 \sqrt{m}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{x^2 y^5}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the radicand as \(x^2 \cdot y^4 \cdot y = (x y^2)^2 \cdot y\). Taking the square root yields \(x y^2 \sqrt{y}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{a^5 b^2}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \(a^4 \cdot a \cdot b^2 = (a^2 b)^2 \cdot a\). Taking the square root gives \(a^2 b \sqrt{a}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{u^5 v^4}\)
qs.s: Separate the perfect square factors: \(\sqrt{u^4 \cdot u \cdot v^4} = \sqrt{(u^2 v^2)^2 \cdot u}\). This simplifies to \(u^2 v^2 \sqrt{u}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{50 a^3 b^7 c^4}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the radicand as \((25 \cdot a^2 \cdot b^6 \cdot c^4)(2 a b) = (5 a b^3 c^2)^2 (2 a b)\). Taking the square root gives \(5 a b^3 c^2 \sqrt{2 a b}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{72 x^5 y^6}\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest perfect square factors: \(\sqrt{36 \cdot 2 \cdot x^4 \cdot x \cdot y^6} = \sqrt{36 x^4 y^6} \cdot \sqrt{2 x} = 6 x^2 y^3 \sqrt{2 x}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[4]{48 x^9 y^6}\)
qs.s: Group factors into fourth powers: \(48 x^9 y^6 = 16 \cdot 3 \cdot x^8 \cdot x \cdot y^4 \cdot y^2 = (2 x^2 y)^4 \cdot (3 x y^2)\). Taking the fourth root gives \(2 x^2 y \sqrt[4]{3 x y^2}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{108 u^9 v^4 w^5}\)
d: \(6 u^4 v^2 w^2 \sqrt{3 u v w}\)
qs.s: Factor into perfect square and remaining terms: \(108 u^9 v^4 w^5 = (36 u^8 v^4 w^4)(3 u w) = (6 u^4 v^2 w^2)^2 (3 u w)\). Taking the square root produces \(6 u^4 v^2 w^2 \sqrt{3 u w}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{54 x^7 y^5}\)
qs.s: Identify the perfect cube factors: \(54 x^7 y^5 = 27 \cdot 2 \cdot x^6 \cdot x \cdot y^3 \cdot y^2 = (3 x^2 y)^3 \cdot (2 x y^2)\). Taking the cube root yields \(3 x^2 y \sqrt[3]{2 x y^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{100x^3 y^9}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \(\sqrt{100 \cdot x^2 \cdot x \cdot y^8 \cdot y} = \sqrt{100x^2 y^8} \cdot \sqrt{xy} = 10xy^4\sqrt{xy}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{64a^7 b^3}\)
qs.s: Factor out the perfect square components: \(\sqrt{64 \cdot a^6 \cdot a \cdot b^2 \cdot b} = \sqrt{64a^6 b^2} \cdot \sqrt{ab} = 8a^3 b\sqrt{ab}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{36u^5 v^7}\)
qs.s: Separate the perfect square factors from the remainder: \(\sqrt{36 \cdot u^4 \cdot u \cdot v^6 \cdot v} = 6u^2 v^3\sqrt{uv}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{81m^3 n^5}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the radicand using perfect squares: \(\sqrt{81 \cdot m^2 \cdot m \cdot n^4 \cdot n} = \sqrt{81m^2 n^4} \cdot \sqrt{mn} = 9mn^2\sqrt{mn}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{25x^5 y^3}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand into perfect square factors: \(\sqrt{25 \cdot x^4 \cdot x \cdot y^2 \cdot y} = \sqrt{25x^4 y^2} \cdot \sqrt{xy} = 5x^2 y\sqrt{xy}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{54x^5 y^8}\)
qs.s: Find the perfect cube factors: \(\sqrt[3]{27 \cdot 2 \cdot x^3 \cdot x^2 \cdot y^6 \cdot y^2} = \sqrt[3]{27x^3 y^6} \cdot \sqrt[3]{2x^2 y^2} = 3xy^2\sqrt[3]{2x^2 y^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{72x^5 y^8}\)
qs.s: Factor 72 as \(36 \cdot 2\) and group perfect squares: \(\sqrt{36 \cdot 2 \cdot x^4 \cdot x \cdot y^8} = 6x^2 y^4\sqrt{2x}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{50a^3 b^6 c^7}\)
qs.s: Factor 50 as \(25 \cdot 2\) and extract perfect squares from all three variables: \(\sqrt{25 \cdot 2 \cdot a^2 \cdot a \cdot b^6 \cdot c^6 \cdot c} = 5ab^3 c^3\sqrt{2ac}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{180x^7 y^4 z^5}\)
qs.s: Factor 180 into \(36 \cdot 5\) and take out the even powers: \(\sqrt{36 \cdot 5 \cdot x^6 \cdot x \cdot y^4 \cdot z^4 \cdot z} = 6x^3 y^2 z^2\sqrt{5xz}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{96a^4 b^7 c^5 d^3}\)
qs.s: Factor 96 as \(16 \cdot 6\) and extract square factors across all four variables: \(\sqrt{16 \cdot 6 \cdot a^4 \cdot b^6 \cdot b \cdot c^4 \cdot c \cdot d^2 \cdot d} = 4a^2 b^3 c^2 d\sqrt{6bcd}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt{12y^4}\)
qs.s: Factor 12 as \(4 \cdot 3\) and write \(y^4\) as \((y^2)^2\). Then \(\sqrt{12y^4} = \sqrt{4(y^2)^2} \cdot \sqrt{3} = 2y^2\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt{50a^8}\)
qs.s: Factor 50 as \(25 \cdot 2\) and write \(a^8\) as \((a^4)^2\). Taking the square roots of the perfect square factors gives \(\sqrt{25(a^4)^2} \cdot \sqrt{2} = 5a^4\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt{75c^6}\)
qs.s: Factor 75 as \(25 \cdot 3\) and write \(c^6\) as \((c^3)^2\). Simplifying yields \(\sqrt{25(c^3)^2} \cdot \sqrt{3} = 5c^3\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt{32k^4}\)
qs.s: Factor 32 as \(16 \cdot 2\) and write \(k^4\) as \((k^2)^2\). Taking the square root of the perfect square factors gives \(\sqrt{16(k^2)^2} \cdot \sqrt{2} = 4k^2\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt{180x^9y^6}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand into perfect square factors and remaining factors: \((36x^8y^6)(5x)\). Evaluating the square roots gives \(6x^4y^3\sqrt{5x}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt{300a^5b^8c^{11}}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \((100a^4b^8c^{10})(3ac)\). Evaluating the square root of the perfect square part gives \(10a^2b^4c^5\sqrt{3ac}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt{72x^5y^4}\)
qs.s: Separate the radicand into perfect squares and remaining factors: \(\sqrt{(36x^4y^4)(2x)}\). Taking the square root of the perfect square part gives \(6x^2y^2\sqrt{2x}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt{108a^7b^3}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \((36a^6b^2)(3ab)\). Taking the square root of the perfect square factor yields \(\sqrt{36a^6b^2} \cdot \sqrt{3ab} = 6a^3b\sqrt{3ab}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt{98x^3y^{10}z^5}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the radicand as \((49x^2y^{10}z^4)(2xz)\). Taking the square root of the perfect square factors results in \(7xy^5z^2\sqrt{2xz}\).

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{81u^3 v^{12}}\)

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{36a^8 b^7}\)

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{180u^{10} v^{13} w^7}\)

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{150a^5 b^8 c^{13}}\)

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{3}{y^6}}\)
qs.s: Using the quotient property of radicals, \(\sqrt{\frac{3}{y^6}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{y^6}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{y^3}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{7}{a^2}}\)
qs.s: Apply the quotient property of radicals to obtain \(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{a^2}} = \frac{\sqrt{7}}{a}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{2}{m^4}}\)
qs.s: Separating the numerator and denominator yields \(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{m^4}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{m^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{11}{x^8}}\)
qs.s: Apply the quotient property to rewrite the expression as \(\frac{\sqrt{11}}{\sqrt{x^8}} = \frac{\sqrt{11}}{x^4}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{13}{b^{10}}}\)
qs.s: Using the quotient rule for radicals gives \(\frac{\sqrt{13}}{\sqrt{b^{10}}} = \frac{\sqrt{13}}{b^5}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{12a^3}{b^8}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the numerator \(\sqrt{12a^3} = \sqrt{4 \cdot 3 \cdot a^2 \cdot a} = 2a\sqrt{3a}\) and the denominator \(\sqrt{b^8} = b^4\) to obtain \(\frac{2a\sqrt{3a}}{b^4}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{50}{9x^4}}\)
qs.s: Simplify numerator and denominator separately: \(\sqrt{50} = \sqrt{25 \cdot 2} = 5\sqrt{2}\) and \(\sqrt{9x^4} = 3x^2\), giving \(\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{3x^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{45x^7}{16y^6}}\)
qs.s: Simplify both parts: \(\sqrt{45x^7} = \sqrt{9 \cdot 5 \cdot x^6 \cdot x} = 3x^3\sqrt{5x}\) and \(\sqrt{16y^6} = 4y^3\), which gives \(\frac{3x^3\sqrt{5x}}{4y^3}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{75x^5}{y^{10}}}\)
qs.s: Factor out perfect squares: \(\sqrt{75x^5} = \sqrt{25 \cdot 3 \cdot x^4 \cdot x} = 5x^2\sqrt{3x}\) and \(\sqrt{y^{10}} = y^5\), yielding \(\frac{5x^2\sqrt{3x}}{y^5}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{7}{27x^6}}\)
qs.s: Apply the quotient property for cube roots: \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{7}{27x^6}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{7}}{\sqrt[3]{27x^6}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{7}}{3x^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{p^8 q^5}{81}}\)
qs.s: Extract the square roots of the perfect square factors: \(\sqrt{\frac{p^8 q^5}{81}} = \frac{\sqrt{p^8 \cdot q^4 \cdot q}}{\sqrt{81}} = \frac{p^4 q^2 \sqrt{q}}{9}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{m^7 n^2}{100}}\)
qs.s: Separate the perfect square factors in the numerator and evaluate the denominator: \(\sqrt{\frac{m^7 n^2}{100}} = \frac{\sqrt{m^6 \cdot m \cdot n^2}}{\sqrt{100}} = \frac{m^3 n \sqrt{m}}{10}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{a^6 b^3}{49}}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerator into perfect squares and take the square root of the denominator: \(\sqrt{\frac{a^6 b^3}{49}} = \frac{\sqrt{a^6 \cdot b^2 \cdot b}}{\sqrt{49}} = \frac{a^3 b \sqrt{b}}{7}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{u^4 v^7}{36}}\)
qs.s: Factor \(v^7\) into \(v^6 \cdot v\) and simplify: \(\sqrt{\frac{u^4 v^7}{36}} = \frac{\sqrt{u^4 \cdot v^6 \cdot v}}{\sqrt{36}} = \frac{u^2 v^3 \sqrt{v}}{6}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{x^{10} y^3}{25}}\)
qs.s: Take the square root of each perfect square component: \(\sqrt{\frac{x^{10} y^3}{25}} = \frac{\sqrt{x^{10} \cdot y^2 \cdot y}}{\sqrt{25}} = \frac{x^5 y \sqrt{y}}{5}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{98 x^9 y^4}{81 z^6}}\)
qs.s: Factor numerator and denominator into perfect squares: \(\frac{\sqrt{49 \cdot 2 \cdot x^8 \cdot x \cdot y^4}}{\sqrt{81 z^6}} = \frac{7 x^4 y^2 \sqrt{2x}}{9 z^3}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{48 x^7 y^{10}}{75}}\)
qs.s: Reduce the fraction by dividing the coefficients by 3 to obtain \(\sqrt{\frac{16 x^7 y^{10}}{25}}\), then take the square root of perfect squares to get \(\frac{4 x^3 y^5 \sqrt{x}}{5}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt{\frac{50 x^5 y^6}{49}}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerical coefficient \(50 = 25 \cdot 2\) and variable terms into perfect squares: \(\frac{\sqrt{25 \cdot 2 \cdot x^4 \cdot x \cdot y^6}}{\sqrt{49}} = \frac{5 x^2 y^3 \sqrt{2x}}{7}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{54y^3}\)
qs.s: Factor 54 into \(27 \times 2\), where 27 is a perfect cube. Taking the cube root of \(27y^3\) gives \(3y\), leaving \(3y\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{135x^3}\)
qs.s: Factor 135 into \(27 \times 5\), where 27 is a perfect cube. Taking the cube root of \(27x^3\) gives \(3x\), leaving \(3x\sqrt[3]{5}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{56b^3}\)
qs.s: Factor 56 into \(8 \times 7\), where 8 is a perfect cube. Taking the cube root of \(8b^3\) gives \(2b\), leaving \(2b\sqrt[3]{7}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{24a^3}\)
qs.s: Factor 24 into \(8 \times 3\), where 8 is a perfect cube. Taking the cube root of \(8a^3\) gives \(2a\), leaving \(2a\sqrt[3]{3}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{320u^8v^5}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \((64u^6v^3)(5u^2v^2)\). Since \(\sqrt[3]{64u^6v^3} = 4u^2v\), the simplest radical form is \(4u^2v\sqrt[3]{5u^2v^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{108x^5y^6}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the radicand as \((27x^3y^6)(4x^2)\). Taking the cube root of the perfect cube factor \(27x^3y^6\) gives \(3xy^2\), leaving \(3xy^2\sqrt[3]{4x^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{500x^{10}y^6z^2}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \((125x^9y^6)(4xz^2)\). The cube root of \(125x^9y^6\) is \(5x^3y^2\), while \(4xz^2\) remains under the cube root, giving \(5x^3y^2\sqrt[3]{4xz^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{432m^4n^9p^5}\)
qs.s: Separate the radicand into the perfect cube factor \(216m^3n^9p^3\) and the remaining factor \(2mp^2\). Taking the cube root gives \(6mn^3p\sqrt[3]{2mp^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-27x^6}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the radicand as a perfect cube: \(-27x^6 = (-3x^2)^3\). Taking the cube root gives \(-3x^2\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-125x^{15}}\)
qs.s: Write the radicand as a perfect cube: \(-125x^{15} = (-5x^5)^3\). Simplifying the cube root gives \(-5x^5\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-64x^{12}}\)
qs.s: Express the radicand as \((-4x^4)^3\). Taking the cube root yields \(\sqrt[3]{(-4x^4)^3} = -4x^4\).

Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-8x^{18}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(-8x^{18}\) as \((-2x^6)^3\). Taking the cube root yields \(-2x^6\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-\frac{24x^{11}}{125}}\)
qs.s: Write as \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{-24x^{11}}}{\sqrt[3]{125}}\). Factoring the numerator gives \(\sqrt[3]{(-8x^9)(3x^2)} = -2x^3\sqrt[3]{3x^2}\), and evaluating the denominator gives \(5\), resulting in \(-\frac{2x^3\sqrt[3]{3x^2}}{5}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-54x^7y^6}\)
qs.s: Separate the radicand into a perfect cube factor and the remainder: \(-54x^7y^6 = (-27x^6y^6)(2x) = (-3x^2y^2)^3(2x)\). Taking the cube root gives \(-3x^2y^2\sqrt[3]{2x}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-16x^8}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand into perfect cube and non-cube parts: \(-16x^8 = (-8x^6)(2x^2) = (-2x^2)^3(2x^2)\). Extracting the cube root of the perfect cube factor gives \(-2x^2\sqrt[3]{2x^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-250x^{10}y^5}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand using prime factorization: \(-250x^{10}y^5 = (-125x^9y^3)(2xy^2) = (-5x^3y)^3(2xy^2)\). Taking the cube root of the perfect cube part yields \(-5x^3y\sqrt[3]{2xy^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-40x^4y^8}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \((-8x^3y^6)(5xy^2) = (-2xy^2)^3(5xy^2)\). Simplifying the perfect cube factor produces \(-2xy^2\sqrt[3]{5xy^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{-216u^6 v^6}\)
qs.s: Since \((-6u^2 v^2)^3 = -216u^6 v^6\), evaluating the cube root yields \(-6u^2 v^2\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{-125x^9 y^3}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \((-5x^3 y)^3\). Taking the cube root gives \(\sqrt[3]{(-5x^3 y)^3} = -5x^3 y\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{-8m^3 n^{12}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the expression as \(\sqrt[3]{(-2mn^4)^3}\). Simplifying the cube root gives \(-2mn^4\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{-343p^3 q^9}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the radicand as \((-7pq^3)^3\). Taking the cube root results in \(-7pq^3\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{-27a^6 b^3}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \((-3a^2 b)^3\). Taking the cube root yields \(\sqrt[3]{(-3a^2 b)^3} = -3a^2 b\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{-16a^4 b^9}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \((-8a^3 b^9)(2a)\). Taking the cube root of the perfect cube factor yields \(-2ab^3\sqrt[3]{2a}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{-108x^8 y^{11}}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \((-27x^6 y^9)(4x^2 y^2)\). Taking the cube root of the perfect cube factor yields \(-3x^2 y^3\sqrt[3]{4x^2 y^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{-54x^5 y^7}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand into perfect cube factors and remaining factors: \(-54x^5 y^7 = (-27x^3 y^6)(2x^2 y)\). Evaluating \(\sqrt[3]{-27x^3 y^6}\) gives \(-3xy^2\sqrt[3]{2x^2 y}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\sqrt[3]{-250x^6 y^4 z^8}\)
qs.s: Separate the radicand into perfect cube and non-cube factors: \((-125x^6 y^3 z^6)(2yz^2)\). Taking the cube root of the perfect cube factors gives \(-5x^2 yz^2\sqrt[3]{2yz^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{125y^4}\)
qs.s: Write \(125y^4\) as \(5^3 \cdot y^3 \cdot y\). Evaluating the cube root of the perfect cube factors gives \(5y\sqrt[3]{y}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{250a^8b^{11}c^3}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the radicand as \((125a^6b^9c^3)(2a^2b^2) = (5a^2b^3c)^3(2a^2b^2)\). Evaluating the cube root gives \(5a^2b^3c\sqrt[3]{2a^2b^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{432x^5y^{10}z^{12}}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \((216x^3y^9z^{12})(2x^2y) = (6xy^3z^4)^3(2x^2y)\). Taking the cube root gives \(6xy^3z^4\sqrt[3]{2x^2y}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{108x^7y^4}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand into perfect cube factors: \(108x^7y^4 = (27x^6y^3)(4xy) = (3x^2y)^3(4xy)\). Taking the cube root yields \(3x^2y\sqrt[3]{4xy}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{54x^7}{125y^6}}\)
qs.s: Apply the quotient rule to simplify \(\sqrt[3]{54x^7} = 3x^2\sqrt[3]{2x}\) in the numerator and \(\sqrt[3]{125y^6} = 5y^2\) in the denominator, resulting in \(\frac{3x^2\sqrt[3]{2x}}{5y^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[5]{32x^5 y^{15}}\)
qs.s: Take the fifth root of 32, which is 2, and divide each exponent by 5 to obtain \(x^{5/5} = x\) and \(y^{15/5} = y^3\), resulting in \(2xy^3\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[4]{81a^8 b^4}\)
qs.s: Evaluate the fourth root of the coefficient and divide each exponent by 4: \(\sqrt[4]{81} = 3\), \(a^{8/4} = a^2\), and \(b^{4/4} = b\), yielding \(3a^2 b\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[4]{16p^{12} q^{16}}\)
qs.s: Find the fourth root of 16, which is 2, and divide each exponent by 4 to get \(p^{12/4} = p^3\) and \(q^{16/4} = q^4\), giving \(2p^3 q^4\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{27x^6 y^3}\)
qs.s: Take the cube root of the coefficient and divide each variable exponent by 3: \(\sqrt[3]{27} = 3\), \(x^{6/3} = x^2\), and \(y^{3/3} = y\), giving \(3x^2 y\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[4]{32x^7 y^9}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand into perfect fourth powers and remainders: \(32x^7 y^9 = (16x^4 y^8)(2x^3 y)\). Taking the fourth root of the perfect powers gives \(2xy^2 \sqrt[4]{2x^3 y}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[4]{162x^{11} y^7 z^5}\)
qs.s: Separate the radicand into perfect fourth powers and remainders: \((81x^8 y^4 z^4)(2x^3 y^3 z)\). Taking the fourth root of the perfect powers yields \(3x^2 y z \sqrt[4]{2x^3 y^3 z}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{54x^7 y^5}{125}}\)
qs.s: Apply the quotient rule for radicals to separate numerator and denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{(27x^6 y^3)(2xy^2)}}{\sqrt[3]{125}} = \frac{3x^2 y\sqrt[3]{2xy^2}}{5}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{108a^7 b^5 c^9}\)
qs.s: Factor out the largest perfect cube factor: \(108a^7 b^5 c^9 = (27a^6 b^3 c^9)(4ab^2)\). Extracting the cube root gives \(3a^2 b c^3 \sqrt[3]{4ab^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[4]{8x^5 y^3} \cdot \sqrt[4]{2x^3 y^5}\)
qs.s: Multiply the radicands under a single fourth root to get \(\sqrt[4]{16x^8 y^8}\), then evaluate each factor to obtain \(2x^2 y^2\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{108x^4 y^7}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand into \((27x^3 y^6)(4xy) = (3xy^2)^3(4xy)\). Taking the cube root gives \(3xy^2\sqrt[3]{4xy}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[4]{405m^6 n^9}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand into \((81m^4 n^8)(5m^2 n) = (3mn^2)^4(5m^2 n)\). Taking the fourth root gives \(3mn^2\sqrt[4]{5m^2 n}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{250p^5 q^8}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand into \((125p^3 q^6)(2p^2 q^2) = (5pq^2)^3(2p^2 q^2)\). Taking the cube root gives \(5pq^2\sqrt[3]{2p^2 q^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[4]{32x^7 y^6}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand into \((16x^4 y^4)(2x^3 y^2) = (2xy)^4(2x^3 y^2)\). Taking the fourth root gives \(2xy\sqrt[4]{2x^3 y^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[4]{48a^7 b^5}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand into \((16a^4 b^4)(3a^3 b) = (2ab)^4(3a^3 b)\). Taking the fourth root gives \(2ab\sqrt[4]{3a^3 b}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[5]{486a^8 b^{11} c^{14}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the radicand as \((243a^5 b^{10} c^{10})(2a^3 b c^4) = (3ab^2 c^2)^5(2a^3 b c^4)\). Taking the fifth root gives \(3ab^2 c^2\sqrt[5]{2a^3 b c^4}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(2a^2 b\sqrt[4]{1250a^5 b^7 c^4}\)
qs.s: Simplify the radical factor to \(\sqrt[4]{1250a^5 b^7 c^4} = 5abc\sqrt[4]{2ab^3}\), then multiply by \(2a^2 b\) to get \(10a^3 b^2 c\sqrt[4]{2ab^3}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{80x^9 y^6}{81z^{12}}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the numerator to \(\sqrt[4]{80x^9 y^6} = 2x^2 y\sqrt[4]{5xy^2}\) and the denominator to \(\sqrt[4]{81z^{12}} = 3z^3\), producing \(\frac{2x^2 y\sqrt[4]{5xy^2}}{3z^3}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(3xy\sqrt[3]{375x^5 y^8}\)
qs.s: First simplify \(\sqrt[3]{375x^5 y^8} = 5xy^2\sqrt[3]{3x^2 y^2}\), then multiply by the outer term \(3xy\) to obtain \(15x^2 y^3\sqrt[3]{3x^2 y^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[4]{512x^7 y^{10} z^{13}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the radicand as \((256x^4 y^8 z^{12})(2x^3 y^2 z) = (4xy^2 z^3)^4(2x^3 y^2 z)\). Taking the fourth root yields \(4xy^2 z^3\sqrt[4]{2x^3 y^2 z}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-27y}\)
qs.s: Since \((-3)^3 = -27\) and the exponent of \(y\) is less than 3, taking the cube root of \(-27\) gives \(-3\sqrt[3]{y}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-64b^2}\)
qs.s: Since \((-4)^3 = -64\) and \(b^2\) cannot be simplified under a cube root, the expression simplifies to \(-4\sqrt[3]{b^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-8x^2}\)
qs.s: Since \((-2)^3 = -8\) and the exponent of \(x^2\) is less than the index 3, we extract \(-2\) from the radical to obtain \(-2\sqrt[3]{x^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[5]{-243a^3}\)
qs.s: Since \((-3)^5 = -243\) and the exponent of \(a^3\) is less than 5, we evaluate \(\sqrt[5]{-243}\) to get \(-3\sqrt[5]{a^3}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-125n^2}\)
qs.s: Since \((-5)^3 = -125\) and the exponent of \(n^2\) is less than 3, extracting the cube root of \(-125\) yields \(-5\sqrt[3]{n^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-135a^7b^4}\)
qs.s: Separate the perfect cube factors: \(\sqrt[3]{(-27a^6b^3)(5ab)} = \sqrt[3]{(-3a^2b)^3 \cdot 5ab} = -3a^2b\sqrt[3]{5ab}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[5]{-96x^8}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \((-32x^5)(3x^3) = (-2x)^5(3x^3)\). Taking the fifth root yields \(-2x\sqrt[5]{3x^3}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[5]{-64x^9y^{11}}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \((-32x^5y^{10})(2x^4y) = (-2xy^2)^5(2x^4y)\). Extracting the fifth root yields \(-2xy^2\sqrt[5]{2x^4y}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-54x^5}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand into perfect cube factors and remaining factors: \(\sqrt[3]{(-27x^3)(2x^2)} = \sqrt[3]{(-3x)^3 \cdot 2x^2} = -3x\sqrt[3]{2x^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{-40x^4y^6}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the radicand as \((-8x^3y^6)(5x) = (-2xy^2)^3(5x)\). Taking the cube root gives \(-2xy^2\sqrt[3]{5x}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[5]{64u^5 v^{10}}\)
qs.s: Factor 64 as \(2^5 \cdot 2\) and rewrite the variables as \(u^5\) and \((v^2)^5\). Extracting the fifth powers leaves \(2uv^2\sqrt[5]{2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{250x^9 y^3}\)
qs.s: Factor 250 as \(5^3 \cdot 2\) and group the variables as \((x^3)^3\) and \(y^3\). Taking the cube root gives \(5x^3 y\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[4]{48x^4 y^8}\)
qs.s: Factor 48 as \(2^4 \cdot 3\) and rewrite the variables as \(x^4\) and \((y^2)^4\). Taking the fourth root of the perfect fourth powers yields \(2xy^2\sqrt[4]{3}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{54a^6 b^3}\)
qs.s: Factor 54 as \(3^3 \cdot 2\) and express the variables as \((a^2)^3\) and \(b^3\). Evaluating the cube roots of the perfect cube factors gives \(3a^2 b\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[4]{512a^{11} b^{19} c^5}\)
qs.s: Factor 512 as \(256 \cdot 2 = 4^4 \cdot 2\) and rewrite the variables as \((a^2)^4 a^3\), \((b^4)^4 b^3\), and \(c^4 c\). Taking the fourth root gives \(4a^2 b^4 c\sqrt[4]{2a^3 b^3 c}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{405a^9 b^{13}}{16c^8}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(3^4 \cdot 5 \cdot (a^2)^4 a \cdot (b^3)^4 b\) and the denominator as \(2^4(c^2)^4\). Taking the fourth root of both numerator and denominator yields \(\frac{3a^2 b^3\sqrt[4]{5ab}}{2c^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[6]{320x^{13} y^{25} z^7}\)
qs.s: Factor 320 as \(64 \cdot 5 = 2^6 \cdot 5\) and express the variables as \((x^2)^6 x\), \((y^4)^6 y\), and \(z^6 z\). Extracting the sixth powers yields \(2x^2 y^4 z\sqrt[6]{5xyz}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[5]{96x^{11} y^{16} z^5}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \(2^5 \cdot 3 \cdot (x^2)^5 x \cdot (y^3)^5 y \cdot z^5\). Extract the fifth powers from under the radical to get \(2x^2 y^3 z\sqrt[5]{3xy}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{432x^8 y^{11} z^6}\)
qs.s: Factor 432 as \(216 \cdot 2 = 6^3 \cdot 2\) and group cube powers of the variables as \((x^2)^3 x^2\), \((y^3)^3 y^2\), and \((z^2)^3\). Taking the cube root gives \(6x^2 y^3 z^2\sqrt[3]{2x^2 y^2}\).

exercises.name: Converting numerical radicals to entire radicals

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(3\sqrt{6}\)
qs.s: \(3\sqrt{6} = \sqrt{3^2 \cdot 6} = \sqrt{9 \cdot 6} = \sqrt{54}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(5\sqrt{2}\)
qs.s: \(5\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{5^2 \cdot 2} = \sqrt{25 \cdot 2} = \sqrt{50}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(2\sqrt{7}\)
qs.s: \(2\sqrt{7} = \sqrt{2^2 \cdot 7} = \sqrt{4 \cdot 7} = \sqrt{28}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(4\sqrt{3}\)
qs.s: \(4\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{4^2 \cdot 3} = \sqrt{16 \cdot 3} = \sqrt{48}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(3\sqrt{2}\)
qs.s: \(3\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{3^2 \cdot 2} = \sqrt{9 \cdot 2} = \sqrt{18}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{5}\)
qs.s: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{5} = \sqrt{\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 \cdot 5} = \sqrt{\frac{4}{9} \cdot 5} = \sqrt{\frac{20}{9}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(6\sqrt{7}\)
qs.s: \(6\sqrt{7} = \sqrt{6^2 \cdot 7} = \sqrt{36 \cdot 7} = \sqrt{252}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-4\sqrt{10}\)
Write as an entire radical: \(12\sqrt{3}\)
Write as an entire radical: \(3\sqrt[3]{4}\)
Write as an entire radical: \(-6\sqrt{2}\)
qs.s: Keep the negative sign in front and place \(6\) under the radical as \(6^2\): \(-\sqrt{6^2 \cdot 2} = -\sqrt{36 \cdot 2} = -\sqrt{72}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-5\sqrt{3}\)
qs.s: Keep the negative sign in front and place \(5\) under the radical as \(5^2\): \(-\sqrt{5^2 \cdot 3} = -\sqrt{25 \cdot 3} = -\sqrt{75}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-3\sqrt{10}\)
qs.s: Keep the negative sign in front and place \(3\) under the radical as \(3^2\): \(-\sqrt{3^2 \cdot 10} = -\sqrt{9 \cdot 10} = -\sqrt{90}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-\frac{5}{3}\sqrt{\frac{6}{5}}\)
qs.s: Square the coefficient \(\frac{5}{3}\) and multiply it by \(\frac{6}{5}\) under the radical: \(-\sqrt{\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^2 \cdot \frac{6}{5}} = -\sqrt{\frac{25}{9} \cdot \frac{6}{5}} = -\sqrt{\frac{10}{3}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-12\sqrt{5}\)
qs.s: Keep the negative sign in front and place \(12\) under the radical as \(12^2\): \(-\sqrt{12^2 \cdot 5} = -\sqrt{144 \cdot 5} = -\sqrt{720}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{20}\)
qs.s: Square the coefficient \(\frac{3}{2}\) and multiply it by \(20\) under the radical: \(-\sqrt{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 \cdot 20} = -\sqrt{\frac{9}{4} \cdot 20} = -\sqrt{45}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{10}\)
qs.s: Square the coefficient \(\frac{3}{4}\) and multiply it by \(10\) under the radical: \(-\sqrt{\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2 \cdot 10} = -\sqrt{\frac{9}{16} \cdot 10} = -\sqrt{\frac{45}{8}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-2\sqrt[4]{5}\)
qs.s: Because the index is \(4\), raise \(2\) to the fourth power under the radical while keeping the negative sign outside: \(-\sqrt[4]{2^4 \cdot 5} = -\sqrt[4]{16 \cdot 5} = -\sqrt[4]{80}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(2\sqrt{5}\)
qs.s: \(2\sqrt{5} = \sqrt{2^2 \cdot 5} = \sqrt{4 \cdot 5} = \sqrt{20}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(3\sqrt{7}\)
qs.s: \(3\sqrt{7} = \sqrt{3^2 \cdot 7} = \sqrt{9 \cdot 7} = \sqrt{63}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{7}\)
qs.s: Square the fractional coefficient and bring it under the radical: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{7} = \sqrt{\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 \cdot 7} = \sqrt{\frac{4}{9} \cdot 7} = \sqrt{\frac{28}{9}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{4}{3}\sqrt{2}\)
qs.s: Square the coefficient to place it under the square root: \(\sqrt{\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)^2 \cdot 2} = \sqrt{\frac{16}{9} \cdot 2} = \sqrt{\frac{32}{9}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{7}\)
qs.s: Square the coefficient to place it under the square root: \(\sqrt{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 \cdot 7} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{4} \cdot 7} = \sqrt{\frac{63}{4}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{5}\)
qs.s: Square the coefficient to place it under the square root: \(\sqrt{\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2 \cdot 5} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{16} \cdot 5} = \sqrt{\frac{45}{16}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{5}{2}\sqrt{3}\)
qs.s: Square the coefficient to place it under the square root: \(\sqrt{\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^2 \cdot 3} = \sqrt{\frac{25}{4} \cdot 3} = \sqrt{\frac{75}{4}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{2}{5}\sqrt{3}\)
qs.s: Square the coefficient to place it under the square root: \(\sqrt{\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^2 \cdot 3} = \sqrt{\frac{4}{25} \cdot 3} = \sqrt{\frac{12}{25}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\frac{8}{15}}\)
qs.s: Square the coefficient and simplify the fraction inside the radical: \(\sqrt{\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2 \cdot \frac{8}{15}} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{16} \cdot \frac{8}{15}} = \sqrt{\frac{3}{10}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[3]{\frac{4}{9}}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient and simplify the product inside the cube root: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 \cdot \frac{4}{9}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{27}{8} \cdot \frac{4}{9}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{2}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-\frac{4}{3}\sqrt{\frac{15}{32}}\)
qs.s: Keep the negative sign outside the square root and square the coefficient inside: \(-\sqrt{\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)^2 \cdot \frac{15}{32}} = -\sqrt{\frac{16}{9} \cdot \frac{15}{32}} = -\sqrt{\frac{5}{6}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{6}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to move it inside the cube root: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3 \cdot 6} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{8}{27} \cdot 6} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{16}{9}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{5}{4}\sqrt{\frac{8}{45}}\)
qs.s: Square the coefficient and multiply by the radicand: \(\sqrt{\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)^2 \cdot \frac{8}{45}} = \sqrt{\frac{25}{16} \cdot \frac{8}{45}} = \sqrt{\frac{5}{18}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(2\sqrt[3]{5}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to move it inside the radical: \(2\sqrt[3]{5} = \sqrt[3]{2^3 \cdot 5} = \sqrt[3]{8 \cdot 5} = \sqrt[3]{40}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(2\sqrt[3]{7}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to move it inside the radical: \(2\sqrt[3]{7} = \sqrt[3]{2^3 \cdot 7} = \sqrt[3]{8 \cdot 7} = \sqrt[3]{56}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(2\sqrt[3]{9}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to move it inside the radical: \(2\sqrt[3]{9} = \sqrt[3]{2^3 \cdot 9} = \sqrt[3]{8 \cdot 9} = \sqrt[3]{72}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(3\sqrt[3]{2}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to move it inside the radical: \(3\sqrt[3]{2} = \sqrt[3]{3^3 \cdot 2} = \sqrt[3]{27 \cdot 2} = \sqrt[3]{54}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{5}\)
qs.s: Cube the fractional coefficient to move it inside the cube root: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{5} = \sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3 \cdot 5} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{8}{27} \cdot 5} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{40}{27}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(3\sqrt[4]{2}\)
qs.s: Raise the coefficient to the fourth power to move it inside the radical: \(3\sqrt[4]{2} = \sqrt[4]{3^4 \cdot 2} = \sqrt[4]{81 \cdot 2} = \sqrt[4]{162}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(2\sqrt[5]{3}\)
qs.s: Raise the coefficient to the fifth power to move it inside the radical: \(2\sqrt[5]{3} = \sqrt[5]{2^5 \cdot 3} = \sqrt[5]{32 \cdot 3} = \sqrt[5]{96}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(5\sqrt[3]{4}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to bring it inside the radical: \(5\sqrt[3]{4} = \sqrt[3]{5^3 \cdot 4} = \sqrt[3]{125 \cdot 4} = \sqrt[3]{500}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-5\sqrt[3]{2}\)
qs.s: Raise \(-5\) to the third power: \((-5)^3 = -125\). Multiplying inside the cube root gives \(\sqrt[3]{-125 \cdot 2} = \sqrt[3]{-250}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-4\sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{16}}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to get \((-4)^3 = -64\). Multiplying by the radicand gives \(\sqrt[3]{-64 \cdot \frac{3}{16}} = \sqrt[3]{-4 \cdot 3} = \sqrt[3]{-12}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{54}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to get \(\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)^3 = -\frac{8}{27}\). Multiplying by the radicand gives \(\sqrt[3]{-\frac{8}{27} \cdot 54} = \sqrt[3]{-16}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-\frac{3}{4}\sqrt[3]{\frac{32}{9}}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient: \(\left(-\frac{3}{4}\right)^3 = -\frac{27}{64}\). Multiplying inside the radical gives \(\sqrt[3]{-\frac{27}{64} \cdot \frac{32}{9}} = \sqrt[3]{-\frac{3}{2}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(4\sqrt[3]{2}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to move it inside the radical: \(4\sqrt[3]{2} = \sqrt[3]{4^3 \cdot 2} = \sqrt[3]{64 \cdot 2} = \sqrt[3]{128}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(3\sqrt[3]{3}\)
qs.s: Cube the outer factor to place it under the radical sign: \(3\sqrt[3]{3} = \sqrt[3]{3^3 \cdot 3} = \sqrt[3]{27 \cdot 3} = \sqrt[3]{81}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(5\sqrt[3]{12}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient and multiply it by the radicand: \(5\sqrt[3]{12} = \sqrt[3]{5^3 \cdot 12} = \sqrt[3]{125 \cdot 12} = \sqrt[3]{1500}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[3]{4}\)
qs.s: Cube the fraction and simplify the resulting radicand: \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[3]{4} = \sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 \cdot 4} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{27}{8} \cdot 4} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{27}{2}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{11}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to bring it under the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^3 \cdot 11} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{27} \cdot 11} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{11}{27}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{3}{5}\sqrt[3]{2}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to bring it under the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^3 \cdot 2} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{27}{125} \cdot 2} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{54}{125}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[3]{7}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to bring it under the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 \cdot 7} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{27}{8} \cdot 7} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{189}{8}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{2}{5}\sqrt[3]{3}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to bring it under the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^3 \cdot 3} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{8}{125} \cdot 3} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{24}{125}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{5}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to bring it under the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 \cdot 5} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{8} \cdot 5} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{5}{8}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{5}{6}\sqrt[3]{\frac{18}{25}}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient and simplify the product under the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^3 \cdot \frac{18}{25}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{125}{216} \cdot \frac{18}{25}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{5}{12}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(1\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{\frac{4}{9}}\)
qs.s: Convert \(1\frac{1}{2}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{3}{2}\), cube it, and simplify inside the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 \cdot \frac{4}{9}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{27}{8} \cdot \frac{4}{9}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{2}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[4]{18}\)
qs.s: Raise the coefficient to the fourth power and simplify under the radical: \(\sqrt[4]{\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^4 \cdot 18} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{16}{81} \cdot 18} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{32}{9}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[4]{\frac{32}{27}}\)
qs.s: Raise the coefficient to the fourth power and simplify the product inside the radical: \(\sqrt[4]{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^4 \cdot \frac{32}{27}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{81}{16} \cdot \frac{32}{27}} = \sqrt[4]{6}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{\frac{9}{4}}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to bring it inside the radical and simplify the fraction: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3 \cdot \frac{9}{4}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{8}{27} \cdot \frac{9}{4}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{2}{3}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(2\sqrt[4]{7}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the coefficient under the radical by raising it to the fourth power: \(2\sqrt[4]{7} = \sqrt[4]{2^4 \cdot 7} = \sqrt[4]{16 \cdot 7} = \sqrt[4]{112}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-2\sqrt[4]{11}\)
qs.s: Keep the negative sign outside the radical and raise the coefficient to the fourth power: \(-2\sqrt[4]{11} = -\sqrt[4]{2^4 \cdot 11} = -\sqrt[4]{16 \cdot 11} = -\sqrt[4]{176}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(4\sqrt[4]{5}\)
qs.s: Raise the coefficient to the fourth power and multiply by the radicand: \(4\sqrt[4]{5} = \sqrt[4]{4^4 \cdot 5} = \sqrt[4]{256 \cdot 5} = \sqrt[4]{1280}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(2\sqrt[5]{9}\)
qs.s: Raise the coefficient to the fifth power and multiply by the radicand: \(2\sqrt[5]{9} = \sqrt[5]{2^5 \cdot 9} = \sqrt[5]{32 \cdot 9} = \sqrt[5]{288}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(5\sqrt[3]{14}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient and multiply by the radicand: \(5\sqrt[3]{14} = \sqrt[3]{5^3 \cdot 14} = \sqrt[3]{125 \cdot 14} = \sqrt[3]{1750}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-3\sqrt[4]{5}\)
qs.s: Since the index is even, the negative sign remains outside the radical: \(-3\sqrt[4]{5} = -\sqrt[4]{3^4 \cdot 5} = -\sqrt[4]{81 \cdot 5} = -\sqrt[4]{405}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-5\sqrt[4]{2}\)
qs.s: Since the index is even, the negative sign remains outside the radical: \(-5\sqrt[4]{2} = -\sqrt[4]{5^4 \cdot 2} = -\sqrt[4]{625 \cdot 2} = -\sqrt[4]{1250}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-2\sqrt[4]{3}\)
qs.s: Since the index is even, the negative sign remains outside the radical: \(-2\sqrt[4]{3} = -\sqrt[4]{2^4 \cdot 3} = -\sqrt[4]{16 \cdot 3} = -\sqrt[4]{48}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-3\sqrt[6]{2}\)
qs.s: Because the index 6 is even, the negative sign stays outside: \(-3\sqrt[6]{2} = -\sqrt[6]{3^6 \cdot 2} = -\sqrt[6]{729 \cdot 2} = -\sqrt[6]{1458}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[4]{2}\)
qs.s: The negative sign remains outside, and simplifying under the radical gives: \(-\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[4]{2} = -\sqrt[4]{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^4 \cdot 2} = -\sqrt[4]{\frac{81}{16} \cdot 2} = -\sqrt[4]{\frac{81}{8}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[4]{5}\)
qs.s: The negative sign stays outside the radical: \(-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[4]{5} = -\sqrt[4]{\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^4 \cdot 5} = -\sqrt[4]{\frac{16}{81} \cdot 5} = -\sqrt[4]{\frac{80}{81}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-6\sqrt[4]{3}\)
qs.s: Because the index 4 is even, the negative sign remains outside the radical: \(-6\sqrt[4]{3} = -\sqrt[4]{6^4 \cdot 3} = -\sqrt[4]{1296 \cdot 3} = -\sqrt[4]{3888}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-2\sqrt[6]{5}\)
qs.s: Because the index 6 is even, the negative sign stays outside the radical: \(-2\sqrt[6]{5} = -\sqrt[6]{2^6 \cdot 5} = -\sqrt[6]{64 \cdot 5} = -\sqrt[6]{320}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{5}{2}\sqrt[3]{24}\)
qs.s: Raise \(\frac{5}{2}\) to the third power and multiply by 24: \(\frac{5}{2}\sqrt[3]{24} = \sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^3 \cdot 24} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{125}{8} \cdot 24} = \sqrt[3]{125 \cdot 3} = \sqrt[3]{375}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(3\sqrt[5]{2}\)
qs.s: Move 3 inside the fifth root by raising it to the fifth power: \(3\sqrt[5]{2} = \sqrt[5]{3^5 \cdot 2} = \sqrt[5]{243 \cdot 2} = \sqrt[5]{486}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[4]{\frac{5}{27}}\)
qs.s: Raise \(\frac{3}{2}\) to the fourth power and multiply by the radicand: \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[4]{\frac{5}{27}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{81}{16} \cdot \frac{5}{27}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{3 \cdot 5}{16}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{15}{16}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(4\sqrt[4]{6}\)
qs.s: Move 4 under the fourth root by raising it to the fourth power: \(4\sqrt[4]{6} = \sqrt[4]{4^4 \cdot 6} = \sqrt[4]{256 \cdot 6} = \sqrt[4]{1536}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[4]{11}\)
qs.s: Move \(\frac{1}{2}\) inside the fourth root by raising it to the fourth power: \(\sqrt[4]{\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^4 \cdot 11} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{1}{16} \cdot 11} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{11}{16}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[4]{3}\)
qs.s: Move \(\frac{3}{2}\) inside the fourth root by raising it to the fourth power: \(\sqrt[4]{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^4 \cdot 3} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{81}{16} \cdot 3} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{243}{16}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[3]{5}\)
qs.s: Move \(\frac{3}{2}\) inside the cube root by cubing it: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 \cdot 5} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{27}{8} \cdot 5} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{135}{8}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{1}{3}\sqrt[4]{7}\)
qs.s: Move \(\frac{1}{3}\) inside the fourth root by raising it to the fourth power: \(\sqrt[4]{\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^4 \cdot 7} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{1}{81} \cdot 7} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{7}{81}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{7}\)
qs.s: Move \(\frac{2}{3}\) under the cube root by cubing it: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3 \cdot 7} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{8}{27} \cdot 7} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{56}{27}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{5}{3}\sqrt[3]{\frac{18}{25}}\)
qs.s: Cube \(\frac{5}{3}\) to move it inside the cube root, then cancel common factors: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^3 \cdot \frac{18}{25}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{125}{27} \cdot \frac{18}{25}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{10}{3}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[4]{\frac{27}{8}}\)
qs.s: The negative sign stays outside the radical because the index is even, then \(\frac{2}{3}\) is raised to the fourth power: \(-\sqrt[4]{\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^4 \cdot \frac{27}{8}} = -\sqrt[4]{\frac{16}{81} \cdot \frac{27}{8}} = -\sqrt[4]{\frac{2}{3}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(1\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{\frac{2}{9}}\)
qs.s: Convert \(1\frac{1}{2}\) to \(\frac{3}{2}\), cube it under the radical, and simplify: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 \cdot \frac{2}{9}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{27}{8} \cdot \frac{2}{9}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{4}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(2\sqrt[5]{5}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the coefficient 2 inside the fifth root as \(2^5 = 32\). Then multiply by the radicand: \(\sqrt[5]{32 \cdot 5} = \sqrt[5]{160}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(3\sqrt[3]{\frac{4}{9}}\)
qs.s: Move 3 inside the cube root as \(3^3 = 27\). Multiplying by \(\frac{4}{9}\) yields \(\sqrt[3]{27 \cdot \frac{4}{9}} = \sqrt[3]{12}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(3\sqrt[5]{4}\)
qs.s: Raise 3 to the fifth power to move it inside the radical: \(3^5 = 243\). Multiplying by 4 gives \(\sqrt[5]{243 \cdot 4} = \sqrt[5]{972}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[3]{\frac{2}{9}}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient to move it inside the radical: \(\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{27}{8}\). Multiplying and simplifying gives \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{27}{8} \cdot \frac{2}{9}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{4}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[4]{162}\)
qs.s: Raise \(\frac{2}{3}\) to the fourth power to move it inside: \(\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^4 = \frac{16}{81}\). Multiplying by 162 gives \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{16}{81} \cdot 162} = \sqrt[4]{16 \cdot 2} = \sqrt[4]{32}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[3]{\frac{5}{9}}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient \(\frac{3}{2}\) under the radical and simplify the fraction: \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{27}{8} \cdot \frac{5}{9}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{3 \cdot 5}{8}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{15}{8}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. \(4\sqrt[3]{\frac{7}{16}}\)
qs.s: Raise 4 to the 3rd power to bring it under the radical and simplify: \(\sqrt[3]{4^3 \cdot \frac{7}{16}} = \sqrt[3]{64 \cdot \frac{7}{16}} = \sqrt[3]{28}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(\sqrt{\frac{1}{10}}\) and \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{10}}\) by expressing each with a common index of \(6\).
qs.s: Converting each radical to index \(6\) yields \(\sqrt{\frac{1}{10}} = \sqrt[6]{\frac{1}{1000}}\) and \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{10}} = \sqrt[6]{\frac{1}{100}}\). Since \(\frac{1}{1000} < \frac{1}{100}\), \(\sqrt{\frac{1}{10}} < \sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{10}}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(\sqrt{\frac{1}{3}}\) and \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{3}}\) by expressing each with a common index of \(6\).
qs.s: Expressing each radical with index \(6\) gives \(\sqrt{\frac{1}{3}} = \sqrt[6]{\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^3} = \sqrt[6]{\frac{1}{27}}\) and \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{3}} = \sqrt[6]{\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^2} = \sqrt[6]{\frac{1}{9}}\). Since \(\frac{1}{27} < \frac{1}{9}\), we have \(\sqrt{\frac{1}{3}} < \sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{3}}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(\sqrt{2}\) and \(\sqrt[3]{2}\) by expressing each with a common index of \(6\).
qs.s: Writing both radicals with index \(6\) gives \(\sqrt{2} = \sqrt[6]{2^3} = \sqrt[6]{8}\) and \(\sqrt[3]{2} = \sqrt[6]{2^2} = \sqrt[6]{4}\). Since \(8 > 4\), we conclude that \(\sqrt{2} > \sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(\sqrt{\frac{1}{5}}\) and \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{5}}\) by expressing each with a common index of \(6\).
qs.s: Rewriting each with a common index of \(6\) yields \(\sqrt{\frac{1}{5}} = \sqrt[6]{\frac{1}{125}}\) and \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{5}} = \sqrt[6]{\frac{1}{25}}\). Since \(\frac{1}{125} < \frac{1}{25}\), it follows that \(\sqrt{\frac{1}{5}} < \sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{5}}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}}\) and \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{3}}\) by expressing each with a common index of \(6\).
qs.s: Writing both radicals with index \(6\) gives \(\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}} = \sqrt[6]{\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3} = \sqrt[6]{\frac{1}{8}}\) and \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{3}} = \sqrt[6]{\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^2} = \sqrt[6]{\frac{1}{9}}\). Since \(\frac{1}{8} > \frac{1}{9}\), we have \(\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}} > \sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{3}}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares the mixed radicals \(3\sqrt{5}\) and \(4\sqrt{3}\) by converting each to an entire radical.
qs.s: Convert both mixed radicals to entire radicals: \(3\sqrt{5} = \sqrt{3^2 \times 5} = \sqrt{45}\) and \(4\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{4^2 \times 3} = \sqrt{48}\). Since \(45 < 48\), it follows that \(3\sqrt{5} < 4\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(\sqrt[3]{2}\) and \(\sqrt[4]{3}\) by expressing each with a common index of \(12\).
qs.s: Expressing each radical with index \(12\) yields \(\sqrt[3]{2} = \sqrt[12]{2^4} = \sqrt[12]{16}\) and \(\sqrt[4]{3} = \sqrt[12]{3^3} = \sqrt[12]{27}\). Since \(16 < 27\), \(\sqrt[3]{2} < \sqrt[4]{3}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares the mixed radicals \(2\sqrt[3]{5}\) and \(3\sqrt[3]{2}\) by converting each to an entire radical.
qs.s: Convert each mixed radical to an entire cube root: \(2\sqrt[3]{5} = \sqrt[3]{2^3 \times 5} = \sqrt[3]{40}\) and \(3\sqrt[3]{2} = \sqrt[3]{3^3 \times 2} = \sqrt[3]{54}\). Since \(40 < 54\), we have \(2\sqrt[3]{5} < 3\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(\sqrt{5}\) and \(\sqrt[3]{11}\) by expressing each with a common index of \(6\).
qs.s: Convert both radicals to index \(6\): \(\sqrt{5} = \sqrt[6]{5^3} = \sqrt[6]{125}\) and \(\sqrt[3]{11} = \sqrt[6]{11^2} = \sqrt[6]{121}\). Since \(125 > 121\), it follows that \(\sqrt{5} > \sqrt[3]{11}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(\sqrt{\frac{5}{6}}\) and \(\sqrt{\frac{4}{5}}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
d: \(\sqrt{\frac{5}{6}} < \sqrt{\frac{4}{5}}\) because fifths are larger parts than sixths
qs.s: Convert the radicands to a common denominator: \(\frac{5}{6} = \frac{25}{30}\) and \(\frac{4}{5} = \frac{24}{30}\). Since \(\frac{25}{30} > \frac{24}{30}\), it follows that \(\sqrt{\frac{5}{6}} > \sqrt{\frac{4}{5}}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(\sqrt{\frac{6}{7}}\) and \(\sqrt{\frac{7}{8}}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
d: \(\sqrt{\frac{6}{7}} > \sqrt{\frac{7}{8}}\) because sevenths are larger parts than eighths
qs.s: Convert the radicands to a common denominator: \(\frac{6}{7} = \frac{48}{56}\) and \(\frac{7}{8} = \frac{49}{56}\). Since \(\frac{48}{56} < \frac{49}{56}\), it follows that \(\sqrt{\frac{6}{7}} < \sqrt{\frac{7}{8}}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(\sqrt{\frac{7}{10}}\) and \(\sqrt{\frac{5}{7}}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
d: \(\sqrt{\frac{7}{10}} > \sqrt{\frac{5}{7}}\) because tenths are larger units than sevenths
qs.s: Express the radicands with a common denominator of 70: \(\frac{7}{10} = \frac{49}{70}\) and \(\frac{5}{7} = \frac{50}{70}\). Since \(\frac{49}{70} < \frac{50}{70}\), we have \(\sqrt{\frac{7}{10}} < \sqrt{\frac{5}{7}}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}}\) and \(\sqrt{\frac{7}{9}}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
d: \(\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}} > \sqrt{\frac{7}{9}}\) because fourths are larger parts than ninths
qs.s: Write each radicand with a common denominator of 36: \(\frac{3}{4} = \frac{27}{36}\) and \(\frac{7}{9} = \frac{28}{36}\). Because \(\frac{27}{36} < \frac{28}{36}\), we conclude \(\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}} < \sqrt{\frac{7}{9}}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(\sqrt{\frac{9}{11}}\) and \(\sqrt{\frac{4}{5}}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
d: \(\sqrt{\frac{9}{11}} < \sqrt{\frac{4}{5}}\) because fifths are larger parts than elevenths
qs.s: Write each radicand with a common denominator of 55: \(\frac{9}{11} = \frac{45}{55}\) and \(\frac{4}{5} = \frac{44}{55}\). Since \(\frac{45}{55} > \frac{44}{55}\), we find that \(\sqrt{\frac{9}{11}} > \sqrt{\frac{4}{5}}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(2\sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{4}}\) and \(\sqrt[3]{5}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
qs.s: Express \(2\sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{4}}\) as an entire radical by cubing the coefficient: \(\sqrt[3]{2^3 \cdot \frac{3}{4}} = \sqrt[3]{8 \cdot \frac{3}{4}} = \sqrt[3]{6}\). Comparing radicands, \(6 > 5\), so \(2\sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{4}} > \sqrt[3]{5}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{18}\) and \(\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{12}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
d: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{18} = \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{12}\) because both coefficients simplify to the same factor
qs.s: Convert both to entire radicals: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{18} = \sqrt{\frac{4}{9} \cdot 18} = \sqrt{8} = \sqrt{\frac{32}{4}}\) and \(\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{12} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{16} \cdot 12} = \sqrt{\frac{27}{4}}\). Since \(\frac{32}{4} > \frac{27}{4}\), \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{18} > \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{12}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares the mixed radicals \(3\sqrt{\frac{2}{5}}\) and \(2\sqrt{\frac{5}{6}}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
qs.s: Convert both to entire radicals: \(3\sqrt{\frac{2}{5}} = \sqrt{9 \cdot \frac{2}{5}} = \sqrt{\frac{18}{5}} = \sqrt{\frac{54}{15}}\) and \(2\sqrt{\frac{5}{6}} = \sqrt{4 \cdot \frac{5}{6}} = \sqrt{\frac{10}{3}} = \sqrt{\frac{50}{15}}\). Since \(\frac{54}{15} > \frac{50}{15}\), \(3\sqrt{\frac{2}{5}} > 2\sqrt{\frac{5}{6}}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(\sqrt{\frac{14}{15}}\) and \(\sqrt{\frac{19}{20}}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
d: \(\sqrt{\frac{14}{15}} > \sqrt{\frac{19}{20}}\) because fifteenths are larger parts than twentieths
qs.s: Express the radicands with a common denominator of 60: \(\frac{14}{15} = \frac{56}{60}\) and \(\frac{19}{20} = \frac{57}{60}\). Since \(\frac{56}{60} < \frac{57}{60}\), we have \(\sqrt{\frac{14}{15}} < \sqrt{\frac{19}{20}}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(4\sqrt{\frac{3}{8}}\) and \(3\sqrt{\frac{5}{7}}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
qs.s: Write each as an entire radical: \(4\sqrt{\frac{3}{8}} = \sqrt{16 \cdot \frac{3}{8}} = \sqrt{6} = \sqrt{\frac{42}{7}}\) and \(3\sqrt{\frac{5}{7}} = \sqrt{9 \cdot \frac{5}{7}} = \sqrt{\frac{45}{7}}\). Since \(\frac{42}{7} < \frac{45}{7}\), \(4\sqrt{\frac{3}{8}} < 3\sqrt{\frac{5}{7}}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, which statement correctly compares the values \(A = \sqrt{\frac{4}{3}}\) and \(B = \sqrt{\frac{5}{4}}\)?
qs.s: Finding a common denominator gives \(\frac{4}{3} = \frac{16}{12}\) and \(\frac{5}{4} = \frac{15}{12}\). Since \(\frac{16}{12} > \frac{15}{12}\), it follows that \(\sqrt{\frac{4}{3}} > \sqrt{\frac{5}{4}}\), so \(A > B\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, which statement correctly compares the values \(A = \sqrt{\frac{10}{9}}\) and \(B = \sqrt{\frac{9}{8}}\)?
qs.s: Expressing both fractions with a common denominator of \(72\) gives \(\frac{10}{9} = \frac{80}{72}\) and \(\frac{9}{8} = \frac{81}{72}\). Since \(\frac{80}{72} < \frac{81}{72}\), it follows that \(\sqrt{\frac{10}{9}} < \sqrt{\frac{9}{8}}\), so \(A < B\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, which statement correctly compares the values \(A = \sqrt{\frac{7}{6}}\) and \(B = \sqrt{\frac{8}{7}}\)?
qs.s: With a common denominator of \(42\), we get \(\frac{7}{6} = \frac{49}{42}\) and \(\frac{8}{7} = \frac{48}{42}\). Because \(\frac{49}{42} > \frac{48}{42}\), we have \(\sqrt{\frac{7}{6}} > \sqrt{\frac{8}{7}}\), so \(A > B\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, which statement correctly compares the values \(A = \sqrt{\frac{6}{5}}\) and \(B = \sqrt{\frac{7}{6}}\)?
qs.s: Using a common denominator of \(30\), we have \(\frac{6}{5} = \frac{36}{30}\) and \(\frac{7}{6} = \frac{35}{30}\). Since \(\frac{36}{30} > \frac{35}{30}\), \(\sqrt{\frac{6}{5}} > \sqrt{\frac{7}{6}}\), which means \(A > B\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, which statement correctly compares the values \(A = \sqrt{\frac{12}{11}}\) and \(B = \sqrt{\frac{11}{10}}\)?
qs.s: Using a common denominator of \(110\), we obtain \(\frac{12}{11} = \frac{120}{110}\) and \(\frac{11}{10} = \frac{121}{110}\). Since \(\frac{120}{110} < \frac{121}{110}\), we have \(\sqrt{\frac{12}{11}} < \sqrt{\frac{11}{10}}\), so \(A < B\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, which statement correctly compares the values \(A = \sqrt{\frac{17}{8}}\) and \(B = \sqrt{\frac{19}{9}}\)?
d: \(A = B\) because both mixed numbers have a whole number part of \(2\)
qs.s: Write each fraction as a mixed number: \(\frac{17}{8} = 2\frac{1}{8}\) and \(\frac{19}{9} = 2\frac{1}{9}\). Since \(\frac{1}{8} > \frac{1}{9}\), we have \(\frac{17}{8} > \frac{19}{9}\), which means \(\sqrt{\frac{17}{8}} > \sqrt{\frac{19}{9}}\) and \(A > B\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, which statement correctly compares the values \(A = 4\sqrt{7}\) and \(B = 7\sqrt{2}\)?
d: \(A < B\) because the outside coefficient \(7\) is greater than \(4\)
qs.s: Write both mixed radicals as entire radicals: \(4\sqrt{7} = \sqrt{16 \cdot 7} = \sqrt{112}\) and \(7\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{49 \cdot 2} = \sqrt{98}\). Since \(112 > 98\), \(\sqrt{112} > \sqrt{98}\), which gives \(A > B\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, which statement correctly compares the values \(A = 2\sqrt[3]{5}\) and \(B = 3\sqrt[3]{2}\)?

qs.s: Because the index is 4, raise the outside coefficients to the fourth power: \(2\sqrt[4]{8} = \sqrt[4]{2^4 \cdot 8} = \sqrt[4]{16 \cdot 8} = \sqrt[4]{128}\) and \(3\sqrt[4]{2} = \sqrt[4]{3^4 \cdot 2} = \sqrt[4]{81 \cdot 2} = \sqrt[4]{162}\). Since \(128 < 162\), \(2\sqrt[4]{8} < 3\sqrt[4]{2}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(-4\sqrt[3]{2}\) and \(-3\sqrt[3]{5}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(-2\sqrt[3]{7}\) and \(-3\sqrt[3]{2}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(-2\sqrt[4]{15}\) and \(-3\sqrt[4]{3}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(-3\sqrt[3]{3}\) and \(-2\sqrt[3]{10}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
qs.s: Rewrite each as an entire radical: \(-3\sqrt[3]{3} = -\sqrt[3]{3^3 \cdot 3} = -\sqrt[3]{81}\) and \(-2\sqrt[3]{10} = -\sqrt[3]{2^3 \cdot 10} = -\sqrt[3]{80}\). Since \(81 > 80\), \(-\sqrt[3]{81} < -\sqrt[3]{80}\), which gives \(-3\sqrt[3]{3} < -2\sqrt[3]{10}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(-2\sqrt[4]{11}\) and \(-3\sqrt[4]{2}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(-2\sqrt[4]{\frac{25}{2}}\) and \(-3\sqrt[4]{\frac{5}{2}}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{44}\) and \(-\frac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{135}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(-2\sqrt[5]{18}\) and \(-3\sqrt[5]{2}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(-4\sqrt{\frac{5}{8}}\) and \(-3\sqrt{\frac{6}{5}}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
qs.s: Rewrite each as an entire radical: \(-4\sqrt{\frac{5}{8}} = -\sqrt{16 \cdot \frac{5}{8}} = -\sqrt{10}\) and \(-3\sqrt{\frac{6}{5}} = -\sqrt{9 \cdot \frac{6}{5}} = -\sqrt{\frac{54}{5}}\). Since \(10 < \frac{54}{5} = 10.8\), \(-\sqrt{10} > -\sqrt{\frac{54}{5}}\), so \(-4\sqrt{\frac{5}{8}} > -3\sqrt{\frac{6}{5}}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(-5\sqrt[3]{6}\) and \(-6\sqrt[3]{\frac{7}{2}}\) using \(>\) or \(<\).
qs.s: Write each as an entire radical: \(-5\sqrt[3]{6} = -\sqrt[3]{5^3 \cdot 6} = -\sqrt[3]{125 \cdot 6} = -\sqrt[3]{750}\) and \(-6\sqrt[3]{\frac{7}{2}} = -\sqrt[3]{6^3 \cdot \frac{7}{2}} = -\sqrt[3]{216 \cdot \frac{7}{2}} = -\sqrt[3]{756}\). Because \(750 < 756\), \(-\sqrt[3]{750} > -\sqrt[3]{756}\), which means \(-5\sqrt[3]{6} > -6\sqrt[3]{\frac{7}{2}}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(3\sqrt{6}\) and \(5\sqrt{3}\).
qs.s: Rewrite both mixed radicals as entire radicals: \(3\sqrt{6} = \sqrt{3^2 \cdot 6} = \sqrt{54}\) and \(5\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{5^2 \cdot 3} = \sqrt{75}\). Since \(54 < 75\), it follows that \(3\sqrt{6} < 5\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(6\sqrt{2}\) and \(2\sqrt{13}\).
qs.s: Rewrite both mixed radicals as entire radicals: \(6\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{6^2 \cdot 2} = \sqrt{72}\) and \(2\sqrt{13} = \sqrt{2^2 \cdot 13} = \sqrt{52}\). Since \(72 > 52\), it follows that \(6\sqrt{2} > 2\sqrt{13}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(4\sqrt{3}\) and \(2\sqrt{11}\).
qs.s: Rewrite both mixed radicals as entire radicals: \(4\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{4^2 \cdot 3} = \sqrt{48}\) and \(2\sqrt{11} = \sqrt{2^2 \cdot 11} = \sqrt{44}\). Since \(48 > 44\), it follows that \(4\sqrt{3} > 2\sqrt{11}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(4\sqrt{5}\) and \(3\sqrt{7}\).
qs.s: Rewrite both mixed radicals as entire radicals: \(4\sqrt{5} = \sqrt{4^2 \cdot 5} = \sqrt{80}\) and \(3\sqrt{7} = \sqrt{3^2 \cdot 7} = \sqrt{63}\). Since \(80 > 63\), it follows that \(4\sqrt{5} > 3\sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(2\sqrt{10}\) and \(3\sqrt{5}\).
qs.s: Rewrite both mixed radicals as entire radicals: \(2\sqrt{10} = \sqrt{2^2 \cdot 10} = \sqrt{40}\) and \(3\sqrt{5} = \sqrt{3^2 \cdot 5} = \sqrt{45}\). Since \(40 < 45\), it follows that \(2\sqrt{10} < 3\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(-5\sqrt{2}\) and \(-3\sqrt{6}\).
qs.s: Express each value as a negative entire radical: \(-5\sqrt{2} = -\sqrt{5^2 \cdot 2} = -\sqrt{50}\) and \(-3\sqrt{6} = -\sqrt{3^2 \cdot 6} = -\sqrt{54}\). Since \(-50 > -54\), \(-\sqrt{50} > -\sqrt{54}\), which gives \(-5\sqrt{2} > -3\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, arrange the values \(3\sqrt{3}\), \(2\sqrt{7}\), and \(4\sqrt{2}\) in order from least to greatest.
qs.s: Express each value as an entire radical: \(3\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{9 \cdot 3} = \sqrt{27}\), \(2\sqrt{7} = \sqrt{4 \cdot 7} = \sqrt{28}\), and \(4\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{16 \cdot 2} = \sqrt{32}\). Since \(27 < 28 < 32\), the order is \(3\sqrt{3} < 2\sqrt{7} < 4\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(3\sqrt[3]{3}\) and \(2\sqrt[3]{10}\).
qs.s: Convert both mixed radicals to entire cube radicals by cubing the outside coefficient: \(3\sqrt[3]{3} = \sqrt[3]{3^3 \cdot 3} = \sqrt[3]{81}\) and \(2\sqrt[3]{10} = \sqrt[3]{2^3 \cdot 10} = \sqrt[3]{80}\). Since \(81 > 80\), \(3\sqrt[3]{3} > 2\sqrt[3]{10}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, arrange the values \(5\sqrt{7}\), \(7\sqrt{3}\), and \(2\sqrt{43}\) in order from least to greatest.
qs.s: Convert each to an entire radical: \(7\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{49 \cdot 3} = \sqrt{147}\), \(2\sqrt{43} = \sqrt{4 \cdot 43} = \sqrt{172}\), and \(5\sqrt{7} = \sqrt{25 \cdot 7} = \sqrt{175}\). Since \(147 < 172 < 175\), the order is \(7\sqrt{3} < 2\sqrt{43} < 5\sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which statement correctly compares \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{6}\) and \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{30}\).
qs.s: Convert both to entire radicals: \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{6} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{4} \cdot 6} = \sqrt{\frac{27}{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{81}{6}}\) and \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{30} = \sqrt{\frac{4}{9} \cdot 30} = \sqrt{\frac{40}{3}} = \sqrt{\frac{80}{6}}\). Since \(\frac{81}{6} > \frac{80}{6}\), it follows that \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{6} > \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{30}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which value is greater using \(>\) or \(<\): \(-5\sqrt{2}\) and \(-3\sqrt{6}\).
qs.s: Express each as an entire radical: \(-5\sqrt{2} = -\sqrt{25 \cdot 2} = -\sqrt{50}\) and \(-3\sqrt{6} = -\sqrt{9 \cdot 6} = -\sqrt{54}\). Because \(-50 > -54\), \(-\sqrt{50} > -\sqrt{54}\), which gives \(-5\sqrt{2} > -3\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which value is greater using \(>\) or \(<\): \(-2\sqrt{7}\) and \(-3\sqrt{3}\).
qs.s: Convert both to entire radicals: \(-2\sqrt{7} = -\sqrt{2^2 \cdot 7} = -\sqrt{28}\) and \(-3\sqrt{3} = -\sqrt{3^2 \cdot 3} = -\sqrt{27}\). Since \(-28 < -27\), \(-\sqrt{28} < -\sqrt{27}\), meaning \(-2\sqrt{7} < -3\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which value is greater using \(>\) or \(<\): \(-4\sqrt{4}\) and \(-3\sqrt{7}\).
qs.s: Rewriting as entire radicals gives \(-4\sqrt{4} = -4(2) = -8 = -\sqrt{64}\) and \(-3\sqrt{7} = -\sqrt{9 \cdot 7} = -\sqrt{63}\). Since \(-64 < -63\), \(-\sqrt{64} < -\sqrt{63}\), which means \(-4\sqrt{4} < -3\sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which value is greater using \(>\) or \(<\): \(-2\sqrt{13}\) and \(-3\sqrt{6}\).
qs.s: Writing both as entire radicals yields \(-2\sqrt{13} = -\sqrt{4 \cdot 13} = -\sqrt{52}\) and \(-3\sqrt{6} = -\sqrt{9 \cdot 6} = -\sqrt{54}\). Since \(-52 > -54\), \(-\sqrt{52} > -\sqrt{54}\), and therefore \(-2\sqrt{13} > -3\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which value is greater using \(>\) or \(<\): \(-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{45}\) and \(-\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{32}\).
qs.s: Convert both into entire radicals: \(-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{45} = -\sqrt{\frac{4}{9} \cdot 45} = -\sqrt{20}\) and \(-\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{32} = -\sqrt{\frac{9}{16} \cdot 32} = -\sqrt{18}\). Because \(-20 < -18\), \(-\sqrt{20} < -\sqrt{18}\), which shows \(-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{45} < -\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{32}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which value is greater using \(>\) or \(<\): \(-6\sqrt{7}\) and \(-5\sqrt{10}\).
