qs.s: Convert both to entire radicals: \(-6\sqrt{7} = -\sqrt{36 \cdot 7} = -\sqrt{252}\) and \(-5\sqrt{10} = -\sqrt{25 \cdot 10} = -\sqrt{250}\). Because \(-252 < -250\), \(-\sqrt{252} < -\sqrt{250}\), which means \(-6\sqrt{7} < -5\sqrt{10}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which value is greater using \(>\) or \(<\): \(-2\sqrt[4]{3}\) and \(-\sqrt[4]{50}\).
qs.s: Move the coefficient into the fourth root: \(-2\sqrt[4]{3} = -\sqrt[4]{2^4 \cdot 3} = -\sqrt[4]{16 \cdot 3} = -\sqrt[4]{48}\). Since \(-48 > -50\), \(-\sqrt[4]{48} > -\sqrt[4]{50}\), so \(-2\sqrt[4]{3} > -\sqrt[4]{50}\).

qs.q: Without using a calculator, determine which value is greater using \(>\) or \(<\): \(-\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{72}\) and \(-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{36}\).
qs.s: Move the coefficients into the radicals: \(-\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{72} = -\sqrt{\frac{72}{9}} = -\sqrt{8}\) and \(-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{36} = -\sqrt{\frac{36}{4}} = -\sqrt{9}\). Since \(-8 > -9\), \(-\sqrt{8} > -\sqrt{9}\), so \(-\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{72} > -\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{36}\).

exercises.name: Converting algebraic radicals to entire radicals

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(p\sqrt{p}\).
qs.s: Square the factor outside and multiply by the radicand: \(p\sqrt{p} = \sqrt{p^2 \cdot p} = \sqrt{p^3}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(a\sqrt{5b}\).
qs.s: Square the outside factor and multiply it by the radicand: \(a\sqrt{5b} = \sqrt{a^2 \cdot 5b} = \sqrt{5a^2 b}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(2x\sqrt{y}\).
qs.s: Square the coefficient and variable outside the radical, then multiply by the radicand: \(2x\sqrt{y} = \sqrt{(2x)^2 \cdot y} = \sqrt{4x^2 y}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(m^2\sqrt{n}\).
qs.s: Square the outside expression and place it under the radical: \(m^2\sqrt{n} = \sqrt{(m^2)^2 \cdot n} = \sqrt{m^4 n}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(y\sqrt{3x}\).
qs.s: Square the factor outside and place it under the radical with the radicand: \(y\sqrt{3x} = \sqrt{y^2 \cdot 3x} = \sqrt{3xy^2}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(3x^2 y\sqrt[3]{2x^2 y^2}\).
qs.s: Cube the expression outside the radical and multiply it by the radicand: \(3x^2 y\sqrt[3]{2x^2 y^2} = \sqrt[3]{(3x^2 y)^3 \cdot 2x^2 y^2} = \sqrt[3]{27x^6 y^3 \cdot 2x^2 y^2} = \sqrt[3]{54x^8 y^5}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{3x^2}{2y}\sqrt{\frac{8y^3}{x}}\).
qs.s: Square the outside fraction and multiply it by the radicand under a single radical: \(\sqrt{\left(\frac{3x^2}{2y}\right)^2 \cdot \frac{8y^3}{x}} = \sqrt{\frac{9x^4}{4y^2} \cdot \frac{8y^3}{x}} = \sqrt{18x^3 y}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\frac{2a^2 b}{3}\sqrt[3]{5ab^2}\).
qs.s: Cube the fraction outside the radical and multiply it by the radicand: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{2a^2 b}{3}\right)^3 \cdot 5ab^2} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{8a^6 b^3}{27} \cdot 5ab^2} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{40a^7 b^5}{27}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(-2x^3 y\sqrt{5xy}\).
qs.s: Keep the negative sign outside the radical and square the factors being moved inside: \(-2x^3 y\sqrt{5xy} = -\sqrt{(2x^3 y)^2 \cdot 5xy} = -\sqrt{4x^6 y^2 \cdot 5xy} = -\sqrt{20x^7 y^3}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(2xy^2\sqrt[4]{3x^3 y}\).
qs.s: Raise the outside factor to the 4th power and multiply by the radicand: \(2xy^2\sqrt[4]{3x^3 y} = \sqrt[4]{(2xy^2)^4 \cdot 3x^3 y} = \sqrt[4]{16x^4 y^8 \cdot 3x^3 y} = \sqrt[4]{48x^7 y^9}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(-8s t^2 \sqrt{s}\)
qs.s: Square the expression outside the radical to get \((8st^2)^2 = 64s^2 t^4\). Multiply by \(s\) under the radical and keep the negative sign outside to get \(-\sqrt{64s^3 t^4}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(-5m^2 n^2 \sqrt{m}\)
qs.s: Square the term outside the radical to obtain \((5m^2 n^2)^2 = 25m^4 n^4\). Multiply by \(m\) under the radical and retain the negative sign outside to arrive at \(-\sqrt{25m^5 n^4}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(-6x y^3 \sqrt{y}\)
qs.s: Square the outside factors to get \((6xy^3)^2 = 36x^2 y^6\). Multiply by the radicand \(y\) and keep the negative sign outside to get \(-\sqrt{36x^2 y^7}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(-7u^3 v \sqrt{u}\)
qs.s: Square the factors outside the radical: \((7u^3 v)^2 = 49u^6 v^2\). Multiply by the radicand \(u\) and keep the negative sign in front to obtain \(-\sqrt{49u^7 v^2}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(-4a^2 b \sqrt{a}\)
qs.s: Square the expression outside the radical to get \((4a^2 b)^2 = 16a^4 b^2\). Multiply this by the radicand \(a\) and keep the negative sign outside the radical to obtain \(-\sqrt{16a^5 b^2}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(-3a^2 b^3 c \sqrt{10a^3 b c^3}\)
qs.s: Square the factors outside the radical: \((3a^2 b^3 c)^2 = 9a^4 b^6 c^2\). Multiply by the radicand \(10a^3 b c^3\) to obtain \(90a^7 b^7 c^5\), giving \(-\sqrt{90a^7 b^7 c^5}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(-7x^3 y z^2 \sqrt{2x^2 y^3 z}\)
qs.s: Square the outside term: \((7x^3 y z^2)^2 = 49x^6 y^2 z^4\). Multiply by \(2x^2 y^3 z\) under the radical to get \(49 \cdot 2 \cdot x^{6+2} y^{2+3} z^{4+1} = 98x^8 y^5 z^5\), which gives \(-\sqrt{98x^8 y^5 z^5}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(-\frac{3a^2 b}{4} \sqrt{\frac{8a b^3}{3}}\)
qs.s: Square the expression outside the radical: \(\left(\frac{3a^2 b}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{9a^4 b^2}{16}\). Multiply by the radicand: \(\frac{9a^4 b^2}{16} \cdot \frac{8a b^3}{3} = \frac{72a^5 b^5}{48} = \frac{3a^5 b^5}{2}\), giving \(-\sqrt{\frac{3a^5 b^5}{2}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(-\frac{5}{2}u^2 v^3 \sqrt{6u^3 v}\)
qs.s: Square the outside factor: \(\left(\frac{5}{2}u^2 v^3\right)^2 = \frac{25}{4}u^4 v^6\). Multiply by the radicand: \(\frac{25}{4}u^4 v^6 \cdot 6u^3 v = \frac{150}{4}u^7 v^7 = \frac{75}{2}u^7 v^7\), producing \(-\sqrt{\frac{75u^7 v^7}{2}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(-4x^3 y^2 \sqrt{6x y^5}\)
qs.s: Square the outside term to get \((4x^3 y^2)^2 = 16x^6 y^4\). Multiply by \(6xy^5\) under the radical to get \(16 \cdot 6 \cdot x^{6+1} y^{4+5} = 96x^7 y^9\), keeping the negative sign outside to yield \(-\sqrt{96x^7 y^9}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(2x\sqrt[3]{7x^2y}\)
qs.s: Move \(2x\) inside the radical as \((2x)^3 = 8x^3\): \(\sqrt[3]{8x^3 \cdot 7x^2y} = \sqrt[3]{56x^5y}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(2y\sqrt[3]{3xy^2}\)
qs.s: Move \(2y\) under the cube root by cubing it: \(\sqrt[3]{(2y)^3 \cdot 3xy^2} = \sqrt[3]{8y^3 \cdot 3xy^2} = \sqrt[3]{24xy^5}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(4a\sqrt[3]{2ab}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the outside term under the cube root as \((4a)^3 = 64a^3\), giving \(\sqrt[3]{64a^3 \cdot 2ab} = \sqrt[3]{128a^4b}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(3x\sqrt[3]{2x^2y}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient outside the radical and multiply into the radicand: \(\sqrt[3]{(3x)^3 \cdot 2x^2y} = \sqrt[3]{27x^3 \cdot 2x^2y} = \sqrt[3]{54x^5y}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(3m\sqrt[3]{4mn^2}\)
qs.s: Raise \(3m\) to the third power and multiply by the radicand: \(\sqrt[3]{(3m)^3 \cdot 4mn^2} = \sqrt[3]{27m^3 \cdot 4mn^2} = \sqrt[3]{108m^4n^2}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{3xy^2}{2}\sqrt[3]{\frac{4x}{9y}}\)
qs.s: Cube the outside expression: \(\left(\frac{3xy^2}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{27x^3y^6}{8}\). Multiplying by \(\frac{4x}{9y}\) gives \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{27 \cdot 4}{8 \cdot 9} \cdot \frac{x^4y^6}{y}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{3x^4y^5}{2}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(3x^2y\sqrt[3]{2xy^2}\)
qs.s: Raise \(3x^2y\) to the third power: \((3x^2y)^3 = 27x^6y^3\). Multiplying by the radicand yields \(\sqrt[3]{27x^6y^3 \cdot 2xy^2} = \sqrt[3]{54x^7y^5}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{x^2}{2y}\sqrt[3]{\frac{16y^4}{x^2}}\)
qs.s: Cube the outer quotient to get \(\frac{x^6}{8y^3}\) and multiply inside: \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{x^6}{8y^3} \cdot \frac{16y^4}{x^2}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{16}{8}x^{6-2}y^{4-3}} = \sqrt[3]{2x^4y}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.

\(\frac{2x}{3}\sqrt[3]{9x^2y}\)
qs.s: Cube the fractional coefficient to get \(\left(\frac{2x}{3}\right)^3 = \frac{8x^3}{27}\), then multiply: \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{8x^3}{27} \cdot 9x^2y} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{8x^5y}{3}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(-2mn^4\sqrt[3]{7}\)
qs.s: Leave the negative sign outside and cube the factors under the radical: \(-2mn^4\sqrt[3]{7} = -\sqrt[3]{(2mn^4)^3 \cdot 7} = -\sqrt[3]{8m^3n^{12} \cdot 7} = -\sqrt[3]{56m^3n^{12}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(-3ab^2\sqrt[3]{2}\)
qs.s: Keep the negative sign outside and cube the factors outside the radical: \(-3ab^2\sqrt[3]{2} = -\sqrt[3]{(3ab^2)^3 \cdot 2} = -\sqrt[3]{27a^3b^6 \cdot 2} = -\sqrt[3]{54a^3b^6}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(-4x^2y^3\sqrt[3]{2}\)
qs.s: Keep the negative sign outside and raise \(4x^2y^3\) to the third power under the radical: \(-4x^2y^3\sqrt[3]{2} = -\sqrt[3]{(4x^2y^3)^3 \cdot 2} = -\sqrt[3]{64x^6y^9 \cdot 2} = -\sqrt[3]{128x^6y^9}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(-5u^3v\sqrt[3]{2}\)
qs.s: Keep the negative sign outside and cube the coefficient inside the radical: \(-5u^3v\sqrt[3]{2} = -\sqrt[3]{(5u^3v)^3 \cdot 2} = -\sqrt[3]{125u^9v^3 \cdot 2} = -\sqrt[3]{250u^9v^3}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(-2x^2y\sqrt[3]{5}\)
qs.s: Leave the negative sign outside the radical and cube the coefficient inside: \(-2x^2y\sqrt[3]{5} = -\sqrt[3]{(2x^2y)^3 \cdot 5} = -\sqrt[3]{8x^6y^3 \cdot 5} = -\sqrt[3]{40x^6y^3}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(-3x^2y\sqrt[3]{4xy^2}\)
qs.s: Cube \(3x^2y\) under the radical and multiply by the radicand: \(-3x^2y\sqrt[3]{4xy^2} = -\sqrt[3]{(3x^2y)^3(4xy^2)} = -\sqrt[3]{27x^6y^3 \cdot 4xy^2} = -\sqrt[3]{108x^7y^5}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(-\frac{2a^2b}{3}\sqrt[3]{9ab^2}\)
qs.s: Cube the fraction outside the radical and multiply by the radicand: \(-\frac{2a^2b}{3}\sqrt[3]{9ab^2} = -\sqrt[3]{\frac{8a^6b^3}{27} \cdot 9ab^2} = -\sqrt[3]{\frac{72a^7b^5}{27}} = -\sqrt[3]{\frac{8a^7b^5}{3}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(-\frac{4x^2y}{3}\sqrt[3]{\frac{9xy^2}{2}}\)
qs.s: Cube the fraction outside the radical and multiply by the radicand: \(-\frac{4x^2y}{3}\sqrt[3]{\frac{9xy^2}{2}} = -\sqrt[3]{\frac{64x^6y^3}{27} \cdot \frac{9xy^2}{2}} = -\sqrt[3]{\frac{576x^7y^5}{54}} = -\sqrt[3]{\frac{32x^7y^5}{3}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(-2a^2bc^3\sqrt[3]{5ab^2c}\)
qs.s: Cube \(2a^2bc^3\) inside the radical while keeping the negative sign outside: \(-2a^2bc^3\sqrt[3]{5ab^2c} = -\sqrt[3]{(2a^2bc^3)^3(5ab^2c)} = -\sqrt[3]{8a^6b^3c^9 \cdot 5ab^2c} = -\sqrt[3]{40a^7b^5c^{10}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(-2 m n^2 \sqrt[4]{m^2 n}\)
qs.s: Keep the negative sign outside and raise \(2mn^2\) to the 4th power inside the radical: \(-\sqrt[4]{(2mn^2)^4 \cdot m^2 n} = -\sqrt[4]{16m^4 n^8 \cdot m^2 n} = -\sqrt[4]{16m^6 n^9}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(3 u^2 v \sqrt[3]{2 u v^2}\)
qs.s: Bring the factor inside by raising it to the power of 3: \(\sqrt[3]{(3u^2 v)^3 \cdot 2uv^2} = \sqrt[3]{27u^6 v^3 \cdot 2uv^2} = \sqrt[3]{54u^7 v^5}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(2 x y \sqrt[3]{3 x^2 y}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient and bring it inside the cube root: \(\sqrt[3]{(2xy)^3 \cdot 3x^2 y} = \sqrt[3]{8x^3 y^3 \cdot 3x^2 y} = \sqrt[3]{24x^5 y^4}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(-a b^2 \sqrt[4]{a^3 b}\)
qs.s: Keep the negative sign outside and raise the coefficient to the 4th power: \(-\sqrt[4]{(a b^2)^4 \cdot a^3 b} = -\sqrt[4]{a^4 b^8 \cdot a^3 b} = -\sqrt[4]{a^7 b^9}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(-x^2 y \sqrt{2 x y}\)
qs.s: The negative sign stays outside the square root while \((x^2 y)\) is squared under the radical: \(-\sqrt{(x^2 y)^2 \cdot 2xy} = -\sqrt{x^4 y^2 \cdot 2xy} = -\sqrt{2x^5 y^3}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(\frac{2 a^2 b c}{3} \sqrt[3]{9 a b^4 c^2}\)
qs.s: Cube the coefficient and simplify the fraction under the cube root: \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{8a^6 b^3 c^3}{27} \cdot 9ab^4 c^2} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{72a^7 b^7 c^5}{27}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{8a^7 b^7 c^5}{3}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers and \(z > 0\).
\(\frac{x^3 y}{2 z} \sqrt[4]{\frac{32 y^2 z^5}{x^2}}\)
qs.s: Raise the outside quotient to the 4th power under the 4th root: \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{x^{12} y^4}{16 z^4} \cdot \frac{32 y^2 z^5}{x^2}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{32 x^{12} y^6 z^5}{16 x^2 z^4}} = \sqrt[4]{2 x^{10} y^6 z}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers and \(b > 0\).
\(-\frac{2 a^2}{3 b} \sqrt[4]{\frac{81 a^3 b^7}{2}}\)
qs.s: Keep the negative outside and raise the quotient to the 4th power: \(-\sqrt[4]{\frac{16 a^8}{81 b^4} \cdot \frac{81 a^3 b^7}{2}} = -\sqrt[4]{\frac{16 \cdot 81 a^{11} b^7}{81 \cdot 2 b^4}} = -\sqrt[4]{8 a^{11} b^3}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
\(-\frac{x^2 y}{2} \sqrt[4]{8 x y^3}\)
qs.s: Raise the outside fraction to the 4th power and multiply under the radical: \(-\sqrt[4]{\frac{x^8 y^4}{16} \cdot 8xy^3} = -\sqrt[4]{\frac{8x^9 y^7}{16}} = -\sqrt[4]{\frac{x^9 y^7}{2}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers and \(y > 0\).
\(-\frac{3 x^3}{2 y} \sqrt{\frac{8 y^5}{3 x}}\)
qs.s: Square the outside factor under the square root and simplify the product: \(-\sqrt{\frac{9x^6}{4y^2} \cdot \frac{8y^5}{3x}} = -\sqrt{\frac{72x^6 y^5}{12xy^2}} = -\sqrt{6x^5 y^3}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(2ab\sqrt[4]{3a^3b^2}\)
qs.s: Raise the outside factor to the 4th power: \((2ab)^4 = 16a^4b^4\). Multiplying by the radicand gives \(\sqrt[4]{16a^4b^4 \cdot 3a^3b^2} = \sqrt[4]{48a^7b^6}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(2mn^2\sqrt[3]{3m^2n}\)
qs.s: Raise the outside factor to the 3rd power: \((2mn^2)^3 = 8m^3n^6\). Multiplying by the radicand gives \(\sqrt[3]{8m^3n^6 \cdot 3m^2n} = \sqrt[3]{24m^5n^7}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(2uv\sqrt[4]{5u^2v^3}\)
qs.s: Raise the outside factor to the 4th power: \((2uv)^4 = 16u^4v^4\). Multiplying by the radicand gives \(\sqrt[4]{16u^4v^4 \cdot 5u^2v^3} = \sqrt[4]{80u^6v^7}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(2x^2y\sqrt[3]{5y^2}\)
qs.s: Raise the outside factor to the 3rd power: \((2x^2y)^3 = 8x^6y^3\). Multiplying by the radicand gives \(\sqrt[3]{8x^6y^3 \cdot 5y^2} = \sqrt[3]{40x^6y^5}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(2xy\sqrt[4]{7x^2}\)
qs.s: Raise the outside factor to the 4th power: \((2xy)^4 = 16x^4y^4\). Multiplying by the radicand gives \(\sqrt[4]{16x^4y^4 \cdot 7x^2} = \sqrt[4]{112x^6y^4}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(2x^2yz^3\sqrt[4]{5xy^3z^2}\)
qs.s: Raise the outside expression to the 4th power: \((2x^2yz^3)^4 = 16x^8y^4z^{12}\). Multiplying by the radicand yields \(\sqrt[4]{16x^8y^4z^{12} \cdot 5xy^3z^2} = \sqrt[4]{80x^9y^7z^{14}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{3x}{2y^2}\sqrt[3]{\frac{4y^5}{9x^2}}\)
qs.s: Raise the outside fraction to the 3rd power: \(\left(\frac{3x}{2y^2}\right)^3 = \frac{27x^3}{8y^6}\). Multiply by the radicand: \(\frac{27x^3}{8y^6} \cdot \frac{4y^5}{9x^2} = \frac{3x}{2y}\), giving \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{3x}{2y}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{x^2}{2y}\sqrt[4]{48xy^5}\)
qs.s: Raise the outside fraction to the 4th power to get \(\frac{x^8}{16y^4}\), then multiply by the radicand: \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{x^8}{16y^4} \cdot 48xy^5} = \sqrt[4]{3x^9y}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(-2x^3y\sqrt[4]{3x^2y^3}\)
qs.s: Keep the negative sign outside because the root index is even: \(-( (2x^3y)^4 \cdot 3x^2y^3 )^{1/4} = -\sqrt[4]{16x^{12}y^4 \cdot 3x^2y^3} = -\sqrt[4]{48x^{14}y^7}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \(\frac{2a^2b^3}{3}\sqrt[4]{6a^3b}\)
qs.s: Raise the outside fraction to the 4th power to get \(\frac{16a^8b^{12}}{81}\). Multiply by \(6a^3b\) to obtain \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{96a^{11}b^{13}}{81}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{32a^{11}b^{13}}{27}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{2m\sqrt{mn}}{n}\)
qs.s: Square the outside factor \(\frac{2m}{n}\) to bring it under the radical: \(\sqrt{\frac{(2m)^2 \cdot mn}{n^2}} = \sqrt{\frac{4m^2 \cdot mn}{n^2}} = \sqrt{\frac{4m^3}{n}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{u\sqrt{3u^3v}}{v}\)
qs.s: Move \(\frac{u}{v}\) inside the square root by squaring it: \(\sqrt{\frac{u^2 \cdot 3u^3v}{v^2}} = \sqrt{\frac{3u^5v}{v^2}} = \sqrt{\frac{3u^5}{v}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x\sqrt{xy^3}}{y^2}\)
qs.s: Square the outside factors to place them inside the square root: \(\sqrt{\frac{x^2 \cdot xy^3}{(y^2)^2}} = \sqrt{\frac{x^3y^3}{y^4}}\). Simplifying the powers of \(y\) yields \(\sqrt{\frac{x^3}{y}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{s^2\sqrt{st}}{t^2}\)
qs.s: Bring \(\frac{s^2}{t^2}\) under the radical by squaring numerator and denominator: \(\sqrt{\frac{(s^2)^2 \cdot st}{(t^2)^2}} = \sqrt{\frac{s^4 \cdot st}{t^4}} = \sqrt{\frac{s^5}{t^3}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{a^3\sqrt{ab}}{b}\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(\frac{a^3}{b}\) under the radical by squaring it to get \(\sqrt{\frac{(a^3)^2}{b^2}} = \sqrt{\frac{a^6}{b^2}}\). Multiply by the existing radicand and simplify: \(\sqrt{\frac{a^6 \cdot ab}{b^2}} = \sqrt{\frac{a^7}{b}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x^2\sqrt[4]{x^3y^2}}{y}\)
qs.s: Raise the outside fraction to the 4th power to bring it under the fourth root: \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{(x^2)^4 \cdot x^3y^2}{y^4}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{x^8 \cdot x^3y^2}{y^4}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{x^{11}}{y^2}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{2x^2\sqrt[3]{3x^2y}}{y}\)
qs.s: Cube the expression outside the radical to bring it inside: \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{(2x^2)^3 \cdot 3x^2y}{y^3}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{8x^6 \cdot 3x^2y}{y^3}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{24x^8}{y^2}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{3xy^2\sqrt[3]{2x^2z}}{2z}\)
qs.s: Cube the outside factors and place them inside the cube root: \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{(3xy^2)^3 \cdot 2x^2z}{(2z)^3}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{27x^3y^6 \cdot 2x^2z}{8z^3}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{54x^5y^6z}{8z^3}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{27x^5y^6}{4z^2}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{5a^3b^2\sqrt{2ab^3c}}{2c^3}\)
qs.s: Square the outside factors to move them under the square root: \(\sqrt{\frac{(5a^3b^2)^2 \cdot 2ab^3c}{(2c^3)^2}} = \sqrt{\frac{25a^6b^4 \cdot 2ab^3c}{4c^6}} = \sqrt{\frac{50a^7b^7c}{4c^6}} = \sqrt{\frac{25a^7b^7}{2c^5}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{3a^2b\sqrt{2ac}}{2c^2}\)
qs.s: Square the outside factors to place them inside the square root: \(\sqrt{\frac{(3a^2b)^2(2ac)}{(2c^2)^2}} = \sqrt{\frac{18a^5b^2c}{4c^4}} = \sqrt{\frac{9a^5b^2}{2c^3}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\frac{-\sqrt[3]{2}}{3y^2}\)
qs.s: Move the denominator into the radical by cubing it: \((3y^2)^3 = 27y^6\). The expression becomes \(-\sqrt[3]{\frac{2}{27y^6}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\frac{-\sqrt[3]{5}}{2x^4}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator under the cube root as \(\sqrt[3]{(2x^4)^3} = \sqrt[3]{8x^{12}}\). Keeping the negative sign outside gives \(-\sqrt[3]{\frac{5}{8x^{12}}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\frac{-\sqrt[3]{4}}{5m^5}\)
qs.s: Express the denominator as a cube root: \(5m^5 = \sqrt[3]{(5m^5)^3} = \sqrt[3]{125m^{15}}\). Combining gives \(-\sqrt[3]{\frac{4}{125m^{15}}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\frac{-\sqrt[3]{3}}{4a^3}\)
qs.s: Cube the denominator to place it under the radical: \((4a^3)^3 = 64a^9\). This gives \(-\sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{64a^9}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\frac{-\sqrt[3]{11}}{2w^3}\)
qs.s: Cube the denominator \(2w^3\) to get \((2w^3)^3 = 8w^9\) under the radical. The result is \(-\sqrt[3]{\frac{11}{8w^9}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\frac{-2x\sqrt[4]{3x^2y}}{3y^2}\)
qs.s: Raise \(2x\) and \(3y^2\) to the 4th power to place them inside the 4th root: \(-\sqrt[4]{\frac{16x^4 \cdot 3x^2y}{81y^8}}\). Simplifying the fraction yields \(-\sqrt[4]{\frac{16x^6}{27y^7}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\frac{-3a^2\sqrt{5ab}}{2b^3}\)
qs.s: Move \(3a^2\) and \(2b^3\) inside the square root by squaring them to get \((3a^2)^2 = 9a^4\) and \((2b^3)^2 = 4b^6\). Simplifying the radicand yields \(-\sqrt{\frac{9a^4 \cdot 5ab}{4b^6}} = -\sqrt{\frac{45a^5}{4b^5}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\frac{-2x\sqrt[3]{3y}}{5y^2}\)
qs.s: Move \(2x\) and \(5y^2\) inside the cube root as \((2x)^3 = 8x^3\) and \((5y^2)^3 = 125y^6\). Then simplify: \(-\sqrt[3]{\frac{8x^3 \cdot 3y}{125y^6}} = -\sqrt[3]{\frac{24x^3}{125y^5}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\frac{-\sqrt[3]{4x}}{3x^3}\)
qs.s: Move the denominator inside the cube root as \((3x^3)^3 = 27x^9\). Simplifying the fraction inside gives \(-\sqrt[3]{\frac{4x}{27x^9}} = -\sqrt[3]{\frac{4}{27x^8}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent non-negative real numbers. \(\frac{-3x^2}{2y}\sqrt[3]{\frac{2y^2}{9x^4}}\)
qs.s: Cube the outside factor to move it inside: \(\left(\frac{3x^2}{2y}\right)^3 = \frac{27x^6}{8y^3}\). Multiplying by the radicand and reducing yields \(-\sqrt[3]{\frac{27x^6 \cdot 2y^2}{8y^3 \cdot 9x^4}} = -\sqrt[3]{\frac{3x^2}{4y}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{18x^2}}{3x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator as \(\sqrt[3]{(3x)^3} = \sqrt[3]{27x^3}\). Dividing the radicands and simplifying gives \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{18x^2}{27x^3}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{2}{3x}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{12x}}{2x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator under the cube root as \((2x)^3 = 8x^3\). Then simplify the fraction under the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{12x}{8x^3}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{2x^2}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{32y^2}}{4y}\)
qs.s: Express \(4y\) under the radical as \(\sqrt[3]{(4y)^3} = \sqrt[3]{64y^3}\). Simplifying the fraction \(\frac{32y^2}{64y^3}\) gives \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{2y}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{50a}}{5a}\)
qs.s: Move the denominator into the cube root as \((5a)^3 = 125a^3\). Simplifying \(\frac{50a}{125a^3}\) yields \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{2}{5a^2}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{40m^5}}{2m^2}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator as \(\sqrt[3]{(2m^2)^3} = \sqrt[3]{8m^6}\). Reducing \(\frac{40m^5}{8m^6}\) gives \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{5}{m}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{32a^5b^2}}{2ab}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator under the fourth root as \((2ab)^4 = 16a^4b^4\). Simplifying \(\frac{32a^5b^2}{16a^4b^4}\) produces \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{2a}{b^2}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2a^2b\sqrt[3]{5ab^2}}{5ab}\)
qs.s: Simplify the outside factor first to \(\frac{2a}{5}\), then move it into the cube root as \(\left(\frac{2a}{5}\right)^3 = \frac{8a^3}{125}\). Multiplying by \(5ab^2\) gives \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{40a^4b^2}{125}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{8a^4b^2}{25}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{108x^7y^2}}{3x^3y}\)
qs.s: Move the denominator into the cube root as \((3x^3y)^3 = 27x^9y^3\). Simplifying the fraction \(\frac{108x^7y^2}{27x^9y^3}\) gives \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{4}{x^2y}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{72x^4y^5}}{6xy^2}\)
qs.s: Express the denominator inside the cube root as \((6xy^2)^3 = 216x^3y^6\). Simplifying \(\frac{72x^4y^5}{216x^3y^6}\) results in \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{x}{3y}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2x\sqrt[3]{3x}}{3y}\)
qs.s: Move both outside terms into the cube root: \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{(2x)^3(3x)}{(3y)^3}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{24x^4}{27y^3}}\). Simplifying the fraction yields \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{8x^4}{9y^3}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{27x^2}}{3x}\)
qs.s: Express the denominator as \(\sqrt[4]{(3x)^4} = \sqrt[4]{81x^4}\), giving \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{27x^2}{81x^4}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{1}{3x^2}}\) after simplifying the fraction inside the radical.

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{3x}}{3x}\)
qs.s: Write the denominator as \(\sqrt[3]{(3x)^3} = \sqrt[3]{27x^3}\), then combine under a single radical to get \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{3x}{27x^3}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{9x^2}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{4x^3}}{2x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator as \(\sqrt[4]{(2x)^4} = \sqrt[4]{16x^4}\) and simplify the fraction under the radical to get \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{4x^3}{16x^4}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{1}{4x}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{4x^2}}{2x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(2x\) as \(\sqrt[3]{(2x)^3} = \sqrt[3]{8x^3}\) and combine under the radical to obtain \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{4x^2}{8x^3}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{2x}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{2x}}{4x}\)
qs.s: Write the denominator as \(\sqrt[3]{(4x)^3} = \sqrt[3]{64x^3}\), so the expression simplifies under a single cube root to \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{2x}{64x^3}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{32x^2}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{3x\sqrt[4]{2xy^3}}{2y}\)
qs.s: Bring the factor \(\frac{3x}{2y}\) into the fourth root by raising it to the fourth power, yielding \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{81x^4}{16y^4} \cdot 2xy^3} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{81x^5}{8y}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2a^2\sqrt[3]{9ab^2}}{3b}\)
qs.s: Cube the outside quotient to bring it inside the cube root: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{2a^2}{3b}\right)^3 \cdot 9ab^2} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{8a^6}{27b^3} \cdot 9ab^2} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{8a^7}{3b}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{16x^4y}}{2xy^2}\)
qs.s: Express the denominator as \(\sqrt[3]{(2xy^2)^3} = \sqrt[3]{8x^3y^6}\), then simplify the radicand \(\frac{16x^4y}{8x^3y^6}\) to obtain \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{2x}{y^5}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[5]{16x^3y^8}}{2xy^2}\)
qs.s: Express the denominator as \(\sqrt[5]{(2xy^2)^5} = \sqrt[5]{32x^5y^{10}}\), then simplify under the fifth root to get \(\sqrt[5]{\frac{16x^3y^8}{32x^5y^{10}}} = \sqrt[5]{\frac{1}{2x^2y^2}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{32x^5y^2}}{4x^2y}\)
qs.s: Write the denominator inside a fourth root as \(\sqrt[4]{(4x^2y)^4} = \sqrt[4]{256x^8y^4}\), and simplify the fraction to obtain \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{32x^5y^2}{256x^8y^4}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{1}{8x^3y^2}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{\sqrt[4]{72}}{3}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator as \(3 = \sqrt[4]{3^4} = \sqrt[4]{81}\). Combining under a single radical and dividing by 9 gives \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{72}{81}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{8}{9}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{3}\)
qs.s: Express the denominator as a cube root: \(3 = \sqrt[3]{3^3} = \sqrt[3]{27}\). Combine under one radical and reduce to get \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{18}{27}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{2}{3}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{20}}{2}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator under the cube root as \(2 = \sqrt[3]{2^3} = \sqrt[3]{8}\). Then combine and simplify the fraction to obtain \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{20}{8}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{5}{2}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{\sqrt[5]{72}}{2}\)
qs.s: Express the denominator as a fifth root, \(2 = \sqrt[5]{2^5} = \sqrt[5]{32}\). Dividing numerator and denominator by 8 under the radical yields \(\sqrt[5]{\frac{72}{32}} = \sqrt[5]{\frac{9}{4}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical: \(\frac{\sqrt[4]{24}}{2}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator under the fourth root as \(2 = \sqrt[4]{2^4} = \sqrt[4]{16}\). Combining into a single radical gives \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{24}{16}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{3}{2}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt[5]{48a^{11}b^4}}{2a^2}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator under the fifth root as \((2a^2)^5 = 32a^{10}\). Combining under a single radical and simplifying \(\frac{48a^{11}b^4}{32a^{10}}\) gives \(\sqrt[5]{\frac{3ab^4}{2}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt[4]{48x^9y^2}}{2x^2}\)
qs.s: Express the denominator as a fourth root, \((2x^2)^4 = 16x^8\), to write the expression as \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{48x^9y^2}{16x^8}}\). Reducing the fraction inside results in \(\sqrt[4]{3xy^2}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{12x^7}}{2x}\)
qs.s: Write the denominator under the cube root as \((2x)^3 = 8x^3\), giving \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{12x^7}{8x^3}}\). Simplifying the coefficients and variable powers yields \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{3x^4}{2}}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{2a^2\sqrt[3]{54ab^4}}{3b}\)
qs.s: Move the coefficient into the cube root by cubing it to get \(\frac{8a^6}{27b^3}\). Multiplying by \(54ab^4\) inside the radical simplifies to \(\sqrt[3]{16a^7b}\).

qs.q: Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{32x^5y^8}}{4xy^2}\)
qs.s: Cube the denominator to place it under the radical as \((4xy^2)^3 = 64x^3y^6\). Simplifying \(\frac{32x^5y^8}{64x^3y^6}\) gives \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{x^2y^2}{2}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{12a^2}}{2a^3}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator under the cube root as \(2a^3 = \sqrt[3]{(2a^3)^3} = \sqrt[3]{8a^9}\). Dividing the radicands gives \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{12a^2}{8a^9}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{2a^7}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{27x}}{3x^2}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator under the radical as \(3x^2 = \sqrt[4]{(3x^2)^4} = \sqrt[4]{81x^8}\). Then simplify the quotient inside the radical: \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{27x}{81x^8}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{1}{3x^7}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{8b}}{2b^3}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator under the fourth root as \(\sqrt[4]{(2b^3)^4} = \sqrt[4]{16b^{12}}\). Combining and simplifying under one radical gives \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{8b}{16b^{12}}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{1}{2b^{11}}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[5]{16y^3}}{2y^2}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator as \(\sqrt[5]{(2y^2)^5} = \sqrt[5]{32y^{10}}\). Simplifying the fraction inside yields \(\sqrt[5]{\frac{16y^3}{32y^{10}}} = \sqrt[5]{\frac{1}{2y^7}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{18n}}{3n^2}\)
qs.s: Express the denominator as \(\sqrt[3]{(3n^2)^3} = \sqrt[3]{27n^6}\). Simplifying the radicand gives \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{18n}{27n^6}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{2}{3n^5}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2a \sqrt[3]{5a^2 b}}{3b^2}\)
qs.s: Move the numerator factor \(2a\) and the denominator \(3b^2\) into the cube root: \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{(2a)^3 \cdot 5a^2 b}{(3b^2)^3}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{8a^3 \cdot 5a^2 b}{27b^6}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{40a^5}{27b^5}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[6]{96x^8 y^3}}{2x^2 y}\)
qs.s: Express the denominator inside the sixth root as \((2x^2 y)^6 = 64x^{12} y^6\). Simplifying the fraction inside gives \(\sqrt[6]{\frac{96x^8 y^3}{64x^{12} y^6}} = \sqrt[6]{\frac{3}{2x^4 y^3}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[5]{48x^3 y^7 z}}{2x y^2 z}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator under the fifth root as \(\sqrt[5]{(2xy^2 z)^5} = \sqrt[5]{32x^5 y^{10} z^5}\). Simplifying the fraction inside yields \(\sqrt[5]{\frac{48x^3 y^7 z}{32x^5 y^{10} z^5}} = \sqrt[5]{\frac{3}{2x^2 y^3 z^4}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{5x^2 y \sqrt[3]{4x y^2}}{2x^3 y^2}\)
qs.s: Simplify the outside factor to \(\frac{5}{2xy}\), then move it inside the cube root: \(\sqrt[3]{\left(\frac{5}{2xy}\right)^3 (4xy^2)} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{125 \cdot 4xy^2}{8x^3 y^3}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{125}{2x^2 y}}\).

qs.q:
Write as an entire radical. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{3x \sqrt[4]{2x y^5}}{2y^2}\)
qs.s: Place factors outside the radical into the fourth root: \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{(3x)^4 \cdot (2xy^5)}{(2y^2)^4}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{81x^4 \cdot 2xy^5}{16y^8}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{162x^5 y^5}{16y^8}} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{81x^5}{8y^3}}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((\sqrt{8u^5 v})(\sqrt{3u^2 v^3})\)
qs.s: Multiply the radicands to get \(\sqrt{24u^7 v^4}\), then simplify by factoring out \(\sqrt{4u^6 v^4} = 2u^3 v^2\) to obtain \(2u^3 v^2 \sqrt{6u}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((\sqrt{10xy^3})(\sqrt{15x^4 y})\)
qs.s: Multiply the radicands to get \(\sqrt{150x^5 y^4}\), then simplify as \(\sqrt{25x^4 y^4 \cdot 6x} = 5x^2 y^2 \sqrt{6x}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((\sqrt{5x^3 y})(\sqrt{10xy^4})\)
qs.s: Multiply under a single radical to get \(\sqrt{50x^4 y^5}\), then factor out the perfect square \(\sqrt{25x^4 y^4} = 5x^2 y^2\), leaving \(5x^2 y^2 \sqrt{2y}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((\sqrt{14c^3 d^5})(\sqrt{7c^2 d^2})\)
qs.s: Multiply the expressions under one radical to get \(\sqrt{98c^5 d^7}\), and factor out \(\sqrt{49c^4 d^6} = 7c^2 d^3\) to obtain \(7c^2 d^3 \sqrt{2cd}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((3x\sqrt{6x^3 y})(2y^2\sqrt{15xy^4})\)
qs.s: Multiply outside terms to get \(6xy^2\) and inside terms to get \(\sqrt{90x^4 y^5} = 3x^2 y^2 \sqrt{10y}\), then multiply together: \(6xy^2 \cdot 3x^2 y^2 \sqrt{10y} = 18x^3 y^4 \sqrt{10y}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((\sqrt{2xy^3})(\sqrt{6x^2 z})(\sqrt{15yz^3})\)
qs.s: Multiply the three radicands to get \(\sqrt{180x^3 y^4 z^4}\), and factor out \(\sqrt{36x^2 y^4 z^4} = 6xy^2 z^2\), giving \(6xy^2 z^2 \sqrt{5x}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((\sqrt[3]{12a^4 b^2})(\sqrt[3]{18a^4 b^5})\)
qs.s: Multiply under one cube root to obtain \(\sqrt[3]{216a^8 b^7}\), then extract perfect cubes: \(\sqrt[3]{216a^6 b^6} = 6a^2 b^2\), leaving \(6a^2 b^2 \sqrt[3]{a^2 b}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt{150a^7 b^5}}{\sqrt{2a^2 b}}\)
qs.s: Combine under a single radical to obtain \(\sqrt{\frac{150a^7 b^5}{2a^2 b}} = \sqrt{75a^5 b^4}\), which simplifies to \(\sqrt{25a^4 b^4 \cdot 3a} = 5a^2 b^2 \sqrt{3a}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{12x^2\sqrt{54x^5 y^7}}{4x\sqrt{3x^2 y^2}}\)
qs.s: Divide outside coefficients to get \(\frac{12x^2}{4x} = 3x\) and simplify the radical quotient \(\sqrt{\frac{54x^5 y^7}{3x^2 y^2}} = \sqrt{18x^3 y^5} = 3xy^2\sqrt{2xy}\), giving a final product of \(9x^2 y^2 \sqrt{2xy}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((3p\sqrt{14pq})(4q\sqrt{7p})\)
qs.s: Multiply the coefficients outside the radical to get \(12pq\), and multiply the radicands to get \(\sqrt{98p^2q} = 7p\sqrt{2q}\). Multiplying these gives \((12pq)(7p\sqrt{2q}) = 84p^2q\sqrt{2q}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((2a\sqrt{6ab})(5b\sqrt{3a})\)
qs.s: Multiply the coefficients outside the radical to get \((2a)(5b) = 10ab\), and multiply the radicands to get \(\sqrt{18a^2b} = 3a\sqrt{2b}\). Multiplying these together yields \((10ab)(3a\sqrt{2b}) = 30a^2b\sqrt{2b}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((5x\sqrt{6xy})(2x\sqrt{3y})\)
qs.s: Multiply the coefficients to get \((5x)(2x) = 10x^2\), and multiply the radicands to get \(\sqrt{18xy^2} = 3y\sqrt{2x}\). Combining them produces \((10x^2)(3y\sqrt{2x}) = 30x^2y\sqrt{2x}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((3u\sqrt{15uv})(2v\sqrt{5u})\)
qs.s: Multiply the terms outside the radicals to get \(6uv\), and multiply the radicands to get \(\sqrt{75u^2v} = 5u\sqrt{3v}\). Then multiply them together to get \((6uv)(5u\sqrt{3v}) = 30u^2v\sqrt{3v}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((6m\sqrt{8mn})(2n\sqrt{2m})\)
qs.s: Multiply the outer factors to get \(12mn\), and multiply the radicands to get \(\sqrt{16m^2n} = 4m\sqrt{n}\). The product is \((12mn)(4m\sqrt{n}) = 48m^2n\sqrt{n}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((2a\sqrt{3ab})(3b\sqrt{10bc})(a\sqrt{15ac})\)
qs.s: Multiply the terms outside the radicals to get \(6a^2b\), and multiply the radicands to get \(\sqrt{450a^2b^2c^2} = 15abc\sqrt{2}\). Multiplying gives \((6a^2b)(15abc\sqrt{2}) = 90a^3b^2c\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{(6x\sqrt{10xy})(2y\sqrt{6x})}{3\sqrt{5y}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator expressions to get \(12xy\sqrt{60x^2y} = 24x^2y\sqrt{15y}\). Then divide by \(3\sqrt{5y}\) to get \(\frac{24x^2y}{3}\sqrt{\frac{15y}{5y}} = 8x^2y\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{18x^3y\sqrt{60x^5y^3}}{3xy\sqrt{3xy}}\)
qs.s: Divide the outer terms to get \(\frac{18x^3y}{3xy} = 6x^2\), and divide the radicands to get \(\sqrt{\frac{60x^5y^3}{3xy}} = \sqrt{20x^4y^2} = 2x^2y\sqrt{5}\). The product is \((6x^2)(2x^2y\sqrt{5}) = 12x^4y\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((5x^2y\sqrt{12xy^3})(3xy^2\sqrt{18x^3y})\)
qs.s: Multiply the outer terms to get \(15x^3y^3\), and multiply the radicands to get \(\sqrt{216x^4y^4} = 6x^2y^2\sqrt{6}\). Combining them yields \((15x^3y^3)(6x^2y^2\sqrt{6}) = 90x^5y^5\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((4a^2b\sqrt{20a^3b})(3ab^3\sqrt{15ab^2})\)
qs.s: Multiply the outer terms to obtain \(12a^3b^4\), and multiply the radicands to obtain \(\sqrt{300a^4b^3} = 10a^2b\sqrt{3b}\). Multiplying these together results in \((12a^3b^4)(10a^2b\sqrt{3b}) = 120a^5b^5\sqrt{3b}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form: \((4a^2\sqrt[3]{2b^5})(3a\sqrt[3]{4b})\). All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
qs.s: Multiply the outside terms to get \((4a^2)(3a) = 12a^3\), and multiply under the radical to get \(\sqrt[3]{8b^6} = 2b^2\). The product is \((12a^3)(2b^2) = 24a^3b^2\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form: \((2x\sqrt[3]{9y^4})(3x^2\sqrt[3]{3y^2})\). All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
qs.s: Multiply the outside terms to get \((2x)(3x^2) = 6x^3\), and multiply the radicands to get \(\sqrt[3]{27y^6} = 3y^2\). Combining them gives \((6x^3)(3y^2) = 18x^3y^2\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form: \((2c^2\sqrt[3]{25d^4})(c\sqrt[3]{5d^2})\). All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
qs.s: Multiply the outside terms to obtain \((2c^2)(c) = 2c^3\) and the radicands to obtain \(\sqrt[3]{125d^6} = 5d^2\). Combining them gives \((2c^3)(5d^2) = 10c^3d^2\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form: \((5x^2y\sqrt[3]{24x^5y^4})(2xy^3\sqrt[3]{36x^4y^2})\). All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
qs.s: Multiply outside terms to get \((5x^2y)(2xy^3) = 10x^3y^4\) and radicands to get \(\sqrt[3]{864x^9y^6} = 6x^3y^2\sqrt[3]{4}\). The product is \((10x^3y^4)(6x^3y^2\sqrt[3]{4}) = 60x^6y^6\sqrt[3]{4}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form: \((2a\sqrt[3]{3b^2})(a^2\sqrt[3]{6b^4})(4b\sqrt[3]{12b^2})\). All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
qs.s: Multiply the outside terms to get \((2a)(a^2)(4b) = 8a^3b\), and multiply the radicands to get \(\sqrt[3]{216b^8} = 6b^2\sqrt[3]{b^2}\). Multiplying these gives \((8a^3b)(6b^2\sqrt[3]{b^2}) = 48a^3b^3\sqrt[3]{b^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form: \((3xy\sqrt[4]{8x^3y^5z^2})(2x^2\sqrt[4]{2x^2y^3z^6})\). All variables represent non-negative real numbers.
qs.s: Multiply the outside terms to get \((3xy)(2x^2) = 6x^3y\), and multiply the fourth roots to get \(\sqrt[4]{16x^5y^8z^8} = 2xy^2z^2\sqrt[4]{x}\). The product is \((6x^3y)(2xy^2z^2\sqrt[4]{x}) = 12x^4y^3z^2\sqrt[4]{x}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form: \(\frac{15x^3\sqrt[3]{54y^7}}{3x\sqrt[3]{2y^2}}\). All variables represent positive real numbers.
qs.s: Divide the outside terms to get \(\frac{15x^3}{3x} = 5x^2\), and divide under the radical to get \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{54y^7}{2y^2}} = \sqrt[3]{27y^5} = 3y\sqrt[3]{y^2}\). Multiplying these yields \((5x^2)(3y\sqrt[3]{y^2}) = 15x^2y\sqrt[3]{y^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form: \(\frac{(4x^2y^2\sqrt[3]{18x^4y})(3x\sqrt[3]{12xy^5})}{2xy\sqrt[3]{8x^2y^3}}\). All variables represent positive real numbers.
qs.s: Multiply the numerator terms to obtain \(12x^3y^2\sqrt[3]{216x^5y^6}\), then divide by the denominator to get \(\frac{12x^3y^2}{2xy}\sqrt[3]{\frac{216x^5y^6}{8x^2y^3}} = (6x^2y)(3xy) = 18x^3y^2\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((3u^2 v\sqrt[3]{5uv^2})(2u\sqrt[3]{25u^2 v^2})\)
qs.s: Multiply the outer terms to get \(6u^3 v\) and the radicands to get \(\sqrt[3]{125u^3 v^4} = 5uv\sqrt[3]{v}\). Combining these products yields \(30u^4 v^2\sqrt[3]{v}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((2xy\sqrt[3]{3x^2 y})(4y\sqrt[3]{9x^2 y^3})\)
qs.s: Multiply the coefficients outside the radical to get \(8xy^2\), and multiply the radicands to get \(\sqrt[3]{27x^4 y^4} = 3xy\sqrt[3]{xy}\). Multiplying these results gives \(24x^2 y^3\sqrt[3]{xy}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((2a^2 b\sqrt[3]{4a^2 b})(ab^2\sqrt[3]{2ab^4})\)
qs.s: Multiplying the outer terms gives \(2a^3 b^3\), while the product of the radicands is \(\sqrt[3]{8a^3 b^5} = 2ab\sqrt[3]{b^2}\). Multiplying these together produces \(4a^4 b^4\sqrt[3]{b^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((x^2 y\sqrt[3]{2x^2 y^2})(5xy\sqrt[3]{16xy})\)
qs.s: Multiply the outer expressions to get \(5x^3 y^2\) and the radicands to get \(\sqrt[3]{32x^3 y^3} = 2xy\sqrt[3]{4}\). The product of both parts is \(10x^4 y^3\sqrt[3]{4}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((2a^2 bc\sqrt[4]{8a^3 b^5 c^2})(3ab^2\sqrt[4]{2a^3 b^2 c^7})\)
qs.s: Multiply the outer expressions to get \(6a^3 b^3 c\) and the radicands to get \(\sqrt[4]{16a^6 b^7 c^9} = 2abc^2\sqrt[4]{a^2 b^3 c}\). Combining these factors gives \(12a^4 b^4 c^3\sqrt[4]{a^2 b^3 c}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{(6a^2 b\sqrt[3]{4a^2 b^2})(2a\sqrt[3]{10a^4 b})}{4b\sqrt[3]{5ab^2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the factors in the numerator to get \(12a^3 b\sqrt[3]{40a^6 b^3}\), then divide by the denominator to obtain \(3a^3\sqrt[3]{8a^5 b}\). Simplifying the radical gives \(3a^3 \cdot 2a\sqrt[3]{a^2 b} = 6a^4\sqrt[3]{a^2 b}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{10x^3 y^2\sqrt[4]{96x^{11} y^{10}}}{2xy\sqrt[4]{6x^2 y}}\)
qs.s: Divide outside the radicals to get \(5x^2 y\) and inside to get \(\sqrt[4]{16x^9 y^9} = 2x^2 y^2\sqrt[4]{xy}\). Multiplying these gives \(10x^4 y^3\sqrt[4]{xy}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{15a^3 b^2\sqrt[3]{54a^7 b^8}}{3ab\sqrt[3]{2ab^3}}\)
qs.s: Divide the coefficients and variables outside to get \(5a^2 b\), and simplify the quotient of radicals \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{54a^7 b^8}{2ab^3}} = \sqrt[3]{27a^6 b^5} = 3a^2 b\sqrt[3]{b^2}\). Multiplying the results yields \(15a^4 b^2\sqrt[3]{b^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent non-negative real numbers: \((2x\sqrt[3]{2x^2 y})(3y\sqrt[3]{4xy^2})(x^2 y\sqrt[3]{3xy^2})\)
qs.s: Multiply the three outer factors to get \(6x^3 y^2\), and multiply the three radicands to get \(\sqrt[3]{24x^4 y^5} = 2xy\sqrt[3]{3xy^2}\). Multiplying these gives \(12x^4 y^3\sqrt[3]{3xy^2}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{15y^3\sqrt{x^7 y^2}}{5y^6\sqrt{x^3 y^6}}\)
qs.s: Divide the outer expressions to get \(\frac{3}{y^3}\) and simplify the radical quotient to \(\sqrt{\frac{x^4}{y^4}} = \frac{x^2}{y^2}\). Multiplying gives \(\frac{3x^2}{y^5}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{8x^3\sqrt{x^4 y^5}}{2x^5\sqrt{x^2 y^2}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the outer terms to \(\frac{4}{x^2}\) and divide under the radical to get \(\sqrt{x^2 y^3} = xy\sqrt{y}\). Multiplying them gives \(\frac{4y\sqrt{y}}{x}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{10x^4\sqrt{x^2 y^3}}{2x^6\sqrt{x^4 y}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the outer terms to \(\frac{5}{x^2}\) and divide the radicands to get \(\sqrt{\frac{y^2}{x^2}} = \frac{y}{x}\). Multiplying these gives \(\frac{5y}{x^3}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{12a^3\sqrt{a^4 b^7}}{4a^7\sqrt{a^8 b^3}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the outer expression to \(\frac{3}{a^4}\) and simplify the radical quotient to \(\sqrt{\frac{b^4}{a^4}} = \frac{b^2}{a^2}\). Multiplying the results yields \(\frac{3b^2}{a^6}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{14x^2\sqrt{x^3 y^7}}{7x^4\sqrt{x^5 y^3}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the outer coefficients and powers to \(\frac{2}{x^2}\), and divide under the radical to get \(\sqrt{\frac{y^4}{x^2}} = \frac{y^2}{x}\). Multiplying gives \(\frac{2y^2}{x^3}\).

qs.q:
Divide and express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{4x^2\sqrt{18x^5 y}}{3y\sqrt{xy}} \div \frac{2x^4\sqrt{2x y^3}}{9y^2\sqrt{x^3 y}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the two quotients to \(\frac{4x^4\sqrt{2}}{y}\) and \(\frac{2x^3\sqrt{2}}{9y}\), then multiply by the reciprocal to obtain \(\frac{4x^4\sqrt{2}}{y} \cdot \frac{9y}{2x^3\sqrt{2}} = 18x\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{12x^2\sqrt[3]{x^8 y^7}}{4x^5\sqrt[3]{x^2 y}}\)
qs.s: Divide the outer terms to obtain \(\frac{3}{x^3}\) and simplify the cube roots to \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{x^8 y^7}{x^2 y}} = \sqrt[3]{x^6 y^6} = x^2 y^2\). Multiplying these results in \(\frac{3y^2}{x}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{15x^3\sqrt{72x^5 y^7}}{3x^6\sqrt{2x y^3}}\)
qs.s: Divide the outer terms to get \(\frac{5}{x^3}\) and simplify the radicand to \(\sqrt{\frac{72x^5 y^7}{2x y^3}} = \sqrt{36x^4 y^4} = 6x^2 y^2\). Multiplying them gives \(\frac{30y^2}{x}\).

qs.q:
Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{8xy^2\sqrt{50x^3 y^5 z^6}}{2x^3 y\sqrt{2xyz^2}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the outer expression to \(\frac{4y}{x^2}\) and divide under the radical to get \(\sqrt{25x^2 y^4 z^4} = 5xy^2 z^2\). Multiplying gives \(\frac{20y^3 z^2}{x}\).

qs.q:
Multiply and express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{6a^2\sqrt{a^3 b^5}}{a^4\sqrt{ab}} \cdot \frac{a^3\sqrt{8b^3}}{2\sqrt{2b}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the first factor to \(\frac{6b^2}{a}\) and the second factor to \(a^3 b\). Multiplying them yields \(6a^2 b^3\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{40x^7 y^2}}{\sqrt[3]{x^2 y^5}}\)
qs.s: Combine into one radical to get \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{40x^5}{y^3}}\). Extracting the perfect cubes \(8\), \(x^3\), and \(y^3\) gives \(\frac{2x\sqrt[3]{5x^2}}{y}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{24xy^5}}{\sqrt[3]{x^4 y}}\)
qs.s: Combine under a single radical to get \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{24y^4}{x^3}}\). Factoring out the perfect cubes gives \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{8y^3 \cdot 3y}}{\sqrt[3]{x^3}} = \frac{2y\sqrt[3]{3y}}{x}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{128m^3 n^7}}{\sqrt[3]{m^6 n^3}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the fraction inside the radical to \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{128n^4}{m^3}}\). Factoring out the perfect cubes \(64\), \(n^3\), and \(m^3\) leaves \(\frac{4n\sqrt[3]{2n}}{m}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{250u^4 v^8}}{\sqrt[3]{u^7 v^3}}\)
qs.s: Combine terms under the cube root to obtain \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{250v^5}{u^3}}\). Removing the perfect cubes \(125\), \(v^3\), and \(u^3\) results in \(\frac{5v\sqrt[3]{2v^2}}{u}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{54a^5 b^2}}{\sqrt[3]{a b^5}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the quotient inside the radical to obtain \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{54a^4}{b^3}}\). Factoring out the perfect cube factors \(27\), \(a^3\), and \(b^3\) yields \(\frac{3a\sqrt[3]{2a}}{b}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{4\sqrt[3]{54x^8 y^2 z^5}}{2\sqrt[3]{x y^8 z^2}}\)
qs.s: Divide the outside coefficients to get \(2\) and combine the radicands to get \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{54x^7 z^3}{y^6}}\). Simplifying the radical gives \(\frac{3x^2 z\sqrt[3]{2x}}{y^2}\), which multiplied by \(2\) gives \(\frac{6x^2 z\sqrt[3]{2x}}{y^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{3\sqrt[3]{500x^2 y^{11} z^8}}{9\sqrt[3]{2x^8 y^2 z}}\)
qs.s: Reduce the outer coefficients \(\frac{3}{9}\) to \(\frac{1}{3}\) and simplify the radicand to \(\frac{250y^9 z^7}{x^6}\). Taking the cube root gives \(\frac{5y^3 z^2 \sqrt[3]{2z}}{x^2}\), which multiplied by \(\frac{1}{3}\) produces \(\frac{5y^3 z^2 \sqrt[3]{2z}}{3x^2}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt[4]{160x^3 y^{11}}}{\sqrt[4]{2x^7 y^2}}\)
qs.s: Combine under a fourth root to get \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{80y^9}{x^4}}\). Factoring into fourth powers yields \(\frac{\sqrt[4]{16y^8 \cdot 5y}}{\sqrt[4]{x^4}} = \frac{2y^2 \sqrt[4]{5y}}{x}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{48a^7 b^5 c}}{\sqrt[3]{2a^2 b^8 c^4}}\)
qs.s: Combine under a single radical to obtain \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{24a^5}{b^3 c^3}}\). Factoring out the perfect cubes \(8\), \(a^3\), \(b^3\), and \(c^3\) yields \(\frac{2a\sqrt[3]{3a^2}}{bc}\).

qs.q: Express in simplest radical form. All variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{20x^5 y^7} \cdot \sqrt[3]{10x^3 y^3}}{\sqrt[3]{5x y^2 z^6}}\)
qs.s: Combine the entire expression under a single cube root to obtain \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{200x^8 y^{10}}{5xy^2 z^6}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{40x^7 y^8}{z^6}}\). Factoring out perfect cubes yields \(\frac{2x^2 y^2 \sqrt[3]{5xy^2}}{z^2}\).

qs.q: A cube-shaped block of ice has a volume of \(250\text{ cm}^3\). What is the length of each edge of the block in simplest radical form?
qs.s: The edge length is the cube root of the volume, \(s = \sqrt[3]{250}\). Factoring 250 as \(125 \cdot 2\), we find \(s = 5\sqrt[3]{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A cube-shaped water tank has a volume of \(54\text{ m}^3\). What is the edge length of the tank in simplest radical form?
qs.s: The edge length of a cube is the cube root of its volume, \(s = \sqrt[3]{54}\). Since \(54 = 27 \cdot 2\), simplifying gives \(s = 3\sqrt[3]{2}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A square artist canvas has an area of \(108\text{ cm}^2\). What is the length of each side of the canvas in simplest radical form?
qs.s: The side length is \(s = \sqrt{108}\). Factoring 108 as \(36 \cdot 3\), this simplifies to \(s = 6\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A square patio has an area of \(72\text{ m}^2\). What is the length of each side of the patio in simplest radical form?
qs.s: The side length of a square is the square root of its area, \(s = \sqrt{72}\). Factoring out the largest perfect square gives \(\sqrt{36 \cdot 2} = 6\sqrt{2}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A cube-shaped storage crate has a volume of \(40\text{ ft}^3\). What is the length of each side of the crate in simplest radical form?
qs.s: The edge length is \(s = \sqrt[3]{40}\). Since \(40 = 8 \cdot 5\), the simplified side length is \(2\sqrt[3]{5}\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A square courtyard has an area of \(54\text{ m}^2\). What is the length of a diagonal path across the courtyard in simplest radical form?
qs.s: By the Pythagorean theorem, the square of the diagonal is \(d^2 = s^2 + s^2 = 54 + 54 = 108\). Thus, \(d = \sqrt{108} = \sqrt{36 \cdot 3} = 6\sqrt{3}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage crate with a square base has a volume of \(360\text{ ft}^3\) and a height of \(5\text{ ft}\). What is the side length of the square base in simplest radical form?
qs.s: The area of the base is \(V / h = 360 / 5 = 72\text{ ft}^2\). The side length of the base is \(s = \sqrt{72} = \sqrt{36 \cdot 2} = 6\sqrt{2}\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A square garden has an area of \(180\text{ m}^2\). What is the perimeter of the garden in simplest radical form?
qs.s: The side length is \(s = \sqrt{180} = \sqrt{36 \cdot 5} = 6\sqrt{5}\text{ m}\). The perimeter is \(4s = 4(6\sqrt{5}) = 24\sqrt{5}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A cube-shaped box has a volume of \(192\text{ cm}^3\). What is the total length of all 12 edges of the box in simplest radical form?
qs.s: Each edge has length \(s = \sqrt[3]{192} = \sqrt[3]{64 \cdot 3} = 4\sqrt[3]{3}\text{ cm}\). The total length of all 12 edges is \(12 \times 4\sqrt[3]{3} = 48\sqrt[3]{3}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A cube-shaped block has a total surface area of \(120\text{ cm}^2\). What is the edge length of the cube in simplest radical form?
qs.s: A cube has 6 congruent square faces, so the area of one face is \(120 / 6 = 20\text{ cm}^2\). The edge length is \(s = \sqrt{20} = \sqrt{4 \cdot 5} = 2\sqrt{5}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The area of a circle has the formula \(A = \pi r^2\). If the area is multiplied by 16, how is the radius affected?
qs.s: Since \(A = \pi r^2\), multiplying the area by 16 gives a new radius of \(\sqrt{16}r = 4r\). Therefore, the radius is multiplied by 4.

qs.q: The volume of a cube has the formula \(V = s^3\). If the volume is multiplied by 27, how is the side length affected?
qs.s: Since \(V = s^3\), multiplying the volume by 27 gives a new side length of \(\sqrt[3]{27}s = 3s\). Therefore, the side length is multiplied by 3.

qs.q: The volume of a cone whose height equals its radius has the formula \(V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^3\). If the volume is multiplied by 125, how is the radius affected?
qs.s: Since \(V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^3\), multiplying the volume by 125 gives a new radius of \(\sqrt[3]{125}r = 5r\). Therefore, the radius is multiplied by 5.

qs.q: The area of an equilateral triangle has the formula \(A = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2\). If the area is multiplied by 36, how is the side length affected?
qs.s: Since \(A = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2\), multiplying the area by 36 gives a new side length of \(\sqrt{36}s = 6s\). Therefore, the side length is multiplied by 6.

qs.q: The area of a square has the formula \(A = s^2\). If the area is multiplied by 49, how is the side length affected?
qs.s: Since \(A = s^2\), multiplying the area by 49 gives a new side length of \(\sqrt{49}s = 7s\). Therefore, the side length is multiplied by 7.

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder whose height equals its radius has the formula \(V = \pi r^3\). If the volume is multiplied by 40, how is the radius affected?
qs.s: Multiplying the volume by 40 means the new radius is \(\sqrt[3]{40}r\). Simplifying gives \(\sqrt[3]{40} = \sqrt[3]{8 \cdot 5} = 2\sqrt[3]{5}\), so the radius is multiplied by \(2\sqrt[3]{5}\).

qs.q: The volume of a square pyramid has the formula \(V = \frac{1}{3}s^2 h\). If the height is multiplied by 5 and the volume is multiplied by 60, how is the base side length \(s\) affected?
qs.s: Setting up the relation gives \(60V = \frac{1}{3}s_{\text{new}}^2(5h)\), so dividing by 5 gives \(s_{\text{new}}^2 = 12s^2\). Thus, \(s_{\text{new}} = \sqrt{12}s = 2\sqrt{3}s\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder has the formula \(V = \pi r^2 h\). If the height is multiplied by 3 and the volume is multiplied by 48, how is the radius affected?
qs.s: Setting up the relation gives \(48V = \pi r_{\text{new}}^2 (3h) = 3\pi r_{\text{new}}^2 h\). Dividing by \(3\pi h\) gives \(r_{\text{new}}^2 = 16r^2\), so \(r_{\text{new}} = \sqrt{16}r = 4r\).

qs.q: The surface area of a cube has the formula \(A = 6s^2\). If the surface area is multiplied by 72, how is the side length affected?
qs.s: Multiplying the surface area by 72 means the new side length is \(\sqrt{72}s\). Simplifying the radical gives \(\sqrt{72} = \sqrt{36 \cdot 2} = 6\sqrt{2}\), so the side length is multiplied by \(6\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cube has the formula \(V = s^3\), and its total surface area has the formula \(A = 6s^2\). If the volume is multiplied by 64, how is the total surface area affected?
qs.s: Multiplying the volume by 64 multiplies the side length by \(\sqrt[3]{64} = 4\). Since the surface area is proportional to \(s^2\), the surface area is multiplied by \(4^2 = 16\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid has a volume of 400 cm³. If the length is five times the width and the height is twice the width, what is the width of the rectangular solid?
qs.s: Letting the width be \(w\), the volume is \(V = (5w)(w)(2w) = 10w^3 = 400\). Solving gives \(w^3 = 40\), so the width is \(w = \sqrt[3]{40} = 2\sqrt[3]{5}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A storage box in the shape of a rectangular solid has a volume of 216 cm³. If the length is three times the width and the height is three times the width, what is the length of the box?
qs.s: The volume is \(V = (3w)(w)(3w) = 9w^3 = 216\), giving \(w^3 = 24\) and width \(w = 2\sqrt[3]{3}\text{ cm}\). Therefore, the length is \(3w = 3(2\sqrt[3]{3}) = 6\sqrt[3]{3}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular wooden block has a volume of 160 cm³. If the length is five times the width and the height is twice the width, what is the height of the block?
qs.s: The volume is \(V = (5w)(w)(2w) = 10w^3 = 160\), so \(w^3 = 16\) and \(w = 2\sqrt[3]{2}\text{ cm}\). The height is \(2w = 2(2\sqrt[3]{2}) = 4\sqrt[3]{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid has a volume of 432 cm³. If the height is twice the width and the length is four times the width, what is the width of the rectangular solid?
qs.s: The volume is given by \(V = (4w)(w)(2w) = 8w^3 = 432\). Dividing by 8 yields \(w^3 = 54\), so the width is \(w = \sqrt[3]{54} = 3\sqrt[3]{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid has a volume of 288 cm³. If the length is twice the width and the height is three times the width, what is the width of the rectangular solid?
qs.s: The volume is \(V = (2w)(w)(3w) = 6w^3 = 288\), which simplifies to \(w^3 = 48\). Taking the cube root gives the width \(w = \sqrt[3]{48} = 2\sqrt[3]{6}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular shipping container has a volume of 1440 m³. The height is three times the width, and the length is four times the height. What is the length of the container?
qs.s: Let the width be \(w\), so \(h = 3w\) and \(l = 4(3w) = 12w\). Then \(V = (12w)(w)(3w) = 36w^3 = 1440\), so \(w^3 = 40\) and \(w = 2\sqrt[3]{5}\text{ m}\), giving a length of \(12w = 24\sqrt[3]{5}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid with a square base has a volume of 3888 cm³. The height of the solid is four times the side length of its base. What is the difference between the height and the side length of the base?
qs.s: Letting the base side be \(s\), \(V = s^2(4s) = 4s^3 = 3888\), so \(s^3 = 972\) and \(s = \sqrt[3]{27 \cdot 36} = 3\sqrt[3]{36}\text{ cm}\). The difference between the height and side length is \(4s - s = 3s = 3(3\sqrt[3]{36}) = 9\sqrt[3]{36}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The base of a rectangular solid has a length that is three times its width. The height of the solid is equal to the perimeter of its base. If the volume of the solid is 1296 cm³, what is the height of the solid?
qs.s: The base perimeter is \(2(3w + w) = 8w\), so \(h = 8w\). Then \(V = (3w)(w)(8w) = 24w^3 = 1296\), giving \(w^3 = 54\) and \(w = 3\sqrt[3]{2}\text{ cm}\), which means the height is \(8w = 24\sqrt[3]{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid has a volume of 540 cm³. The length is five times the width, and the height is twice the width. What is the sum of the lengths of all 12 edges of the solid?
qs.s: From \(V = (5w)(w)(2w) = 10w^3 = 540\), we find \(w^3 = 54\), so \(w = 3\sqrt[3]{2}\text{ cm}\). The sum of all 12 edges is \(4(l + w + h) = 4(5w + w + 2w) = 32w = 32(3\sqrt[3]{2}) = 96\sqrt[3]{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage container has a volume of 3125 cm³. The length is five times the width, and the height is one-half of the length. What is the length of the container?
qs.s: With width \(w\), \(l = 5w\) and \(h = \frac{5}{2}w\), so \(V = (5w)(w)\left(\frac{5}{2}w\right) = \frac{25}{2}w^3 = 3125\). Solving yields \(w^3 = 250\), so \(w = 5\sqrt[3]{2}\text{ cm}\) and \(l = 5w = 25\sqrt[3]{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An octagonal stop sign has sides of length 10 cm. What is the perpendicular distance between two opposite parallel sides of the sign?
qs.s: Each corner right triangle has a hypotenuse of \(10\text{ cm}\), so its legs are \(x = \sqrt{100/2} = 5\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\). The perpendicular distance between opposite sides is \(10 + 2(5\sqrt{2}) = 10 + 10\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A regular octagonal wall mirror has sides of length 12 cm. Find the distance between opposite parallel sides of the mirror.
qs.s: Each corner triangle leg is \(x = \sqrt{144/2} = 6\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\). The distance between opposite parallel sides is \(12 + 2(6\sqrt{2}) = 12 + 12\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A paved patio is constructed in the shape of a regular octagon with each side measuring 8 m. What is the distance between opposite parallel sides of the patio?
qs.s: The legs of the corner isosceles right triangles are \(x = \sqrt{64/2} = 4\sqrt{2}\text{ m}\). Thus, the distance between opposite parallel sides is \(8 + 2(4\sqrt{2}) = 8 + 8\sqrt{2}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A carpenter is building a regular octagonal tabletop where each side measures 6 in. Find the distance between opposite parallel edges of the tabletop.
qs.s: The corner right triangles have legs of length \(x = \sqrt{36/2} = 3\sqrt{2}\text{ in}\). Adding the side and both corner projections gives a total distance of \(6 + 2(3\sqrt{2}) = 6 + 6\sqrt{2}\text{ in}\).

qs.q: Find the distance between the opposite parallel sides of a regular octagon with sides of length 2 cm.
qs.s: The legs of each \(45^\circ\)-\(45^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) corner triangle satisfy \(2x^2 = 2^2\), giving \(x = \sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\). The total distance between opposite parallel sides is \(s + 2x = 2 + 2\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A regular octagonal plate with side length 4 cm fits snugly inside a square box such that each side of the box touches one side of the octagon. Find the exact area of the base of the square box.
qs.s: The side of the square box equals the span of the octagon, \(W = 4 + 4\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\). The area of the base is \(W^2 = (4 + 4\sqrt{2})^2 = 16 + 32\sqrt{2} + 32 = 48 + 32\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A regular octagon is formed by cutting four identical isosceles right triangles from the corners of a square. If the area of each cut corner triangle is \(8\text{ cm}^2\), find the distance between opposite parallel sides of the octagon.
qs.s: Each corner triangle has area \(\frac{1}{2}x^2 = 8\), so \(x = 4\text{ cm}\), and the octagon's side length is \(s = \sqrt{4^2 + 4^2} = 4\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\). The distance between opposite parallel sides is \(s + 2x = 4\sqrt{2} + 2(4) = 8 + 4\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Find the distance between the opposite parallel sides of a regular octagon with sides of length \(3\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The corner triangle legs satisfy \(2x^2 = (3\sqrt{2})^2 = 18\), which gives \(x = 3\text{ cm}\). The distance between opposite sides is \(s + 2x = 3\sqrt{2} + 2(3) = 6 + 3\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Find the exact area of a regular octagon with sides of length 6 cm.
qs.s: The enclosing square has side \(6 + 6\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\) and area \((6 + 6\sqrt{2})^2 = 108 + 72\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}^2\). Subtracting the four cut corner triangles, each with area \(\frac{1}{2}(3\sqrt{2})^2 = 9\text{ cm}^2\), yields \((108 + 72\sqrt{2}) - 36 = 72 + 72\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A regular octagonal garden has a perimeter of 48 m. Find the distance between two opposite parallel sides of the garden.
qs.s: Each side of the octagon is \(s = 48 / 8 = 6\text{ m}\). The corner right triangles have legs \(x = \sqrt{36/2} = 3\sqrt{2}\text{ m}\), so the distance between parallel sides is \(6 + 2(3\sqrt{2}) = 6 + 6\sqrt{2}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A cube-shaped storage box has edge lengths of 8 cm. What is the length of the diagonal connecting two opposite corners of the box?
qs.s: The space diagonal of a cube is given by \(d = \sqrt{s^2 + s^2 + s^2} = s\sqrt{3}\). For \(s = 8\text{ cm}\), the diagonal length is \(8\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: What is the length of the diagonal that connects two opposite corners of a cube with sides 6 cm?
qs.s: The length of the space diagonal of a cube with side length \(s\) is \(d = \sqrt{s^2 + s^2 + s^2} = s\sqrt{3}\). Substituting \(s = 6\text{ cm}\) yields \(6\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: What is the length of the diagonal connecting two opposite corners of a rectangular prism with dimensions 2 cm by 4 cm by 6 cm?
qs.s: The diagonal is \(d = \sqrt{2^2 + 4^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{4 + 16 + 36} = \sqrt{56}\text{ cm}\). Simplifying \(\sqrt{56} = \sqrt{4 \cdot 14}\) gives \(2\sqrt{14}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: What is the length of the diagonal that connects two opposite corners of a cube with sides 10 m?
qs.s: The diagonal connecting opposite corners of a cube is \(d = s\sqrt{3}\). For \(s = 10\text{ m}\), the length of the diagonal is \(10\sqrt{3}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: What is the length of the interior diagonal connecting two opposite corners of a rectangular box with length 3 cm, width 4 cm, and height 5 cm?
qs.s: The interior diagonal is \(d = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2 + 5^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16 + 25} = \sqrt{50}\text{ cm}\). Simplifying the radical gives \(\sqrt{25 \cdot 2} = 5\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular shipping crate has a length of \(2\sqrt{2}\text{ m}\), a width of \(3\sqrt{3}\text{ m}\), and a height of \(\sqrt{5}\text{ m}\). What is the length of the diagonal connecting two opposite corners of the crate?
qs.s: The interior diagonal is \(d = \sqrt{(2\sqrt{2})^2 + (3\sqrt{3})^2 + (\sqrt{5})^2} = \sqrt{8 + 27 + 5} = \sqrt{40}\text{ m}\). Simplifying \(\sqrt{40} = \sqrt{4 \cdot 10}\) gives \(2\sqrt{10}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular box has a length of 6 cm and a width of 4 cm. If the diagonal connecting two opposite corners of the box is 10 cm, what is the height of the box?
qs.s: Using \(l^2 + w^2 + h^2 = d^2\), we have \(6^2 + 4^2 + h^2 = 10^2\), which simplifies to \(52 + h^2 = 100\). Thus \(h = \sqrt{48} = 4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The total surface area of a cube is \(120\text{ cm}^2\). What is the length of the diagonal that connects two opposite corners of the cube?
qs.s: The surface area of a cube is \(6s^2 = 120\), giving \(s^2 = 20\). The space diagonal is \(d = \sqrt{3s^2} = \sqrt{3 \cdot 20} = \sqrt{60} = 2\sqrt{15}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The diagonal connecting two opposite corners of a cube is 15 cm. What is the side length of the cube?
qs.s: For a cube of side length \(s\), the space diagonal satisfies \(3s^2 = 15^2 = 225\). Dividing by 3 gives \(s^2 = 75\), so \(s = \sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The diagonal connecting two opposite corners of a cube has a length of 9 cm. What is the length of the diagonal across one of its faces?
qs.s: Since the space diagonal is \(s\sqrt{3} = 9\text{ cm}\), we have \(s^2 = \frac{81}{3} = 27\). The face diagonal is \(\sqrt{2s^2} = \sqrt{2 \cdot 27} = \sqrt{54} = 3\sqrt{6}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: What is the length of the diagonal of a rectangular solid with lengths 2 cm, 5 cm, and 5 cm?
qs.s: The diagonal is given by \(d = \sqrt{2^2 + 5^2 + 5^2} = \sqrt{4 + 25 + 25} = \sqrt{54}\). Simplifying the radical gives \(\sqrt{9 \cdot 6} = 3\sqrt{6}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: What is the length of the diagonal of a rectangular crate measuring 3 m by 5 m by 8 m?
qs.s: The diagonal is given by \(d = \sqrt{3^2 + 5^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{9 + 25 + 64} = \sqrt{98}\). Simplifying the radical gives \(\sqrt{49 \cdot 2} = 7\sqrt{2}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Find the length of the diagonal of a rectangular prism with lengths 4 cm, 4 cm, and 6 cm.
qs.s: The diagonal is given by \(d = \sqrt{4^2 + 4^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{16 + 16 + 36} = \sqrt{68}\). Simplifying the radical gives \(\sqrt{4 \cdot 17} = 2\sqrt{17}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular box has dimensions 1 cm by 5 cm by 7 cm. What is the length of the diagonal of the box?
qs.s: The diagonal is given by \(d = \sqrt{1^2 + 5^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{1 + 25 + 49} = \sqrt{75}\). Simplifying the radical gives \(\sqrt{25 \cdot 3} = 5\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Find the length of the diagonal of a rectangular solid with dimensions 2 cm, 4 cm, and 6 cm.
qs.s: The diagonal is given by \(d = \sqrt{2^2 + 4^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{4 + 16 + 36} = \sqrt{56}\). Simplifying the radical gives \(\sqrt{4 \cdot 14} = 2\sqrt{14}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Find the length of the diagonal of a rectangular solid with length \(2\sqrt{6}\text{ cm}\), width \(\sqrt{21}\text{ cm}\), and height \(\sqrt{35}\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The diagonal is \(d = \sqrt{(2\sqrt{6})^2 + (\sqrt{21})^2 + (\sqrt{35})^2} = \sqrt{24 + 21 + 35} = \sqrt{80}\). Simplifying gives \(\sqrt{16 \cdot 5} = 4\sqrt{5}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage room has a length of 12 m, a width of 16 m, and a height of 24 m. What is the length of the diagonal connecting two opposite corners of the room?
qs.s: The diagonal is \(d = \sqrt{12^2 + 16^2 + 24^2} = \sqrt{144 + 256 + 576} = \sqrt{976}\). Factoring out the largest perfect square yields \(\sqrt{16 \cdot 61} = 4\sqrt{61}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A cube has an edge length of \(3\sqrt{6}\text{ cm}\). What is the length of its interior diagonal?
qs.s: The interior diagonal of a cube with edge \(s\) is \(d = \sqrt{s^2 + s^2 + s^2} = s\sqrt{3}\). Substituting \(s = 3\sqrt{6}\text{ cm}\) gives \(d = 3\sqrt{6} \cdot \sqrt{3} = 3\sqrt{18} = 9\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular box has a square base. The height of the box is 9 cm, and the interior diagonal is \(3\sqrt{19}\text{ cm}\). What is the side length of the square base?
qs.s: Letting \(s\) be the side length of the base, \(s^2 + s^2 + 9^2 = (3\sqrt{19})^2\), which simplifies to \(2s^2 + 81 = 171\). Solving gives \(2s^2 = 90\), so \(s = \sqrt{45} = 3\sqrt{5}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid has a length of 6 cm, a width of 4 cm, and an interior diagonal of \(2\sqrt{26}\text{ cm}\). What is the height of the solid?
One isosceles triangular garden bed has sides 10 m, 10 m, and 12 m. Another isosceles triangular garden bed has sides 10 m, 10 m, and 16 m. Which garden bed has the greatest area?
qs.a: Both garden beds have the same area of 48 m\(^2\)
d: The garden bed with base 16 m, with an area of 96 m\(^2\)
The garden bed with base 12 m, with an area of 60 m\(^2\)
The garden bed with base 16 m, with an area of 64 m\(^2\)
qs.s: The height of the first bed is \(\sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = 8\text{ m}\), giving an area of \(\frac{1}{2}(12)(8) = 48\text{ m}^2\). The height of the second bed is \(\sqrt{10^2 - 8^2} = 6\text{ m}\), giving an area of \(\frac{1}{2}(16)(6) = 48\text{ m}^2\), so both areas are equal.

qs.q: One isosceles triangular sign has sides 15 cm, 15 cm, and 18 cm. Another isosceles triangular sign has sides 13 cm, 13 cm, and 10 cm. Which sign has the greatest area?
qs.a: The sign with sides 15 cm, 15 cm, and 18 cm, with an area of 108 cm\(^2\)
d: The sign with sides 13 cm, 13 cm, and 10 cm, with an area of 60 cm\(^2\)
Both signs have the same area of 108 cm\(^2\)
The sign with sides 15 cm, 15 cm, and 18 cm, with an area of 216 cm\(^2\)
qs.s: The first sign has height \(\sqrt{15^2 - 9^2} = 12\text{ cm}\) and area \(\frac{1}{2}(18)(12) = 108\text{ cm}^2\). The second sign has height \(\sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = 12\text{ cm}\) and area \(\frac{1}{2}(10)(12) = 60\text{ cm}^2\), so the first sign has the greatest area.

qs.q: One isosceles triangular sail has sides 20 m, 20 m, and 24 m. Another isosceles triangular sail has sides 20 m, 20 m, and 32 m. Which sail has the greatest area?
qs.a: Both sails have the same area of 192 m\(^2\)
d: The sail with base 32 m, with an area of 384 m\(^2\)
The sail with base 24 m, with an area of 240 m\(^2\)
The sail with base 32 m, with an area of 256 m\(^2\)
qs.s: The first sail has height \(\sqrt{20^2 - 12^2} = 16\text{ m}\) and area \(\frac{1}{2}(24)(16) = 192\text{ m}^2\). The second sail has height \(\sqrt{20^2 - 16^2} = 12\text{ m}\) and area \(\frac{1}{2}(32)(12) = 192\text{ m}^2\), so both sails have the same area.

qs.q: One isosceles triangular roof truss has sides 17 ft, 17 ft, and 16 ft. Another isosceles triangular roof truss has sides 17 ft, 17 ft, and 30 ft. Which roof truss encloses the greatest area?
qs.a: Both roof trusses have the same area of 120 ft\(^2\)
d: The truss with base 30 ft, with an area of 240 ft\(^2\)
The truss with base 16 ft, with an area of 136 ft\(^2\)
The truss with base 30 ft, with an area of 128 ft\(^2\)
qs.s: The first truss has height \(\sqrt{17^2 - 8^2} = 15\text{ ft}\) and area \(\frac{1}{2}(16)(15) = 120\text{ ft}^2\). The second truss has height \(\sqrt{17^2 - 15^2} = 8\text{ ft}\) and area \(\frac{1}{2}(30)(8) = 120\text{ ft}^2\), meaning both enclose the exact same area.

qs.q: One isosceles triangular pennant has sides 13 cm, 13 cm, and 10 cm. Another isosceles triangular pennant has sides 13 cm, 13 cm, and 24 cm. Which pennant has the greatest area?
qs.a: Both pennants have the same area of 60 cm\(^2\)
d: The pennant with base 24 cm, with an area of 120 cm\(^2\)
The pennant with base 10 cm, with an area of 65 cm\(^2\)
The pennant with base 24 cm, with an area of 72 cm\(^2\)
qs.s: The first pennant has height \(\sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = 12\text{ cm}\) and area \(\frac{1}{2}(10)(12) = 60\text{ cm}^2\). The second pennant has height \(\sqrt{13^2 - 12^2} = 5\text{ cm}\) and area \(\frac{1}{2}(24)(5) = 60\text{ cm}^2\), so both pennants have the same area.

qs.q: Field A is an isosceles triangle with sides 65 m, 65 m, and 50 m. Field B is an isosceles triangle with sides 65 m, 65 m, and 78 m. Which field has the greatest area?
qs.a: Field B, with an area of 2028 m\(^2\)
d: Field A, with an area of 1500 m\(^2\)
Both fields have the same area of 1500 m\(^2\)
Field B, with an area of 4056 m\(^2\)
