qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(3(6\sqrt{3}) - 2(4\sqrt{3}) - 4(3\sqrt{3}) = 18\sqrt{3} - 8\sqrt{3} - 12\sqrt{3}\). Combining the coefficients yields \(-2\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt{200} - 4\sqrt{98} + 2\sqrt{162}\)
qs.s: Factor out the largest perfect squares: \(3(10\sqrt{2}) - 4(7\sqrt{2}) + 2(9\sqrt{2}) = 30\sqrt{2} - 28\sqrt{2} + 18\sqrt{2}\). Combining coefficients gives \(20\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{72} - \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{32} + \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{128}\)
qs.s: Simplify the radicals and multiply by the fractions: \(\frac{2}{3}(6\sqrt{2}) - \frac{3}{4}(4\sqrt{2}) + \frac{1}{2}(8\sqrt{2}) = 4\sqrt{2} - 3\sqrt{2} + 4\sqrt{2} = 5\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt{12} - 2\sqrt{75} + \sqrt{147} - \sqrt{48}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(3(2\sqrt{3}) - 2(5\sqrt{3}) + 7\sqrt{3} - 4\sqrt{3} = 6\sqrt{3} - 10\sqrt{3} + 7\sqrt{3} - 4\sqrt{3}\). Combining like terms gives \(-\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(2\sqrt{63} - 4\sqrt{28} + 3\sqrt{112}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(2(3\sqrt{7}) - 4(2\sqrt{7}) + 3(4\sqrt{7}) = 6\sqrt{7} - 8\sqrt{7} + 12\sqrt{7}\). Combining coefficients gives \((6 - 8 + 12)\sqrt{7} = 10\sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(5\sqrt{18} - 2\sqrt{50} + 3\sqrt{8}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(5(3\sqrt{2}) - 2(5\sqrt{2}) + 3(2\sqrt{2}) = 15\sqrt{2} - 10\sqrt{2} + 6\sqrt{2}\). Combining like terms yields \(11\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(4\sqrt{24} - \sqrt{54} - 2\sqrt{96}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(4(2\sqrt{6}) - 3\sqrt{6} - 2(4\sqrt{6}) = 8\sqrt{6} - 3\sqrt{6} - 8\sqrt{6}\). Combining like terms results in \(-3\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(2\sqrt{48} - 5\sqrt{12} + 4\sqrt{27}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(2(4\sqrt{3}) - 5(2\sqrt{3}) + 4(3\sqrt{3}) = 8\sqrt{3} - 10\sqrt{3} + 12\sqrt{3}\). Combining like terms gives \(10\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt{20} + 2\sqrt{45} - \sqrt{80}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(3(2\sqrt{5}) + 2(3\sqrt{5}) - 4\sqrt{5} = 6\sqrt{5} + 6\sqrt{5} - 4\sqrt{5}\). Combining like terms gives \(8\sqrt{5}\).

Factor out perfect cubes: \(2(-2\sqrt[3]{3}) + 3(3\sqrt[3]{3}) - 4\sqrt[3]{3} = -4\sqrt[3]{3} + 9\sqrt[3]{3} - 4\sqrt[3]{3}\). Combining like terms results in \((-4 + 9 - 4)\sqrt[3]{3} = \sqrt[3]{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt{18} - 2\sqrt{48} + \sqrt{50} - 4\sqrt{12}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(3(3\sqrt{2}) - 2(4\sqrt{3}) + 5\sqrt{2} - 4(2\sqrt{3}) = 9\sqrt{2} - 8\sqrt{3} + 5\sqrt{2} - 8\sqrt{3}\). Combine like radicals to get \(14\sqrt{2} - 16\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt{150} - 2\sqrt{216} + 4\sqrt{96} - \sqrt{384}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(3(5\sqrt{6}) - 2(6\sqrt{6}) + 4(4\sqrt{6}) - 8\sqrt{6} = 15\sqrt{6} - 12\sqrt{6} + 16\sqrt{6} - 8\sqrt{6}\). Combining terms gives \((15 - 12 + 16 - 8)\sqrt{6} = 11\sqrt{6}\).
Factor out perfect cubes: \(2(3\sqrt[3]{2}) - 5(2\sqrt[3]{2}) + 3(4\sqrt[3]{2}) = 6\sqrt[3]{2} - 10\sqrt[3]{2} + 12\sqrt[3]{2}\). Combining like radicals gives \(8\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{72} + \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{162} - \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{32}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(\frac{1}{2}(6\sqrt{2}) + \frac{2}{3}(9\sqrt{2}) - \frac{3}{4}(4\sqrt{2}) = 3\sqrt{2} + 6\sqrt{2} - 3\sqrt{2}\). Combining like terms gives \(6\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt{28} - 5\sqrt{63} + 2\sqrt{112}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(3(2\sqrt{7}) - 5(3\sqrt{7}) + 2(4\sqrt{7}) = 6\sqrt{7} - 15\sqrt{7} + 8\sqrt{7}\). Combining like terms gives \(-\sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt{80} - 2\sqrt{45} - 4\sqrt{20}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(3(4\sqrt{5}) - 2(3\sqrt{5}) - 4(2\sqrt{5}) = 12\sqrt{5} - 6\sqrt{5} - 8\sqrt{5}\). Combining like terms yields \(-2\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(6\sqrt{8} + 3\sqrt{32} - 2\sqrt{98}\)
qs.s: Factoring out perfect squares gives \(6(2\sqrt{2}) + 3(4\sqrt{2}) - 2(7\sqrt{2}) = 12\sqrt{2} + 12\sqrt{2} - 14\sqrt{2}\). Combining like terms results in \(10\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(4\sqrt{27} - 2\sqrt{75} + 3\sqrt{48}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(4(3\sqrt{3}) - 2(5\sqrt{3}) + 3(4\sqrt{3}) = 12\sqrt{3} - 10\sqrt{3} + 12\sqrt{3}\). Combining like terms gives \(14\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(4\sqrt{40} - \sqrt{90} - 2\sqrt{250}\)
qs.s: Factoring out perfect squares yields \(4(2\sqrt{10}) - 3\sqrt{10} - 2(5\sqrt{10}) = 8\sqrt{10} - 3\sqrt{10} - 10\sqrt{10}\). Combining like terms gives \(-5\sqrt{10}\).
Factor out perfect cubes to obtain \(3(3\sqrt[3]{2}) - 2(2\sqrt[3]{2}) + 4(5\sqrt[3]{2}) = 9\sqrt[3]{2} - 4\sqrt[3]{2} + 20\sqrt[3]{2}\). Combining like terms gives \(25\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt{200} - 2\sqrt{288} + \sqrt{450} - \sqrt{98}\)
qs.s: Factor the large radicands to get \(3(10\sqrt{2}) - 2(12\sqrt{2}) + 15\sqrt{2} - 7\sqrt{2} = 30\sqrt{2} - 24\sqrt{2} + 15\sqrt{2} - 7\sqrt{2}\). Combining like terms gives \(14\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(2\sqrt{48} - 3\sqrt{50} + \sqrt{108} - 2\sqrt{18}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(2(4\sqrt{3}) - 3(5\sqrt{2}) + 6\sqrt{3} - 2(3\sqrt{2}) = 8\sqrt{3} - 15\sqrt{2} + 6\sqrt{3} - 6\sqrt{2}\). Grouping like radicals gives \(14\sqrt{3} - 21\sqrt{2}\).
Factor out perfect cubes, noting \(\sqrt[3]{-54} = -3\sqrt[3]{2}\), giving \(2(-3\sqrt[3]{2}) + 4(4\sqrt[3]{2}) - 5\sqrt[3]{2} = -6\sqrt[3]{2} + 16\sqrt[3]{2} - 5\sqrt[3]{2} = 5\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{54} - \frac{5}{2}\sqrt{24} + 3\sqrt{96}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(\frac{2}{3}(3\sqrt{6}) - \frac{5}{2}(2\sqrt{6}) + 3(4\sqrt{6}) = 2\sqrt{6} - 5\sqrt{6} + 12\sqrt{6}\). Combining like terms yields \(9\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt{18} - 2\sqrt{75} + 4\sqrt{12}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(3(3\sqrt{2}) - 2(5\sqrt{3}) + 4(2\sqrt{3}) = 9\sqrt{2} - 10\sqrt{3} + 8\sqrt{3}\). Combining like radicals yields \(9\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(5\sqrt{27} - 2\sqrt{48} + 3\sqrt{80}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(5(3\sqrt{3}) - 2(4\sqrt{3}) + 3(4\sqrt{5}) = 15\sqrt{3} - 8\sqrt{3} + 12\sqrt{5}\). Combining the \(\sqrt{3}\) terms gives \(7\sqrt{3} + 12\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(4\sqrt{28} - 2\sqrt{98} + 3\sqrt{63}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \(4(2\sqrt{7}) - 2(7\sqrt{2}) + 3(3\sqrt{7}) = 8\sqrt{7} - 14\sqrt{2} + 9\sqrt{7}\). Combining like radicals gives \(17\sqrt{7} - 14\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt{32} + 2\sqrt{45} - 5\sqrt{20}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(3(4\sqrt{2}) + 2(3\sqrt{5}) - 5(2\sqrt{5}) = 12\sqrt{2} + 6\sqrt{5} - 10\sqrt{5}\). Combining like radicals gives \(12\sqrt{2} - 4\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(5\sqrt{24} + 2\sqrt{45} - 2\sqrt{54}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(5(2\sqrt{6}) + 2(3\sqrt{5}) - 2(3\sqrt{6}) = 10\sqrt{6} + 6\sqrt{5} - 6\sqrt{6}\). Combining the \(\sqrt{6}\) terms gives \(4\sqrt{6} + 6\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt{200} - 2\sqrt{147} - \sqrt{288} + 5\sqrt{75}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(3(10\sqrt{2}) - 2(7\sqrt{3}) - 12\sqrt{2} + 5(5\sqrt{3}) = 30\sqrt{2} - 14\sqrt{3} - 12\sqrt{2} + 25\sqrt{3}\). Combining like terms gives \((30 - 12)\sqrt{2} + (-14 + 25)\sqrt{3} = 18\sqrt{2} + 11\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(2\sqrt{180} - \sqrt{252} - 3\sqrt{45} + 2\sqrt{112}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(2(6\sqrt{5}) - 6\sqrt{7} - 3(3\sqrt{5}) + 2(4\sqrt{7}) = 12\sqrt{5} - 6\sqrt{7} - 9\sqrt{5} + 8\sqrt{7}\). Combining like radicals gives \((12 - 9)\sqrt{5} + (-6 + 8)\sqrt{7} = 3\sqrt{5} + 2\sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(2\sqrt{108} - 3\sqrt{98} - \sqrt{48} + 2\sqrt{50}\)
qs.s: Factor perfect squares to get \(2(6\sqrt{3}) - 3(7\sqrt{2}) - 4\sqrt{3} + 2(5\sqrt{2}) = 12\sqrt{3} - 21\sqrt{2} - 4\sqrt{3} + 10\sqrt{2}\). Combining like terms gives \((12 - 4)\sqrt{3} + (-21 + 10)\sqrt{2} = 8\sqrt{3} - 11\sqrt{2}\).
Factor perfect cubes: \(5(2\sqrt[3]{3}) + 3(2\sqrt[3]{2}) - 2(3\sqrt[3]{3}) = 10\sqrt[3]{3} + 6\sqrt[3]{2} - 6\sqrt[3]{3}\). Combining like terms results in \(4\sqrt[3]{3} + 6\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{3}{5}\sqrt{500} - \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{108} + \frac{1}{4}\sqrt{80}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(\frac{3}{5}(10\sqrt{5}) - \frac{2}{3}(6\sqrt{3}) + \frac{1}{4}(4\sqrt{5}) = 6\sqrt{5} - 4\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{5}\). Combining the \(\sqrt{5}\) terms yields \(7\sqrt{5} - 4\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(6\sqrt{24} - 2\sqrt{54} + 5\sqrt{40}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(6(2\sqrt{6}) - 2(3\sqrt{6}) + 5(2\sqrt{10}) = 12\sqrt{6} - 6\sqrt{6} + 10\sqrt{10}\). Combine like terms: \((12 - 6)\sqrt{6} + 10\sqrt{10} = 6\sqrt{6} + 10\sqrt{10}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt{75} - 2\sqrt{45} + 4\sqrt{12}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(3(5\sqrt{3}) - 2(3\sqrt{5}) + 4(2\sqrt{3}) = 15\sqrt{3} - 6\sqrt{5} + 8\sqrt{3}\). Combine the like terms: \((15 + 8)\sqrt{3} - 6\sqrt{5} = 23\sqrt{3} - 6\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(2\sqrt{98} - 5\sqrt{32} + 3\sqrt{20}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(2(7\sqrt{2}) - 5(4\sqrt{2}) + 3(2\sqrt{5}) = 14\sqrt{2} - 20\sqrt{2} + 6\sqrt{5}\). Combine the like radical terms: \((14 - 20)\sqrt{2} + 6\sqrt{5} = -6\sqrt{2} + 6\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt{63} - 4\sqrt{28} + 2\sqrt{44}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(3(3\sqrt{7}) - 4(2\sqrt{7}) + 2(2\sqrt{11}) = 9\sqrt{7} - 8\sqrt{7} + 4\sqrt{11}\). Combine the like terms: \((9 - 8)\sqrt{7} + 4\sqrt{11} = \sqrt{7} + 4\sqrt{11}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(4\sqrt{50} - 2\sqrt{27} - 3\sqrt{18}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(4(5\sqrt{2}) - 2(3\sqrt{3}) - 3(3\sqrt{2}) = 20\sqrt{2} - 6\sqrt{3} - 9\sqrt{2}\). Combine the like radical terms: \((20 - 9)\sqrt{2} - 6\sqrt{3} = 11\sqrt{2} - 6\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{48} - \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{54} + \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{192}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(\frac{3}{4}(4\sqrt{3}) - \frac{2}{3}(3\sqrt{6}) + \frac{1}{2}(8\sqrt{3}) = 3\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{6} + 4\sqrt{3}\). Combine the \(\sqrt{3}\) terms to get \(7\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt{180} - 2\sqrt{112} - \sqrt{405} + 5\sqrt{63}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(3(6\sqrt{5}) - 2(4\sqrt{7}) - 9\sqrt{5} + 5(3\sqrt{7}) = 18\sqrt{5} - 8\sqrt{7} - 9\sqrt{5} + 15\sqrt{7}\). Combine like terms: \((18 - 9)\sqrt{5} + (-8 + 15)\sqrt{7} = 9\sqrt{5} + 7\sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{45} + \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{96} - \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{80} - \frac{1}{5}\sqrt{150}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(\frac{2}{3}(3\sqrt{5}) + \frac{3}{4}(4\sqrt{6}) - \frac{1}{2}(4\sqrt{5}) - \frac{1}{5}(5\sqrt{6}) = 2\sqrt{5} + 3\sqrt{6} - 2\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{6}\). Combining like terms yields \((2 - 2)\sqrt{5} + (3 - 1)\sqrt{6} = 2\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(2\sqrt{200} - 4\sqrt{108} + 3\sqrt{98} - \sqrt{288}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(2(10\sqrt{2}) - 4(6\sqrt{3}) + 3(7\sqrt{2}) - 12\sqrt{2} = 20\sqrt{2} - 24\sqrt{3} + 21\sqrt{2} - 12\sqrt{2}\). Combine the \(\sqrt{2}\) terms: \((20 + 21 - 12)\sqrt{2} - 24\sqrt{3} = 29\sqrt{2} - 24\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(4\sqrt{75} - 3\sqrt{125} + 2\sqrt{300} - \sqrt{500}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(4(5\sqrt{3}) - 3(5\sqrt{5}) + 2(10\sqrt{3}) - 10\sqrt{5} = 20\sqrt{3} - 15\sqrt{5} + 20\sqrt{3} - 10\sqrt{5}\). Combine like terms: \((20 + 20)\sqrt{3} + (-15 - 10)\sqrt{5} = 40\sqrt{3} - 25\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\sqrt{12} - \sqrt{27} + \sqrt{63} - \sqrt{28}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to \(2\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{7} - 2\sqrt{7}\). Combining like radicals results in \(-\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{7}\), or \(\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\sqrt{72} - \sqrt{18} + \sqrt{45} - \sqrt{80}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(6\sqrt{2} - 3\sqrt{2} + 3\sqrt{5} - 4\sqrt{5}\). Combining like terms yields \(3\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\sqrt{98} - \sqrt{32} + \sqrt{48} - \sqrt{147}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(7\sqrt{2} - 4\sqrt{2} + 4\sqrt{3} - 7\sqrt{3}\). Combining like radicals gives \((7 - 4)\sqrt{2} + (4 - 7)\sqrt{3} = 3\sqrt{2} - 3\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\sqrt{200} - \sqrt{72} - \sqrt{125} + \sqrt{45}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to \(10\sqrt{2} - 6\sqrt{2} - 5\sqrt{5} + 3\sqrt{5}\). Combining like radicals gives \(4\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\sqrt{54} - \sqrt{24} + \sqrt{90} - \sqrt{40}\)
qs.s: Factor out perfect squares to obtain \(3\sqrt{6} - 2\sqrt{6} + 3\sqrt{10} - 2\sqrt{10}\). Combining like radicals gives \(\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{10}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{72} - \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{108} + \frac{3}{5}\sqrt{200} - \frac{1}{4}\sqrt{48}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(\frac{1}{2}(6\sqrt{2}) - \frac{2}{3}(6\sqrt{3}) + \frac{3}{5}(10\sqrt{2}) - \frac{1}{4}(4\sqrt{3}) = 3\sqrt{2} - 4\sqrt{3} + 6\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{3}\). Combining like terms gives \(9\sqrt{2} - 5\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\sqrt{288} - \sqrt{128} + \sqrt{300} - \sqrt{147} - \sqrt{72}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical yields \(12\sqrt{2} - 8\sqrt{2} + 10\sqrt{3} - 7\sqrt{3} - 6\sqrt{2}\). Combining like terms gives \((12 - 8 - 6)\sqrt{2} + (10 - 7)\sqrt{3} = -2\sqrt{2} + 3\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(4\sqrt{98} - 2\sqrt{243} + 3\sqrt{162} - \sqrt{363}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(4(7\sqrt{2}) - 2(9\sqrt{3}) + 3(9\sqrt{2}) - 11\sqrt{3} = 28\sqrt{2} - 18\sqrt{3} + 27\sqrt{2} - 11\sqrt{3}\). Combining like radicals yields \(55\sqrt{2} - 29\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\sqrt[3]{250} - \sqrt[3]{375} - \sqrt[3]{54} + \sqrt[3]{192}\)
qs.s: Factoring out perfect cubes gives \(5\sqrt[3]{2} - 5\sqrt[3]{3} - 3\sqrt[3]{2} + 4\sqrt[3]{3}\). Combining like radicals results in \((5 - 3)\sqrt[3]{2} + (-5 + 4)\sqrt[3]{3} = 2\sqrt[3]{2} - \sqrt[3]{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(2\sqrt{180} - 3\sqrt{112} - \sqrt{405} + 2\sqrt{252}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(2(6\sqrt{5}) - 3(4\sqrt{7}) - 9\sqrt{5} + 2(6\sqrt{7}) = 12\sqrt{5} - 12\sqrt{7} - 9\sqrt{5} + 12\sqrt{7}\). The \(\sqrt{7}\) terms cancel out, leaving \(3\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\sqrt{20} + \sqrt{45} - \sqrt{24} + \sqrt{54}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(2\sqrt{5} + 3\sqrt{5} - 2\sqrt{6} + 3\sqrt{6}\). Combining like terms gives \((2\sqrt{5} + 3\sqrt{5}) + (-2\sqrt{6} + 3\sqrt{6}) = 5\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\sqrt{72} - \sqrt{40} + \sqrt{90} - \sqrt{50}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(\sqrt{72} = 6\sqrt{2}\), \(\sqrt{40} = 2\sqrt{10}\), \(\sqrt{90} = 3\sqrt{10}\), and \(\sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}\). Combining like radicals gives \((6\sqrt{2} - 5\sqrt{2}) + (-2\sqrt{10} + 3\sqrt{10}) = \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{10}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\sqrt{28} + \sqrt{98} - \sqrt{63} - \sqrt{18}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(2\sqrt{7} + 7\sqrt{2} - 3\sqrt{7} - 3\sqrt{2}\). Grouping like radicals yields \((7\sqrt{2} - 3\sqrt{2}) + (2\sqrt{7} - 3\sqrt{7}) = 4\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\sqrt{75} - \sqrt{18} - \sqrt{12} + \sqrt{50}\)
qs.s: Write each radical in simplest form: \(\sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3}\), \(\sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}\), \(\sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}\), and \(\sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}\). Combining like terms gives \((5\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{3}) + (-3\sqrt{2} + 5\sqrt{2}) = 3\sqrt{3} + 2\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\sqrt{80} - \sqrt{108} - \sqrt{45} + \sqrt{48}\)
qs.s: Express each term in simplest radical form: \(4\sqrt{5} - 6\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{5} + 4\sqrt{3}\). Combine like terms to obtain \((4\sqrt{5} - 3\sqrt{5}) + (-6\sqrt{3} + 4\sqrt{3}) = \sqrt{5} - 2\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(3\sqrt{180} - 2\sqrt{112} - 4\sqrt{45} + 3\sqrt{63}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical term: \(3(6\sqrt{5}) - 2(4\sqrt{7}) - 4(3\sqrt{5}) + 3(3\sqrt{7}) = 18\sqrt{5} - 8\sqrt{7} - 12\sqrt{5} + 9\sqrt{7}\). Combining like terms gives \(6\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{48} - \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{27} + \frac{3}{5}\sqrt{75} - \frac{1}{4}\sqrt{192}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term by factoring out perfect squares: \(\frac{1}{2}(4\sqrt{3}) - \frac{2}{3}(3\sqrt{3}) + \frac{3}{5}(5\sqrt{3}) - \frac{1}{4}(8\sqrt{3}) = 2\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{3}\). Combining like terms yields \(\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(3\sqrt[3]{40} + 2\sqrt[3]{54} - \sqrt[3]{135} - 4\sqrt[3]{16}\)
qs.s: Factor out perfect cubes: \(3(2\sqrt[3]{5}) + 2(3\sqrt[3]{2}) - 3\sqrt[3]{5} - 4(2\sqrt[3]{2}) = 6\sqrt[3]{5} + 6\sqrt[3]{2} - 3\sqrt[3]{5} - 8\sqrt[3]{2}\). Combining like radicals gives \(3\sqrt[3]{5} - 2\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\sqrt[3]{128} + \sqrt[3]{81} - \sqrt[3]{250} - \sqrt[3]{24}\)
qs.s: Factor out perfect cubes from each radical: \(4\sqrt[3]{2} + 3\sqrt[3]{3} - 5\sqrt[3]{2} - 2\sqrt[3]{3}\). Combining like terms results in \((3 - 2)\sqrt[3]{3} + (4 - 5)\sqrt[3]{2} = \sqrt[3]{3} - \sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\sqrt{200} - \sqrt{147} - \sqrt{72} + \sqrt{192} - \sqrt{98}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \(10\sqrt{2} - 7\sqrt{3} - 6\sqrt{2} + 8\sqrt{3} - 7\sqrt{2}\). Grouping like radicals gives \((10 - 6 - 7)\sqrt{2} + (-7 + 8)\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{160} - \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{40} + \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{90}\)
qs.s: Factor out perfect squares from each radical: \(\frac{3}{4}(4\sqrt{10}) - \frac{1}{2}(2\sqrt{10}) + \frac{2}{3}(3\sqrt{10}) = 3\sqrt{10} - \sqrt{10} + 2\sqrt{10}\). Combining like terms gives \(4\sqrt{10}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{28} - \frac{1}{3}\sqrt{63} + \frac{1}{4}\sqrt{112}\)
qs.s: Rewrite each radical in simplest form: \(\frac{3}{2}(2\sqrt{7}) - \frac{1}{3}(3\sqrt{7}) + \frac{1}{4}(4\sqrt{7}) = 3\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{7} + \sqrt{7}\). Combining like terms yields \(3\sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{48} - \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{27} + \frac{3}{5}\sqrt{75}\)
qs.s: Factor each radical into a perfect square and 3 to get \(\frac{1}{2}(4\sqrt{3}) - \frac{2}{3}(3\sqrt{3}) + \frac{3}{5}(5\sqrt{3})\). Simplifying the coefficients gives \(2\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{3} = 3\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{5}{3}\sqrt{18} + \frac{1}{4}\sqrt{32} - \frac{2}{5}\sqrt{50}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical by factoring out perfect squares: \(\frac{5}{3}(3\sqrt{2}) + \frac{1}{4}(4\sqrt{2}) - \frac{2}{5}(5\sqrt{2})\). Combining like terms gives \(5\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{2} = 4\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{24} + \frac{4}{3}\sqrt{54} - \frac{2}{5}\sqrt{150}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(\frac{1}{2}(2\sqrt{6}) + \frac{4}{3}(3\sqrt{6}) - \frac{2}{5}(5\sqrt{6}) = \sqrt{6} + 4\sqrt{6} - 2\sqrt{6}\). Combining like radicals gives \(3\sqrt{6}\).

Factor out perfect cubes from each radical: \(\frac{3}{2}(2\sqrt[3]{2}) + \frac{2}{3}(3\sqrt[3]{2}) - \frac{3}{5}(5\sqrt[3]{2})\). Simplifying and combining like terms yields \(3\sqrt[3]{2} + 2\sqrt[3]{2} - 3\sqrt[3]{2} = 2\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{72} - \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{48} + \frac{3}{8}\sqrt{128} + \frac{4}{5}\sqrt{75}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(2\sqrt{2} - 3\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{2} + 4\sqrt{3}\). Grouping like radicals gives \((2\sqrt{2} + 3\sqrt{2}) + (-3\sqrt{3} + 4\sqrt{3}) = 5\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3}\).
Factor out perfect cubes, noting that \(\sqrt[3]{-192} = -4\sqrt[3]{3}\), to get \(5\sqrt[3]{3} - 3\sqrt[3]{3} + 2\sqrt[3]{3}\). Combining like terms gives \(4\sqrt[3]{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{7}{12}\sqrt{288} - \frac{3}{5}\sqrt{200} + \frac{5}{9}\sqrt{162}\)
qs.s: Factor out the largest perfect square from each radicand: \(\frac{7}{12}(12\sqrt{2}) - \frac{3}{5}(10\sqrt{2}) + \frac{5}{9}(9\sqrt{2})\). Combining the simplified terms yields \(7\sqrt{2} - 6\sqrt{2} + 5\sqrt{2} = 6\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{5}{6}\sqrt{80} + \frac{1}{4}\sqrt{45} - \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{20}\)
qs.s: Simplify the radicals to get \(\frac{10}{3}\sqrt{5} + \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{5} - \frac{4}{3}\sqrt{5}\). Combine the like terms by finding a common denominator: \(\left(2 + \frac{3}{4}\right)\sqrt{5} = \frac{11}{4}\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{5}{6}\sqrt{27} - \frac{3}{10}\sqrt{75} + \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{48}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \(\frac{5}{2}\sqrt{3} - \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{3} + \frac{8}{3}\sqrt{3}\). Combining the coefficients gives \((1 + \frac{8}{3})\sqrt{3} = \frac{11}{3}\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{20} + \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{45} - \frac{5}{6}\sqrt{80}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(\frac{3}{4}(2\sqrt{5}) + \frac{2}{3}(3\sqrt{5}) - \frac{5}{6}(4\sqrt{5}) = \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{5} + 2\sqrt{5} - \frac{10}{3}\sqrt{5}\). Combining the coefficients gives \((\frac{7}{2} - \frac{10}{3})\sqrt{5} = \frac{1}{6}\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{28} - \frac{5}{6}\sqrt{63} + \frac{1}{8}\sqrt{112}\)
qs.s: Rewrite each term in simplest radical form as \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{7} - \frac{5}{2}\sqrt{7} + \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{7}\). Combining like terms yields \((\frac{3 - 5 + 1}{2})\sqrt{7} = -\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{18} - \frac{3}{5}\sqrt{50} + \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{72}\)
qs.s: Factor out perfect squares to get \(\frac{1}{2}(3\sqrt{2}) - \frac{3}{5}(5\sqrt{2}) + \frac{2}{3}(6\sqrt{2}) = \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{2} - 3\sqrt{2} + 4\sqrt{2}\). Combining like terms gives \((\frac{3}{2} + 1)\sqrt{2} = \frac{5}{2}\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{5}{4}\sqrt{24} + \frac{1}{6}\sqrt{54} - \frac{3}{8}\sqrt{96}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(\frac{5}{2}\sqrt{6} + \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{6} - \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{6}\). Combining like radicals gives \((\frac{5 + 1 - 3}{2})\sqrt{6} = \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{2}{9}\sqrt{180} - \frac{3}{8}\sqrt{320} + \frac{5}{14}\sqrt{245}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(\frac{4}{3}\sqrt{5} - 3\sqrt{5} + \frac{5}{2}\sqrt{5}\). Combining the coefficients over a common denominator of 6 gives \((\frac{8 - 18 + 15}{6})\sqrt{5} = \frac{5}{6}\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{3}{8}\sqrt{32} - \frac{5}{9}\sqrt{72} + \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{162} - \frac{7}{10}\sqrt{200}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to obtain \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{2} - \frac{10}{3}\sqrt{2} + 6\sqrt{2} - 7\sqrt{2}\). Combining the coefficients gives \((\frac{3}{2} - \frac{10}{3} - 1)\sqrt{2} = -\frac{17}{6}\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{12} - \frac{2}{5}\sqrt{20} + \frac{1}{10}\sqrt{75} - \frac{5}{6}\sqrt{45}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{3} - \frac{4}{5}\sqrt{5} + \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{3} - \frac{5}{2}\sqrt{5}\). Grouping like radical terms yields \((\frac{3}{2} + \frac{1}{2})\sqrt{3} + (-\frac{4}{5} - \frac{5}{2})\sqrt{5} = 2\sqrt{3} - \frac{33}{10}\sqrt{5}\).

Factor out perfect cubes to rewrite the expression as \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[3]{3} - \frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{3} + \frac{5}{2}\sqrt[3]{3} - \frac{4}{3}\sqrt[3]{3}\). Combining like terms gives \((4 - 2)\sqrt[3]{3} = 2\sqrt[3]{3}\).

Extract perfect cube factors to get \(\frac{5}{2}\sqrt[3]{2} + \frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{2} - 2\sqrt[3]{2}\). Finding a common denominator and combining coefficients gives \((\frac{15 + 4 - 12}{6})\sqrt[3]{2} = \frac{7}{6}\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(4\sqrt[3]{54} + 3\sqrt[3]{6} \cdot \sqrt[3]{9}\)
qs.s: Combine the terms as \(4\sqrt[3]{54} + 3\sqrt[3]{54} = 7\sqrt[3]{54}\). Factoring out the perfect cube \(27\) gives \(7 \cdot 3\sqrt[3]{2} = 21\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt[4]{48} + 5\sqrt[4]{6} \cdot \sqrt[4]{8}\)
qs.s: Combine the terms to get \(3\sqrt[4]{48} + 5\sqrt[4]{48} = 8\sqrt[4]{48}\). Factoring out \(16\) gives \(8 \cdot 2\sqrt[4]{3} = 16\sqrt[4]{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(6\sqrt[4]{162} - 2\sqrt[4]{18} \cdot \sqrt[4]{9}\)
qs.s: Multiply the radicals in the second term to get \(6\sqrt[4]{162} - 2\sqrt[4]{162} = 4\sqrt[4]{162}\). Factoring out \(81\) yields \(4 \cdot 3\sqrt[4]{2} = 12\sqrt[4]{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(2\sqrt[3]{128} + 3\sqrt[3]{4} \cdot \sqrt[3]{32}\)
qs.s: Combine the terms to get \(2\sqrt[3]{128} + 3\sqrt[3]{128} = 5\sqrt[3]{128}\). Factoring out the perfect cube \(64\) gives \(5 \cdot 4\sqrt[3]{2} = 20\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(7\sqrt[3]{40} - 2\sqrt[3]{4} \cdot \sqrt[3]{10}\)
qs.s: Combine the terms to get \(7\sqrt[3]{40} - 2\sqrt[3]{40} = 5\sqrt[3]{40}\). Factoring out the perfect cube \(8\) yields \(5 \cdot 2\sqrt[3]{5} = 10\sqrt[3]{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(4\sqrt[3]{24} - \sqrt[3]{375} + 2\sqrt[3]{9} \cdot \sqrt[3]{9}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term by factoring out perfect cubes: \(4(2\sqrt[3]{3}) - 5\sqrt[3]{3} + 2(3\sqrt[3]{3}) = 8\sqrt[3]{3} - 5\sqrt[3]{3} + 6\sqrt[3]{3}\). Combining like terms gives \(9\sqrt[3]{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{5}{2}\sqrt[4]{80} - \frac{2}{3}\sqrt[4]{15} \cdot \sqrt[4]{27}\)
qs.s: Factoring out perfect 4th powers gives \(\frac{5}{2}(2\sqrt[4]{5}) - \frac{2}{3}(3\sqrt[4]{5}) = 5\sqrt[4]{5} - 2\sqrt[4]{5}\). Subtracting like terms yields \(3\sqrt[4]{5}\).
Extract perfect 4th powers from each term: \(3(4\sqrt[4]{3}) - 5(2\sqrt[4]{3}) + 2(3\sqrt[4]{3}) = 12\sqrt[4]{3} - 10\sqrt[4]{3} + 6\sqrt[4]{3}\). Combining like terms gives \(8\sqrt[4]{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(2\sqrt[3]{10} \cdot \sqrt[3]{25} + 5\sqrt[3]{6} \cdot \sqrt[3]{9}\)
qs.s: Multiply inside the radicals to get \(2\sqrt[3]{250} + 5\sqrt[3]{54}\), then factor out perfect cubes to obtain \(2(5\sqrt[3]{2}) + 5(3\sqrt[3]{2}) = 10\sqrt[3]{2} + 15\sqrt[3]{2} = 25\sqrt[3]{2}\).

Simplify each term by factoring out perfect cubes: \(2(4\sqrt[3]{5}) - 3(3\sqrt[3]{5}) + 2\sqrt[3]{5} + 2(5\sqrt[3]{5}) = 8\sqrt[3]{5} - 9\sqrt[3]{5} + 2\sqrt[3]{5} + 10\sqrt[3]{5}\). Combining like terms yields \(11\sqrt[3]{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(4\sqrt[3]{162} - 5\sqrt[3]{4} \cdot \sqrt[3]{12}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(4\sqrt[3]{162} = 4(3\sqrt[3]{6}) = 12\sqrt[3]{6}\) and \(5\sqrt[3]{4 \cdot 12} = 5\sqrt[3]{48} = 5(2\sqrt[3]{6}) = 10\sqrt[3]{6}\). Subtracting gives \(12\sqrt[3]{6} - 10\sqrt[3]{6} = 2\sqrt[3]{6}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(9\sqrt[3]{16} - 4\sqrt[3]{5} \cdot \sqrt[3]{50}\)
qs.s: Simplify both terms to like radicals: \(9\sqrt[3]{16} = 9(2\sqrt[3]{2}) = 18\sqrt[3]{2}\) and \(4\sqrt[3]{5 \cdot 50} = 4\sqrt[3]{250} = 4(5\sqrt[3]{2}) = 20\sqrt[3]{2}\). Subtracting yields \(18\sqrt[3]{2} - 20\sqrt[3]{2} = -2\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(5\sqrt[3]{32} - 4\sqrt[3]{6} \cdot \sqrt[3]{18}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(5\sqrt[3]{32} = 5(2\sqrt[3]{4}) = 10\sqrt[3]{4}\) and \(4\sqrt[3]{6 \cdot 18} = 4\sqrt[3]{108} = 4(3\sqrt[3]{4}) = 12\sqrt[3]{4}\). Subtracting yields \(10\sqrt[3]{4} - 12\sqrt[3]{4} = -2\sqrt[3]{4}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(4\sqrt[3]{40} + 2\sqrt[3]{9} \cdot \sqrt[3]{15}\)
qs.s: Factor each term: \(4\sqrt[3]{40} = 4(2\sqrt[3]{5}) = 8\sqrt[3]{5}\) and \(2\sqrt[3]{9} \cdot \sqrt[3]{15} = 2\sqrt[3]{135} = 2(3\sqrt[3]{5}) = 6\sqrt[3]{5}\). Adding the like radicals gives \(8\sqrt[3]{5} + 6\sqrt[3]{5} = 14\sqrt[3]{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(7\sqrt[3]{81} - 8\sqrt[3]{2} \cdot \sqrt[3]{12}\)
Simplify: \(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[3]{16} + \frac{5}{6}\sqrt[3]{54} - \frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{4} \cdot \sqrt[3]{32}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(\frac{3}{2}(2\sqrt[3]{2}) = 3\sqrt[3]{2}\), \(\frac{5}{6}(3\sqrt[3]{2}) = \frac{5}{2}\sqrt[3]{2}\), and \(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{128} = \frac{1}{2}(4\sqrt[3]{2}) = 2\sqrt[3]{2}\). Combining gives \(\left(3 - 2 + \frac{5}{2}\right)\sqrt[3]{2} = \frac{7}{2}\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(7\sqrt[4]{32} - 3\sqrt[4]{6} \cdot \sqrt[4]{27}\)
qs.s: Simplify the fourth roots: \(7\sqrt[4]{32} = 7\sqrt[4]{16 \cdot 2} = 14\sqrt[4]{2}\) and \(3\sqrt[4]{6 \cdot 27} = 3\sqrt[4]{162} = 3\sqrt[4]{81 \cdot 2} = 9\sqrt[4]{2}\). Subtracting gives \(14\sqrt[4]{2} - 9\sqrt[4]{2} = 5\sqrt[4]{2}\).

Simplify each term: \(5\sqrt[3]{128} = 20\sqrt[3]{2}\), \(3\sqrt[3]{54} = 9\sqrt[3]{2}\), and \(4\sqrt[3]{16} = 8\sqrt[3]{2}\). Combining like radicals gives \(20\sqrt[3]{2} - 9\sqrt[3]{2} - 8\sqrt[3]{2} = 3\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(7\sqrt[3]{4} \cdot \sqrt[3]{6} - 2\sqrt[3]{12} \cdot \sqrt[3]{16}\)
qs.s: Simplify each product: \(7\sqrt[3]{24} = 7(2\sqrt[3]{3}) = 14\sqrt[3]{3}\) and \(2\sqrt[3]{192} = 2(4\sqrt[3]{3}) = 8\sqrt[3]{3}\). Subtracting gives \(14\sqrt[3]{3} - 8\sqrt[3]{3} = 6\sqrt[3]{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{2x^2} + \sqrt{18x^2}\)
qs.s: Factor the perfect squares from each radical: \(\sqrt{2x^2} = x\sqrt{2}\) and \(\sqrt{18x^2} = 3x\sqrt{2}\). Combining like terms gives \(x\sqrt{2} + 3x\sqrt{2} = 4x\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{8a^2} + \sqrt{32a^2}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical by removing perfect square factors: \(\sqrt{8a^2} = 2a\sqrt{2}\) and \(\sqrt{32a^2} = 4a\sqrt{2}\). Adding the terms gives \(2a\sqrt{2} + 4a\sqrt{2} = 6a\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{12t^2} + \sqrt{27t^2}\)
qs.s: Write each term in simplest radical form: \(\sqrt{12t^2} = 2t\sqrt{3}\) and \(\sqrt{27t^2} = 3t\sqrt{3}\). Summing the terms results in \(2t\sqrt{3} + 3t\sqrt{3} = 5t\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{50w^2} + \sqrt{18w^2}\)
qs.s: Simplify the radicals to \(5w\sqrt{2}\) and \(3w\sqrt{2}\). Combining like terms gives \(5w\sqrt{2} + 3w\sqrt{2} = 8w\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{5y^2} + \sqrt{20y^2}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(\sqrt{5y^2} = y\sqrt{5}\) and \(\sqrt{20y^2} = 2y\sqrt{5}\). Adding the like radical terms yields \(y\sqrt{5} + 2y\sqrt{5} = 3y\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{18x^2y} + \sqrt{50x^2y} - \sqrt{8x^2y}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(3x\sqrt{2y} + 5x\sqrt{2y} - 2x\sqrt{2y}\). Combining the like radical terms results in \(6x\sqrt{2y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{27x^2} + \sqrt{48x^2} - \sqrt{12x^2}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(\sqrt{27x^2} = 3x\sqrt{3}\), \(\sqrt{48x^2} = 4x\sqrt{3}\), and \(\sqrt{12x^2} = 2x\sqrt{3}\). Combining like terms yields \((3 + 4 - 2)x\sqrt{3} = 5x\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle 5x\sqrt{32} - 3\sqrt{50x^2} + 2x\sqrt{18}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(5x\sqrt{32} = 20x\sqrt{2}\), \(3\sqrt{50x^2} = 15x\sqrt{2}\), and \(2x\sqrt{18} = 6x\sqrt{2}\). Combining like terms gives \((20 - 15 + 6)x\sqrt{2} = 11x\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle 2x\sqrt{24x} + \sqrt{54x^3}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(2x\sqrt{24x} = 2x(2\sqrt{6x}) = 4x\sqrt{6x}\) and \(\sqrt{54x^3} = 3x\sqrt{6x}\). Adding the like terms gives \(4x\sqrt{6x} + 3x\sqrt{6x} = 7x\sqrt{6x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle 3\sqrt{20x^2} + 2\sqrt{45x^2}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term by extracting the square root of the square factor: \(3\sqrt{20x^2} = 3(2x\sqrt{5}) = 6x\sqrt{5}\) and \(2\sqrt{45x^2} = 2(3x\sqrt{5}) = 6x\sqrt{5}\). Adding the terms gives \(6x\sqrt{5} + 6x\sqrt{5} = 12x\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(4x\sqrt{32x} + \sqrt{50x^3}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(4x\sqrt{32x} = 4x(4\sqrt{2x}) = 16x\sqrt{2x}\) and \(\sqrt{50x^3} = 5x\sqrt{2x}\). Combining like terms gives \(16x\sqrt{2x} + 5x\sqrt{2x} = 21x\sqrt{2x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(5\sqrt{2y^3} + 3y\sqrt{18y}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(5\sqrt{2y^3} = 5y\sqrt{2y}\) and \(3y\sqrt{18y} = 3y(3\sqrt{2y}) = 9y\sqrt{2y}\). Adding the like terms yields \(5y\sqrt{2y} + 9y\sqrt{2y} = 14y\sqrt{2y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(2\sqrt{3x^3} + 4x\sqrt{12x}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(2\sqrt{3x^3} = 2x\sqrt{3x}\) and \(4x\sqrt{12x} = 4x(2\sqrt{3x}) = 8x\sqrt{3x}\). Combining like terms gives \(2x\sqrt{3x} + 8x\sqrt{3x} = 10x\sqrt{3x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(8\sqrt{5t^3} - 2t\sqrt{45t}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(8\sqrt{5t^3} = 8t\sqrt{5t}\) and \(2t\sqrt{45t} = 2t(3\sqrt{5t}) = 6t\sqrt{5t}\). Subtracting yields \(8t\sqrt{5t} - 6t\sqrt{5t} = 2t\sqrt{5t}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(5xy\sqrt{24x^3y} - 2x^2\sqrt{54xy^3}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(5xy(2x\sqrt{6xy}) - 2x^2(3y\sqrt{6xy}) = 10x^2y\sqrt{6xy} - 6x^2y\sqrt{6xy}\). Subtracting gives \(4x^2y\sqrt{6xy}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(4a\sqrt{18ab^2} - 3b\sqrt{50a^3}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(4a(3b\sqrt{2a}) - 3b(5a\sqrt{2a}) = 12ab\sqrt{2a} - 15ab\sqrt{2a}\). Subtracting yields \(-3ab\sqrt{2a}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(2x\sqrt{75x^3} - \sqrt{12x^5} + 3x^2\sqrt{27x}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(2x(5x\sqrt{3x}) - 2x^2\sqrt{3x} + 3x^2(3\sqrt{3x}) = 10x^2\sqrt{3x} - 2x^2\sqrt{3x} + 9x^2\sqrt{3x}\). Combining coefficients gives \((10 - 2 + 9)x^2\sqrt{3x} = 17x^2\sqrt{3x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(3\sqrt{8x^3} - 2\sqrt{12y^3} + 5x\sqrt{18x} + y\sqrt{75y}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(6x\sqrt{2x} - 4y\sqrt{3y} + 15x\sqrt{2x} + 5y\sqrt{3y}\). Group like radicals to obtain \((6 + 15)x\sqrt{2x} + (-4 + 5)y\sqrt{3y} = 21x\sqrt{2x} + y\sqrt{3y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{32x^3} - \frac{1}{3}x\sqrt{72x} + 2x\sqrt{50x}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(\frac{3}{4}(4x\sqrt{2x}) - \frac{1}{3}x(6\sqrt{2x}) + 2x(5\sqrt{2x}) = 3x\sqrt{2x} - 2x\sqrt{2x} + 10x\sqrt{2x}\). Combining gives \(11x\sqrt{2x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{18y^5} - y\sqrt{8y^3} + 2y^2\sqrt{2y}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(3y^2\sqrt{2y} - 2y^2\sqrt{2y} + 2y^2\sqrt{2y}\). Combining like terms yields \((3 - 2 + 2)y^2\sqrt{2y} = 3y^2\sqrt{2y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(3x\sqrt{4x^5} + \sqrt{49x^7} - 2x^2\sqrt{9x^3}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to obtain \(6x^3\sqrt{x} + 7x^3\sqrt{x} - 6x^3\sqrt{x}\). Combining the terms yields \((6 + 7 - 6)x^3\sqrt{x} = 7x^3\sqrt{x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{9x^5} + 2x\sqrt{x^3} - 4x^2\sqrt{x}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(3x^2\sqrt{x} + 2x^2\sqrt{x} - 4x^2\sqrt{x}\). Combining the like terms gives \((3 + 2 - 4)x^2\sqrt{x} = x^2\sqrt{x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(5a\sqrt{a^5} - \sqrt{16a^7} + 3a^2\sqrt{a^3}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(5a^3\sqrt{a} - 4a^3\sqrt{a} + 3a^3\sqrt{a}\). Combining like terms gives \((5 - 4 + 3)a^3\sqrt{a} = 4a^3\sqrt{a}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2x\sqrt{27x} - y\sqrt{20y} + \sqrt{75x^3} + 3\sqrt{45y^3}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical yields \(6x\sqrt{3x} - 2y\sqrt{5y} + 5x\sqrt{3x} + 9y\sqrt{5y}\). Combining the like radical terms results in \(11x\sqrt{3x} + 7y\sqrt{5y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{98x^9} - 2x^2\sqrt{18x^5} + 3x^3\sqrt{8x^3} - x^4\sqrt{50x}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(7x^4\sqrt{2x} - 6x^4\sqrt{2x} + 6x^4\sqrt{2x} - 5x^4\sqrt{2x}\). Combining like terms gives \((7 - 6 + 6 - 5)x^4\sqrt{2x} = 2x^4\sqrt{2x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{32x^5} - \frac{1}{3}x\sqrt{72x^3} + \sqrt{50x^5}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to obtain \(3x^2\sqrt{2x} - 2x^2\sqrt{2x} + 5x^2\sqrt{2x}\). Combining the like terms gives \((3 - 2 + 5)x^2\sqrt{2x} = 6x^2\sqrt{2x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2x\sqrt{50x^3y^3} - 3y\sqrt{18x^5y} + \sqrt{8x^5y^3}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical gives \(10x^2y\sqrt{2xy} - 9x^2y\sqrt{2xy} + 2x^2y\sqrt{2xy}\). Combining like terms results in \((10 - 9 + 2)x^2y\sqrt{2xy} = 3x^2y\sqrt{2xy}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(5ab\sqrt{12a^3b} - 2a^2\sqrt{27ab^3} + \sqrt{48a^5b^3}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(10a^2b\sqrt{3ab} - 6a^2b\sqrt{3ab} + 4a^2b\sqrt{3ab}\). Combining like terms gives \((10 - 6 + 4)a^2b\sqrt{3ab} = 8a^2b\sqrt{3ab}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression \(\sqrt{81y^3} - \sqrt{16y^3} - y\sqrt{4y}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(\sqrt{81y^3} = 9y\sqrt{y}\), \(\sqrt{16y^3} = 4y\sqrt{y}\), and \(y\sqrt{4y} = 2y\sqrt{y}\). Combining like terms gives \((9 - 4 - 2)y\sqrt{y} = 3y\sqrt{y}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression \(\sqrt{64n^3} + n\sqrt{25n} - \sqrt{121n^3}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(\sqrt{64n^3} = 8n\sqrt{n}\), \(n\sqrt{25n} = 5n\sqrt{n}\), and \(\sqrt{121n^3} = 11n\sqrt{n}\). Combining like terms gives \((8 + 5 - 11)n\sqrt{n} = 2n\sqrt{n}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression \(\sqrt{4x^3} + \sqrt{36x^3} - x\sqrt{49x}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(\sqrt{4x^3} = 2x\sqrt{x}\), \(\sqrt{36x^3} = 6x\sqrt{x}\), and \(x\sqrt{49x} = 7x\sqrt{x}\). Combining like terms gives \((2 + 6 - 7)x\sqrt{x} = x\sqrt{x}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression \(a\sqrt{36a} + \sqrt{49a^3} - \sqrt{81a^3}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(a\sqrt{36a} = 6a\sqrt{a}\), \(\sqrt{49a^3} = 7a\sqrt{a}\), and \(\sqrt{81a^3} = 9a\sqrt{a}\). Combining like terms gives \((6 + 7 - 9)a\sqrt{a} = 4a\sqrt{a}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression \(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{72x^3} - \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{18x^3} + x\sqrt{50x}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{72x^3} = \frac{1}{2}(6x\sqrt{2x}) = 3x\sqrt{2x}\), \(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{18x^3} = \frac{2}{3}(3x\sqrt{2x}) = 2x\sqrt{2x}\), and \(x\sqrt{50x} = 5x\sqrt{2x}\). Combining gives \((3 - 2 + 5)x\sqrt{2x} = 6x\sqrt{2x}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression \(3\sqrt{12x^3} - x\sqrt{27x} + 2\sqrt{75x^3}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(3\sqrt{12x^3} = 3(2x\sqrt{3x}) = 6x\sqrt{3x}\), \(x\sqrt{27x} = 3x\sqrt{3x}\), and \(2\sqrt{75x^3} = 2(5x\sqrt{3x}) = 10x\sqrt{3x}\). Combining like terms gives \((6 - 3 + 10)x\sqrt{3x} = 13x\sqrt{3x}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression \(\sqrt{18x^3} + \sqrt{12y^3} - \sqrt{50x^3} + \sqrt{75y^3}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(3x\sqrt{2x} + 2y\sqrt{3y} - 5x\sqrt{2x} + 5y\sqrt{3y}\). Grouping like radicals gives \((3x - 5x)\sqrt{2x} + (2y + 5y)\sqrt{3y} = -2x\sqrt{2x} + 7y\sqrt{3y}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression \(\sqrt{28x^5} - 3x\sqrt{63x^3} + 2x^2\sqrt{112x}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(\sqrt{28x^5} = 2x^2\sqrt{7x}\), \(3x\sqrt{63x^3} = 9x^2\sqrt{7x}\), and \(2x^2\sqrt{112x} = 8x^2\sqrt{7x}\). Combining gives \((2 - 9 + 8)x^2\sqrt{7x} = x^2\sqrt{7x}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(2u\sqrt{98v} + 3\sqrt{50u^2v}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(2u\sqrt{98v} = 2u(7)\sqrt{2v} = 14u\sqrt{2v}\) and \(3\sqrt{50u^2v} = 3(5u)\sqrt{2v} = 15u\sqrt{2v}\). Combining like terms gives \(14u\sqrt{2v} + 15u\sqrt{2v} = 29u\sqrt{2v}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(4x\sqrt{45y} + 2\sqrt{20x^2y}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(4x\sqrt{45y} = 4x(3)\sqrt{5y} = 12x\sqrt{5y}\) and \(2\sqrt{20x^2y} = 2(2x)\sqrt{5y} = 4x\sqrt{5y}\). Adding like terms gives \(12x\sqrt{5y} + 4x\sqrt{5y} = 16x\sqrt{5y}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(7x\sqrt{24y} - 2\sqrt{54x^2y}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(7x\sqrt{24y} = 7x(2)\sqrt{6y} = 14x\sqrt{6y}\) and \(2\sqrt{54x^2y} = 2(3x)\sqrt{6y} = 6x\sqrt{6y}\). Subtracting yields \(14x\sqrt{6y} - 6x\sqrt{6y} = 8x\sqrt{6y}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(2\sqrt{72a^2b} - 5a\sqrt{18b}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(2\sqrt{72a^2b} = 2(6a)\sqrt{2b} = 12a\sqrt{2b}\) and \(5a\sqrt{18b} = 5a(3)\sqrt{2b} = 15a\sqrt{2b}\). Subtracting like terms gives \(12a\sqrt{2b} - 15a\sqrt{2b} = -3a\sqrt{2b}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(5\sqrt{48m^2n} - 2m\sqrt{27n}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(5\sqrt{48m^2n} = 5(4m)\sqrt{3n} = 20m\sqrt{3n}\) and \(2m\sqrt{27n} = 2m(3)\sqrt{3n} = 6m\sqrt{3n}\). Subtracting like terms yields \(20m\sqrt{3n} - 6m\sqrt{3n} = 14m\sqrt{3n}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(5xy\sqrt{72x^3y} + 2x^2\sqrt{98xy^3} - 3y\sqrt{128x^5y}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(5xy(6x)\sqrt{2xy} = 30x^2y\sqrt{2xy}\), \(2x^2(7y)\sqrt{2xy} = 14x^2y\sqrt{2xy}\), and \(3y(8x^2)\sqrt{2xy} = 24x^2y\sqrt{2xy}\). Combining like terms gives \((30 + 14 - 24)x^2y\sqrt{2xy} = 20x^2y\sqrt{2xy}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(4x\sqrt{18x^3y} - \sqrt{50x^5y} + 3x^2\sqrt{72xy}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(4x(3x)\sqrt{2xy} = 12x^2\sqrt{2xy}\), \(5x^2\sqrt{2xy}\), and \(3x^2(6)\sqrt{2xy} = 18x^2\sqrt{2xy}\). Combining like terms gives \((12 - 5 + 18)x^2\sqrt{2xy} = 25x^2\sqrt{2xy}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(2a\sqrt{75ab^4} + 3b^2\sqrt{48a^3} - b\sqrt{108a^3b^2}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(2a(5b^2)\sqrt{3a} = 10ab^2\sqrt{3a}\), \(3b^2(4a)\sqrt{3a} = 12ab^2\sqrt{3a}\), and \(b(6ab)\sqrt{3a} = 6ab^2\sqrt{3a}\). Combining like terms yields \((10 + 12 - 6)ab^2\sqrt{3a} = 16ab^2\sqrt{3a}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(3x\sqrt{75y} - 2y\sqrt{28x} + x\sqrt{12y} + 5y\sqrt{63x}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify all radicals: \(15x\sqrt{3y} - 4y\sqrt{7x} + 2x\sqrt{3y} + 15y\sqrt{7x}\). Group like radical terms to get \((15 + 2)x\sqrt{3y} + (-4 + 15)y\sqrt{7x} = 17x\sqrt{3y} + 11y\sqrt{7x}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\frac{2}{3}x\sqrt{45x^2y^3} - \frac{1}{4}y\sqrt{80x^4y} + \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{20x^4y^3}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(\frac{2}{3}x(3xy)\sqrt{5y} = 2x^2y\sqrt{5y}\), \(\frac{1}{4}y(4x^2)\sqrt{5y} = x^2y\sqrt{5y}\), and \(\frac{3}{2}(2x^2y)\sqrt{5y} = 3x^2y\sqrt{5y}\). Combining like terms gives \((2 - 1 + 3)x^2y\sqrt{5y} = 4x^2y\sqrt{5y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2\sqrt{45y} + 3\sqrt{20y}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(2(3\sqrt{5y}) + 3(2\sqrt{5y}) = 6\sqrt{5y} + 6\sqrt{5y}\). Adding like radicals gives \(12\sqrt{5y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(7\sqrt{24n} - 4\sqrt{54n}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(7(2\sqrt{6n}) - 4(3\sqrt{6n}) = 14\sqrt{6n} - 12\sqrt{6n}\). Subtracting like terms results in \(2\sqrt{6n}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(3\sqrt{75m} - 2\sqrt{48m}\)
qs.s: Rewrite each term in simplest radical form: \(3(5\sqrt{3m}) - 2(4\sqrt{3m}) = 15\sqrt{3m} - 8\sqrt{3m}\). Subtracting gives \(7\sqrt{3m}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(6\sqrt{8a} - \sqrt{72a}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \(6(2\sqrt{2a}) - 6\sqrt{2a} = 12\sqrt{2a} - 6\sqrt{2a}\). Combining like radicals yields \(6\sqrt{2a}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(4\sqrt{18x} - 2\sqrt{50x}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(4(3\sqrt{2x}) - 2(5\sqrt{2x}) = 12\sqrt{2x} - 10\sqrt{2x}\). Subtracting like radicals gives \(2\sqrt{2x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2\sqrt{75x} - \sqrt{54y} - \sqrt{12x} + 4\sqrt{24y}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \(10\sqrt{3x} - 3\sqrt{6y} - 2\sqrt{3x} + 8\sqrt{6y}\). Grouping like radical terms gives \((10-2)\sqrt{3x} + (-3+8)\sqrt{6y} = 8\sqrt{3x} + 5\sqrt{6y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2\sqrt{180x} - \sqrt{80x} - 3\sqrt{45x}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(12\sqrt{5x} - 4\sqrt{5x} - 9\sqrt{5x}\). Combining coefficients gives \((12 - 4 - 9)\sqrt{5x} = -\sqrt{5x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(5x\sqrt{48x} - 2\sqrt{75x^3}\)
qs.s: Factor out perfect squares from each radical to get \(5x(4\sqrt{3x}) - 2(5x\sqrt{3x}) = 20x\sqrt{3x} - 10x\sqrt{3x}\). Subtracting like terms yields \(10x\sqrt{3x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(3\sqrt{98a} - 2\sqrt{162a} + 5\sqrt{32a}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(3(7\sqrt{2a}) - 2(9\sqrt{2a}) + 5(4\sqrt{2a}) = 21\sqrt{2a} - 18\sqrt{2a} + 20\sqrt{2a}\). Combining the coefficients gives \(23\sqrt{2a}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2y\sqrt{63x^3} - x\sqrt{28xy^2}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical by extracting perfect square factors to get \(2y(3x\sqrt{7x}) - x(2y\sqrt{7x}) = 6xy\sqrt{7x} - 2xy\sqrt{7x}\). Subtracting like terms results in \(4xy\sqrt{7x}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(6\sqrt{75u^2v} - 2u\sqrt{48v}\)
qs.s: Extracting square factors yields \(6(5u\sqrt{3v}) - 2u(4\sqrt{3v}) = 30u\sqrt{3v} - 8u\sqrt{3v}\). Combining like terms gives \(22u\sqrt{3v}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(3y\sqrt{50x} + 2\sqrt{98xy^2}\)
qs.s: Simplifying the radicals gives \(3y(5\sqrt{2x}) + 2(7y\sqrt{2x}) = 15y\sqrt{2x} + 14y\sqrt{2x}\). Adding them gives \(29y\sqrt{2x}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(2a\sqrt{72b} + 5\sqrt{18a^2b}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical gives \(2a(6\sqrt{2b}) + 5(3a\sqrt{2b}) = 12a\sqrt{2b} + 15a\sqrt{2b}\). Combining the terms yields \(27a\sqrt{2b}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(4x\sqrt{45y} - 2\sqrt{20x^2y}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(4x(3\sqrt{5y}) - 2(2x\sqrt{5y}) = 12x\sqrt{5y} - 4x\sqrt{5y}\). Combining like terms gives \(8x\sqrt{5y}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(7m\sqrt{12n} - 4\sqrt{27m^2n}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(7m(2\sqrt{3n}) - 4(3m\sqrt{3n}) = 14m\sqrt{3n} - 12m\sqrt{3n}\). Subtracting like terms results in \(2m\sqrt{3n}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(4ab\sqrt{24a^3b} - a^2\sqrt{54ab^3} + 2\sqrt{96a^5b^3}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each term yields \(4ab(2a\sqrt{6ab}) - a^2(3b\sqrt{6ab}) + 2(4a^2b\sqrt{6ab}) = 8a^2b\sqrt{6ab} - 3a^2b\sqrt{6ab} + 8a^2b\sqrt{6ab}\). Combining the coefficients gives \(13a^2b\sqrt{6ab}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(3x^2\sqrt{112y} - x\sqrt{63x^2y} + 2\sqrt{175x^4y}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical gives \(3x^2(4\sqrt{7y}) - x(3x\sqrt{7y}) + 2(5x^2\sqrt{7y}) = 12x^2\sqrt{7y} - 3x^2\sqrt{7y} + 10x^2\sqrt{7y}\). Combining the terms yields \(19x^2\sqrt{7y}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(\frac{1}{2}x\sqrt{72xy^2} + \frac{2}{3}y\sqrt{18x^3} - \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{32x^3y^2}\)
qs.s: Simplifying gives \(\frac{1}{2}x(6y\sqrt{2x}) + \frac{2}{3}y(3x\sqrt{2x}) - \frac{3}{4}(4xy\sqrt{2x}) = 3xy\sqrt{2x} + 2xy\sqrt{2x} - 3xy\sqrt{2x}\). Combining like terms results in \(2xy\sqrt{2x}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(2x\sqrt{27y} - 5y\sqrt{20x} + 4\sqrt{12x^2y} + 2\sqrt{45xy^2}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each term gives \(6x\sqrt{3y} - 10y\sqrt{5x} + 8x\sqrt{3y} + 6y\sqrt{5x}\). Combining like radical terms yields \(14x\sqrt{3y} - 4y\sqrt{5x}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(2x\sqrt{80xy} + 3\sqrt{45x^3y} - \sqrt{125x^3y}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical gives \(2x(4\sqrt{5xy}) + 3(3x\sqrt{5xy}) - 5x\sqrt{5xy} = 8x\sqrt{5xy} + 9x\sqrt{5xy} - 5x\sqrt{5xy}\). Combining like terms gives \(12x\sqrt{5xy}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(5x\sqrt{28xy^2} + 2y\sqrt{63x^3}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical produces \(5x(2y\sqrt{7x}) + 2y(3x\sqrt{7x}) = 10xy\sqrt{7x} + 6xy\sqrt{7x}\). Adding the terms gives \(16xy\sqrt{7x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(5m\sqrt{45mn^2} - 2n\sqrt{20m^3}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical yields \(5m(3n\sqrt{5m}) - 2n(2m\sqrt{5m}) = 15mn\sqrt{5m} - 4mn\sqrt{5m}\). Subtracting like terms yields \(11mn\sqrt{5m}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(7a\sqrt{24ab^2} - 3b\sqrt{96a^3}\)
qs.s: Simplifying both radicals gives \(7a(2b\sqrt{6a}) - 3b(4a\sqrt{6a}) = 14ab\sqrt{6a} - 12ab\sqrt{6a}\). Subtracting like terms results in \(2ab\sqrt{6a}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2a\sqrt{18b^3} + 5b\sqrt{32a^2b}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical gives \(2a(3b\sqrt{2b}) + 5b(4a\sqrt{2b}) = 6ab\sqrt{2b} + 20ab\sqrt{2b}\). Combining like terms results in \(26ab\sqrt{2b}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(4y\sqrt{27x^3} + 2x\sqrt{48xy^2}\)
qs.s: Factoring perfect squares out of each radical gives \(4y(3x\sqrt{3x}) + 2x(4y\sqrt{3x}) = 12xy\sqrt{3x} + 8xy\sqrt{3x}\). Combining like terms gives \(20xy\sqrt{3x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2b\sqrt{108a^4b} - a\sqrt{147a^2b^3} + \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{192a^4b^3}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical gives \(2b(6a^2\sqrt{3b}) - a(7ab\sqrt{3b}) + \frac{1}{2}(8a^2b\sqrt{3b}) = 12a^2b\sqrt{3b} - 7a^2b\sqrt{3b} + 4a^2b\sqrt{3b}\). Combining like terms yields \(9a^2b\sqrt{3b}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2a^2b\sqrt{48ab^3} + a\sqrt{75a^3b^5}\)
qs.s: Factoring perfect squares out yields \(2a^2b(4b\sqrt{3ab}) + a(5ab^2\sqrt{3ab}) = 8a^2b^2\sqrt{3ab} + 5a^2b^2\sqrt{3ab}\). Combining like terms gives \(13a^2b^2\sqrt{3ab}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(3yz\sqrt{20x^3y} + 2xz\sqrt{45xy^3} - xy\sqrt{125xyz^2}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each term gives \(3yz(2x\sqrt{5xy}) + 2xz(3y\sqrt{5xy}) - xy(5z\sqrt{5xy}) = 6xyz\sqrt{5xy} + 6xyz\sqrt{5xy} - 5xyz\sqrt{5xy}\). Combining terms results in \(7xyz\sqrt{5xy}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\frac{3}{4}x\sqrt{32x^2y^3} + \frac{2}{3}y\sqrt{72x^4y}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical gives \(\frac{3}{4}x(4xy\sqrt{2y}) + \frac{2}{3}y(6x^2\sqrt{2y}) = 3x^2y\sqrt{2y} + 4x^2y\sqrt{2y}\). Adding like terms yields \(7x^2y\sqrt{2y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2y\sqrt{50x^3} + 3x\sqrt{72xy^2} - \sqrt{98x^3y^2}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical yields \(2y(5x\sqrt{2x}) + 3x(6y\sqrt{2x}) - 7xy\sqrt{2x} = 10xy\sqrt{2x} + 18xy\sqrt{2x} - 7xy\sqrt{2x}\). Combining like terms gives \(21xy\sqrt{2x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{\frac{27}{b^2}} + \sqrt{\frac{48}{25b^2}}\)
qs.s: Simplifying the radicals gives \(\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{b} + \frac{4\sqrt{3}}{5b}\). Finding the common denominator \(5b\) results in \(\frac{15\sqrt{3} + 4\sqrt{3}}{5b} = \frac{19\sqrt{3}}{5b}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{\frac{12}{y^2}} + \sqrt{\frac{75}{4y^2}}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \(\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{y} + \frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2y}\). Combining over the common denominator \(2y\) yields \(\frac{4\sqrt{3} + 5\sqrt{3}}{2y} = \frac{9\sqrt{3}}{2y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{\frac{50}{a^2}} - \sqrt{\frac{18}{25a^2}}\)
qs.s: Express each term in simplest radical form to get \(\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{a} - \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{5a}\). Writing with a common denominator gives \(\frac{25\sqrt{2} - 3\sqrt{2}}{5a} = \frac{22\sqrt{2}}{5a}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{\frac{45}{x^2}} - \sqrt{\frac{5}{9x^2}}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{x} - \frac{\sqrt{5}}{3x}\). Finding a common denominator gives \(\frac{9\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{5}}{3x} = \frac{8\sqrt{5}}{3x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{\frac{8}{x^2}} + \sqrt{\frac{50}{9x^2}}\)
qs.s: Simplify each square root to \(\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{x} + \frac{5\sqrt{2}}{3x}\). Combining terms over the common denominator \(3x\) yields \(\frac{6\sqrt{2} + 5\sqrt{2}}{3x} = \frac{11\sqrt{2}}{3x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{\frac{32}{x^2}} - \sqrt{\frac{50}{9x^2}} - \sqrt{\frac{18}{25x^2}}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical gives \(\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{x} - \frac{5\sqrt{2}}{3x} - \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{5x}\). Finding the common denominator \(15x\) yields \(\frac{60\sqrt{2} - 25\sqrt{2} - 9\sqrt{2}}{15x} = \frac{26\sqrt{2}}{15x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{\frac{80}{x^2}} - \sqrt{\frac{45}{4x^2}} + \sqrt{\frac{5}{9x^2}}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to \(\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{x} - \frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2x} + \frac{\sqrt{5}}{3x}\). Using the common denominator \(6x\), combine the numerators to get \(\frac{24\sqrt{5} - 9\sqrt{5} + 2\sqrt{5}}{6x} = \frac{17\sqrt{5}}{6x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{\frac{72}{25x^4}} + \sqrt{\frac{98}{9x^4}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the radicals to \(\frac{6\sqrt{2}}{5x^2} + \frac{7\sqrt{2}}{3x^2}\). Finding the common denominator \(15x^2\) gives \(\frac{18\sqrt{2} + 35\sqrt{2}}{15x^2} = \frac{53\sqrt{2}}{15x^2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{\frac{27x^3}{y^2}} + \sqrt{\frac{12x^3}{25y^2}}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \(\frac{3x\sqrt{3x}}{y} + \frac{2x\sqrt{3x}}{5y}\). Combining over the common denominator \(5y\) gives \(\frac{15x\sqrt{3x} + 2x\sqrt{3x}}{5y} = \frac{17x\sqrt{3x}}{5y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{\frac{48a^5}{b^2}} - \sqrt{\frac{75a^5}{4b^2}} + \sqrt{\frac{12a^5}{9b^2}}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to obtain \(\frac{4a^2\sqrt{3a}}{b} - \frac{5a^2\sqrt{3a}}{2b} + \frac{2a^2\sqrt{3a}}{3b}\). Combining like terms over the common denominator \(6b\) gives \(\frac{24a^2\sqrt{3a} - 15a^2\sqrt{3a} + 4a^2\sqrt{3a}}{6b} = \frac{13a^2\sqrt{3a}}{6b}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{\frac{50}{y^2}} - \frac{\sqrt{18}}{3y}\)
qs.s: Simplify both terms to get \(\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{y} - \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{3y} = \frac{5\sqrt{2}}{y} - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{y}\). Subtracting yields \(\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{75}}{2x} + \sqrt{\frac{48}{x^2}}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2x} + \frac{4\sqrt{3}}{x}\). Finding the common denominator \(2x\) gives \(\frac{5\sqrt{3} + 8\sqrt{3}}{2x} = \frac{13\sqrt{3}}{2x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{98}}{3x} + \sqrt{\frac{32}{x^2}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the terms to \(\frac{7\sqrt{2}}{3x} + \frac{4\sqrt{2}}{x}\). Combining them over the common denominator \(3x\) gives \(\frac{7\sqrt{2} + 12\sqrt{2}}{3x} = \frac{19\sqrt{2}}{3x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{45}}{4a} + \sqrt{\frac{80}{a^2}}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{4a} + \frac{4\sqrt{5}}{a}\). Converting to the common denominator \(4a\) yields \(\frac{3\sqrt{5} + 16\sqrt{5}}{4a} = \frac{19\sqrt{5}}{4a}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{\frac{63}{b^2}} - \frac{\sqrt{28}}{3b}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the radicals as \(\frac{3\sqrt{7}}{b} - \frac{2\sqrt{7}}{3b}\). Using the common denominator \(3b\), this becomes \(\frac{9\sqrt{7} - 2\sqrt{7}}{3b} = \frac{7\sqrt{7}}{3b}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{72}}{5x^2} + \sqrt{\frac{50}{x^4}} - \frac{\sqrt{8}}{2x^2}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to obtain \(\frac{6\sqrt{2}}{5x^2} + \frac{5\sqrt{2}}{x^2} - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{x^2}\). Combining over the common denominator \(5x^2\) gives \(\frac{6\sqrt{2} + 25\sqrt{2} - 5\sqrt{2}}{5x^2} = \frac{26\sqrt{2}}{5x^2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{\frac{75x^3}{y^2}} - \frac{x\sqrt{48x}}{3y}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(\frac{5x\sqrt{3x}}{y} - \frac{4x\sqrt{3x}}{3y}\). Writing over the common denominator \(3y\) gives \(\frac{15x\sqrt{3x} - 4x\sqrt{3x}}{3y} = \frac{11x\sqrt{3x}}{3y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{250}}{2x} - \sqrt[3]{\frac{16}{x^3}}\)
qs.s: Simplify each cube root to get \(\frac{5\sqrt[3]{2}}{2x} - \frac{2\sqrt[3]{2}}{x}\). Using the common denominator \(2x\) gives \(\frac{5\sqrt[3]{2} - 4\sqrt[3]{2}}{2x} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{2}}{2x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{72}}{4x} + \sqrt{\frac{50}{x^2}} - \frac{\sqrt{98}}{6x}\)
qs.s: Simplify the radicals to get \(\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2x} + \frac{5\sqrt{2}}{x} - \frac{7\sqrt{2}}{6x}\). Converting to the common denominator \(6x\) yields \(\frac{9\sqrt{2} + 30\sqrt{2} - 7\sqrt{2}}{6x} = \frac{32\sqrt{2}}{6x} = \frac{16\sqrt{2}}{3x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{45x^3}}{2y} - x\sqrt{\frac{20x}{y^2}} + \frac{3\sqrt{5x^3}}{y}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(\frac{3x\sqrt{5x}}{2y} - \frac{2x\sqrt{5x}}{y} + \frac{3x\sqrt{5x}}{y}\). Finding the common denominator \(2y\) gives \(\frac{3x\sqrt{5x} - 4x\sqrt{5x} + 6x\sqrt{5x}}{2y} = \frac{5x\sqrt{5x}}{2y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(4\sqrt{27a^2b^3} - 2b\sqrt{12a^2b}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(12ab\sqrt{3b} - 4ab\sqrt{3b}\). Subtracting like terms gives \(8ab\sqrt{3b}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2x\sqrt{45xy^2} + 3\sqrt{20x^3y^2}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical term yields \(6xy\sqrt{5x} + 6xy\sqrt{5x}\). Adding the like terms gives \(12xy\sqrt{5x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(6\sqrt{24x^5y} + 2x^2\sqrt{54xy}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \(12x^2\sqrt{6xy} + 6x^2\sqrt{6xy}\). Adding the coefficients gives \(18x^2\sqrt{6xy}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2\sqrt{12m^3n^2} - 5m\sqrt{27mn^2}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(4mn\sqrt{3m} - 15mn\sqrt{3m}\). Subtracting the coefficients gives \(-11mn\sqrt{3m}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(3u\sqrt{75uv^4} - 2v\sqrt{48u^3v^2}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical expression to \(15uv^2\sqrt{3u} - 8uv^2\sqrt{3u}\). Combining like terms gives \(7uv^2\sqrt{3u}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(5xy\sqrt{32xz^3} - 2z\sqrt{72x^3y^2z} + x\sqrt{98xy^2z^3}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \(20xyz\sqrt{2xz} - 12xyz\sqrt{2xz} + 7xyz\sqrt{2xz}\). Combining like terms gives \(15xyz\sqrt{2xz}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{48a^5b^3} - \frac{2}{3}ab\sqrt{108a^3b} + 3a^2b\sqrt{12ab}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical gives \(2a^2b\sqrt{3ab} - 4a^2b\sqrt{3ab} + 6a^2b\sqrt{3ab}\). Combining like terms results in \(4a^2b\sqrt{3ab}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(4x\sqrt{45xy} + y\sqrt{28xy} - 3\sqrt{20x^3y} + 2\sqrt{63xy^3}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each term yields \(12x\sqrt{5xy} + 2y\sqrt{7xy} - 6x\sqrt{5xy} + 6y\sqrt{7xy}\). Combining like radicals gives \(6x\sqrt{5xy} + 8y\sqrt{7xy}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2a^2\sqrt{75ab^5} - 3b^2\sqrt{108a^5b} + ab\sqrt{147a^3b^3}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(10a^2b^2\sqrt{3ab} - 18a^2b^2\sqrt{3ab} + 7a^2b^2\sqrt{3ab}\). Combining the like terms yields \(-a^2b^2\sqrt{3ab}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(3x\sqrt{72xy^3} - 2y\sqrt{50x^3y} + 4\sqrt{18x^3y^3}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical term to get \(18xy\sqrt{2xy} - 10xy\sqrt{2xy} + 12xy\sqrt{2xy}\). Combining the like terms results in \(20xy\sqrt{2xy}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(\sqrt{16m+32} + \sqrt{m+2}\)
qs.s: Factor 16 from the first radicand to get \(\sqrt{16(m+2)} + \sqrt{m+2} = 4\sqrt{m+2} + \sqrt{m+2}\). Adding like radicals gives \(5\sqrt{m+2}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(\sqrt{4x+20} + \sqrt{x+5}\)
qs.s: Factor 4 from the first radicand to get \(\sqrt{4(x+5)} + \sqrt{x+5} = 2\sqrt{x+5} + \sqrt{x+5}\). Combining like radicals gives \(3\sqrt{x+5}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(\sqrt{p-4} + \sqrt{25p-100}\)
qs.s: Factor 25 from the second radicand to get \(\sqrt{p-4} + \sqrt{25(p-4)} = \sqrt{p-4} + 5\sqrt{p-4}\). Combining like radicals gives \(6\sqrt{p-4}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(\sqrt{36t+36} - \sqrt{t+1}\)
qs.s: Factor 36 from the first radicand to get \(\sqrt{36(t+1)} - \sqrt{t+1} = 6\sqrt{t+1} - \sqrt{t+1}\). Subtracting like radicals gives \(5\sqrt{t+1}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(\sqrt{25a-50} - \sqrt{a-2}\)
qs.s: Factor 25 from the first radicand to get \(\sqrt{25(a-2)} - \sqrt{a-2} = 5\sqrt{a-2} - \sqrt{a-2}\). Subtracting gives \(4\sqrt{a-2}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(\sqrt{50a+75} - \sqrt{18a+27}\)
qs.s: Factor 25 from the first radicand and 9 from the second to get \(5\sqrt{2a+3} - 3\sqrt{2a+3}\). Subtracting gives \(2\sqrt{2a+3}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(\sqrt{4x+16} + \sqrt{25x+100} - \sqrt{9x+36}\)
qs.s: Factor the perfect square from each radicand: \(2\sqrt{x+4} + 5\sqrt{x+4} - 3\sqrt{x+4}\). Combining like terms gives \((2 + 5 - 3)\sqrt{x+4} = 4\sqrt{x+4}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(3\sqrt{16y-32} - 2\sqrt{49y-98}\)
qs.s: Factor each radical: \(3(4)\sqrt{y-2} - 2(7)\sqrt{y-2} = 12\sqrt{y-2} - 14\sqrt{y-2}\). Combining terms gives \(-2\sqrt{y-2}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(4\sqrt{9m-9} + 2\sqrt{36m-36} - 3\sqrt{25m-25}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \(4(3)\sqrt{m-1} + 2(6)\sqrt{m-1} - 3(5)\sqrt{m-1} = 12\sqrt{m-1} + 12\sqrt{m-1} - 15\sqrt{m-1}\). Combining coefficients gives \(9\sqrt{m-1}\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers: \(\sqrt{9x^3+18x^2} + \sqrt{25x^3+50x^2}\)
qs.s: Factor the perfect square terms \(9x^2\) and \(25x^2\) out of each radical to obtain \(3x\sqrt{x+2} + 5x\sqrt{x+2}\). Combining like radicals gives \(8x\sqrt{x+2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{16x - 32} - \sqrt{x - 2}\)
qs.s: Factor 16 from the first radical to get \(\sqrt{16(x - 2)} = 4\sqrt{x - 2}\). Then combine like radicals: \(4\sqrt{x - 2} - \sqrt{x - 2} = 3\sqrt{x - 2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{36x - 36} + \sqrt{x - 1}\)
qs.s: Factor 36 from the first radical to get \(\sqrt{36(x - 1)} = 6\sqrt{x - 1}\). Then combine like radicals: \(6\sqrt{x - 1} + \sqrt{x - 1} = 7\sqrt{x - 1}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{y - 5} + \sqrt{25y - 125}\)
qs.s: Factor 25 from the second radical to get \(\sqrt{25(y - 5)} = 5\sqrt{y - 5}\). Then combine like radicals: \(\sqrt{y - 5} + 5\sqrt{y - 5} = 6\sqrt{y - 5}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{4x + 12} + \sqrt{x + 3}\)
qs.s: Factor 4 from the first radical to get \(\sqrt{4(x + 3)} = 2\sqrt{x + 3}\). Then combine like radicals: \(2\sqrt{x + 3} + \sqrt{x + 3} = 3\sqrt{x + 3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{9a + 36} - \sqrt{a + 4}\)
qs.s: Factor 9 from the first radical to get \(\sqrt{9(a + 4)} = 3\sqrt{a + 4}\). Then combine like radicals: \(3\sqrt{a + 4} - \sqrt{a + 4} = 2\sqrt{a + 4}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2\sqrt{25x^3 - 50x^2} - x\sqrt{9x - 18}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(2(5x)\sqrt{x - 2} - 3x\sqrt{x - 2} = 10x\sqrt{x - 2} - 3x\sqrt{x - 2} = 7x\sqrt{x - 2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(3\sqrt{16x + 32} - 2\sqrt{25x + 50} + \sqrt{9x + 18}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical term: \(3(4)\sqrt{x + 2} - 2(5)\sqrt{x + 2} + 3\sqrt{x + 2} = 12\sqrt{x + 2} - 10\sqrt{x + 2} + 3\sqrt{x + 2} = 5\sqrt{x + 2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{36x - 72} + \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{81x - 162} - \sqrt{49x - 98}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical term: \(\frac{1}{2}(6)\sqrt{x - 2} + \frac{2}{3}(9)\sqrt{x - 2} - 7\sqrt{x - 2} = 3\sqrt{x - 2} + 6\sqrt{x - 2} - 7\sqrt{x - 2} = 2\sqrt{x - 2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{9x^3 + 9x^2} - \sqrt{4x^3 + 4x^2}\)
qs.s: Factor \(9x^2\) and \(4x^2\) from the respective radicands to get \(3x\sqrt{x + 1} - 2x\sqrt{x + 1}\). Combining like terms gives \(x\sqrt{x + 1}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{25x - 50} + \sqrt{4x - 8} - \sqrt{9x - 18}\)
qs.s: Factor each radical to get \(5\sqrt{x - 2} + 2\sqrt{x - 2} - 3\sqrt{x - 2}\). Combining coefficients gives \((5 + 2 - 3)\sqrt{x - 2} = 4\sqrt{x - 2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(5p\sqrt{16p^2q} - 3p\sqrt{49q} - 2p\sqrt{9q}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(5p(4p\sqrt{q}) - 3p(7\sqrt{q}) - 2p(3\sqrt{q}) = 20p^2\sqrt{q} - 21p\sqrt{q} - 6p\sqrt{q}\). Combining the like terms gives \(20p^2\sqrt{q} - 27p\sqrt{q}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2u\sqrt{36u^2v} + 6u\sqrt{4v} - 8u\sqrt{81v}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \(2u(6u\sqrt{v}) + 6u(2\sqrt{v}) - 8u(9\sqrt{v}) = 12u^2\sqrt{v} + 12u\sqrt{v} - 72u\sqrt{v}\). Combining like terms results in \(12u^2\sqrt{v} - 60u\sqrt{v}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(3x\sqrt{49x^2y} - 4x\sqrt{25y} + 2x\sqrt{64y}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(3x(7x\sqrt{y}) - 4x(5\sqrt{y}) + 2x(8\sqrt{y}) = 21x^2\sqrt{y} - 20x\sqrt{y} + 16x\sqrt{y}\). Combining like terms yields \(21x^2\sqrt{y} - 4x\sqrt{y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(3a\sqrt{9a^2b} + 4a\sqrt{16b} - 7a\sqrt{25b}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(3a(3a\sqrt{b}) + 4a(4\sqrt{b}) - 7a(5\sqrt{b}) = 9a^2\sqrt{b} + 16a\sqrt{b} - 35a\sqrt{b}\). Combining the like terms gives \(9a^2\sqrt{b} - 19a\sqrt{b}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\frac{1}{2}x\sqrt{32x^2y} - \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{72x^4y} + \frac{3}{4}x^2\sqrt{8y}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to obtain \(2x^2\sqrt{2y} - 4x^2\sqrt{2y} + \frac{3}{2}x^2\sqrt{2y}\). Combining the coefficients gives \((2 - 4 + \frac{3}{2})x^2\sqrt{2y} = -\frac{1}{2}x^2\sqrt{2y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2x\sqrt{18x} - 3y\sqrt{12y} + x\sqrt{50x} + 4y\sqrt{27y}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical gives \(6x\sqrt{2x} - 6y\sqrt{3y} + 5x\sqrt{2x} + 12y\sqrt{3y}\). Combining like terms results in \(11x\sqrt{2x} + 6y\sqrt{3y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(5ab\sqrt{12a} - 2b\sqrt{27a^3} + 3a\sqrt{75ab^2}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical yields \(5ab(2\sqrt{3a}) - 2b(3a\sqrt{3a}) + 3a(5b\sqrt{3a}) = 10ab\sqrt{3a} - 6ab\sqrt{3a} + 15ab\sqrt{3a}\). Combining all like terms gives \(19ab\sqrt{3a}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(4x\sqrt{20x^3y} - 2\sqrt{45x^5y} + 3x^2\sqrt{80xy}\)
qs.s: Factor out perfect squares to get \(4x(2x\sqrt{5xy}) - 2(3x^2\sqrt{5xy}) + 3x^2(4\sqrt{5xy}) = 8x^2\sqrt{5xy} - 6x^2\sqrt{5xy} + 12x^2\sqrt{5xy}\). Combining like terms gives \(14x^2\sqrt{5xy}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2x\sqrt{18x^2y} + 3\sqrt{50x^4y} - 4x^2\sqrt{72y}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(2x(3x\sqrt{2y}) + 3(5x^2\sqrt{2y}) - 4x^2(6\sqrt{2y}) = 6x^2\sqrt{2y} + 15x^2\sqrt{2y} - 24x^2\sqrt{2y}\). Since all three terms have the like radical factor \(x^2\sqrt{2y}\), combine coefficients to obtain \(-3x^2\sqrt{2y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(\displaystyle -\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{b^2} + \frac{5}{6}\sqrt{b^2} - \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{b^2}\)
qs.s: Since \(b > 0\), \(\sqrt{b^2} = b\). Finding a common denominator of 12 gives \((-\frac{3}{12} + \frac{10}{12} - \frac{8}{12})b = -\frac{1}{12}b\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{x^2} - \frac{7}{4}\sqrt{x^2} + \frac{5}{8}\sqrt{x^2}\)
qs.s: Since \(x > 0\), \(\sqrt{x^2} = x\). Combining the coefficients with a common denominator of 8 yields \((\frac{12}{8} - \frac{14}{8} + \frac{5}{8})x = \frac{3}{8}x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{y^2} - \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{y^2} + \frac{5}{8}\sqrt{y^2}\)
qs.s: Since \(y > 0\), \(\sqrt{y^2} = y\). Combining the coefficients over a common denominator of 8 gives \((\frac{6}{8} - \frac{4}{8} + \frac{5}{8})y = \frac{7}{8}y\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2}{5}\sqrt{a^2} + \frac{1}{10}\sqrt{a^2} - \frac{4}{5}\sqrt{a^2}\)
qs.s: Since \(a > 0\), \(\sqrt{a^2} = a\). Combining the fractional coefficients over a common denominator of 10 gives \((\frac{4}{10} + \frac{1}{10} - \frac{8}{10})a = -\frac{3}{10}a\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{3}\sqrt{45x^3} - \frac{3}{2}x\sqrt{20x} + \frac{5}{6}\sqrt{80x^3}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term to get \(x\sqrt{5x} - 3x\sqrt{5x} + \frac{10}{3}x\sqrt{5x}\). Combining the coefficients gives \((1 - 3 + \frac{10}{3})x\sqrt{5x} = \frac{4}{3}x\sqrt{5x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{18x^2} - \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{50x^2} + \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{32x^2}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(2x\sqrt{2} - \frac{5}{2}x\sqrt{2} + 3x\sqrt{2}\). Combining like terms gives \((2 - \frac{5}{2} + 3)x\sqrt{2} = \frac{5}{2}x\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{12x} + \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{45y} - \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{48x} + \frac{1}{6}\sqrt{20y}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical gives \(\sqrt{3x} + 2\sqrt{5y} - 3\sqrt{3x} + \frac{1}{3}\sqrt{5y}\). Grouping and combining like radicals results in \(-2\sqrt{3x} + \frac{7}{3}\sqrt{5y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{5}{6}\sqrt{24y^3} - \frac{1}{4}y\sqrt{54y} - \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{96y^3}\)
qs.s: Simplifying each radical gives \(\frac{5}{3}y\sqrt{6y} - \frac{3}{4}y\sqrt{6y} - \frac{8}{3}y\sqrt{6y}\). Combining coefficients gives \((\frac{5}{3} - \frac{8}{3} - \frac{3}{4})y\sqrt{6y} = -\frac{7}{4}y\sqrt{6y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{4}{5}\sqrt{50a^2b} - \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{18a^2b} + \frac{3}{8}a\sqrt{32b}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \(4a\sqrt{2b} - 2a\sqrt{2b} + \frac{3}{2}a\sqrt{2b}\). Combining like terms yields \((4 - 2 + \frac{3}{2})a\sqrt{2b} = \frac{7}{2}a\sqrt{2b}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{3}{5}\sqrt{25y^2} + \frac{4}{5}\sqrt{9y^2} + \sqrt{16y^2}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \(\frac{3}{5}(5y) + \frac{4}{5}(3y) + 4y = 3y + \frac{12}{5}y + 4y\). Combining the like terms gives \(\frac{47}{5}y\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{4}{3}\sqrt{36m^2} + \sqrt{49m^2} - \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{25m^2}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(\frac{4}{3}(6m) + 7m - \frac{2}{3}(5m) = 8m + 7m - \frac{10}{3}m\). Combining like terms gives \(15m - \frac{10}{3}m = \frac{35}{3}m\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{64a^2} - \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{16a^2} + \frac{5}{2}\sqrt{9a^2}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(\frac{1}{2}(8a) - \frac{3}{4}(4a) + \frac{5}{2}(3a) = 4a - 3a + \frac{15}{2}a\). Combining like terms yields \(a + \frac{15}{2}a = \frac{17}{2}a\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\sqrt{64b^2} - \frac{3}{5}\sqrt{100b^2} + \frac{7}{5}\sqrt{4b^2}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(8b - \frac{3}{5}(10b) + \frac{7}{5}(2b) = 8b - 6b + \frac{14}{5}b\). Combining like terms gives \(2b + \frac{14}{5}b = \frac{24}{5}b\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{5}{4}\sqrt{16x^2} + \frac{1}{4}\sqrt{81x^2} + \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{4x^2}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \(\frac{5}{4}(4x) + \frac{1}{4}(9x) + \frac{3}{2}(2x) = 5x + \frac{9}{4}x + 3x\). Combining like terms results in \(8x + \frac{9}{4}x = \frac{41}{4}x\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{5}{6}\sqrt{72x^2} - \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{98x^2} + \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{32x^2} - \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{50x^2}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(\frac{5}{6}(6x\sqrt{2}) - \frac{2}{3}(7x\sqrt{2}) + \frac{3}{4}(4x\sqrt{2}) - \frac{1}{2}(5x\sqrt{2}) = 5x\sqrt{2} - \frac{14}{3}x\sqrt{2} + 3x\sqrt{2} - \frac{5}{2}x\sqrt{2}\). Combining coefficients over 6 gives \(\frac{48 - 28 - 15}{6}x\sqrt{2} = \frac{5}{6}x\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{4}{3}\sqrt{18x^3} - \frac{1}{2}x\sqrt{50x} + \frac{5}{6}\sqrt{8x^3}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical to like terms: \(\frac{4}{3}(3x\sqrt{2x}) - \frac{1}{2}x(5\sqrt{2x}) + \frac{5}{6}(2x\sqrt{2x}) = 4x\sqrt{2x} - \frac{5}{2}x\sqrt{2x} + \frac{5}{3}x\sqrt{2x}\). Combining with common denominator 6 gives \(\frac{19}{6}x\sqrt{2x}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{48x^2} - \frac{5}{6}\sqrt{12x^2} + \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{27x^2}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical by factoring out perfect squares: \(\frac{3}{4}(4x\sqrt{3}) - \frac{5}{6}(2x\sqrt{3}) + \frac{2}{3}(3x\sqrt{3}) = 3x\sqrt{3} - \frac{5}{3}x\sqrt{3} + 2x\sqrt{3}\). Combining like terms yields \(\frac{10}{3}x\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{3}{5}\sqrt{75a^3} + \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{48a^3} - \frac{4}{3}a\sqrt{12a}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \(\frac{3}{5}(5a\sqrt{3a}) + \frac{1}{2}(4a\sqrt{3a}) - \frac{4}{3}a(2\sqrt{3a}) = 3a\sqrt{3a} + 2a\sqrt{3a} - \frac{8}{3}a\sqrt{3a}\). Combining gives \((5 - \frac{8}{3})a\sqrt{3a} = \frac{7}{3}a\sqrt{3a}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{5}{3}\sqrt{18x^2y} - \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{50x^2y} + 2x\sqrt{8y}\). All variables represent positive numbers.
qs.s: Simplify each radical to get \(\frac{5}{3}(3x\sqrt{2y}) - \frac{1}{2}(5x\sqrt{2y}) + 2x(2\sqrt{2y}) = 5x\sqrt{2y} - \frac{5}{2}x\sqrt{2y} + 4x\sqrt{2y}\). Combining the terms gives \(\frac{13}{2}x\sqrt{2y}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{x^2+8x+16} - \sqrt{x^2+2x+1}\)
qs.s: Factor each radicand as a perfect square: \(\sqrt{(x+4)^2} - \sqrt{(x+1)^2}\). Since \(x > 0\), this simplifies to \((x+4) - (x+1) = x + 4 - x - 1 = 3\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression, where \(x > 5\). All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{x^2-10x+25} - \sqrt{x^2-4x+4}\)
qs.s: Factor each radicand as a perfect square: \(\sqrt{(x-5)^2} - \sqrt{(x-2)^2}\). Since \(x > 5\), this simplifies to \((x-5) - (x-2) = x - 5 - x + 2 = -3\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{x^2+20x+100} - \sqrt{x^2+8x+16}\)
qs.s: Factor each radicand as a perfect square: \(\sqrt{(x+10)^2} - \sqrt{(x+4)^2}\). Since \(x > 0\), this simplifies to \((x+10) - (x+4) = x + 10 - x - 4 = 6\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{x^2+6x+9} - \sqrt{x^2+14x+49}\)
qs.s: Factor each radicand as a perfect square: \(\sqrt{(x+3)^2} - \sqrt{(x+7)^2}\). Since \(x > 0\), this simplifies to \((x+3) - (x+7) = x + 3 - x - 7 = -4\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{x^2+6x+9} - \sqrt{x^2+10x+25}\)
qs.s: Factor each radicand as a perfect square: \(\sqrt{(x+3)^2} - \sqrt{(x+5)^2}\). Since \(x > 0\), this simplifies to \((x+3) - (x+5) = x + 3 - x - 5 = -2\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(3\sqrt{x^2+6x+9} - 2\sqrt{x^2+2x+1}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicals to get \(3\sqrt{(x+3)^2} - 2\sqrt{(x+1)^2} = 3(x+3) - 2(x+1)\). Expanding and combining like terms yields \(3x + 9 - 2x - 2 = x + 7\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(2\sqrt{4x^2+12x+9} - \sqrt{9x^2+24x+16}\)
qs.s: Factor each radicand to get \(2\sqrt{(2x+3)^2} - \sqrt{(3x+4)^2} = 2(2x+3) - (3x+4)\). Distributing and combining like terms yields \(4x + 6 - 3x - 4 = x + 2\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{x^2+4x+4} + \sqrt{x^2+12x+36} - \sqrt{x^2+8x+16}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to obtain \((x+2) + (x+6) - (x+4)\). Combining like terms gives \(x + 2 + x + 6 - x - 4 = x + 4\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{4x^2+20x+25} - \sqrt{4x^2+4x+1}\)
qs.s: Factor each radicand as a perfect square: \(\sqrt{(2x+5)^2} - \sqrt{(2x+1)^2}\). Since \(x > 0\), this evaluates to \((2x+5) - (2x+1) = 2x + 5 - 2x - 1 = 4\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{x^2+6xy+9y^2} - \sqrt{x^2+2xy+y^2}\)
qs.s: Factor each radicand into a binomial squared: \(\sqrt{(x+3y)^2} - \sqrt{(x+y)^2} = (x+3y) - (x+y)\). Subtracting yields \(x + 3y - x - y = 2y\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{m^2+18m+81} - \sqrt{m^2+20m+100}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the radicands as perfect squares to get \(\sqrt{(m+9)^2} - \sqrt{(m+10)^2}\). Since \(m > 0\), this simplifies to \((m+9) - (m+10) = -1\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{a^2+8a+16} + \sqrt{a^2+12a+36}\)
qs.s: Rewrite each radical as \(\sqrt{(a+4)^2} + \sqrt{(a+6)^2}\). Since \(a > 0\), this simplifies to \((a+4) + (a+6) = 2a + 10\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{y^2+16y+64} - \sqrt{y^2+6y+9}\)
qs.s: Factoring the trinomials gives \(\sqrt{(y+8)^2} - \sqrt{(y+3)^2}\). Since \(y > 0\), simplifying yields \((y+8) - (y+3) = 5\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{x^2+10x+25} + \sqrt{x^2+2x+1}\)
qs.s: Factoring each radicand gives \(\sqrt{(x+5)^2} + \sqrt{(x+1)^2}\). Since \(x > 0\), combining terms gives \((x+5) + (x+1) = 2x + 6\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle 2\sqrt{4x^2+20x+25} - 3\sqrt{x^2+6x+9}\)
qs.s: Factor each radicand to obtain \(2\sqrt{(2x+5)^2} - 3\sqrt{(x+3)^2} = 2(2x+5) - 3(x+3)\). Expanding and combining like terms gives \(4x + 10 - 3x - 9 = x + 1\).

qs.q:
Simplify the expression. All variables represent positive numbers:
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{4x^2+12x+9} - \sqrt{9x^2+24x+16}\)
