qs.q: Find the product and simplify: \((2\sqrt[3]{2} + \sqrt[3]{5})(4\sqrt[3]{4} - 2\sqrt[3]{10} + \sqrt[3]{25})\)
qs.s: Using the sum of cubes formula with \(a = 2\sqrt[3]{2}\) and \(b = \sqrt[3]{5}\), the product equals \((2\sqrt[3]{2})^3 + (\sqrt[3]{5})^3 = 8(2) + 5 = 21\).

qs.q: Find the product and simplify: \((\sqrt[3]{4} - 2)(2\sqrt[3]{2} + 2\sqrt[3]{4} + 4)\)
qs.s: Recognizing that \(2\sqrt[3]{2} = \sqrt[3]{16} = (\sqrt[3]{4})^2\), the product matches \((a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2) = a^3 - b^3\) with \(a = \sqrt[3]{4}\) and \(b = 2\), giving \((\sqrt[3]{4})^3 - 2^3 = 4 - 8 = -4\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((\sqrt[3]{7} - \sqrt[3]{3})(\sqrt[3]{49} + \sqrt[3]{21} + \sqrt[3]{9})\)
Expand and simplify: \((\sqrt[3]{6} + \sqrt[3]{2})(\sqrt[3]{36} - \sqrt[3]{12} + \sqrt[3]{4})\)
qs.s: Using the sum of cubes formula \((a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2) = a^3+b^3\) with \(a=\sqrt[3]{6}\) and \(b=\sqrt[3]{2}\), the product evaluates to \((\sqrt[3]{6})^3 + (\sqrt[3]{2})^3 = 6 + 2 = 8\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((\sqrt[3]{5} + \sqrt[3]{2})(\sqrt[3]{25} - \sqrt[3]{10} + \sqrt[3]{4})\)
qs.s: Using the sum of cubes formula \((a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2) = a^3+b^3\) with \(a=\sqrt[3]{5}\) and \(b=\sqrt[3]{2}\), the expression simplifies to \((\sqrt[3]{5})^3 + (\sqrt[3]{2})^3 = 5 + 2 = 7\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((\sqrt[3]{7} - \sqrt[3]{2})(\sqrt[3]{49} + \sqrt[3]{14} + \sqrt[3]{4})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of cubes formula \((a-b)(a^2+ab+b^2) = a^3-b^3\) with \(a=\sqrt[3]{7}\) and \(b=\sqrt[3]{2}\), the product is \((\sqrt[3]{7})^3 - (\sqrt[3]{2})^3 = 7 - 2 = 5\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((\sqrt[3]{5} - \sqrt[3]{3})(\sqrt[3]{25} + \sqrt[3]{15} + \sqrt[3]{9})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of cubes formula \((a-b)(a^2+ab+b^2) = a^3-b^3\) with \(a=\sqrt[3]{5}\) and \(b=\sqrt[3]{3}\), we get \((\sqrt[3]{5})^3 - (\sqrt[3]{3})^3 = 5 - 3 = 2\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((3\sqrt[3]{2} - 2\sqrt[3]{3})(9\sqrt[3]{4} + 6\sqrt[3]{6} + 4\sqrt[3]{9})\)
qs.s: Applying the difference of cubes formula \((a-b)(a^2+ab+b^2) = a^3-b^3\) with \(a=3\sqrt[3]{2}\) and \(b=2\sqrt[3]{3}\) gives \((3\sqrt[3]{2})^3 - (2\sqrt[3]{3})^3 = 27(2) - 8(3) = 54 - 24 = 30\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((\sqrt[3]{9} - \sqrt[3]{4})(3\sqrt[3]{3} + \sqrt[3]{36} + 2\sqrt[3]{2})\)
qs.s: Rewriting \(3\sqrt[3]{3} = \sqrt[3]{81} = (\sqrt[3]{9})^2\) and \(2\sqrt[3]{2} = \sqrt[3]{16} = (\sqrt[3]{4})^2\) reveals the difference of cubes \((a-b)(a^2+ab+b^2) = a^3-b^3\), which simplifies to \((\sqrt[3]{9})^3 - (\sqrt[3]{4})^3 = 9 - 4 = 5\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((2\sqrt[3]{3} + \sqrt[3]{5})(4\sqrt[3]{9} - 2\sqrt[3]{15} + \sqrt[3]{25})\)
qs.s: Recognizing the sum of cubes pattern \((a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2) = a^3+b^3\) with \(a=2\sqrt[3]{3}\) and \(b=\sqrt[3]{5}\), we calculate \((2\sqrt[3]{3})^3 + (\sqrt[3]{5})^3 = 8(3) + 5 = 29\).
Apply the sum of cubes to the first product to get \(4+3=7\), and difference of cubes to the second to get \(5-2=3\). Subtracting gives \(7 - 3 = 4\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((2\sqrt[3]{4} + 3)(8\sqrt[3]{2} - 6\sqrt[3]{4} + 9)\)

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{5x}(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{5})\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\sqrt{5x}\) across the binomial to obtain \(\sqrt{5x^2} + \sqrt{25x}\). Simplifying each radical gives \(x\sqrt{5} + 5\sqrt{x}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{7x}(\sqrt{7} + 2\sqrt{x})\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\sqrt{7x}\) to get \(\sqrt{49x} + 2\sqrt{7x^2}\). Simplifying each radical produces \(7\sqrt{x} + 2x\sqrt{7}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{3x}(\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{x})\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\sqrt{3x}\) to get \(\sqrt{9x} - \sqrt{3x^2}\). Simplifying the perfect square factors yields \(3\sqrt{x} - x\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{2y}(\sqrt{8} - \sqrt{y})\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\sqrt{2y}\) to obtain \(\sqrt{16y} - \sqrt{2y^2}\). Extracting perfect squares simplifies the expression to \(4\sqrt{y} - y\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{3a}(\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{12})\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\sqrt{3a}\) to get \(\sqrt{3a^2} - \sqrt{36a}\). Simplifying both radicals yields \(a\sqrt{3} - 6\sqrt{a}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle (2\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{3})(\sqrt{x} + 4\sqrt{3})\)
qs.s: Expand using FOIL: \(2\sqrt{x}\cdot\sqrt{x} + 8\sqrt{3x} - \sqrt{3x} - 4(\sqrt{3})^2 = 2x + 8\sqrt{3x} - \sqrt{3x} - 12\). Combining like radicals yields \(2x + 7\sqrt{3x} - 12\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle (2\sqrt{5x} - 3\sqrt{3})(2\sqrt{5x} + 3\sqrt{3})\)
qs.s: Use the difference of squares formula \((a - b)(a + b) = a^2 - b^2\) to get \((2\sqrt{5x})^2 - (3\sqrt{3})^2\). Simplifying gives \(4(5x) - 9(3) = 20x - 27\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{3x}(\sqrt{12x} - 2\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{27})\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\sqrt{3x}\) across the trinomial to obtain \(\sqrt{36x^2} - 2\sqrt{3x^2} + \sqrt{81x}\). Simplifying each term gives \(6x - 2x\sqrt{3} + 9\sqrt{x}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle (3\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y})(2\sqrt{x} + 5\sqrt{y})\)
qs.s: Multiply the binomials using the distributive property: \(6x + 15\sqrt{xy} - 4\sqrt{xy} - 10y\). Combining the middle radical terms gives \(6x + 11\sqrt{xy} - 10y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle (2\sqrt{x} - 3\sqrt{2})^2\)
qs.s: Apply the square of a binomial formula \((a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2\) to obtain \((2\sqrt{x})^2 - 2(2\sqrt{x})(3\sqrt{2}) + (3\sqrt{2})^2 = 4x - 12\sqrt{2x} + 18\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume \(a > 0\).
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{3a}(\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{3})\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\sqrt{3a}\) across the difference: \(\sqrt{3a}\cdot\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{3a}\cdot\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{3a^2} - \sqrt{9a} = a\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{a}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume \(b > 0\).
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{10b}(\sqrt{10} - \sqrt{b})\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\sqrt{10b}\) across the difference: \(\sqrt{10b}\cdot\sqrt{10} - \sqrt{10b}\cdot\sqrt{b} = \sqrt{100b} - \sqrt{10b^2} = 10\sqrt{b} - b\sqrt{10}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume \(x > 0\).
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{5x}(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{5})\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\sqrt{5x}\) across the sum: \(\sqrt{5x}\cdot\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{5x}\cdot\sqrt{5} = \sqrt{5x^2} + \sqrt{25x} = x\sqrt{5} + 5\sqrt{x}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume \(m > 0\).
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{2m}(\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{m})\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\sqrt{2m}\) across the sum: \(\sqrt{2m}\cdot\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{2m}\cdot\sqrt{m} = \sqrt{4m} + \sqrt{2m^2} = 2\sqrt{m} + m\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume \(w > 0\).
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{6w}(\sqrt{w} - \sqrt{6})\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\sqrt{6w}\) across the difference: \(\sqrt{6w}\cdot\sqrt{w} - \sqrt{6w}\cdot\sqrt{6} = \sqrt{6w^2} - \sqrt{36w} = w\sqrt{6} - 6\sqrt{w}\).

qs.q:
Expand and simplify. Assume \(x, y > 0\).
\(\displaystyle (2\sqrt{x} - 3\sqrt{y})^2\)
qs.s: Use the formula \((a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2\): \((2\sqrt{x})^2 - 2(2\sqrt{x})(3\sqrt{y}) + (3\sqrt{y})^2 = 4x - 12\sqrt{xy} + 9y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume \(x > 0\).
\(\displaystyle (2\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{2})(\sqrt{x} - 4\sqrt{2})\)
qs.s: Multiply using FOIL: \(2\sqrt{x}\cdot\sqrt{x} - 8\sqrt{2x} + 3\sqrt{2x} - 12(\sqrt{2})^2 = 2x - 5\sqrt{2x} - 24\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume \(x, y > 0\).
\(\displaystyle (3\sqrt{2x} + 4\sqrt{y})(3\sqrt{2x} - 4\sqrt{y})\)
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares formula \((a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2\): \((3\sqrt{2x})^2 - (4\sqrt{y})^2 = 9(2x) - 16y = 18x - 16y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume \(x > 0\).
\(\displaystyle 3\sqrt{2x}(\sqrt{8x} - 2\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{18})\)
qs.s: Distribute \(3\sqrt{2x}\) to each term: \(3\sqrt{2x}\cdot\sqrt{8x} - 3\sqrt{2x}\cdot 2\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{2x}\cdot\sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{16x^2} - 6\sqrt{2x^2} + 3\sqrt{36x} = 12x - 6x\sqrt{2} + 18\sqrt{x}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume \(x, y > 0\).
\(\displaystyle (3\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y})(2\sqrt{x} + 5\sqrt{y})\)
qs.s: Multiply using FOIL: \(6(\sqrt{x})^2 + 15\sqrt{xy} - 4\sqrt{xy} - 10(\sqrt{y})^2 = 6x + 11\sqrt{xy} - 10y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive:
\((5y + \sqrt{2})(5y - \sqrt{2})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula \((a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2\), we get \((5y)^2 - (\sqrt{2})^2 = 25y^2 - 2\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive:
\((6b + \sqrt{10})(6b - \sqrt{10})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula, \((6b)^2 - (\sqrt{10})^2 = 36b^2 - 10\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive:
\((3x - \sqrt{5})(3x + \sqrt{5})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula \((a - b)(a + b) = a^2 - b^2\), we have \((3x)^2 - (\sqrt{5})^2 = 9x^2 - 5\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive:
\((2w - \sqrt{13})(2w + \sqrt{13})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula, \((2w)^2 - (\sqrt{13})^2 = 4w^2 - 13\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive:
\((4a - \sqrt{7})(4a + \sqrt{7})\)
qs.s: Applying the difference of squares identity, \((4a)^2 - (\sqrt{7})^2 = 16a^2 - 7\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive:
\((3x - \sqrt{2})(3x + \sqrt{2})(9x^2 + 2)\)
qs.s: First multiply the first two factors to get \((3x)^2 - (\sqrt{2})^2 = 9x^2 - 2\). Then multiply \((9x^2 - 2)(9x^2 + 2) = (9x^2)^2 - 2^2 = 81x^4 - 4\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive:
\((5x - 2\sqrt{3y})(5x + 2\sqrt{3y})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula, \((5x)^2 - (2\sqrt{3y})^2 = 25x^2 - 4(3y) = 25x^2 - 12y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive:
\((2x^2 - 3\sqrt{x})(2x^2 + 3\sqrt{x})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((2x^2)^2 - (3\sqrt{x})^2 = 4x^4 - 9x\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive:
\((3\sqrt{2x} - 2\sqrt{5y})(3\sqrt{2x} + 2\sqrt{5y})\)

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive:
\((2x\sqrt{y} + 5y\sqrt{x})(2x\sqrt{y} - 5y\sqrt{x})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula, \((2x\sqrt{y})^2 - (5y\sqrt{x})^2 = 4x^2(y) - 25y^2(x) = 4x^2y - 25xy^2\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((3x - \sqrt{10})(3x - \sqrt{10})\)

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((2x + \sqrt{5})(2x + \sqrt{5})\)
qs.s: Use the special product formula \((a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2\): \((2x)^2 + 2(2x)(\sqrt{5}) + (\sqrt{5})^2 = 4x^2 + 4x\sqrt{5} + 5\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((4y - \sqrt{7})(4y - \sqrt{7})\)

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((5a + \sqrt{3})(5a + \sqrt{3})\)

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((3x - \sqrt{2})(3x - \sqrt{2})\)
qs.s: Use the special product formula \((a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2\): \((3x)^2 - 2(3x)(\sqrt{2}) + (\sqrt{2})^2 = 9x^2 - 6x\sqrt{2} + 2\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((3x\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{5})(3x\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{5})\)

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((2\sqrt{x} - 3)(4x + 6\sqrt{x} + 9)\)
qs.s: Distribute each term across the trinomial: \(2\sqrt{x}(4x + 6\sqrt{x} + 9) - 3(4x + 6\sqrt{x} + 9) = (8x\sqrt{x} + 12x + 18\sqrt{x}) - (12x + 18\sqrt{x} + 27) = 8x\sqrt{x} - 27\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((3\sqrt{2x} - 2\sqrt{3})(2\sqrt{2x} + 5\sqrt{3})\)

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((2x\sqrt{5} - 3\sqrt{x})(2x\sqrt{5} - 3\sqrt{x})\)

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((2\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{6})(5\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{24})\)
qs.s: Simplify \(\sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6}\) to get \((2\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{6})(5\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{6})\), then expand by FOIL: \(10x - 4\sqrt{6x} + 15\sqrt{6x} - 36 = 10x + 11\sqrt{6x} - 36\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{x+7})^2\)
qs.s: Squaring a principal square root eliminates the radical, giving \((\sqrt{x+7})^2 = x+7\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{5b+6})^2\)
qs.s: Applying the rule \((\sqrt{A})^2 = A\), the expression simplifies directly to \(5b+6\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{3y+4})^2\)
qs.s: Using the property \((\sqrt{A})^2 = A\) for any positive expression \(A\), we obtain \((\sqrt{3y+4})^2 = 3y+4\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{2a+9})^2\)
qs.s: Squaring the radical undoes the square root, yielding \((\sqrt{2a+9})^2 = 2a+9\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{4n+1})^2\)
qs.s: Squaring the square root produces the radicand directly: \((\sqrt{4n+1})^2 = 4n+1\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((3\sqrt{2x+5})^2\)
qs.s: Square both the coefficient and the radical to get \(3^2(\sqrt{2x+5})^2 = 9(2x+5)\), then distribute to get \(18x + 45\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((2x\sqrt{3x+4})^2\)
qs.s: Square the monomial \((2x)^2 = 4x^2\) and the radical \((\sqrt{3x+4})^2 = 3x+4\), then multiply to obtain \(4x^2(3x+4) = 12x^3 + 16x^2\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{2x+3})^2(\sqrt{x+4})^2\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical squared to get \((2x+3)(x+4)\), then expand using the distributive property: \(2x^2 + 8x + 3x + 12 = 2x^2 + 11x + 12\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{7x+11})^2 - (\sqrt{3x+4})^2\)
qs.s: Simplify each squared radical to obtain \((7x+11) - (3x+4)\), then distribute the negative sign and combine like terms: \(7x - 3x + 11 - 4 = 4x + 7\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((2\sqrt{4x+1})^2 - (\sqrt{6x+5})^2\)
qs.s: Simplify the squares to get \(4(4x+1) - (6x+5) = 16x + 4 - 6x - 5\), which simplifies to \(10x - 1\).

qs.q: Find the product and simplify: \((\sqrt{x} + 7)^2\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the formula \((a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2\), we expand to get \((\sqrt{x})^2 + 2(\sqrt{x})(7) + 7^2 = x + 14\sqrt{x} + 49\).

qs.q: Find the product and simplify: \((\sqrt{m} + 8)^2\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the formula \((a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2\), we expand to get \((\sqrt{m})^2 + 2(\sqrt{m})(8) + 8^2 = m + 16\sqrt{m} + 64\).

qs.q: Find the product and simplify: \((\sqrt{a} - 3)^2\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the formula \((a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2\), we expand to get \((\sqrt{a})^2 - 2(\sqrt{a})(3) + 3^2 = a - 6\sqrt{a} + 9\).

qs.q: Find the product and simplify: \((\sqrt{y} + 5)^2\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the formula \((a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2\), we expand to get \((\sqrt{y})^2 + 2(\sqrt{y})(5) + 5^2 = y + 10\sqrt{y} + 25\).

qs.q: Find the product and simplify: \((\sqrt{w} - 4)^2\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the formula \((a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2\), we expand to get \((\sqrt{w})^2 - 2(\sqrt{w})(4) + 4^2 = w - 8\sqrt{w} + 16\).

qs.q: Find the product and simplify: \((2\sqrt{3x} - 5)^2\). Assume all variables are positive.
Find the product and simplify: \((2\sqrt{a} - 5\sqrt{b})^2\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the formula \((a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2\), we get \((2\sqrt{a})^2 - 2(2\sqrt{a})(5\sqrt{b}) + (5\sqrt{b})^2 = 4a - 20\sqrt{ab} + 25b\).

qs.q: Find the product and simplify: \((3\sqrt{x} + 4)^2\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the formula \((a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2\), we have \((3\sqrt{x})^2 + 2(3\sqrt{x})(4) + 4^2 = 9x + 24\sqrt{x} + 16\).

qs.q: Find the product and simplify: \((2\sqrt{x} + 3)(\sqrt{x} - 5)\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the FOIL method, \((2\sqrt{x})(\sqrt{x}) - 5(2\sqrt{x}) + 3(\sqrt{x}) - 15 = 2x - 10\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{x} - 15 = 2x - 7\sqrt{x} - 15\).

qs.q: Find the product and simplify: \((3\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y})(2\sqrt{x} + 5\sqrt{y})\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using FOIL, expand to get \((3\sqrt{x})(2\sqrt{x}) + (3\sqrt{x})(5\sqrt{y}) - (2\sqrt{y})(2\sqrt{x}) - (2\sqrt{y})(5\sqrt{y}) = 6x + 15\sqrt{xy} - 4\sqrt{xy} - 10y = 6x + 11\sqrt{xy} - 10y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{x+6} + 3)^2\)
qs.s: Expand using \((A + B)^2 = A^2 + 2AB + B^2\) to get \((\sqrt{x+6})^2 + 2(3)\sqrt{x+6} + 3^2 = x + 6 + 6\sqrt{x+6} + 9\). Combining like terms yields \(x + 15 + 6\sqrt{x+6}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{x-2} + 5)^2\)
qs.s: Apply the special product formula \((A + B)^2 = A^2 + 2AB + B^2\) to get \((\sqrt{x-2})^2 + 2(5)\sqrt{x-2} + 5^2 = x - 2 + 10\sqrt{x-2} + 25\). Combining constant terms yields \(x + 23 + 10\sqrt{x-2}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{a-5} - 2)^2\)
qs.s: Expand using \((A - B)^2 = A^2 - 2AB + B^2\) to get \((\sqrt{a-5})^2 - 2(2)\sqrt{a-5} + 2^2 = a - 5 - 4\sqrt{a-5} + 4\). Combining like terms gives \(a - 1 - 4\sqrt{a-5}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{x+5} - 3)^2\)
qs.s: Apply the special product formula \((A - B)^2 = A^2 - 2AB + B^2\) to get \((\sqrt{x+5})^2 - 2(3)\sqrt{x+5} + 3^2 = x + 5 - 6\sqrt{x+5} + 9\). Combining like terms gives \(x + 14 - 6\sqrt{x+5}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{y+4} - 6)^2\)
qs.s: Expand using \((A - B)^2 = A^2 - 2AB + B^2\) to obtain \((\sqrt{y+4})^2 - 2(6)\sqrt{y+4} + 6^2 = y + 4 - 12\sqrt{y+4} + 36\). Combining constant terms yields \(y + 40 - 12\sqrt{y+4}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((3\sqrt{x+2} - 1)(2\sqrt{x+2} + 5)\)
qs.s: Use FOIL to multiply the terms: \(6(\sqrt{x+2})^2 + 15\sqrt{x+2} - 2\sqrt{x+2} - 5 = 6(x+2) + 13\sqrt{x+2} - 5\). Distributing and combining constants produces \(6x + 12 + 13\sqrt{x+2} - 5 = 6x + 7 + 13\sqrt{x+2}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((2\sqrt{x-1} + 3)(\sqrt{x-1} - 5)\)
qs.s: Use the distributive property (FOIL) to get \(2(\sqrt{x-1})^2 - 10\sqrt{x-1} + 3\sqrt{x-1} - 15 = 2(x-1) - 7\sqrt{x-1} - 15\). Expanding and combining like terms yields \(2x - 2 - 7\sqrt{x-1} - 15 = 2x - 17 - 7\sqrt{x-1}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{2x+3} - 4)(\sqrt{2x+3} + 6)\)
qs.s: Use FOIL to expand: \((\sqrt{2x+3})^2 + 6\sqrt{2x+3} - 4\sqrt{2x+3} - 24 = 2x + 3 + 2\sqrt{2x+3} - 24\). Combining constant terms gives \(2x - 21 + 2\sqrt{2x+3}\).

qs.q:

\((3\sqrt{2x-1} - 4)^2\)

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((2\sqrt{x+5} - 3)^2\)
qs.s: Using \((A - B)^2 = A^2 - 2AB + B^2\), expand to get \((2\sqrt{x+5})^2 - 2(2\sqrt{x+5})(3) + 3^2 = 4(x+5) - 12\sqrt{x+5} + 9\). Distribute and combine like terms to get \(4x + 20 - 12\sqrt{x+5} + 9 = 4x + 29 - 12\sqrt{x+5}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{m+3} - 7)(\sqrt{m+3} + 7)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula, \((\sqrt{m+3})^2 - 7^2 = (m + 3) - 49 = m - 46\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{x+7} - 3)(\sqrt{x+7} + 3)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula \((a-b)(a+b) = a^2 - b^2\), we obtain \((\sqrt{x+7})^2 - 3^2 = (x + 7) - 9 = x - 2\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{a+2} + 5)(\sqrt{a+2} - 5)\)
qs.s: Applying the difference of squares formula gives \((\sqrt{a+2})^2 - 5^2 = (a + 2) - 25 = a - 23\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{y-5} - 6)(\sqrt{y-5} + 6)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula, \((\sqrt{y-5})^2 - 6^2 = (y - 5) - 36 = y - 41\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{w-8} + 4)(\sqrt{w-8} - 4)\)
qs.s: Applying the difference of squares formula yields \((\sqrt{w-8})^2 - 4^2 = (w - 8) - 16 = w - 24\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{10x+7} - 3\sqrt{x})(\sqrt{10x+7} + 3\sqrt{x})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula, \((\sqrt{10x+7})^2 - (3\sqrt{x})^2 = (10x + 7) - 9x = x + 7\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((3\sqrt{x-2} - \sqrt{2x+5})(3\sqrt{x-2} + \sqrt{2x+5})\)
qs.s: Applying the difference of squares formula, \([3\sqrt{x-2}]^2 - [\sqrt{2x+5}]^2 = 9(x-2) - (2x+5) = 9x - 18 - 2x - 5 = 7x - 23\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{4x+9} - \sqrt{x+1})(\sqrt{4x+9} + \sqrt{x+1})\)
qs.s: Applying the difference of squares gives \((\sqrt{4x+9})^2 - (\sqrt{x+1})^2 = (4x + 9) - (x + 1) = 4x + 9 - x - 1 = 3x + 8\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((2\sqrt{3x-1} - 3\sqrt{x+2})(2\sqrt{3x-1} + 3\sqrt{x+2})\)
qs.s: Applying the difference of squares formula, \([2\sqrt{3x-1}]^2 - [3\sqrt{x+2}]^2 = 4(3x-1) - 9(x+2) = 12x - 4 - 9x - 18 = 3x - 22\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((2\sqrt{x+3} - 5)(2\sqrt{x+3} + 5)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula, \((2\sqrt{x+3})^2 - 5^2 = 4(x+3) - 25 = 4x + 12 - 25 = 4x - 13\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((2\sqrt{u} + 3\sqrt{v})^2\)
qs.s: Apply the special product formula \((a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2\): \((2\sqrt{u})^2 + 2(2\sqrt{u})(3\sqrt{v}) + (3\sqrt{v})^2 = 4u + 12\sqrt{uv} + 9v\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{x} + 5\sqrt{y})^2\)
qs.s: Apply the special product formula \((a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2\): \((\sqrt{x})^2 + 2(\sqrt{x})(5\sqrt{y}) + (5\sqrt{y})^2 = x + 10\sqrt{xy} + 25y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((2\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y})^2\)
qs.s: Apply the special product formula \((a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2\): \((2\sqrt{x})^2 + 2(2\sqrt{x})(\sqrt{y}) + (\sqrt{y})^2 = 4x + 4\sqrt{xy} + y\).

qs.q:

\((4\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b})^2\)
qs.s: Apply the special product formula \((a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2\): \((4\sqrt{a})^2 - 2(4\sqrt{a})(\sqrt{b}) + (\sqrt{b})^2 = 16a - 8\sqrt{ab} + b\).

qs.q:

\((3\sqrt{2x} - 2\sqrt{5y})^2\)

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{5x} + 2\sqrt{3y})(\sqrt{5x} - 4\sqrt{3y})\)
qs.s: Expand using the distributive property (FOIL): \((\sqrt{5x})^2 - 4\sqrt{15xy} + 2\sqrt{15xy} - 8(\sqrt{3y})^2 = 5x - 2\sqrt{15xy} - 8(3y) = 5x - 2\sqrt{15xy} - 24y\).

qs.q:

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((4\sqrt{3x} - 5\sqrt{2y})(4\sqrt{3x} + 5\sqrt{2y})\)
qs.s: Use the difference of squares formula \((a - b)(a + b) = a^2 - b^2\): \((4\sqrt{3x})^2 - (5\sqrt{2y})^2 = 16(3x) - 25(2y) = 48x - 50y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{y} + 2\sqrt{5})(\sqrt{y} - 2\sqrt{5})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula \((a+b)(a-b) = a^2 - b^2\), we calculate \((\sqrt{y})^2 - (2\sqrt{5})^2 = y - 4(5) = y - 20\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{w} - 2\sqrt{7})(\sqrt{w} + 2\sqrt{7})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula, \((\sqrt{w})^2 - (2\sqrt{7})^2 = w - 4(7) = w - 28\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{a} + 5\sqrt{2})(\sqrt{a} - 5\sqrt{2})\)
qs.s: Applying the difference of squares formula yields \((\sqrt{a})^2 - (5\sqrt{2})^2 = a - 25(2) = a - 50\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{p} + 3\sqrt{3})(\sqrt{p} - 3\sqrt{3})\)
qs.s: Applying the difference of squares formula gives \((\sqrt{p})^2 - (3\sqrt{3})^2 = p - 9(3) = p - 27\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{x} - 4\sqrt{3})(\sqrt{x} + 4\sqrt{3})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula, \((\sqrt{x})^2 - (4\sqrt{3})^2 = x - 16(3) = x - 48\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((3\sqrt{2x} + 4\sqrt{5})(3\sqrt{2x} - 4\sqrt{5})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula, \((3\sqrt{2x})^2 - (4\sqrt{5})^2 = 9(2x) - 16(5) = 18x - 80\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((5\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{3y})(5\sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{3y})\)
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares formula to obtain \((5\sqrt{x})^2 - (2\sqrt{3y})^2 = 25x - 4(3y) = 25x - 12y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

qs.q:

Expand and simplify: \((\sqrt{y} + 3)^2 - (\sqrt{y} - 3)^2\). Assume \(y > 0\).
qs.s: Expand both squares to get \((y + 6\sqrt{y} + 9) - (y - 6\sqrt{y} + 9)\). Subtracting like terms leaves \(6\sqrt{y} - (-6\sqrt{y}) = 12\sqrt{y}\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((\sqrt{w} + 4)^2 - (\sqrt{w} - 4)^2\). Assume \(w > 0\).
qs.s: Expand the squares to get \((w + 8\sqrt{w} + 16) - (w - 8\sqrt{w} + 16)\). Combining like terms results in \(8\sqrt{w} - (-8\sqrt{w}) = 16\sqrt{w}\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((\sqrt{a} - 5)^2 - (\sqrt{a} + 5)^2\). Assume \(a > 0\).
qs.s: Expand each binomial to get \((a - 10\sqrt{a} + 25) - (a + 10\sqrt{a} + 25)\). Subtracting like terms yields \(-10\sqrt{a} - 10\sqrt{a} = -20\sqrt{a}\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((\sqrt{m} - 1)^2 - (\sqrt{m} + 1)^2\). Assume \(m > 0\).
qs.s: Expanding both terms yields \((m - 2\sqrt{m} + 1) - (m + 2\sqrt{m} + 1)\). Subtracting gives \(-2\sqrt{m} - 2\sqrt{m} = -4\sqrt{m}\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((\sqrt{z} - 6)^2 - (\sqrt{z} + 6)^2\). Assume \(z > 0\).
qs.s: Expand each square to obtain \((z - 12\sqrt{z} + 36) - (z + 12\sqrt{z} + 36)\). Simplifying gives \(-12\sqrt{z} - 12\sqrt{z} = -24\sqrt{z}\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((\sqrt{x} - 3\sqrt{y})^2 - (\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{y})^2\). Assume \(x > 0\) and \(y > 0\).
qs.s: Expand both squared binomials: \((x - 6\sqrt{xy} + 9y) - (x + 6\sqrt{xy} + 9y)\). Subtracting like terms yields \(-6\sqrt{xy} - 6\sqrt{xy} = -12\sqrt{xy}\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((3\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y})(3\sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{y}) - (3\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y})^2\). Assume \(x > 0\) and \(y > 0\).
qs.s: Using special product rules, expand to \((9x - 4y) - (9x - 12\sqrt{xy} + 4y)\). Distributing the negative gives \(9x - 4y - 9x + 12\sqrt{xy} - 4y = 12\sqrt{xy} - 8y\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((2\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y})^2 - (\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y})^2\). Assume \(x > 0\) and \(y > 0\).
qs.s: Expand each square: \((4x + 4\sqrt{xy} + y) - (x - 4\sqrt{xy} + 4y)\). Subtracting like terms yields \((4x - x) + (4\sqrt{xy} - (-4\sqrt{xy})) + (y - 4y) = 3x + 8\sqrt{xy} - 3y\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((2\sqrt{x} - 3)^2 - (\sqrt{x} + 2)^2\). Assume \(x > 0\).
qs.s: Expand each square: \((4x - 12\sqrt{x} + 9) - (x + 4\sqrt{x} + 4)\). Combine like terms to get \((4x - x) + (-12\sqrt{x} - 4\sqrt{x}) + (9 - 4) = 3x - 16\sqrt{x} + 5\).

qs.q: Expand and simplify: \((\sqrt{x} - 4)^2 - (\sqrt{x} + 5)(\sqrt{x} - 5)\). Assume \(x > 0\).
qs.s: Expand \((\sqrt{x} - 4)^2 = x - 8\sqrt{x} + 16\) and \((\sqrt{x} + 5)(\sqrt{x} - 5) = x - 25\). Subtracting gives \((x - 8\sqrt{x} + 16) - (x - 25) = -8\sqrt{x} + 41\).

qs.q:

\((7 + \sqrt{w})(7 - \sqrt{w})\)
qs.s: Using \((A + B)(A - B) = A^2 - B^2\), we evaluate \(7^2 - (\sqrt{w})^2 = 49 - w\).

\((x - \sqrt{y})(x + \sqrt{y})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula \((A - B)(A + B) = A^2 - B^2\), we obtain \((x)^2 - (\sqrt{y})^2 = x^2 - y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{m} - 6)(\sqrt{m} + 6)\)
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares formula \((A - B)(A + B) = A^2 - B^2\) to get \((\sqrt{m})^2 - 6^2 = m - 36\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{p} - 2q)(\sqrt{p} + 2q)\)
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares formula \((A - B)(A + B) = A^2 - B^2\) to obtain \((\sqrt{p})^2 - (2q)^2 = p - 4q^2\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b})(\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b})\)
qs.s: Using \((A - B)(A + B) = A^2 - B^2\), we calculate \((\sqrt{a})^2 - (\sqrt{b})^2 = a - b\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((2\sqrt{x} - 5\sqrt{y})^2\)
qs.s: Expand using \((A - B)^2 = A^2 - 2AB + B^2\): \((2\sqrt{x})^2 - 2(2\sqrt{x})(5\sqrt{y}) + (5\sqrt{y})^2 = 4x - 20\sqrt{xy} + 25y\).

qs.q:

\((3\sqrt{2x} - 4\sqrt{y})(3\sqrt{2x} + 4\sqrt{y})\)
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares formula: \((3\sqrt{2x})^2 - (4\sqrt{y})^2 = 9(2x) - 16y = 18x - 16y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{x} - 3)(\sqrt{x} + 3)(x + 9)\)
qs.s: First multiply the conjugate pair to get \((\sqrt{x})^2 - 3^2 = x - 9\), then multiply \((x - 9)(x + 9) = x^2 - 9^2 = x^2 - 81\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{3x} - 2\sqrt{y})(\sqrt{12x} + \sqrt{y})\)
qs.s: Multiplying the terms yields \(\sqrt{36x^2} + \sqrt{3xy} - 2\sqrt{12xy} - 2y = 6x + \sqrt{3xy} - 4\sqrt{3xy} - 2y = 6x - 3\sqrt{3xy} - 2y\).

qs.q:

\((\sqrt{x+3} - 5)(\sqrt{x+3} + 5)\)
qs.s: Applying the difference of squares formula, we have \((\sqrt{x+3})^2 - 5^2 = x + 3 - 25 = x - 22\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{w+11} + 3)(\sqrt{w+11} - 3)\)
qs.s: Applying \((A+B)(A-B) = A^2 - B^2\), we simplify \((\sqrt{w+11})^2 - 3^2 = w + 11 - 9 = w + 2\).

qs.q:

\((\sqrt{a+1} - 7)(\sqrt{a+1} + 7)\)

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

qs.q:

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((3\sqrt{2x+1} - 2\sqrt{x+4})(3\sqrt{2x+1} + 2\sqrt{x+4})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula, \((3\sqrt{2x+1})^2 - (2\sqrt{x+4})^2 = 9(2x+1) - 4(x+4) = 18x + 9 - 4x - 16 = 14x - 7\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{x+2} + 3)(\sqrt{x+2} - 5)\)
qs.s: Multiplying using the distributive property yields \((\sqrt{x+2})^2 - 5\sqrt{x+2} + 3\sqrt{x+2} - 15 = x + 2 - 2\sqrt{x+2} - 15 = x - 2\sqrt{x+2} - 13\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{2x+1} - 3)^2\)
qs.s: Expand using the formula \((A-B)^2 = A^2 - 2AB + B^2\) to get \((\sqrt{2x+1})^2 - 2(3)\sqrt{2x+1} + 3^2 = 2x + 1 - 6\sqrt{2x+1} + 9 = 2x - 6\sqrt{2x+1} + 10\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{x+5} + 4)^2\)
qs.s: Using the special product formula \((A+B)^2 = A^2 + 2AB + B^2\), expand to obtain \((\sqrt{x+5})^2 + 2(4)\sqrt{x+5} + 4^2 = x + 5 + 8\sqrt{x+5} + 16 = x + 21 + 8\sqrt{x+5}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{x+3} - 2)^2\)
qs.s: Using the formula \((A-B)^2 = A^2 - 2AB + B^2\), expand to obtain \((\sqrt{x+3})^2 - 2(2)\sqrt{x+3} + 2^2 = x + 3 - 4\sqrt{x+3} + 4 = x + 7 - 4\sqrt{x+3}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{y+4} + 5)^2\)
qs.s: Using the formula \((A+B)^2 = A^2 + 2AB + B^2\), expand to obtain \((\sqrt{y+4})^2 + 2(5)\sqrt{y+4} + 5^2 = y + 4 + 10\sqrt{y+4} + 25 = y + 29 + 10\sqrt{y+4}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{x+1} - 5)^2\)
qs.s: Using the formula \((A-B)^2 = A^2 - 2AB + B^2\), expand to obtain \((\sqrt{x+1})^2 - 2(5)\sqrt{x+1} + 5^2 = x + 1 - 10\sqrt{x+1} + 25 = x + 26 - 10\sqrt{x+1}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{x+7} + 1)^2\)
qs.s: Using the formula \((A+B)^2 = A^2 + 2AB + B^2\), expand to obtain \((\sqrt{x+7})^2 + 2(1)\sqrt{x+7} + 1^2 = x + 7 + 2\sqrt{x+7} + 1 = x + 8 + 2\sqrt{x+7}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((2\sqrt{x+3} - 5)(3\sqrt{x+3} + 2)\)
qs.s: Use the distributive property (FOIL): \((2\sqrt{x+3})(3\sqrt{x+3}) + 2(2\sqrt{x+3}) - 5(3\sqrt{x+3}) - 10 = 6(x+3) + 4\sqrt{x+3} - 15\sqrt{x+3} - 10 = 6x + 18 - 11\sqrt{x+3} - 10 = 6x + 8 - 11\sqrt{x+3}\).

qs.q:

\((4\sqrt{x+2} - 3)(4\sqrt{x+2} + 3)\)
qs.s: Use the difference of squares formula \((A-B)(A+B) = A^2 - B^2\): \((4\sqrt{x+2})^2 - 3^2 = 16(x+2) - 9 = 16x + 32 - 9 = 16x + 23\).

qs.q:

qs.q:

\((\sqrt{2t+7} - \sqrt{2t+2})(\sqrt{2t+7} + \sqrt{2t+2})\)

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{w+8} + \sqrt{w-5})(\sqrt{w+8} - \sqrt{w-5})\)

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{3x + 5\sqrt{x}} + \sqrt{3x - 5\sqrt{x}})(\sqrt{3x + 5\sqrt{x}} - \sqrt{3x - 5\sqrt{x}})\)
qs.s: Using \((a+b)(a-b) = a^2 - b^2\), we get \((\sqrt{3x+5\sqrt{x}})^2 - (\sqrt{3x-5\sqrt{x}})^2 = (3x+5\sqrt{x}) - (3x-5\sqrt{x}) = 10\sqrt{x}\).

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{5x+3y} + \sqrt{2x-y})(\sqrt{5x+3y} - \sqrt{2x-y})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula, \((\sqrt{5x+3y})^2 - (\sqrt{2x-y})^2 = (5x+3y) - (2x-y) = 3x + 4y\).

\((3\sqrt{2x+5} + 2\sqrt{3x-1})(3\sqrt{2x+5} - 2\sqrt{3x-1})\)

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{x^2+6x+2} + \sqrt{x^2-2x-3})(\sqrt{x^2+6x+2} - \sqrt{x^2-2x-3})\)

Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{5a} + 2\sqrt{b})(\sqrt{5a} - 6\sqrt{b})\)
qs.s: Expand using FOIL: \((\sqrt{5a})^2 - 6\sqrt{5ab} + 2\sqrt{5ab} - 12(\sqrt{b})^2 = 5a - 4\sqrt{5ab} - 12b\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{6x} + 3\sqrt{y})(\sqrt{6x} - 2\sqrt{y})\)
qs.s: Expand using FOIL: \((\sqrt{6x})^2 - 2\sqrt{6xy} + 3\sqrt{6xy} - 6(\sqrt{y})^2 = 6x + \sqrt{6xy} - 6y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{2a} - 3\sqrt{b})(\sqrt{2a} + 4\sqrt{b})\)
qs.s: Expand using FOIL: \((\sqrt{2a})^2 + 4\sqrt{2ab} - 3\sqrt{2ab} - 12(\sqrt{b})^2 = 2a + \sqrt{2ab} - 12b\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{3x} + \sqrt{y})(\sqrt{3x} - 4\sqrt{y})\)
qs.s: Expand using FOIL: \((\sqrt{3x})^2 - 4\sqrt{3xy} + \sqrt{3xy} - 4(\sqrt{y})^2 = 3x - 3\sqrt{3xy} - 4y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((3\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y})(2\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y}) - (\sqrt{x} - 4\sqrt{y})^2\)
qs.s: Expand the first product to get \(6x - \sqrt{xy} - 2y\), and expand the square to get \(x - 8\sqrt{xy} + 16y\). Subtracting the two expressions yields \((6x - \sqrt{xy} - 2y) - (x - 8\sqrt{xy} + 16y) = 5x + 7\sqrt{xy} - 18y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{2x} - 3\sqrt{y})(\sqrt{2x} + 3\sqrt{y})(2x + 9y)\)
qs.s: First multiply the conjugate pair: \((\sqrt{2x} - 3\sqrt{y})(\sqrt{2x} + 3\sqrt{y}) = 2x - 9y\). Then multiply by the remaining factor: \((2x - 9y)(2x + 9y) = 4x^2 - 81y^2\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((2\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{y})(4x - 6\sqrt{xy} + 9y)\)
qs.s: Distribute each term of the binomial into the trinomial: \(2\sqrt{x}(4x - 6\sqrt{xy} + 9y) + 3\sqrt{y}(4x - 6\sqrt{xy} + 9y) = (8x\sqrt{x} - 12x\sqrt{y} + 18y\sqrt{x}) + (12x\sqrt{y} - 18y\sqrt{x} + 27y\sqrt{y}) = 8x\sqrt{x} + 27y\sqrt{y}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{8x} + \sqrt{3y})(\sqrt{2x} - 2\sqrt{12y})\)
qs.s: Multiply terms: \((\sqrt{8x})(\sqrt{2x}) - 2\sqrt{96xy} + \sqrt{6xy} - 2\sqrt{36y^2} = 4x - 8\sqrt{6xy} + \sqrt{6xy} - 12y = 4x - 7\sqrt{6xy} - 12y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{3x} + \sqrt{2y} - 5)(\sqrt{3x} + \sqrt{2y} + 5)\)
qs.s: Group as \([(\sqrt{3x} + \sqrt{2y}) - 5][(\sqrt{3x} + \sqrt{2y}) + 5] = (\sqrt{3x} + \sqrt{2y})^2 - 25\). Expanding the square gives \(3x + 2\sqrt{6xy} + 2y - 25\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{m+16})^2 - (\sqrt{m} - 4)^2\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \((m + 16) - (m - 8\sqrt{m} + 16)\). Distributing the negative yields \(m + 16 - m + 8\sqrt{m} - 16 = 8\sqrt{m}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{2x+1})^2 - (\sqrt{2x} + 1)^2\)
qs.s: Expanding each term yields \((2x + 1) - (2x + 2\sqrt{2x} + 1)\). Subtracting gives \(2x + 1 - 2x - 2\sqrt{2x} - 1 = -2\sqrt{2x}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{x+y})^2 - (\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y})^2\)
qs.s: Expanding both terms gives \((x + y) - (x + 2\sqrt{xy} + y)\). Distributing the negative and combining like terms results in \(-2\sqrt{xy}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{a} + 3)^2 - (\sqrt{a+9})^2\)
qs.s: Expanding the binomial square gives \((\sqrt{a} + 3)^2 = a + 6\sqrt{a} + 9\), and squaring the radical gives \((\sqrt{a+9})^2 = a + 9\). Subtracting yields \((a + 6\sqrt{a} + 9) - (a + 9) = 6\sqrt{a}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{x+4})^2 - (\sqrt{x} + 2)^2\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \((\sqrt{x+4})^2 - (\sqrt{x} + 2)^2 = (x + 4) - (x + 4\sqrt{x} + 4)\). Distributing the negative sign and combining like terms yields \(-4\sqrt{x}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((3\sqrt{2x+1})^2 - (\sqrt{18x} + 1)^2\)
qs.s: Squaring the first term gives \(9(2x + 1) = 18x + 9\), and squaring the binomial gives \((\sqrt{18x} + 1)^2 = 18x + 2\sqrt{18x} + 1 = 18x + 6\sqrt{2x} + 1\). Subtracting gives \((18x + 9) - (18x + 6\sqrt{2x} + 1) = 8 - 6\sqrt{2x}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{2x+5} + 3)^2 - (\sqrt{2x+5} - 3)^2\)
qs.s: Expanding both binomial squares gives \((2x + 14 + 6\sqrt{2x+5}) - (2x + 14 - 6\sqrt{2x+5})\). Distributing the negative cancels the rational terms, leaving \(6\sqrt{2x+5} + 6\sqrt{2x+5} = 12\sqrt{2x+5}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((\sqrt{x+4} + 3)(\sqrt{x+4} - 3) - (\sqrt{x} - 2)^2\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares gives \((\sqrt{x+4})^2 - 3^2 = x + 4 - 9 = x - 5\), and expanding the square gives \((\sqrt{x} - 2)^2 = x - 4\sqrt{x} + 4\). Subtracting gives \((x - 5) - (x - 4\sqrt{x} + 4) = 4\sqrt{x} - 9\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((2\sqrt{x} + 1)^2 - (\sqrt{3x+4})^2\)
qs.s: Expanding the binomial square gives \(4x + 4\sqrt{x} + 1\), and squaring the radical gives \(3x + 4\). Subtracting yields \((4x + 4\sqrt{x} + 1) - (3x + 4) = x + 4\sqrt{x} - 3\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.

\((2\sqrt{x+3})^2 - (2\sqrt{x} + 3)^2\)
qs.s: Squaring each term gives \(4(x + 3) - (4x + 12\sqrt{x} + 9) = (4x + 12) - (4x + 12\sqrt{x} + 9)\). Distributing the negative and combining like terms yields \(3 - 12\sqrt{x}\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle (\sqrt[3]{y} + 2)(\sqrt[3]{y^2} - 2\sqrt[3]{y} + 4)\)
qs.s: Using the sum of cubes formula \((a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2) = a^3 + b^3\) with \(a = \sqrt[3]{y}\) and \(b = 2\), we get \((\sqrt[3]{y})^3 + 2^3 = y + 8\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle (\sqrt[3]{m} - 3)(\sqrt[3]{m^2} + 3\sqrt[3]{m} + 9)\)
qs.s: Recognizing the difference of cubes pattern \((a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2) = a^3 - b^3\) with \(a = \sqrt[3]{m}\) and \(b = 3\), the expression simplifies to \((\sqrt[3]{m})^3 - 3^3 = m - 27\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle (\sqrt[3]{w} + 4)(\sqrt[3]{w^2} - 4\sqrt[3]{w} + 16)\)
qs.s: Applying the sum of cubes formula \((a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2) = a^3 + b^3\) with \(a = \sqrt[3]{w}\) and \(b = 4\), we obtain \((\sqrt[3]{w})^3 + 4^3 = w + 64\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle (\sqrt[3]{x} - 1)(\sqrt[3]{x^2} + \sqrt[3]{x} + 1)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of cubes formula \((a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2) = a^3 - b^3\) with \(a = \sqrt[3]{x}\) and \(b = 1\), the product simplifies to \((\sqrt[3]{x})^3 - 1^3 = x - 1\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle (\sqrt[3]{x} - \sqrt[3]{y})(\sqrt[3]{x^2} + \sqrt[3]{xy} + \sqrt[3]{y^2})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of cubes formula \((a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2) = a^3 - b^3\) with \(a = \sqrt[3]{x}\) and \(b = \sqrt[3]{y}\), the product simplifies to \((\sqrt[3]{x})^3 - (\sqrt[3]{y})^3 = x - y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle (5\sqrt[3]{2x} - 2)(25\sqrt[3]{4x^2} + 10\sqrt[3]{2x} + 4)\)
qs.s: Applying the difference of cubes formula with \(a = 5\sqrt[3]{2x}\) and \(b = 2\), the product is \((5\sqrt[3]{2x})^3 - 2^3 = 125(2x) - 8 = 250x - 8\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle (\sqrt[3]{x} + 2)(\sqrt[3]{x^2} - 5\sqrt[3]{x} + 3)\)
qs.s: Distribute each term of the binomial across the trinomial to obtain \(x - 5\sqrt[3]{x^2} + 3\sqrt[3]{x} + 2\sqrt[3]{x^2} - 10\sqrt[3]{x} + 6\). Combining like radicals gives \(x - 3\sqrt[3]{x^2} - 7\sqrt[3]{x} + 6\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle (2\sqrt[3]{x} - 5)(4\sqrt[3]{x^2} + 10\sqrt[3]{x} + 25)\)
qs.s: This matches the difference of cubes formula \((a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2) = a^3 - b^3\) with \(a = 2\sqrt[3]{x}\) and \(b = 5\), giving \((2\sqrt[3]{x})^3 - 5^3 = 8x - 125\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle (3\sqrt[3]{2x} + 2\sqrt[3]{y})(9\sqrt[3]{4x^2} - 6\sqrt[3]{2xy} + 4\sqrt[3]{y^2})\)
qs.s: Using the sum of cubes formula with \(a = 3\sqrt[3]{2x}\) and \(b = 2\sqrt[3]{y}\), we find \((3\sqrt[3]{2x})^3 + (2\sqrt[3]{y})^3 = 27(2x) + 8y = 54x + 8y\).

qs.q:
Find the product and simplify. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle (3\sqrt[3]{x} + 2\sqrt[3]{y})(9\sqrt[3]{x^2} - 6\sqrt[3]{xy} + 4\sqrt[3]{y^2})\)
qs.s: Using the sum of cubes formula \((a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2) = a^3 + b^3\) with \(a = 3\sqrt[3]{x}\) and \(b = 2\sqrt[3]{y}\), we compute \((3\sqrt[3]{x})^3 + (2\sqrt[3]{y})^3 = 27x + 8y\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{a} \cdot \sqrt[4]{a}\)
qs.s: Convert each radical to exponential form using a common denominator: \(a^{1/3} \cdot a^{1/4} = a^{4/12 + 3/12} = a^{7/12}\). Written in radical notation, the product is \(\sqrt[12]{a^7}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{y} \cdot \sqrt[4]{y}\)
qs.s: Convert to fractional exponents: \(y^{1/2} \cdot y^{1/4} = y^{2/4 + 1/4} = y^{3/4}\). In radical form, this simplifies to \(\sqrt[4]{y^3}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{c} \cdot \sqrt[5]{c}\)
qs.s: Convert to exponential notation using a common denominator of 15: \(c^{1/3} \cdot c^{1/5} = c^{5/15 + 3/15} = c^{8/15}\). In radical form, this gives \(\sqrt[15]{c^8}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{b} \cdot \sqrt[5]{b}\)
qs.s: Write with fractional exponents having a common denominator of 10: \(b^{1/2} \cdot b^{1/5} = b^{5/10 + 2/10} = b^{7/10}\). In radical form, this is \(\sqrt[10]{b^7}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[4]{z} \cdot \sqrt[6]{z}\)
qs.s: Use fractional exponents with a common denominator of 12: \(z^{1/4} \cdot z^{1/6} = z^{3/12 + 2/12} = z^{5/12}\). In radical form, this is \(\sqrt[12]{z^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{2x} \cdot \sqrt[3]{4x}\)
qs.s: Express under a common index of 6: \(\sqrt[6]{(2x)^3} \cdot \sqrt[6]{(4x)^2} = \sqrt[6]{8x^3 \cdot 16x^2} = \sqrt[6]{128x^5}\). Since \(128 = 2^6 \cdot 2\), simplify to \(2\sqrt[6]{2x^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{x^3 y} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x y^2}\)
qs.s: Convert to a common index of 6: \(\sqrt[6]{(x^3 y)^3} \cdot \sqrt[6]{(x y^2)^2} = \sqrt[6]{x^9 y^3 \cdot x^2 y^4} = \sqrt[6]{x^{11} y^7}\). Simplifying by removing full powers yields \(xy\sqrt[6]{x^5 y}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{a^3 b^3}}{\sqrt[3]{a^2 b}}\)
qs.s: Convert both radicals to index 6: \(\sqrt[6]{(a^3 b^3)^3 / (a^2 b)^2} = \sqrt[6]{a^9 b^9 / (a^4 b^2)} = \sqrt[6]{a^5 b^7}\). Factoring out \(b^6\) gives \(b\sqrt[6]{a^5 b}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{x} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x^2} \cdot \sqrt[4]{x^3}\)
qs.s: Convert each factor to fractional exponents: \(x^{1/2} \cdot x^{2/3} \cdot x^{3/4} = x^{6/12 + 8/12 + 9/12} = x^{23/12}\). Converting to radical form and simplifying yields \(x\sqrt[12]{x^{11}}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{x^5}}{\sqrt[3]{x^2}}\)
qs.s: Convert to fractional exponents: \(x^{5/2} / x^{2/3} = x^{15/6 - 4/6} = x^{11/6}\). In radical form, \(x^{11/6} = \sqrt[6]{x^{11}} = x\sqrt[6]{x^5}\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt{y}}{\sqrt[4]{y}}\)
qs.s: Converting to fractional exponents, \(\frac{y^{1/2}}{y^{1/4}} = y^{2/4 - 1/4} = y^{1/4} = \sqrt[4]{y}\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt{b}}{\sqrt[5]{b}}\)
qs.s: Writing in exponential form gives \(\frac{b^{1/2}}{b^{1/5}} = b^{5/10 - 2/10} = b^{3/10} = \sqrt[10]{b^3}\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{a}}{\sqrt[4]{a}}\)
qs.s: Converting to a common denominator for the exponents, \(\frac{a^{1/3}}{a^{1/4}} = a^{4/12 - 3/12} = a^{1/12} = \sqrt[12]{a}\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{m}}{\sqrt[5]{m}}\)
qs.s: Using fractional exponents, \(\frac{m^{1/3}}{m^{1/5}} = m^{5/15 - 3/15} = m^{2/15} = \sqrt[15]{m^2}\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt[6]{x}}\)
qs.s: Converting to exponential notation yields \(\frac{x^{1/2}}{x^{1/6}} = x^{3/6 - 1/6} = x^{2/6} = x^{1/3} = \sqrt[3]{x}\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt[4]{a^3 b^5}}{\sqrt[3]{a b^2}}\)
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt{x^3 y^5}}{\sqrt[3]{x^2 y}}\)
qs.s: Using the common index 6, \(\frac{\sqrt[6]{(x^3 y^5)^3}}{\sqrt[6]{(x^2 y)^2}} = \sqrt[6]{\frac{x^9 y^{15}}{x^4 y^2}} = \sqrt[6]{x^5 y^{13}} = y^2\sqrt[6]{x^5 y}\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt{x} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x}}{\sqrt[4]{x}}\)
qs.s: Converting to fractional exponents with a common denominator of 12, \(x^{1/2 + 1/3 - 1/4} = x^{6/12 + 4/12 - 3/12} = x^{7/12} = \sqrt[12]{x^7}\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers: \(\frac{\sqrt{8x}}{\sqrt[3]{2x}}\)
qs.s: Converting to the common index 6, \(\frac{\sqrt[6]{(8x)^3}}{\sqrt[6]{(2x)^2}} = \sqrt[6]{\frac{512x^3}{4x^2}} = \sqrt[6]{128x} = \sqrt[6]{64 \cdot 2x} = 2\sqrt[6]{2x}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{x^2} \cdot \sqrt[4]{x^3}\)
qs.s: Convert the radicals to fractional exponents: \(x^{2/3} \cdot x^{3/4} = x^{8/12 + 9/12} = x^{17/12}\). Writing in simplest radical form gives \(x\sqrt[12]{x^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{x} \cdot \sqrt[5]{x^3}\)
qs.s: Convert to rational exponents: \(x^{1/2} \cdot x^{3/5} = x^{5/10 + 6/10} = x^{11/10}\). In simplest radical form, this is \(x\sqrt[10]{x}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{x} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x^2}\)
qs.s: Convert to fractional exponents: \(x^{1/2} \cdot x^{2/3} = x^{3/6 + 4/6} = x^{7/6}\). In simplest radical form, this simplifies to \(x\sqrt[6]{x}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{x} \cdot \sqrt[4]{x^3}\)
qs.s: Write with rational exponents: \(x^{1/3} \cdot x^{3/4} = x^{4/12 + 9/12} = x^{13/12}\). In simplest radical form, this is \(x\sqrt[12]{x}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{y^2} \cdot \sqrt[5]{y^3}\)
qs.s: Convert to rational exponents: \(y^{2/3} \cdot y^{3/5} = y^{10/15 + 9/15} = y^{19/15}\). In simplest radical form, this simplifies to \(y\sqrt[15]{y^4}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{x^5 y^3}}{\sqrt[3]{x^2 y}}\)
qs.s: Convert both radicals to index 6: \(\frac{x^{5/2} y^{3/2}}{x^{2/3} y^{1/3}} = x^{15/6 - 4/6} y^{9/6 - 2/6} = x^{11/6} y^{7/6}\). Factoring out whole powers gives \(x y\sqrt[6]{x^5 y}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle 3\sqrt{x^3} \cdot 2\sqrt[3]{x^4}\)
qs.s: Multiply the coefficients \(3 \cdot 2 = 6\) and the radicals \(x^{3/2} \cdot x^{4/3} = x^{9/6 + 8/6} = x^{17/6}\). Combining and simplifying gives \(6x^2\sqrt[6]{x^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[4]{a^3 b} \cdot \sqrt[3]{a^2 b^2}\)
qs.s: Convert each variable to fractional exponents: \(a^{3/4 + 2/3} b^{1/4 + 2/3} = a^{17/12} b^{11/12}\). Simplifying the power of \(a\) yields \(a\sqrt[12]{a^5 b^{11}}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{x^8}}{\sqrt[4]{x^5}}\)
qs.s: Convert to fractional exponents and subtract: \(x^{8/3} \div x^{5/4} = x^{32/12 - 15/12} = x^{17/12}\). Simplifying gives \(x\sqrt[12]{x^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt{x^5}}{\sqrt[3]{x^4}}\)
qs.s: Convert to fractional exponents: \(\frac{x^{5/2}}{x^{4/3}} = x^{5/2 - 4/3} = x^{15/6 - 8/6} = x^{7/6}\). In simplified radical form, \(x^{7/6} = x\sqrt[6]{x}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt{a^5}}{\sqrt[5]{a^3}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite with fractional exponents: \(\frac{a^{5/2}}{a^{3/5}} = a^{5/2 - 3/5} = a^{25/10 - 6/10} = a^{19/10}\). Simplifying gives \(a^{19/10} = a\sqrt[10]{a^9}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt[4]{b^7}}{\sqrt[3]{b^2}}\)
qs.s: Convert to fractional exponents: \(\frac{b^{7/4}}{b^{2/3}} = b^{7/4 - 2/3} = b^{21/12 - 8/12} = b^{13/12}\). Simplifying gives \(b^{13/12} = b\sqrt[12]{b}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt[3]{y^5}}{\sqrt[4]{y^3}}\)
qs.s: Convert to fractional exponents: \(\frac{y^{5/3}}{y^{3/4}} = y^{5/3 - 3/4} = y^{20/12 - 9/12} = y^{11/12}\). Converting back to radical form yields \(\sqrt[12]{y^{11}}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt[3]{x^7}}{\sqrt{x^3}}\)
qs.s: Express with fractional exponents: \(\frac{x^{7/3}}{x^{3/2}} = x^{7/3 - 3/2} = x^{14/6 - 9/6} = x^{5/6}\). In radical form, this is \(\sqrt[6]{x^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt{x^5 y^3}}{\sqrt[3]{x^2 y^2}}\)
qs.s: Express under a common index of 6: \(\sqrt[6]{\frac{(x^5 y^3)^3}{(x^2 y^2)^2}} = \sqrt[6]{\frac{x^{15}y^9}{x^4 y^4}} = \sqrt[6]{x^{11}y^5}\). Factoring out \(x^6\) gives \(x\sqrt[6]{x^5 y^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt[3]{27x^4}}{\sqrt[4]{9x^2}}\)

Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt{x^5} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x^2}}{\sqrt[4]{x^3}}\)
qs.s: Convert each radical to a fractional exponent: \(x^{5/2} \cdot x^{2/3} / x^{3/4} = x^{5/2 + 2/3 - 3/4}\). Using a common denominator of 12 gives \(x^{30/12 + 8/12 - 9/12} = x^{29/12} = x^2\sqrt[12]{x^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt{8x^5}}{\sqrt[3]{4x^2}}\)
qs.s: Write with base 2 and a common index of 6: \(\sqrt[6]{\frac{(2^3 x^5)^3}{(2^2 x^2)^2}} = \sqrt[6]{\frac{2^9 x^{15}}{2^4 x^4}} = \sqrt[6]{32x^{11}} = x\sqrt[6]{32x^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt[4]{a^7 b^5}}{\sqrt[6]{a^2 b^3}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite under a common index of 12: \(\sqrt[12]{\frac{(a^7 b^5)^3}{(a^2 b^3)^2}} = \sqrt[12]{\frac{a^{21}b^{15}}{a^4 b^6}} = \sqrt[12]{a^{17}b^9}\). Extracting \(a^{12}\) yields \(a\sqrt[12]{a^5 b^9}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{z^3}}{\sqrt[4]{z}}\)
qs.s: Express with fractional exponents: \(z^{3/2 - 1/4} = z^{6/4 - 1/4} = z^{5/4}\). Converting to mixed radical form gives \(z\sqrt[4]{z}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[4]{w^3} \cdot \sqrt[6]{w^5}\)
qs.s: Rewrite using fractional exponents: \(w^{3/4 + 5/6} = w^{9/12 + 10/12} = w^{19/12}\). In simplest radical form, this is \(w\sqrt[12]{w^7}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{b} \cdot \sqrt[4]{b^3}\)
qs.s: Convert to exponential form to obtain \(b^{1/3} \cdot b^{3/4} = b^{4/12 + 9/12} = b^{13/12}\). Simplifying \(b^{13/12}\) gives \(b\sqrt[12]{b}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{x^2} \cdot \sqrt{x}\)
qs.s: Convert the radicals to fractional exponents to get \(x^{2/3} \cdot x^{1/2} = x^{4/6 + 3/6} = x^{7/6}\). In simplest radical form, this simplifies to \(x\sqrt[6]{x}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{y^4}}{\sqrt[4]{y^3}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite with fractional exponents to get \(y^{4/3 - 3/4} = y^{16/12 - 9/12} = y^{7/12}\). Converting back to radical form yields \(\sqrt[12]{y^7}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle 2\sqrt[4]{2x^3} \cdot 3\sqrt{2x}\)
qs.s: Multiply the coefficients to get \(6\), then write radicals with a common index of 4: \(\sqrt[4]{2x^3} \cdot \sqrt[4]{(2x)^2} = \sqrt[4]{8x^5} = x\sqrt[4]{8x}\). Combining gives \(6x\sqrt[4]{8x}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{a} \cdot \sqrt[3]{a^2} \cdot \sqrt[4]{a^3}\)
qs.s: Convert to fractional exponents with common denominator 12: \(a^{6/12 + 8/12 + 9/12} = a^{23/12}\). Simplifying the improper power gives \(a\sqrt[12]{a^{11}}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{a^2} \cdot \sqrt{a}}{\sqrt[6]{a^5}}\)
qs.s: Convert each radical to exponential form: \(a^{2/3 + 1/2 - 5/6} = a^{4/6 + 3/6 - 5/6} = a^{2/6} = a^{1/3}\). In simplest radical form, this is \(\sqrt[3]{a}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{x^2 y} \cdot \sqrt[4]{x^3 y^2}\)
qs.s: Using a common index of 12, the product is \(\sqrt[12]{(x^2 y)^4 (x^3 y^2)^3} = \sqrt[12]{x^{17} y^{10}}\). Extracting \(x^{12}\) yields \(x\sqrt[12]{x^5 y^{10}}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{x^7 y^5}}{\sqrt[6]{x^3 y}}\)
qs.s: Express exponents with a common denominator of 12: \(x^{21/12 - 6/12} y^{15/12 - 2/12} = x^{15/12} y^{13/12}\). Factoring out whole powers gives \(xy\sqrt[12]{x^3 y}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt{u^3 v}}{\sqrt[5]{u^6 v^2}}\)
qs.s: Express both radicals with a common index of 10 to obtain \(\frac{\sqrt[10]{u^{15} v^5}}{\sqrt[10]{u^{12} v^4}} = \sqrt[10]{u^3 v}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt[3]{a^2 b^4}}{\sqrt[4]{a b^3}}\)
qs.s: Convert to a common index of 12 to get \(\frac{\sqrt[12]{a^8 b^{16}}}{\sqrt[12]{a^3 b^9}}\), then divide radicands to obtain \(\sqrt[12]{a^5 b^7}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt[3]{x^2 y^4}}{\sqrt[5]{x^2 y^3}}\)
qs.s: Using a common index of 15, the expression becomes \(\frac{\sqrt[15]{x^{10} y^{20}}}{\sqrt[15]{x^6 y^9}} = \sqrt[15]{x^4 y^{11}}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt{x^3 y}}{\sqrt[3]{x^2 y}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite with a common index of 6 to get \(\frac{\sqrt[6]{x^9 y^3}}{\sqrt[6]{x^4 y^2}}\), then divide radicands to obtain \(\sqrt[6]{x^5 y}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt{m n^3}}{\sqrt[3]{m n^2}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite using a common index of 6 to obtain \(\frac{\sqrt[6]{m^3 n^9}}{\sqrt[6]{m^2 n^4}} = \sqrt[6]{m n^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{x^3y} \cdot \sqrt[4]{16xy^3}\)
qs.s: Convert to a common index of 4: \(\sqrt[4]{(x^3y)^2} \cdot 2\sqrt[4]{xy^3} = 2\sqrt[4]{x^7y^5}\). Extracting perfect 4th powers leaves \(2xy\sqrt[4]{x^3y}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{25x^3y} \cdot \sqrt[3]{27x^2y^4}\)
qs.s: Rewrite with fractional exponents as \(5x^{3/2}y^{1/2} \cdot 3x^{2/3}y^{4/3} = 15x^{9/6+4/6}y^{3/6+8/6} = 15x^{13/6}y^{11/6}\). Simplifying gives \(15x^2y\sqrt[6]{xy^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{4a^3b^5} \cdot \sqrt[3]{a^2b}\)
qs.s: Express using a common index of 6: \(\sqrt[6]{(4a^3b^5)^3 \cdot (a^2b)^2} = \sqrt[6]{64a^{13}b^{17}}\). Simplifying by extracting perfect 6th powers yields \(2a^2b^2\sqrt[6]{ab^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{8x^5y^2} \cdot \sqrt{9xy^3}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to \(2x^{5/3}y^{2/3} \cdot 3x^{1/2}y^{3/2} = 6x^{10/6+3/6}y^{4/6+9/6} = 6x^{13/6}y^{13/6}\). Extracting whole powers gives \(6x^2y^2\sqrt[6]{xy}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{49x^3y^5} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x^4y}\)
qs.s: Write with fractional exponents as \(7x^{3/2}y^{5/2} \cdot x^{4/3}y^{1/3} = 7x^{17/6}y^{17/6}\). Converting back to radical form yields \(7x^2y^2\sqrt[6]{x^5y^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{36x^5y^3z} \cdot \sqrt[3]{27x^2y^4z^5}\)
qs.s: Convert to common index 6: \(\sqrt[6]{(6^2x^5y^3z)^3 \cdot (3^3x^2y^4z^5)^2} = \sqrt[6]{18^6x^{19}y^{17}z^{13}}\). Extracting 6th powers gives \(18x^3y^2z^2\sqrt[6]{xy^5z}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{2x^2y} \cdot \sqrt[4]{8x^3y^3}\)
qs.s: Use the common index 12: \(\sqrt[12]{(2x^2y)^4 \cdot (8x^3y^3)^3} = \sqrt[12]{16x^8y^4 \cdot 512x^9y^9} = \sqrt[12]{8192x^{17}y^{13}}\). Extracting 12th powers leaves \(2xy\sqrt[12]{2x^5y}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{32x^7y^5}}{\sqrt[3]{4x^2y^4}}\)
qs.s: Express under a common index of 6 as \(\sqrt[6]{\frac{(32x^7y^5)^3}{(4x^2y^4)^2}} = \sqrt[6]{\frac{2^{15}x^{21}y^{15}}{2^4x^4y^8}} = \sqrt[6]{2^{11}x^{17}y^7}\). Simplifying gives \(2x^2y\sqrt[6]{32x^5y}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[6]{m^5 n^4}}{\sqrt[3]{m^2 n}}\)
qs.s: Convert the denominator to index 6: \(\sqrt[3]{m^2 n} = \sqrt[6]{(m^2 n)^2} = \sqrt[6]{m^4 n^2}\). Dividing gives \(\sqrt[6]{\frac{m^5 n^4}{m^4 n^2}} = \sqrt[6]{m n^2}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[6]{x^5 y^5}}{\sqrt[3]{x y^2}}\)
qs.s: Convert the denominator to index 6: \(\sqrt[3]{xy^2} = \sqrt[6]{x^2 y^4}\). Dividing gives \(\sqrt[6]{\frac{x^5 y^5}{x^2 y^4}} = \sqrt[6]{x^3 y}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{a^3 b^2}}{\sqrt{a b}}\)
qs.s: Convert the denominator to index 4: \(\sqrt{ab} = \sqrt[4]{a^2 b^2}\). Dividing gives \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{a^3 b^2}{a^2 b^2}} = \sqrt[4]{a}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{x^3 y^3}}{\sqrt{x y}}\)
qs.s: Convert the denominator to index 4: \(\sqrt{xy} = \sqrt[4]{x^2 y^2}\). Dividing gives \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{x^3 y^3}{x^2 y^2}} = \sqrt[4]{xy}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[6]{u^5 v^4}}{\sqrt{u v}}\)
qs.s: Convert the denominator to index 6: \(\sqrt{uv} = \sqrt[6]{u^3 v^3}\). Dividing gives \(\sqrt[6]{\frac{u^5 v^4}{u^3 v^3}} = \sqrt[6]{u^2 v}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{x^3 y} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x y^2}}{\sqrt[6]{x^5 y}}\)
qs.s: Express each radical with a common index of 6: \(\frac{\sqrt[6]{x^9 y^3} \cdot \sqrt[6]{x^2 y^4}}{\sqrt[6]{x^5 y}} = \sqrt[6]{\frac{x^{11} y^7}{x^5 y}} = \sqrt[6]{x^6 y^6} = xy\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{x^3 y^7 z^2}}{\sqrt[6]{x^2 y^3 z}}\)
qs.s: Convert both radicals to index 12: \(\frac{\sqrt[12]{x^9 y^{21} z^6}}{\sqrt[12]{x^4 y^6 z^2}} = \sqrt[12]{x^5 y^{15} z^4} = y \sqrt[12]{x^5 y^3 z^4}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{32 x^7 y^5}}{\sqrt{2 x y}}\)
qs.s: Convert the denominator to index 4: \(\sqrt{2xy} = \sqrt[4]{4x^2 y^2}\). Then divide to get \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{32x^7 y^5}{4x^2 y^2}} = \sqrt[4]{8x^5 y^3} = x\sqrt[4]{8x y^3}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{4 a^2 b^4} \cdot \sqrt{2 a^3 b}\)

Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{16 x^5 y^4}}{\sqrt{2 x y}}\)

Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\sqrt{(4x + 3)^5} \cdot \sqrt[3]{(4x + 3)^2}\)
qs.s: Write with fractional exponents using a common denominator of 6: \((4x + 3)^{5/2 + 2/3} = (4x + 3)^{15/6 + 4/6} = (4x + 3)^{19/6}\). Simplifying \(\frac{19}{6} = 3\frac{1}{6}\) gives \((4x + 3)^3\sqrt[6]{4x + 3}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\sqrt{(5x + 2)^3} \cdot \sqrt[3]{5x + 2}\)
qs.s: Express the radicals with fractional exponents: \((5x + 2)^{3/2} \cdot (5x + 2)^{1/3} = (5x + 2)^{9/6 + 2/6} = (5x + 2)^{11/6}\). Because \(\frac{11}{6} = 1\frac{5}{6}\), this simplifies to \((5x + 2)\sqrt[6]{(5x + 2)^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\sqrt{(2x + 1)^3} \cdot \sqrt[3]{(2x + 1)^4}\)
qs.s: Convert to fractional exponents: \((2x + 1)^{3/2} \cdot (2x + 1)^{4/3} = (2x + 1)^{9/6 + 8/6} = (2x + 1)^{17/6}\). Since \(\frac{17}{6} = 2\frac{5}{6}\), this simplifies to \((2x + 1)^2\sqrt[6]{(2x + 1)^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\sqrt[3]{(3x + 4)^5} \cdot \sqrt{3x + 4}\)
qs.s: Convert each radical to exponential form: \((3x + 4)^{5/3} \cdot (3x + 4)^{1/2} = (3x + 4)^{10/6 + 3/6} = (3x + 4)^{13/6}\). Expressing \(\frac{13}{6} = 2\frac{1}{6}\) in radical form yields \((3x + 4)^2\sqrt[6]{3x + 4}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\sqrt{(x + 6)^3} \cdot \sqrt[4]{(x + 6)^3}\)
qs.s: Convert each radical to exponential form: \((x + 6)^{3/2} \cdot (x + 6)^{3/4} = (x + 6)^{6/4 + 3/4} = (x + 6)^{9/4}\). Since \(\frac{9}{4} = 2\frac{1}{4}\), the expression simplifies to \((x + 6)^2\sqrt[4]{x + 6}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\sqrt{3x + 1} \cdot \sqrt[3]{(3x + 1)^2} \cdot \sqrt[4]{(3x + 1)^3}\)
qs.s: Convert the three factors to a common denominator of 12: \((3x + 1)^{6/12 + 8/12 + 9/12} = (3x + 1)^{23/12}\). Since \(\frac{23}{12} = 1\frac{11}{12}\), the expression simplifies to \((3x + 1)\sqrt[12]{(3x + 1)^{11}}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\sqrt{x^5(y + 2)} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x^2(y + 2)^4}\)
qs.s: Convert exponents for each factor using the common denominator 6: for \(x\), \(\frac{5}{2} + \frac{2}{3} = \frac{19}{6} = 3\frac{1}{6}\), giving \(x^3\sqrt[6]{x}\); for \((y + 2)\), \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{4}{3} = \frac{11}{6} = 1\frac{5}{6}\), giving \((y + 2)\sqrt[6]{(y + 2)^5}\). Combining both yields \(x^3(y + 2)\sqrt[6]{x(y + 2)^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\sqrt[3]{(x^2 + 6x + 9)^2} \cdot \sqrt{(x + 3)^3}\)
qs.s: Factor \(x^2 + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)^2\), so the expression becomes \(\sqrt[3]{(x + 3)^4} \cdot \sqrt{(x + 3)^3} = (x + 3)^{4/3 + 3/2} = (x + 3)^{17/6}\). Converting \(\frac{17}{6} = 2\frac{5}{6}\) into radical form yields \((x + 3)^2\sqrt[6]{(x + 3)^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\frac{4\sqrt[4]{(3a + 2)^7} \cdot \sqrt[3]{(3a + 2)^2}}{2\sqrt[6]{(3a + 2)^5}}\)
qs.s: Divide the coefficients \(\frac{4}{2} = 2\) and combine exponents using the common denominator 12: \(\frac{7}{4} + \frac{2}{3} - \frac{5}{6} = \frac{21 + 8 - 10}{12} = \frac{19}{12} = 1\frac{7}{12}\). This simplifies to \(2(3a + 2)\sqrt[12]{(3a + 2)^7}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\frac{\sqrt{(2x + 5)^5} \cdot \sqrt[3]{(2x + 5)^2}}{\sqrt[4]{(2x + 5)^3}}\)
qs.s: Express using fractional exponents with a common denominator of 12: \((2x + 5)^{30/12 + 8/12 - 9/12} = (2x + 5)^{29/12}\). Since \(\frac{29}{12} = 2\frac{5}{12}\), the result in simplest radical form is \((2x + 5)^2\sqrt[12]{(2x + 5)^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables and expressions represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{(x+2)^2}}{\sqrt[6]{x+2}}\)
qs.s: Convert the radicals to fractional exponents: \(\frac{(x+2)^{2/3}}{(x+2)^{1/6}} = (x+2)^{4/6 - 1/6} = (x+2)^{3/6} = (x+2)^{1/2} = \sqrt{x+2}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables and expressions represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{2x+1}}{\sqrt[3]{2x+1}}\)

Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables and expressions represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{(y-3)^3}}{\sqrt[3]{y-3}}\)

Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables and expressions represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{(a+5)^3}}{\sqrt[6]{a+5}}\)
qs.s: Convert to rational exponents using a common denominator: \(\frac{(a+5)^{3/4}}{(a+5)^{1/6}} = (a+5)^{9/12 - 2/12} = (a+5)^{7/12} = \sqrt[12]{(a+5)^7}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables and expressions represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[6]{(m-4)^5}}{\sqrt[4]{(m-4)^3}}\)

Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{32x^4}}{\sqrt[6]{2x^2}}\)

Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{a^3 b^5}}{\sqrt[6]{a b^2}}\)

Perform the indicated operations and simplify. Assume all variables and expressions represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{(x+1)^4} \cdot \sqrt[4]{x+1}}{\sqrt[6]{(x+1)^5}}\)
qs.s: Combine exponents with a common denominator of 12: \((x+1)^{16/12 + 3/12 - 10/12} = (x+1)^{9/12} = (x+1)^{3/4} = \sqrt[4]{(x+1)^3}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables and expressions represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{16(x+2)^2}}{\sqrt[6]{4(x+2)}}\)
qs.s: Express numerical bases as powers of 2 and use rational exponents: \(\frac{2^{4/3}(x+2)^{2/3}}{2^{2/6}(x+2)^{1/6}} = 2^{4/3 - 1/3}(x+2)^{4/6 - 1/6} = 2(x+2)^{1/2} = 2\sqrt{x+2}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Express your answer in radical form. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{4x + 3}}{\sqrt[4]{4x + 3}}\)
qs.s: Express the quotient using fractional exponents: \(\frac{(4x + 3)^{1/3}}{(4x + 3)^{1/4}} = (4x + 3)^{4/12 - 3/12} = (4x + 3)^{1/12}\). In radical form, this is \(\sqrt[12]{4x + 3}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Express your answer in radical form. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{5x - 2} \cdot \sqrt[5]{5x - 2}\)
qs.s: Convert to exponential form: \((5x - 2)^{1/3} \cdot (5x - 2)^{1/5} = (5x - 2)^{5/15 + 3/15} = (5x - 2)^{8/15}\). Writing as a single radical yields \(\sqrt[15]{(5x - 2)^8}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Express your answer in radical form. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{3x + 1} \cdot \sqrt[3]{3x + 1}\)
qs.s: Convert the radicals to exponential notation: \((3x + 1)^{1/2} \cdot (3x + 1)^{1/3} = (3x + 1)^{3/6 + 2/6} = (3x + 1)^{5/6}\). In radical form, this is \(\sqrt[6]{(3x + 1)^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Express your answer in radical form. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt[4]{x + 7} \cdot \sqrt[5]{x + 7}\)
qs.s: Convert to rational exponents: \((x + 7)^{1/4} \cdot (x + 7)^{1/5} = (x + 7)^{5/20 + 4/20} = (x + 7)^{9/20}\). Expressing in radical form gives \(\sqrt[20]{(x + 7)^9}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Express your answer in radical form. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{2x + 5} \cdot \sqrt[5]{2x + 5}\)
qs.s: Write with fractional exponents: \((2x + 5)^{1/2} \cdot (2x + 5)^{1/5} = (2x + 5)^{5/10 + 2/10} = (2x + 5)^{7/10}\). Converting back to radical form gives \(\sqrt[10]{(2x + 5)^7}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Express your answer in radical form. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{8\sqrt[4]{(3x + 1)^7}}{2\sqrt[3]{(3x + 1)^2}}\)
qs.s: Divide the coefficients to get \(8 \div 2 = 4\), then subtract exponents: \(\frac{7}{4} - \frac{2}{3} = \frac{21 - 8}{12} = \frac{13}{12} = 1 + \frac{1}{12}\). The simplified form is \(4(3x + 1)\sqrt[12]{3x + 1}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Express your answer in radical form. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{4x + 1} \cdot \sqrt[3]{(4x + 1)^2}}{\sqrt[4]{4x + 1}}\)
qs.s: Combine exponents by adding for multiplication and subtracting for division: \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{2}{3} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{6 + 8 - 3}{12} = \frac{11}{12}\). Expressing as a radical gives \(\sqrt[12]{(4x + 1)^{11}}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Express your answer in radical form. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt{x + 3} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x + 3} \cdot \sqrt[4]{x + 3}\)
qs.s: Sum the fractional exponents: \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{6 + 4 + 3}{12} = \frac{13}{12}\). Simplifying \((x + 3)^{13/12} = (x + 3)^{1 + 1/12}\) gives \((x + 3)\sqrt[12]{x + 3}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Express your answer in radical form. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{(3x + 2)^5}}{\sqrt[3]{(3x + 2)^2}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite with fractional exponents: \(\frac{(3x + 2)^{5/2}}{(3x + 2)^{2/3}} = (3x + 2)^{15/6 - 4/6} = (3x + 2)^{11/6}\). Decomposing the exponent into \(1 + \frac{5}{6}\) gives \((3x + 2)\sqrt[6]{(3x + 2)^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Express your answer in radical form. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{(2x + 1)^2} \cdot \sqrt[4]{(2x + 1)^3}\)

Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{(5x + 3)^5}}{\sqrt{(5x + 3)^3}}\)
qs.s: Convert the exponents to a common denominator of 6: \((5x + 3)^{5/3 - 3/2} = (5x + 3)^{10/6 - 9/6} = (5x + 3)^{1/6}\). In radical notation, this is \(\sqrt[6]{5x + 3}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{(3x + 1)^3}}{\sqrt[4]{3x + 1}}\)
qs.s: Convert the radicals to fractional exponents: \((3x + 1)^{3/2} \div (3x + 1)^{1/4} = (3x + 1)^{6/4 - 1/4} = (3x + 1)^{5/4}\). In simplest radical form, this is \((3x + 1)\sqrt[4]{3x + 1}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{(x + 6)^3}}{\sqrt[3]{(x + 6)^2}}\)
qs.s: Express with fractional exponents using a common denominator of 6: \((x + 6)^{3/2 - 2/3} = (x + 6)^{9/6 - 4/6} = (x + 6)^{5/6}\). Converting back to radical form yields \(\sqrt[6]{(x + 6)^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{(2x + 5)^4}}{\sqrt[4]{(2x + 5)^7}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the expressions with fractional exponents: \((2x + 5)^{4/2} \div (2x + 5)^{7/4} = (2x + 5)^{8/4 - 7/4} = (2x + 5)^{1/4}\). In radical form, this simplifies to \(\sqrt[4]{2x + 5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{(4x + 1)^3}}{\sqrt[3]{4x + 1}}\)
qs.s: Convert to a common index of 6: \(\frac{(4x + 1)^{9/6}}{(4x + 1)^{2/6}} = (4x + 1)^{7/6}\). Factoring out the whole power gives \((4x + 1)\sqrt[6]{4x + 1}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{8(3x + 2)^5}}{\sqrt[4]{32(3x + 2)^3}}\)

Perform the indicated operations and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{2x + 3} \cdot \sqrt[3]{(2x + 3)^4}}{\sqrt[4]{(2x + 3)^3}}\)
qs.s: Convert each radical to a fractional exponent with common denominator 12: \((2x + 3)^{6/12} \cdot (2x + 3)^{16/12} \div (2x + 3)^{9/12} = (2x + 3)^{13/12}\). Factoring out the integer power yields \((2x + 3)\sqrt[12]{2x + 3}\).

qs.q:
