\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{(x^2 + 6x + 9)^3}}{\sqrt[4]{(x + 3)^5}}\)
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt{x+5} \cdot \sqrt[6]{(x+5)^3}\)
qs.s: Convert the radicals to fractional exponents: \((x+5)^{1/2} \cdot (x+5)^{3/6} = (x+5)^{1/2 + 1/2} = (x+5)^1 = x+5\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt[5]{m+6} \cdot \sqrt[10]{(m+6)^8}\)
qs.s: Convert the radicals to fractional exponents: \((m+6)^{1/5} \cdot (m+6)^{8/10} = (m+6)^{1/5 + 4/5} = m+6\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt[4]{3a+4} \cdot \sqrt[8]{(3a+4)^6}\)
qs.s: Convert the radicals to fractional exponents: \((3a+4)^{1/4} \cdot (3a+4)^{6/8} = (3a+4)^{1/4 + 3/4} = 3a+4\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{y+2} \cdot \sqrt[6]{(y+2)^4}\)
qs.s: Convert the radicals to fractional exponents: \((y+2)^{1/3} \cdot (y+2)^{4/6} = (y+2)^{1/3 + 2/3} = (y+2)^1 = y+2\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt{2x+1} \cdot \sqrt[4]{(2x+1)^2}\)
qs.s: Convert the radicals to fractional exponents: \((2x+1)^{1/2} \cdot (2x+1)^{2/4} = (2x+1)^{1/2 + 1/2} = 2x+1\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers. \(\frac{\sqrt{(x+4)^5}}{\sqrt[4]{(x+4)^2}}\)
qs.s: Convert to fractional exponents and subtract powers: \((x+4)^{5/2} \div (x+4)^{2/4} = (x+4)^{5/2 - 1/2} = (x+4)^{4/2} = (x+4)^2\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers. \(3\sqrt[3]{2x+1} \cdot 2\sqrt[6]{(2x+1)^4}\)
qs.s: Multiply the coefficients \(3 \cdot 2 = 6\) and add the exponents \((2x+1)^{1/3 + 4/6} = (2x+1)^1\), yielding \(6(2x+1)\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers. \(\frac{\sqrt{3x+1} \cdot \sqrt[3]{(3x+1)^2}}{\sqrt[6]{3x+1}}\)
qs.s: Convert to fractional exponents and combine: \((3x+1)^{1/2 + 2/3 - 1/6} = (3x+1)^{3/6 + 4/6 - 1/6} = (3x+1)^{6/6} = 3x+1\).

qs.q: Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt[4]{x^2+10x+25} \cdot \sqrt[6]{(x+5)^3}\)
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers. \(\sqrt[3]{x+2} \cdot \sqrt[4]{x+2} \cdot \sqrt[12]{(x+2)^5}\)
qs.s: Write each radical with fractional exponents: \((x+2)^{1/3} \cdot (x+2)^{1/4} \cdot (x+2)^{5/12} = (x+2)^{4/12 + 3/12 + 5/12} = (x+2)^{12/12} = x+2\).

qs.q:

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[5]{(y+2)^4}}{\sqrt[3]{(y+2)^2}}\)

Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{(x+2)^7}}{\sqrt[4]{(x+2)^3}}\)
qs.s: Subtract exponents: \(\frac{7}{3} - \frac{3}{4} = \frac{28-9}{12} = \frac{19}{12} = 1 + \frac{7}{12}\). Simplifying by extracting \((x+2)\) yields \((x+2)\sqrt[12]{(x+2)^7}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{x^5 y^4}}{\sqrt[4]{x^3 y^2}}\)
qs.s: Subtract fractional exponents for each variable: for \(x\), \(\frac{5}{3} - \frac{3}{4} = \frac{11}{12}\); for \(y\), \(\frac{4}{3} - \frac{2}{4} = \frac{10}{12}\). Writing under a single radical gives \(\sqrt[12]{x^{11}y^{10}}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{x^4} \cdot \sqrt[4]{x^3}}{\sqrt[6]{x^5}}\)
qs.s: Combine using fractional exponents: \(x^{\frac{4}{3} + \frac{3}{4} - \frac{5}{6}} = x^{\frac{16+9-10}{12}} = x^{15/12} = x^{5/4} = x\sqrt[4]{x}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{a^7 b^5}}{\sqrt[3]{a^2 b}}\)
qs.s: Subtract fractional exponents: for \(a\), \(\frac{7}{4} - \frac{2}{3} = \frac{13}{12} = 1 + \frac{1}{12}\); for \(b\), \(\frac{5}{4} - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{11}{12}\). Simplifying gives \(a\sqrt[12]{ab^{11}}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{(2x+1)^5}}{\sqrt[5]{(2x+1)^6}}\)

Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{x} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x} \cdot \sqrt[6]{x^5}\)
qs.s: Write each radical with fractional exponents to get \(x^{1/2} \cdot x^{1/3} \cdot x^{5/6} = x^{3/6 + 2/6 + 5/6} = x^{10/6} = x^{5/3}\). Rewriting in simplified radical form gives \(x\sqrt[3]{x^2}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{x} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x} \cdot \sqrt[4]{x}\)
qs.s: Express the product using fractional exponents: \(x^{1/2} \cdot x^{1/3} \cdot x^{1/4} = x^{6/12 + 4/12 + 3/12} = x^{13/12}\). Converting back to simplified radical form gives \(x\sqrt[12]{x}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{x} \cdot \sqrt[4]{x^3} \cdot \sqrt[6]{x}\)
qs.s: Convert each factor to fractional exponents to get \(x^{1/3} \cdot x^{3/4} \cdot x^{1/6} = x^{4/12 + 9/12 + 2/12} = x^{15/12} = x^{5/4}\). In simplified radical form, this equals \(x\sqrt[4]{x}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{x} \cdot \sqrt[4]{x^3} \cdot \sqrt[8]{x^5}\)
qs.s: Convert to exponential notation with a common denominator of 8: \(x^{4/8 + 6/8 + 5/8} = x^{15/8}\). Rewriting as a mixed radical yields \(x\sqrt[8]{x^7}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{x^2} \cdot \sqrt[4]{x} \cdot \sqrt[6]{x^5}\)
qs.s: Add the fractional exponents with common denominator 12: \(x^{2/3 + 1/4 + 5/6} = x^{8/12 + 3/12 + 10/12} = x^{21/12} = x^{7/4}\). In simplified radical form, this yields \(x\sqrt[4]{x^3}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{x} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x^2} \cdot \sqrt[4]{x^3} \cdot \sqrt[6]{x^5}\)
qs.s: Sum the fractional exponents: \(x^{1/2 + 2/3 + 3/4 + 5/6} = x^{6/12 + 8/12 + 9/12 + 10/12} = x^{33/12} = x^{11/4}\). In simplified radical form, this gives \(x^2\sqrt[4]{x^3}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[4]{x^3 y^3} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x^2 y}}{\sqrt[6]{x y^2}}\)
qs.s: Convert to index 12: \(\sqrt[12]{\frac{(x^3 y^3)^3 (x^2 y)^4}{(x y^2)^2}} = \sqrt[12]{\frac{x^{17} y^{13}}{x^2 y^4}} = \sqrt[12]{x^{15} y^9}\). Dividing exponents and index by 3 gives \(\sqrt[4]{x^5 y^3} = x\sqrt[4]{x y^3}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{x^3} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x^2}}{\sqrt[4]{x^3}}\)
qs.s: Combine exponents by adding for multiplication and subtracting for division: \(x^{3/2 + 2/3 - 3/4} = x^{18/12 + 8/12 - 9/12} = x^{17/12}\). Simplifying to radical form gives \(x\sqrt[12]{x^5}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt[3]{x^2 y} \cdot \sqrt[4]{x^3 y^2} \cdot \sqrt[6]{x y^5}\)
qs.s: Convert all factors to a common index of 12: \(\sqrt[12]{(x^2 y)^4 (x^3 y^2)^3 (x y^5)^2} = \sqrt[12]{x^{19} y^{20}}\). Factoring out whole powers gives \(x y\sqrt[12]{x^7 y^8}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.
\(\displaystyle \sqrt{2x} \cdot \sqrt[3]{4x^2} \cdot \sqrt[6]{2x^5}\)
qs.s: Express under a common radical index of 6: \(\sqrt[6]{(2x)^3 \cdot (4x^2)^2 \cdot (2x^5)} = \sqrt[6]{256 x^{12}} = \sqrt[6]{2^8 x^{12}}\). Simplifying yields \(x^2\sqrt[3]{2^4} = 2x^2\sqrt[3]{2}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt[3]{a} \cdot \sqrt[4]{a^3}}{\sqrt{a}}\)
qs.s: Convert the radicals to fractional exponents: \(a^{1/3} \cdot a^{3/4} \div a^{1/2} = a^{4/12 + 9/12 - 6/12} = a^{7/12} = \sqrt[12]{a^7}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt[3]{x} \cdot \sqrt[6]{x}}{\sqrt[4]{x}}\)
qs.s: Express the radicals using fractional exponents: \(x^{1/3 + 1/6 - 1/4} = x^{4/12 + 2/12 - 3/12} = x^{3/12} = x^{1/4} = \sqrt[4]{x}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt[3]{y^2} \cdot \sqrt[6]{y^5}}{\sqrt{y}}\)
qs.s: Convert to rational exponents with a common denominator of 6: \(y^{2/3 + 5/6 - 1/2} = y^{4/6 + 5/6 - 3/6} = y^{6/6} = y\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt[3]{m^2} \cdot \sqrt{m}}{\sqrt[4]{m}}\)
qs.s: Convert the radicals to fractional exponents with a common denominator of 12: \(m^{2/3 + 1/2 - 1/4} = m^{8/12 + 6/12 - 3/12} = m^{11/12} = \sqrt[12]{m^{11}}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt[4]{b} \cdot \sqrt{b}}{\sqrt[3]{b^2}}\)
qs.s: Write each radical with exponent base \(b\): \(b^{1/4 + 1/2 - 2/3} = b^{3/12 + 6/12 - 8/12} = b^{1/12} = \sqrt[12]{b}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt{x^3 y} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x y^2}}{\sqrt[6]{x^5 y^4}}\)
qs.s: For \(x\), the exponent is \(\frac{3}{2} + \frac{1}{3} - \frac{5}{6} = 1\), and for \(y\), the exponent is \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{2}{3} - \frac{4}{6} = \frac{1}{2}\). Combining these yields \(x y^{1/2} = x\sqrt{y}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt[3]{a^2 b} \cdot \sqrt{a b^3}}{\sqrt[6]{a^5 b^4} \cdot \sqrt[4]{a b}}\)
qs.s: Find the exponents using denominator 12: for \(a\), \(\frac{8+6-10-3}{12} = \frac{1}{12}\); for \(b\), \(\frac{4+18-8-3}{12} = \frac{11}{12}\). This simplifies to \(\sqrt[12]{ab^{11}}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt{x^3} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x^2}}{\sqrt[4]{x^3} \cdot \sqrt[6]{x}}\)
qs.s: Combine exponents with common denominator 12: \(x^{3/2 + 2/3 - 3/4 - 1/6} = x^{18/12 + 8/12 - 9/12 - 2/12} = x^{15/12} = x^{5/4}\). Since \(x^{5/4} = x^{1 + 1/4}\), the simplified form is \(x\sqrt[4]{x}\).

qs.q:
Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt[3]{z^2} \cdot \sqrt[4]{z^3}}{\sqrt[8]{z}}\)

Perform the indicated operation and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive real numbers.

\(\frac{\sqrt{8x} \cdot \sqrt[3]{4x^2}}{\sqrt[6]{2x^5}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the numerical coefficients as powers of 2: \(2^{3/2 + 2/3 - 1/6} \cdot x^{1/2 + 2/3 - 5/6} = 2^{12/6} x^{2/6} = 2^2 x^{1/3} = 4\sqrt[3]{x}\).

qs.q:
Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator.

\(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3x-5}}\)
qs.s: To eliminate the radical in the denominator, multiply both numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{3x-5}\), which is multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{3x-5}}{\sqrt{3x-5}}\).

qs.q:
Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator.

\(\frac{2}{\sqrt{6-x}}\)
qs.s: To remove the square root from the denominator, multiply the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{6-x}}{\sqrt{6-x}}\).

qs.q:
Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator.

\(\frac{3}{\sqrt{5x+1}}\)
qs.s: To rationalize the denominator, multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{5x+1}\), which corresponds to multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{5x+1}}{\sqrt{5x+1}}\).

qs.q:
Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator.

\(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2-y}}\)
qs.s: Multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{2-y}}{\sqrt{2-y}}\) eliminates the square root in the denominator while keeping the fraction's value unchanged.

qs.q:
Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator.

\(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+7}}\)
qs.s: To rationalize the denominator without changing the value of the fraction, multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{x+7}\), which means multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{x+7}}{\sqrt{x+7}}\).

qs.q:
Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator.

\(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: The denominator contains two radical terms \(\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{5}\), so multiply the fraction by its conjugate over itself, \(\frac{\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{5}}\).

qs.q:
Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator.

\(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{x}}\)
qs.s: For a cube root \(\sqrt[3]{x}\), the radicand must be made a perfect cube (\(x^3\)), which requires multiplying numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{x^2}\), or the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{x^2}}{\sqrt[3]{x^2}}\).

qs.q:
Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator.

\(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{2x}}\)
qs.s: To create a perfect cube under the cube root, multiply \(2x\) by \(2^2 x^2 = 4x^2\). Thus, the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{4x^2}}{\sqrt[3]{4x^2}}\).

qs.q:
Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator.

\(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}-7}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the binomial denominator \(2\sqrt{x}-7\) is \(2\sqrt{x}+7\), so the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{2\sqrt{x}+7}{2\sqrt{x}+7}\).

qs.q:
Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator.

\(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}-3}\)
qs.s: The denominator is the binomial \(\sqrt{x}-3\), so its conjugate is \(\sqrt{x}+3\). Multiply the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{x}+3}{\sqrt{x}+3}\) to rationalize the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{w} - \sqrt{10}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the fraction by the conjugate of the denominator over itself, giving \(\frac{\sqrt{w} + \sqrt{10}}{\sqrt{w} + \sqrt{10}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{m}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the fraction by the conjugate over itself, which is \(\frac{\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{m}}{\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{m}}\), producing a rational denominator of \(2 - m\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: To rationalize the denominator, multiply the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{3}}\), which uses the conjugate of \(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{3}\) to form a difference of squares in the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{y} - \sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator is \(\sqrt{y} + \sqrt{5}\), so multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{y} + \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{y} + \sqrt{5}}\) rationalizes the denominator without changing the value.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{a}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator is \(\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{a}\), so the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{a}}{\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{a}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2x} + 4\sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of \(3\sqrt{2x} + 4\sqrt{5}\) is \(3\sqrt{2x} - 4\sqrt{5}\), so the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{3\sqrt{2x} - 4\sqrt{5}}{3\sqrt{2x} - 4\sqrt{5}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{4x}}\)
qs.s: Since \(4x = 2^2 x\), multiplying by \(\sqrt[3]{2x^2}\) produces the perfect cube radicand \(2^3 x^3 = 8x^3\), so the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{2x^2}}{\sqrt[3]{2x^2}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[4]{8x^3}}\)
qs.s: Since \(8x^3 = 2^3 x^3\), multiplying by \(\sqrt[4]{2x}\) yields the perfect fourth power radicand \(2^4 x^4 = 16x^4\), so the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt[4]{2x}}{\sqrt[4]{2x}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{5\sqrt{3a} - 2\sqrt{7b}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of \(5\sqrt{3a} - 2\sqrt{7b}\) is \(5\sqrt{3a} + 2\sqrt{7b}\), so the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{5\sqrt{3a} + 2\sqrt{7b}}{5\sqrt{3a} + 2\sqrt{7b}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x} - 3\sqrt{y}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the binomial denominator \(2\sqrt{x} - 3\sqrt{y}\) is \(2\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{y}\), so the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{2\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{y}}{2\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{y}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{2x+3}}\)
qs.s: To make the radicand under the cube root a perfect cube, the power of \((2x+3)\) must reach \(3\). Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{(2x+3)^2}\), which is \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{(2x+3)^2}}{\sqrt[3]{(2x+3)^2}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{(y-4)^2}}\)
qs.s: The radicand \((y-4)\) already has an exponent of \(2\), so it only needs \(3 - 2 = 1\) more factor of \((y-4)\) to complete the cube. Therefore, the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{y-4}}{\sqrt[3]{y-4}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{(3a+1)^2}}\)
qs.s: Because \((3a+1)\) is already squared, only one additional factor of \((3a+1)\) is needed to form a cube. Thus, multiply the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{3a+1}}{\sqrt[3]{3a+1}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{7-b}}\)
qs.s: The denominator contains \(\sqrt[3]{(7-b)^1}\), which needs \((7-b)^2\) to form a perfect cube inside the radical. Hence, the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{(7-b)^2}}{\sqrt[3]{(7-b)^2}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{2x^2-20x+50}}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand as \(2(x^2-10x+25) = 2(x-5)^2\). Under the cube root, \(2^1\) needs \(2^2 = 4\) and \((x-5)^2\) needs \((x-5)^1\), so multiply by \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{4(x-5)}}{\sqrt[3]{4(x-5)}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{x^2-8x+16}}\)
qs.s: Factor the radicand first: \(x^2 - 8x + 16 = (x-4)^2\). Under the cube root, \((x-4)^2\) needs one more factor of \((x-4)\) to become a cube, so multiply by \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{x-4}}{\sqrt[3]{x-4}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{12(x-1)}}\)
qs.s: Write \(12\) in prime factors as \(2^2 \cdot 3^1\); to complete the cube, we need \(2^{3-2} \cdot 3^{3-1} = 2 \cdot 9 = 18\), and \((x-1)\) needs \((x-1)^2\). Therefore, multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{18(x-1)^2}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[5]{16a^2(b-1)^3}}\)
qs.s: For an index of \(5\): \(16 = 2^4\) needs \(2^1 = 2\), \(a^2\) needs \(a^{5-2} = a^3\), and \((b-1)^3\) needs \((b-1)^{5-3} = (b-1)^2\). The fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt[5]{2a^3(b-1)^2}}{\sqrt[5]{2a^3(b-1)^2}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[4]{8(x+3)^3}}\)
qs.s: In the fourth root, \(8 = 2^3\), which requires \(2^1\) to reach an exponent of \(4\), and \((x+3)^3\) requires \((x+3)^1\). The multiplier is therefore \(\frac{\sqrt[4]{2(x+3)}}{\sqrt[4]{2(x+3)}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{5 - \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: To eliminate the radical from the denominator, multiply both numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{3}\), so the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{a} + 3}{\sqrt{a}}\)
qs.s: To rationalize the denominator without changing the value of the fraction, multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{a}\), which means multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{a}}{\sqrt{a}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{2x} - 5}{\sqrt{2x}}\)
qs.s: Multiplying both numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{2x}\) produces a rational denominator \(2x\), so the fraction is multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt{2x}}{\sqrt{2x}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{y} + 4}{\sqrt{5y}}\)
qs.s: To rationalize the denominator without changing the fraction's value, multiply both the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{5y}\), giving the multiplier \(\frac{\sqrt{5y}}{\sqrt{5y}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{2 + \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{7}}\)
qs.s: To rationalize the denominator \(\sqrt{7}\), multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{7}\), which is equivalent to multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{7}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{5}{\sqrt[3]{x}}\)
qs.s: Because \(\sqrt[3]{x} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x^2} = \sqrt[3]{x^3} = x\), the radicand needs two more factors of \(x\) to form a perfect cube, so the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{x^2}}{\sqrt[3]{x^2}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{4}{3 - \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: The denominator is the binomial \(3 - \sqrt{2}\), whose conjugate is \(3 + \sqrt{2}\). Multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate means multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{3 + \sqrt{2}}{3 + \sqrt{2}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{x} + 2}{\sqrt{x} - 5}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(\sqrt{x} - 5\) is \(\sqrt{x} + 5\), so the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt{x} + 5}{\sqrt{x} + 5}\) to rationalize the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of \(\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b}\) is \(\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b}\), so multiplying numerator and denominator by this conjugate means multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b}}{\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{2}}\)
qs.s: To create a perfect cube in the radicand of the denominator, multiply by \(\sqrt[3]{2^2} = \sqrt[3]{4}\) since \(2 \cdot 4 = 8 = 2^3\); hence, the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{4}}{\sqrt[3]{4}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{5}\) is \(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{5}\). Thus, the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{5}}\) to rationalize the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{2}\) is \(\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{2}\). Multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{2}}\) creates a difference of squares in the denominator, rationalizing it.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{3}\) is \(\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{3}\). Multiplying numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{3}\) means multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{3}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{5}\) is \(\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{5}\). Multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{5}}\) rationalizes the denominator without changing the value of the expression.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2}\) is \(\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2}\). Therefore, the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{2\sqrt{x} - 5}{3\sqrt{x} - 7}\), where \(x > 0\) and \(x \neq \frac{49}{9}\).
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(3\sqrt{x} - 7\) is \(3\sqrt{x} + 7\). Multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{3\sqrt{x} + 7}{3\sqrt{x} + 7}\) rationalizes the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{4\sqrt{2} - 3\sqrt{7}}{5\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{7}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(5\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{7}\) is \(5\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{7}\). Multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{5\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{7}}{5\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{7}}\) eliminates radicals in the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{5}}{2\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the binomial denominator \(2\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{5}\) is \(2\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{5}\). To rationalize the denominator, multiply the fraction by \(\frac{2\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{5}}{2\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{5}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{5 + \sqrt{6}}{3 - 2\sqrt{6}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(3 - 2\sqrt{6}\) is \(3 + 2\sqrt{6}\). Multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{3 + 2\sqrt{6}}{3 + 2\sqrt{6}}\) produces a rational denominator via the difference of squares.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{2\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{y}}{3\sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{y}}\), where \(x > 0\) and \(y > 0\).
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(3\sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{y}\) is \(3\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y}\). Therefore, multiply the fraction by \(\frac{3\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y}}{3\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{x} + 6}{\sqrt{x} + 2}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(\sqrt{x} + 2\) is \(\sqrt{x} - 2\). Multiply the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{x} - 2}{\sqrt{x} - 2}\) to eliminate the radical from the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{y} + 2}{\sqrt{y} - 5}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(\sqrt{y} - 5\), so its conjugate is \(\sqrt{y} + 5\). To rationalize the denominator without changing the value of the expression, multiply the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{y} + 5}{\sqrt{y} + 5}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{3 - \sqrt{a}}{4 + \sqrt{a}}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(4 + \sqrt{a}\), which has the conjugate \(4 - \sqrt{a}\). Multiplying numerator and denominator by this conjugate yields \(\frac{4 - \sqrt{a}}{4 - \sqrt{a}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{5 + \sqrt{w}}{\sqrt{w} - 8}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of \(\sqrt{w} - 8\) is \(\sqrt{w} + 8\). Multiplying both the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{w} + 8\) means the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt{w} + 8}{\sqrt{w} + 8}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{m} - 4}{7 - \sqrt{m}}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(7 - \sqrt{m}\), so its conjugate is \(7 + \sqrt{m}\). Rationalize the denominator by multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{7 + \sqrt{m}}{7 + \sqrt{m}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{5 - 2\sqrt{3y}}{6 + 4\sqrt{5y}}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(6 + 4\sqrt{5y}\), which has the conjugate \(6 - 4\sqrt{5y}\). Multiply the fraction by \(\frac{6 - 4\sqrt{5y}}{6 - 4\sqrt{5y}}\) to rationalize the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{2\sqrt{a} - 5\sqrt{b}}{3\sqrt{a} + 4\sqrt{b}}\)
qs.s: The denominator contains two radical terms with coefficients, \(3\sqrt{a} + 4\sqrt{b}\), so its conjugate is \(3\sqrt{a} - 4\sqrt{b}\). The fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{3\sqrt{a} - 4\sqrt{b}}{3\sqrt{a} - 4\sqrt{b}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y}}{\sqrt{x} - 3\sqrt{y}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(\sqrt{x} - 3\sqrt{y}\) is \(\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{y}\). Multiply the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{y}}{\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{y}}\) to create a difference of squares in the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{4\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2x}}{5\sqrt{2x} - 3\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(5\sqrt{2x} - 3\sqrt{3}\), so its conjugate is \(5\sqrt{2x} + 3\sqrt{3}\). Multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{5\sqrt{2x} + 3\sqrt{3}}{5\sqrt{2x} + 3\sqrt{3}}\) eliminates all radicals from the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{3\sqrt{x} - 2}{2\sqrt{x} + 5}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(2\sqrt{x} + 5\), which has the conjugate \(2\sqrt{x} - 5\). To rationalize the denominator, multiply the fraction by \(\frac{2\sqrt{x} - 5}{2\sqrt{x} - 5}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{m}}{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{m}}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{m}\), so its conjugate is \(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{m}\). Thus, the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{m}}{\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{m}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{a}}{\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b}}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b}\), so its conjugate is \(\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b}\). To rationalize the denominator without changing the fraction's value, multiply the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b}}{\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{u} + \sqrt{7}}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(\sqrt{u} + \sqrt{7}\), which has the conjugate \(\sqrt{u} - \sqrt{7}\). Therefore, the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt{u} - \sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{u} - \sqrt{7}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{3}{\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{5}\), so its conjugate is \(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{5}\). Multiply the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{5}}\) to rationalize the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{5\sqrt{6}}{4\sqrt{5x} - 7\sqrt{3y}}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(4\sqrt{5x} - 7\sqrt{3y}\), which has the conjugate \(4\sqrt{5x} + 7\sqrt{3y}\). Thus, the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{4\sqrt{5x} + 7\sqrt{3y}}{4\sqrt{5x} + 7\sqrt{3y}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{xy}}{x\sqrt{2y} - y\sqrt{2x}}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(x\sqrt{2y} - y\sqrt{2x}\), so its conjugate is \(x\sqrt{2y} + y\sqrt{2x}\). Multiply the fraction by \(\frac{x\sqrt{2y} + y\sqrt{2x}}{x\sqrt{2y} + y\sqrt{2x}}\) to rationalize the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{2\sqrt{x}}{5x + 3\sqrt{2y}}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(5x + 3\sqrt{2y}\), so its conjugate is \(5x - 3\sqrt{2y}\). To rationalize the denominator, multiply the fraction by \(\frac{5x - 3\sqrt{2y}}{5x - 3\sqrt{2y}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{3a} + 5\sqrt{2b}}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(2\sqrt{3a} + 5\sqrt{2b}\), which has the conjugate \(2\sqrt{3a} - 5\sqrt{2b}\). Therefore, the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{2\sqrt{3a} - 5\sqrt{2b}}{2\sqrt{3a} - 5\sqrt{2b}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{2\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y}}{3\sqrt{x} - 4\sqrt{y}}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(3\sqrt{x} - 4\sqrt{y}\), so its conjugate is \(3\sqrt{x} + 4\sqrt{y}\). To rationalize the denominator, multiply the fraction by \(\frac{3\sqrt{x} + 4\sqrt{y}}{3\sqrt{x} + 4\sqrt{y}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{3}{\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{w}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator is \(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{w}\). Multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{w}}{\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{w}}\) rationalizes the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{u} - 1}{\sqrt{u} + \sqrt{v}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(\sqrt{u} + \sqrt{v}\) is \(\sqrt{u} - \sqrt{v}\), so the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt{u} - \sqrt{v}}{\sqrt{u} - \sqrt{v}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{x}{\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of \(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{5}\) is \(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{5}\), so the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{5}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{b}}{\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b}\) is \(\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b}\). To rationalize the denominator without changing the fraction's value, multiply the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b}}{\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of \(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{3}\) is \(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{3}\). Multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{3}}\) rationalizes the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{7\sqrt{a}}{5\sqrt{6a} - 4\sqrt{7b}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(5\sqrt{6a} - 4\sqrt{7b}\) is \(5\sqrt{6a} + 4\sqrt{7b}\). Multiply numerator and denominator by this conjugate expression as \(\frac{5\sqrt{6a} + 4\sqrt{7b}}{5\sqrt{6a} + 4\sqrt{7b}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{5}{3\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the binomial denominator \(3\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y}\) is \(3\sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{y}\). Multiply the fraction by \(\frac{3\sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{y}}{3\sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{y}}\) to rationalize the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{xy}}{2\sqrt{3x} + 5\sqrt{2y}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of \(2\sqrt{3x} + 5\sqrt{2y}\) is \(2\sqrt{3x} - 5\sqrt{2y}\). Multiplying the fraction by \(\frac{2\sqrt{3x} - 5\sqrt{2y}}{2\sqrt{3x} - 5\sqrt{2y}}\) rationalizes the denominator.

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{2x - 3}{4 - 3\sqrt{5x}}\)
qs.s: The conjugate of the denominator \(4 - 3\sqrt{5x}\) is \(4 + 3\sqrt{5x}\), so the fraction must be multiplied by \(\frac{4 + 3\sqrt{5x}}{4 + 3\sqrt{5x}}\).

qs.q: Determine what the fraction must be multiplied by to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{3x} + \sqrt{2y}}{7\sqrt{2x} + 3\sqrt{5y}}\)
qs.s: Rationalizing the denominator requires multiplying by the conjugate of the denominator over itself, which is \(\frac{7\sqrt{2x} - 3\sqrt{5y}}{7\sqrt{2x} - 3\sqrt{5y}}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\sqrt{14} + \sqrt{5}\)
qs.s: The radicands 14 and 5 are square-free and distinct, meaning the radicals are not like radicals and the expression cannot be simplified.

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\sqrt{10} + \sqrt{3}\)
qs.s: Neither radical has a perfect square factor, and because their radicands (10 and 3) are different, the terms cannot be combined.

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\sqrt{13} + \sqrt{2}\)
qs.s: Because 13 and 2 are distinct prime numbers, \(\sqrt{13}\) and \(\sqrt{2}\) are unlike radicals and cannot be added together.

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{7}\)
qs.s: The radicals \(\sqrt{3}\) and \(\sqrt{7}\) have different radicands and neither can be simplified, so they are not like radicals. Therefore, the expression cannot be simplified.

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{11}\)
qs.s: Since \(\sqrt{6}\) and \(\sqrt{11}\) are in simplest radical form and do not have the same radicand, they are unlike radicals and cannot be combined.

qs.q: Simplify: \(2\sqrt{45} + 3\sqrt{20}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(2\sqrt{45} = 2(3\sqrt{5}) = 6\sqrt{5}\) and \(3\sqrt{20} = 3(2\sqrt{5}) = 6\sqrt{5}\). Combining like terms gives \(6\sqrt{5} + 6\sqrt{5} = 12\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\sqrt{12} + \sqrt{27}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to find like terms: \(\sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}\) and \(\sqrt{27} = 3\sqrt{3}\). Adding the coefficients gives \(2\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{3} = 5\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\sqrt{75} + \sqrt{48} - \sqrt{108}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(\sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3}\), \(\sqrt{48} = 4\sqrt{3}\), and \(\sqrt{108} = 6\sqrt{3}\). Combine the coefficients: \((5 + 4 - 6)\sqrt{3} = 3\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\sqrt{50} - \sqrt{18}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(\sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}\) and \(\sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}\). Subtracting the like radicals gives \(5\sqrt{2} - 3\sqrt{2} = 2\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(3\sqrt{8} - 5\sqrt{32} + 2\sqrt{50}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(3\sqrt{8} = 6\sqrt{2}\), \(5\sqrt{32} = 20\sqrt{2}\), and \(2\sqrt{50} = 10\sqrt{2}\). Combining the like radicals yields \((6 - 20 + 10)\sqrt{2} = -4\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\sqrt{3} \cdot \sqrt{5}\)
qs.s: Using the product rule for radicals, \(\sqrt{3} \cdot \sqrt{5} = \sqrt{3 \cdot 5} = \sqrt{15}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{13}\)
qs.s: Multiply the radicands together: \(\sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{13} = \sqrt{2 \cdot 13} = \sqrt{26}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\sqrt{5} \cdot \sqrt{7}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numbers under the radical to get \(\sqrt{5 \cdot 7} = \sqrt{35}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\sqrt{3} \cdot \sqrt{7}\)
qs.s: Use the product rule for radicals, \(\sqrt{a} \cdot \sqrt{b} = \sqrt{a \cdot b}\). Multiplying the radicands gives \(\sqrt{3 \cdot 7} = \sqrt{21}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{11}\)
qs.s: Apply the product rule for radicals: \(\sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{11} = \sqrt{2 \cdot 11} = \sqrt{22}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\sqrt{2}(\sqrt{18} + \sqrt{10})\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\sqrt{2}\) to each term: \(\sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{18} + \sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{10} = \sqrt{36} + \sqrt{20}\). Simplifying each radical yields \(6 + 2\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{6} \cdot \sqrt{15}\)
qs.s: Multiply all three radicands: \(\sqrt{2 \cdot 6 \cdot 15} = \sqrt{180}\). Factor out the largest perfect square: \(\sqrt{36 \cdot 5} = 6\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(3\sqrt{6} \cdot 2\sqrt{3}\)
qs.s: Multiply the coefficients and radicands separately to get \((3 \cdot 2)\sqrt{6 \cdot 3} = 6\sqrt{18}\). Simplify \(\sqrt{18}\) to \(3\sqrt{2}\), giving \(6 \cdot 3\sqrt{2} = 18\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\sqrt{10} \cdot \sqrt{15}\)
qs.s: Multiply the radicands to get \(\sqrt{150}\), then simplify by factoring out the perfect square: \(\sqrt{25 \cdot 6} = 5\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible. Assume \(x \geq 0\).
\(2\sqrt{5x} \cdot 3\sqrt{10x}\)
qs.s: Multiply coefficients and radicands to obtain \((2 \cdot 3)\sqrt{5x \cdot 10x} = 6\sqrt{50x^2}\). Simplify \(\sqrt{50x^2} = 5x\sqrt{2}\) and multiply by \(6\) to get \(30x\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\sqrt{14} - \sqrt{7}\)
qs.s: Because neither \(\sqrt{14}\) nor \(\sqrt{7}\) can be simplified and their radicands are different, they are not like radicals. Therefore, the expression cannot be simplified.

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\sqrt{21} - \sqrt{7}\)
qs.s: Since \(21\) and \(7\) share no square factors, the radicals are not like radicals and cannot be combined. Therefore, the expression cannot be simplified.

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\sqrt{22} - \sqrt{11}\)
qs.s: The radicals \(\sqrt{22}\) and \(\sqrt{11}\) are unlike radicals that cannot be simplified further, so they cannot be combined. Therefore, the expression cannot be simplified.

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\sqrt{15} - \sqrt{3}\)
qs.s: The terms \(\sqrt{15}\) and \(\sqrt{3}\) have no square factors and are not like radicals, so they cannot be subtracted. Therefore, the expression cannot be simplified.

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\sqrt{10} - \sqrt{5}\)
qs.s: The radicands \(10\) and \(5\) contain no perfect square factors and are not like radicals, so they cannot be combined. Therefore, the expression cannot be simplified.

qs.q: Simplify: \(\sqrt{50} - \sqrt{12} - \sqrt{18} + \sqrt{27}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(\sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}\), \(\sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}\), \(\sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}\), and \(\sqrt{27} = 3\sqrt{3}\). Grouping like radicals gives \((5\sqrt{2} - 3\sqrt{2}) + (-2\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{3}) = 2\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(4\sqrt{45} - 3\sqrt{20} - \sqrt{80}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(4(3\sqrt{5}) - 3(2\sqrt{5}) - 4\sqrt{5} = 12\sqrt{5} - 6\sqrt{5} - 4\sqrt{5}\). Combining the coefficients gives \((12 - 6 - 4)\sqrt{5} = 2\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(5\sqrt{18} - 2\sqrt{50}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(5\sqrt{18} = 5(3\sqrt{2}) = 15\sqrt{2}\) and \(2\sqrt{50} = 2(5\sqrt{2}) = 10\sqrt{2}\). Subtracting the like radicals gives \(15\sqrt{2} - 10\sqrt{2} = 5\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\sqrt{75} - \sqrt{12}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical to like terms: \(\sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3}\) and \(\sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}\). Subtracting the coefficients gives \(5\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{3} = 3\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\sqrt{18} - \sqrt{8} + \sqrt{12}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(\sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}\), \(\sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2}\), and \(\sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}\). Combining the like radicals yields \((3\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{2}) + 2\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{\sqrt{22}}{\sqrt{11}}\)
qs.s: Divide the radicands under a single radical: \(\frac{\sqrt{22}}{\sqrt{11}} = \sqrt{\frac{22}{11}} = \sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{\sqrt{30}}{\sqrt{6}}\)
qs.s: Divide the radicands under a single radical: \(\frac{\sqrt{30}}{\sqrt{6}} = \sqrt{\frac{30}{6}} = \sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{\sqrt{15}}{\sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: Divide the radicands under a single radical: \(\frac{\sqrt{15}}{\sqrt{5}} = \sqrt{\frac{15}{5}} = \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{\sqrt{14}}{\sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Divide the radicands under a single radical: \(\frac{\sqrt{14}}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{14}{2}} = \sqrt{7}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{\sqrt{33}}{\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Divide the radicands under a single radical: \(\frac{\sqrt{33}}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{\frac{33}{3}} = \sqrt{11}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{\sqrt{90}}{\sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: Divide the radicands to get \(\sqrt{\frac{90}{5}} = \sqrt{18}\), then simplify by factoring out the perfect square: \(\sqrt{9 \cdot 2} = 3\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{\sqrt{21}}{\sqrt{14}}\)
qs.s: Reduce under the radical to get \(\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}\), then multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{2}\) to rationalize, giving \(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{8\sqrt{60}}{4\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Divide the coefficients and the radicands separately: \(\frac{8}{4}\sqrt{\frac{60}{3}} = 2\sqrt{20}\). Then simplify \(2\sqrt{4 \cdot 5} = 2(2\sqrt{5}) = 4\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{\sqrt{20} \cdot \sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{8}}\)
qs.s: Combine the terms under a single radical: \(\sqrt{\frac{20 \cdot 6}{8}} = \sqrt{\frac{120}{8}} = \sqrt{15}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{\sqrt{72x^5}}{\sqrt{2x^2}}\), where \(x > 0\).
qs.s: Divide under a single radical to obtain \(\sqrt{\frac{72x^5}{2x^2}} = \sqrt{36x^3}\). Simplify the perfect squares: \(\sqrt{36 \cdot x^2 \cdot x} = 6x\sqrt{x}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\sqrt{6} - 2\sqrt{6}\)
qs.s: Subtract the coefficients of the like radicals: \((1 - 2)\sqrt{6} = -1\sqrt{6} = -\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\sqrt{5} - 4\sqrt{5}\)
qs.s: Combine like radicals by subtracting their coefficients: \((1 - 4)\sqrt{5} = -3\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(2\sqrt{3} - 7\sqrt{3}\)
qs.s: Combine the like radicals by subtracting their coefficients: \((2 - 7)\sqrt{3} = -5\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(5\sqrt{2} - 8\sqrt{2}\)
qs.s: Subtract the coefficients of the like radicals: \((5 - 8)\sqrt{2} = -3\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\sqrt{7} - 3\sqrt{7}\)
qs.s: Combine like radicals by subtracting their coefficients: \((1 - 3)\sqrt{7} = -2\sqrt{7}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\sqrt{75} - 4\sqrt{12}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical first: \(\sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3}\) and \(4\sqrt{12} = 4(2\sqrt{3}) = 8\sqrt{3}\). Then combine like radicals: \(5\sqrt{3} - 8\sqrt{3} = -3\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(3\sqrt{20} - \sqrt{45} - 2\sqrt{80}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(3\sqrt{20} = 6\sqrt{5}\), \(\sqrt{45} = 3\sqrt{5}\), and \(2\sqrt{80} = 8\sqrt{5}\). Combining the coefficients gives \((6 - 3 - 8)\sqrt{5} = -5\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(2\sqrt{28} - 5\sqrt{63} + \sqrt{112}\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical: \(2\sqrt{28} = 4\sqrt{7}\), \(5\sqrt{63} = 15\sqrt{7}\), and \(\sqrt{112} = 4\sqrt{7}\). Then combine like radicals: \((4 - 15 + 4)\sqrt{7} = -7\sqrt{7}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\sqrt{2} + 3\sqrt{32} - 2\sqrt{50}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(3\sqrt{32} = 3(4\sqrt{2}) = 12\sqrt{2}\) and \(2\sqrt{50} = 2(5\sqrt{2}) = 10\sqrt{2}\). Then combine like radicals: \((1 + 12 - 10)\sqrt{2} = 3\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\sqrt{48} + \sqrt{8} - \sqrt{27} - \sqrt{32}\)
qs.s: Simplify each term: \(\sqrt{48} = 4\sqrt{3}\), \(\sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2}\), \(\sqrt{27} = 3\sqrt{3}\), and \(\sqrt{32} = 4\sqrt{2}\). Grouping like radicals yields \((4\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{3}) + (2\sqrt{2} - 4\sqrt{2}) = \sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\sqrt{5} \cdot 4\sqrt{5}\)
qs.s: Multiply the coefficients and the radicals separately: \(1 \cdot 4 \cdot (\sqrt{5} \cdot \sqrt{5}) = 4 \cdot 5 = 20\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(3\sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{2}\)
qs.s: Multiply the coefficients and the radicals separately: \(3 \cdot 1 \cdot (\sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{2}) = 3 \cdot 2 = 6\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\sqrt{10} \cdot 3\sqrt{10}\)
qs.s: Multiply the coefficients and the radicals separately: \(1 \cdot 3 \cdot (\sqrt{10} \cdot \sqrt{10}) = 3 \cdot 10 = 30\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(6\sqrt{3} \cdot \sqrt{3}\)
qs.s: Multiply the coefficients and the radicals separately: \(6 \cdot 1 \cdot (\sqrt{3} \cdot \sqrt{3}) = 6 \cdot 3 = 18\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\sqrt{7} \cdot 2\sqrt{7}\)
qs.s: Multiply the coefficients and the radicals separately: \(1 \cdot 2 \cdot (\sqrt{7} \cdot \sqrt{7}) = 2 \cdot 7 = 14\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(3\sqrt{10} \cdot 2\sqrt{15}\)
qs.s: Multiply coefficients and radicands to obtain \(6\sqrt{150}\), then simplify \(\sqrt{150} = \sqrt{25 \cdot 6} = 5\sqrt{6}\) to get \(6 \cdot 5\sqrt{6} = 30\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(2\sqrt{5}(3\sqrt{5} - 4\sqrt{2})\)
qs.s: Distribute \(2\sqrt{5}\) across the binomial to get \((2\sqrt{5})(3\sqrt{5}) - (2\sqrt{5})(4\sqrt{2}) = 6(5) - 8\sqrt{10} = 30 - 8\sqrt{10}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(2\sqrt{6} \cdot 3\sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{3}\)
qs.s: Multiply the coefficients \(2 \cdot 3 \cdot 1 = 6\) and the radicands \(\sqrt{6 \cdot 2 \cdot 3} = \sqrt{36} = 6\), giving \(6 \cdot 6 = 36\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(-4\sqrt{12} \cdot 2\sqrt{18}\)
qs.s: Multiply coefficients and radicands to get \(-8\sqrt{216}\), then simplify \(\sqrt{216} = \sqrt{36 \cdot 6} = 6\sqrt{6}\) to yield \(-8 \cdot 6\sqrt{6} = -48\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible. Assume \(x > 0\): \(3\sqrt{2x} \cdot 5\sqrt{6x}\)
qs.s: Multiply coefficients and radicands to get \(15\sqrt{12x^2}\), then simplify \(\sqrt{12x^2} = \sqrt{4x^2 \cdot 3} = 2x\sqrt{3}\) to obtain \(15 \cdot 2x\sqrt{3} = 30x\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{10}}{8\sqrt{10}}\)
qs.s: Divide numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{10}\) to arrive at \(\frac{1}{8}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{2}}{6\sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Cancel the common factor of \(\sqrt{2}\) from the numerator and denominator to obtain \(\frac{1}{6}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{11}}{2\sqrt{11}}\)
qs.s: Cancel the like radical \(\sqrt{11}\) in the numerator and denominator to get \(\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3\sqrt{6}}\)
qs.s: Divide both the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{6}\) to simplify the fraction to \(\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{7}}{5\sqrt{7}}\)
qs.s: Cancel the common factor of \(\sqrt{7}\) from both the numerator and denominator to get \(\frac{1}{5}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{3\sqrt{32}}{4\sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Simplify \(\sqrt{32}\) as \(4\sqrt{2}\), giving a numerator of \(3(4\sqrt{2}) = 12\sqrt{2}\). Then \(\frac{12\sqrt{2}}{4\sqrt{2}} = 3\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{5\sqrt{18} - \sqrt{50}}{4\sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the radicals in the numerator to get \(15\sqrt{2} - 5\sqrt{2} = 10\sqrt{2}\). Dividing by \(4\sqrt{2}\) yields \(\frac{10}{4} = \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2\sqrt{6} \cdot \sqrt{10}}{3\sqrt{15}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the radicals in the numerator to get \(2\sqrt{60} = 4\sqrt{15}\). Dividing by \(3\sqrt{15}\) gives \(\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible. Assume that \(x > 0\).
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{72x^3}}{2\sqrt{2x}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the numerator as \(\sqrt{72x^3} = 6x\sqrt{2x}\). Dividing by \(2\sqrt{2x}\) cancels \(\sqrt{2x}\) and gives \(\frac{6x}{2} = 3x\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{96}}{2\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Simplify \(\sqrt{96}\) to \(4\sqrt{6}\). Then \(\frac{4\sqrt{6}}{2\sqrt{3}} = 2\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{2}}{5\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{3}\) to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{3}}{5\sqrt{3}\cdot\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{5\cdot 3} = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{15}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{5}\) to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{3}\cdot\sqrt{5}}{2\sqrt{5}\cdot\sqrt{5}} = \frac{\sqrt{15}}{2\cdot 5} = \frac{\sqrt{15}}{10}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{7}}{2\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{3}\) to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{7}\cdot\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{3}\cdot\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{21}}{2\cdot 3} = \frac{\sqrt{21}}{6}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{5}}{3\sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{2}\) to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{5}\cdot\sqrt{2}}{3\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{10}}{3\cdot 2} = \frac{\sqrt{10}}{6}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{5}}{4\sqrt{7}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{7}\) to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{\sqrt{5}\cdot\sqrt{7}}{4\sqrt{7}\cdot\sqrt{7}} = \frac{\sqrt{35}}{4\cdot 7} = \frac{\sqrt{35}}{28}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{3\sqrt{8}}{4\sqrt{27}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the radicals first: \(\frac{3(2\sqrt{2})}{4(3\sqrt{3})} = \frac{6\sqrt{2}}{12\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{3}}\). Rationalizing gives \(\frac{\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{3}}{2\cdot 3} = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{15} - 3}{2\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{3}\) to obtain \(\frac{\sqrt{45} - 3\sqrt{3}}{2\cdot 3} = \frac{3\sqrt{5} - 3\sqrt{3}}{6}\). Dividing numerator and denominator by \(3\) gives \(\frac{\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{3}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{10}}{3\sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{2}\) to get \(\frac{2\sqrt{12} - \sqrt{20}}{3\cdot 2} = \frac{4\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{5}}{6}\), which reduces to \(\frac{2\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{5}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{21}}{6\sqrt{14}}\)
qs.s: Reduce the radicals by dividing numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{7}\) to get \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6\sqrt{2}}\), then multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{2}\) to obtain \(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6\cdot 2} = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{12}\).

qs.q:
Simplify, if possible.
\(\displaystyle \frac{4\sqrt{15}}{9\sqrt{10}}\)
qs.s: Divide the radicals by \(\sqrt{5}\) to get \(\frac{4\sqrt{3}}{9\sqrt{2}}\), then multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{2}\) to get \(\frac{4\sqrt{6}}{18}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{9}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{10}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{10^2} = \sqrt[3]{100}\) to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1 \cdot \sqrt[3]{100}}{\sqrt[3]{10} \cdot \sqrt[3]{100}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{100}}{\sqrt[3]{1000}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{100}}{10}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{5}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{5^2} = \sqrt[3]{25}\) to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1 \cdot \sqrt[3]{25}}{\sqrt[3]{5} \cdot \sqrt[3]{25}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{25}}{\sqrt[3]{125}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{25}}{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{6}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{6^2} = \sqrt[3]{36}\) to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1 \cdot \sqrt[3]{36}}{\sqrt[3]{6} \cdot \sqrt[3]{36}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{36}}{\sqrt[3]{216}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{36}}{6}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{2^2} = \sqrt[3]{4}\) to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1 \cdot \sqrt[3]{4}}{\sqrt[3]{2} \cdot \sqrt[3]{4}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{4}}{\sqrt[3]{8}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{4}}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{7}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{7^2} = \sqrt[3]{49}\) to rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1 \cdot \sqrt[3]{49}}{\sqrt[3]{7} \cdot \sqrt[3]{49}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{49}}{\sqrt[3]{343}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{49}}{7}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{4}{3}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite as \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{4}}{\sqrt[3]{3}}\) and multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{3^2} = \sqrt[3]{9}\) to get \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{36}}{\sqrt[3]{27}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{36}}{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{5}}{\sqrt[3]{4}}\)
qs.s: Since \(4 = 2^2\), multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{2}\) to rationalize: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{5} \cdot \sqrt[3]{2}}{\sqrt[3]{4} \cdot \sqrt[3]{2}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{10}}{\sqrt[3]{8}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{10}}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{12}}\)
qs.s: Factor \(12 = 2^2 \cdot 3\), so multiplying numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{2 \cdot 3^2} = \sqrt[3]{18}\) yields \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{\sqrt[3]{216}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{6}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{6}{\sqrt[4]{8}}\)
qs.s: Since \(8 = 2^3\), multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[4]{2}\) to get \(\frac{6\sqrt[4]{2}}{\sqrt[4]{16}} = \frac{6\sqrt[4]{2}}{2} = 3\sqrt[4]{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{6}{\sqrt[3]{9}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{3}\) to obtain \(\frac{6\sqrt[3]{3}}{\sqrt[3]{27}} = \frac{6\sqrt[3]{3}}{3}\), which simplifies to \(2\sqrt[3]{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{4}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(4\) as \(2^2\), then multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{2}\) to complete the cube. This gives \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\sqrt[3]{8}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{2}}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[4]{8}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(8\) as \(2^3\) and multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[4]{2}\) to complete the fourth power. This simplifies to \(\frac{\sqrt[4]{2}}{\sqrt[4]{16}} = \frac{\sqrt[4]{2}}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[4]{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[4]{3^3} = \sqrt[4]{27}\) to rationalize the denominator. This gives \(\frac{1 \cdot \sqrt[4]{27}}{\sqrt[4]{3^4}} = \frac{\sqrt[4]{27}}{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\sqrt[4]{\frac{5}{8}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite as \(\frac{\sqrt[4]{5}}{\sqrt[4]{2^3}}\), then multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[4]{2}\) to rationalize. This gives \(\frac{\sqrt[4]{10}}{\sqrt[4]{16}} = \frac{\sqrt[4]{10}}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\sqrt[3]{3x}}\), where \(x > 0\).
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{(3x)^2} = \sqrt[3]{9x^2}\) to produce a perfect cube in the denominator. This yields \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{2 \cdot 9x^2}}{\sqrt[3]{27x^3}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{18x^2}}{3x}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{4x}{\sqrt[4]{8x}}\), where \(x > 0\).
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[4]{2x^3}\) so the denominator becomes \(\sqrt[4]{2^4x^4} = 2x\). Then simplify \(\frac{4x\sqrt[4]{2x^3}}{2x} = 2\sqrt[4]{2x^3}\).

qs.q: Simplify, if possible: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{4x^2}}\), where \(x > 0\).
qs.s: Express the radicand as \(2^2x^2\) and multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{2x}\) to form a perfect cube. This simplifies to \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{2x}}{\sqrt[3]{8x^3}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{2x}}{2x}\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{11} + \sqrt{2})(\sqrt{11} - \sqrt{2})\)
Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{7} + 2)(\sqrt{7} - 2)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity \((a+b)(a-b) = a^2 - b^2\), we have \((\sqrt{7})^2 - 2^2 = 7 - 4 = 3\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((6 - \sqrt{5})(6 + \sqrt{5})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity \((a-b)(a+b) = a^2 - b^2\), we obtain \(6^2 - (\sqrt{5})^2 = 36 - 5 = 31\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{10} - 3)(\sqrt{10} + 3)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity \((a-b)(a+b) = a^2 - b^2\), we calculate \((\sqrt{10})^2 - 3^2 = 10 - 9 = 1\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((5 + \sqrt{3})(5 - \sqrt{3})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity \((a+b)(a-b) = a^2 - b^2\), we calculate \(5^2 - (\sqrt{3})^2 = 25 - 3 = 22\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((3\sqrt{a} - 2\sqrt{b})(3\sqrt{a} + 2\sqrt{b})\)
qs.s: Applying \((a-b)(a+b) = a^2 - b^2\), we get \((3\sqrt{a})^2 - (2\sqrt{b})^2 = 9a - 4b\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((3\sqrt{5} + 2\sqrt{3})(3\sqrt{5} - 2\sqrt{3})\)
Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((4\sqrt{x} + 3)(4\sqrt{x} - 3)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((4\sqrt{x})^2 - 3^2 = 16x - 9\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((2\sqrt{7} + 5)(2\sqrt{7} - 5)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((2\sqrt{7})^2 - 5^2 = 4(7) - 25 = 28 - 25 = 3\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((\sqrt{x} - 3)(\sqrt{x} + 3)(x + 9)\)
qs.s: First multiply the radical conjugates to get \((\sqrt{x})^2 - 3^2 = x - 9\), then multiply \((x - 9)(x + 9) = x^2 - 81\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{11} - \sqrt{6})(\sqrt{11} + \sqrt{6})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{11} - \sqrt{6})(\sqrt{11} + \sqrt{6}) = (\sqrt{11})^2 - (\sqrt{6})^2 = 11 - 6 = 5\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{10} + \sqrt{3})(\sqrt{10} - \sqrt{3})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{10} + \sqrt{3})(\sqrt{10} - \sqrt{3}) = (\sqrt{10})^2 - (\sqrt{3})^2 = 10 - 3 = 7\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{5})(\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{5})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{5})(\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{5}) = (\sqrt{6})^2 - (\sqrt{5})^2 = 6 - 5 = 1\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2})(\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2})(\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2}) = (\sqrt{5})^2 - (\sqrt{2})^2 = 5 - 2 = 3\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3})(\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{3})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3})(\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{3}) = (\sqrt{7})^2 - (\sqrt{3})^2 = 7 - 3 = 4\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((3\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{3})(3\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{3})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((3\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{3})(3\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{3}) = (3\sqrt{2})^2 - (2\sqrt{3})^2 = 18 - 12 = 6\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((3\sqrt{2x} - 4)(3\sqrt{2x} + 4)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((3\sqrt{2x} - 4)(3\sqrt{2x} + 4) = (3\sqrt{2x})^2 - 4^2 = 18x - 16\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((4\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{5})(4\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{5})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((4\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{5})(4\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{5}) = (4\sqrt{3})^2 - (3\sqrt{5})^2 = 48 - 45 = 3\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((2\sqrt{6} - 5)(2\sqrt{6} + 5)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((2\sqrt{6} - 5)(2\sqrt{6} + 5) = (2\sqrt{6})^2 - 5^2 = 24 - 25 = -1\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((2\sqrt{x} - 5\sqrt{y})(2\sqrt{x} + 5\sqrt{y})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((2\sqrt{x} - 5\sqrt{y})(2\sqrt{x} + 5\sqrt{y}) = (2\sqrt{x})^2 - (5\sqrt{y})^2 = 4x - 25y\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((6 - \sqrt{7})(6 + \sqrt{7})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity \((a-b)(a+b) = a^2 - b^2\), we calculate \(6^2 - (\sqrt{7})^2 = 36 - 7 = 29\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((3 + \sqrt{6})(3 - \sqrt{6})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity \((a+b)(a-b) = a^2 - b^2\), we calculate \(3^2 - (\sqrt{6})^2 = 9 - 6 = 3\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((8 - \sqrt{11})(8 + \sqrt{11})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity \((a-b)(a+b) = a^2 - b^2\), we calculate \(8^2 - (\sqrt{11})^2 = 64 - 11 = 53\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((7 + \sqrt{5})(7 - \sqrt{5})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity \((a+b)(a-b) = a^2 - b^2\), we calculate \(7^2 - (\sqrt{5})^2 = 49 - 5 = 44\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((5 + \sqrt{2})(5 - \sqrt{2})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity \((a+b)(a-b) = a^2 - b^2\), we calculate \(5^2 - (\sqrt{2})^2 = 25 - 2 = 23\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((2\sqrt{11} - 5\sqrt{2})(2\sqrt{11} + 5\sqrt{2})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, we calculate \((2\sqrt{11})^2 - (5\sqrt{2})^2 = 4(11) - 25(2) = 44 - 50 = -6\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((5\sqrt{x} - 2)(5\sqrt{x} + 2)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, we compute \((5\sqrt{x})^2 - 2^2 = 25x - 4\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((4\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{y})(4\sqrt{x} - 3\sqrt{y})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, we obtain \((4\sqrt{x})^2 - (3\sqrt{y})^2 = 16x - 9y\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((2\sqrt{5} + 3)(2\sqrt{5} - 3)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, we have \((2\sqrt{5})^2 - 3^2 = 4(5) - 9 = 20 - 9 = 11\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((3\sqrt{6} + 2\sqrt{3})(3\sqrt{6} - 2\sqrt{3})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, we get \((3\sqrt{6})^2 - (2\sqrt{3})^2 = 9(6) - 4(3) = 54 - 12 = 42\).

qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{u} - \sqrt{v})(\sqrt{u} + \sqrt{v}) = (\sqrt{u})^2 - (\sqrt{v})^2 = u - v\).

qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{p} - q)(\sqrt{p} + q) = (\sqrt{p})^2 - q^2 = p - q^2\).

\((9 - \sqrt{w})(9 + \sqrt{w})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((9 - \sqrt{w})(9 + \sqrt{w}) = 9^2 - (\sqrt{w})^2 = 81 - w\).

\((b + \sqrt{c})(b - \sqrt{c})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((b + \sqrt{c})(b - \sqrt{c}) = b^2 - (\sqrt{c})^2 = b^2 - c\).

qs.q:

\((3\sqrt{x} - 2y)(3\sqrt{x} + 2y)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((3\sqrt{x} - 2y)(3\sqrt{x} + 2y) = (3\sqrt{x})^2 - (2y)^2 = 9x - 4y^2\).

qs.q:

\((\sqrt{x^3} - 3y^2)(\sqrt{x^3} + 3y^2)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{x^3} - 3y^2)(\sqrt{x^3} + 3y^2) = (\sqrt{x^3})^2 - (3y^2)^2 = x^3 - 9y^4\).

qs.q:
Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive.
\((5\sqrt{a} + 4\sqrt{b})(5\sqrt{a} - 4\sqrt{b})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((5\sqrt{a} + 4\sqrt{b})(5\sqrt{a} - 4\sqrt{b}) = (5\sqrt{a})^2 - (4\sqrt{b})^2 = 25a - 16b\).

qs.q:
Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{x} - 2)(\sqrt{x} + 2)(x + 4)\)
qs.s: First multiply the conjugate radical binomials to get \((\sqrt{x} - 2)(\sqrt{x} + 2) = x - 4\). Then apply the difference of squares again: \((x - 4)(x + 4) = x^2 - 16\).

qs.q:

\((2\sqrt{3x} - 5)(2\sqrt{3x} + 5)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((2\sqrt{3x} - 5)(2\sqrt{3x} + 5) = (2\sqrt{3x})^2 - 5^2 = 4(3x) - 25 = 12x - 25\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((\sqrt{k} + \sqrt{6})(\sqrt{k} - \sqrt{6})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares, \((\sqrt{k})^2 - (\sqrt{6})^2 = k - 6\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b})(\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity \((u-v)(u+v) = u^2 - v^2\), we have \((\sqrt{a})^2 - (\sqrt{b})^2 = a - b\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((\sqrt{m} + 5)(\sqrt{m} - 5)\)
qs.s: Applying the difference of squares gives \((\sqrt{m})^2 - 5^2 = m - 25\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{13} - \sqrt{5})(\sqrt{13} + \sqrt{5})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{13})^2 - (\sqrt{5})^2 = 13 - 5 = 8\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((4\sqrt{5} - 3\sqrt{2})(4\sqrt{5} + 3\sqrt{2})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares, \((4\sqrt{5})^2 - (3\sqrt{2})^2 = 16(5) - 9(2) = 80 - 18 = 62\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((3\sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{y})(3\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((3\sqrt{x})^2 - (2\sqrt{y})^2 = 9x - 4y\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((2\sqrt{a^3} + \sqrt{3b})(2\sqrt{a^3} - \sqrt{3b})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares, \((2\sqrt{a^3})^2 - (\sqrt{3b})^2 = 4a^3 - 3b\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((5\sqrt{2x} - 3\sqrt{3y})(5\sqrt{2x} + 3\sqrt{3y})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares, \((5\sqrt{2x})^2 - (3\sqrt{3y})^2 = 25(2x) - 9(3y) = 50x - 27y\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{3k+7} - 2)(\sqrt{3k+7} + 2)\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{3k+7} - 2)(\sqrt{3k+7} + 2) = (\sqrt{3k+7})^2 - 2^2 = (3k + 7) - 4 = 3k + 3\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{2a+1} + 1)(\sqrt{2a+1} - 1)\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{2a+1} + 1)(\sqrt{2a+1} - 1) = (\sqrt{2a+1})^2 - 1^2 = (2a + 1) - 1 = 2a\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{y+5} - 1)(\sqrt{y+5} + 1)\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{y+5} - 1)(\sqrt{y+5} + 1) = (\sqrt{y+5})^2 - 1^2 = (y + 5) - 1 = y + 4\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{x+4} - 2)(\sqrt{x+4} + 2)\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{x+4} - 2)(\sqrt{x+4} + 2) = (\sqrt{x+4})^2 - 2^2 = (x + 4) - 4 = x\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{m+9} - 3)(\sqrt{m+9} + 3)\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{m+9} - 3)(\sqrt{m+9} + 3) = (\sqrt{m+9})^2 - 3^2 = (m + 9) - 9 = m\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((2\sqrt{3x+4} - 3\sqrt{x-1})(2\sqrt{3x+4} + 3\sqrt{x-1})\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((2\sqrt{3x+4})^2 - (3\sqrt{x-1})^2 = 4(3x + 4) - 9(x - 1) = 12x + 16 - 9x + 9 = 3x + 25\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{4x+9} - \sqrt{4x-7})(\sqrt{4x+9} + \sqrt{4x-7})\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{4x+9})^2 - (\sqrt{4x-7})^2 = (4x + 9) - (4x - 7) = 4x + 9 - 4x + 7 = 16\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{7x+5} - \sqrt{3x-2})(\sqrt{7x+5} + \sqrt{3x-2})\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{7x+5})^2 - (\sqrt{3x-2})^2 = (7x + 5) - (3x - 2) = 7x + 5 - 3x + 2 = 4x + 7\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((3\sqrt{2x+1} - \sqrt{6x-5})(3\sqrt{2x+1} + \sqrt{6x-5})\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((3\sqrt{2x+1})^2 - (\sqrt{6x-5})^2 = 9(2x + 1) - (6x - 5) = 18x + 9 - 6x + 5 = 12x + 14\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((2\sqrt{x+3} - 3)(2\sqrt{x+3} + 3)\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((2\sqrt{x+3})^2 - 3^2 = 4(x + 3) - 9 = 4x + 12 - 9 = 4x + 3\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{a+7} - \sqrt{b+3})(\sqrt{a+7} + \sqrt{b+3})\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity \((u-v)(u+v) = u^2 - v^2\), we have \((\sqrt{a+7})^2 - (\sqrt{b+3})^2 = (a+7) - (b+3) = a - b + 4\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{2x+5} - \sqrt{x+5})(\sqrt{2x+5} + \sqrt{x+5})\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{2x+5})^2 - (\sqrt{x+5})^2 = (2x+5) - (x+5) = x\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{3x+1} - \sqrt{y+1})(\sqrt{3x+1} + \sqrt{y+1})\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{3x+1})^2 - (\sqrt{y+1})^2 = (3x+1) - (y+1) = 3x - y\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{x+3y} - \sqrt{x+y})(\sqrt{x+3y} + \sqrt{x+y})\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{x+3y})^2 - (\sqrt{x+y})^2 = (x+3y) - (x+y) = 2y\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product: \((\sqrt{2a+3} - \sqrt{a+8})(\sqrt{2a+3} + \sqrt{a+8})\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{2a+3})^2 - (\sqrt{a+8})^2 = (2a+3) - (a+8) = a - 5\).

qs.q: Find the product: \((4\sqrt{2x+5} - 3\sqrt{3x+1})(4\sqrt{2x+5} + 3\sqrt{3x+1})\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares identity: \((4\sqrt{2x+5})^2 - (3\sqrt{3x+1})^2 = 16(2x+5) - 9(3x+1) = 32x + 80 - 27x - 9 = 5x + 71\).

qs.q: Find the product: \((2\sqrt{3x+5y} - \sqrt{5x+2y})(2\sqrt{3x+5y} + \sqrt{5x+2y})\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares identity: \((2\sqrt{3x+5y})^2 - (\sqrt{5x+2y})^2 = 4(3x+5y) - (5x+2y) = 12x + 20y - 5x - 2y = 7x + 18y\).

qs.q: Find the product: \((3\sqrt{x+4} - 2\sqrt{x+1})(3\sqrt{x+4} + 2\sqrt{x+1})\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares identity: \((3\sqrt{x+4})^2 - (2\sqrt{x+1})^2 = 9(x+4) - 4(x+1) = 9x + 36 - 4x - 4 = 5x + 32\).

qs.q: Find the product: \((\sqrt{x^2+5x+7} - \sqrt{x^2+x+2})(\sqrt{x^2+5x+7} + \sqrt{x^2+x+2})\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares identity: \((\sqrt{x^2+5x+7})^2 - (\sqrt{x^2+x+2})^2 = (x^2+5x+7) - (x^2+x+2) = 4x + 5\).

qs.q: Find the product: \((\sqrt{2x+1} - \sqrt{x+3})(\sqrt{2x+1} + \sqrt{x+3})(x + 2)\). Assume all variables are positive.
qs.s: First multiply the conjugate radicals: \((\sqrt{2x+1})^2 - (\sqrt{x+3})^2 = (2x+1) - (x+3) = x - 2\). Then multiply the remaining factors: \((x - 2)(x + 2) = x^2 - 4\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((y + \sqrt{y-3})(y - \sqrt{y-3})\)
qs.s: Using \((A+B)(A-B) = A^2 - B^2\), we get \(y^2 - (\sqrt{y-3})^2 = y^2 - (y-3)\). Distributing the negative yields \(y^2 - y + 3\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((w - \sqrt{2w-7})(w + \sqrt{2w-7})\)
qs.s: Applying \((A-B)(A+B) = A^2 - B^2\) gives \(w^2 - (\sqrt{2w-7})^2 = w^2 - (2w-7)\). Distributing the negative gives \(w^2 - 2w + 7\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((t + \sqrt{3t+4})(t - \sqrt{3t+4})\)
qs.s: Using \((A+B)(A-B) = A^2 - B^2\), the product is \(t^2 - (\sqrt{3t+4})^2 = t^2 - (3t+4)\). Distributing the negative yields \(t^2 - 3t - 4\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((x - \sqrt{x+5})(x + \sqrt{x+5})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity \((A-B)(A+B) = A^2 - B^2\), we have \((x)^2 - (\sqrt{x+5})^2 = x^2 - (x+5)\). Distributing the negative gives \(x^2 - x - 5\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((x - \sqrt{4x-5})(x + \sqrt{4x-5})\)
qs.s: Using \((A-B)(A+B) = A^2 - B^2\), we have \(x^2 - (\sqrt{4x-5})^2 = x^2 - (4x-5)\). Distributing the negative gives \(x^2 - 4x + 5\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((\sqrt{5x+4} - \sqrt{2x-3})(\sqrt{5x+4} + \sqrt{2x-3})\)
qs.s: Using \((A-B)(A+B) = A^2 - B^2\), we obtain \((5x+4) - (2x-3) = 5x + 4 - 2x + 3\). Combining like terms gives \(3x + 7\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((3x - \sqrt{5x-7})(3x + \sqrt{5x-7})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((3x)^2 - (\sqrt{5x-7})^2 = 9x^2 - (5x-7)\). Distributing the negative yields \(9x^2 - 5x + 7\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((2x^2 + \sqrt{3x^2-4})(2x^2 - \sqrt{3x^2-4})\)
qs.s: Applying \((A+B)(A-B) = A^2 - B^2\) gives \((2x^2)^2 - (\sqrt{3x^2-4})^2 = 4x^4 - (3x^2-4)\). Distributing the negative gives \(4x^4 - 3x^2 + 4\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((x - 3\sqrt{x+2})(x + 3\sqrt{x+2})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares, \((x)^2 - (3\sqrt{x+2})^2 = x^2 - 9(x+2)\). Distributing \(-9\) gives \(x^2 - 9x - 18\).

qs.q: Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive: \((2x - 3\sqrt{x-1})(2x + 3\sqrt{x-1})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((2x)^2 - (3\sqrt{x-1})^2 = 4x^2 - 9(x-1)\). Distributing \(-9\) results in \(4x^2 - 9x + 9\).

qs.q:

\((2\sqrt{3x+y} - \sqrt{5x-2y})(2\sqrt{3x+y} + \sqrt{5x-2y})\)

\((\sqrt{x^2+5x-2} - \sqrt{x^2-3x+6})(\sqrt{x^2+5x-2} + \sqrt{x^2-3x+6})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares, \((x^2+5x-2) - (x^2-3x+6) = x^2 - x^2 + 5x - (-3x) - 2 - 6 = 8x - 8\).

qs.q:
Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive.
\((3\sqrt{x+2} - 2\sqrt{2x-1})(3\sqrt{x+2} + 2\sqrt{2x-1})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((3\sqrt{x+2})^2 - (2\sqrt{2x-1})^2 = 9(x+2) - 4(2x-1) = 9x + 18 - 8x + 4 = x + 22\).

qs.q:

\((5\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{3x-4})(5\sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{3x-4})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares, \((5\sqrt{x})^2 - (2\sqrt{3x-4})^2 = 25x - 4(3x-4) = 25x - 12x + 16 = 13x + 16\).

qs.q:
Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{3x+5} + \sqrt{3x-2})(\sqrt{3x+5} - \sqrt{3x-2})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity \((a+b)(a-b) = a^2 - b^2\), we have \((\sqrt{3x+5})^2 - (\sqrt{3x-2})^2 = (3x+5) - (3x-2) = 7\).

qs.q:

qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity \((a-b)(a+b) = a^2 - b^2\), we obtain \((\sqrt{4x+1})^2 - (\sqrt{4x-5})^2 = (4x+1) - (4x-5) = 6\).

qs.q:
Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{2x+9} - \sqrt{2x+1})(\sqrt{2x+9} + \sqrt{2x+1})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula, \((\sqrt{2x+9})^2 - (\sqrt{2x+1})^2 = (2x+9) - (2x+1) = 8\).

qs.q:
Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{5x+8} + \sqrt{5x-3})(\sqrt{5x+8} - \sqrt{5x-3})\)
qs.s: Applying the difference of squares identity gives \((\sqrt{5x+8})^2 - (\sqrt{5x-3})^2 = (5x+8) - (5x-3) = 11\).

qs.q:
Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{x+7} + \sqrt{x-7})(\sqrt{x+7} - \sqrt{x-7})\)
qs.s: By the difference of squares identity, \((\sqrt{x+7})^2 - (\sqrt{x-7})^2 = (x+7) - (x-7) = 14\).

qs.q:
Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive.
\((3\sqrt{4x+1} + 2\sqrt{9x-2})(3\sqrt{4x+1} - 2\sqrt{9x-2})\)
qs.s: By the difference of squares formula, \((3\sqrt{4x+1})^2 - (2\sqrt{9x-2})^2 = 9(4x+1) - 4(9x-2) = 36x + 9 - 36x + 8 = 17\).

qs.q:
Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive.
\((2\sqrt{3x + 4y} + \sqrt{12x - 5y})(2\sqrt{3x + 4y} - \sqrt{12x - 5y})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((2\sqrt{3x + 4y})^2 - (\sqrt{12x - 5y})^2 = 4(3x + 4y) - (12x - 5y) = 12x + 16y - 12x + 5y = 21y\).

qs.q:
Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive.
\((\sqrt{x^2 + 5x + 8} + \sqrt{x^2 + 5x - 4})(\sqrt{x^2 + 5x + 8} - \sqrt{x^2 + 5x - 4})\)
qs.s: By the difference of squares identity, the product simplifies to \((x^2 + 5x + 8) - (x^2 + 5x - 4) = 8 - (-4) = 12\).

qs.q:

\((4x - \sqrt{16x^2 - 9})(4x + \sqrt{16x^2 - 9})\)

Mentally find the product. Assume all variables are positive.
\((2\sqrt{x+5} + \sqrt{4x-3})(2\sqrt{x+5} - \sqrt{4x-3})\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares identity, \((2\sqrt{x+5})^2 - (\sqrt{4x-3})^2 = 4(x+5) - (4x-3) = 4x + 20 - 4x + 3 = 23\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{6}\) to obtain \(\frac{1 \cdot \sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{6} \cdot \sqrt{6}} = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{3}\) to obtain \(\frac{1 \cdot \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3} \cdot \sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{7}\) to obtain \(\frac{1 \cdot \sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{7} \cdot \sqrt{7}} = \frac{\sqrt{7}}{7}\).

qs.q:
