Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{x}\) to obtain \(\frac{1 \cdot \sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x} \cdot \sqrt{x}} = \frac{\sqrt{x}}{x}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{5}\) to obtain \(\frac{1 \cdot \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5} \cdot \sqrt{5}} = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\frac{4}{\sqrt{6}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{6}\) to get \(\frac{4\sqrt{6}}{6}\), then divide the numerator and denominator by \(2\) to simplify to \(\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\frac{5}{\sqrt{x} - 2}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{x} + 2\) to get \(\frac{5(\sqrt{x} + 2)}{(\sqrt{x})^2 - 2^2} = \frac{5\sqrt{x} + 10}{x - 4}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2}\) to get \(\frac{\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2}}{(\sqrt{5})^2 - (\sqrt{2})^2} = \frac{\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\sqrt{\frac{3}{5x}}\)
qs.s: Rewrite as \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{5x}}\) and multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{5x}\) to get \(\frac{\sqrt{15x}}{5x}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\frac{2}{3 - \sqrt{7}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(3 + \sqrt{7}\) to obtain \(\frac{2(3 + \sqrt{7})}{3^2 - (\sqrt{7})^2} = \frac{2(3 + \sqrt{7})}{2} = 3 + \sqrt{7}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{4}}\)
qs.s: Since \(4 = 2^2\), multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{2}\) to make a perfect cube in the radicand. This yields \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\sqrt[3]{8}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{2}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{x}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{x^2}\). The denominator simplifies to \(\sqrt[3]{x^3} = x\), resulting in \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{x^2}}{x}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{6}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{6^2} = \sqrt[3]{36}\). The denominator becomes \(\sqrt[3]{216} = 6\), giving \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{36}}{6}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{5}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{5^2} = \sqrt[3]{25}\). The denominator becomes \(\sqrt[3]{125} = 5\), giving \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{25}}{5}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{3^2} = \sqrt[3]{9}\). This gives \(\frac{1 \cdot \sqrt[3]{9}}{\sqrt[3]{3} \cdot \sqrt[3]{9}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{9}}{\sqrt[3]{27}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{9}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{4}{\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3}\) to obtain \(\frac{4(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3})}{(\sqrt{7})^2 - (\sqrt{3})^2} = \frac{4(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3})}{4}\). Canceling \(4\) gives \(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt[3]{5}}{\sqrt[3]{12}}\)
qs.s: Since \(12 = 2^2 \cdot 3\), multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{2 \cdot 3^2} = \sqrt[3]{18}\). This gives \(\frac{\sqrt[3]{5 \cdot 18}}{\sqrt[3]{216}} = \frac{\sqrt[3]{90}}{6}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \frac{4x}{\sqrt[3]{2x^2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{4x}\) to obtain \(\frac{4x\sqrt[3]{4x}}{\sqrt[3]{8x^3}} = \frac{4x\sqrt[3]{4x}}{2x}\). Simplifying the common factor of \(2x\) leaves \(2\sqrt[3]{4x}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{6}{\sqrt[3]{9}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{3}\) to get \(\frac{6\sqrt[3]{3}}{\sqrt[3]{27}} = \frac{6\sqrt[3]{3}}{3}\). Dividing the integers gives \(2\sqrt[3]{3}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{6}{3 - \sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(3 + \sqrt{3}\) to obtain \(\frac{6(3 + \sqrt{3})}{3^2 - (\sqrt{3})^2} = \frac{6(3 + \sqrt{3})}{6}\). Canceling \(6\) leaves \(3 + \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{7 + \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{2}\) to obtain \(\frac{(7 + \sqrt{2})\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{2}} = \frac{7\sqrt{2} + 2}{2}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{4 - \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{5}\) to obtain \(\frac{(4 - \sqrt{5})\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}\cdot\sqrt{5}} = \frac{4\sqrt{5} - 5}{5}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{1 + \sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{6}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{6}\) to obtain \(\frac{(1 + \sqrt{6})\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{6}\cdot\sqrt{6}} = \frac{\sqrt{6} + 6}{6}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{2 - \sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{7}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{7}\) to obtain \(\frac{(2 - \sqrt{7})\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{7}\cdot\sqrt{7}} = \frac{2\sqrt{7} - 7}{7}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{5 + \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{3}\) to obtain \(\frac{(5 + \sqrt{3})\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}\cdot\sqrt{3}} = \frac{5\sqrt{3} + 3}{3}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive: \(\frac{\sqrt{x} + 4}{\sqrt{x} - 2}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{x} + 2\): \(\frac{(\sqrt{x} + 4)(\sqrt{x} + 2)}{(\sqrt{x} - 2)(\sqrt{x} + 2)} = \frac{x + 6\sqrt{x} + 8}{x - 4}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{4\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{6}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{6}\) to get \(\frac{4\sqrt{18} - 3\sqrt{12}}{6} = \frac{12\sqrt{2} - 6\sqrt{3}}{6}\). Dividing both terms by \(6\) yields \(2\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{\sqrt{3} + 2}{\sqrt{3} - 1}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{3} + 1\): \(\frac{(\sqrt{3} + 2)(\sqrt{3} + 1)}{(\sqrt{3} - 1)(\sqrt{3} + 1)} = \frac{3 + 3\sqrt{3} + 2}{3 - 1} = \frac{5 + 3\sqrt{3}}{2}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{3\sqrt{2} - 2}{3\sqrt{2} + 2}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(3\sqrt{2} - 2\): \(\frac{(3\sqrt{2} - 2)^2}{(3\sqrt{2})^2 - 2^2} = \frac{18 - 12\sqrt{2} + 4}{18 - 4} = \frac{22 - 12\sqrt{2}}{14}\). Dividing by \(2\) gives \(\frac{11 - 6\sqrt{2}}{7}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2}\): \(\frac{(\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2})^2}{(\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2})(\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2})} = \frac{5 - 2\sqrt{10} + 2}{5 - 2} = \frac{7 - 2\sqrt{10}}{3}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{6 - \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{7}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{7}\) to obtain \(\frac{(6 - \sqrt{5})\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{7}\cdot\sqrt{7}} = \frac{6\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{35}}{7}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{4 + \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{5}\) to obtain \(\frac{(4 + \sqrt{3})\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}\cdot\sqrt{5}} = \frac{4\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{15}}{5}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{7 + \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{5}\) to obtain \(\frac{(7 + \sqrt{2})\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}\cdot\sqrt{5}} = \frac{7\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{10}}{5}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{2 + \sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{3}\) to obtain \(\frac{(2 + \sqrt{7})\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}\cdot\sqrt{3}} = \frac{2\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{21}}{3}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{3 - \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{2}\) to obtain \(\frac{(3 - \sqrt{5})\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{2}} = \frac{3\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{10}}{2}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{7}{4 - \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(4 + \sqrt{2}\) to obtain \(\frac{7(4 + \sqrt{2})}{4^2 - (\sqrt{2})^2} = \frac{7(4 + \sqrt{2})}{14}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{4 + \sqrt{2}}{2}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3}\) to get \(\frac{(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3})^2}{(\sqrt{7})^2 - (\sqrt{3})^2} = \frac{10 + 2\sqrt{21}}{4}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{5 + \sqrt{21}}{2}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{6 - \sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{12}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the denominator to \(2\sqrt{3}\) and multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{3}\) to get \(\frac{6\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{18}}{6} = \frac{6\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{2}}{6}\), then divide numerator and denominator by \(3\) to obtain \(\frac{2\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}{2}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive: \(\frac{\sqrt{x} + 3}{\sqrt{x} - 1}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{x} + 1\) to obtain \(\frac{(\sqrt{x} + 3)(\sqrt{x} + 1)}{(\sqrt{x})^2 - 1^2} = \frac{x + 4\sqrt{x} + 3}{x - 1}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{\sqrt{5} + 1}{\sqrt{5} - 1}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{5} + 1\) to get \(\frac{(\sqrt{5} + 1)^2}{(\sqrt{5})^2 - 1^2} = \frac{6 + 2\sqrt{5}}{4}\), which reduces to \(\frac{3 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3}\) to obtain \(\frac{\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3}}{(\sqrt{7})^2 - (\sqrt{3})^2} = \frac{\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3}}{7 - 3} = \frac{\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3}}{4}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{4 + \sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(4 - \sqrt{3}\) to obtain \(\frac{4 - \sqrt{3}}{4^2 - (\sqrt{3})^2} = \frac{4 - \sqrt{3}}{16 - 3} = \frac{4 - \sqrt{3}}{13}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{5 - \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(5 + \sqrt{2}\) to obtain \(\frac{5 + \sqrt{2}}{5^2 - (\sqrt{2})^2} = \frac{5 + \sqrt{2}}{25 - 2} = \frac{5 + \sqrt{2}}{23}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{3 - \sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(3 + \sqrt{5}\) to obtain \(\frac{3 + \sqrt{5}}{3^2 - (\sqrt{5})^2} = \frac{3 + \sqrt{5}}{9 - 5} = \frac{3 + \sqrt{5}}{4}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2}\) to obtain \(\frac{\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2}}{(\sqrt{5})^2 - (\sqrt{2})^2} = \frac{\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2}}{5 - 2} = \frac{\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{x} + 4}{\sqrt{x} - 3}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{x} + 3\) to get \(\frac{(\sqrt{x} + 4)(\sqrt{x} + 3)}{(\sqrt{x} - 3)(\sqrt{x} + 3)}\). Expanding gives \(\frac{x + 3\sqrt{x} + 4\sqrt{x} + 12}{x - 9} = \frac{x + 7\sqrt{x} + 12}{x - 9}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{3\sqrt{2} + 2}{2\sqrt{2} - 1}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(2\sqrt{2} + 1\) to get \(\frac{(3\sqrt{2} + 2)(2\sqrt{2} + 1)}{(2\sqrt{2})^2 - 1^2} = \frac{12 + 3\sqrt{2} + 4\sqrt{2} + 2}{8 - 1} = \frac{14 + 7\sqrt{2}}{7}\). Dividing each term by \(7\) gives \(2 + \sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{4\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3}\) to get \(\frac{4\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3})}{7 - 3} = \frac{4\sqrt{21} + 12}{4}\). Factoring out and dividing by \(4\) leaves \(3 + \sqrt{21}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}\) to get \(\frac{(\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2})^2}{6 - 2} = \frac{6 + 2\sqrt{12} + 2}{4} = \frac{8 + 4\sqrt{3}}{4} = 2 + \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive and \(x \neq y\).
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{y}}{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{y}\) to get \(\frac{(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{y})^2}{(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y})(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{y})}\). Expanding both gives \(\frac{x - 2\sqrt{xy} + y}{x - y}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\frac{1}{3 + \sqrt{7}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(3 - \sqrt{7}\). This results in \(\frac{3 - \sqrt{7}}{3^2 - (\sqrt{7})^2} = \frac{3 - \sqrt{7}}{9 - 7} = \frac{3 - \sqrt{7}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5} - 1}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{5} + 1\). This gives \(\frac{\sqrt{5} + 1}{(\sqrt{5})^2 - 1^2} = \frac{\sqrt{5} + 1}{5 - 1} = \frac{\sqrt{5} + 1}{4}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\frac{1}{6 - \sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(6 + \sqrt{5}\). This gives \(\frac{6 + \sqrt{5}}{6^2 - (\sqrt{5})^2} = \frac{6 + \sqrt{5}}{36 - 5} = \frac{6 + \sqrt{5}}{31}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\frac{6}{3\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(3\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{3}\). The denominator simplifies to \((3\sqrt{2})^2 - (2\sqrt{3})^2 = 18 - 12 = 6\), which cancels with the 6 in the numerator to leave \(3\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\frac{\sqrt{x} - 3}{\sqrt{x} + 2}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{x} - 2\). Expanding the numerator gives \(x - 5\sqrt{x} + 6\) and the denominator gives \((\sqrt{x})^2 - 2^2 = x - 4\), resulting in \(\frac{x - 5\sqrt{x} + 6}{x - 4}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\frac{\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\). The denominator becomes \((\sqrt{3})^2 - (\sqrt{2})^2 = 1\) and the numerator expands to \((\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2})^2 = 3 + 2\sqrt{6} + 2 = 5 + 2\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\frac{\sqrt{5} + 2}{\sqrt{5} - 1}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{5} + 1\). Expanding the numerator gives \((\sqrt{5} + 2)(\sqrt{5} + 1) = 5 + 3\sqrt{5} + 2 = 7 + 3\sqrt{5}\), and the denominator is \((\sqrt{5})^2 - 1^2 = 4\), yielding \(\frac{7 + 3\sqrt{5}}{4}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2}\). The expression becomes \(\frac{\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2})}{(\sqrt{5})^2 - (\sqrt{2})^2} = \frac{\sqrt{15} + \sqrt{6}}{5 - 2} = \frac{\sqrt{15} + \sqrt{6}}{3}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and simplify: \(\frac{\sqrt{20}}{\sqrt{5} - 1}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{5} + 1\) to get \(\frac{\sqrt{20}(\sqrt{5} + 1)}{5 - 1} = \frac{10 + 2\sqrt{5}}{4}\). Dividing the numerator and denominator by 2 yields \(\frac{5 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and simplify: \(\frac{\sqrt{72}}{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}\) to obtain \(\frac{6\sqrt{2}(\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2})}{6 - 2} = \frac{12\sqrt{3} - 12}{4}\). Dividing by 4 gives \(3\sqrt{3} - 3\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and simplify: \(\frac{\sqrt{24}}{\sqrt{6} + 2}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{6} - 2\) to get \(\frac{\sqrt{24}(\sqrt{6} - 2)}{6 - 4} = \frac{12 - 4\sqrt{6}}{2}\). Dividing each term by 2 gives \(6 - 2\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and simplify: \(\frac{\sqrt{18}}{3 - \sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(3 + \sqrt{3}\) to obtain \(\frac{3\sqrt{2}(3 + \sqrt{3})}{9 - 3} = \frac{9\sqrt{2} + 3\sqrt{6}}{6}\). Dividing the numerator and denominator by 3 gives \(\frac{3\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{6}}{2}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and simplify: \(\frac{\sqrt{8}}{3 - \sqrt{7}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(3 + \sqrt{7}\) to obtain \(\frac{2\sqrt{2}(3 + \sqrt{7})}{9 - 7} = \frac{6\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{14}}{2}\). Dividing by 2 simplifies the expression to \(3\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{14}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and simplify: \(\frac{5\sqrt{2} + 2}{3\sqrt{2} - 4}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(3\sqrt{2} + 4\) to get \(\frac{(5\sqrt{2} + 2)(3\sqrt{2} + 4)}{(3\sqrt{2})^2 - 4^2} = \frac{38 + 26\sqrt{2}}{18 - 16} = \frac{38 + 26\sqrt{2}}{2}\). Dividing each term by 2 yields \(19 + 13\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and simplify. Assume all variables represent positive numbers: \(\frac{2\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y}}{\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{y}\) to get \(\frac{(2\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y})(\sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{y})}{(\sqrt{x})^2 - (2\sqrt{y})^2}\). Expanding the numerator gives \(\frac{2x + 5\sqrt{xy} + 2y}{x - 4y}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and simplify: \(\frac{\sqrt{48} - \sqrt{18}}{\sqrt{6} - 2}\)
qs.s: Simplify the numerator to \(4\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{2}\) and multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{6} + 2\) to obtain \(\frac{(4\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{2})(\sqrt{6} + 2)}{6 - 4} = \frac{6\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{3}}{2}\). Dividing by 2 yields \(3\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and simplify: \(\frac{3\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{5}\) to obtain \(\frac{(3\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{5})(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{5})}{7 - 5} = \frac{26 + 4\sqrt{35}}{2}\). Dividing by 2 gives \(13 + 2\sqrt{35}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and simplify: \(\frac{2\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{5} - 3\sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(2\sqrt{5} + 3\sqrt{2}\) to get \(\frac{(2\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2})(2\sqrt{5} + 3\sqrt{2})}{(2\sqrt{5})^2 - (3\sqrt{2})^2} = \frac{14 + 4\sqrt{10}}{20 - 18} = \frac{14 + 4\sqrt{10}}{2}\). Dividing by 2 yields \(7 + 2\sqrt{10}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{\sqrt{8}}{\sqrt{2} + 1}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{2} - 1\) to get \(\frac{\sqrt{8}(\sqrt{2} - 1)}{(\sqrt{2})^2 - 1^2} = \frac{\sqrt{16} - \sqrt{8}}{2 - 1}\). Simplifying the radicals yields \(4 - 2\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{\sqrt{24}}{\sqrt{6} - 2}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{6} + 2\) to get \(\frac{\sqrt{24}(\sqrt{6} + 2)}{(\sqrt{6})^2 - 2^2} = \frac{12 + 4\sqrt{6}}{2}\). Dividing both terms by 2 yields \(6 + 2\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{\sqrt{12}}{\sqrt{3} - 1}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{3} + 1\) to get \(\frac{\sqrt{12}(\sqrt{3} + 1)}{(\sqrt{3})^2 - 1^2} = \frac{6 + 2\sqrt{3}}{2}\). Dividing each term by 2 gives \(3 + \sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{\sqrt{20}}{\sqrt{5} + 2}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{5} - 2\) to get \(\frac{\sqrt{20}(\sqrt{5} - 2)}{(\sqrt{5})^2 - 2^2} = \frac{\sqrt{100} - 2\sqrt{20}}{5 - 4}\). Simplifying the numerator gives \(10 - 4\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{\sqrt{27}}{2 - \sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(2 + \sqrt{3}\) to obtain \(\frac{\sqrt{27}(2 + \sqrt{3})}{2^2 - (\sqrt{3})^2} = \frac{2\sqrt{27} + \sqrt{81}}{4 - 3}\). Simplifying gives \(6\sqrt{3} + 9\), or \(9 + 6\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive: \(\frac{\sqrt{x} + 4}{\sqrt{x} - 2}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{x} + 2\) to get denominator \((\sqrt{x})^2 - 2^2 = x - 4\). Expanding the numerator gives \((\sqrt{x} + 4)(\sqrt{x} + 2) = x + 2\sqrt{x} + 4\sqrt{x} + 8 = x + 6\sqrt{x} + 8\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{3\sqrt{5} + 2}{\sqrt{5} - 2}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{5} + 2\) to obtain denominator \((\sqrt{5})^2 - 2^2 = 1\). Expanding the numerator gives \((3\sqrt{5} + 2)(\sqrt{5} + 2) = 15 + 6\sqrt{5} + 2\sqrt{5} + 4 = 19 + 8\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{4\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply by the conjugate \(2\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}\) to obtain denominator \((2\sqrt{3})^2 - (\sqrt{2})^2 = 12 - 2 = 10\). The numerator expands to \(24 - 4\sqrt{6} - 2\sqrt{6} + 2 = 26 - 6\sqrt{6}\), which reduces to \(\frac{13 - 3\sqrt{6}}{5}\) after dividing by 2.

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{\sqrt{54}}{3\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(3\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{3}\) to get denominator \((3\sqrt{2})^2 - (2\sqrt{3})^2 = 18 - 12 = 6\). The numerator expands to \(3\sqrt{6}(3\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{3}) = 18\sqrt{3} + 18\sqrt{2}\), and dividing each term by 6 gives \(3\sqrt{2} + 3\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q: Rationalize the denominator and write the quotient in lowest terms: \(\frac{2\sqrt{6} + 3\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}\) to get denominator \(6 - 2 = 4\). Expanding the numerator yields \(12 + 2\sqrt{12} + 3\sqrt{12} + 6 = 18 + 10\sqrt{3}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{9 + 5\sqrt{3}}{2}\) after dividing by 2.

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{4 + \sqrt{5}}{2 - \sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(2 + \sqrt{5}\) to get \(\frac{(4 + \sqrt{5})(2 + \sqrt{5})}{4 - 5} = \frac{8 + 4\sqrt{5} + 2\sqrt{5} + 5}{-1} = \frac{13 + 6\sqrt{5}}{-1} = -13 - 6\sqrt{5}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{3 - \sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(3 + \sqrt{5}\) to get \(\frac{(1 + \sqrt{5})(3 + \sqrt{5})}{9 - 5} = \frac{3 + \sqrt{5} + 3\sqrt{5} + 5}{4} = \frac{8 + 4\sqrt{5}}{4} = 2 + \sqrt{5}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{3 - \sqrt{2}}{3 + \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(3 - \sqrt{2}\) to obtain \(\frac{(3 - \sqrt{2})^2}{3^2 - (\sqrt{2})^2} = \frac{9 - 6\sqrt{2} + 2}{9 - 2} = \frac{11 - 6\sqrt{2}}{7}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{5 + \sqrt{3}}{2 + \sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(2 - \sqrt{3}\) to get \(\frac{(5 + \sqrt{3})(2 - \sqrt{3})}{4 - 3} = \frac{10 - 5\sqrt{3} + 2\sqrt{3} - 3}{1} = 7 - 3\sqrt{3}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{4 - \sqrt{2}}{2 - \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(2 + \sqrt{2}\) to obtain \(\frac{(4 - \sqrt{2})(2 + \sqrt{2})}{4 - 2} = \frac{8 + 4\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{2} - 2}{2} = \frac{6 + 2\sqrt{2}}{2} = 3 + \sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{6 + \sqrt{24}}{\sqrt{6} - 2}\)
qs.s: Simplify \(\sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6}\) to write \(\frac{6 + 2\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{6} - 2}\), then multiply by conjugate \(\sqrt{6} + 2\) to yield \(\frac{(6 + 2\sqrt{6})(\sqrt{6} + 2)}{6 - 4} = \frac{24 + 10\sqrt{6}}{2} = 12 + 5\sqrt{6}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{3\sqrt{2} + 2}{2\sqrt{2} - 3}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(2\sqrt{2} + 3\) to get \(\frac{(3\sqrt{2} + 2)(2\sqrt{2} + 3)}{(2\sqrt{2})^2 - 3^2} = \frac{12 + 9\sqrt{2} + 4\sqrt{2} + 6}{8 - 9} = \frac{18 + 13\sqrt{2}}{-1} = -18 - 13\sqrt{2}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{4\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply by \(2\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{2}\) in numerator and denominator: \(\frac{24 - 12\sqrt{6} - 2\sqrt{6} + 6}{12 - 18} = \frac{30 - 14\sqrt{6}}{-6} = \frac{-15 + 7\sqrt{6}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3}\) to obtain \(\frac{(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3})^2}{7 - 3} = \frac{7 + 2\sqrt{21} + 3}{4} = \frac{10 + 2\sqrt{21}}{4} = \frac{5 + \sqrt{21}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2\sqrt{x} - 3}{\sqrt{x} + 4}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{x} - 4\) to obtain \(\frac{(2\sqrt{x} - 3)(\sqrt{x} - 4)}{(\sqrt{x})^2 - 4^2} = \frac{2x - 8\sqrt{x} - 3\sqrt{x} + 12}{x - 16} = \frac{2x - 11\sqrt{x} + 12}{x - 16}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{3}\). The denominator is \(7 - 3 = 4\), which results in \(\frac{\sqrt{5}(\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{3})}{4} = \frac{\sqrt{35} - \sqrt{15}}{4}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{7}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{7}\). The denominator is \(2 - 7 = -5\), giving \(\frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{21}}{-5} = -\frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{21}}{5}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2}\). The denominator is \((\sqrt{5})^2 - (\sqrt{2})^2 = 5 - 2 = 3\), giving \(\frac{\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2})}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{15} - \sqrt{6}}{3}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\). The denominator becomes \((\sqrt{3})^2 - (\sqrt{2})^2 = 3 - 2 = 1\), giving \(\sqrt{7}(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}) = \sqrt{21} + \sqrt{14}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{11} - \sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{11} + \sqrt{5}\). The denominator becomes \(11 - 5 = 6\), giving \(\frac{\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{11} + \sqrt{5})}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{33} + \sqrt{15}}{6}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{3y}}{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{3y}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{3y}\). Expanding gives \(\frac{(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{3y})^2}{(\sqrt{x})^2 - (\sqrt{3y})^2} = \frac{x - 2\sqrt{3xy} + 3y}{x - 3y}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2}\). Expanding the numerator gives \((\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{2})^2 = 5 + 2\sqrt{10} + 2 = 7 + 2\sqrt{10}\), and the denominator becomes \(5 - 2 = 3\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{18}}{3\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Write \(\sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}\) and multiply numerator and denominator by \(3\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{3}\). The denominator is \((3\sqrt{2})^2 - (2\sqrt{3})^2 = 18 - 12 = 6\), and the numerator is \(18 + 6\sqrt{6}\), giving \(\frac{18 + 6\sqrt{6}}{6} = 3 + \sqrt{6}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.
\(\displaystyle \frac{3 + \sqrt{5}}{3 - \sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(3 + \sqrt{5}\). The numerator is \((3 + \sqrt{5})^2 = 14 + 6\sqrt{5}\) and the denominator is \(3^2 - (\sqrt{5})^2 = 4\), which reduces to \(\frac{7 + 3\sqrt{5}}{2}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{\sqrt{y} - \sqrt{5}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{y} + \sqrt{5}\). The denominator becomes \((\sqrt{y})^2 - (\sqrt{5})^2 = y - 5\), resulting in \(\frac{\sqrt{y} + \sqrt{5}}{y - 5}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{\sqrt{2u} - \sqrt{v}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{2u} + \sqrt{v}\). The denominator simplifies to \((\sqrt{2u})^2 - (\sqrt{v})^2 = 2u - v\), yielding \(\frac{\sqrt{2u} + \sqrt{v}}{2u - v}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{3}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{3}\). The denominator simplifies to \((\sqrt{x})^2 - (\sqrt{3})^2 = x - 3\), yielding \(\frac{\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{3}}{x - 3}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{\sqrt{m} - \sqrt{n}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{m} + \sqrt{n}\). The denominator becomes \((\sqrt{m})^2 - (\sqrt{n})^2 = m - n\), giving \(\frac{\sqrt{m} + \sqrt{n}}{m - n}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b}\). The denominator simplifies as \((\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b})(\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b}) = a - b\), giving \(\frac{\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b}}{a - b}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y}}{\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{y}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y}\). The numerator expands to \((\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y})^2 = x + 2\sqrt{xy} + y\), and the denominator simplifies to \(x - y\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{2\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y}}{\sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{y}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y}\). Expanding the numerator gives \((2\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y})(\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y}) = 2x - 3\sqrt{xy} - 2y\), and the denominator simplifies to \((\sqrt{x})^2 - (2\sqrt{y})^2 = x - 4y\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x - 9y}{\sqrt{x} - 3\sqrt{y}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{y}\) to get \(\frac{(x - 9y)(\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{y})}{x - 9y}\). Canceling the common factor \((x - 9y)\) gives \(\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{y}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{4}{3\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{y}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(3\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y}\). The denominator becomes \((3\sqrt{x})^2 - (\sqrt{y})^2 = 9x - y\), giving \(\frac{4(3\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y})}{9x - y} = \frac{12\sqrt{x} + 4\sqrt{y}}{9x - y}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{p} - 5}{\sqrt{p} + 5}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{p} - 5\). This produces \((\sqrt{p} - 5)^2 = p - 10\sqrt{p} + 25\) in the numerator and \((\sqrt{p})^2 - 5^2 = p - 25\) in the denominator.

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{m} + 3}{\sqrt{m} - 3}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{m} + 3\). The numerator expands to \((\sqrt{m} + 3)^2 = m + 6\sqrt{m} + 9\), and the denominator becomes \((\sqrt{m})^2 - 3^2 = m - 9\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{u} + 2v}{\sqrt{u} - 2v}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{u} + 2v\). The numerator expands to \((\sqrt{u} + 2v)^2 = u + 4v\sqrt{u} + 4v^2\), and the denominator becomes \((\sqrt{u})^2 - (2v)^2 = u - 4v^2\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{x} - y}{\sqrt{x} + y}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{x} - y\). Expanding the numerator gives \((\sqrt{x} - y)^2 = x - 2y\sqrt{x} + y^2\), and the denominator becomes \((\sqrt{x})^2 - y^2 = x - y^2\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{c + \sqrt{d}}{c - \sqrt{d}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(c + \sqrt{d}\). Expanding gives \((c + \sqrt{d})^2 = c^2 + 2c\sqrt{d} + d\) in the numerator and \(c^2 - (\sqrt{d})^2 = c^2 - d\) in the denominator.

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{6x} - \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{6x} + \sqrt{2}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{6x} - \sqrt{2}\) to obtain \(\frac{6x - 2\sqrt{12x} + 2}{6x - 2} = \frac{6x - 4\sqrt{3x} + 2}{6x - 2}\). Dividing numerator and denominator by \(2\) reduces the quotient to \(\frac{3x - 2\sqrt{3x} + 1}{3x - 1}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{2\sqrt{x} + 3\sqrt{y}}{3\sqrt{x} - 2\sqrt{y}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(3\sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{y}\). Expanding the numerator gives \(6x + 4\sqrt{xy} + 9\sqrt{xy} + 6y = 6x + 13\sqrt{xy} + 6y\), and the denominator becomes \((3\sqrt{x})^2 - (2\sqrt{y})^2 = 9x - 4y\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{4\sqrt{x} - 3y}{2\sqrt{x} + 5y}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(2\sqrt{x} - 5y\). Expanding the numerator gives \(8x - 20y\sqrt{x} - 6y\sqrt{x} + 15y^2 = 8x - 26y\sqrt{x} + 15y^2\), and the denominator simplifies to \((2\sqrt{x})^2 - (5y)^2 = 4x - 25y^2\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{3x} + 3}{\sqrt{3x} - 3}\)
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{3x} + 3\) to obtain \(\frac{3x + 6\sqrt{3x} + 9}{3x - 9}\). Dividing both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor \(3\) gives \(\frac{x + 2\sqrt{3x} + 3}{x - 3}\).

qs.q:
Rationalize the denominator. Write the quotient in lowest terms. Assume all variables are positive.

\(\displaystyle \frac{3\sqrt{2x} + 2\sqrt{3y}}{3\sqrt{2x} - 2\sqrt{3y}}\)
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(3\sqrt{2x} + 2\sqrt{3y}\) to get \(\frac{18x + 12\sqrt{6xy} + 12y}{18x - 12y}\). Factoring out the common factor \(6\) from numerator and denominator simplifies the expression to \(\frac{3x + 2\sqrt{6xy} + 2y}{3x - 2y}\).

qs.q: The kinetic energy of an object is given by \(E = \frac{1}{2}mv^2\), where \(m\) is the mass in kilograms and \(v\) is the velocity in meters per second. If an object with a mass of \(6\text{ kg}\) has a kinetic energy of \(75\text{ J}\), what is its velocity?
qs.s: Substitute the values into \(75 = \frac{1}{2}(6)v^2 = 3v^2\). Dividing both sides by \(3\) gives \(v^2 = 25\), so \(v = \sqrt{25} = 5\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: The surface area of a sphere is \(A = 4\pi r^2\). If the surface area of a sphere is \(144\pi\text{ cm}^2\), what is the radius?
qs.s: Substitute \(A = 144\pi\) into the formula to obtain \(144\pi = 4\pi r^2\). Dividing by \(4\pi\) gives \(r^2 = 36\), so \(r = \sqrt{36} = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is \(V = \pi r^2 h\). If the volume of a cylinder is \(80\pi\text{ cm}^3\) and the height is \(5\text{ cm}\), what is the radius?
qs.s: Substitute the values into the formula: \(80\pi = \pi r^2 (5) = 5\pi r^2\). Divide both sides by \(5\pi\) to get \(r^2 = 16\), which yields \(r = \sqrt{16} = 4\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a square pyramid is \(V = \frac{1}{3}s^2 h\), where \(s\) is the side length of the base and \(h\) is the height. If the volume is \(96\text{ m}^3\) and the height is \(8\text{ m}\), what is the side length of the base?
qs.s: Substitute the given values into the formula: \(96 = \frac{1}{3}s^2(8) = \frac{8}{3}s^2\). Multiply both sides by \(\frac{3}{8}\) to find \(s^2 = 36\), giving \(s = \sqrt{36} = 6\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cone is \(V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). If the volume of a cone is \(100\pi\text{ cm}^3\) and the height is \(12\text{ cm}\), what is the radius?
qs.s: Substitute the given values into the formula to get \(100\pi = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 (12) = 4\pi r^2\). Dividing both sides by \(4\pi\) gives \(r^2 = 25\), so \(r = \sqrt{25} = 5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a pyramid with a square base is \(V = \frac{1}{3}s^2 h\), where \(s\) is the side length of the base and \(h\) is the height. If the volume is \(280\text{ m}^3\) and the height is \(6\text{ m}\), what is the perimeter of the square base in simplest radical form?
qs.s: Substitute the given values into \(280 = \frac{1}{3}s^2(6) = 2s^2\), which gives \(s^2 = 140\) and \(s = \sqrt{140} = 2\sqrt{35}\text{ m}\). The perimeter is \(4s = 4(2\sqrt{35}) = 8\sqrt{35}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The area of an equilateral triangle is given by \(A = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2\), where \(s\) is the side length. If the area of an equilateral triangle is \(18\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2\), what is its side length in simplest radical form?
qs.s: Substitute \(A = 18\sqrt{3}\) into the formula: \(18\sqrt{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2\). Divide by \(\sqrt{3}\) and multiply by \(4\) to get \(s^2 = 72\), so \(s = \sqrt{72} = 6\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cone is \(V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). If the volume of a cone is \(150\pi\text{ cm}^3\) and the height is \(10\text{ cm}\), what is the radius in simplest radical form?
qs.s: Substitute the known values into the equation: \(150\pi = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2(10) = \frac{10}{3}\pi r^2\). Multiply both sides by \(\frac{3}{10\pi}\) to get \(r^2 = 45\), so \(r = \sqrt{45} = 3\sqrt{5}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is \(V = \pi r^2 h\). If a cylinder has a volume of \(40\pi\text{ cm}^3\) and a height of \(6\text{ cm}\), what is its radius in simplest radical form?
qs.s: Substitute into \(40\pi = 6\pi r^2\) to find \(r^2 = \frac{40}{6} = \frac{20}{3}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing the denominator gives \(r = \frac{\sqrt{20}}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{2\sqrt{5}\cdot\sqrt{3}}{3} = \frac{2\sqrt{15}}{3}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is \(V = \pi r^2 h\). A cylinder has a height of \(8\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(384\pi\text{ cm}^3\). What is the diameter of the cylinder in simplest radical form?
qs.s: Substitute the values into \(384\pi = 8\pi r^2\), giving \(r^2 = 48\) and \(r = \sqrt{48} = 4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\). The diameter is \(2r = 2(4\sqrt{3}) = 8\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The kinetic energy of an object is given by \(E = \frac{1}{2}mv^2\), where \(m\) is mass and \(v\) is speed. If an object with mass \(m = 10\text{ kg}\) has a kinetic energy of \(49\text{ J}\), what is its speed?
qs.s: Substitute the given values into \(\frac{1}{2}(10)v^2 = 49\), which simplifies to \(5v^2 = 49\), so \(v^2 = \frac{49}{5}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing the denominator gives \(v = \frac{7}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{7\sqrt{5}}{5}\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: The curved surface area of an open cylinder with equal height and radius is given by \(A = 2\pi r^2\). If the curved surface area is \(32\text{ cm}^2\), what is the radius?
qs.s: Setting \(2\pi r^2 = 32\) gives \(r^2 = \frac{16}{\pi}\), so \(r = \sqrt{\frac{16}{\pi}} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi}}\). Multiplying numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{\pi}\) yields \(r = \frac{4\sqrt{\pi}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The power dissipated by an electrical resistor is given by \(P = I^2 R\), where \(I\) is current and \(R\) is resistance. If a resistor with resistance \(R = 7\ \Omega\) dissipates \(36\text{ W}\) of power, what is the current?
qs.s: Substitute \(P = 36\) and \(R = 7\) to get \(7I^2 = 36\), so \(I^2 = \frac{36}{7}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing the denominator yields \(I = \frac{6}{\sqrt{7}} = \frac{6\sqrt{7}}{7}\text{ A}\).

qs.q: The area of a circle is given by \(A = \pi r^2\). If the area of the circle is \(64\text{ m}^2\), what is its radius?
qs.s: Setting \(\pi r^2 = 64\) gives \(r^2 = \frac{64}{\pi}\), so \(r = \sqrt{\frac{64}{\pi}} = \frac{8}{\sqrt{\pi}}\). Rationalizing the denominator yields \(r = \frac{8\sqrt{\pi}}{\pi}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The total surface area of a cube is given by \(S = 6s^2\), where \(s\) is the side length. If the surface area of the cube is \(50\text{ cm}^2\), what is its side length?
qs.s: Solving \(6s^2 = 50\) yields \(s^2 = \frac{25}{3}\), which gives \(s = \sqrt{\frac{25}{3}} = \frac{5}{\sqrt{3}}\). Rationalizing the denominator gives \(s = \frac{5\sqrt{3}}{3}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The area of a rectangle is \(A = l \cdot w\). If the area of the rectangle is \(8\text{ m}^2\) and its width is \(\sqrt{5} - 1\text{ m}\), what is its length?
qs.s: The length is \(l = \frac{8}{\sqrt{5}-1}\). Multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{5}+1\) gives \(l = \frac{8(\sqrt{5}+1)}{5-1} = \frac{8(\sqrt{5}+1)}{4} = 2\sqrt{5} + 2\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The surface area of a sphere is \(S = 4\pi r^2\), and its diameter is \(d = 2r\). If the surface area of a sphere is \(72\text{ cm}^2\), what is its diameter?
qs.s: Setting \(4\pi r^2 = 72\) gives \(r^2 = \frac{18}{\pi}\), so \(r = \frac{\sqrt{18}}{\sqrt{\pi}} = \frac{3\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\). Multiplying by 2 to find the diameter gives \(d = 2r = \frac{6\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The total surface area of a closed cylinder is given by \(S = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh\), where \(r\) is the radius and \(h\) is the height. If the height is three times the radius (\(h = 3r\)) and the total surface area is \(96\text{ cm}^2\), what is the radius?
qs.s: Substitute \(h = 3r\) into the formula to get \(S = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r(3r) = 8\pi r^2\). Setting \(8\pi r^2 = 96\) gives \(r^2 = \frac{12}{\pi}\), so \(r = \sqrt{\frac{12}{\pi}} = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{\pi}} = \frac{2\sqrt{3\pi}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The area of a circle is given by \(A = \pi r^2\). Two concentric circles have areas of \(32\text{ cm}^2\) and \(72\text{ cm}^2\). What is the width of the ring between them (the difference between the larger radius and the smaller radius)?
qs.s: The radii are \(r_1 = \sqrt{\frac{32}{\pi}} = \frac{4\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\) and \(r_2 = \sqrt{\frac{72}{\pi}} = \frac{6\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\). Subtracting the radii yields the ring width \(r_2 - r_1 = \frac{6\sqrt{2\pi} - 4\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi} = \frac{2\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder whose height equals its radius is given by \(V = \pi r^3\). If the volume of the cylinder is \(24\text{ m}^3\), what is its radius?
qs.s: Solving \(\pi r^3 = 24\) gives \(r^3 = \frac{24}{\pi}\), so \(r = \frac{\sqrt[3]{24}}{\sqrt[3]{\pi}} = \frac{2\sqrt[3]{3}}{\sqrt[3]{\pi}}\). Multiplying numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt[3]{\pi^2}\) to rationalize the denominator gives \(r = \frac{2\sqrt[3]{3\pi^2}}{\pi}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The kinetic energy of an object is given by \(E = \frac{1}{2}mv^2\), where \(m\) is its mass in kilograms and \(v\) is its speed in meters per second. If an object with a mass of \(6\text{ kg}\) has a kinetic energy of \(25\text{ J}\), what is its speed?
qs.s: Substituting the values gives \(25 = \frac{1}{2}(6)v^2 = 3v^2\), so \(v^2 = \frac{25}{3}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing the denominator gives \(v = \frac{5}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{5\sqrt{3}}{3}\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is given by \(V = \pi r^2 h\). If a cylinder has a height of \(h = 6\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(V = 48\text{ cm}^3\), what is its radius?
qs.s: Setting \(48 = \pi r^2(6)\) gives \(r^2 = \frac{8}{\pi}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing the denominator yields \(r = \frac{\sqrt{8}}{\sqrt{\pi}} = \frac{2\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The surface area of a sphere is \(A = 4\pi r^2\). If the surface area of a sphere is \(72\text{ cm}^2\), what is its radius?
qs.s: Setting \(4\pi r^2 = 72\) gives \(r^2 = \frac{18}{\pi}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing the denominator yields \(r = \frac{\sqrt{18}}{\sqrt{\pi}} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{\sqrt{\pi}} = \frac{3\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a sphere is \(V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\). If the volume of a sphere is \(32\text{ cm}^3\), what is its radius?
qs.s: Setting \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = 32\) gives \(r^3 = \frac{24}{\pi}\). Taking the cube root and rationalizing the denominator yields \(r = \frac{\sqrt[3]{24}}{\sqrt[3]{\pi}} \cdot \frac{\sqrt[3]{\pi^2}}{\sqrt[3]{\pi^2}} = \frac{2\sqrt[3]{3\pi^2}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cone is given by \(V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). If a cone has a height of \(h = 5\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(V = 20\text{ cm}^3\), what is its radius?
qs.s: Substituting the given values gives \(20 = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2(5)\), so \(r^2 = \frac{12}{\pi}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing gives \(r = \frac{\sqrt{12}}{\sqrt{\pi}} = \frac{2\sqrt{3\pi}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The surface area of a cube is given by \(A = 6s^2\), and its volume is given by \(V = s^3\), where \(s\) is the side length. If the surface area of a cube is \(20\text{ cm}^2\), what is its volume?
qs.s: From \(6s^2 = 20\), we have \(s^2 = \frac{10}{3}\) and \(s = \frac{\sqrt{30}}{3}\text{ cm}\). Then the volume is \(V = s^2 \cdot s = \frac{10}{3} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{30}}{3} = \frac{10\sqrt{30}}{9}\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is \(V = \pi r^2 h\) and its total surface area is \(A = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh\). If a cylinder has a height of \(h = 4\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(V = 32\text{ cm}^3\), what is its total surface area?
qs.s: From \(32 = 4\pi r^2\), we find \(r^2 = \frac{8}{\pi}\) and \(r = \frac{2\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\). Substituting into the total surface area formula gives \(A = 2\pi\left(\frac{8}{\pi}\right) + 2\pi\left(\frac{2\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi}\right)(4) = (16 + 16\sqrt{2\pi})\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: The volume of a sphere is given by \(V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\). Two spheres have volumes of \(V_1 = 500\text{ cm}^3\) and \(V_2 = 108\text{ cm}^3\). What is the sum of their radii, \(r_1 + r_2\)?
qs.s: Solving for each radius gives \(r_1 = \sqrt[3]{\frac{375}{\pi}} = \frac{5\sqrt[3]{3\pi^2}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\) and \(r_2 = \sqrt[3]{\frac{81}{\pi}} = \frac{3\sqrt[3]{3\pi^2}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\). Adding these like radical expressions gives \(r_1 + r_2 = \frac{8\sqrt[3]{3\pi^2}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The area of a circle is \(A = \pi r^2\). A circular washer has an outer circle with area \(A_1 = 75\text{ cm}^2\) and an inner circular opening with area \(A_2 = 12\text{ cm}^2\). What is the width of the washer, given by \(w = r_1 - r_2\)?
qs.s: The radii are \(r_1 = \sqrt{\frac{75}{\pi}} = \frac{5\sqrt{3\pi}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\) and \(r_2 = \sqrt{\frac{12}{\pi}} = \frac{2\sqrt{3\pi}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\). Subtracting the inner radius from the outer radius gives \(w = \frac{3\sqrt{3\pi}}{\pi}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a sphere is \(V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\), and its surface area is \(A = 4\pi r^2\). If the volume of a sphere is \(288\text{ cm}^3\), what is its surface area?
qs.s: From \(288 = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\), we find \(r^3 = \frac{216}{\pi}\), so \(r = \frac{6}{\sqrt[3]{\pi}}\text{ cm}\). Substituting into the surface area formula gives \(A = 4\pi \left(\frac{6}{\sqrt[3]{\pi}}\right)^2 = \frac{144\pi}{\sqrt[3]{\pi^2}} = 144\sqrt[3]{\pi}\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A simple pendulum has a period of \(T\) seconds given by the formula \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}\), where \(L\) is the length of the pendulum in metres and \(g\) is the acceleration due to gravity. On an experimental platform where \(g = 6\text{ m/s}^2\), the pendulum has a period of \(4\pi\text{ seconds}\). What is the length \(L\) of the pendulum?
qs.s: Substitute \(T = 4\pi\) and \(g = 6\) into \(4\pi = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{6}}\). Dividing both sides by \(2\pi\) gives \(2 = \sqrt{\frac{L}{6}}\), and squaring both sides gives \(4 = \frac{L}{6}\), so \(L = 24\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The velocity \(v\) (in metres per second) of a cart with mass \(m\) (in kilograms) and kinetic energy \(E_k\) (in joules) is given by \(v = \sqrt{\frac{2E_k}{m}}\). If the cart has a mass of \(8\text{ kg}\) and travels at a velocity of \(6\text{ m/s}\), what is its kinetic energy \(E_k\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(v = 6\) and \(m = 8\) into \(6 = \sqrt{\frac{2E_k}{8}} = \sqrt{\frac{E_k}{4}}\). Squaring both sides yields \(36 = \frac{E_k}{4}\), so \(E_k = 36 \times 4 = 144\text{ J}\).

qs.q: The speed \(v\) (in metres per second) of an object dropped from a height \(h\) (in metres) is given by \(v = \sqrt{2gh}\), where \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\). If the object strikes the ground with a speed of \(14\text{ m/s}\), from what height \(h\) was it dropped?
qs.s: Substitute \(v = 14\) and \(g = 9.8\) into \(14 = \sqrt{2(9.8)h} = \sqrt{19.6h}\). Squaring both sides yields \(196 = 19.6h\), so \(h = \frac{196}{19.6} = 10\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The speed \(s\) (in metres per second) of a tsunami wave across the ocean is modeled by \(s = \sqrt{gd}\), where \(d\) is the ocean depth in metres and \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\). If a tsunami travels at a speed of \(42\text{ m/s}\), what is the ocean depth \(d\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(s = 42\) and \(g = 9.8\) into \(42 = \sqrt{9.8d}\). Squaring both sides gives \(1764 = 9.8d\), which simplifies to \(d = \frac{1764}{9.8} = 180\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An investigator uses the formula \(v = \sqrt{20d}\) to estimate the speed \(v\) (in metres per second) of a car that left skid marks of length \(d\) (in metres). If the car's estimated speed was \(30\text{ m/s}\), what was the length of the skid marks?
qs.s: Substitute \(v = 30\) into \(30 = \sqrt{20d}\). Squaring both sides yields \(900 = 20d\), so \(d = \frac{900}{20} = 45\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Two pendulums have swing periods given by \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}\), where \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\) and \(L\) is the length in metres. Pendulum \(A\) has a period of \(2\pi\text{ seconds}\) and pendulum \(B\) has a period of \(4\pi\text{ seconds}\). How many metres longer is pendulum \(B\) than pendulum \(A\)?
qs.s: For pendulum \(A\), \(2\pi = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L_A}{9.8}} \implies L_A = 9.8\text{ m}\); for pendulum \(B\), \(4\pi = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L_B}{9.8}} \implies 2 = \sqrt{\frac{L_B}{9.8}} \implies L_B = 39.2\text{ m}\). The difference in length is \(39.2 - 9.8 = 29.4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The side length \(s\) of an equilateral triangle with area \(A\) is given by \(s = \sqrt{\frac{4A}{\sqrt{3}}}\). If an equilateral triangular sign has an area of \(18\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2\), what is its side length \(s\) in simplest radical form?
qs.s: Substitute \(A = 18\sqrt{3}\) into \(s = \sqrt{\frac{4(18\sqrt{3})}{\sqrt{3}}} = \sqrt{72}\). Simplifying \(\sqrt{72} = \sqrt{36 \times 2}\) gives \(s = 6\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The radius \(r\) of the base of a cone is related to its volume \(V\) and height \(h\) by the formula \(r = \sqrt{\frac{3V}{\pi h}}\). A conical storage tank has a volume of \(72\pi\text{ m}^3\) and a base radius of \(3\sqrt{2}\text{ m}\). What is the height \(h\) of the tank?
qs.s: Substitute \(r = 3\sqrt{2}\) and \(V = 72\pi\) to get \(3\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{\frac{3(72\pi)}{\pi h}} = \sqrt{\frac{216}{h}}\). Squaring both sides gives \(18 = \frac{216}{h}\), which yields \(h = \frac{216}{18} = 12\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The speed \(v\) (in \(\text{m/s}\)) of water exiting a drain at the bottom of a tank filled to height \(h\) (in metres) is given by \(v = \sqrt{2gh}\), where \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\). Water is drained from an initial depth of \(15\text{ m}\) until the exit speed decreases to \(7\text{ m/s}\). By how many metres did the water depth decrease?
qs.s: Find the final depth using \(7 = \sqrt{2(9.8)h_2} \implies 49 = 19.6h_2\), so \(h_2 = \frac{49}{19.6} = 2.5\text{ m}\). The depth decreased by \(15 - 2.5 = 12.5\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The speed \(v\) (in \(\text{m/s}\)) of a roller coaster car at the bottom of a hill is given by \(v = \sqrt{v_0^2 + 2gh}\), where \(v_0\) is the initial speed at the top, \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\), and \(h\) is the vertical drop in metres. If the car enters the top of the hill at \(v_0 = 7\text{ m/s}\) and reaches \(v = 21\text{ m/s}\) at the bottom, what is the height \(h\) of the vertical drop?
qs.s: Substitute the given values into \(21 = \sqrt{7^2 + 2(9.8)h} = \sqrt{49 + 19.6h}\). Squaring both sides gives \(441 = 49 + 19.6h\), so \(19.6h = 392\), yielding \(h = 20\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cone is \(V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\), where \(r\) is the radius of the base and \(h\) is the height. If the volume of a cone is \(75\pi\text{ m}^3\) and the height is \(9\text{ m}\), what is the radius of the base?
qs.s: Using \(V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\), we have \(75\pi = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2(9) = 3\pi r^2\). Dividing by \(3\pi\) gives \(r^2 = 25\), so \(r = \sqrt{25} = 5\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The kinetic energy of an object is given by \(E = \frac{1}{2}mv^2\), where \(m\) is the mass in kilograms and \(v\) is the velocity in meters per second. If an object with a mass of \(6\text{ kg}\) has a kinetic energy of \(48\text{ J}\), what is its velocity?
qs.s: Substitute the values into \(E = \frac{1}{2}mv^2\) to get \(48 = \frac{1}{2}(6)v^2 = 3v^2\). Dividing by 3 yields \(v^2 = 16\), so \(v = \sqrt{16} = 4\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: The distance \(d\), in feet, that an object falls in \(t\) seconds is given by \(d = 16t^2\). If a stone falls a distance of \(144\text{ ft}\), how many seconds has it been falling?
qs.s: Substitute \(d = 144\) into \(d = 16t^2\) to get \(144 = 16t^2\), which simplifies to \(t^2 = 9\). Taking the square root gives \(t = \sqrt{9} = 3\text{ seconds}\).

qs.q: The volume of a pyramid is \(V = \frac{1}{3}Bh\), where \(B\) is the area of the base. If the volume of a square-based pyramid is \(128\text{ cm}^3\) and the height is \(6\text{ cm}\), what is the length of one side of the base?
qs.s: Substitute the given values into \(V = \frac{1}{3}s^2h\) to get \(128 = \frac{1}{3}s^2(6) = 2s^2\). Dividing by 2 gives \(s^2 = 64\), so \(s = \sqrt{64} = 8\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The surface area of a cube is given by \(A = 6s^2\), where \(s\) is the length of one edge. If the surface area of a cube is \(150\text{ cm}^2\), what is the length of one edge?
qs.s: Setting up the equation \(150 = 6s^2\) and dividing by 6 gives \(s^2 = 25\). Taking the square root gives \(s = \sqrt{25} = 5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a pyramid is \(V = \frac{1}{3}Bh\), where \(B\) is the area of the base. If the volume of a square-based pyramid is \(50\text{ cm}^3\) and the height is \(9\text{ cm}\), what is the length of one side of the base in simplest radical form?
qs.s: Substitute values into \(V = \frac{1}{3}s^2h\) to get \(50 = \frac{1}{3}s^2(9) = 3s^2\), so \(s^2 = \frac{50}{3}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing the denominator yields \(s = \frac{\sqrt{50}}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{5\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{5\sqrt{6}}{3}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a pyramid is \(V = \frac{1}{3}Bh\), where \(B\) is the area of the base. If the volume of a square-based pyramid is \(360\text{ m}^3\) and the height is \(5\text{ m}\), what is the length of one side of the base in simplest radical form?
qs.s: Using \(V = \frac{1}{3}s^2h\), we obtain \(360 = \frac{1}{3}s^2(5)\), which gives \(s^2 = \frac{360 \times 3}{5} = 216\). Taking the square root and simplifying gives \(s = \sqrt{216} = 6\sqrt{6}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The volume of a pyramid is \(V = \frac{1}{3}Bh\), where \(B\) is the area of the base. If the volume of a square-based pyramid is \(72\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^3\) and its height is \(2\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\), what is the length of one side of the base in simplest radical form?
qs.s: Substitute the given values into \(72\sqrt{3} = \frac{1}{3}s^2(2\sqrt{3}) = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}s^2\). Multiplying by \(\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3}}\) gives \(s^2 = 108\), so \(s = \sqrt{108} = 6\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a pyramid is \(V = \frac{1}{3}Bh\), where \(B\) is the area of the base. A tent in the shape of a square-based pyramid has a volume of \(144\text{ m}^3\) and a height of \(8\text{ m}\). What is the perimeter of the base of the tent in simplest radical form?
qs.s: Using \(144 = \frac{1}{3}s^2(8)\), we find \(s^2 = \frac{144 \times 3}{8} = 54\), which gives side length \(s = \sqrt{54} = 3\sqrt{6}\text{ m}\). The perimeter is \(P = 4s = 4(3\sqrt{6}) = 12\sqrt{6}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The volume of a pyramid is \(V = \frac{1}{3}Bh\), where \(B\) is the area of the base. A pyramid has a height of \(9\text{ cm}\) and a rectangular base whose length is twice its width. If the volume of the pyramid is \(288\text{ cm}^3\), what is the width of the base in simplest radical form?
qs.s: Let \(w\) be the width, so the base area is \(B = w(2w) = 2w^2\). Substituting into \(V = \frac{1}{3}Bh\) gives \(288 = \frac{1}{3}(2w^2)(9) = 6w^2\), so \(w^2 = 48\) and \(w = \sqrt{48} = 4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The distance formula of a falling object is given by \(d = \frac{1}{2}gt^2\). On the Moon, where \(g = 1.6\text{ m/s}^2\), what time does it take for an object to fall \(36\text{ m}\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(d = 36\) and \(g = 1.6\) into \(d = \frac{1}{2}gt^2\) to get \(36 = 0.8t^2\), which yields \(t^2 = 45\). Taking the principal square root gives \(t = \sqrt{45} = 3\sqrt{5}\text{ s}\).

qs.q: The velocity of a falling object just before impact is given by the formula \(v = \sqrt{2gd}\). What is the velocity of an object that falls from a height of \(15\text{ m}\)? (\(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\))
qs.s: Substitute \(g = 9.8\) and \(d = 15\) into \(v = \sqrt{2gd}\) to obtain \(v = \sqrt{2(9.8)(15)} = \sqrt{294}\). Simplifying the radical gives \(v = \sqrt{49 \cdot 6} = 7\sqrt{6}\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: The area of an equilateral triangle is given by the formula \(A = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2\), where \(s\) is the side length. What is the side length of an equilateral triangle with an area of \(18\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(A = 18\sqrt{3}\) into \(A = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2\) to obtain \(18\sqrt{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2\), so \(s^2 = 72\). Taking the principal square root gives \(s = \sqrt{72} = 6\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The distance formula of a falling object is given by \(d = \frac{1}{2}gt^2\). What time does it take for an object to fall \(98\text{ m}\)? (\(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\))
qs.s: Substitute \(d = 98\) and \(g = 9.8\) into \(d = \frac{1}{2}gt^2\) to get \(98 = 4.9t^2\), which simplifies to \(t^2 = 20\). Taking the principal square root gives \(t = \sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}\text{ s}\).

qs.q: The kinetic energy of an object in motion is given by the formula \(E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2\). What is the velocity of an object with a mass of \(10\text{ kg}\) and a kinetic energy of \(140\text{ J}\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(E_k = 140\) and \(m = 10\) into \(E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2\) to get \(140 = 5v^2\), which gives \(v^2 = 28\). Taking the principal square root yields \(v = \sqrt{28} = 2\sqrt{7}\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: The orbital period \(T\) (in Earth years) of a minor planet orbiting the Sun is given by Kepler's formula \(T = \sqrt{a^3}\), where \(a\) is the average distance to the Sun in astronomical units (AU). What is the orbital period of a minor planet with an average distance of \(a = 12\text{ AU}\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(a = 12\) into the formula to get \(T = \sqrt{12^3} = \sqrt{1728}\). Simplifying the radical gives \(T = \sqrt{144 \cdot 12} = 12\sqrt{12} = 12(2\sqrt{3}) = 24\sqrt{3}\text{ years}\).

qs.q: The distance an object falls from rest is given by \(d = \frac{1}{2}gt^2\), where \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\). How much additional time does it take for an object to fall from a distance of \(39.2\text{ m}\) to a total distance of \(88.2\text{ m}\)?
qs.s: Find each fall time using \(t = \sqrt{2d/g}\): \(t_1 = \sqrt{39.2/4.9} = \sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2}\text{ s}\) and \(t_2 = \sqrt{88.2/4.9} = \sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}\text{ s}\). The additional time is the difference \(3\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{2}\text{ s}\).

qs.q: The final velocity \(v\) of an object thrown downward with initial velocity \(v_0\) is given by \(v = \sqrt{v_0^2 + 2gd}\), where \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\) and \(d\) is the distance fallen. What is the final velocity of an object thrown downward at \(v_0 = 7\text{ m/s}\) after it falls \(10\text{ m}\)?
qs.s: Substitute the given values into the formula: \(v = \sqrt{7^2 + 2(9.8)(10)} = \sqrt{49 + 196} = \sqrt{245}\). Simplifying the radical gives \(v = \sqrt{49 \cdot 5} = 7\sqrt{5}\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: The length of the space diagonal of a rectangular prism is given by \(d = \sqrt{l^2 + w^2 + h^2}\). A box has a length of \(8\text{ cm}\), a width of \(6\text{ cm}\), and a space diagonal of \(12\text{ cm}\). What is the height of the box in simplest radical form?
qs.s: Substitute the known dimensions into \(d^2 = l^2 + w^2 + h^2\) to get \(12^2 = 8^2 + 6^2 + h^2\), which simplifies to \(144 = 100 + h^2\), so \(h^2 = 44\). Taking the principal square root gives \(h = \sqrt{44} = 2\sqrt{11}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The power \(P\) (in kilowatts) generated by a prototype wind turbine is modeled by \(P = \frac{3}{7}v^2\), where \(v\) is the wind speed in meters per second. If the turbine produces 14 kilowatts of power, what is the wind speed in meters per second?
qs.s: Substitute \(P = 14\) to obtain \(v^2 = 14 \cdot \frac{7}{3} = \frac{98}{3}\). Simplifying the radical and rationalizing gives \(v = \frac{\sqrt{49\cdot 2}}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{7\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{3}}{3} = \frac{7\sqrt{6}}{3}\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: The kinetic energy \(E\) (in joules) of a model car is given by the formula \(E = \frac{3}{5}v^2\), where \(v\) is the speed in meters per second. If the car has a kinetic energy of 10 joules, what is its speed in meters per second?
qs.s: Substitute \(E = 10\) into \(10 = \frac{3}{5}v^2\) to find \(v^2 = \frac{50}{3}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing the denominator yields \(v = \frac{\sqrt{50}}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{5\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{3}}{3} = \frac{5\sqrt{6}}{3}\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: The distance \(d\) (in feet) required for a vehicle to stop on a gravel road is modeled by \(d = \frac{3}{8}s^2\), where \(s\) is the speed in miles per hour. If a vehicle takes 20 feet to stop, what was its speed in miles per hour?
qs.s: Setting \(20 = \frac{3}{8}s^2\) gives \(s^2 = \frac{160}{3}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing yields \(s = \frac{\sqrt{160}}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{4\sqrt{10}\cdot\sqrt{3}}{3} = \frac{4\sqrt{30}}{3}\text{ mph}\).

qs.q: In an electronic circuit, the power dissipation \(P\) (in watts) across a resistor is given by \(P = \frac{2}{5}I^2\), where \(I\) is the current in amperes. If the resistor dissipates 9 watts of power, what is the current in amperes?
qs.s: Substitute \(P = 9\) into \(9 = \frac{2}{5}I^2\) to get \(I^2 = \frac{45}{2}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing gives \(I = \frac{\sqrt{9\cdot 5}}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{3\sqrt{5}\cdot\sqrt{2}}{2} = \frac{3\sqrt{10}}{2}\text{ A}\).

qs.q: The maximum height \(h\) (in feet) reached by water spraying from a fountain nozzle is given by \(h = \frac{5}{7}v^2\), where \(v\) is the spray velocity in feet per second. If the water reaches a height of 14 feet, what is the spray velocity in feet per second?
qs.s: Substitute \(h = 14\) into the formula to get \(v^2 = 14 \cdot \frac{7}{5} = \frac{98}{5}\). Simplifying and rationalizing gives \(v = \frac{\sqrt{49\cdot 2}}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{7\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{5}}{5} = \frac{7\sqrt{10}}{5}\text{ ft/s}\).

qs.q: The mass \(M\) (in kilograms) of a solid metal cube is related to its edge length \(x\) (in decimeters) by the formula \(M = \frac{5}{8}x^3\). If a metal cube has a mass of 2 kilograms, find its edge length in decimeters.
qs.s: Solve \(2 = \frac{5}{8}x^3\) to get \(x^3 = \frac{16}{5}\), so \(x = \frac{\sqrt[3]{16}}{\sqrt[3]{5}} = \frac{2\sqrt[3]{2}}{\sqrt[3]{5}}\). Rationalizing the cube root denominator by multiplying by \(\sqrt[3]{25}\) gives \(\frac{2\sqrt[3]{50}}{5}\text{ dm}\).

qs.q: The distance \(d\) (in miles) to the ocean horizon from an elevation \(h\) (in feet) is given by \(h = \frac{2}{3}d^2\). A passenger on a cruise ship walks from the promenade deck at an elevation of 25 feet to the upper sun deck at an elevation of 49 feet. How much farther can the passenger see to the horizon from the upper sun deck?
qs.s: Solve for each horizon distance: \(d_1 = \sqrt{\frac{75}{2}} = \frac{5\sqrt{6}}{2}\text{ miles}\) and \(d_2 = \sqrt{\frac{147}{2}} = \frac{7\sqrt{6}}{2}\text{ miles}\). Subtracting gives \(d_2 - d_1 = \frac{7\sqrt{6} - 5\sqrt{6}}{2} = \sqrt{6}\text{ miles}\).

qs.q: Two ships at sea are sailing toward each other. The lookout on ship A is at an elevation of 15 feet above the water, and the lookout on ship B is at an elevation of 135 feet above the water. Using the horizon formula \(h = \frac{2}{3}d^2\), where \(h\) is elevation in feet and \(d\) is distance to the horizon in miles, find the maximum distance between the two ships at which the lookouts can first see each other.
qs.s: The maximum sighting distance between the ships is \(d_A + d_B\). Solve to find \(d_A = \sqrt{\frac{45}{2}} = \frac{3\sqrt{10}}{2}\) and \(d_B = \sqrt{\frac{405}{2}} = \frac{9\sqrt{10}}{2}\), then add them to get \(\frac{12\sqrt{10}}{2} = 6\sqrt{10}\text{ miles}\).

qs.q: The length \(l\) of a rectangle with area \(A\) and width \(w\) is given by the formula \(l = \frac{A}{w}\). If a rectangular solar panel has an area of 22 square meters and a width of \(2\sqrt{3} - 1\) meters, find its length in meters.
qs.s: Set up \(l = \frac{22}{2\sqrt{3} - 1}\) and multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(2\sqrt{3} + 1\). The denominator becomes \((2\sqrt{3})^2 - 1^2 = 12 - 1 = 11\), and dividing 22 by 11 gives \(2(2\sqrt{3} + 1) = (4\sqrt{3} + 2)\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The height \(h\) (in meters) of a launch ramp is related to the exit velocity \(v\) (in meters per second) of a stunt car by the formula \(h = \frac{3}{7}v^2 + 4\). If the ramp height is 24 meters, what is the exit velocity in meters per second?
qs.s: Subtract 4 from both sides to get \(\frac{3}{7}v^2 = 20\), which yields \(v^2 = \frac{140}{3}\). Taking the square root and rationalizing gives \(v = \frac{\sqrt{4\cdot 35}}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{2\sqrt{35}\cdot\sqrt{3}}{3} = \frac{2\sqrt{105}}{3}\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: Two hiking trails branch off at a 90° angle from a ranger station. One group of hikers walks along the first trail to an observation deck 80 m from the station. A second group walks along the other trail to a campsite 50 m from the station. What is the direct straight-line distance between the observation deck and the campsite?
qs.s: The trails form the legs of a right triangle with lengths 80 m and 50 m, so the direct distance is \(\sqrt{80^2 + 50^2} = \sqrt{6400 + 2500} = \sqrt{8900} = 10\sqrt{89}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A soccer field has two perpendicular boundary lines meeting at a corner flag: the goal line and the sideline. A coach stands along the extended goal line, 70 m from the corner flag. A referee stands on the sideline, 40 m from the same corner flag. What is the straight-line distance between the coach and the referee?
qs.s: The goal line and sideline form a right angle, giving a distance of \(\sqrt{70^2 + 40^2} = \sqrt{4900 + 1600} = \sqrt{6500} = 10\sqrt{65}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular warehouse courtyard has adjacent walls that meet at a 90° corner. A security camera is mounted along one wall line, 110 ft from the corner. A motion sensor is mounted along the perpendicular wall line, 40 ft from the corner. What is the direct straight-line distance between the camera and the sensor?
qs.s: The perpendicular wall lines give legs of lengths 110 ft and 40 ft, so the direct distance is \(\sqrt{110^2 + 40^2} = \sqrt{12100 + 1600} = \sqrt{13700} = 10\sqrt{137}\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: Two survey teams depart from the same base station. Team A travels directly to a site 120 m east and 40 m north of the station. Team B travels directly to a site 30 m west and 90 m north of the station. How much farther did Team A travel from the base station than Team B?
qs.s: Team A traveled \(\sqrt{120^2 + 40^2} = \sqrt{16000} = 40\sqrt{10}\text{ m}\) and Team B traveled \(\sqrt{(-30)^2 + 90^2} = \sqrt{9000} = 30\sqrt{10}\text{ m}\), so the difference is \(40\sqrt{10} - 30\sqrt{10} = 10\sqrt{10}\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular plaza measures 150 m by 90 m. A pedestrian wants to travel from one corner of the plaza to the diagonally opposite corner. How much shorter is the direct diagonal walk across the plaza than walking along the two outer edges?
qs.s: Walking along the edges takes \(150 + 90 = 240\text{ m}\), while the diagonal is \(\sqrt{150^2 + 90^2} = \sqrt{30600} = 30\sqrt{34}\text{ m}\), so the distance saved is \((240 - 30\sqrt{34})\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A baseball diamond is a square with sides of 90 ft. A ball is caught on the right field foul line 250 ft from home plate. What distance must the fielder throw the ball to reach second base?
qs.s: Second base is 90 ft perpendicularly away from the right field line and 90 ft from home plate along it, so the legs to the fielder are \(250 - 90 = 160\text{ ft}\) and \(90\text{ ft}\). The throw distance is \(\sqrt{160^2 + 90^2} = \sqrt{25600 + 8100} = \sqrt{33700} = 10\sqrt{337}\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{5x + 1}\)
qs.s: Squaring a square root eliminates the radical: \((\sqrt{5x + 1})^2 = 5x + 1\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{x - 4}\)
qs.s: Squaring a square root eliminates the radical: \((\sqrt{x - 4})^2 = x - 4\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{2x + 3}\)
qs.s: Squaring a square root eliminates the radical: \((\sqrt{2x + 3})^2 = 2x + 3\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{3x - 7}\)
qs.s: Squaring a square root eliminates the radical: \((\sqrt{3x - 7})^2 = 3x - 7\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{x + 5}\)
qs.s: Squaring a square root eliminates the radical: \((\sqrt{x + 5})^2 = x + 5\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(2\sqrt{x + 3} - 1\)
Square the expression: \(2\sqrt{x} - 3\)
Square the expression: \(\sqrt{x + 5} + 2\)
qs.s: Expand as a binomial square: \((\sqrt{x + 5} + 2)^2 = (\sqrt{x + 5})^2 + 2(2)\sqrt{x + 5} + 2^2 = (x + 5) + 4\sqrt{x + 5} + 4 = x + 9 + 4\sqrt{x + 5}\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{x - 2} - 3\)
qs.s: Expand as a binomial square: \((\sqrt{x - 2} - 3)^2 = (\sqrt{x - 2})^2 - 2(3)\sqrt{x - 2} + 3^2 = (x - 2) - 6\sqrt{x - 2} + 9 = x + 7 - 6\sqrt{x - 2}\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{x} + 3\)
Square the expression: \(\sqrt{m} - 1\)
qs.s: Expanding the square gives \((\sqrt{m} - 1)^2 = (\sqrt{m})^2 - 2(\sqrt{m})(1) + 1^2 = m - 2\sqrt{m} + 1\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{a} + 5\)
qs.s: Expanding the square gives \((\sqrt{a} + 5)^2 = (\sqrt{a})^2 + 2(\sqrt{a})(5) + 5^2 = a + 10\sqrt{a} + 25\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{x} + 7\)
qs.s: Expanding the square gives \((\sqrt{x} + 7)^2 = (\sqrt{x})^2 + 2(\sqrt{x})(7) + 7^2 = x + 14\sqrt{x} + 49\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{y} - 4\)
Square the expression: \(\sqrt{x + 4} + 5\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \((\sqrt{x + 4})^2 + 2(5)\sqrt{x + 4} + 5^2 = x + 4 + 10\sqrt{x + 4} + 25 = x + 10\sqrt{x + 4} + 29\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{2x + 1} + 3\)
Square the expression: \(3\sqrt{x} + 5\)
Square the expression: \(\sqrt{x - 6} - 3\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \((\sqrt{x - 6})^2 - 2(3)\sqrt{x - 6} + (-3)^2 = x - 6 - 6\sqrt{x - 6} + 9 = x - 6\sqrt{x - 6} + 3\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(2\sqrt{x + 2} - 3\)
Square the expression: \(\sqrt{5x - 3}\)
qs.s: Squaring eliminates the radical sign, leaving the radicand: \((\sqrt{5x - 3})^2 = 5x - 3\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{6x - 5}\)
qs.s: Applying an exponent of 2 cancels the square root: \((\sqrt{6x - 5})^2 = 6x - 5\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{2x + 7}\)
qs.s: Squaring a square root cancels the radical: \((\sqrt{2x + 7})^2 = 2x + 7\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{7x + 4}\)
qs.s: Squaring the square root leaves only the radicand: \((\sqrt{7x + 4})^2 = 7x + 4\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{4x + 1}\)
qs.s: Squaring the square root yields the expression under the radical: \((\sqrt{4x + 1})^2 = 4x + 1\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(-4\sqrt{2x + 5}\)
qs.s: Square the negative coefficient and the radical: \((-4\sqrt{2x + 5})^2 = (-4)^2 \cdot (\sqrt{2x + 5})^2 = 16(2x + 5) = 32x + 80\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{x + 6} + 2\)
Square the expression: \(2\sqrt{3x + 4}\)
qs.s: Square both the coefficient and the radical: \((2\sqrt{3x + 4})^2 = 2^2 \cdot (\sqrt{3x + 4})^2 = 4(3x + 4) = 12x + 16\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(3\sqrt{5x - 2}\)
qs.s: Square the coefficient and the square root, then distribute: \((3\sqrt{5x - 2})^2 = 3^2 \cdot (\sqrt{5x - 2})^2 = 9(5x - 2) = 45x - 18\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{6a} + 7\)
Square the expression: \(\sqrt{5x} + 4\)
Square the expression: \(\sqrt{10x} - 2\)
Square the expression: \(\sqrt{7y} - 6\)
Square the expression: \(2\sqrt{3x} + \sqrt{2y}\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \((2\sqrt{3x})^2 + 2(2\sqrt{3x})(\sqrt{2y}) + (\sqrt{2y})^2 = 4(3x) + 4\sqrt{6xy} + 2y = 12x + 4\sqrt{6xy} + 2y\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(2\sqrt{x - 3} + 5\)
Square the expression: \(3\sqrt{2x} - 4\)
Square the expression: \(2x - \sqrt{5x}\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \((2x)^2 - 2(2x)(\sqrt{5x}) + (\sqrt{5x})^2 = 4x^2 - 4x\sqrt{5x} + 5x\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{3x + 5} - 4\)
Square the expression: \(\sqrt{2x + 5}\)
qs.s: Squaring the square root cancels the radical, yielding \((\sqrt{2x + 5})^2 = 2x + 5\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{8 - 9x}\)
qs.s: Squaring the square root cancels the radical, yielding \((\sqrt{8 - 9x})^2 = 8 - 9x\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{10x + 3}\)
qs.s: Squaring the square root cancels the radical, yielding \((\sqrt{10x + 3})^2 = 10x + 3\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{7 - 3x}\)
qs.s: Squaring the square root cancels the radical, yielding \((\sqrt{7 - 3x})^2 = 7 - 3x\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(3\sqrt{7 - 2x}\)
qs.s: Square both the coefficient and the radical: \((3\sqrt{7 - 2x})^2 = 3^2(\sqrt{7 - 2x})^2 = 9(7 - 2x) = 63 - 18x\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{2x - 1} - 4\)
Square the expression: \(5 - \sqrt{3x + 2}\)
Square the expression: \(2\sqrt{5x + 3}\)
qs.s: Square both the coefficient and the radical: \((2\sqrt{5x + 3})^2 = 2^2(\sqrt{5x + 3})^2 = 4(5x + 3) = 20x + 12\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(2 - 3\sqrt{x}\)
Square the expression: \(5 - 2\sqrt{x}\)
Square the expression: \(1 - 6\sqrt{x}\)
Square the expression: \(3 + 4\sqrt{x}\)
Square the expression: \(1 + 5\sqrt{x}\)
Square the expression: \(4 + 3\sqrt{x-2}\)
Square the expression: \(3 - 2\sqrt{5x-1}\)
Square the expression: \(\sqrt{x+4} - 6\)
Square the expression: \(2\sqrt{3x+1} - 5\)
Square the expression: \(4\sqrt{x} - 3\sqrt{y}\)
qs.s: Expand using \((a-b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2\): \((4\sqrt{x})^2 - 2(4\sqrt{x})(3\sqrt{y}) + (3\sqrt{y})^2 = 16x - 24\sqrt{xy} + 9y\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(x + 6\)
Square the expression: \(x - 2\)
Square the expression: \(x + 4\)
Square the expression: \(x - 5\)
Square the expression: \(x - 7\)
Square the expression: \(\sqrt{x} - 5\) (assume \(x > 0\))
qs.s: Expanding \((\sqrt{x} - 5)^2\) gives \((\sqrt{x})^2 - 2(5)\sqrt{x} + 5^2 = x - 10\sqrt{x} + 25\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(2 + \sqrt{3x - 1}\) (assume \(x > 1\))
Square the expression: \(2x - 5\)
Square the expression: \(3x + 4\)
Square the expression: \(\sqrt{x + 5} - 3\) (assume \(x > 0\))
Square the expression: \(\sqrt{b} - \sqrt{10}\)
qs.s: Expanding \((\sqrt{b} - \sqrt{10})^2\) gives \((\sqrt{b})^2 - 2(\sqrt{b})(\sqrt{10}) + (\sqrt{10})^2 = b - 2\sqrt{10b} + 10\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{7}\)
qs.s: Expanding \((\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{7})^2\) gives \((\sqrt{a})^2 - 2(\sqrt{a})(\sqrt{7}) + (\sqrt{7})^2 = a - 2\sqrt{7a} + 7\).

qs.q: Square the expression: \(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{5}\)
