Divide and simplify. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2x^2 + 8x}{3x^2 - 9x} \div \frac{2x^2 + 7x - 4}{x^2 - 5x + 6}\)
qs.s: Factor each expression and multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{2x(x+4)}{3x(x-3)} \cdot \frac{(x-3)(x-2)}{(2x-1)(x+4)}\). Canceling the common factors \(x\), \(x+4\), and \(x-3\) leaves \(\frac{2(x-2)}{3(2x-1)}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{3x^2 - 15x}{6x^2 - 4x} \div \frac{2x^2 - 9x - 5}{3x^2 + x - 2}\)
qs.s: Factor each numerator and denominator to get \(\frac{3x(x-5)}{2x(3x-2)} \cdot \frac{(3x-2)(x+1)}{(x-5)(2x+1)}\). Canceling the common factors \(x\), \(x-5\), and \(3x-2\) leaves \(\frac{3(x+1)}{2(2x+1)}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{5x^2 + 10x}{2x^2 - 3x} \div \frac{x^2 - 4x - 12}{2x^2 - 5x + 3}\)
qs.s: Factor all polynomials to obtain \(\frac{5x(x+2)}{x(2x-3)} \cdot \frac{(2x-3)(x-1)}{(x-6)(x+2)}\). Canceling \(x\), \(x+2\), and \(2x-3\) yields \(\frac{5(x-1)}{x-6}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2x^2 - 6x}{4x^2 + 8x} \div \frac{x^2 - 2x - 3}{2x^2 + 7x + 6}\)
qs.s: Factor each numerator and denominator to get \(\frac{2x(x-3)}{4x(x+2)} \cdot \frac{(2x+3)(x+2)}{(x-3)(x+1)}\). Canceling the common factors \(x\), \(2\), \(x-3\), and \(x+2\) gives \(\frac{2x+3}{2(x+1)}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{4x^2 - 2x}{3x^2 + 6x} \div \frac{2x^2 + 5x - 3}{x^2 - x - 6}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the division as multiplication by the reciprocal: \(\frac{2x(2x-1)}{3x(x+2)} \cdot \frac{(x-3)(x+2)}{(2x-1)(x+3)}\). Canceling common factors \(x\), \(2x-1\), and \(x+2\) leaves \(\frac{2(x-3)}{3(x+3)}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify completely. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{4x^2 - 9}{2x^2 - 5x - 12} \div \frac{9 - 6x}{x^2 - 16}\)
qs.s: Factor the expressions to obtain \(\frac{(2x-3)(2x+3)}{(2x+3)(x-4)} \cdot \frac{(x-4)(x+4)}{-3(2x-3)}\). Since \(\frac{2x-3}{9-6x} = -\frac{1}{3}\), canceling common factors \((2x+3)\), \((x-4)\), and \((2x-3)\) leaves \(-\frac{x+4}{3}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify completely. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2x^2 + xy - y^2}{2x^2 + 7xy + 3y^2} \div \frac{2x^2 - 3xy + y^2}{x^2 + 2xy - 3y^2}\)
qs.s: Factor each two-variable quadratic: \(\frac{(2x-y)(x+y)}{(2x+y)(x+3y)} \cdot \frac{(x+3y)(x-y)}{(2x-y)(x-y)}\). Canceling \((2x-y)\), \((x+3y)\), and \((x-y)\) simplifies the expression to \(\frac{x+y}{2x+y}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify completely. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{x^3 - 2x^2 - 9x + 18}{2x^2 + 5x - 3} \div \frac{x^2 - 4}{2x^2 + 3x - 2}\)
qs.s: Factor the cubic by grouping to get \(x^2(x-2) - 9(x-2) = (x-3)(x+3)(x-2)\), then rewrite the division as \(\frac{(x-3)(x+3)(x-2)}{(2x-1)(x+3)} \cdot \frac{(2x-1)(x+2)}{(x-2)(x+2)}\). Canceling all matching factors leaves \(x-3\).

qs.q:
Perform the operations and simplify completely. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{x^2 - 9}{x^2 - x - 2} \div \frac{2x^2 + 5x - 3}{x^2 - 4} \cdot \frac{2x - 1}{x - 3}\)
qs.s: Evaluate left to right by multiplying by the reciprocal of the divisor: \(\frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{(x-2)(x+1)} \cdot \frac{(x-2)(x+2)}{(2x-1)(x+3)} \cdot \frac{2x-1}{x-3}\). Canceling common factors \((x-3)\), \((x+3)\), \((x-2)\), and \((2x-1)\) leaves \(\frac{x+2}{x+1}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify completely. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{6x^3 - 24x}{2x^2 + 9x + 10} \div \frac{8 - 4x}{4x^2 + 20x + 25}\)
qs.s: Factor each term: \(\frac{6x(x-2)(x+2)}{(2x+5)(x+2)} \cdot \frac{(2x+5)^2}{-4(x-2)}\). Canceling \((x+2)\), \((x-2)\), and one factor of \((2x+5)\), and simplifying \(\frac{6x}{-4}\) to \(-\frac{3x}{2}\), gives \(-\frac{3x(2x+5)}{2}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x^2+2x-y^2-2y}{2x^2-2y^2} \div \frac{3x+3y+6}{5x^2y+5xy^2}\)
qs.s: Factor each numerator and denominator to get \(\frac{(x-y)(x+y+2)}{2(x-y)(x+y)} \cdot \frac{5xy(x+y)}{3(x+y+2)}\). Cancelling the common factors \((x-y)\), \((x+y)\), and \((x+y+2)\) yields \(\frac{5xy}{6}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{a^2-a-b^2+b}{4a^2-4b^2} \div \frac{7a+7b-7}{2a^2b+2ab^2}\)
qs.s: Factor each expression to obtain \(\frac{(a-b)(a+b-1)}{4(a-b)(a+b)} \cdot \frac{2ab(a+b)}{7(a+b-1)}\). Cancelling \((a-b)\), \((a+b)\), and \((a+b-1)\) leaves \(\frac{2ab}{28} = \frac{ab}{14}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x^2+3x-y^2-3y}{5x^2-5y^2} \div \frac{2x+2y+6}{3x^2y+3xy^2}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the division as multiplication by the reciprocal: \(\frac{(x-y)(x+y+3)}{5(x-y)(x+y)} \cdot \frac{3xy(x+y)}{2(x+y+3)}\). Cancelling the common binomial factors simplifies the product to \(\frac{3xy}{10}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{m^2+4m-n^2-4n}{6m^2-6n^2} \div \frac{5m+5n+20}{4m^2n+4mn^2}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerators and denominators to get \(\frac{(m-n)(m+n+4)}{6(m-n)(m+n)} \cdot \frac{4mn(m+n)}{5(m+n+4)}\). Cancelling common factors \((m-n)\), \((m+n)\), and \((m+n+4)\) leaves \(\frac{4mn}{30} = \frac{2mn}{15}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{u^2+5u-v^2-5v}{7u^2-7v^2} \div \frac{3u+3v+15}{2u^2v+2uv^2}\)
qs.s: Factoring the expressions yields \(\frac{(u-v)(u+v+5)}{7(u-v)(u+v)} \cdot \frac{2uv(u+v)}{3(u+v+5)}\). Cancelling \((u-v)\), \((u+v)\), and \((u+v+5)\) gives \(\frac{2uv}{21}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x^3+2x^2-9x-18}{x^3-3x^2-4x+12} \div \frac{x^2+5x+6}{x^2-4x+4}\)
qs.s: Factor both cubics by grouping and the quadratics to obtain \(\frac{(x-3)(x+3)(x+2)}{(x-2)(x+2)(x-3)} \cdot \frac{(x-2)^2}{(x+2)(x+3)}\). Cancelling all common factors leaves \(\frac{x-2}{x+2}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{2x^3+x^2-2xy^2-y^2}{4x^2-1} \div \frac{x^2-y^2}{6x^2-3x}\)
qs.s: Factor the first numerator by grouping to get \((x^2-y^2)(2x+1)\), factor the denominators and multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{(x^2-y^2)(2x+1)}{(2x-1)(2x+1)} \cdot \frac{3x(2x-1)}{x^2-y^2}\). Cancelling all common factors leaves \(3x\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{a^2-b^2+3a-3b}{2b-2a} \div \frac{a^2+2ab+b^2+3a+3b}{4a^2b+4ab^2}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerators and denominators, noting that \(2b-2a = -2(a-b)\), to obtain \(\frac{(a-b)(a+b+3)}{-2(a-b)} \cdot \frac{4ab(a+b)}{(a+b)(a+b+3)}\). Cancelling the common factors leaves \(\frac{4ab}{-2} = -2ab\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{6x^2-7x-3}{2x^2-7x+6} \div \frac{9x^2-1}{x^2-4}\)
qs.s: Factor each quadratic expression completely: \(\frac{(2x-3)(3x+1)}{(2x-3)(x-2)} \cdot \frac{(x-2)(x+2)}{(3x-1)(3x+1)}\). Cancelling \((2x-3)\), \((x-2)\), and \((3x+1)\) leaves \(\frac{x+2}{3x-1}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x^3+2x^2-xy^2-2y^2}{3x^2-12} \div \frac{x^2-y^2+5x-5y}{6x-12}\)
qs.s: Factor all parts to obtain \(\frac{(x-y)(x+y)(x+2)}{3(x-2)(x+2)} \cdot \frac{6(x-2)}{(x-y)(x+y+5)}\). Cancelling \((x-y)\), \((x-2)\), and \((x+2)\) and reducing \(\frac{6}{3} = 2\) gives \(\frac{2(x+y)}{x+y+5}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x+4}{x-2} \div \left( \frac{5x}{x^2-2x} \cdot \frac{x^2+8x+16}{x^2+2x-8} \right)\)
qs.s: Inside the parentheses, factoring gives \(\frac{5x}{x(x-2)} \cdot \frac{(x+4)^2}{(x+4)(x-2)} = \frac{5(x+4)}{(x-2)^2}\). Multiplying \(\frac{x+4}{x-2}\) by the reciprocal yields \(\frac{x+4}{x-2} \cdot \frac{(x-2)^2}{5(x+4)} = \frac{x-2}{5}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x-1}{x+3} \div \left( \frac{3x}{x^2+3x} \cdot \frac{x^2-1}{x^2+4x+3} \right)\)
qs.s: Factoring inside the parentheses yields \(\frac{3x}{x(x+3)} \cdot \frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{(x+1)(x+3)} = \frac{3(x-1)}{(x+3)^2}\). Multiplying \(\frac{x-1}{x+3}\) by the reciprocal gives \(\frac{x-1}{x+3} \cdot \frac{(x+3)^2}{3(x-1)} = \frac{x+3}{3}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x+2}{x-4} \div \left( \frac{x^2-4x}{x^2-16} \cdot \frac{x^2+5x+6}{x^2-x-12} \right)\)
qs.s: Inside the parentheses, factoring gives \(\frac{x(x-4)}{(x-4)(x+4)} \cdot \frac{(x+2)(x+3)}{(x-4)(x+3)} = \frac{x(x+2)}{(x+4)(x-4)}\). Dividing by this product gives \(\frac{x+2}{x-4} \cdot \frac{(x+4)(x-4)}{x(x+2)} = \frac{x+4}{x}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x-3}{x-5} \div \left( \frac{2x}{x^2-5x} \cdot \frac{x^2-9}{x^2-2x-15} \right)\)
qs.s: Factor the expressions inside the parentheses to get \(\frac{2x}{x(x-5)} \cdot \frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{(x-5)(x+3)} = \frac{2(x-3)}{(x-5)^2}\). Multiplying \(\frac{x-3}{x-5}\) by the reciprocal of this product yields \(\frac{x-3}{x-5} \cdot \frac{(x-5)^2}{2(x-3)} = \frac{x-5}{2}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x+3}{x+6} \div \left( \frac{6x}{x^2+6x} \cdot \frac{x^2+6x+9}{x^2+9x+18} \right)\)
qs.s: Factoring the expressions inside the parentheses gives \(\frac{6x}{x(x+6)} \cdot \frac{(x+3)^2}{(x+3)(x+6)} = \frac{6(x+3)}{(x+6)^2}\). Dividing \(\frac{x+3}{x+6}\) by this product means multiplying by its reciprocal, giving \(\frac{x+3}{x+6} \cdot \frac{(x+6)^2}{6(x+3)} = \frac{x+6}{6}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{3x^2-11x+6}{2x^2-7x-4} \div \left( \frac{3x^2+4x-4}{4x^2-1} \cdot \frac{2x^2+9x-5}{x^2+7x+10} \right)\)
qs.s: Factoring the product inside gives \(\frac{(3x-2)(x+2)}{(2x-1)(2x+1)} \cdot \frac{(2x-1)(x+5)}{(x+2)(x+5)} = \frac{3x-2}{2x+1}\). Dividing \(\frac{(3x-2)(x-3)}{(2x+1)(x-4)}\) by \(\frac{3x-2}{2x+1}\) results in \(\frac{(3x-2)(x-3)}{(2x+1)(x-4)} \cdot \frac{2x+1}{3x-2} = \frac{x-3}{x-4}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{2x+y}{x+2y} \div \left( \frac{4x^2-y^2}{x^2+3xy+2y^2} \cdot \frac{x^2-y^2}{2x^2+xy-y^2} \right)\)
qs.s: Factoring inside the parentheses yields \(\frac{(2x-y)(2x+y)}{(x+y)(x+2y)} \cdot \frac{(x-y)(x+y)}{(2x-y)(x+y)} = \frac{(2x+y)(x-y)}{(x+2y)(x+y)}\). Multiplying \(\frac{2x+y}{x+2y}\) by the reciprocal gives \(\frac{2x+y}{x+2y} \cdot \frac{(x+2y)(x+y)}{(2x+y)(x-y)} = \frac{x+y}{x-y}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x^2-9}{2x^2+7x+3} \div \left( \frac{x^2-3x}{2x^2-x-1} \cdot \frac{x^2-1}{x^2+4x+3} \right)\)
qs.s: Factoring gives \(\frac{x-3}{2x+1}\) for the first fraction, and the product inside is \(\frac{x(x-3)}{(2x+1)(x-1)} \cdot \frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{(x+1)(x+3)} = \frac{x(x-3)}{(2x+1)(x+3)}\). Dividing by multiplying by the reciprocal yields \(\frac{x-3}{2x+1} \cdot \frac{(2x+1)(x+3)}{x(x-3)} = \frac{x+3}{x}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x^2-x-6}{x^2-6x+9} \div \left( \frac{x^2-4}{9-x^2} \cdot \frac{x^2+8x+15}{x^2-4x+4} \right)\)
qs.s: The first expression simplifies to \(\frac{x+2}{x-3}\), and the product inside simplifies to \(\frac{(x-2)(x+2)}{-(x-3)(x+3)} \cdot \frac{(x+3)(x+5)}{(x-2)^2} = \frac{-(x+2)(x+5)}{(x-3)(x-2)}\). Dividing gives \(\frac{x+2}{x-3} \cdot \frac{-(x-3)(x-2)}{(x+2)(x+5)} = -\frac{x-2}{x+5} = \frac{2-x}{x+5}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{2x^2-5x-3}{4x^2-1} \div \left( \frac{6x-18}{2x^2+5x-3} \cdot \frac{x^2-9}{3x^2-8x-3} \right)\)
qs.s: Factoring yields \(\frac{(2x+1)(x-3)}{(2x-1)(2x+1)} = \frac{x-3}{2x-1}\) for the first expression, and the product inside simplifies to \(\frac{6(x-3)}{(2x-1)(x+3)} \cdot \frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{(3x+1)(x-3)} = \frac{6(x-3)}{(2x-1)(3x+1)}\). Multiplying by the reciprocal gives \(\frac{x-3}{2x-1} \cdot \frac{(2x-1)(3x+1)}{6(x-3)} = \frac{3x+1}{6}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\frac{x-5}{x-1} \div \left( \frac{x^2-6x+5}{10x} \cdot \frac{x^2-5x}{x^2-2x+1} \right)\)
qs.s: Factor the expressions inside the parentheses to get \(\frac{(x-1)(x-5)}{10x} \cdot \frac{x(x-5)}{(x-1)^2} = \frac{(x-5)^2}{10(x-1)}\). Then multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{x-5}{x-1} \cdot \frac{10(x-1)}{(x-5)^2} = \frac{10}{x-5}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\frac{x+5}{x-5} \div \left( \frac{x^2-25}{3x} \cdot \frac{3x^2+15x}{x^2-10x+25} \right)\)
qs.s: Factor the expressions inside the parentheses to get \(\frac{(x-5)(x+5)}{3x} \cdot \frac{3x(x+5)}{(x-5)^2} = \frac{(x+5)^2}{x-5}\). Then multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{x+5}{x-5} \cdot \frac{x-5}{(x+5)^2} = \frac{1}{x+5}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\frac{x+4}{x-2} \div \left( \frac{x^2+2x-8}{4x} \cdot \frac{x^2+4x}{x^2-4x+4} \right)\)
qs.s: Factor the expressions inside the parentheses to get \(\frac{(x-2)(x+4)}{4x} \cdot \frac{x(x+4)}{(x-2)^2} = \frac{(x+4)^2}{4(x-2)}\). Then multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{x+4}{x-2} \cdot \frac{4(x-2)}{(x+4)^2} = \frac{4}{x+4}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\frac{x+2}{x+3} \div \left( \frac{x^2+5x+6}{2x} \cdot \frac{x^2+2x}{x^2+6x+9} \right)\)
qs.s: Factor the expressions inside the parentheses to get \(\frac{(x+2)(x+3)}{2x} \cdot \frac{x(x+2)}{(x+3)^2} = \frac{(x+2)^2}{2(x+3)}\). Then multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{x+2}{x+3} \cdot \frac{2(x+3)}{(x+2)^2} = \frac{2}{x+2}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\frac{x-6}{x-3} \div \left( \frac{x^2-9x+18}{6x} \cdot \frac{x^2-6x}{x^2-6x+9} \right)\)
qs.s: Factor the expressions inside the parentheses to get \(\frac{(x-3)(x-6)}{6x} \cdot \frac{x(x-6)}{(x-3)^2} = \frac{(x-6)^2}{6(x-3)}\). Then divide by multiplying by the reciprocal: \(\frac{x-6}{x-3} \cdot \frac{6(x-3)}{(x-6)^2} = \frac{6}{x-6}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\frac{2x+5}{2x+3} \div \left( \frac{4x^2-25}{4x^2-9} \cdot \frac{2x-3}{2x^2+x-15} \right)\)
qs.s: Factor the expressions inside the parentheses to obtain \(\frac{(2x-5)(2x+5)}{(2x-3)(2x+3)} \cdot \frac{2x-3}{(2x-5)(x+3)} = \frac{2x+5}{(2x+3)(x+3)}\). Then multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{2x+5}{2x+3} \cdot \frac{(2x+3)(x+3)}{2x+5} = x+3\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\frac{2x-3}{x+4} \div \left( \frac{2x^2+5x-12}{3x^2-7x+2} \cdot \frac{2x^2-7x+6}{x^2+8x+16} \right)\)
qs.s: Factor all quadratics inside the parentheses to obtain \(\frac{(2x-3)(x+4)}{(3x-1)(x-2)} \cdot \frac{(2x-3)(x-2)}{(x+4)^2} = \frac{(2x-3)^2}{(3x-1)(x+4)}\). Then multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{2x-3}{x+4} \cdot \frac{(3x-1)(x+4)}{(2x-3)^2} = \frac{3x-1}{2x-3}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\frac{x-2y}{x+3y} \div \left( \frac{x^2+xy-6y^2}{4xy} \cdot \frac{4xy-8y^2}{x^2+6xy+9y^2} \right)\)
qs.s: Factor the expressions inside the parentheses to obtain \(\frac{(x+3y)(x-2y)}{4xy} \cdot \frac{4y(x-2y)}{(x+3y)^2} = \frac{(x-2y)^2}{x(x+3y)}\). Then multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{x-2y}{x+3y} \cdot \frac{x(x+3y)}{(x-2y)^2} = \frac{x}{x-2y}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\frac{x-3}{x+5} \div \left( \frac{x^2-2x-15}{3x} \cdot \frac{3x^2-9x}{25-x^2} \right)\)
qs.s: Factor the expressions inside the parentheses, noting \(25-x^2 = -(x-5)(x+5)\), to get \(\frac{(x-5)(x+3)}{3x} \cdot \frac{3x(x-3)}{-(x-5)(x+5)} = -\frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x+5}\). Dividing by this expression gives \(\frac{x-3}{x+5} \cdot \left(-\frac{x+5}{(x-3)(x+3)}\right) = -\frac{1}{x+3}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\frac{3x-2}{x+3} \div \left( \frac{3x^2+7x-6}{4x^2-1} \cdot \frac{2x^2-x}{x^2+6x+9} \right)\)
qs.s: Factor each term inside the parentheses to obtain \(\frac{(3x-2)(x+3)}{(2x-1)(2x+1)} \cdot \frac{x(2x-1)}{(x+3)^2} = \frac{x(3x-2)}{(2x+1)(x+3)}\). Then multiply \(\frac{3x-2}{x+3}\) by the reciprocal to get \(\frac{3x-2}{x+3} \cdot \frac{(2x+1)(x+3)}{x(3x-2)} = \frac{2x+1}{x}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{a^2 - 9b^2}{2a - 4b} \div \frac{a + 3b}{a^2 - 4b^2}\)
qs.s: Multiply by the reciprocal and factor each polynomial: \(\frac{(a - 3b)(a + 3b)}{2(a - 2b)} \cdot \frac{(a - 2b)(a + 2b)}{a + 3b}\). Canceling \((a + 3b)\) and \((a - 2b)\) leaves \(\frac{(a - 3b)(a + 2b)}{2}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{5x + 10y}{x^2 - 4xy + 4y^2} \div \frac{x^2 - 4y^2}{x - 2y}\)
qs.s: Factor to get \(\frac{5(x + 2y)}{(x - 2y)^2} \cdot \frac{x - 2y}{(x - 2y)(x + 2y)}\). Canceling common factors \((x + 2y)\) and \((x - 2y)\) simplifies to \(\frac{5}{(x - 2y)^2}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{2x - 2y}{3x + y} \div \frac{x^2 - y^2}{9x^2 + 6xy + y^2}\)
qs.s: Multiply by the reciprocal of the second expression: \(\frac{2(x - y)}{3x + y} \cdot \frac{(3x + y)^2}{(x - y)(x + y)}\). Canceling the common factors \((x - y)\) and \((3x + y)\) gives \(\frac{2(3x + y)}{x + y}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{4m - 4n}{m^2 - n^2} \div \frac{12m}{m^2 + 2mn + n^2}\)
qs.s: Factor each term to get \(\frac{4(m - n)}{(m - n)(m + n)} \cdot \frac{(m + n)^2}{12m}\). Canceling \((m - n)\) and \((m + n)\) and simplifying \(\frac{4}{12m}\) gives \(\frac{m + n}{3m}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x^2 - x - 6}{x^2 - 9} \div \frac{x^2 - 4}{x^2 + 5x + 6}\)
qs.s: Factor all polynomials to rewrite the division as \(\frac{(x - 3)(x + 2)}{(x - 3)(x + 3)} \cdot \frac{(x + 2)(x + 3)}{(x - 2)(x + 2)}\). Canceling common factors leaves \(\frac{x + 2}{x - 2}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{3a^2 - 7ab + 2b^2}{9a^2 - b^2} \div \frac{2a^2 - 5ab + 2b^2}{3a^2 + 7ab + 2b^2}\)
qs.s: Factor each quadratic expression: \(\frac{(3a - b)(a - 2b)}{(3a - b)(3a + b)} \cdot \frac{(3a + b)(a + 2b)}{(2a - b)(a - 2b)}\). Canceling \((3a - b)\), \((a - 2b)\), and \((3a + b)\) simplifies the product to \(\frac{a + 2b}{2a - b}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{ax + 2bx - 3a - 6b}{2x^2 - 5x - 3} \div \frac{a^2 - 4b^2}{4x^2 - 1}\)
qs.s: Factor by grouping and differences of squares to obtain \(\frac{(a + 2b)(x - 3)}{(2x + 1)(x - 3)} \cdot \frac{(2x - 1)(2x + 1)}{(a - 2b)(a + 2b)}\). Canceling \((x - 3)\), \((a + 2b)\), and \((2x + 1)\) leaves \(\frac{2x - 1}{a - 2b}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x^2 - 16}{x^2 - 2x - 15} \div \frac{x^2 + 8x + 16}{x^2 - 9} \div \frac{x - 3}{x - 5}\)
qs.s: Rewrite both divisions by multiplying by reciprocals: \(\frac{(x - 4)(x + 4)}{(x - 5)(x + 3)} \cdot \frac{(x - 3)(x + 3)}{(x + 4)^2} \cdot \frac{x - 5}{x - 3}\). Canceling \((x - 5)\), \((x + 3)\), \((x - 3)\), and \((x + 4)\) leaves \(\frac{x - 4}{x + 4}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x^3 - 2x^2 - 9x + 18}{2x^2 + 7x + 3} \div \frac{x^2 - 5x + 6}{2x^2 - x - 1}\)
qs.s: Factor the 4-term polynomial by grouping as \((x - 2)(x - 3)(x + 3)\) and factor all trinomials: \(\frac{(x - 2)(x - 3)(x + 3)}{(2x + 1)(x + 3)} \cdot \frac{(2x + 1)(x - 1)}{(x - 2)(x - 3)}\). Canceling all matching factors leaves \(x - 1\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{2x^2 + 5xy - 3y^2}{x^2 - y^2} \div \frac{2x^2 - xy}{y - x}\)
qs.s: Factor the expressions, using \(y - x = -(x - y)\): \(\frac{(2x - y)(x + 3y)}{(x - y)(x + y)} \cdot \frac{-(x - y)}{x(2x - y)}\). Canceling \((2x - y)\) and \((x - y)\) yields \(-\frac{x + 3y}{x(x + y)}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{x^2-4y^2+3x+6y}{xy-2y^2+3y}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerator by grouping into \((x + 2y)(x - 2y + 3)\) and the denominator as \(y(x - 2y + 3)\). Divide out the common factor \((x - 2y + 3)\) to obtain \(\frac{x + 2y}{y}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{9a^2-b^2+12a-4b}{3a^2+ab+4a}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerator by grouping as \((3a - b)(3a + b) + 4(3a - b) = (3a - b)(3a + b + 4)\) and the denominator as \(a(3a + b + 4)\). Canceling the common factor \((3a + b + 4)\) leaves \(\frac{3a - b}{a}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{p^2-q^2+7p-7q}{pq+q^2+7q}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerator by grouping into \((p - q)(p + q + 7)\) and factor out \(q\) from the denominator to get \(q(p + q + 7)\). Canceling \((p + q + 7)\) yields \(\frac{p - q}{q}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{4u^2-9v^2-2u+3v}{2u^2+3uv-u}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerator by grouping as \((2u - 3v)(2u + 3v - 1)\) and the denominator as \(u(2u + 3v - 1)\). Canceling the common factor \((2u + 3v - 1)\) gives \(\frac{2u - 3v}{u}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{m^2-9n^2+2m-6n}{m^2+3mn+2m}\)
qs.s: Group the numerator as \((m - 3n)(m + 3n) + 2(m - 3n) = (m - 3n)(m + 3n + 2)\) and factor the denominator as \(m(m + 3n + 2)\). Canceling \((m + 3n + 2)\) results in \(\frac{m - 3n}{m}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{9x^2-4y^2+12x-8y}{6x^2-4xy+15x-10y}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerator by grouping as \((3x - 2y)(3x + 2y + 4)\) and the denominator by grouping pairs as \((3x - 2y)(2x + 5)\). Canceling the common factor \((3x - 2y)\) gives \(\frac{3x + 2y + 4}{2x + 5}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{4x^2-9y^2-10x+15y}{6x^2-7xy-3y^2}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerator by grouping as \((2x - 3y)(2x + 3y - 5)\) and factor the denominator trinomial as \((2x - 3y)(3x + y)\). Canceling \((2x - 3y)\) results in \(\frac{2x + 3y - 5}{3x + y}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{12a^2-27b^2+30a-45b}{12a^2+18ab+30a}\)
qs.s: Factor out \(3\) from the numerator to get \(3(2a - 3b)(2a + 3b + 5)\) and factor \(6a\) from the denominator to get \(6a(2a + 3b + 5)\). Canceling \((2a + 3b + 5)\) and reducing \(\frac{3}{6a}\) leaves \(\frac{2a - 3b}{2a}\).

qs.q:
Divide. Simplify answers if possible. Assume the denominators do not equal zero.

\(\displaystyle \frac{4u^2-v^2+6u-3v}{4u^2-v^2-8u+4v}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerator by grouping as \((2u - v)(2u + v + 3)\) and the denominator as \((2u - v)(2u + v - 4)\). Canceling the common binomial factor \((2u - v)\) yields \(\frac{2u + v + 3}{2u + v - 4}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{x^{2a}+x^a-12}{x^{2a}+5x^a+4} \div \frac{x^{2a}-x^a-6}{x^{2a}-4x^a-5}\)
qs.s: Factor each quadratic expression in terms of \(x^a\) and multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{(x^a-3)(x^a+4)}{(x^a+1)(x^a+4)} \cdot \frac{(x^a-5)(x^a+1)}{(x^a-3)(x^a+2)}\). Canceling common factors yields \(\frac{x^a-5}{x^a+2}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{a^{2m}+7a^m+12}{a^{2m}+8a^m+16} \div \frac{a^{2m}-9}{a^{2m}-16}\)
qs.s: Factor each expression and multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{(a^m+3)(a^m+4)}{(a^m+4)^2} \cdot \frac{(a^m-4)(a^m+4)}{(a^m-3)(a^m+3)}\). Canceling common factors results in \(\frac{a^m-4}{a^m-3}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{y^{2n}+3y^n-10}{y^{2n}-4y^n+4} \div \frac{y^{2n}+6y^n+5}{y^{2n}+y^n-6}\)
qs.s: Multiply by the reciprocal and factor all expressions: \(\frac{(y^n+5)(y^n-2)}{(y^n-2)^2} \cdot \frac{(y^n+3)(y^n-2)}{(y^n+5)(y^n+1)}\). Canceling all identical factors gives \(\frac{y^n+3}{y^n+1}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{x^{2a}-2x^a-15}{x^{2a}-25} \div \frac{x^{2a}-9}{x^{2a}+8x^a+15}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerators and denominators and multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{(x^a-5)(x^a+3)}{(x^a-5)(x^a+5)} \cdot \frac{(x^a+3)(x^a+5)}{(x^a-3)(x^a+3)}\). Simplifying common factors gives \(\frac{x^a+3}{x^a-3}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{x^{2b}-9}{x^{2b}+5x^b+6} \div \frac{x^{2b}-4x^b+3}{x^{2b}+6x^b+8}\)
qs.s: Factor each polynomial and multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{(x^b-3)(x^b+3)}{(x^b+2)(x^b+3)} \cdot \frac{(x^b+2)(x^b+4)}{(x^b-1)(x^b-3)}\). Canceling common factors leaves \(\frac{x^b+4}{x^b-1}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2x^{2a}-5x^a-12}{3x^{2a}-13x^a+4} \div \frac{2x^{2a}+7x^a+6}{6x^{2a}-17x^a+5}\)
qs.s: Factor each quadratic trinomial by grouping and multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{(2x^a+3)(x^a-4)}{(3x^a-1)(x^a-4)} \cdot \frac{(3x^a-1)(2x^a-5)}{(2x^a+3)(x^a+2)}\). Canceling common binomial factors gives \(\frac{2x^a-5}{x^a+2}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2x^{2a}+5x^a-3}{3x^{2a}+7x^a-6} \div \frac{2x^{2a}+7x^a-4}{6x^{2a}+11x^a-10}\)
qs.s: Factor the non-monic quadratics and multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{(2x^a-1)(x^a+3)}{(3x^a-2)(x^a+3)} \cdot \frac{(3x^a-2)(2x^a+5)}{(2x^a-1)(x^a+4)}\). Canceling the common factors \((2x^a-1)\), \((x^a+3)\), and \((3x^a-2)\) leaves \(\frac{2x^a+5}{x^a+4}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2x^{2a}-5x^a-3}{x^{2a}-9} \div \frac{1-4x^{2a}}{2x^{2a}+7x^a-4}\)
qs.s: Factor all terms, noting \(1-4x^{2a} = -(2x^a-1)(2x^a+1)\), then multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{(2x^a+1)(x^a-3)}{(x^a-3)(x^a+3)} \cdot \frac{(2x^a-1)(x^a+4)}{-(2x^a-1)(2x^a+1)}\). Canceling common factors leaves \(-\frac{x^a+4}{x^a+3}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{x^{2a}-4y^{2b}}{x^{2a}-3x^ay^b+2y^{2b}} \div \frac{2x^{2a}+5x^ay^b+2y^{2b}}{3x^{2a}-2x^ay^b-y^{2b}}\)
qs.s: Factor the two-variable expressions in terms of \(x^a\) and \(y^b\), then multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{(x^a-2y^b)(x^a+2y^b)}{(x^a-2y^b)(x^a-y^b)} \cdot \frac{(3x^a+y^b)(x^a-y^b)}{(2x^a+y^b)(x^a+2y^b)}\). Canceling identical binomials leaves \(\frac{3x^a+y^b}{2x^a+y^b}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2x^{2a+1}-8x}{x^{2a+1}+3x^{a+1}-10x} \div \frac{4x^{2a}+8x^a}{x^{2a}+4x^a-5}\)
qs.s: Factor out common monomials first to obtain \(\frac{2x(x^a-2)(x^a+2)}{x(x^a-2)(x^a+5)} \cdot \frac{(x^a+5)(x^a-1)}{4x^a(x^a+2)}\). Canceling common factors and reducing \(\frac{2}{4}\) yields \(\frac{x^a-1}{2x^a}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify completely. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{x^{2p}-16}{x^{2p}-3x^p-4} \div \frac{x^{2p}+3x^p-4}{x^{2p}-2x^p+1}\)
qs.s: Factoring gives \(\frac{(x^p-4)(x^p+4)}{(x^p-4)(x^p+1)} \cdot \frac{(x^p-1)^2}{(x^p+4)(x^p-1)}\). After canceling \((x^p-4)\), \((x^p+4)\), and one factor of \((x^p-1)\), the result is \(\frac{x^p-1}{x^p+1}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify completely. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{y^{2a}-y^a-6}{y^{2a}-9} \div \frac{y^{2a}-4}{y^{2a}+5y^a+6}\)
qs.s: Multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor to get \(\frac{(y^a-3)(y^a+2)}{(y^a-3)(y^a+3)} \cdot \frac{(y^a+2)(y^a+3)}{(y^a-2)(y^a+2)}\). Canceling common factors yields \(\frac{y^a+2}{y^a-2}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify completely. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{x^{2m}-2x^m-3}{x^{2m}-9} \div \frac{x^{2m}-1}{x^{2m}+2x^m-3}\)
qs.s: Rewriting division as multiplication by the reciprocal gives \(\frac{(x^m-3)(x^m+1)}{(x^m-3)(x^m+3)} \cdot \frac{(x^m+3)(x^m-1)}{(x^m-1)(x^m+1)} = 1\) after canceling identical factors.

qs.q:
Divide and simplify completely. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{x^{2n}+7x^n+10}{x^{2n}+4x^n-5} \div \frac{x^{2n}+x^n-2}{x^{2n}-1}\)
qs.s: Factor all polynomials to get \(\frac{(x^n+5)(x^n+2)}{(x^n+5)(x^n-1)} \cdot \frac{(x^n-1)(x^n+1)}{(x^n+2)(x^n-1)}\). Canceling common factors leaves \(\frac{x^n+1}{x^n-1}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify completely. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{x^{2k}+3x^k-10}{x^{2k}+6x^k+5} \div \frac{x^{2k}-4}{x^{2k}+3x^k+2}\)
qs.s: Factoring gives \(\frac{(x^k+5)(x^k-2)}{(x^k+5)(x^k+1)} \cdot \frac{(x^k+1)(x^k+2)}{(x^k-2)(x^k+2)}\). All factors cancel completely, leaving \(1\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify completely. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{x^{2b+1}-4x^{b+1}-5x}{x^{2b+1}-25x} \div \frac{x^{2b}-1}{2x^{b+1}+10x}\)
qs.s: Factor out common monomials first, giving \(\frac{x(x^b-5)(x^b+1)}{x(x^b-5)(x^b+5)} \cdot \frac{2x(x^b+5)}{(x^b-1)(x^b+1)}\). Canceling all common binomial and monomial factors leaves \(\frac{2x}{x^b-1}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify completely. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{x^{2k}+x^k-12}{9-x^{2k}} \div \frac{x^{2k}+3x^k-4}{x^{2k}+4x^k+3}\)
qs.s: Factor \(9-x^{2k}\) as \(-(x^k-3)(x^k+3)\) and multiply by the reciprocal to get \(\frac{(x^k+4)(x^k-3)}{-(x^k-3)(x^k+3)} \cdot \frac{(x^k+3)(x^k+1)}{(x^k+4)(x^k-1)}\). Canceling terms leaves \(-\frac{x^k+1}{x^k-1}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify completely. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{3x^{2a}-x^a-2}{9x^{2a}-4} \div \frac{x^{2a}+3x^a-4}{3x^{2a}+14x^a+8}\)
qs.s: Factor the non-monic quadratics to obtain \(\frac{(3x^a+2)(x^a-1)}{(3x^a-2)(3x^a+2)} \cdot \frac{(3x^a+2)(x^a+4)}{(x^a+4)(x^a-1)}\). Canceling common binomial factors leaves \(\frac{3x^a+2}{3x^a-2}\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify completely. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2x^{2n+2}+7x^{n+2}+3x^2}{4x^{2n+1}-x} \div \frac{x^{n+3}+3x^3}{2x^{n+2}-x^2}\)
qs.s: Factor out common powers of \(x\) to get \(\frac{x^2(2x^n+1)(x^n+3)}{x(2x^n-1)(2x^n+1)} \cdot \frac{x^2(2x^n-1)}{x^3(x^n+3)}\). Both the powers of \(x\) and all binomial factors cancel entirely, resulting in \(1\).

qs.q:
Divide and simplify completely. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
\(\displaystyle \frac{x^{2a}-y^{2b}}{x^{2a}+3x^a y^b+2y^{2b}} \div \frac{x^{2a}-2x^a y^b+y^{2b}}{x^{2a}-x^a y^b-6y^{2b}}\)
qs.s: Factor the two-variable quadratic expressions to get \(\frac{(x^a-y^b)(x^a+y^b)}{(x^a+y^b)(x^a+2y^b)} \cdot \frac{(x^a-3y^b)(x^a+2y^b)}{(x^a-y^b)^2}\). Canceling common factors leaves \(\frac{x^a-3y^b}{x^a-y^b}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{3x + 2}{x - 1} - \frac{x - 3}{x - 1} = \frac{2x + 5}{x - 1}\). If false, choose the correct simplified expression.
qs.s: Subtracting the numerators gives \((3x + 2) - (x - 3) = 3x + 2 - x + 3 = 2x + 5\). Retaining the common denominator gives \(\frac{2x + 5}{x - 1}\), so the statement is true.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{3 - x}{x + 4} - \frac{5 - x}{x + 4} = -\frac{2}{x + 4}\). If false, choose the correct simplified expression.
qs.s: Subtracting the numerators gives \((3 - x) - (5 - x) = 3 - x - 5 + x = -2\). Over the denominator \(x + 4\), this simplifies to \(\frac{-2}{x + 4} = -\frac{2}{x + 4}\), so the statement is true.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{4x - 1}{x - 2} - \frac{3x + 5}{x - 2} = \frac{x + 4}{x - 2}\). If false, choose the correct simplified expression.
qs.s: Distribute the negative sign across the second numerator: \((4x - 1) - (3x + 5) = 4x - 1 - 3x - 5 = x - 6\). Over the common denominator \(x - 2\), the result is \(\frac{x - 6}{x - 2}\), making the statement false.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{2x}{x + 3} - \frac{x - 4}{x + 3} = \frac{x - 4}{x + 3}\). If false, choose the correct simplified expression.
qs.s: Subtracting the numerators requires distributing the negative sign: \(2x - (x - 4) = 2x - x + 4 = x + 4\). Over the common denominator \(x + 3\), the correct result is \(\frac{x + 4}{x + 3}\), so the statement is false.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{2x + 1}{x + 5} - \frac{x - 4}{x + 5} = \frac{x - 3}{x + 5}\). If false, choose the correct simplified expression.
qs.s: Distributing the subtraction gives \((2x + 1) - (x - 4) = 2x + 1 - x + 4 = x + 5\). Since \(\frac{x + 5}{x + 5} = 1\), the statement is false.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{3x + 1}{x + 2} - \frac{x - 4}{x + 2} - \frac{2x - 1}{x + 2} = \frac{6}{x + 2}\). If false, choose the correct simplified expression.
qs.s: Distributing the negative sign across both subtracted numerators gives \((3x + 1) - (x - 4) - (2x - 1) = 3x + 1 - x + 4 - 2x + 1 = 6\). Over the common denominator \(x + 2\), this equals \(\frac{6}{x + 2}\), making the statement true.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{5}{x - 3} - \frac{2}{3 - x} = \frac{3}{x - 3}\). If false, choose the correct simplified expression.
qs.s: Since \(3 - x = -(x - 3)\), subtracting \(\frac{2}{3 - x}\) is equivalent to adding \(\frac{2}{x - 3}\), giving \(\frac{5 + 2}{x - 3} = \frac{7}{x - 3}\). Therefore, the statement is false.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x^2}{x - 5} - \frac{25}{x - 5} = x - 5\). If false, choose the correct simplified expression.
qs.s: Combine the numerators to get \(\frac{x^2 - 25}{x - 5}\). Factoring the numerator as a difference of squares gives \(\frac{(x - 5)(x + 5)}{x - 5} = x + 5\), so the statement is false.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{2x - 3}{x - 2} - \frac{x + 1}{2x - 4} = \frac{x - 4}{2x - 4}\). If false, choose the correct simplified expression.
d: False; the correct result is \(\frac{x - 4}{2 - x}\)
qs.s: The common denominator is \(2(x - 2) = 2x - 4\). Multiply the first fraction by \(\frac{2}{2}\) to get \(\frac{2(2x - 3) - (x + 1)}{2x - 4} = \frac{4x - 6 - x - 1}{2x - 4} = \frac{3x - 7}{2x - 4}\), so the statement is false.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{3}{4x} - \frac{1}{6x^2} = \frac{9x - 2}{12x^2}\). If false, choose the correct simplified expression.
qs.s: The least common denominator of \(4x\) and \(6x^2\) is \(12x^2\). Rewriting gives \(\frac{3(3x)}{12x^2} - \frac{1(2)}{12x^2} = \frac{9x - 2}{12x^2}\), which means the statement is true.

qs.q: True or false: For all \(x \neq 0\), \(\frac{2}{x} + \frac{3}{x} = \frac{5}{2x}\).
qs.a: False, because the common denominator is kept, giving \(\frac{5}{x}\).
d: True, because both the numerators and the denominators are added together.
False, because the expression simplifies to \(\frac{6}{x^2}\).
False, because the expression simplifies to \(\frac{5}{x^2}\).
qs.s: When adding rational expressions with a common denominator, add the numerators and keep the common denominator: \(\frac{2 + 3}{x} = \frac{5}{x}\). Therefore, the statement is false.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{2x + 6}{2} = x + 3\).
qs.a: True, because factoring the numerator gives \(\frac{2(x + 3)}{2} = x + 3\).
d: False, because cancelling \(2\) from the first term leaves \(x + 6\).
False, because dividing only the constant term gives \(2x + 3\).
False, because the \(2\) in the denominator cancels completely leaving \(0\).
qs.s: Factoring the numerator yields \(\frac{2(x + 3)}{2}\), and cancelling the common factor of \(2\) results in \(x + 3\). Therefore, the statement is true.

qs.q: True or false: For all \(x \neq \pm 3\), \(\frac{x}{x^2 - 9} - \frac{3}{x^2 - 9} = \frac{1}{x + 3}\).
d: False, because the numerators subtract to \(0\), making the result \(0\).
False, because the expression simplifies to \(\frac{1}{x - 3}\).
False, because the expression simplifies to \(x - 3\).
qs.s: Subtracting the numerators gives \(\frac{x - 3}{x^2 - 9}\). Factoring the denominator yields \(\frac{x - 3}{(x - 3)(x + 3)} = \frac{1}{x + 3}\), so the statement is true.

qs.q: True or false: For all \(x \neq -3\), \(\frac{x}{x + 3} - \frac{x - 2}{x + 3} = \frac{-2}{x + 3}\).
qs.a: False, because distributing the negative sign gives \(\frac{x - (x - 2)}{x + 3} = \frac{2}{x + 3}\).
d: True, because subtracting the numerators gives \(x - x - 2 = -2\).
False, because the denominators subtract to give a denominator of \(0\).
False, because the expression simplifies to \(0\).
qs.s: Subtracting the numerators requires distributing the negative sign: \(x - (x - 2) = x - x + 2 = 2\), yielding \(\frac{2}{x + 3}\). Therefore, the statement is false.

qs.q: True or false: For all \(x \neq 7\), \(\frac{x - 7}{7 - x} = 1\).
d: True, because the terms cancel out to \(1\).
False, because the expression simplifies to \(0\).
False, because the expression cannot be simplified.
qs.s: Factoring \(-1\) from the denominator yields \(\frac{x - 7}{-(x - 7)} = -1\). Therefore, the statement is false.

qs.q: True or false: For all values of \(x\) where defined, \(\frac{x}{x^2 - 4} - \frac{1}{x^2 - 2x} = \frac{x - 1}{x(x + 2)}\).
qs.a: False, because factoring \(x^2 - x - 2\) gives \((x - 2)(x + 1)\), simplifying to \(\frac{x + 1}{x(x + 2)}\).
d: True, because \(x^2 - x - 2\) factors into \((x + 2)(x - 1)\), leaving \(\frac{x - 1}{x(x + 2)}\).
False, because subtracting numerators directly gives \(\frac{x - 1}{2x}\).
False, because the expression simplifies to \(\frac{1}{x(x - 2)}\).
qs.s: The LCD is \(x(x - 2)(x + 2)\), which gives the numerator \(x^2 - (x + 2) = (x - 2)(x + 1)\). Cancelling \((x - 2)\) results in \(\frac{x + 1}{x(x + 2)}\), so the statement is false.

qs.q: True or false: For all values of \(x\) where defined, \(\frac{x^2 - 9}{x^2 + 4x + 3} \cdot \frac{x^2 - 1}{x^2 - 2x - 3} = \frac{x - 1}{x + 1}\).
qs.a: True, because factoring and cancelling all common factors leaves \(\frac{x - 1}{x + 1}\).
d: False, because all factors cancel out, leaving \(1\).
False, because all factors cancel out, leaving \(0\).
False, because the expression simplifies to \(\frac{x + 1}{x - 1}\).
qs.s: Factoring yields \(\frac{(x - 3)(x + 3)}{(x + 1)(x + 3)} \cdot \frac{(x - 1)(x + 1)}{(x - 3)(x + 1)}\). Cancelling common factors leaves \(\frac{x - 1}{x + 1}\), so the statement is true.

qs.q: True or false: For all \(x \neq 4\), \(\frac{3x - 5}{x - 4} + \frac{x + 3}{4 - x} = 2\).
qs.a: True, because rewriting with a common denominator gives \(\frac{2x - 8}{x - 4} = 2\).
d: False, because adding the numerators directly yields \(\frac{4x - 2}{x - 4}\).
False, because the expression simplifies to \(\frac{2x - 2}{x - 4}\).
False, because the expression simplifies to \(0\).
qs.s: Rewriting \(\frac{x + 3}{4 - x}\) as \(-\frac{x + 3}{x - 4}\) allows subtraction of the numerators: \(\frac{(3x - 5) - (x + 3)}{x - 4} = \frac{2x - 8}{x - 4} = 2\). Therefore, the statement is true.

qs.q: True or false: For all values of \(x\) where defined, \(\frac{2}{x - 3} - \frac{1}{x + 2} - \frac{5}{x^2 - x - 6} = \frac{1}{x - 3}\).
qs.a: True, because the combined numerator simplifies to \(x + 2\), which cancels to leave \(\frac{1}{x - 3}\).
d: False, because failing to distribute the negative sign leaves \(\frac{x - 4}{(x - 3)(x + 2)}\).
False, because all terms in the numerator cancel out to \(0\).
False, because the expression simplifies to \(\frac{1}{x + 2}\).
qs.s: Using the common denominator \((x - 3)(x + 2)\), the numerator becomes \(2(x + 2) - (x - 3) - 5 = x + 2\). Cancelling \((x + 2)\) leaves \(\frac{1}{x - 3}\), so the statement is true.

qs.q: True or false: For all values of \(x\) where defined, \(\frac{x^2 - 25}{2x - 6} \div \frac{5 - x}{x^2 - 9} = \frac{(x + 5)(x + 3)}{2}\).
qs.a: False, because \(\frac{x - 5}{5 - x} = -1\), making the result \(-\frac{(x + 5)(x + 3)}{2}\).
d: True, because common factors cancel out to leave positive \(1\).
False, because dividing rational expressions does not invert the second fraction.
False, because the expression simplifies to \(-1\).
qs.s: Multiplying by the reciprocal gives \(\frac{(x - 5)(x + 5)}{2(x - 3)} \cdot \frac{(x - 3)(x + 3)}{5 - x}\). Because \(\frac{x - 5}{5 - x} = -1\), the simplified result is \(-\frac{(x + 5)(x + 3)}{2}\), so the statement is false.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{4}{x - 3} + \frac{2}{3 - x} = \frac{6}{x - 3}\) for all real numbers \(x \neq 3\).
qs.a: False, because the sum simplifies to \(\frac{2}{x - 3}\).
d: True, because adding the numerators over the common denominator gives \(\frac{4 + 2}{x - 3} = \frac{6}{x - 3}\).
False, because the sum simplifies to \(-\frac{2}{x - 3}\).
False, because the sum simplifies to \(\frac{6}{(x - 3)^2}\).
qs.s: Since \(3 - x = -(x - 3)\), the second fraction is \(-\frac{2}{x - 3}\), so \(\frac{4}{x - 3} - \frac{2}{x - 3} = \frac{2}{x - 3}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x - 1}{x + 2} + \frac{x + 2}{x - 1} = 2\) for all real numbers \(x \neq -2, 1\).
qs.a: False, because the sum simplifies to \(\frac{2x^2 + 2x + 5}{(x + 2)(x - 1)}\).
d: True, because the terms cross-cancel to \(1 + 1 = 2\).
False, because the sum simplifies to \(1\).
False, because the sum simplifies to \(\frac{2x + 1}{(x + 2)(x - 1)}\).
qs.s: Finding the common denominator \((x + 2)(x - 1)\) gives \(\frac{(x - 1)^2 + (x + 2)^2}{(x + 2)(x - 1)} = \frac{2x^2 + 2x + 5}{(x + 2)(x - 1)}\), which does not equal \(2\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x}{x + 2} + \frac{2}{x - 2} = \frac{x^2 + 4}{x^2 - 4}\) for all real numbers \(x \neq \pm 2\).
qs.a: True, because finding the common denominator gives \(\frac{x(x - 2) + 2(x + 2)}{x^2 - 4} = \frac{x^2 + 4}{x^2 - 4}\).
d: False, because the sum simplifies to \(1\).
False, because the sum simplifies to \(\frac{x + 2}{x^2 - 4}\).
False, because the sum simplifies to \(\frac{x^2 - 4x + 4}{x^2 - 4}\).
qs.s: Writing both terms over the LCD \((x + 2)(x - 2)\) yields \(\frac{x(x - 2) + 2(x + 2)}{x^2 - 4} = \frac{x^2 - 2x + 2x + 4}{x^2 - 4} = \frac{x^2 + 4}{x^2 - 4}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x}{2x - 4} - \frac{1}{x - 2} = \frac{1}{2}\) for all real numbers \(x \neq 2\).
d: False, because the expression simplifies to \(\frac{x - 1}{2x - 4}\).
False, because the expression simplifies to \(\frac{x - 1}{x - 2}\).
False, because the expression simplifies to \(0\).
qs.s: Factoring the first denominator gives \(2(x - 2)\), so subtracting gives \(\frac{x - 2}{2(x - 2)}\), which reduces to \(\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{x + 2} = \frac{2}{2x + 2}\) for all real numbers \(x \neq -2, 0\).
qs.a: False, because the sum simplifies to \(\frac{2x + 2}{x(x + 2)}\).
d: True, because adding numerators gives \(2\) and adding denominators gives \(2x + 2\).
False, because the sum simplifies to \(\frac{2}{x(x + 2)}\).
False, because the sum simplifies to \(\frac{1}{x(x + 2)}\).
qs.s: Rational expressions cannot be added by adding denominators; finding the LCD \(x(x + 2)\) gives \(\frac{(x + 2) + x}{x(x + 2)} = \frac{2x + 2}{x(x + 2)}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x + 1}{x - 1} - \frac{x - 1}{x + 1} - \frac{4x}{x^2 - 1} = 0\) for all real numbers \(x \neq \pm 1\).
d: False, because the expression simplifies to \(\frac{8x}{x^2 - 1}\).
False, because the expression simplifies to \(\frac{2}{x^2 - 1}\).
False, because the first two terms cancel to \(0\), leaving \(-\frac{4x}{x^2 - 1}\).
qs.s: Placing all terms over the LCD \(x^2 - 1\) gives \(\frac{(x^2 + 2x + 1) - (x^2 - 2x + 1) - 4x}{x^2 - 1} = \frac{4x - 4x}{x^2 - 1} = 0\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x}{x^2 - 4x + 3} - \frac{2}{x^2 - 2x - 3} = \frac{x - 2}{(x - 3)(x - 1)(x + 1)}\) for all real numbers \(x \neq -1, 1, 3\).
qs.a: False, because the difference simplifies to \(\frac{x^2 - x + 2}{(x - 3)(x - 1)(x + 1)}\).
d: True, because the common denominator is \((x - 3)(x - 1)(x + 1)\) and the numerators subtract to \(x - 2\).
False, because the difference simplifies to \(\frac{x - 2}{(x - 3)(x - 1)}\).
False, because the difference simplifies to \(\frac{x^2 + x - 2}{(x - 3)(x - 1)(x + 1)}\).
qs.s: Factoring the denominators gives \((x - 3)(x - 1)\) and \((x - 3)(x + 1)\); the numerator becomes \(x(x + 1) - 2(x - 1) = x^2 - x + 2\), not \(x - 2\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{1}{x - 2} - \frac{4}{x^2 - 4} = \frac{1}{x + 2}\) for all real numbers \(x \neq \pm 2\).
d: False, because the difference simplifies to \(\frac{-3}{x^2 - 4}\).
False, because the difference simplifies to \(\frac{x - 6}{(x - 2)(x + 2)}\).
False, because the difference simplifies to \(\frac{1}{x - 2}\).
qs.s: Factoring \(x^2 - 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2)\) gives the common denominator; subtracting gives \(\frac{x + 2 - 4}{(x - 2)(x + 2)} = \frac{x - 2}{(x - 2)(x + 2)} = \frac{1}{x + 2}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x^2 + 3x}{x^2 - 25} - \frac{x - 5}{x + 5} = \frac{8x - 25}{x^2 - 25}\) for all real numbers \(x \neq \pm 5\).
qs.a: False, because \((x - 5)^2 = x^2 - 10x + 25\), so the difference simplifies to \(\frac{13x - 25}{x^2 - 25}\).
d: True, because \((x^2 + 3x) - (x^2 - 5x + 25) = 8x - 25\) over the common denominator.
False, because the difference simplifies to \(\frac{3x + 5}{x^2 - 25}\).
False, because the difference simplifies to \(\frac{13x + 25}{x^2 - 25}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{5x - 3}{x^2 - 9} + \frac{x}{x + 3} = \frac{x - 1}{x - 3}\) for all real numbers \(x \neq \pm 3\).
d: False, because the sum simplifies to \(\frac{6x - 3}{x^2 - 9}\).
False, because the numerator factors to \((x - 3)(x + 1)\), giving \(\frac{x + 1}{x + 3}\).
False, because the sum simplifies to \(\frac{x^2 + 5x - 3}{(x - 3)(x + 3)}\).
qs.s: Combining over \((x - 3)(x + 3)\) gives numerator \((5x - 3) + x(x - 3) = x^2 + 2x - 3 = (x + 3)(x - 1)\); dividing out \((x + 3)\) leaves \(\frac{x - 1}{x - 3}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x + 2}{x - 1} + \frac{x - 3}{x + 2} = \frac{2x - 1}{2x + 1}\)
qs.s: To add expressions with unlike denominators, find the LCD \((x - 1)(x + 2)\) and rewrite the numerators: \(\frac{(x + 2)^2 + (x - 3)(x - 1)}{(x - 1)(x + 2)} = \frac{2x^2 + 7}{(x - 1)(x + 2)}\), not \(\frac{2x - 1}{2x + 1}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{3}{x} + \frac{2}{x + 1} = \frac{5}{2x + 1}\)
qs.s: The denominators cannot simply be added together; using the LCD \(x(x + 1)\) gives \(\frac{3(x + 1) + 2x}{x(x + 1)} = \frac{5x + 3}{x(x + 1)}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{3x + 1}{x - 2} - \frac{x - 5}{x - 2} = \frac{2x - 4}{x - 2}\)
qs.s: When subtracting expressions with like denominators, distribute the negative sign across the entire second numerator: \((3x + 1) - (x - 5) = 3x + 1 - x + 5 = 2x + 6\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{2}{x - 3} - \frac{1}{x + 1} = \frac{x + 5}{(x - 3)(x + 1)}\)
qs.s: Using the LCD \((x - 3)(x + 1)\), we obtain \(\frac{2(x + 1) - (x - 3)}{(x - 3)(x + 1)} = \frac{2x + 2 - x + 3}{(x - 3)(x + 1)} = \frac{x + 5}{(x - 3)(x + 1)}\), so the statement is true.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{5}{x - 3} + \frac{2}{3 - x} = \frac{3}{x - 3}\)
qs.s: Since \(3 - x = -(x - 3)\), the second fraction can be rewritten as \(-\frac{2}{x - 3}\), giving \(\frac{5}{x - 3} - \frac{2}{x - 3} = \frac{3}{x - 3}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{1}{x - 1} - \frac{2}{x + 1} + \frac{x - 3}{x^2 - 1} = \frac{x - 4}{x^2 - 1}\)
qs.a: False, the correct simplified expression is \(0\)
d: False, the correct simplified expression is \(\frac{2x - 4}{x^2 - 1}\)
False, the correct simplified expression is \(\frac{x - 4}{x - 1}\)
qs.s: Using the common denominator \((x - 1)(x + 1)\), the combined numerator is \((x + 1) - 2(x - 1) + (x - 3) = x + 1 - 2x + 2 + x - 3 = 0\), so the entire expression simplifies to \(0\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x + 1}{x^2 - 2x - 3} - \frac{1}{x^2 - 9} = \frac{x + 2}{(x - 3)(x + 3)}\)
qs.s: Simplifying \(\frac{x + 1}{(x - 3)(x + 1)}\) gives \(\frac{1}{x - 3}\), and subtracting \(\frac{1}{(x - 3)(x + 3)}\) yields \(\frac{(x + 3) - 1}{(x - 3)(x + 3)} = \frac{x + 2}{(x - 3)(x + 3)}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x - 1}{x^2 - 4} + \frac{2}{x^2 - x - 2} = \frac{x + 1}{2x^2 - x - 6}\)
qs.s: Factoring the denominators gives \((x - 2)(x + 2)\) and \((x - 2)(x + 1)\) with LCD \((x - 2)(x + 2)(x + 1)\); the sum is \(\frac{(x - 1)(x + 1) + 2(x + 2)}{(x - 2)(x + 2)(x + 1)} = \frac{x^2 + 2x + 3}{(x - 2)(x + 2)(x + 1)}\).
The LCD is \((x - 2)(x + 2)(x + 3)\) and the numerator simplifies to \(4(x + 3) - 5(x + 2) = -(x - 2)\), which cancels with \((x - 2)\) in the denominator to leave \(-\frac{1}{(x + 2)(x + 3)}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{2x}{x^2 + 5x + 6} + \frac{x - 1}{x^2 + 2x - 3} = \frac{3x - 1}{2x^2 + 7x + 3}\)
qs.s: The second fraction simplifies to \(\frac{x - 1}{(x - 1)(x + 3)} = \frac{1}{x + 3}\), so over the LCD \((x + 2)(x + 3)\), the sum is \(\frac{2x + (x + 2)}{(x + 2)(x + 3)} = \frac{3x + 2}{(x + 2)(x + 3)}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{2x - 3}{5x + 2} + \frac{3x + 8}{5x + 2} = \frac{5x + 5}{10x + 4}\)
qs.s: When adding rational expressions with a common denominator, the denominator remains \(5x + 2\) rather than being added together, giving \(\frac{5x + 5}{5x + 2}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{4x - 1}{x - 3} - \frac{3x + 2}{x - 3} = 1\)
qs.s: Subtracting the numerators yields \((4x - 1) - (3x + 2) = x - 3\), and simplifying \(\frac{x - 3}{x - 3}\) results in \(1\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x + 4}{3x - 2} - \frac{x + 9}{3x - 2} = \frac{13}{3x - 2}\)
qs.s: Subtracting the numerators with like denominators gives \((x + 4) - (x + 9) = x + 4 - x - 9 = -5\), so the difference is \(-\frac{5}{3x - 2}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{2x - 1}{x + 5} - \frac{x - 4}{x + 5} = \frac{x - 5}{x + 5}\)
qs.s: Distributing the negative sign gives \((2x - 1) - (x - 4) = 2x - 1 - x + 4 = x + 3\), so the correct result is \(\frac{x + 3}{x + 5}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{3x + 2}{2x + 1} - \frac{x - 2}{2x + 1} = \frac{2x + 4}{2x + 1}\)
qs.s: Subtracting the numerators gives \((3x + 2) - (x - 2) = 3x + 2 - x + 2 = 2x + 4\) over the common denominator \(2x + 1\), making the statement true.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x^2 + 2x}{x - 4} + \frac{7x - 4}{4 - x} = x - 1\)
qs.s: Rewriting \(4 - x\) as \(-(x - 4)\) changes addition to subtraction: \(\frac{x^2 + 2x - (7x - 4)}{x - 4} = \frac{x^2 - 5x + 4}{x - 4} = \frac{(x - 4)(x - 1)}{x - 4} = x - 1\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{3x - 1}{x + 2} - \frac{x + 5}{x + 2} - \frac{x - 4}{x + 2} = \frac{x - 10}{x + 2}\)
qs.s: Distributing the negative signs to both subtracted numerators gives \((3x - 1) - (x + 5) - (x - 4) = 3x - 1 - x - 5 - x + 4 = x - 2\), so the expression equals \(\frac{x - 2}{x + 2}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x^2 + 2x}{x^2 - 9} - \frac{x + 6}{x^2 - 9} = \frac{x - 2}{x - 3}\)
qs.s: Combining numerators gives \(\frac{x^2 + x - 6}{x^2 - 9} = \frac{(x + 3)(x - 2)}{(x + 3)(x - 3)} = \frac{x - 2}{x - 3}\), which confirms the statement is true.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{2x - 1}{x^2 - 4} - \frac{1}{x - 2} = \frac{2x - 2}{x^2 - 4}\)
qs.s: The common denominator is \((x - 2)(x + 2) = x^2 - 4\), so subtracting yields \(\frac{(2x - 1) - 1(x + 2)}{x^2 - 4} = \frac{x - 3}{x^2 - 4}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{5}{4x} + \frac{3}{4x} = \frac{2}{x}\)
d: False, because the denominators should be added, giving \(\frac{1}{x}\)
False, because the numerators should be multiplied, giving \(\frac{15}{4x}\)
False, because the denominator should be squared, giving \(\frac{2}{x^2}\)
qs.s: Adding the numerators over the common denominator gives \(\frac{8}{4x}\), which reduces to \(\frac{2}{x}\) upon dividing the numerator and denominator by 4.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{9}{z} - \frac{5}{z} = \frac{4}{2z}\)
d: True, because denominators must be added together
qs.s: Subtracting rational expressions with like denominators keeps the common denominator unchanged: \(\frac{9 - 5}{z} = \frac{4}{z}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{2x}{9} + \frac{4x}{9} = \frac{2x}{3}\)
d: False, because the denominators should be added to give \(\frac{x}{3}\)
False, because the expression cannot be simplified beyond \(\frac{6x}{18}\)
False, because the numerators are multiplied to give \(\frac{8x^2}{9}\)
qs.s: Adding the numerators over the common denominator gives \(\frac{6x}{9}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{2x}{3}\) after dividing the numerator and denominator by 3.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{4}{y} + \frac{5}{y} = \frac{4 + 5}{y + y}\)
d: True, because numerators and denominators are both added
qs.s: When adding rational expressions with a common denominator, add the numerators and keep the common denominator: \(\frac{4}{y} + \frac{5}{y} = \frac{9}{y}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{7}{a} - \frac{2}{a} = \frac{7 - 2}{a - a}\)
d: True, because numerators and denominators are both subtracted
qs.s: When subtracting rational expressions with a common denominator, subtract the numerators and keep the common denominator: \(\frac{7}{a} - \frac{2}{a} = \frac{5}{a}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{3}{2x} + \frac{1}{4x^2} = \frac{4}{2x + 4x^2}\)
qs.a: False, because using the common denominator \(4x^2\) gives \(\frac{6x + 1}{4x^2}\)
d: True, because numerators and denominators are added directly
False, because the correct sum is \(\frac{4}{4x^2}\)
False, because the correct sum is \(\frac{6x + 1}{8x^3}\)
qs.s: To add expressions with unlike denominators, find the LCD (\(4x^2\)) and rewrite: \(\frac{3(2x)}{4x^2} + \frac{1}{4x^2} = \frac{6x + 1}{4x^2}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x^2}{x - 4} - \frac{16}{x - 4} = x - 4\)
d: False, because the expression cannot be simplified and must remain \(\frac{x^2 - 16}{x - 4}\)
False, because the denominator becomes zero: \((x - 4) - (x - 4) = 0\)
qs.s: Subtracting the numerators gives \(\frac{x^2 - 16}{x - 4}\), and factoring the difference of squares gives \(\frac{(x - 4)(x + 4)}{x - 4} = x + 4\), not \(x - 4\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{5x + 3}{x - 2} - \frac{2x - 1}{x - 2} = \frac{3x + 2}{x - 2}\)
qs.a: False, because subtracting \((2x - 1)\) requires distributing the negative sign, giving \(\frac{3x + 4}{x - 2}\)
d: True, because the minus sign applies only to the first term \(2x\)
False, because the denominators must also be subtracted, giving \(\frac{3x + 4}{0}\)
False, because the expression simplifies to \(3\)
qs.s: Distributing the negative sign across the second numerator yields \((5x + 3) - (2x - 1) = 3x + 4\), so the correct result is \(\frac{3x + 4}{x - 2}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{2x + 5}{x + 1} + \frac{x - 2}{x + 1} - \frac{x + 1}{x + 1} = 2\)
d: False, because the negative sign is not distributed, giving \(\frac{2x + 4}{x + 1}\)
False, because the expression can only simplify to \(\frac{2x + 2}{x + 1}\)
False, because the denominators cancel out to give \(0\)
qs.s: Combining all three numerators over the common denominator gives \(\frac{2x + 5 + x - 2 - x - 1}{x + 1} = \frac{2x + 2}{x + 1}\), which factors to \(\frac{2(x + 1)}{x + 1} = 2\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{9}{x - 5} + \frac{4}{5 - x} = \frac{5}{x - 5}\)
d: False, because the terms should be added directly to give \(\frac{13}{x - 5}\)
False, because the denominators add to zero: \((x - 5) + (5 - x) = 0\)
False, because the numerators should be multiplied to give \(\frac{36}{x - 5}\)
qs.s: Since \(5 - x = -(x - 5)\), the expression can be rewritten as \(\frac{9}{x - 5} - \frac{4}{x - 5} = \frac{5}{x - 5}\), making the statement true.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{3}{x - 4} + \frac{3}{4 - x} = 0\) (for all \(x \neq 4\))
qs.s: True. Since \(4 - x = -(x - 4)\), the second term can be rewritten as \(-\frac{3}{x - 4}\), which gives \(\frac{3}{x - 4} - \frac{3}{x - 4} = 0\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} = \frac{2}{x + y}\)
qs.s: False. Fractions cannot be added by simply adding their numerators and denominators; using a common denominator gives \(\frac{x + y}{xy}\), which is not equivalent to \(\frac{2}{x + y}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x}{4} - \frac{x - 8}{4} = -2\)
qs.s: False. Subtracting the numerator requires distributing the negative sign to both terms: \(\frac{x - (x - 8)}{4} = \frac{x - x + 8}{4} = \frac{8}{4} = 2\), not \(-2\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{1}{x - 3} = \frac{1}{x} - \frac{1}{3}\)
qs.s: False. A denominator cannot be split across subtraction; finding a common denominator on the right gives \(\frac{3 - x}{3x}\), which is not equivalent to \(\frac{1}{x - 3}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x + 5}{5} = \frac{x}{5} + 1\)
qs.s: True. A numerator with multiple terms over a single denominator can be split into separate fractions: \(\frac{x + 5}{5} = \frac{x}{5} + \frac{5}{5} = \frac{x}{5} + 1\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{2}{x^2 - 1} + \frac{1}{x - 1} = \frac{3}{x^2 - 1}\) (for all \(x \neq \pm 1\))
qs.s: False. The second fraction must be converted to the common denominator \((x - 1)(x + 1)\) by multiplying numerator and denominator by \((x + 1)\), giving \(\frac{2 + (x + 1)}{x^2 - 1} = \frac{x + 3}{x^2 - 1}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{1}{x - 2} - \frac{4}{x^2 - 4} = \frac{1}{x + 2}\) (for all \(x \neq \pm 2\))
qs.s: True. Using the LCD \((x - 2)(x + 2)\), the numerator is \((x + 2) - 4 = x - 2\), which cancels with the \((x - 2)\) factor in the denominator to give \(\frac{1}{x + 2}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x}{x - 1} - \frac{1}{x + 1} = \frac{x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 1}\) (for all \(x \neq \pm 1\))
qs.s: True. Using the common denominator \((x - 1)(x + 1) = x^2 - 1\), the numerator becomes \(x(x + 1) - (x - 1) = x^2 + x - x + 1 = x^2 + 1\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{1}{x^2 - 4} = \frac{1}{x^2} - \frac{1}{4}\)
qs.s: False. The denominator \(x^2 - 4\) cannot be split into separate fractions; for example, when \(x = 3\), the left side equals \(\frac{1}{5}\) while the right side equals \(\frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{4} = -\frac{5}{36}\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{5x}{x - 3} + \frac{15}{3 - x} = -5\) (for all \(x \neq 3\))
qs.s: False. Factoring a \(-1\) from the second denominator gives \(\frac{5x}{x - 3} - \frac{15}{x - 3} = \frac{5(x - 3)}{x - 3} = 5\), not \(-5\).

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{1}{x + 4} + \frac{1}{x - 4} = \frac{2}{x^2 - 16}\)
qs.s: Using the LCD \((x + 4)(x - 4) = x^2 - 16\), the numerator is \((x - 4) + (x + 4) = 2x\). The resulting sum is \(\frac{2x}{x^2 - 16}\), not \(\frac{2}{x^2 - 16}\), so the statement is false.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{4}{x + 2} + \frac{4}{x - 2} = \frac{8}{2x}\)
qs.s: The common denominator is \((x + 2)(x - 2) = x^2 - 4\). Adding gives \(\frac{4(x - 2) + 4(x + 2)}{x^2 - 4} = \frac{8x}{x^2 - 4}\), so the statement is false.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x}{x^2 - 9} - \frac{3}{x^2 - 9} = \frac{1}{x + 3}\)
qs.s: Combining the fractions over the common denominator gives \(\frac{x - 3}{x^2 - 9}\). Factoring the denominator as \((x - 3)(x + 3)\) and canceling \((x - 3)\) results in \(\frac{1}{x + 3}\), so the statement is true.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{2}{x} - \frac{1}{x + 1} = \frac{1}{x(x + 1)}\)
qs.s: The LCD is \(x(x + 1)\), so the numerator becomes \(2(x + 1) - 1(x) = 2x + 2 - x = x + 2\). Subtracting numerators directly without scaling is incorrect, so the statement is false.

Factoring the denominators gives \((x - 1)(x - 2)\) and \((x + 2)(x - 2)\) with LCD \((x - 1)(x - 2)(x + 2)\). The numerator is \(3(x + 2) - 2(x - 1) = 3x + 6 - 2x + 2 = x + 8\), not \(x + 4\), so the statement is false.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{1}{x - 1} + \frac{2}{x + 1} - \frac{2x}{x^2 - 1} = \frac{3 - 2x}{x^2 - 1}\)
qs.s: The LCD is \((x - 1)(x + 1) = x^2 - 1\). The scaled numerator is \((x + 1) + 2(x - 1) - 2x = x - 1\), which simplifies to \(\frac{x - 1}{(x - 1)(x + 1)} = \frac{1}{x + 1}\), so the statement is false.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{2}{x^2 - 1} - \frac{1}{x^2 - x} = \frac{1}{x(x + 1)}\)
qs.s: Factoring gives denominators \((x - 1)(x + 1)\) and \(x(x - 1)\) with LCD \(x(x - 1)(x + 1)\). The numerator is \(2x - (x + 1) = x - 1\), which cancels with \((x - 1)\) in the denominator to leave \(\frac{1}{x(x + 1)}\), so the statement is true.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{1}{x^2 - 4} - \frac{1}{x^2 + 2x} = \frac{-2}{x(x - 2)(x + 2)}\)
qs.s: Factoring the denominators gives the LCD \(x(x - 2)(x + 2)\). The numerator is \(x - (x - 2) = x - x + 2 = 2\), not \(-2\), so the statement is false.

qs.q: True or false: \(\frac{x + 2}{x^2 - 2x} - \frac{x - 2}{x^2 + 2x} = \frac{8}{x^2 - 4}\)
qs.s: The LCD is \(x(x - 2)(x + 2)\). The numerator expands to \((x + 2)^2 - (x - 2)^2 = (x^2 + 4x + 4) - (x^2 - 4x + 4) = 8x\), and dividing out \(x\) leaves \(\frac{8}{(x - 2)(x + 2)} = \frac{8}{x^2 - 4}\), so the statement is true.

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{4}{9}, \frac{5}{63}\)
qs.s: Since \(63 = 9 \times 7\), 63 is a multiple of 9. Therefore, the least common denominator is 63.

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{5}{6}, \frac{7}{48}\)
qs.s: Since \(48 = 6 \times 8\), 48 is a multiple of 6. Therefore, the least common denominator is 48.

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{3}{14}, \frac{5}{56}\)
qs.s: Since \(56 = 14 \times 4\), 56 is a multiple of 14. Therefore, the least common denominator is 56.

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{5}{12}, \frac{7}{18}\)
qs.s: The prime factorizations of the denominators are \(12 = 2^2 \times 3\) and \(18 = 2 \times 3^2\). The LCD is \(2^2 \times 3^2 = 36\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{7}{15}, \frac{3}{20}\)
qs.s: The prime factorizations are \(15 = 3 \times 5\) and \(20 = 2^2 \times 5\). The LCD is \(2^2 \times 3 \times 5 = 60\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{3}{x^2 + 5x + 4}, \frac{7}{x^2 + 7x + 12}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators: \(x^2 + 5x + 4 = (x + 1)(x + 4)\) and \(x^2 + 7x + 12 = (x + 3)(x + 4)\). The LCD is the product of all unique factors to their highest powers: \((x + 1)(x + 3)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{1}{x^2 - 9}, \frac{4}{x^2 - 3x}\)
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(x^2 - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3)\) and \(x^2 - 3x = x(x - 3)\). Taking each unique factor to its highest power gives the LCD \(x(x - 3)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{2}{x^2 + x - 6}, \frac{5}{x^2 - 4}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators into \((x + 3)(x - 2)\) and \((x + 2)(x - 2)\). The LCD contains each unique factor to the highest power, giving \((x - 2)(x + 2)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{5}{12x^3}, \frac{7}{18x^5}\)
qs.s: The LCM of the numerical coefficients 12 and 18 is 36, and the highest power of \(x\) is \(x^5\). Thus, the LCD is \(36x^5\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{3}{10a^2b^4}, \frac{7}{15a^3b^2}\)
qs.s: The LCM of 10 and 15 is 30, and the highest powers of the variables are \(a^3\) and \(b^4\). Therefore, the LCD is \(30a^3b^4\).

qs.q: Find the LCD of the rational expressions \(\frac{1}{b^5}\) and \(\frac{6}{b^8}\).
qs.s: The denominators are \(b^5\) and \(b^8\). Taking the highest power of the common base gives an LCD of \(b^8\).

qs.q: Find the LCD of the rational expressions \(\frac{4}{m}\) and \(\frac{9}{m^4}\).
qs.s: The denominators are \(m^1\) and \(m^4\). The LCD is the factor with the highest power, which is \(m^4\).

qs.q: Find the LCD of the rational expressions \(\frac{7}{t^6}\) and \(\frac{3}{t^4}\).
qs.s: The denominators are \(t^6\) and \(t^4\). The LCD is determined by the highest exponent of \(t\), which is \(t^6\).

qs.q: Find the LCD of the rational expressions \(\frac{5}{a^7}\) and \(\frac{4}{a^2}\).
qs.s: The denominators are \(a^7\) and \(a^2\). The LCD is the variable with the highest exponent, which is \(a^7\).

qs.q: Find the LCD of the rational expressions \(\frac{2}{y^3}\) and \(\frac{7}{y^6}\).
qs.s: The denominators are \(y^3\) and \(y^6\). The least common denominator is the variable base raised to the highest power, which is \(y^6\).

qs.q: Find the LCD of the rational expressions \(\frac{3}{10c^4d}\) and \(\frac{7}{15c^2d^3}\).
qs.s: The LCM of 10 and 15 is 30. Taking the highest power for each variable factor, \(c^4\) and \(d^3\), gives an LCD of \(30c^4d^3\).

qs.q: Find the LCD of the rational expressions \(\frac{5}{6x^3}\) and \(\frac{7}{8x^5}\).
qs.s: The least common multiple of the numerical coefficients 6 and 8 is 24, and the highest power of \(x\) is \(x^5\). Thus, the LCD is \(24x^5\).

qs.q: Find the LCD of the rational expressions \(\frac{1}{8p^2q^4r}\) and \(\frac{5}{12pq^3r^5}\).
qs.s: The LCM of the coefficients 8 and 12 is 24. Selecting the highest exponent for each variable factor yields \(p^2\), \(q^4\), and \(r^5\), so the LCD is \(24p^2q^4r^5\).

qs.q: Find the LCD of the rational expressions \(\frac{7}{4a^3b^2}\) and \(\frac{3}{12ab^5}\).
qs.s: The LCM of 4 and 12 is 12, the highest power of \(a\) is \(a^3\), and the highest power of \(b\) is \(b^5\). Therefore, the LCD is \(12a^3b^5\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{4}{5x}, \frac{7}{15x^2}\)
qs.s: The least common multiple of \(5\) and \(15\) is \(15\), and the highest power of \(x\) is \(x^2\), so the LCD is \(15x^2\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{7}{8z^3}, \frac{5}{12z^2}\)
qs.s: The least common multiple of \(8\) and \(12\) is \(24\), and the highest power of \(z\) is \(z^3\), so the LCD is \(24z^3\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{3}{4y^3}, \frac{7}{10y}\)
qs.s: The least common multiple of \(4\) and \(10\) is \(20\), and the highest power of \(y\) is \(y^3\), so the LCD is \(20y^3\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{1}{2a}, \frac{5}{8a^2}\)
qs.s: The least common multiple of \(2\) and \(8\) is \(8\), and the highest power of \(a\) is \(a^2\), so the LCD is \(8a^2\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{7}{2x^2 + 6x}, \frac{1}{x^2 + 6x + 9}\)
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(2x^2 + 6x = 2x(x + 3)\) and \(x^2 + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)^2\). Taking the highest power of each factor yields the LCD \(2x(x + 3)^2\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{4}{x^2 - x - 6}, \frac{x}{x^2 - 4x + 3}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators as \((x - 3)(x + 2)\) and \((x - 3)(x - 1)\). Taking each unique factor to the first power gives the LCD \((x - 3)(x + 2)(x - 1)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{5}{12a^3b^2}, \frac{7}{18a^2b^5}\)
qs.s: The least common multiple of \(12\) and \(18\) is \(36\). Taking the highest power of each variable, \(a^3\) and \(b^5\), gives the LCD \(36a^3b^5\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{3}{x^2 - 16}, \frac{2}{3x + 12}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators into \((x - 4)(x + 4)\) and \(3(x + 4)\). The LCD is the product of all unique factors to their highest powers, which is \(3(x - 4)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{1}{x^2 - 2x}, \frac{5}{x^2 - 4}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators into \(x(x - 2)\) and \((x - 2)(x + 2)\). The LCD is the product of each distinct factor to its highest power, giving \(x(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) for the rational expressions: \(\frac{3}{4a^2b^5}, \frac{-1}{6a^4b^3}\)
qs.s: The least common multiple of the numerical coefficients 4 and 6 is 12, and the highest powers of the variables are \(a^4\) and \(b^5\). Therefore, the LCD is \(12a^4b^5\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) for the rational expressions: \(\frac{1}{10p^3q^5}, \frac{-3}{4p^6q^2}\)
qs.s: The least common multiple of 10 and 4 is 20, and the highest powers of the variable factors are \(p^6\) and \(q^5\). Thus, the LCD is \(20p^6q^5\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) for the rational expressions: \(\frac{-4}{6u^5v}, \frac{11}{9u^2v^4}\)
qs.s: The least common multiple of 6 and 9 is 18, and the highest powers of the variable factors are \(u^5\) and \(v^4\). Hence, the LCD is \(18u^5v^4\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) for the rational expressions: \(\frac{-7}{5x^4y^2}, \frac{2}{15x^2y^7}\)
qs.s: The least common multiple of 5 and 15 is 15, and the highest powers of the variable factors are \(x^4\) and \(y^7\). Thus, the LCD is \(15x^4y^7\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) for the rational expressions: \(\frac{3}{10u^3v^2w^4}, \frac{9}{15u^5vw^2}, \frac{-2}{6u^2v^4w}\)
qs.s: The LCM of 10, 15, and 6 is 30, and taking the highest exponent for each variable yields \(u^5\), \(v^4\), and \(w^4\). Therefore, the LCD is \(30u^5v^4w^4\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) for the rational expressions: \(\frac{7}{18a^4b^2c^5}, \frac{-11}{24a^2b^6c^3}\)
qs.s: The LCM of 18 and 24 is 72, and the highest power of each variable factor is \(a^4\), \(b^6\), and \(c^5\). Thus, the LCD is \(72a^4b^6c^5\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) for the rational expressions: \(\frac{1}{6x^3y^2}, \frac{-5}{8x^2y^5}, \frac{7}{12x^4y}\)
qs.s: The LCM of the coefficients 6, 8, and 12 is 24, and the highest powers of \(x\) and \(y\) appearing in any denominator are \(x^4\) and \(y^5\). Therefore, the LCD is \(24x^4y^5\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) for the rational expressions: \(\frac{-5}{28x^6y^3z^2}, \frac{3}{42x^2y^7z^5}\)
qs.s: The LCM of 28 and 42 is 84, and the highest powers of the variables are \(x^6\), \(y^7\), and \(z^5\). Hence, the LCD is \(84x^6y^7z^5\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{7}{6n}, \frac{4}{9n - 45}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators: \(6n = 6 \cdot n\) and \(9n - 45 = 9(n - 5)\). The LCM of \(6\) and \(9\) is \(18\), so the LCD is \(18n(n - 5)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{1}{15a}, \frac{7}{10a - 20}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators: \(15a = 15 \cdot a\) and \(10a - 20 = 10(a - 2)\). The LCM of \(15\) and \(10\) is \(30\), which gives the LCD \(30a(a - 2)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{3}{10y}, \frac{11}{4y - 12}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators: \(10y = 10 \cdot y\) and \(4y - 12 = 4(y - 3)\). The LCM of \(10\) and \(4\) is \(20\), giving an LCD of \(20y(y - 3)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{5}{12m}, \frac{2}{9m + 27}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators: \(12m = 12 \cdot m\) and \(9m + 27 = 9(m + 3)\). The LCM of \(12\) and \(9\) is \(36\), resulting in an LCD of \(36m(m + 3)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{7}{8x}, \frac{5}{6x + 18}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators: \(8x = 8 \cdot x\) and \(6x + 18 = 6(x + 3)\). The LCM of the numerical coefficients \(8\) and \(6\) is \(24\), so the least common denominator is \(24x(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{3}{2x}, \frac{5}{x^2 - 4}, \frac{1}{4x - 8}\)
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(2x\), \((x - 2)(x + 2)\), and \(4(x - 2)\). The LCM of the coefficients \(2\) and \(4\) is \(4\), and combining all distinct variable and binomial factors yields \(4x(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{3}{2x^2 - 8x}, \frac{5x}{x^2 - 6x + 8}\)
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(2x^2 - 8x = 2x(x - 4)\) and \(x^2 - 6x + 8 = (x - 2)(x - 4)\). The LCD includes the monomial factor \(2x\) and each distinct binomial factor: \(2x(x - 2)(x - 4)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{2}{x^2 - 4x + 3}, \frac{5}{x^2 - 1}\)
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(x^2 - 4x + 3 = (x - 1)(x - 3)\) and \(x^2 - 1 = (x - 1)(x + 1)\). Taking the product of each distinct factor to its highest power gives \((x - 1)(x + 1)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{x}{x^2 + 5x + 6}, \frac{4}{x^2 + x - 2}\)
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(x^2 + 5x + 6 = (x + 2)(x + 3)\) and \(x^2 + x - 2 = (x + 2)(x - 1)\). The LCD consists of all distinct factors to the first power: \((x + 2)(x + 3)(x - 1)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{3}{x^2 - 2x + 1}, \frac{7}{x^2 - 1}\)
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(x^2 - 2x + 1 = (x - 1)^2\) and \(x^2 - 1 = (x - 1)(x + 1)\). Taking each factor to its highest power gives \((x - 1)^2(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{3}{10y}, \frac{-1}{15y - 30}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators into \(10y\) and \(15(y - 2)\). The LCM of 10 and 15 is 30, so the LCD is \(30y(y - 2)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{-1}{8m}, \frac{3}{20m - 40}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators into \(8m\) and \(20(m - 2)\). The LCM of 8 and 20 is 40, so the LCD is \(40m(m - 2)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{1}{4a}, \frac{5}{6a - 18}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators into \(4a\) and \(6(a - 3)\). The LCM of 4 and 6 is 12, giving the LCD \(12a(a - 3)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{7}{6x}, \frac{5}{9x + 18}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators to get \(6x\) and \(9(x + 2)\). The LCM of the coefficients 6 and 9 is 18, so the LCD is \(18x(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{4}{9x}, \frac{-5}{15x + 15}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators into \(9x\) and \(15(x + 1)\). The LCM of 9 and 15 is 45, which gives the LCD \(45x(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{x + 2}{2x^2 - 7x + 3}, \frac{3x}{3x^2 - 7x - 6}\)
qs.s: Factor the trinomial denominators into \((2x - 1)(x - 3)\) and \((3x + 2)(x - 3)\). Including every distinct factor to its highest power yields the LCD \((2x - 1)(3x + 2)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{2x}{x^2 - 2x - 15}, \frac{5}{2x^2 - 50}\)
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(x^2 - 2x - 15 = (x - 5)(x + 3)\) and \(2(x^2 - 25) = 2(x - 5)(x + 5)\). Taking the product of the highest power of each unique factor gives \(2(x - 5)(x + 5)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{7}{6x^2 - 24x + 24}, \frac{5}{4x^2 - 16}\)
qs.s: Factor completely to obtain \(6(x - 2)^2\) and \(4(x - 2)(x + 2)\). The LCM of 6 and 4 is 12, and taking the highest power of each factor gives \(12(x - 2)^2(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{3}{3x^2 - 12x}, \frac{x + 1}{2x^2 - 7x - 4}\)
qs.s: Factor the denominators into \(3x(x - 4)\) and \((2x + 1)(x - 4)\). Combining the highest power of each distinct factor results in the LCD \(3x(x - 4)(2x + 1)\).

qs.q: Find the LCD for the rational expressions: \(\frac{5}{6x^2 - 54}, \frac{-2}{8x^2 + 24x}\)
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(6(x^2 - 9) = 6(x - 3)(x + 3)\) and \(8x(x + 3)\). Taking the LCM of 6 and 8 (which is 24) and each unique variable factor to its highest power gives \(24x(x - 3)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{9}{8z^5}, \frac{3}{12z - 36}\)
qs.s: Factoring the denominators yields \(8z^5\) and \(12(z - 3)\). The LCM of \(8\) and \(12\) is \(24\), so the LCD is \(24z^5(z - 3)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{4}{25y^4}, \frac{1}{5y + 20}\)
qs.s: Factoring the denominators gives \(25y^4\) and \(5(y + 4)\). The LCM of \(25\) and \(5\) is \(25\), so the LCD is \(25y^4(y + 4)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{11}{12a^3}, \frac{5}{8a - 16}\)
qs.s: Factoring the denominators gives \(12a^3\) and \(8(a - 2)\). The LCM of \(12\) and \(8\) is \(24\), so the LCD is \(24a^3(a - 2)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{7}{16x^2}, \frac{3}{4x - 12}\)
qs.s: Factoring the denominators gives \(16x^2\) and \(4(x - 3)\). The LCM of \(16\) and \(4\) is \(16\), so the LCD is \(16x^2(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{5}{x^2 + 5x + 6}, \frac{2}{x^2 + 7x + 12}\)
qs.s: Factoring gives \(x^2 + 5x + 6 = (x + 2)(x + 3)\) and \(x^2 + 7x + 12 = (x + 3)(x + 4)\). The LCD is the product of all distinct factors: \((x + 2)(x + 3)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{x}{x^2 - 9}, \frac{4}{2x^2 + 6x}\)
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(x^2 - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3)\) and \(2x^2 + 6x = 2x(x + 3)\). Taking each distinct factor to its highest power gives the LCD \(2x(x - 3)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{2}{x^2 - 6x + 9}, \frac{3x}{x^2 - 9}\)
qs.s: Factoring yields \(x^2 - 6x + 9 = (x - 3)^2\) and \(x^2 - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3)\). Taking the highest power of each distinct factor gives the LCD \((x - 3)^2(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{7}{6x^3 - 24x}, \frac{5}{4x^2 - 8x}\)
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(6x^3 - 24x = 6x(x - 2)(x + 2)\) and \(4x^2 - 8x = 4x(x - 2)\). Since the LCM of \(6x\) and \(4x\) is \(12x\), the LCD is \(12x(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions: \(\frac{3}{2x^2 - 5x - 3}, \frac{x - 1}{x^2 - 9}\)
qs.s: Factoring the denominators gives \(2x^2 - 5x - 3 = (2x + 1)(x - 3)\) and \(x^2 - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3)\). Combining all distinct factors yields the LCD \((2x + 1)(x - 3)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions \(\frac{3}{4x - 12}\) and \(\frac{7}{6x - 18}\).
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(4x - 12 = 4(x - 3)\) and \(6x - 18 = 6(x - 3)\). The LCM of \(4\) and \(6\) is \(12\), so the LCD is \(12(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions \(\frac{4}{5x + 15}\) and \(\frac{1}{2x + 6}\).
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(5x + 15 = 5(x + 3)\) and \(2x + 6 = 2(x + 3)\). The LCM of \(5\) and \(2\) is \(10\), so the LCD is \(10(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions \(\frac{2}{8x + 40}\) and \(\frac{3}{12x + 60}\).
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(8x + 40 = 8(x + 5)\) and \(12x + 60 = 12(x + 5)\). The LCM of \(8\) and \(12\) is \(24\), so the LCD is \(24(x + 5)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions \(\frac{1}{3x + 6}\) and \(\frac{5}{2x + 4}\).
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(3x + 6 = 3(x + 2)\) and \(2x + 4 = 2(x + 2)\). The LCM of \(3\) and \(2\) is \(6\), so the LCD is \(6(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions \(\frac{5}{6x - 24}\) and \(\frac{2}{9x - 36}\).
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(6x - 24 = 6(x - 4)\) and \(9x - 36 = 9(x - 4)\). The LCM of \(6\) and \(9\) is \(18\), so the LCD is \(18(x - 4)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions \(\frac{5}{4x^2 - 12x}\) and \(\frac{1}{6x^2 - 54}\).
qs.s: Factor each denominator completely: \(4x^2 - 12x = 4x(x - 3)\) and \(6x^2 - 54 = 6(x - 3)(x + 3)\). The LCM of \(4\) and \(6\) is \(12\), and including each variable factor gives \(12x(x - 3)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of the rational expressions \(\frac{4}{x^2 - 6x + 9}\) and \(\frac{7}{2x^2 - 18}\).
qs.s: Factor each denominator: \(x^2 - 6x + 9 = (x - 3)^2\) and \(2x^2 - 18 = 2(x - 3)(x + 3)\). Taking each factor to its highest power gives the LCD \(2(x - 3)^2(x + 3)\).
